en: Having ascended my celestial chariot, he went to my imperishable abode;
moreover, he became my heir, a lord of yoga and a king among devotees.
Sādhudharma, Sādhuvarmā, and Sādhusādhvīsamarcaka, having caused me to be worshipped with devotion, went to my imperishable abode. ||94||
Thus, O Lakṣmī, has the greatness of my devotee been described;
indeed, I shall protect my devotee in whatever manner is necessary. 95.
Wherever there is a devotee and one devoted to me, there I dwell,
whether within range or beyond it, by means of my power and my weapon.
By the power of my attendant, I protect those who have taken refuge in me—whether they be a man, a woman, or even a eunuch—who are solely devoted to me. (97)
With me as his self and my actions as his activity, he is perfectly protected by his inner self,
while I dwell at his side— in his heart, nearby, or before him.
Whether on the back, above, below, on the ground, in the middle, or even within the limbs—by my dwelling there, protection is provided in every way for my devotee. (99)
If those daughters-in-law of mine are indeed devoted to me and dependent on others,
they will certainly be protected at all times by me while remaining with them.
For I am indeed the protector of the protectorless; I always provide protection.
Through the recitation and hearing of this, there is enjoyment, liberation, and protection.

Thus ends the sixty-first chapter, titled "The Description of the Protection of Queen Citāmbarā from the Hosts of Rākṣasas such as Bhadraka by the Lord’s Mace," in the *Vadhūgītā* within the third section, the *Dvāpara-santāna*, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Puruṣottama said: Listen, O Nārāyaṇī Śrī; you should know me as Nārāyaṇa, who is the self of all, and indeed as Nārāyaṇa who is connected with all ritual actions.
One should constantly recite the name of Nārāyaṇa and bow to me, Puruṣottama;
during sleep one should remember Nārāyaṇa, and while traveling or going about, one should remember me, Nārāyaṇa.
One should remember me, Nārāyaṇa, in one's station; me, Nārāyaṇa, at the time of eating; and indeed me, Nārāyaṇa, during both the opening and the closing of the eyes.
Even while awake, one should bow to and remember me, Nārāyaṇa;
likewise, whatever is eaten, drunk, or licked, [one should offer it] with the words, "Salutation to Nārāyaṇa."
She who causes others to drink and then herself partakes attains the supreme goal;
she also leads others, even those of low birth, to a happy state. || 5 ||
For that woman who is rich in the recollection and proclamation of my name,
you, Lakṣmī— the beloved of Kṛṣṇa— are my very own universal form.
Whether in her house, field, dwelling, or body, you dwell there;
O daughter of Indra, you are reciting my sixteen-syllable mantra before me.
Born mute, Jayantī attained omniscience and Sarasvatī;
she acquired supreme scholarship and became equal to Bṛhaspati.
"Oṃ, salutations to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord; salutations!"—by reciting this very mantra, proficiency indeed arises in the intellect of the one who performs the japa.
"Oṃ, salutations to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord; Svāhā!
For her who performs this recitation, good fortune shall become firmly established. 3.62.10.
Out of fear of Time, Illusion, evil karma, enemies, Yama, and treacherous friends,
he bore the marks of the trident, fish, banner, bow, wheel, and the svastika.
To her who was thus chanting, I, the Lord Nārāyaṇa, having become present,
gave my own abode, the imperishable and eternally blissful state.
I am a Brahmin woman, an eternal devotee of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa;
the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa is my master and my husband.
Thus muttering these words, I indeed assume the form of Lakṣmī;
Bālakṛṣṇa, the Supreme Brahman, is truly my eternal husband.
"May he be my father, kinsman, well-wisher, friend, protector, and guardian"—reciting thus, I indeed perform the *brahmapriyā* rite. (15)
"May Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa be my refuge at all times.
To her who thus recites this prayer, I shall destroy the accumulation of her sins.
The beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama, is the Supreme Brahman beyond the imperishable, who assumes the essential forms of all incarnations. (17)
The Lord, the inner controller, is always within us; He is the cause of all, the inner self of all, the Lord of all, untainted, and indeed the bestower of liberation. 18.
"May the Purifier, when served, who bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation, protect her always!
To her who thus recites this prayer, I grant the station of Kamalā. (19)
All the beloveds of Brahmā, as well as the women such as Rādhā and Lakṣmī,
are the very nature of the Supreme Brahman and are half-manifestations of the Supreme Brahman.
The divine [mantras] which constitute the entire essence of the Supreme Brahman grant both worldly enjoyment and liberation;
likewise, the rituals associated with them are always devoid of attributes (nirguṇa) and bestow liberation. ||21||
"Reciting thus, I indeed bring liberation to everyone—whosoever and whomever worships Bālakṛṣṇa and his beloved consorts. (22)
"Sa sa sā sā" is her very nature—divine, eternally bestowing liberation.
As she thus recites this mantra, a divine form arises. (23)
"Oṃ, salutations to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord; Svāhā!
Reciting thus, I cause myself to be absorbed into His own form. 24.
For her who recites the mantra "Oṃ Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa is my refuge," I indeed accomplish the four goals of human existence.
I am the beloved devotee of Kṛṣṇa; Śrī Hari is my refuge.
Śrī Svāmī, the ocean of all knowledge of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, is my refuge.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the beloved master, Śrī Hari, is my refuge.
"Because I mutter these mantras, she has a constant dwelling place within me. (27)
O Lakṣmī, these mantras have been revealed by me as my own forms;
they are equal to me, identical in nature to me, and like me, they accomplish all purposes and goals. (28)
"Śrī Kṛṣṇa is my beloved, my lord, and my refuge"—this is the mantra.
It bestows all goals and consists of twelve syllables; I shall describe its greatness to you. (29)
Sarasvatī Subālikā was born as the daughter of Vedhas;
she was completely filled with all branches of knowledge and endowed with the Vedas and their auxiliary sciences (vedāṅgas).
Then, Śāradā, the daughter of Brahmā, was also born.

Sarasvatī indeed uttered the most excellent speech in Sanskrit; yet Śāradā, though she had already undergone the sacred thread ceremony, was unable to speak. Her tongue became as if mute, for it would not move at all despite her efforts. (3.1)
The Creator became weary, and Sāvitrī grew exhausted;
then the maiden Śāradā grieved deeply in her mind and went to the side of Sarasvatī, displaying her own tongue.
Sarasvatī, having reflected upon it like the twelve-syllable mantra,
consecrated the water and placed that purifying substance upon his tongue.
"Śrī Kṛṣṇavallabhācārya is my refuge," he said repeatedly;
having thus consecrated the water with mantras, he gave it to him to drink again and again upon his tongue. (34)
Meanwhile, the speech of the goddess Śāradā descended upon his tongue:
the vowels, consonants, and sentences, as well as the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas. (35)
By the power of her mantra, she sang of all things past and future;
thus the virtuous Śāradā indeed became endowed with divine speech.
The Creator of the Universe, Sāvitrī, and Sarasvatī became pleased.
O Lakṣmī, this indeed has been told: the majesty of the twelve-syllable mantra.
For those who recite or even listen to it, the supreme state is indeed certain;
even those of sinful conduct, provided they are devoted to the twelve-syllable mantra. (38)
He attains my supreme, auspicious abode known as the Imperishable;
by chanting the single-syllable mantra "Om," he goes to the highest goal. (39)
By chanting the two-syllabled mantra of Kṛṣṇa, one attains Goloka;
by chanting the three-syllabled mantra of Śrīkṛṣṇa, one attains the supreme Goloka.
Reciting either the mantra "Vāsudeva" or "Rādhākṛṣṇa," he attains the four-fold abode created by you.
Reciting the five-syllable mantra of Nārāyaṇa, one attains the white-syllable state;
by reciting "namo nārāyaṇāya" excessively, one attains the syllable of Brahman. ||42||
One who chants "Oṃ Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa" goes to the imperishable state;
one who utters "Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa Śrī-rom" goes to Vikuṇṭha. (43)
The syllable "Anādikṛṣṇanārāyaṇa" is also an imperishable word;
the divine syllable "Anādiśrīkṛṣṇanārāyaṇa" is likewise imperishable. (44)
Oṃ, "Māṇikī Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa"—by chanting this supreme syllable, one attains the state; O Lakṣmī, grant me the most excellent of all abodes. (45)
The devotee who recites "Oṃ sukhadā lakṣmī kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa," my name, attains my state; so too does the female devotee who is joined with this recitation. 46.
"Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Beloved Lord, is my refuge"—reciting this mantra, the foremost of all mantras, with enthusiasm, one enters into my inner being. (47)
Oṃ, salutation to Śrī Kṛṣṇa; Oṃ, and salutation to Nārāyaṇa.
Oṃ, salutation to Vāsudeva; Oṃ, salutation to Mahāviṣṇu. ||48||
"Oṃ, salutation to Viṣṇu," thus [he says]; "Oṃ, salutation to Sadāśiva"; "Oṃ, salutation to Hiraṇyagarbha," and likewise, "Oṃ, salutation to Śiva. (49)
Oṃ, salutation to Rāmāditya; Oṃ, and salutation to Nṛsiṃha.
Oṃ, salutation to Kapila; Oṃ, and salutation to Śrī Hari. ||3.62.50||
Oṃ, salutations to Dattātreya; Oṃ, salutations to Ṛṣabha;
Oṃ, salutations to Vāmana; Oṃ, salutations to Paraśurāma. ||91||
Oṃ, salutation to Yajña; Oṃ, salutation to Sanatkumāra;
Oṃ, salutation to Vyāsa; and likewise, Oṃ, salutation to Buddha. ||52||
Oṃ, salutations to Nara-Nārāyaṇa; Oṃ, salutations to Brahmā. Oṃ, salutations to the Supreme Brahman; Oṃ, salutations to the Inner Controller. ||53||
Oṃ, obeisance to Mādhava; and Oṃ, obeisance to Govinda.
Oṃ, obeisance to Keśava; and Oṃ, obeisance to Śrīpati. ||54||
Oṃ, salutation to the Master; Oṃ, salutation to Him who transcends the syllables. Oṃ, salutation to the Supreme Person; Oṃ, salutation to the Supreme Self. ||55||
We know Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, who is from Oḍḍiyāna; we meditate upon Him, the son of Gopāla Kṛṣṇa;
may that son of Kambharā-Śrī inspire us. ||56||

O Lakṣmī, these mantras always bestow the fruits of worldly enjoyment and liberation; they all grant the respective abodes, destroy sins and afflictions, grant all the aims of human life, and likewise fulfill all desires. (57)
A thousand, ten thousand, a hundred thousand, and even ten million recitations are considered [efficacious];
they bestow their fruits according to one's faith, according to the number, and according to one's intensity.
Oṃ, salutation to Śrī; Oṃ, salutation to Lakṣmī; Oṃ, salutation to Ramā.
Oṃ, salutation to Mahālakṣmī; and indeed, Oṃ, salutation to Nārāyaṇī. ||59||
Oṃ, salutations to Brāhmī; Oṃ, and likewise salutations to Puruṣottamī;
Oṃ, salutations to Vaiṣṇavī; Oṃ, salutations to Kamalā; Oṃ, salutations to Māyā. ||3.62.60||
Oṃ, obeisance to Vāsudevī; Oṃ, obeisance to Kṛṣṇā. Also:
Oṃ, obeisance to Mādhavī; Oṃ, obeisance to Parameśvarī. ||61||
Oṃ, obeisance to Śivā; Oṃ, obeisance to Antaryāmiṇī.
Oṃ, obeisance to Mahāvaiṣṇavī; likewise, Oṃ, obeisance to Padmā. ||62||
Oṃ, salutation to Kambharālakṣmī; Oṃ, likewise salutation to Prajñā;
Oṃ, salutation to Rādhā; and Oṃ, salutation to Brahmapriyā. ||63||
Oṃ, salutation to Hariṇī; likewise, Oṃ, salutation to Haripriyā.
Oṃ, salutation to Hiraṇyamayī; Oṃ, salutation to Kārṣṇavāllabhī. ||64||
Oṃ, salutation to Pārvatī; Oṃ, salutation also to Māṇikyā.
Oṃ, salutation to Lakṣmī, the bestower of happiness; Oṃ, salutation to Śrī, the queen of Śiva. ||65||
Oṃ, obeisance to Nārāyaṇī-Śrī; Oṃ, obeisance to Dhāminī.
Oṃ, may we know Lakṣmī, the bestower of happiness; may we meditate upon Nārāyaṇī-Śrī.
May that Śivarājñī-Śrī inspire us. ||66||
We know Krishna, we meditate upon the Beloved;
may wisdom impel us.
Om, we know the Teacher, we meditate upon the Guru.
May Pārvatī impel us. ||67||
O Lakṣmī, these mantras always bestow the fruits of worldly enjoyment and liberation;
they grant all goals of human life and fulfill every desire for happiness. (68)

Whether recited a hundred, a thousand, ten thousand, a hundred thousand, or even ten million times, those who chant with faith while remembering you and me shall have their eternal desires fulfilled. (69)
"Thou art I, I am thou, O Lakṣmī; he is I, I am he"—whoever mutters this while remembering me, to him and to her I give my very self. (3.62.70)
I give my seat, my abode, and even my own self;
for the sake of my devotees, I withhold nothing of mine, nor do I offer it as a mere gift.
Worship me, Lakṣmī; worship me, Rādhā; worship me, Kṛṣṇa, your beloved husband! Worship me, O beloved, both in public and in private, whether in light or in secret. (72)

Worship Him in the body, worship Him in the home, and likewise worship Him within as the Beloved of life; worship Him in the secret place, worship Him in the state of deep sleep—the source of eternal bliss and absolute happiness.
Devotion is service characterized by supreme love that brings delight;
one should serve me, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Self and the Highest Lord, through the means of material resources, gardens, and so forth, and by the activities of speech, mind, and body. (74)
Men and women should indeed serve me, who am present before their very eyes;
for I am of divine form, established in the supreme imperishable abode, and it is I myself who have now become the son of Kambharā here in Saurāṣṭra. (75)
O Lakṣmī, the son of the glorious Gopālakṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord,
shall remain right here in every way throughout all the Manvantaras.
I am the purifier in the form of the Guru, just as I am in the form of Lomaśa;
indeed, I dwell within minerals, stones, idols, and so forth.
Thus, I am indeed the supreme Lord myself among the Vaiṣṇava teachers—those men and women who are worthy and have been consecrated in the position of a Guru. (78)
Indeed, O Lotus-born One, I shall dwell among them and with them together with you;
therefore, those divine beings in the world are truly my own forms as gurus.
For through seeing, touching, and serving you, they are indeed saviors;
without me, the earth never becomes empty anywhere.
I function and I abide through the forms of the continuous flow and the partial immersion;
all conscious forms in the three worlds consist of the Guru. 8.1
In the Imperishable, I am eternally liberated, and I am the Lord of the Liberated;
in Goloka, I am the Lord of both the cowherd girls and the cowherds.
In Vaikuṇṭha, I am likewise the lord of the male and female attendants;
and I exist even in the unmanifest, as well as in the immortal state.
In Śrīpura I am Wisdom herself; on Kailāsa I am Śaṅkara;
in Satyaloka I am Brahmā and the Guru; and likewise in the world of the ancestors, I am Aryaman.
In the world of the gods I am Bṛhaspati; among men I am the virtuous one;
among the Daityas I am Uśanas; and among the Brāhmaṇas I am Vasiṣṭha.
Among women I am the chaste one, and among men I am the illustrious Dhiṣṇyaśobhana. (85)
Among serpents I am Śeṣa alone, and among cattle I am the bull;
among aquatic creatures I am the tortoise, and among the cruel I am the śarabha. 86.
The Kalpalatā is the best among creepers, and the Kalpavṛkṣa is the best among trees;
I am the teacher of those seeking knowledge, and the mother-in-law of my daughters-in-law. (87)
Thus, O beloved, the Guru alone is everywhere my very essence;
I always abide there within that Guru, the most excellent of all sacred places.
For him who, knowing me as the Guru and the object of perception, worships me incessantly, no other search for me remains to be made. 89.
Abiding in the Guru, I indeed wait for those who serve me;
in whatever manner they approach me, in that very same way do I honor them.
I fulfill all desires for those endowed with the state of faith;
I always make fruitful those who are bound by the moisture of love and affection. 9.1
I am a kinsman who removes bondage; I abide entirely within the Guru.
Bondage, however, consists of latent impressions (vāsanā), and these impressions arise from mental fluctuations (vṛtti). ||92||
The functions are obtained through yoga, while conjunction arises from objects of enjoyment;
indeed, the non-attainment of objects of enjoyment and so forth accompanies disjunction. (93)

By that, the dissolution of the mental fluctuations occurs, and from that, the dissolution of latent impressions follows; through this, there arises a state free from bondage, so one should always strive in such a manner. (94)
For the yoga of the Guru is indeed a persistent application that always brings about meditative realization;
it leads to the state of liberation and likewise bestows great bliss. ||95||
Association with the virtuous brings about divine splendor and is a treasure-trove of the Guru;
thus, O Lakṣmī, may I always be attained through loving devotion. 96.
I liberate all who are bound; I am the beloved Guru, free from attachment. I deliver men, women, and eunuchs from great sins.
I deliver the beasts, flocks of birds, those dwelling in the waters, and even the forest-dwellers; I rescue the trees, the creepers, the gods, the ancestors, and the sages as well. (98)
I, the Blessed One, am the protector of those who have come for refuge;
my purpose is indeed to bestow happiness and to deliver embodied beings from suffering. (99)
I perform that very same [function] at the beginning of every creation, and likewise throughout all creations;
and at the end of a creation, I likewise provide protection.
All this has been told to you, O beloved, exactly as you asked;
this knowledge consisting of the Vadhūgīta brings liberation to all women, my dear.
From reciting and hearing this, nothing remains to be known;
it truly bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation, as well as the transmission of identity with Me.

Thus ends the sixty-second chapter, titled "The Description of Various Divine Mantras and the Power of the Guru," within the *Vadhūgītā* of the third section, the *Dvāpara-santāna*, of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇī Śrī said: O beloved of Kṛṣṇa, O ocean of mercy, who indeed are the Vaiṣṇava servants?
Who are the devotees, and of what nature are they? And what is their majesty like?
Śrī Puruṣottama said: Those who perform service to my body are indeed considered my servants;
those who serve me in secret are the best—free from doubt and possessing divine vision. (2)
I wander among people in human form;
seeing me as one of the world, they serve me without any suspicion.
They consider [Him] to be like themselves, filled with the very nature of desire and anger;
they do not recognize Him as the Lord who fulfills the intentions of His devotees.
All my auspicious deeds born of my body, whether remembered or even merely seen, undoubtedly bestow liberation. || 5 ||
In that regard, those wicked ones who harbor doubts do not serve me;
perceiving me as non-divine, they consequently utter my censure.
On account of that sin, they go to hell and even among the animals;
O Lakṣmī, the state of being an Asura never ceases for them at any time.
For servitude, O Lakṣmī, is indeed difficult; it is great and consists of the total surrender of oneself.
Whether a man or a woman, one should offer up the body and everything pertaining to the body. (8)
One should offer everything without hesitation; that is the most excellent form of service.
One should not allow reasoning, deliberation, or doubt to intervene in the performance of the rite.
One should not place Dharma, shame, or legal conduct between me and Nārāyaṇa; for Dharma was created by Nārāyaṇa, and shame rests upon Nārāyaṇa.
Thinking that the practice of Nārāyaṇa alone bestows liberation and no other, one should contemplate all my activities as being of the nature of dharma. (11)
Lust, anger, greed, delusion, pride, and jesting, as well as vulgarity and the improper—all these are indeed divine for me in every respect. (12)
Desire is not mine, for it is indeed hellish; anger is not mine, for it is a slayer; greed is not mine, for it bears sin; and delusion is not mine, for it is a deceiver. || 13 ||
I have no intoxication that causes bondage, nor any jesting devoid of virtue; I have no vulgar speech nor anything mean, nor is there anything in me that is inconsistent.
Indeed, everything performed with divine intent becomes a bestower of liberation;
therefore, service is difficult for all people here to perform. (15)
Those men and women who always desire to perform service for me must likewise always remain free from apprehension.
Furthermore, one should consider that his wives must be free from suspicion;
indeed, they should be considered equal to Lakṣmī, Rādhā, and Śacī. (17)
Thereafter, one should practice the supreme, unobstructed service (dāsya);
all service filled with love shines forth and increases exceedingly. (18)
Without the sense of separation, servitude increases eternally;
without doubt, supreme servitude becomes the bestower of great bliss. (19)
When the Supreme Lord, the Consort of Kṛṣṇa, the Master and the Supreme Self, is present, how could doubt or hostility arise in one possessed of discrimination? (3.63.20)
Whatever Kṛṣṇa performs himself, all that indeed bestows liberation;
whatever Kṛṣṇa performs himself is indeed dharma and a source of merit.
Therefore, O beloved, virtuous women should indeed perform service that bestows identity;
and now hear from me, dear one, about the veils that create differentiation within that state of identity.
In the state of oneness, the absence of duality is indeed considered the veil;
the perception that "I am one" and "Hari is another" is the second [veil]. (23)
An obscuration that creates an obstacle causes harm to servitude; [it conceives]:
"I am a woman, Kṛṣṇa is a man, and this Supreme Person is indeed another. (24)
The thought "I am separate [from Him]" is the third obscuration;
and so too is the fear that another might have toward Her as She stands by the side of Hari. (25)
Even that fourth veil indeed causes injury to my service;
this is certainly not the proper occasion, for that is the fifth veil.
My mind has no concern here at all, for that is the sixth veil.
The desire for wealth is also found as the seventh obscuration;
pride is a great obstacle in service, and that is indeed declared to be the eighth. (27)
The ninth is the obstruction to the accomplishment of one's own purpose and to the state of servitude;
the tenth is the obstruction to divinity and to service at all times. ||28||
O Lotus-born One, in servitude there is the power to employ one according to one's will;
if that is absent, then even the highest form of servitude is not truly attained. (29)
Ownership, servitude, belonging to you, being intent on that, and having that as one's very self—this pentad woven from servitude is beautiful; it is servitude indeed. (3.63.30)
O Lakṣmī, just as your servitude is entirely beautiful, so too does the service rendered by men or women shine with splendor. (3.1)
Everything performed with devotion and full of love shines for me;
he who is free from all veils shines and rejoices in me.
Constantly delighting in the performance of sacred rites and devoted to my service, the Vaiṣṇavas—marked with the conch, the discus, and other signs—indeed rejoice in me. (33)
Furthermore, those Vaiṣṇavas who are devoted to serving the virtuous, likewise devoted to serving saintly women, and devoted to the worship of Viṣṇu, indeed rejoice in me. (34)
The servants of Hari, those dear to Hari, and those who act for the sake of Hari—the Vaiṣṇavas, ever enriched with devotion to me, indeed rejoice in me. (35)
Furthermore, those Vaiṣṇavas who are devoted to great enthusiasm, who partake of the great food offering (naivedya), who speak with grace toward all, truly rejoice in me. (36)
Since he resides here belonging to Viṣṇu, he is indeed my Vaiṣṇava; and since he resides here belonging to me, Nārāyaṇa, he is therefore my Nārāyaṇīyaka.
He is indeed the supreme devotee of all, devoted solely to Nārāyaṇa;
he is a devotee of Brahmā through Brahmā, and likewise an imperishable devotee of the Imperishable (Akṣara). ||38||
This [devotee] belongs to Kṛṣṇa; the devotees of Kṛṣṇa, the Vaiṣṇavas, rejoice in me.
Likewise, the followers of Nārāyaṇa, the Brāhmas, and those of the Imperishable (Akṣara) are my attendants. ||39||
Those devotees who bear the form of Brahman are proclaimed as Brāhmaṇas;
from whose presence the Brāhmaṇas, who have mastered the Vedas, were born. (3.63.40)
In ancient times, those virtuous ones beginning with Sanaka were the Brahmin gurus;
they, being virtuous yogis of Brahman, were the gurus for the Brahmins and the other castes. ||41||
Indeed, the virtuous Sanaka and others were created by Brahmā in the past, as were the ascetics of Brahmanic character, as well as Skanda and Hanumān. ||42||
Thus, these teachers, who are always devoted to the work of creation, are indeed the twice-born gurus for the Śūdra householders. 43.
Among the twice-born and others, householders who are Brahmins are the gurus;
for Brahmins, virtuous men are the gurus, since they are the bestowers of liberation. ||44||
The virtuous are the most excellent of all, honored by gods, sages, and ancestors;
the virtuous are superior even to the gods and supreme even among the great sages. (45)
The virtuous are superior to the ancestors and always most excellent among the gods on earth;
there is nothing in the three worlds that possesses such excellence as that which is found in the virtuous.
From the virtuous, the excellent ascetics who perceive Brahman are superior;
and from cows, those who are virtuous and eternally devoted to Brahman are superior. (47)
And those virtuous ones who are superior even to the Earth-goddess, endowed with forgiveness, are the best among the embodied beings by virtue of their knowledge, generosity, and liberation. 48.
For the virtuous who serve the Lord of Śrī are superior to those in the abodes of the gods; indeed, they are superior even to the virtuous who are devoted to their husbands. 49.
The virtuous devotees of Hari are superior to Brahmins learned in the six limbs of the Vedas;
and from the Vedas, the words of the saintly are superior because they lead one to Kṛṣṇa. (3.63.50)
The virtuous are superior to the Vedas because the Vedas depend upon virtue;
the virtuous are superior to sacred fords because they swiftly destroy sin. (51)
The virtuous are superior to religious vows, for they bestow infinite merit according to one's desire;
the virtuous are superior even to fire, as they purify the defilement of illusion.
Even the Brahman-sages indeed worship the feet of the virtuous;
for I am the Supreme Lord, Acyuta, who possesses the form of Kṛṣṇa and is the Lord of all lords.
We worship the virtuous, the devotees, the holy ones, who purify all with their very selves;
for they are the saints, enriched with excellent qualities, and truly they are the most eminent among those possessed of virtues.
They are the peaceful universal monarchs ruling the kingdom of Brahman;
they are the storehouses of knowledge, the learned ones, the supreme gurus. (55)
These teachers are indeed virtuous, bestowers of liberation and likewise givers of mantras;
they are saintly, knowers of the Vedas, sciences, and so forth, and are the most excellent of Brahmins. (56)
In my view, only those Brahmins who are devoted to the six duties are truly virtuous;
O Lakṣmī, the virtuous are my very self, and I am indeed always the self of the virtuous. (57)

Endowed with truthfulness, purity, and forbearance, free from attachment and aversion, possessing the knowledge of Brahman and the wisdom of discrimination—such Vaiṣṇavas are the supreme holy ones. (58)
They were devoted to the Agnihotra sacrifice, constant worshippers of guests, devoted to their fathers and mothers, and were supreme, virtuous Vaiṣṇavas. (59)
Endowed with compassion, righteousness, and other virtues, likewise devoted to merit,
and marked with the signs of the conch, discus, and so forth— these are the supreme, virtuous Vaiṣṇavas.
Those who wear a garland of *tulasī* on their necks and hold Hari in their mouths, singing the praises of Kṛṣṇa—they are indeed the supreme, virtuous Vaiṣṇavas. (6.1)
Constantly devoted to the Saṃhitās and likewise to sacrifices,
respectful toward all dharmas, they are the supreme Vaiṣṇava saints.
They liberate men from sin after sin and never reproach them;
indeed, these supreme and virtuous Vaiṣṇavas bring happiness to all embodied beings. 63.
Those who worship me as Gopālakṛṣṇa, Śrīkṛṣṇa, or Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa in my image are indeed Vaiṣṇavas, the most excellent of holy men.
The supreme, virtuous Vaiṣṇavas worship the Śālagrāma, they worship the Incarnate One, and they worship me, the beginningless Śrī Hari. (65)
"This is Gopāla, this is Kṛṣṇa, this is Rāmāditya, this is Acyuta"—
thus do the supreme, virtuous Vaiṣṇavas worship me.
Just as my form is at Kuṅkumavāpī and at Siddhapattana,
and as it is at Gokula, so too is it at the Himālaya.
And just as I assumed a particular form on the banks of the Narmadā, in that very same form do the supreme, virtuous Vaiṣṇavas worship me. (68)
Four-armed and two-eyed, holding a conch, discus, mace, and lotus, she is clad in yellow garments, possesses a flute, and is adorned with a forest garland and other ornaments. (69)
My golden image, adorned with a crown, beautiful, illuminated by the Kaustubha gem, and accompanied by Rādhā, Ramā, and the others.
One should likewise install [the image] made of silver, copper, bronze, or even precious gems, specifically using the mantras of the Āgamas and the utterances of the Vedas.
The supreme, virtuous Vaiṣṇavas should worship according to the prescribed ritual with the mantras of the sixteen services, offering from their hearts with loving devotion. (72)
Those virtuous ones are indeed Vaiṣṇavas, consisting of me and possessing the nature of merit;
as is Viṣṇu, so are they all—there is not even the slightest difference between them.
Having understood this, O King, one should always honor the virtuous;
for I am Viṣṇu, I am the virtuous man, and I am the chaste wife devoted to her husband. (74)
I am the mother and I am the father; I am the husband and the virtuous yoginī.
I am the saintly Nārāyaṇa, and I am the mistress Nārāyaṇī. (75)
I am Rudra and Rudrī, Aja and Ajī, Sura and Surī;
I dwell eternally within all beings and I manifest forth from them.
To her who desires a husband, I am to be worshipped as the husband;
to her who desires liberation, I am to be worshipped as Śrī Puruṣottama.
Śrī Nārāyaṇī Śrī said:
O Keśava, how, when, and by what objects are you to be worshipped? O Blessed One, tell me the procedure for one who desires her husband. (78)
Śrī Puruṣottama said: On the auspicious morning of the eleventh day (Ekādaśī) in the bright fortnight of the month of Caitra,
one should go to the grove and gather divine damana blossoms.
The worship of Damana must indeed be performed by the command of the Guru;
for within Damana dwells Kāmadeva together with Rati.
O Kāmadeva, homage be to you; you are eternally the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama). I seek Hari, the Desire; have mercy upon me! ||8 1||
He should be brought toward the house with the sounds of singing and musical instruments, following the preliminary consecration (*adhivāsana*) within the *sarvatobhadra* maṇḍala. (82)
O beloved, having set aside Hari, Kāma, Rati, and the Damanaka tree,
and having covered [the image] with a white cloth, one should worship the maiden.
Klīṃ, salutations to Kāmadeva; Hrīṃ, repeated salutations to Rati. At the onset of night, I worship Kandarpa with Hrīṃ in the eastern direction. ||84||
With auspicious perfumes, flowers, unbroken grains, incense, lamps, and food offerings, as well as the waving of lights and other rites, I worship my divine husband, the Lord. (85)
Salutation to Madana in the east; salutation to Manmatha in the southeast;
salutation to Kandarpa in the south; salutation to Anaṅga in the southwest. ||86||
Salutation to Mohana in the west; salutation to Smara in the northwest;
salutation to Īśvara in the north; and salutation to Puṣpabāṇa in the northeast. (87)
Then, having paid homage in all directions, the maiden should worship me with this mantra:
"Oṃ, let us know Kandarpa-puruṣa; let us meditate upon Kāmadeva; may Anaṅga inspire us. (88)
Thus, one should perform one hundred and eight recitations in his presence:
"Homage be to the Lord of Desire; homage to you, whose arrows are flowers. (89)
Salutations to you, the giver of bliss to Manmatha; salutations to you, the creator of delight. May there be salutations to you, the bestower of affection; salutations to you, the seed of all.
Salutation to you who are beloved, whose form is beautiful, and who is the dwelling place of all;
salutation to you who possess the form of the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama) and who are the god Anaṅga. ||91||
O beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, granter of desired wishes!
O Lord, beloved of Kāmeśvarī, fulfill the desires within my heart. 92.
Having thus offered praise, Mañjarī should offer water at my feet;
furthermore, a great festival should be celebrated with songs, instrumental music, and dance. 93.
One should remain awake through the night, and having bathed in the morning, one should worship Hari;
one should also honor the preceptor with wealth, clothing, ornaments, and food.
One should indeed offer gifts to the preceptor and eat together with the Vaiṣṇavas;
one should perform the gift of land, the gift of cows, and great gifts in abundance. (95)
By worshipping Mañjarī with me, you have given all gifts;
the fruit of giving a thousand cows is obtained through the worship of Damanaka. (96)
She who, in the spring, worships me with jasmine flowers with supreme devotion shall certainly obtain a beloved husband. (97)
Madhuka and Damanaka are exceedingly dear to Hari;
when I am worshipped with these two, I quickly grant a husband to a woman. (98)
Being pleased with the maiden who is the very embodiment of Rati, Puruṣottama said:
"I shall grant her a husband worthy of her—a beloved, auspicious treasure-house of splendor. (99)
Delightful like the god of love, of similar age, full of passion, gentle in character, free from disease, endowed with prosperity, and a mine of virtues. (3.63.100)
"I give you a husband who is a vessel of joy and a vessel of love.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, has been described this vow which bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation. (10.1)
In this world, worship of me and my supreme devotion, as well as the form of the holy guru and the virtuous man and woman, are likewise most excellent. (102)
Likewise, O beloved, the forms of male and female servants, Vaiṣṇavas, and so forth, as well as unobstructed service, have been described for the sake of attaining Me. (103)
Through reciting this, hearing it, remembering it, and likewise performing it,
a devotee— whether a lay devotee or a monastic— necessarily attains the fruit as described.

Thus ends the sixty-third chapter, titled "The Description of Unobstructed Service, the Excellence of Male and Female Devotees, and the Vow of Damana," within the *Vadhūgītā* of the third section, the *Dvāpara-yuga-santāna*, of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇī Śrī said:
O Hari, Nārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇa, Supreme Lord, Eternal One!
On which lunar day (tithi) are you to be worshipped in what form? Please explain this to me.
Śrī Puruṣottama said: The first lunar day (pratipad) has been declared as belonging to the Lord of Wealth; on that day, I alone am indeed to be worshipped.
For in the form of the image of Kubera, I truly become the Giver of Wealth.
Indeed, you have Lakṣmī as your second; you are the worshipful Puruṣottamī. You are the bestower of all prosperity, my very self, Narāyaṇī.
O beloved, the third lunar day is declared to be the auspicious day of the goddess Pārvatī;
on that day, Pārvatī should be worshipped, for she is considered the bestower of good fortune.
Indeed, Gaṇeśa is to be worshipped on the fourth lunar day, for he is the remover of obstacles;
he is the form of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa and the bestower of gains and other blessings.
The fifth lunar day of the moon is proclaimed; indeed, I am the moon who is to be worshipped.
I shall become a donor of cow-pens and bulls, and a giver of immortal food.
On the sixth lunar day of the month of Kārttika, one should worship Kārttika;
then, as the embodiment of Kārttika, I shall become the bestower of victory and the remover of planetary afflictions.
But on the seventh day, O beloved, the Sun is to be awakened; at that time Sūrya is to be worshipped.
I am Sūryanārāyaṇa, and I bestow manifold splendor.
The eighth day is to be known as that of Durgā; Durgā, the bestower of auspiciousness, is to be worshipped.
She is the remover of all hardships and my eternal power (śakti). || 9 ||
And on the ninth day, the auspicious Mothers indeed should be worshipped;
for they become the protectors and the bringers of well-being to those of one's lineage.
On the tenth day, Yama is to be awakened; at that time, Yama is auspicious when worshipped.
Indeed, I myself manifest as Yama, the destroyer of the suffering of sinful hells.
On this Ekādaśī, Śrī Kamalā is to be worshipped in every way; one attains the state of all auspicious things, for I grant prosperity to the one who worships her well.
"O beloved, on the twelfth day of the month of Mādhava, I was worshipped by you;
therefore, I grant you every kind of excellent honey, filled with essence."
And on the thirteenth day, I am always to be worshipped there by Kāma;
as the fulfiller of all desires, I grant all desires in their entirety.
The fourteenth day belongs to Hara; for I am indeed identical with Mahādeva.
Śaṅkara is to be worshipped, the bestower of prosperity and the granter of sovereign power. (15)
The fifteenth day is for Brahmā; Brahmā is worthy of worship, the bestower of auspiciousness, the giver of the increase of one’s lineage, and like a father, the bestower of all that is beneficial.
The lunar day known as Ācyutī, which is designated as Puruṣottama, is superior;
I alone, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, am to be worshipped there.
I am the ancient Supreme Lord, the bestower of all desired things;
for the new moon day is the sacred occasion of the gods, and the deities are indeed to be worshipped. || 18 ||
Beginning with the invocation and ending with the dismissal, worship is always considered to be firmly enriched by the beauty of all ritual offerings. (19)
Bathing, clothing, ornaments, garlands of mantras, moist sandalwood paste, incense, lamps, excellent food offerings, water, betel, and acts of pleasing [the deity]. (3.64.20)
Salutation, patience, and the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā)—these are indeed essential for worship;
thus, the complete worship shall consist of one hundred and eight items.
O Lakṣmī, it bestows all prosperity, likewise it bestows all perfections,
it bestows all desires, and it shall also bestow both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
Thus, let my devotee perform this great propitiatory worship, by the performance of which I, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the doer of what is dear, become pleased. (23)
A garland of lamps should be offered upon my palace and temple;
and one should present the fourfold food offering, consisting of most delicious delicacies.
Having honored me with the rite of garments and ornaments, one should worship the Guru;
may that worship of yours, even if devoid of the proper rites of mantra and devotion, be complete. (25)
I am blessed, I have accomplished my purpose, and I am fortunate to dwell upon this earth,
since my Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the bestower of liberation, has accepted me as his own.
Completely liberated from all latent impressions (vāsanās) and having attained divine splendor through the Rāgha-samādhi,
I have indeed been born on earth and have acquired greatness through the power of my Guru.
Salutations to the Guru, whose nature is Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Self;
you are the Guru, the divine image of the installation, for Kṛṣṇa is indeed the savior. (28)
You, Hari, are my Guru, the bestower of all bliss and the giver of liberation;
you are the destroyer of all bonds and the eradicator of the torment of sin. ||29||
You are the giver of Brahman and absolute liberation to me, the bestower of the supreme imperishable abode;
you are the very nature of the Supreme Self—salutations to you, the Supreme Self.
I am blessed, I have accomplished my purpose, and my life is fruitful;
both my parents, who were the cause of my birth, are blessed. (31)
"O Kṛṣṇa, act in such a way that I, who have acquired you as my beloved Lord from time immemorial, shall not be separated from you. (32)
"Charity, austerity, vows, devotion, and service were previously performed by me, by which I have indeed obtained the beloved Kṛṣṇa today upon this earth. (33)
By the power of her great merit, she obtained Hari as her guru;
for Viṣṇu is ever present in every way within his own devotees. (34)
One should contemplate the greatness [of the Guru] by realizing that Hari resides within the Guru;
thus, when the Guru is seen, saluted, bathed, and likewise worshipped, [Hari is so treated].
Even a woman who is constantly endowed with a spirit of devotion, though she may be possessed of faults, bestows upon the one who serves her guru merit equal to ten million sacrifices. (36)
One should worship the form of the Guru; she becomes inseparable from Acyuta within one's own abode.
The form of the Guru is the destroyer of the sin of great slaughter and the most heinous crimes. (37)
When remembered, praised, meditated upon, worshipped, and saluted, that image of the Great Goddess bestows the imperishable abode. (38)
Having obtained and served an Ācāryāṇī—one who is virtuous, venerable, chaste, divine, devoted to her husband, dedicated to Hari, and a yoginī—one is liberated. 39.
Just as female deer flee in fear upon seeing a lioness, so indeed do all illusions consisting of sin vanish here through the attainment of the Guru. 3.64.40.
That disciple who pays homage to the guru’s wife—who is pure and chaste—with devotion or even without devotion, is meritorious and destined for liberation. 41.
There is no fear of Vaivasvata for her at birth or death, who, being virtuous, performs service and worship of the preceptor’s wife. (42)
One should delight the goddess Guṇī with perfumes, water for the feet, respectful offerings, food offerings, lamps, incense, ointments, songs, musical instruments, and hymns of praise. ||43||
A virtuous woman who worships me with devotion dedicated to truth shall rejoice in my abode for tens of millions of billions of kalpas. 44.
She who has offered salutation to the divine Guru even with her inner being is a goddess in the world of mortals and a fit recipient for my grace. 45.
Arrogant due to the power of my devotion, devoted solely to me, intent on serving her guru, and virtuous, she rejoices in my abode. (46)
O Lakṣmī, I always dwell within the image of my Guru-deva;
indeed, the fruit of worshipping Viṣṇu with thousands of millions of lotuses resides there. ||47||
The virtuous woman obtains that very fruit which is gained through the worship of the Guru-deva;
however, those people in the mortal world who have not performed the worship of the Guru-deva do not obtain it. 48.
Though they have indeed died, they are born again and again as partakers of their own karma;
yet, in the presence of the Guru and the Deity, everything attains purity. 49.
Having partaken of the Guru’s grace, one obtains the fruit of ten million sacrifices;
by drinking the water from the Guru’s feet, ten million killings are destroyed.
Residing in Kāśī for eight yugas is equaled by serving one’s guru for a single day;
therefore, one who desires liberation must indeed perform the worship of the guru. 5.1
Wherever the Lord of Śrī, who is the very embodiment of the spiritual master, resides,
there indeed dwell the gods, the demigods, saintly women, and the lords.
Whatever fruit may arise from all the millions of recitations of the gods, that same fruit arises from the recitation of the names of Śrī Hari and the Guru. ||53||
Having offered oblations into the mouth of the Guru-deva even once with a single piṇḍa, the ancestors attain eternal satisfaction imbued with nectar. (54)
For those people who drink water purified by the feet of the Guru, what need is there for the consumption of thousands of *pañcagavya*? (55)

Once an expiation has arisen, what is the use of gifts, what is the use of fasts, or even of Cāndrāyaṇa penances? Indeed, [all these are rendered unnecessary] by drinking the water from the feet of the Guru.
He who gives ghee, milk, and sugar here to the preceptor has, by that act,
offered all desired foods and performed hundreds of sacrifices.
Even while dwelling at home, he performed the ritual bath of a pilgrimage site day after day;
he was initiated into all sacrifices by him through whom the Guru was satisfied.
In heaven, on earth, and in the netherworld, there are teachers who grant liberation;
yet there is nothing else in the three worlds that is as supremely purifying as the teacher-god. (59)
In this auspicious human world, life is fruitful for one by whom the attainment of a guru has been achieved, or by whom the service of a guru has been performed. (3.64.60)
A leaf, a flower, a fruit, water, clothing, wealth, or food—
by offering these to the guru and the deity, they become equal to Mount Meru.
Even a woman who is devoid of ritual procedure and lacks the performance of rites and mantras,
if she is devoted to her guru and worships with devotion, shall obtain the fruit declared by the scriptures.
I always dwell there, within the body, and always within the teacher of the teacher; for that person who, having placed the teacher upon his shoulder as a vehicle, carries him along the road. ||63||
Indeed, the path to my abode is never obstructed for him;
wherever the Guru and the Deity reside, there Hari is ever present.
In that regard, there are the holy sites of Mahādāna, Kurukṣetra, Naimiṣa,
Puṣkara, Prayāga, and likewise the Aśvapaṭṭasara lake.
There is also the Bālakṛṣṇa lake and likewise the Viṣaturyasa lake;
there too is the Nārāyaṇī and the river Irāvatikā.
Menakāṅgā is right there, and the daughter of Brahmā is also there;
wherever the Guru resides, all sacred fords (tīrthas) are indeed present there.
Whatever sin arises among people, such as the killing of a Brahmin and so forth, all that is quickly consumed by serving the Guru and the Deity. (68)
Where there is a union of both the form of the Guru and the form of Hari, that place should be understood as Dvāravatī; there, devotion to Acyuta bestows liberation.

In the worship of the Guru, there are no mantras, no recitation, and no meditative visualization; there is no ritual substance, no diamonds and the like, no offerings, nor anything else whatsoever. (3.64.70)
Neither praise nor even supplication is required; it depends solely on love, even when one has taken what should not be done, what should not be eaten, or what should not be drunk. (71)
Whatever sin there may be, it shall surely perish when the venerable Guru and Hari are satisfied;
for the disciple who is a virtuous woman performs the worship of the Guru’s wife daily.
If she performs service for her elder, such as massaging her feet and so forth,
she will certainly never experience widowhood after that endless period of time.
Having attained the good fortune of Kṛṣṇa, the lotus-like Ramā becomes manifest;
having taken refuge in the shadow of the Guru, she indeed always bestows gifts.
A person here who fears Yama should not leave the side of the guru;
for the messengers of Yama never come into the presence of the guru.
The life of that woman whose home always contains these three—the service of the guru, the service of Hari, and the service of the husband—is truly fruitful. (76)
Restraining her faculties from other objects, that virtuous woman who performs the pleasing of the Guru and the Deity, as well as service and worship with devotion, [attains success]. //77//
When objects are offered and presented as water according to what is appropriate,
and given with faith to the guru, there is for every flower the merit born of an Ashvamedha sacrifice.
That disciple who has directly taken refuge in Guru Hari attains the fruit;
liberated from birth, suffering, old age, and disease, she is considered one who has gone to liberation. 79.
Whatever fruit is obtained here by the gift of ten thousand cows,
that very fruit one shall indeed obtain by offering a lotus garland to the preceptor.
Even that which is rare and difficult to attain within the three worlds, including all things mobile and immobile—
that very wealth, O Lakṣmī, when sought, is indeed bestowed by service to the Guru.
Sovereignty, progeny, knowledge, kingdom, and the riches of happiness—the Guru’s grace bestows these very things; for that grace is held to be attainable through service. 82.
Sins as vast as Mount Meru and Mandara go to complete dissolution through service to the Guru; for the Guru is indeed Hari manifest. (83)
Having uttered "Namo Nārāyaṇāya" as well as "Namaḥ Śrīgurave," one should daily bow to the God, the Guru, Hari, the Lord, and the Master. (84)
She shall go to the Supreme Self, who dwells in the imperishable abode, the bestower of eternal bliss, and who stands in the state free from all affliction. ||85||
She who repeatedly chants the name of the Guru and the name of Hari goes to the supreme abode and does not undergo rebirth again. ||86||
And those born in her family, by the hundreds and thousands,
they too go to the supreme abode, once the Guru has been satisfied by her.
In all great festivals, a virtuous woman should worship her guru;
in the home of one who worships him, great festivals shall indeed occur constantly. (88)
In the month of Āṣāḍha, on the full moon day, a virtuous woman who possesses the super-knowledges of meditation should worship the Guru;
that chaste lady obtains its fruit, which is eternal good fortune.
One should bathe [the image] with warm water, anoint it with fragrant substances,
massage it with scented oils, and wipe it clean with pure materials.
One should cause the consecration to be performed, have garments worn, adorn [the deity] with ornaments, and worship with unbroken rice grains and other offerings. || 91 ||
The virtuous woman should worship the Guru with flowers, sandalwood, and garlands;
she should also wear ornaments and offer incense, lamps, and other such offerings. ||92||
Thereafter, one should offer fruits, desirable food, drink, and so forth to the venerable Guru, and also present an excellent sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) according to one's means. 93.
A virtuous female disciple should drink the nectar of her teacher's feet, perform the massaging of her feet, and always provide auspicious services such as rubbing her limbs. (94)
Having placed [the image] in a vehicle, a courtyard, a great garden, or likewise in a house, she, filled with devotion, should lead the Guru or the Gurvi there and satisfy them. 95.
O Śrī Narāyaṇī, that virtuous bride who thus propitiates me, the supreme guru, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, [attains her goal].96
Or any other virtuous woman might indeed propitiate her own husband Kṛṣṇa with her inner feeling;
likewise, she might propitiate her own guru through service. 97.
O Lotus-born one, all those indeed possess the form of Brahman and lead to liberation;
they are divine, possessing divine natures, and are supreme, bestowing divinity.
Whatever women come into union with him, they shall become divine and proceed to the supreme state. (99)
I am Hari, eternally divine, and my power is eternally divine;
and you are that Śrī, as well as Rādhā, Ramā, Prajñā, and Māṇikī.
Lakṣmī, Gaṅgā, Virajā, Padmāvatī, Mādhavī, and others such as these are my divine Śaktis; for they are indeed the beloveds of Brahmā.
The beloveds of Hari are not divided from me; they are always undivided from me.
All those powers, ever dear to the Guru, reside within the Guru, who is my teacher.
Accompanied by Śakti, I indeed dwell among the womenfolk;
I dwell among my masters, and I dwell with my virtuous husband.
Assuming the role of various gurus, I fulfill the desires of the mind;
thus, O Śrī, Queen of Śiva, serve me, Mādhava. 104.
From reciting this, from hearing it, from remembering it, or even from bowing to it, liberation will surely come through grasping it with devotion; of this there is no doubt.

Thus ends the sixty-fourth chapter, titled "The Description of the Constant Worship of Hari in His Various Forms on All Lunar Days and of the Guru-form," within the *Vadhūgītā* of the third section, the *Dvāpara-santāna*, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
Listen, O Śrī, Queen of Śiva, to the majesty of the Supreme Lord, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, who appears in the form of the Guru. 1.
I shall indeed proclaim my own greatness to you exactly as it is; yet, being constrained by compassion for women, I am not satiated with speaking.
A virtuous woman desiring liberation and good fortune should worship me constantly;
she should devoutly bathe me with water, honey, milk, and ghee.
With the five products of the cow, with waters, with waters scented with sandalwood, with fragrant sandalwood, with saffron, and with gulāla; || 4 ||
Likewise, one should smear me with *abīra*, saffron (*kāśmīra*), and water from the filaments of flowers,
mixed with camphor and *uśīra*, along with liquid unguents.
One should worship with beautiful flowers accompanied by perfumes and incense; indeed, O virtuous lady, one should offer guggulu resin smeared with cow's ghee in my presence.
The beautiful woman should offer a lamp with ghee day and night;
she should present as an offering milk-drinks and the like, and most excellently offer milk-rice.
Thus one should worship me, bowing down and prostrating repeatedly;
one should mutter the mantra "Oṃ, obeisance to Kṛṣṇakānta" one hundred and eight times.
And one should offer oblations of sesame, rice, barley, and so forth, smeared with ghee;
likewise, one should offer them under my name for the sake of the complete satisfaction of all the liberated ones.
One should worship my two feet with lotuses to increase devotion;
one should worship the region of my knees with bilva leaves to become playful.
She should worship my hips with royal campaka flowers;
the virtuous woman should worship my chest with land-lotuses and excellent lotuses;
and the beautiful woman should worship my head with mālatī and vṛndā flowers.
And one should worship my entire body with sandalwood paste.
Having abandoned the notion of a physical body, one should worship with the thought that it is Hari;
one should perform every kind of service to me while endowed with celibacy. 13.
Wives must perform my worship at the command of their husbands;
widows must do so at my command for the increase of liberation and happiness. (14)
For the sake of fulfilling all desires, my worship should be performed by maidens;
for the sake of attaining all prosperity, my thorough worship should be performed by men.
O beloved, such worship as this bestows liberation and prosperity;
indeed, this worship is the destroyer of the sin of selling a woman.
O Lakṣmī, you have been told what worship and devotion are; now hear about that which is most excellent:
that devotion in which the mind is absorbed is considered by me to be the supreme devotion. (17)
The inability to endure separation from me, being immersed in a stream of love, and having one's mind fixed on my own essential nature and form—that is the most supreme devotion. 18.
Devotion through one's own self is the highest; that through the mind is middling; and devotion through the body is the lowest—thus devotion, which bestows liberation, is threefold. (19)
Devotion for the liberated is spiritual; likewise, for yogis it is mental;
and for the ignorant, it is born of the body—this threefold devotion is considered to bestow liberation.
Through devotion to the Self, happiness is supreme; through the mind, it is middling; and through the body, happiness is indeed slight. Thus, happiness is divided into three kinds. (21)
Indeed, through the self in the form of Brahman, my bliss is eternal;
indeed, through the mind in its divine state, my bliss has yoga as its limit. (22)

Bliss derived from the body through ritual action, which depends upon the momentary existence of the body and so forth, and devotion intent solely on one's own self-interest—this, I consider to be *tāmasī* (of the nature of darkness). //23//
That devotion to Acyuta which contains both types of bliss is the rājasa;
that devotion which is intent on the bliss of Hari and is devoid of self-interest is the sāttvika. (24)
O Lakṣmī, if devotion to the guru and devotion to Hari are performed with a sense of identity, they yield fruit quickly; for the guru is indeed directly Hari himself. (25)
The deities always bestow peace upon a devoted woman;
Śambhu and the others grant her security, and the virtuous bestow blessings upon her. (26)
The sages, intent on bestowing blessings, grant merit;
the planets proceed auspiciously, and the piśācas also proceed auspiciously. (27)
Even Rākṣasas attain auspiciousness, as do the serene sages;
auspicious Lakṣmī herself remains forever established in his home.
Just as juices and honeys abide within her palace,
so do sweet nectars and ambrosia abide in the house of one endowed with devotion.
All nectars and great festivals abide there;
all kinds of heavens abide in the house of the devotee. (3.65.30)
The devoted woman Rādhā is always considered by me to be Lakṣmī;
she is considered by me to be Śāradā, Kamalā, Kāntā, Śrī, and Padmā. (3.1)
Whosoever, endowed with noble birth, worships me with undivided devotion, she alone is dear to me; as my devotee, she shall become Mukta-anika in liberation.
By the mere sight of her, even a killer of a Brahmin is purified; therefore, her house is considered superior to all sacred fords (tīrthas) and is like a day of fasting. 33.
Where there may be such a devoted woman, auspicious as Nārāyaṇī—she is indeed this very form of Kamalā, the devotee who removes all sins. (34)
Indeed, she who bestows the fruit of liberation—just like Gaṅgā, Ramā, and Yamī—resides in such a manner wherever a devotee stays, whether in a sacred place or in a temple. (35)
Whatever exists in his lineage or upon this earth, it indeed bestows liberation upon all.
What is the use of much speaking here? She is the beloved of Ramā; she is indeed Ramā herself.
Those virtuous women who, considering Ramā to be my devotee, shall bow down to her—even a woman who has killed a Brahmin is indeed purified by the mere sight of them. (37)
O Lotus-born One, even Brahmā indeed does not know the merit of that woman who serves her in the capacity of a maidservant. (38)
Whoever worships the Vaiṣṇavī goddess, who is devoted and endowed with the conch and the discus, by him indeed the entire world, both stationary and moving, is worshipped. (39)
That very day is blessed, blessed is her mother and that family as well;
blessed is the father by whom a virtuous woman, devoted and honored, was brought forth. (3.65.40)
All these virtuous women are most blessed and devoted to me;
by the mere sight of them, even great sin is dissolved. (41)
Indeed, all minor sins and those miscellaneous ones are entirely destroyed by the mere sight of Vaiṣṇava women. 42.
Like purifying fires, women who are always devoted to Viṣṇu indeed destroy all impurity—whether it be moist or dry, light or heavy. (43)
Indeed, whatever sin is committed through negligence, whether done knowingly or unknowingly, as well as sin born of association, perishes most swiftly. 44.
O Lakṣmī, by the sight of virtuous women and likewise by the service of the righteous,
those who are sinless go to heaven, while even the most wicked attain purity.
She is indeed skilled in liberating one from the snares of karma in saṃsāra;
she is the purifier of purifiers, and my devotee is always auspicious. 46.
That devotee of mine who remembers me day and night every single day should be known as my very own form; she is Hariṇī, without a doubt. (47)
[Behold] me, shining white as camphor, with eyes as broad as lotus petals, bearing the conch, discus, mace, lotus, fish, banner, and bow. 48.

He was resplendent in yellow garments, brilliantly illuminated by the Kaustubha gem, with the Śrīvatsa mark upon his chest, well-nourished, and adorned with a forest garland and other ornaments. ||49||
Hari, whose face and cheeks were pervaded by the luster of golden earrings,
was endowed with bracelets, armlets, anklets, a crown, and a girdle.
[He beheld] the Lord, the all-pervading Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa,
whose face was serene and who was resplendent with the mark of the white Śrīvatsa situated on his left thigh.
The supreme male [image] measures fifty-six and a quarter finger-breadths in height;
it has four arms, a face as white as the moon, and eyebrows adorned with bow-like curves.
That virtuous woman who meditates upon me, the beginningless Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, is indeed a Vaiṣṇava devotee; she is the embodiment of Śrī and possesses my own essential nature.
O Kamalā, by even the sight of her, or through devotion, or by feeding her, or by worshipping her, one becomes a female friend who attains liberation.
Just as one afflicted by thirst [longs for] water, so too does she remember me;
and just as one overcome by cold [longs for] fire, so too does she remember me. (55)
Just as a woman devoted to her husband remembers him, so too does she remember me;
just as one who is afraid remembers her protector, so too does she remember me. (56)
Just as one possessed by greed remembers wealth, so too does she remember me;
just as one desiring a son remembers a son, so too does she remember me. (57)
Just as one who has been exiled longs for home, so too does she remember me;
and just as the female cātaka bird longs for the cloud, so too does she remember me. (58)
Just as one who knows Brahman remembers Brahman, so too does she remember me;
and just as the ancestors [remember] the funeral cake, and the gods [remember] the oblation at the sacrifice. (59)
Just as sages [remember] their mantras, as humans [remember] their wealth,
and as swans [remember] Lake Mānasa, even so does she remember me.
Just as a lustful woman remembers her lover, or as a devotee remembers Him who is being worshipped,
or as a mother remembers her child, even so does that virtuous lady remember me.
Just as the devotees [remember] Kṛṣṇa, just as the Vaiṣṇavas [cherish] devotion,
and just as animals [crave] grass, even so does she remember me.

The virtuous remember the Dharma, the good remember forgiveness, the merchant remembers his profit, the living being remembers its life, and the wife remembers her husband; likewise, she also remembers me.
Just as living beings [depend on] life, bees on flowers, and female pigeons on the sun, so too does she remember me as her beloved remembers his beloved. (64)
Just as one staying at night remembers the light, or as one afflicted by fatigue remembers rest, or as one who is awake remembers sleep— so too does she remember me.
Just as diligent elephants seek out the forest regions for their success,
and just as lions frequent the dense woods, even so does she remember me.
Just as fire arises in a sun-crystal upon encountering a ray of the sun,
so too does a virtuous woman become filled with love for Hari through association with the truly good.
Just as the moonstone would ooze nectar through contact with the rays of the moon, so indeed, through union with Viṣṇu, devotion to Hari arises within you. 68.
Just as the night-lotus blossoms upon encountering the moonlight,
so too does the lotus of the heart blossom upon encountering the weighty devotee.
Just as a female insect, by remembering a bee, is born as a bee, so too a virtuous woman, by remembering me through the memory of yoga, becomes equal to me. ||3.65.70||
And the brides, through the very thought of desire, attained the supreme form of Kṛṣṇa;
likewise, by remembering me, the cowherd woman becomes Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa.
One virtuous woman acts as my laughter, and another acts as my affection;
one acts as my longing, and another acts as my sovereign.
One passionate woman acts like a lover, and another acts like Kṛṣṇa;
in this way, through the yoga of devotion, she finds me in her presence in an instant.
Even though I am ever present, I remain far away for those who lack devotion;
the Supreme Lord is perceived by devoted ones through the yoga of devotion.
Even though the gods and others have obtained the nectar of immortality, they are nonetheless subject to suffering;
yet, by obtaining devotion alone as their nectar, all suffering is destroyed.
Having reached Vaikuṇṭha through devotion, one rejoices in the presence of Viṣṇu;
therefore, abandoning everything else, one should take refuge in devotion to me. (76)
Whatever is performed without devotion after having obtained this body is indeed in vain;
for without devotion to Viṣṇu, there can be no boat to cross the ocean of worldly existence.
My devotion extinguishes the forest fire of suffering;
indeed, it establishes my devotion even in future births. (78)
Having become my maidservant Māmakī, Lakṣmī is then born;
she indeed bestows upon me even a particle of devotion as my abode.
Devotion is heard of by hundreds, understood even by thousands, and practiced by hundreds of thousands; among them, a certain devotee may become like Ramā herself. (3.65.80)
In this world, many grant intelligence, yet only a rare few truly worship; even among them, one who has attained identity with That remains non-dual amidst millions. (8.1)
Devotion is mocked by ritual worship, and likewise, devotion is ridiculed by mere recitations;
yet through devotion, devotion is praised, and by me, devotion alone is embraced.
Just as branches, leaves, and fruits arise from a tree that has been watered at its root,
so too does Hari, when watered with devotion, produce the fruit of bliss for his devotees.
O Lakṣmī, whatever kind of conduct one has, one indeed performs devotion accordingly; from such worship alone, the fruit shall be obtained hereafter.
Just as a water-carrier gives her attention to drawing up the water from the jar onto the bank, if she likewise directs her mind toward me, she is liberated. (85)
Just as the sky, though situated in the world, is not defiled by the elements, so too the devotee, though situated in the world, is not defiled by actions. 86.
For day and night my devotees subsist upon my bliss; though they remain here, they are considered to be established in my abode, divine and liberated. (87)
The fruit of sacrifices such as the *sarvamedha* is heaven, which is like a water-shed;
but the fruit of the sacrifice of devotion to me is free from returning [to saṃsāra]. (88)
By my grace, the infinity of this devotion of mine has been seen;
like a stone situated in the midst of water, it is not wetted by the water. (89)
Even though my devotee remains within the realm of Māyā, he is not tainted by Māyā;
for, by my power, there is coolness within my devotee even without water.
The frog dwells in the water, yet it does not perceive the fragrance of the lotus;
but the bee, though its dwelling is in the forest, truly perceives the fragrance of the lotus.
I dwell within the heart; outward activity does not know me. One endowed with love and devotion knows me as abiding in the heart, even if standing far away. (92)
Some dwell on the banks of the Gaṅgā, while others dwell on Mount Arbuda;
yet it is the person who knows the greatness [of these places] and is endowed with devotion who attains the fruit. ||93||
A donkey carries a load of sandalwood, yet it perceives no fragrance;
likewise, that which is situated outside does not know me who am situated within, nor does it attain my bliss.
Deer, perceiving the scent of musk, smell its delicious fragrance; yet they do not know it resides in their own navels. In the same way, those whose faces are turned outward do not know Me.
Instruction is useless for fools who are devoid of knowledge;
likewise, even bliss is useless for those who are devoid of devotion to Me. (96)

Just as one who has drunk poison does not [enjoy] milk, or as one whose devotion is for a rogue does not [find] such [benefit], so too a blind man does not see a lamp; likewise, one whose face is turned outward does not perceive me.
Just as the skin covers the body, the body covers the sense organs, and the sense organs [cover] the latent impressions (vāsanā), so too is it with the dress. (98)
The individual soul (jīvātman) is enveloped by that [intellect], and by it, indeed, am I enveloped.
Subtler than the subtle, dwelling within, I abide as the Self, yet the Self does not perceive me. 99.
Ghee exists in milk and oil in sesame; in that same way, I exist everywhere.
Though I am present everywhere, those whose desires are directed outward do not know me.
Just as jewels strung upon a single thread are held by me in that manner,
so too all creations and individual selves are strung together in every way, yet they do not know me.
Just as fire, though residing within wood and other materials, is seen externally through friction, so too am I, though situated within the self, perceived through the churning of devotion. 102.
Just as lamps arise from a lamp and depend upon others, so too do all those who possess knowledge and attain liberation through devotion spring forth from the Guru. 103.
Just as light shines everywhere at the rising of the sun, so too does the master himself shine forth when fortune rises. 104.
Just as the wind is all-pervading and the bearer of all fragrances,
so too is Lord Hari the Guru, all-pervading and the bringer of the fruits of action and devotion.
Just as water is rich in its own flavor, so too shall the flavor exist in the mouth;
and just as the Self is full of love, so too shall the flavor of bliss exist within one's own being.
The earth is endowed with many flavors and takes the form of various crops;
likewise, the Self is enriched by manifold pleasures and is possessed of the diverse bliss of Brahman.
This self, whose nature is truth, consciousness, and bliss, becomes exceedingly joyful through devotion;
united with my bliss, he becomes one who possesses great bliss.
O Lakṣmī, she who truly knows my bliss and my devotion within her heart is a devotee equal to Kamalā, destined for my abode.
I dwell everywhere, yet the worlds do not know me;
they do not know me because of ignorance, nor do they find me because of a lack of devotion.
If they should perform all rites dedicated to Viṣṇu as their deity,
they attain that which stands before them through those very qualities-less yogas.
Thus it was said by me, O Lakṣmī: having reflected upon, attained, and understood my wonderful presence, and having worshipped me, one shall obtain me. 1.12.

Thus ends the sixty-fifth chapter, titled "The Description of the Excellence and Greatness of Devotion as Spoken by the Blessed Lord," within the *Vadhūgītā* of the third section, the *Dvāpara-santāna*, of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Puruṣottama said: Listen, O Śivarājñī, for I am one, yet I am also manifold through the distinction of names and forms, and likewise through the distinctions of the ages (yugas). || 1 ||
Indeed, I manifest through the diversity of devotees and through the diversity of tasks;
I am eternally established within every living being, determined by each individual soul.
For my will is indeed Mahāmāyā; she is the very root-nature (mūlaprakṛti). Rādhā and Lakṣmī are my two powers, for they are identical with me.
I have likewise created Pradhāna, which consists of the three guṇas;
therein indeed dwell infinite individual souls (jīvas) endowed with consciousness.
From Pradhāna alone the elements arise, which are the causes of the body;
from them the bodies are produced, serving indeed as dwellings for the individual souls and the rest.
O Lotus-born one, I am Viṣṇu, consisting of the *sattva* aspect of *māyā*;
and I am Brahmā, the lotus-born, consisting of the *rajas* aspect of *māyā*.
I am Śambhu, consisting of darkness and illusion, and I am born from your forehead;
indeed, I, the Supreme Lord, dwell everywhere there.
Therefore, I am omnipresent within the mandala of the creation of the three gods;
yet, due to ignorance, worldly beings do not know me, who am hidden and dwelling in the cave of the heart.
By means of this knowledge, indeed, the virtuous and best of ascetics understand;
for that is the knowledge of Brahman, wherein my supreme refuge resides.
This is indeed the conclusion of the Vedas, O beloved, wherein I have been described;
and by this, one attains for oneself the supreme, all-pervading, and eternal Brahman.
Brahman is contemplated by the mind and likewise seen with the eye;
Brahman is embraced by the body, and Hari is attained through grace.
Hari is served by one whose self is disciplined through a pure mind;
the eternal Supreme Brahman is to be grasped by means of the mind as its kinsman. 12.
Indeed, the veil of illusion must be cast off by the mind as its kinsman;
through the mind as its kinsman, living beings are carried across by the yogi of Brahman.
Living beings are cast down by the mind, that enemy which seeks after sense objects;
yet, by meditating with the divine mind upon me, the Lord of Śrī, the Supreme Lord— (14)
Indeed, even while performing divine actions, one is not defiled;
just as a lotus leaf situated in water is not smeared by the waters. || 15 ||
Even when my mind has entered into illusion, I, the yogi, am indeed not stained;
when one knows the essence of Brahman, then everything else tastes like salt water.
When one knows the essence of devotion, then everything else becomes like poison;
when one knows the essence of service, for him even sovereignty becomes like filth.
When one experiences the essence of divine love, everything else appears loathsome;
when one knows my true value, everything indeed seems like mere refuse.
When one knows the food of bliss, nothing such as liberation pleases him;
and when he stands within the flow of my bliss, he truly knows nothing else.
Then, by way of a continuous flow, the mind attains a state of fluidity;
through this fluid devotion, having reached me, it attains the yoga of identity.
Through union with the Guru and through union with the scripture, divine knowledge is attained;
through repeated practice, higher realization (vijñāna) is attained, and from that, the object of knowledge (jñeya) is reached. ||21||
I am to be known as the Supreme Self, the Lord of Śrī, the Puruṣottama;
when I have been attained, then that which consists of Māyā becomes void.
Purity of being is the foremost step; purity of mind is superior to that;
and purity of the self is the highest step; through these, Hari is attained. (23)
Indeed, women are of many kinds and embrace in manifold ways;
according to the disposition and the relationship, so too are the results, such as the ritual action and so forth. (24)
As is one's inner disposition, so is the fruit; as one embraces one's own beloved, so is the result.
As living beings embrace Lord Hari, so is the result. ||25||
By whatever understanding one attains [me], in that same way the fruit is obtained;
for according to the understanding with which one approaches me, so indeed do I grant the fruit.
The supreme fruit, which is the bliss of the Self, is always to be attained through service;
indeed, when one is rendered gracious, the Great Bliss is bestowed by Me. (27)
Through favorability characterized by clarity, through the avoidance of hostility, and through service free from apprehension, clarity arises through devotion. (28)
It cannot be obtained by purchase, nor by moments of cognition such as those arising from the sense organs;
it is not attained at that very moment, nor is it gained through activity for one's own sake. (29)
She is not attained through pride, nor through cleverness, nor through skill;
she is not attained through the functioning of one's own desired mind, but rather through total self-surrender.
It is obtained solely by the observance of all commands with a spirit of humility;
it is obtained through service, through servitude, and by being possessed of Him. ||3.1||
Thinking that he was my own and considering her to be such a virtuous woman,
I felt great joy and subsequently attained [liberation].
By that means by which I am to be attained, one must become a revealer;
just as when one wears one's own sandals, the earth becomes free of thorns. //33//
When one has attained the state of being a servant, Māyā grants divinity through her persistence;
when one has attained the state of being a master, Māyā indeed results in the absence of lordship.
When one’s own wretchedness has been overcome, illusion (māyā) becomes entirely devoid of existence for him;
when everything has been offered to the Self and that state is attained, illusion reaches a state of hopelessness. //35//
If the intellect were of the nature of Brahman, the effect of Māyā would dissolve;
however, that intellect which consists of Māyā is the giver of birth to the world. (36)
A poisonous creeper, even when sprinkled with milk, does not relinquish its poisonous nature;
likewise, if the intellect is possessed by demonic states, it does not relinquish its demoniac character.
Even if a neem tree were to drink the juice of sugar, it would remain more bitter;
likewise, the nature of an asura never pleases me.
For such worldlings, the multitude of scriptures is useless;
they do not abandon their inherent nature, nor do they even seek the company of the virtuous. (39)
He to whom devotion does not appeal, who possesses no natural affection, and who has no desire for liberation—such a person delights in atheism. (3.66.40)
His hope for eternal joy always becomes like a flower in the sky;
for once the mango tree has been cut down, how can its fruit or flowers be obtained? (41)
Having abandoned devotion and service, how can happiness be attained?
For if one seeks the pleasure of the senses, the birth of an embodied being is indeed in vain. 42.
Having cut down clumps of camphor, he instead protects mere weeds;
his effort there is indeed in vain, for they are devoid of sap, flowers, and other qualities.
Indeed, he censures the service of the virtuous and practices the service of the wicked;
being devoid of meritorious deeds, all his effort is entirely in vain. (44)
In a golden vessel, the food of dogs is cooked by an outcaste;
but within a human body, the torments of Yama are cooked by one's own sin.

One who lacks Hari has a birth that is diseased and a birth in vain; his mind is afflicted by the disease of illusion; his exertion is fruitless as he possesses no home or treasure; and his death is likewise in vain.
Words are in vain for the great fool, and medicine is in vain for one who lacks self-restraint;
a journey is in vain without Hari, and indeed, birth is in vain for a dung-eating worm.
But he who, having abandoned Hari, the Lord of all, serves a monkey, is equal to one who nourishes only his own body and is devoid of liberation. ||48||
What indeed is the fruit of even many sciences and scriptures without devotion, since there is no peace of self? Therefore, one should worship that which bestows peace. 49.
O Lakṣmī, what is the use of that body which indulges in sandalwood and such luxuries, yet neither serves Hari nor provides liberation for the virtuous? (3.66.50)
