Even a dog-eater (outcaste), if endowed with devotion, makes his birth meaningful; even a Brahmin's body, if devoid of devotion, makes his birth a source of hell.
Just as one who has fastened a jeweled bracelet finds a mirror useless, so too,
having attained the company of the virtuous, all other means are in vain.
Those who have taken firm refuge do not accept the sovereignty offered by the gods and others;
those of firm devotion do not accept even the sovereignty offered by Hari himself. (53)
For one who eats without desire, victory resides at every step;
indeed, even Nārāyaṇa himself is not able to entice him.
By desire the embodied being is bound, but by craving he is destroyed;
for one who stands above both of these, even a lord is not able to give [anything] here.
Indeed, nothing in the three worlds is capable of depriving one who is eternally contented, peaceful, and fearless of their fortitude, even though they are a devotee. (56)
In order to please such a devoted one, Narayana becomes manifest before him,
and he becomes meditated upon by him.
Having meditated upon me, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa—who indeed possesses a form, a divine appearance, and who is the eternal abode—people [attain me]. (58)
Innumerable embodied beings, having performed worship, devotion, divine service, and likewise servitude, have gone to my supreme imperishable state. (59)
Even after making me their slave, and even after practicing devotion to their husbands,
women have gone to my imperishable state by making me their servant.
Devotion does not arise toward the void; devotion arises toward the one who possesses form—toward me, the Lord, the Consort of Śrī, the Supreme Sovereign who is the very nature of the support. 6.1
Having indeed practiced loving devotion toward me, their husband and master, as if I were Śrī [the Goddess Lakṣmī],
the women of former times attained [their goal] by resorting to the state of being a paramour.
How much more so, then, my own wives who have taken refuge by surrendering all their possessions?
Therefore, O Lakṣmī, I am the Lord myself—the embodied Master, the Sovereign, and the Husband.
Becoming a bestower of happiness and a giver of eternal bliss, I lead them away;
for some there is affection upon seeing me, while for others it is greater through touch. (64)
For some there was affection for amorous play; for some, even for sleep;
for some, in the enjoyment of desire; and for some, in the act of the rāsa dance.
For some, there was affection for food; for some, for the play of bathing;
for some, for kissing and the like; and for others, for the great festival.
In the company of some, in the non-separation from others, on their own beds for some, and in playful jests for others. (67)
Indeed, in some there is perceived a secret affection for me;
having fulfilled their desires, I bow to my own imperishable abode.
Having indeed made that virtuous Muktānikā my wife,
I, possessing a beautiful form, shall lead her to my own abode of eternal bliss.
Indeed, the flavor of service is obtained in embodied form by groups of beautiful women;
however, the full flavor of service is attained by devotees in Me, the Abode. (3.66.70)
Indeed, by my grace alone, this bride shall become a handmaid to liberation, her body bristling with joy and her eyes filled with tears of bliss. (71)
The maidservant sings of me with her speech, remembers me even with her mind,
and delights me through her actions by offering the gift of her hips and so forth.
Through worship, recitation, adoration, service, massaging the feet, and other such acts, as well as through the disposition of offering the secret [of one's being], one attains eternal bliss. ||73||
Those who are devoted to me while I possess form serve me through their bodily states;
with all their senses, they obtain great bliss like a worldly friend.
Having become a bride, she serves me, her husband and lord, as her chosen beloved;
for I fulfill all desires through women, who are indeed the gateway to desire.
I have no desire, nor even any pleasure; I do not cherish sensual happiness.
For me, whose desires are fulfilled, what use is there for passion or for desire? (76)
For me, whose form is completely filled with all-bliss, there is no incompleteness; nor is there any dependence on the senses. What, then, is the use of desire? (77)
In the past, desire was created by me for the sake of providing pleasure to those engaged in action;
for desire is indeed composed of illusion, and likewise, delight is composed of illusion.
I have no concern with her, nor with that which is illusory;
for people, both men and women, under the sway of the body, [behave] as if toward their own kin. (79)
They imagine objects of desire within me, the perfect and eternal;
thus, being conditioned by desire, they grasp those various objects through those various mental states.
Even through the gateway of desire, having granted me union, I lead them to my own abode; O beautiful ones, I cause even those possessed by passion to attain the state of liberation. ||81||
Such compassion for me must be understood, for cyclic existence is indeed of such a nature;
for those who are devoted to the senses are held by me to be my devotees on this earth. (82)
Likewise, devotees attached to sense objects dwell here and there;
however, truly wise ones who possess the nature of Brahman exist only rarely. (83)
Therefore, having reached those who approach Me in whatever manner they do, I, being of that same nature,
bestow upon them the yoga of liberation and lead them thus to My imperishable abode.
For the most part, I become filled with desire in order to bring about the spiritual accomplishment of women;
how else could there be the deliverance of those who are so deeply attached to desire? (85)
Therefore, becoming subject to compassion, I shall always serve them like a lover;
having fashioned them with divine forms, I lead them to supreme liberation.
A bride, a maiden, young women, or even elderly women devoted to their husbands; a eunuch, a widow, a woman whose husband is living, or a female student (brahmacāriṇī). ||87||
The female ascetic, the yoginī, the virtuous woman, the chaste wife, the noble lady, the dispassionate one, the renunciant, the mindless one, the female ascetic, and the forest-dweller. ||88||
Whether she be a renunciant established in Sāṃkhya and Yoga, or a courtesan,
a wanton woman, a self-willed woman, or even a passionate woman, she is free from desire.

A widow, a eunuch, one devoid of passion, one in her menses, or one who has passed her menses; whether she be a Gaurī, a Rohiṇī, a maiden, or one whose nature is like a corpse—(these are not to be approached). ||3.66.90||
Whether conditioned or unconditioned, pure or impure, she is free from [duality];
she is both abandoned and possessed of mantra, initiated and yet disparaged. ||91||

Whether she be a woman exiled to the forest, a woman who carries off forest produce, a dog-eater's daughter, a sister-in-law, a young woman, or one devoid of passion, she is solely devoted to sexual misconduct. (92)
Whether she be shaven-headed or long-haired, unfortunate or fortunate, humpbacked or short, possessed of her senses or devoid of them, she remains indeed indifferent. (93)
Whether she be of such a kind or otherwise, whether she belongs to the animal realm, or follows the nature of a cow, or the nature of a deer— whatever she may be— (94)
Whether she is clad in bark garments or red, dispassionate or dressed in yellow robes;
whether she is a goddess, a female demon, or a rakshasi, her garment is the banner. (95)

Whether she be a female donor, a female serpent, a naked woman, a female bird, or a female camel; or a female tree-spirit, one devoid of a creeper-like body, a female Sharabha, or even a lioness. (96)
Whether she be a beast of prey, a many-legged creature, or a back-crawling ogress;
whether she be a female seer, a goddess, a female ancestor, a mother, or a guardian of the field. (97)
Whether she be a female bird, a Kinnarī, a Gandharvī, or a dancer; whether she be a courtesan engaged in sexual union, or even one who possesses a thousand male organs. ||98||
Whether she be a goddess, a human woman, a spirit, a ghost, or a ḍākinī; whether she be lowly, a doer of evil, or whoever she may be who has come to me— (99)
Having obtained her through my own being, and having purified even that queen who was impure, I shall lead her, once she has been consecrated, to my imperishable abode.
For that purpose, I, Hari, become a human being in male form in order to deliver tens of billions of groups of women.
O Lakṣmī, the secret has been told to you here: desire characterized by the qualities of pleasure is the bull. For when desire reaches me, it becomes righteous and brings about liberation.
The connection through the womb of women produces the highest affection;
having established it in such a way, I lead all women to the supreme, imperishable state.
Having heard and recited this secret teaching, which bestows divinity,
is rich in liberation, and belongs to Nārāyaṇa, they shall go to my abode.
But those women or men who entertain doubt in this matter shall fall into sin;
having lost the merit previously performed, they will go downwards.
Those who speak according to worldly opinion are indeed full of doubt regarding unworthy recipients; but those who know the divine have no doubt regarding my worthy recipients.
Indeed, the secret of the Vadhūgītā which resides in my heart—
that which bestows liberation upon the bride— is here explained to you without reservation.
The bride-price, being drawn from my home, and even the affection [of the husband]—nothing more than this remains to be understood regarding women in this world. (108)
For those joined with the state of desire, I am the giver of liberation; of this there is no doubt.
One should worship Hari, having first placed one's own duty at the forefront. 1.09
For the duty of a woman consists in pleasure, while the duty of a man is placed before him as desire; yet in their union there is celibacy—this is the supreme vow for a woman.
Death in one's own dharma is better, for the dharma of Hari bestows liberation. Indeed, through the yoga of Hari within one's own dharma, liberation shall surely occur; of this there is no doubt.

Thus ends the sixty-sixth chapter, titled "The Exposition of the Secret of Devotion of the Bride," within the *Vadhūgītā* of the third section, the *Dvāpara-santāna*, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
Listen, O Śrī Nārāyaṇī; I shall declare to you what is dear to my heart.
Indeed, I am the common Great Lord of all living beings.
"Only by propitiating me have all those endowed with sovereignty been created here;
therefore, I grant them whatever sovereignty they desire."
"Rewards must be given according to the fruit of one's actions; this is my constant principle.
But the fruit of favor is empty—this is the distinction in my house."
For my satisfaction toward a servant takes the form of a reward;
however, toward one who is diligent in performing his duty, my satisfaction is innate.
Whether among women or men, wherever they may be created—be it among the daughters of Pārvatī, those of the ocean, those of the islands, or among other women—I [bestow this]. || 5 ||
In a woman who is Hārītī, or likewise Amaryā, Gaurī, Paryā, Rāśiyānī, Brāhmī, Raudrī, or Vaninī;
or in one who is Mānasī, Īśānī, or Daridrā— (6).
Whether she be of the lowest caste, the first-born caste, or even the middle caste.
Whether she be a Dhīvarī, a Śabarī, or a Yavanī, or likewise a Piśaṅgī, a Prācīnakāyā, or even an Abriktā; || 8 ||
Whether it be toward a woman who is fair, dark, or variegated in complexion, or likewise toward a man, or toward a devotee of the gods or of the sages; (9)
Whether it be in the Lord or in the liberated one, wherever my grace resides,
there indeed shall be an incalculable abundance of all jewels for everyone.
There would be an incalculable number of all sovereignties and spiritual accomplishments;
there would be an incalculable number of all prosperities and miraculous powers. || 11 ||
There is an incalculable number of joys, pleasures, and delights; likewise, there is an incalculable number of festivals, as well as exultations and playful diversions. (12)
There shall be an incalculable abundance of fortunes, blessings, and objects of enjoyment;
there shall be an incalculable abundance of all desires and satisfactions. (13)
Wherever I may be pleased and manifest in the form of a reward,
there my imperishable state and even the supreme heaven abide.
Speak, Lakṣmī, how could there be any deficiency from that?
Everything is indeed divine for me; everything is the most excellent.
"The devotee's house is my house; I am the devotee, and I am he indeed.
Thinking thus, that family dwells within my heart as my very own.
For me and for my devotee, there is not even the slightest difference;
what is illusion, and what is time? For the Lord indeed dwells within my abode.
That supreme, imperishable abode where I indeed dwell is truly of the nature of an earthen house; that eternal state is the highest goal. || 18 ||
That palace where I am not present is like a celestial chariot turned into hell;
this ground where I do not dwell is like a cremation ground; and that woman who is not attended by me is but a demoness. (19)
That Lakṣmī by whom I was not embraced is but a malevolent spirit (piśācinī);
and he by whom I was not saluted nor Mādhava embraced has no prosperity at all.
And that real Rākṣasa, the devourer of births, exists here;
and by taking refuge in me, even Piśācas become the highest deities. || 21 ||
Even piśācinīs, upon reaching me, become the wives of Brahmā;
for defects are indeed piśācas, and those possessing them become piśācinīs.
For just as pearls possess their strings, so too do those who possess these qualities become liberated when they are cast off;
indeed, those who possess the knowledge "I am Brahman" truly become the consorts of Brahman.
All those who have taken refuge in the Supreme Brahman indeed become wives of Hari.
Having abandoned me, who am Hari, why would she practice the hardship of penance? (24)
Without the Supreme Lord, no one at all can attain perfection;
for bodies and the infinite attributes of the body were indeed created by Brahmā. (25)

The qualities of Brahmā, the qualities of the body, the qualities of the mind, as well as those that are internal, and likewise the qualities of the world—all these, which bestow every happiness, were created by him. (26)
My dharmas are indeed eternal; even Brahmā was created by me.
Relying upon my supreme, eternal dharmas, he returns to me.
Indeed, my very grace is the dharma that bestows divinity upon me;
having duly honored the dharmas of Brahmā, one should practice my dharmas. (28)
There remains nothing further to be done by me, whose wife is Dharma;
for this is my own duty, and that duty is pure and free from worldly qualities.
One should indeed abide by pure dharma and always give what is pure;
even a very small gift of purity given by me results in infinity.
Whether a pure act is performed here even as a mere play for my sake alone,
or whether it is performed by the senses and so forth, that pure merit is attained in the Abode.
My task is merit, which is pure; for one who possesses that, no evil arises.
There is no suffering, nor indeed illusion, nor birth—how then could there be death? (32)
Therefore, those who have taken refuge in me should always remain in a state of fullness of eternal bliss.
Those who do not take refuge in me are carried away here by the bondage of karma.
Indeed, they repeatedly take up the burden born of latent impressions (vāsanā);
for just as a monkey goes from tree to tree, so does he. ||34||
The individual soul is led by its karma through the various wombs in the forest of saṃsāra, just as a ball is thrown for the sake of play by children on a playground. (35)
Likewise, by means of karmas, this [being] is cast into a field within the illusory realm;
bound like a horse, it possesses no independence to move about or even to go. (36)
Bound by karma, one is not independent among gods, sages, ancestors, or humans;
though humans on earth are superior, they are nonetheless devoid of wings. (37)
Even birds that travel through the sky are devoid of the means of hands;
and the gods, possessing divine forms, are devoid of the grossness of the earth and other such qualities. ||38||
Women, though rich in beauty and virtue, were made subject; likewise, the elderly were ordained as venerable, yet they were deprived of authority. (39)
The youths possess authority yet lack long-standing experience;
indeed, the elephant stands strong, but he is devoid of means.
The lion is indeed a powerful king, while the buffalo is the lowest among the tamasic; the deer is pure, yet it is made a wild beast. (41)
Even Brahmins who are treasuries of knowledge are tormented by the anger of poverty;
while crows are clever at interpreting omens, they are nonetheless born from a foul womb.
Jewels and pearls are excellent, yet they have become difficult to obtain;
indeed, while bitter weeds are abundant, sweet things are truly hard to find. 43.
O beloved, base men are indeed easy to find, while the virtuous are rare;
truthful women are difficult to find, whereas courtesans are easily obtained. (44)
Leaves are indeed many, but fruits are truly difficult to find;
those who indulge in pleasures are easy to find, but those who are dispassionate are rare. (45)
"Insects exist everywhere, O beloved, but those who possess hoods are rare. Death is easy to attain, O Lakṣmī, but nectar is very difficult to obtain. (46)
O Lakṣmī, quarrel is easily found, but union is very difficult to attain;
self-interest is everywhere easy to find, but the interest of others is always difficult to find. (47)
O Lakṣmī, enjoyment is easily obtained, but liberation is always difficult to attain;
O Lakṣmī, men are easily found, but the supreme man is difficult to find. (48)
An ordinary man is easily found, but the Supreme Man is difficult to find; women are obtained everywhere, but a woman who is Nārāyaṇī is rare. 49.
Exertion is attainable in every way, but service is difficult to obtain, O beloved;
the body may be acquired in many ways, but the Self, indeed, is difficult to find, O beloved.
A house is easily obtained and accessible, but the imperishable abode is difficult to attain;
O Lakṣmī, birth in a womb is easy, but indeed, being the Golden Embryo (Hiraṇyagarbha) is difficult to achieve.
O Lakṣmī, caves are easily found, but the peak of Brahmā is indeed difficult to attain;
O Lakṣmī, latent desires are easily found, but Vāsudeva is indeed difficult to attain. (52)
O Lakṣmī, husbands are easy to find, but an eternal husband is difficult to find;
masters are easy to find in this world, for a supreme master is indeed difficult to find. (13)
O Lakṣmī, everything indeed is easily obtained; I, Kṛṣṇa, am always difficult to attain.
Illusion (Māyā) is indeed easy to obtain in the world, but I, the Lord of Māyā, am difficult to attain.
O Lakṣmī, the womb of karma is cast aside by a capable Lord;
I am Kṛṣṇa, and I truly deliver the entire world bound by karma.
Water is easily found everywhere, but it is difficult to find at the gateway of Viṣṇu;
indeed, among all things that are difficult to attain, the gateway of Viṣṇu is the most difficult to reach.
I shall make that which is difficult to attain easily accessible for those possessed of devotion in every way;
by acting thus, all the actions of my worshippers shall indeed grant liberation. 57.
Speak, Lakṣmī! Let there be compassion here; let there be a reward for this. Having obtained that, one shall attain the state of supreme merit and my own abode of bliss. (58)
Renunciation toward me is indeed difficult to attain, whereas that which is other than this is easy;
entrustment toward me is indeed difficult to attain, whereas that which is other than this is always easy. (59)
Offering to another is easy, but offering to me is indeed difficult; effort for another's sake is easy, but effort for my sake is difficult. (3.67.60)
For being for the sake of another is easy to find, but being for my sake is difficult to find;
the state of being a woman to another is easy to find, but the state of being my wife is difficult to find. (61)
O beloved, everything illusory is easily obtained, whereas that which belongs to Me is difficult to attain;
for one who has taken refuge in the performed [rites] knows this, but one free from exertion does not perceive it.
Śrī Nārāyaṇī knows with how much effort I am to be obtained;
Satī Haimī knows how Śaṅkara is indeed to be obtained.
How indeed can Māṇikyāśvī understand how dharma is attained?
Rādhā, Kṛṣṇā, and Kamalā alone know the true effort involved. ||64||
Gāyatrī does not know it at all, nor does the daughter of the ocean (Lakṣmī) know it;
Padmāvatī alone knows how the Supreme Lord is to be attained.
A woman who has obtained a portion of His grace does not experience the toil of penance.
Yogis who are disciplined know it; virtuous women know its hardship.
The yoginīs and the female ascetics who wither their bodies understand this;
but what do you know, Lakṣmī, regarding the penance on Hanumat Mountain? (67)
Having attained me, the Supreme Person, through your exertion, you have succeeded;
for I am to be obtained only in exchange for death, O beloved, and not otherwise.
He whose entire external and internal life is for my sake,
and who renounces everything for my sake— he indeed attains me through his exertion.
She whose entire being is for my sake, whose actions are directed toward me,
and whose renunciations are for my sake— she indeed attains me through her exertion.
With her body having reached a pure abode, the Yoginī, the daughter of the Yogins,
who has surrendered all her possessions for my sake, seems as if she has attained me, like the daughter of Bhṛgu.
In yoga, she knows me as the yogi; she also remembers me in meditation.
Having surrendered her entire being for my sake, she indeed attains me, like a lotus flower.
Though her efforts were slight, that auspicious Mādhavī, distressed by separation from me for my sake, has indeed attained me, who am composed of consciousness and bliss. 73.
All sacrifices performed with every desire are indeed bestowers of all happiness upon me;
those women who are devoted to me abide in me and obtain eternal bliss. (74)
O beautiful woman, my devotee attains sovereignty over all syllables and words, the bliss residing in the Lord of All, and the joy arising from all incarnations. (75)

She whose mind is not divided by desires for anyone other than me and the like, having made me—who is otherwise difficult to attain—her beloved, she indeed comes to me as one who is easily attained. 76.
Both Kāla and Yama abandon a woman who is devoted to the service of Kṛṣṇa;
even if she has committed a thousand offenses, I render her free from fault.
I am the protector dwelling within the heart, yet I quickly stand outside;
though difficult to attain, I become easily accessible, like [the cowherds] at the cowherd’s dwelling.
Though difficult to attain, I indeed become easy to reach, just like Vāmana;
though very far away, I indeed become close at hand, like the elephant's water-trunk.
Though invisible, I appear as if visible, reaching the pinnacle of delight; though inaccessible, I become accessible like a lord who is his own master.
O Lakṣmī, through the offering of my affection, I give and bestow everything;
I make all things, even those difficult to obtain, easy to attain for the sake of my servant.
Everything is done for your sake, and likewise everything is done for the sake of the devotees;
indeed, everything is performed with devotion and under your influence for the sake of that which is dear to Brahmā.
Only by knowing me in this way does she who brings an end to rebirth become endowed with divine splendor and is born as my own in the imperishable realm.
Deluded by the pleasure of the body, they sleep in the slumber of ignorance;
yet, if awakened by my instruction, they shall indeed attain wakefulness. (84)
Then, men and women who attain me as their beloved husband—the supreme among persons—become eternally liberated, possessing divine bodies. (85)
Constantly filled with divine bliss, no lesser happiness exists there; in that world, every happiness is found to be perfectly complete. (86)
As if manifest within my very form, the treasure-trove of bliss resides in me alone;
indeed, streams of bliss flow forth from my form. (87)
Having gladdened my devotees, they enter into me;
for from my very form, those who possess an ocean of supreme bliss emerge.
Having remained for a long time among my devotees, they indeed return to me;
all these great joys never undergo any diminution.
They do not become diminished, nor indeed do they ever come to an end;
for the currents of these streams arise solely from one's own will.
Inexhaustible and ever-increasing, my forms born of excellent yoga abide as that very bliss of Brahman for the liberated ones in my abode.
O Lotus-born One, enjoy that supreme bliss together with all of them;
these companions of yours, who have come into your hands, are known as your sisters. (92)
The co-wives, numbering in the hundreds of millions, tens of millions, millions, and billions, are all forms composed of me;
for they are non-different from you, and they are likewise non-different from me.
Then indeed, my own forms—consisting of the qualities and consisting of my own power—were divided; and all those powers of mine, commanded by me, became women. (94)
Having attained me, they have been made one with my own essential nature;
indeed, I myself have traveled throughout the entire earth to seek them out.
Having sought out my own beloved, my powers have been restored;
honoring the duties of a wife, may they enjoy me who am truly delighted. (96)
May they enjoy me, the Supreme Lord—the imperishable, the undecaying, the immutable, the eternal, the supreme, and the treasury of all bliss. 97.
Whosoever, placing me before her and holding me entirely within her heart, hears this "Song of the Bride" spoken by me concerning the eternal Beloved; 98.
Those who shall desire their own bliss in the form of Śrīpati, Puruṣottama—to them I shall become attained, and I shall take their hand. 99.
"I shall lead her to the supreme abode; indeed, I shall make her my mistress.
I shall make Muktānikā the beloved of Brahmā and the beloved of Hari."

Thus ends the sixty-seventh chapter, titled "The Description of the Fruit that is the Entirety of Hari’s Grace," within the *Vadhūgītā* of the third section, the *Dvāpara-santāna*, in the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇī Śrī said:
O Blessed One, this Vadhūgītā has indeed been proclaimed by you as the bestower of liberation, entirely granting the attainment of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. (1)
I am eager to hear the mantra of you, the most excellent of beloveds; for this supreme mantra is the medicine for the diseases of worldly existence. (2)
O ocean of mercy, tell me by which mantra one reaches the supreme state of Śrī Hari; [tell this] for the sake of the liberation of all.
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
Listen, O Śivarājñīśrī, to this auspicious and most excellent mantra;
by good fortune, I shall here reveal to you my supreme secret.
Neither all the gods, nor the sages, nor even the lords know [this];
and at the beginning of creation, I spoke it to Brahmā, the supreme lord.
He likewise spoke [the names] for Vairāja, Mahāviṣṇu, and Bhūman;
and he spoke them for Vāsudeva, Kṛṣṇa, and Nārāyaṇa.
They do not reach the further shore of me, the Supreme Self, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, together with my sovereign goddesses.
To them he gave the mantras sought after,
which are intent upon the upliftment of devotees and are endowed with my form, essential nature, self, power, and sovereignty.
I am the mantra, I am the form of the mantra, the Ancient Supreme Person;
by their uttering me even once, the supreme state is surely attained.
O Lakṣmī, these most excellent mantras, which are my own deities and my very incarnations, bestow both worldly enjoyment and liberation even without the preliminary rite of *puraścaraṇa*. 3.68.10.
Listen, O Lakṣmī, to the jewel among mantras, which brings auspiciousness;
by the mere recollection of it, it bestows the imperishable abode. 1.1.111.
The supreme Manu, the bestower of dharma, desire, wealth, and liberation, protects the one who has come for refuge, saying, "O Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa! (12).
This great mantra of ten syllables is joined with the ten incarnations:
the syllable *a* is the form of the Fish, and the syllable *na* is Narasiṃha.
Here, the letter *da* is Varāha, the letter *śa* is Hayagrīva, the letter *ka* is Kṛṣṇa, and the letter *ṇa* is the Lord Vāmana. (14)
The letter *na* is the axe-bearing Śiva; the letter *ra* is King Rāma;
the letter *ya* is Viṣṇu, the awakener; and the letter *ṇa* is the destroyer of impurity. || 15 ||
Thus, this mantra, whose essence is the ten incarnations, grants all desires to me;
by its mere recitation, I am forever completely satisfied.
Listen, Lakṣmī; likewise, you, the beginningless Śrī, shine forth within the mantra.
And I, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, shine forth as Puruṣottama. (17)
This mantra, which conveys the meaning of a couple, bestows happiness upon couples; it grants the prosperity, good fortune, abundance, and joy of marital bliss.
When recited, this mantra increases one's lineage, augments wealth, grain, and other assets, and bestows the great bliss of the world of Brahmā and other realms free from obstacles. (19)
The great mantra, whose essence is the couple, bestows health, fame, existence, glory, sovereignty, heaven, and so forth; it fulfills all desires and bestows bliss. (3.68.20)
Listen, Lakṣmī, within that mantra there shines a quartet:
Anādiśrī herself, Rādhā, Kṛṣṇa, and the Sun of Goloka. (21)
Anādiśrī and Lakṣmī, and Nārāyaṇa who dwells in Vaikuṇṭha—Manu was accompanied by these two pairs. (22)
This mantra bestows the attainment of all desired fruits, grants the supreme abode, confers all good fortune, and accomplishes every purpose. (23)
Listen, Lakṣmī, likewise regarding that mantra, there is a supreme quartet:
those who are liberated from beginningless time, and the hosts of Śrī’s liberated female attendants.
The cowherd boys and the cowherd girls, with Kṛṣṇa himself—the Lord—as their companion, and likewise Nārāyaṇa and I; indeed, these four constitute that [group]. (25)
I am indeed Nārāyaṇa joined with the hosts of liberated souls,
as well as Kṛṣṇa accompanied by the cowherds and cowherdesses, the dweller in Goloka.
Listen, Lakṣmī, for likewise there exists a supreme group of six mantras:
the soundless, the one denoted by Oṃ, the resonance (nāda), and that which is beyond Brahman. ||27||
Because it possesses sound (*nāda*), it is indeed called *nādī*; likewise, the Veda itself is so regarded.
All the Vedas belong to that which possesses sound (*nādī*), being always auspicious and distinguished by the syllable *oṃ*.
All forms of prosperity, powers, and women are established as the intellect of Brahman;
indeed, they should be understood as being of the nature of knowledge, for they are of the nature of the knowledge of Brahman. (29)
And Kṛṣṇa is the giver of liberation; all the incarnations are celebrated here.
Furthermore, all men, virtuous beings, and saintly women are givers of liberation. (3.68.30)
In all those instances— whether in the syllable Om, in the Vedas, in the sciences, or in the incarnations— it is indeed the refuge of that glorious Supreme Self.
I, who reside among the virtuous men and women, have been described in this mantra;
listen, O Lakṣmī, for I shall tell you of the triad situated therein within that mantra. 32.
The beginningless and imperishable abode, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, and the lords of the dwellings—the multitudes of Nārā and Brahmāṇḍas—therein I make my path. (33)
Thus, I am Śrī Puruṣottama, abiding within the threefold creation;
I am the bestower of all desires. Understand this meaning which is for the sake of the supreme goal.
Listen, Lakṣmī, to this twofold meaning here, designated as the insentient and the sentient:
Anādiśrī is Mahāmāyā, Prakṛti, and the Śakti of Acyuta. (35)
"I am Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama) residing therein"—
thus, in that context, he should also awaken [the disciple] to the meaning of the mantra which bestows knowledge.
Listen, Lakṣmī, and likewise there is the independent meaning as well:
the letter *a* is Vāsudeva, and the letter *na* is Nārāyaṇa. (37)
The letter *da* represents all the gods collectively and Śrī; all powers (*śakti*) are indeed contained therein.
The letter *kṛ* represents the incarnations beginning with Kṛṣṇa; *ṣṇa* is the vein, the stalk-born, and the unborn. (38)
Nor are Niyāmī, Muktā, and the others, nor the hosts of sages (Ṛ), nor Śambhu, the Lord of Yogins (Ya), nor even I, the Controller (Ṇa). ||39||
All of this is indeed distinguished and established within the meaning of the mantra, O beloved;
listen, Lakṣmī, likewise to another auspicious and beautiful meaning of the mantra.
Those for whom there is no beginning—that is, birth—are considered eternal.
You are the eternal Śrī, Lakṣmī; likewise, I am the eternal Kṛṣṇa. (41)
I am Śrī Kṛṣṇa, dwelling within the selves of men, established in the mind; I am the eternal inner controller, the auspicious and beautiful meaning of the mantra. 42.
This supreme mantra, the crest-jewel of all mantras, has been told to you by me;
there can be no mantra superior to this, for it is the most excellent among all mantras. (43)
Furthermore, another Manu, Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, is also my opinion:
you are Lakṣmī, Śrī; and I am Hari, the supreme Lord Nārāyaṇa. (44)
Those women who possess the mark of devotion to me as their husband are all Lakṣmīs, beloveds of Brahmā; may they be my wives by the millions.
All my men and women are liberated souls, dear to Hari;
for me, my abode is always in Lakṣmīs and in Nārās. ||46||
I am that very Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa; thus the meaning of the mantra has been declared to you.
"Lakṣman" refers to my tilaka, my mark, and such signs as the branding of the conch and the discus. ||47||
All those who possess that [devotion], whether women or men, are my devotees; indeed, all such sentient beings are truly dependent upon me. ||48||
Among them, the path has been attained by me; therefore, I am situated within the heart of the mantra.
Since the fruit of the action belongs to the *lā* vowels, and the *lā*s are the inhabitants of the Brahmāṇḍa. (49)
Those who possess the quality of forbearance (kṣa) endure and flourish; those who possess the quality of sovereignty (kṣā) are supreme lords of power.
Those who possess the quality of measurement (mā) are measured in the world of Brahmā, as are those who possess liberation (mukta) and the like.
Nara, Māyā, and the principles (tattvas)—I am he who has attained their ultimate resort; O Lakṣmī, I am the Supreme Lord, distinguished and residing within the heart of the mantra. (51)
Furthermore, it is my conviction that another mantra is "Śrīman Nārāyaṇa";
both sentient and insentient beings, having come for refuge, take shelter in me. (52)
I am the glorious Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Person endowed with Śrī;
you are Śrī, and I am he who possesses her, for my women here are indeed by the millions. (53)
Established together with you, I am always the Lord among them;
I am the glorious one in the water, in the Ocean of Milk, and likewise elsewhere.
The glorious Nāra is my imperishable abode; my station is therein.
By means of that [Nāra] and by means of her [the Śrī], I indeed become the Lord Śrīmannārāyaṇa. (55)
"Śrīkṛṣṇa-vallabha"—this mantra indicates attainment;
it signifies that the Lord of Śrī, Puruṣottama, is obtained as one who is like Śrīkṛṣṇa himself. (56)
Out of compassion, I am indeed easily accessible to both men and women;
and even during the month of Puruṣottama, I am easily accessible through my grace.
In every creation and in every aeon, I become Kṛṣṇa;
I am easily accessible to the gopīs, to the cowherds, and to other embodied beings.
Just as Kṛṣṇa himself, residing in Goloka, is easily attainable on earth, so too am I, the Supreme Lord, easily attainable while residing in the imperishable abode (Akṣaradhāma). ||59||
In age after age, I myself appear here on this earth as the compassionate one—Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama. (3.68.60)
Thus indeed, O Lakṣmī, this mantra beloved of Śrī Kṛṣṇa is easily obtained;
for Śrī Kṛṣṇa is my beloved, and it is for that reason that I have assumed this form.
I am Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the beloved of all, who assumes a form easily accessible to everyone, bringing joy to the gopīs for the sake of pleasing Rādhā. 62.
The Lord is indeed the beloved, the charming one, the husband, the Supreme Person;
as such, I draw my devotees toward Me and lead them to My supreme abode.
Thus, I am the master, the lord, the glorious Kṛṣṇa, the sovereign devoted to Brahman;
I am Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the beloved, and in the sense of the mantra, I am Hari himself.
The beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama, am forever satisfied by the mere utterance of my mantra. 65.

All castes and stages of life—men, women, and eunuchs; all those entitled to the use of mantras, as well as those of mixed birth and those who have not undergone the purificatory rites—are [eligible]. (66)
Nāgas, sarpas, dānavas, daityas, and even rākṣasas—all these are subject to mantras; how much more so, then, are humans on earth? (67)
Beasts, birds, living creatures, and even trees—all these embodied beings possess the qualification for the practice of mantra. (68)
Indeed, this mantra of mine, which bestows liberation, has been heard by animals, as well as by yakṣas, gandharvas, sūtas, piśācas, kinnaras, and birds. (69)
The Kimpuruṣas, Puṇyajanas, Bhūtas, Pretas, and deities;
the Vināyakas, Vetālas, Gaṇas, and likewise the Gaṇikās.
Yoginīs and ascetics, virtuous women and devoted wives, daughters-in-law, the elderly, children, and even infants at the breast—[all were present]. (7.1)
The Vasus, the Ṛṣis, the Rudras, the Suns, and the Moon;
Kāma, the Manus, and even the gods headed by Mahendra. ||72||
The world-protectors and the guardians of the quarters, as well as the lunar mansions and the planets, the stars and human beings, and likewise the Siddhas and Cāraṇas. ||73||
Kings, subjects, Yama, the messengers of Yama, as well as the lords (īśvara),
the female lords (īśvarāṇī), those of the nature of Brahman, and those characterized by tamas and rajas.
Those who possess fortitude, who dwell in the sacred abodes, and are all authorized for the mantras—
having received the supreme mantra from the guru, they shall liberate themselves from worldly existence.
All those who are entitled to the mantras are my devotees and have taken refuge in me;
likewise, I am the refuge for those who seek shelter and for those who serve no other.
And for those who have no other means of accomplishment, the mantra is the supreme means;
when recited even once or repeatedly, it yields fruit swiftly for those in distress. (77)
My fourfold mantra is the preventer of rebirth for even radiant embodied beings, and it is the bestower of liberation upon all. (78)
One who is suffering, one who seeks their own welfare, or one who possesses discernment—and who desires that [liberation]—is qualified;
having taken refuge and received the mantra, such a person shall attain the fruit of liberation. ||79||
He is initiated, devoted, free from pride, a believer, and skillful; he is grateful, endowed with faith, desirous of learning, and devoid of faults. ||3.68.80||
One who is fit for the practice of identifying with the intoxicated [state] should take up this supreme mantra;
it must be spoken even to sinners, as it is a purifier that destroys worldly existence. 81.
Even one who eats meat might attain purity, how much more so one who has entered the path of Dharma?
Even one who commits sexual misconduct might attain purity, how much more so one who has entered the path of ethical conduct? ||82||
Moreover, even one devoted to theft would be purified, how much more so one who follows the path of justice?
Even a drinker of liquor would indeed be purified, how much more so one who observes the dharma of a Brahmin? 83.
There is no restriction regarding place, time, and so forth for its reception;
there is no restriction regarding ritual bathing, giving, and so forth for its reception. ||84||
No restriction regarding vows, festivals, and the like exists during its eclipse.
There is no restriction regarding women, men, and so forth, in the undertaking of this. ||85||
This rule must indeed be received from a Vaiṣṇava guru and from the female guru (gurvi).
When there is grasping, one must always possess devotion toward me with devotion.
By my body being marked with my signs, by my worship of me, by the offering of your actions to me, and by having come for refuge to me; ||87||
By the offering of the fruits [of action] unto me, by abiding in trust toward me, and indeed by the offering of everything unto me as my sole means; ||88||
A devotee of the Lord must indeed have no other deity;
thus are the rules to be observed by a devotee who has received the mantra. (89)
For that [mantra], I, the Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, am the Ṛṣi;
and the deities, endowed with Śrī and born from my own portions, are the beloveds of Brahmā.
Accompanied by Brahmapriyā and Śrī, I am indeed the Supreme Lord in the Manu-mantra; it should be understood that Gāyatrī is the meter and my mantra consists of ten syllables. (91)
Likewise the six-syllable [mantra], the six-syllable, and the six-syllable; these three other mantras of mine one should apply to the limbs. (92)
The ten-syllable mantra is to be placed upon the ten limbs: on the head, eyes, and face;
and on the neck, arms, heart, abdomen, waist, thighs, and feet.
One should indeed place the six syllables on the head, the neck, the two arms, the heart, the abdomen, the two thighs, and the two feet. (94)
Meditation upon Nārāyaṇa accompanied by Lakṣmī is my opinion; likewise, meditation upon the true deities accompanied by me is my opinion. (95)
Then one should worship me, the son of the glorious Gopāla-Kṛṣṇa, the child of Kambharā, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa. (96)
[He saw] Hari, the Lord of Kamalā, holding in his hands the conch, discus, mace, and lotus, and marked with the trident, fish, banner, bow, wheel, and svastika. 97.

One should worship the Supreme Lord, the Master of Lakṣmī, who is joined by Śrī seated upon his left lap, with perfumes, flowers, and other offerings, as well as food offerings, garments, and so forth. 98.
With ornaments and decorations, with lustration rites, hymns of praise and the like, with circumambulations and sacrificial fees, and with dancing, chanting, and singing; ||99||
O beloved, one should perform my worship in this manner with the rites of dismissal (*visarjana*) and so forth;
and one should give excellent gifts according to one's ability to virtuous men and women.
One should feed him, delight him, gladden him, and likewise serve him;
one should abide in the state of being a Vaiṣṇava and conduct oneself with the disposition of a servant. || 101 ||
One should indeed perform worship daily with one's chosen mantras a thousand times,
or recite them a hundred times, or even recite them from a single rosary.
If one recites it ten times daily at dawn, at nightfall,
or even at midday, I shall indeed become the bestower of liberation.
I am indeed the bestower of prosperity upon those who possess desires,
and I am also the bestower of the highest good upon those who are free from desire.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, this secret of my mind has been told to you;
whether a woman or a man, one should recite it and give it to a living being who asks for it.

Thus ends the sixty-eighth chapter, titled "The Description of the Mantras, Their Meanings, Nyāsa, and Other Rituals," within the section on the Secrets of Great Mantras in the Third Age (Dvāpara) of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmīnārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
The illustrious Śrī Nārāyaṇī said: "O beloved, you have spoken the most excellent secret gathered from Manu;
the power of this great mantra is vast and fulfills all desires. (1)
You are the lord, you are the master, and you alone are the preceptor of the worlds;
you are the sovereign, you are the friend, you are the protector, you are the refuge, and you are the helper.
You are the enjoyer, you are the deliverer, the protector, the nourisher, and the eternal friend;
you are the progenitor of the worlds, for you are indeed the bearer of the embryo within embodied beings.
I am your disciple, your daughter-in-law, your wife, your beloved, and your friend; I am your servant, your handmaid, your maidservant, your consort, your woman, and your wife. (4)
All these beloved of Brahmā are the powers (śaktis) of your half-body;
likewise, there are your supreme powers who are beloved of Hari.
You are the source of compassion for all of us, the eternal sovereign;
you alone are the giver of the mantra, and you also are the giver of initiation.
Out of a desire for the welfare of the world, please tell me the ritual procedure for initiation into the mantra;
show me your compassion so that, having received initiation, they may attain great liberation.
Śrī Puruṣottama said: Listen, O beloved, for I shall explain to you the procedure for initiation into the mantra,
which indeed occurs when the resolve arises through the power of the company of the virtuous.
Whether by the power of past merit or prompted by another,
having then bathed and remembered Hari, one should quickly go toward the Guru.
The true guru is one who is perfected in dharma, possessed of renunciation, with senses restrained, a great devotee of the Lord, devoted, learned, and solely intent upon devotion. || 3.69.10 ||

The preceptor should be a knower of the Vedas, one who understands the true meaning of the mantras, a knower of the secrets, devoted to the recitation of mantras, and endowed with my own tradition. || 11 ||

One who has received initiation into the tradition of the Supreme Brahman, who has taken refuge at my feet, who is proficient in the sciences of Brahman-knowledge, who has no other deity, and who is pure; || 12 ||
The virtuous man, the virtuous woman, the chaste wife, the Brahmin, and even he who has taken refuge at the feet of the Guru—
having surrendered all his possessions for the sake of the Guru, such a Guru is a teacher who bestows liberation.
One should approach such a preeminent guru, or a guru who is a knower of mantras—one who bestows knowledge and possesses a divine form—with offerings held in one's hands. (14)
One should approach and likewise bow down to the supreme, divine teacher and guru, who teaches right conduct, teaches devotion, and bestows the Brahman.
On the day of my birth, the eighth lunar day, one should inform the preceptor, who is the very essence of the mantra, of one's own resolve, keeping in mind the words as they have been spoken.
Either on the twelfth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Kārttika, or on the twelfth day of the bright fortnight of Kārttika,
or on any auspicious day, or at whatever time one so desires.
Holding water from a sacred ford (tīrtha) in his hand— the water which is the nectar of Hari’s feet—
and having performed the ritual sipping of water (ācamana), he should indeed sit before the Guru.
The preceptor, having caused him to hear the name of Hari again and again,
should cause the marks of the conch, discus, mace, and lotus to be impressed upon him with water.
Alternatively, one should establish the fire according to the ritual procedure for the fire-mantra,
and offer cow-ghee mixed with the mantra upon the sacrificial mound (sthaṇḍila) or other such site.
One should indeed perform one thousand and eight, or one hundred and eight,
oblations with fruits and other offerings, conjoined with the great mantra.
One should offer milk-rice (pāyasa) and clarified butter (ghṛta) and other substances with the mantras beginning with the Puruṣasūkta and the Lakṣmīsūkta, as well as with the names of Me.
Then, one should consecrate with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta) a conch, a discus, a mace, and a lotus, made either of silver, gold, or even copper. ||23||
Then one should worship [the deity] in the fire and heat the object suitable for sealing;
thereafter, one should perform ten *homa* offerings or six *homa* offerings.
Having raised the discus, the preceptor should indeed mark the disciple who has taken refuge with it on both arms;
specifically, the discus alone on the upper right arm, and the conch quickly on the left.
Having thus marked the two arms— with a mace on the lower right side and a lotus on the lower left— he [should bathe them] with water from the sacred pitcher.
Having consecrated [the water] with the mantra itself, one should perform the consecration upon the head of the disciple;
one should then provide the ritual sipping of water (ācamana) and cause the vertical mark (ūrdhvapuṇḍra) to be applied.

Then, the Guru should teach the mantra together with the *candraka* and the *kauṃkuma*; he should indeed recite it three times into the right ear of the male disciple, or into the left ear of the female.
One should explain all the meanings of the mantras and then grant fearlessness;
one should prescribe the rules for recitation and give a garland made of *tulasī*.
He should hand over the rosary and conclude the ritual exemption;
thereafter, the disciple should worship the guru with devotion using ornaments, garments, and other offerings.
Thus, endowed with the mantra, the disciple should bow and go to his own home.
O Lakṣmī, this supreme secret has been declared to you. 31.
This supreme quartet of mantras bestows liberation and grants divine status; indeed, through their recitation, there shall be liberation that cuts through all that is to be done. (32)
The previously mentioned group of ten mantras, as well as this group of four,
bestow upon me the state of identity with all enjoyments, all liberations, and so forth.
Likewise, thirteen other mantras have been previously shown;
O Lakṣmī, they are auspicious, bestowing both worldly enjoyment and liberation, and they bring about emancipation. (34)
Likewise, thirty-three mantras ending with the Gāyatrī have been proclaimed;
O Lakṣmī, they all bestow success and grant the auspicious goals of human endeavor.
O Lakṣmī, those other thirty-three mantras proclaimed by you are auspicious, bestowing the goals of human life, and are beloved by the Gāyatrī. (36)
Then [he taught] the two excellent Gāyatrīs of Ramā and Pārvatī;
thereafter, the Lord Kṛṣṇa [taught] the triad of mantras, his own beloved deity.
O Lakṣmī, [this] accomplishes all aims and is the most excellent among all mantras. Now listen also to the auspicious Gāyatrīs that bestow liberation. (38)
We know the Supreme Lord; we meditate upon the Best of Men;
may He, the Incarnate One, inspire us. ||39||
We know Gopīśvara; we meditate upon Śrī Rādheśī;
may that Kṛṣṇa inspire us. 3.69.40.
We know Nārāyaṇa; we meditate upon Vāsudeva.
May that Viṣṇu inspire us. ||41||
We meditate upon that excellent splendor of the divine Savitṛ;
may he inspire our thoughts. ||42||
We know that Tatpuruṣa; we meditate upon Mahādeva.
May that Rudra inspire us. 43.
We know him who is born from the lotus; we meditate upon him whose mouth is the Veda;
may that Creator inspire us. 44.
Let us know Mahāviṣṇu; let us meditate upon Hiraṇyagarbha; may that Infinite Being inspire us. ||45||
Listen, O Rame, to these seven Gāyatrīs which are of my own nature; they abide within your form as well, bestowing auspiciousness and granting all human goals. 46.
We know her who is dear to Brahmā; we meditate upon her who is dear to Hari;
may that Brāhmī inspire us. 47.
We know Nārāyaṇī; we meditate upon Vāsudevī;
may Vaiṣṇavī inspire us. ||48||
We know Mahālakṣmī; we meditate upon the Consort of Viṣṇu;
may that Lakṣmī inspire us. ||49||
We know her who is golden-hued; we meditate upon Śrī, the yellow-hued one.
May that Lakṣmī inspire us. 3.69.50.
May we know Mahāmbikā; may we meditate upon Pārvatī, the Truth;
may Gaurī inspire us. ||51||
We know the Great Sāvitrī; we meditate upon the Vedic Gāyatrī.
May that Speech inspire us. 52.
May we know the Goddess Lakṣmī who bestows happiness; may we meditate upon the glory of the Queen of Śiva;
may that Kārṣṇī inspire us. ||53||
We know Nārāyaṇī; we meditate upon Māṇikī;
may that Rādhā inspire us. ||54||
We know Nārāyaṇī; we meditate upon the goddess Ramā;
may that Lakṣmī inspire us. ||55||
We know Nārāyaṇī; we meditate upon Padmāvatī;
may she, the all-pervading one, inspire us. 96.
We know Nārāyaṇī; we meditate upon the goddess Ramā;
may that Sovereign inspire us. 97.
We know the Goddess of Dharma; we meditate upon the Goddess of Devotion;
may Hari inspire us. ||58||
Thus, O Lakṣmī, these twelve Gāyatrīs are your names;
they are auspicious and bestow the four aims of human life known as dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa. (59)
Thus, all these one hundred and fifteen mantras are the deities of the one hundred and fifteen powers (śaktis) above, whose essence is myself.
The secret, devoted to the Supreme Lord, has been told to you here;
by reciting even a single mantra from among them, whether a man or a woman, [one attains the goal]. //61//
He would go from heaven to a higher heaven, from realm to a higher realm,
from festival to a more abundant festival, and from bliss to a bliss filled with even greater joy.
There is no god higher than Puruṣottama who bestows liberation;
therefore, service should be rendered by me to the one known as Puruṣottama. (63)
My mantras should always be recited day and night according to one's capacity;
my initiation should be received, and my symbols should always be worn.
I am the Reality, Nārāyaṇa, and likewise Vāsudeva;
I am the Supreme Self, the Supreme Brahman, the Supreme Light, and the Supreme Lord. ||65||
I am Viṣṇu, higher than the highest, and indeed Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Person;
I am Janārdana, the eternal self, the inner self, and the witness.
I am Hṛṣīkeśa, as well as the sacrifice; I am the Lord, the Master of Līlā.
I am the head of all, the eye of all, and the feet of all—the Blessed One.
I am the soul of the universe and the Lord of Śrī; I am Savitṛ and I am Ramaṇa;
I alone am the Lord of all, the omniscient one, and the Master of the world.
I abide within all branches of knowledge, and I am the wielder of all weapons;
I am the teacher of all and the object of all perception—I am the illustrious Puruṣottama.
My well-known mark is indeed the auspicious Sudarśana discus, as well as the vertical Puṇḍra, the Tilaka, and likewise the conch and other symbols. (3.69.70)
O beloved, I, the Supreme Person, am to be honored with food and with items to be worn; one should perform my worship adorned with the marks of the conch, the discus, and so forth.
Having indeed maintained the [prescribed] marks, one should perform the rites of Brahman.
The upholder and sustainer of the two arms goes to my supreme state. ||72||
Having marked [the disciple] and recited the mantra, he is liberated from the bonds of worldly existence.
A virtuous woman should feed a devotee who possesses the Sudarśana [mark] at the beginning of a śrāddha ceremony and other rites.
The ancestors indeed become eternally satisfied by eating the food of a Vaiṣṇava;
one should give cows, land, gold, and other gifts to one whose arms are marked with the discus.
Those whose bodies are marked with the discus and other signs, being purified and freed from sin, go to my supreme abode,
O beloved, when their bodies have been sanctified by the Vaiṣṇava marks.
All sacred fords and sacrifices, along with millions of liberated souls, reside [therein];
therefore, for the sake of mantra-siddhi and for worship, the cakra should especially be worn.
For the sake of attaining the status of a Vaiṣṇava, especially for the attainment of knowledge,
and for the sake of attaining the state of being my servant, the discus must be worn with particular care.
One should always place the marks of the conch, discus, mace, and lotus upon the two arms;
as well as the fish, trident, banner, bow, arrow, svastika, and staff.
One should always perform the nyāsa with lines made of sandalwood paste or heated [metal];
enriched with the lines of the pavitra-cakra, these cross over the ocean of sins.
The foot of Hari is a sacred rim, his discus is the Sudarśana;
those whose bodies have been purified by it indeed go to my abode.
Purify us with that Brahman which is pure, heated by fire;
O Agni, purify us with that flame of yours which is purifying and radiant. 81.
By that purifier with which the gods always purify themselves, by that thousand-streamed one, may the Pāvamānī verses purify me. 82.
That purifier belonging to Prajāpati, which is bright and golden—by means of it, we who know Brahman purify the Brahman that has been purified. 83.
The wheel of the syllable *sa* (sanemi-cakra) belongs eternally to the Great-Souled One;
when that wheel was turned within his body, he attained the state of supreme exaltation.
Thus, my own words and even the Vedas declare:
"Those marks, such as the conch and the discus, should be worn according to the prescribed rule. (85)
And likewise, they are to be supported by wives, children, servants, and the like, as well as by domestic animals, trees, creepers, and so forth, and by houses, gardens, and the like. (86)
The weapons, such as the lines [of the body], are to be borne by means of vehicles, carriages, chests, and so forth;
likewise, my form is within, and my symbols are on the outside. (87)
The yoga of exclusive devotion, preceded by the offering of all things and so forth, must both be practiced and maintained; for my Vaiṣṇava devotees are indeed my servants. (88)
Likewise, one should apply the vertical mark (ūrdhvapuṇḍra) on the forehead, joined with the dot (bindu) of Lakṣmī;
for together with you, O Lakṣmī, I indeed dwell within that vertical mark.
A body marked with the vertical *ūrdhvapuṇḍra* is indeed my divine abode;
one who has bathed while marked with the *ūrdhvapuṇḍra* is considered to have bathed in all sacred fords (*tīrthas*). (3.69.90)
Initiated in all sacrifices and honored in all worlds, he ascends an excellent celestial chariot and goes to my supreme abode. ||9.1||
Upon seeing a devotee wearing the vertical mark (ūrdhvapuṇḍra), one is liberated from sins;
or by bowing with devotion, one obtains the fruit of all possible gifts. (92)
Indeed, by feeding him at a śrāddha ceremony, his ancestors attain satisfaction for ten million kalpas; they shall obtain the very fruit of one who performs a śrāddha at Gayā.
For the yogi who bears the vertical mark (ūrdhvapuṇḍra) upon his forehead, infinite merit arises from sacrifices, charity, the practice of austerity, recitation, burnt offerings, and so forth. 94.
The single-minded, highly fortunate, virtuous, and celibate practitioners should indeed fashion my mark (puṇḍra) in the shape of my foot, including the space between the toes. 95.
The mark on my foot is my temple, complete with the moon;
I abide in the center of the forehead, while Hari stands there with you and Śrī.
People should always apply the *puṇḍra* mark for the sake of attaining the same world as Kṛṣṇa, using either clay from a sacred ford (*tīrtha*), sandalwood paste, saffron, or liquid [fragrance]. 97.
Or they may indeed apply the vertical mark (ūrdhvapuṇḍra) along with the crescent moon using water and other substances;
by wearing these marks upon their limbs, they shall attain union with me. 98.
One should meditate on me, Hari, on the forehead; then on Nārāyaṇa in the belly;
one should meditate on Śrī on the chest, and on Śrī Puruṣottama on the throat. (99)
Likewise, one should meditate on Nara and Kṛṣṇa upon the two arms, the Lord of Māṇikī on the neck,
Śrībhūpati on the two sides, and me, Janārdana, upon the back.
And on the two hands, one should indeed remember me as the Lord of Ramā, Padmā, and Āvatī;
thus, my devotee should always wear twelve marks (puṇḍras).

A woman who is a great devotee of the Lord, or a man who is a great devotee of the Lord, adorned with the excellent upward-mark (ūrdhvapuṇḍra) and the beautiful moon [tilaka], is my very own form; of this there is no doubt.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, I have indeed explained to you the mantras along with the vertical marks (ūrdhvapuṇḍra),
as well as all those accompanied by the moon-marks (candraka) and joined with garlands of tulasī.
Empowered by the remembrance of me, men become givers of what is dear to me;
indeed, men become Nārāyaṇas and women become Nārāyaṇīs.
What more need be said? They indeed become dear to me;
by reciting or hearing this, the path to liberation becomes certain.

Thus ends the sixty-ninth chapter, titled "Description of the Greatness of the Great Mantras, the Gāyatrī and Others, the Moon-Adorned Urdhvapuṇḍra, and Other [Rituals]," in the Third Section on the Continuation of the Dvāpara Age of the Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā.
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
Listen, O Nārāyaṇī Śrī; you should cause the mantras of the true guru to be grasped.
One who has studied the thousand branches [of the Veda] and is initiated into all sacrifices [should do so]. (1)
Even an ascetic who is the best of brahmins would not be my guru if he were not a Vaiṣṇava; rather, one who is a great devotee of the Lord and intent on meditation upon me is my guru.
A wise Vaiṣṇava who is a proponent of the path of devotion shall be the guru;
he is the teacher, the true preceptor, the saintly one who tears asunder the bonds of worldly existence. (3)
Therefore, being pure, one should indeed receive the mantras accompanied by the syllable Oṃ;
at the beginning of all mantras, one should employ the Lord Praṇava.
I am the syllable Om, the Supreme Brahman, the Praṇava, the leader of mantras.
The single syllable "Om" is my primordial name, ending in the dative case.
Then, one should also complete the two-syllable name with "namaḥ";
the Guru should speak thus: "Oṃ śrīkṛṣṇanandajāya namaḥ."
The four mantras are excellent, and the ten mantras are supreme;
seven, twelve, and two are my most excellent Gāyatrīs.
Likewise, thirteen mantras are always my three most excellent ones;
similarly, thirty-three incarnation-mantras are my most excellent ones. (8)
The thirty-three mantras of Śrī are all considered by me to be supreme;
whether one, or all of them, or even many, they may be used according to one's desire.
Indeed, the mantras should be received by the disciple; the Guru, having examined him, should bestow them.
I am Hari himself, the deity of fifteen hundred and more mantras.
My thirty-three mantras and others that resemble my own form are indeed joined to me in every respect through the identity of form and the embodied.

Whatever devotee hears from the guru the mantra of that particular deity’s essential nature—he becomes a branch of the tree of the Supreme Brahman; indeed, there are one hundred and fifteen such branches.
Having worshipped those various forms with their respective mantras and having propitiated them as my own manifestations, they shall indeed come to me, Hari.
O Lotus-born One, all the traditions of the Supreme Brahman are my limbs;
all this has arisen from me and is not distinct from me.
The lords, as well as the incarnations and liberated souls, are strung upon me, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa; likewise, all living beings are strung upon Hari within me.
These powers, which indeed bring about descent, abide within me;
all of them, having the nature of mantra, are woven into me, the Lord Hari.
Having thus understood this, the learned man, having discerned them, should indeed bestow the one hundred and fifteen mantras upon a qualified scholar.
He shall indeed be an Ācāryasamrāṭ, a Guru who bestows all mantras;
he is declared to be an Ācāryasamrāṭ of the tradition of the Supreme Brahman (Parabrahma). || 18 ||
Those who bestow deficient mantras are indeed deficient preceptors;
I, however, establish as my Guru the Blessed One, who is self-luminous.
The imperial preceptor of the tradition of the Supreme Brahman, the bestower of the Manu-mantras, and the instructor of all Manus—he indeed becomes my very own form. (3.70.20)
And you, O beloved, shall likewise be established by me as the venerable Lakṣmī—
the sovereign queen of the lineage of the Supreme Brahman, and the bestower of mantras.
"You are the instructor of all mantras, for you are indeed identical with my own nature.
Furthermore, O Lakṣmī, listen to another thing: whatever name exists within the mantra," ||22||
That Tanmanas and likewise that Ācārya are always a portion of me;
and that Tanmanas and likewise that Ācāryāṇī are to be understood as such by my command. ||23||
In this manner, one should employ the mantras and receive them from the mouth of the guru;
thus the mantra becomes possessed of seed-syllables (sabīja), radiant with the splendor of the guru’s vital energy.
If the strength of destiny is greater than that of the preceptor, the mantra will grant liberation;
if the strength of the disciple is superior, the mantra will indeed bestow both worldly enjoyment and liberation. (25)
In all mantras, I alone am the seed-syllable, the beloved of Kṛṣṇa;
the eternal, inseparable Śakti, Śrī Lakṣmī, resides within the mantra. (26)
The syllable *oṃ* is my name; the letter *śrī* am I, the Supreme Lord;
the letter *u* is you yourself, Śrī; and the letter *m* is indeed my devotee. (27)
The letter *a* is I, the Supreme Self; the letter *u* is considered to be the Lord (*Īśvara*);
and the letter *m* is the multitude of individual souls (*jīva*). Therefore, that which consists of them is, in my view, *Oṃ*. (28)
The letter *a* is Aniruddha, the letter *u* is Pradyumna, and the letter *m* is Saṃkarṣaṇa; thus, the threefold *oṃ* am I, Śrī Hari. (29)
The syllable *A* is Viṣṇu himself, the syllable *U* is Śaṅkara, and the syllable *M* is the creator of the universe; indeed, as the threefold Supreme Lord, I am these.

The syllable *a* is Brahman, the Imperishable; the syllable *u* is the infinite millions of liberated ones; and the syllable *m* is my incarnations. Thus, I am the Supreme Person (*Puruṣottama*) in three forms.

The letter *a* is my creation as Brahmā, the letter *u* is the creation as Īśvara, and the letter *m* is the creation as the individual soul (*jīva*); thus, I am the Supreme Lord in a threefold manner.
The letter ‘A’ am I, the Supreme Brahman; ‘U’ is my beloved Brahmanī; and ‘Ma’ is all the beloveds of Hari. Thus, in three ways, I am the Supreme Lord. (33)
"I am the master and you are the mistress; all others are likewise servants.
Such is my heart's conviction, for within the meaning of the Praṇava lies this state of servitude.
My male and female servants are my devotees, always dependent upon me; the body, senses, mind, ego, intellect, and qualities of my devotee are under my control. (35)
For they have been offered to me; they are divine, under my control, and their very life depends on me.
Therefore, while abiding in my state, their conduct must be subject to my will.
By my very will alone, his prārabdha-karma exists;
by my power alone, O Lakṣmī, there is nothing unattainable for him. (37)
Having entrusted the burden to Me, the Lord of Śrī, one should perform only My work;
for I am the Supreme Self, the Master, while the devotee is indeed My servant. (38)
For a male servant should always be employed according to one's will;
likewise, a female servant, a maidservant, or a handmaid who has taken refuge with me should be employed [according to my will]. (39)

"I" and "mine" are indeed my own essential nature, and not those of anyone other than my devotee; therefore, by taking refuge in me, he is eternally liberated from the bonds of the body and so forth. (3.70.40)
For even while performing actions, those very deeds are indeed performed by Me;
thus, my devotee, freed from bondage, incurs no taint from them. 41.
The divine power of my devotee certainly delights the devotee;
that divine power gladdens him and even unites him with the goal of liberation. 42.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, the greatness of my mind has been declared to you;
I am the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of Akṣara. ||43||
I am known as Puruṣottama, the incarnate Lord of others;
I am indeed the Supreme Lord, the eternal Supreme Self. ||44||
The Lord, the cause of all, is both the full Brahman and the supreme Brahman; my incarnations include Kṛṣṇa and others, as well as Vāsudeva and the rest.

Brahmā and the others, as well as the lords such as Īśvara, and the powers such as Rādhā and Lakṣmī, are my portions; Viṣṇu, Rudra, and the kings of the gods are portions of portions and sub-portions.
Human beings and others who are portions of that [energy], as well as animals and trees—there are indeed creations of mine born from minute portions of those portions. (47)
In that regard, I am Nārāyaṇa; "nārāḥ" refers to the collection of selves (ātman), and because I make that my "ayana" (abode or resort), I am therefore Nārāyaṇa. ||48||
Among the principles born from Nara, I am Vāsudeva;
within the world of moving and unmoving beings, I am Nārāyaṇa. ||49||
The Puruṣa has a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, and a thousand feet;
from whom all this has arisen, he indeed is I, the Supreme Lord.
Whatever has been and whatever is to be, all that proceeds from the Supreme Lord;
I am that Śrī Puruṣottama, the sovereign of immortality. ||5 1||
Since Vāsudeva shines forth, as does Hiraṇyagarbha,
and since Savitṛ shines forth, I am that Śrī Puruṣottama.
I am that Śrī Puruṣottama, whose speech is the supreme Vedic word and whose highly refined Sanskrit language issues forth as a melody from my very throat.
I am that Supreme Self who exists as the wielder of Māyā, honored by Māyā, the Lord of Māyā, yet devoid of Māyā; I am Śrī Puruṣottama. ||54||
In one quarter there is creation, and in three quarters there is the imperishable abode;
I am that Śrī Puruṣottama, who is the Lord of the Earth, the Divine Play, and Śrī. ||55||
I am Yajñanārāyaṇa, and I am Sarvanārāyaṇa;
as Śrī Puruṣottama, I am that very one who exists in the form of the various Nārāyaṇas.
Whatever forms exist as manifestations of my form—humans such as Brahmins and others, gods, the moon, the sun, fire, heaven, and lightning—I am that, the illustrious Puruṣottama. (57)
Having received this secret mantra, which bestows liberation, men and women should respectfully perform service to me, who am such as this. (58)
I have hands and feet everywhere, and likewise, I possess eyes on all sides;
indeed, all worlds and all abodes exist within Me. (59)
Thus, I am the Great Being, the Lord of Śrī, the Supreme Person,
possessing a divine and auspicious form together with you, the Sovereign Lady.
Your husband Hari, the eternal one, possessed a vast body, was free from human frailty, and was youthful; he took delight, indeed, in sporting with you, Lakṣmī, his eternal consort Śrī.
I am indeed the youth of eternal youth to the Mother of the World;
possessing the beauty of ten million Cupids, I abide in the supreme state.
The supreme ether is the abode of liberation, resorted to by those who are liberated and those yet to be liberated;
it is my imperishable state, filled with eternal bliss, happiness, and other such qualities. 63.
Goloka, Vaikuṇṭha, the Unmanifest, and the Immortal— indeed,
these abodes were created by me for the purpose of enjoyment.
Likewise, there are the golden [worlds], as well as those beginning with Vairāja, which are illusory (māyika);
and the planes belonging to Sadāśiva, Viṣṇu, and Pradhāna. ||65||
All obscurations— beginning with pride regarding the truths and so forth,
and extending down to the underworlds— are filled with the fortune of play through her divine sport.
All the worlds were created by me for the purpose of my playful pastimes and the like;
my state is eternally established in enjoyment within my abodes in the form of incarnations.
But withdraw your play, O Lakṣmī, for that is composed of Māyā;
my supreme, eternal abode is indeed the imperishable realm pervading the three quarters.
That three-quartered manifestation is eternal; therein are those abodes which belong to Me—Goloka and all others—which are indeed eternally supreme.
The worlds beginning with Aiśvara and Jaiva constitute one quarter of this [universe] and are designated as impermanent;
for all of them are essentially composed of divine play (līlā), created by me solely for the purpose of sport.
In the eternal, imperishable Goloka, in Vaikuṇṭha, the unmanifest, and the immortal,
He is Acyuta, the perpetual, divine one, who always abides in youth.
I abide as the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Person;
likewise as Śrī Kṛṣṇa, as Nārāyaṇa, as the Infinite (Bhūmā), and as the Lord.
O Lakṣmī, Vāsudeva is always endowed with your forms,
joined by Muktānikā, Brahmapriyā, Haripriyā, and the others.
In Goloka, I am served by my energies—the gopīs Rādhā and Virajā; in Vikuṇṭha, I am served by Lakṣmī, Hariṇī, Kamalā, and others. (74)
The Lord is served by the female attendants of Ramā in the unmanifest state;
He is served by the lotus-like women of Vāsudeva in the abode of nectar.
Served by liberated cowherds, servants, and attendants,
I indeed dwell here in various forms as the very embodiment of my incarnations.
Together with Īśvarī Śrī, Lakṣmī, and Rādhā, who are eternally in union;
and with you, Ramā Vāsudevī, along with Kamalā.
O Lakṣmī, I have always found you, both on earth and in heaven;
you are eternal, the Mother of the World, my inseparable Śrī. (78)
She is eternally all-pervading and omnipresent, the perpetual sovereign of all worlds;
she is endowed with hands and feet everywhere, and has eyes, heads, and faces on every side.
The Supreme Sovereign, Mother of the World, Nārāyaṇī, the Golden One—in you alone is situated the entire universe, both the stationary and the moving. (3.70.80)
The sustenance and dissolution of the world occur through Your opening and closing [of the eyes];
You are the primordial Great Brāhmī, the Great Lakṣmī, the Supreme Sovereign of all. (8.1)
You, whose nature is both manifest and unmanifest, abide pervading the entire universe;
you are the sovereign power in the supreme abode, Rādhā, the dweller of Goloka. 82.
I am Lakṣmī, the dweller in Vaikuṇṭha; I am Ramā, who resides in the unmanifest; I am Padmā, whose abode is nectar; and I am my own imperishable sovereign power (vibhūti). 83.
In the worlds of the lords and within the eggs of living beings,
you indeed become the embodiment of playful sovereignty, assuming the nature of various planes of existence.
The grounds of the lords, their palaces, millions of mansions, their riches, their gardens, and the lands of their divine fields and territories—[all these were given]. (85)
"I exist, indeed, I exist"—this is my play, which is all my perfections;
you are the veils and the principles (tattvas) belonging to Sādāśiva. (86)
The Vaiṣṇava principles, as well as those consisting of Māyā, the principles composed of gold, and those beginning with Vairāja; ||87||

Those which are the abodes of the Satya-loka and others, as well as those belonging to the realm of humans, and likewise those principles (tattvas) in the netherworlds (pātālas) which are the grounds for enjoyment; ||88||
O Lakṣmī, whatever things exist composed of water, earth, fire, and air—all those are indeed Your playful manifestations. 89.
You are of the nature of form, taste, smell, and touch; you are embodied as sound itself.
Having attained the form of Lakṣmī, you are named after wealth, property, and the like.
Thus, you are the very nature of the world; O Lotus-born One, you are the Fortune (Śrī) of the world who has taken refuge in Him, and indeed, all that is to be known is your form.
O Lakṣmī, every female form is your form; your body is beauty, character, brilliance, good fortune, gentleness, and happiness. (92)
O Lotus-like One, this beauty, fragrance, charm, and exquisite flavor—all such forms as these reside within you among all women. (93)
Brāhmī, Nārāyaṇī, Śrī, Akṣarī, Muktānikā, Ramā, Brahmapriyā, Kamalā, Haripriyā, and Māṇikī. ||94||
Rādhā, Lakṣmī, Parāvidyā, Ramā, Śrī, Nārāyaṇī, Vidyā, Sarasvatī, Mātā, Vaiṣṇavī, Padminī, and Satī. (95)
Padmā, Padmajā, the daughter of the ocean, Rambhā, Rādhikā, Bhūrlīlā, Sukhadā, Lakṣmī, Hariṇī, and Mādhavīśvarī. ||96||
Gaurī, Kārṣṇī, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇī, Svāhā, Svadhā, Rati, Sampat, Smṛddhi, Vāsudevī, Virajā, and Hiraṇmayī. ||97||
"Bhārgavī, Śivarājñī, Śrī, Rāmā, and Śrīkāntavallabhā—
whosoever indeed recites these names of yours every morning," (98)
He attains great prosperity, fortune, and glory that is imperishable—golden-hued, radiant, and adorned with garlands of gold and silver. (99)
One attains the golden splendor of moonlight, which is my own form—
possessing the nature of supreme fragrance, beauty, and other qualities, and increasing nourishment.
Your giver is the glorious Lord, Puruṣottama himself;
he is the Supreme Nārāyaṇa, the Master, an ocean of affection and compassion. || 10.1 ||
He is of virtuous character, fortunate, one whose desires are fulfilled, and possessed of all powers;
he is the bestower of the happiness of heaven and liberation, and the refuge of all embodied beings.
Therefore, O Goddess of gods, I offer myself to my female servant who is devoted to me, together with you; I surrender myself to her, for we have realized our mutual identity as the Self.
The glorious Lord Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of Śrī, the Supreme Person, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa—he is I, the supreme goal. 1.04.
He is the refuge, the temple, the dwelling, the kinsman, the father, the husband, the friend, the mother, the brother, the protector, the guardian, and the Lord of the worlds. (1.05)
The Lord of Śrī possesses auspicious qualities and bestows the fruits of all desires;
I am devoid of material qualities, free from attributes, yet possessed of a divine form.
Endowed with divine, innumerable qualities, sovereignty, beauty, and charm,
[he abides] in the immortal, eternal, divine, infinite, imperishable, supreme state.
I dwell in the world of Brahmā, which is endowed with the bliss of Brahman-joy,
consisting of supreme splendor, pure, and free from dissolution and the like.
In that which is incalculable, undecaying, eternal, devoid of waking, dreaming, and the like; free from equality and superiority, and untouched by end or beginning—that auspicious state.
To Him who possesses the most supreme splendor, the ocean of bliss,
the imperishable one known through the Vedas, in whom the gods and the Sādhyas have taken their seat.
The gods have sat down within the All; they know that and remain there.
The wise always behold that supreme imperishable of mine. 111.
Where the many-horned, tireless cows dwell on all sides, those Sādhya-yogins indeed know the majesty of the celestial realm (nāka). 1.12.
O youthful Śrī and Narāyaṇa, we shall dwell there eternally,
where your sisters, young women such as yourself, are my beloveds.
Having reached that supreme abode of Mine, the imperishable, they do not return;
those who know the Mantras proceed to this divine state of liberation.

Thus ends the seventieth chapter, titled "The Description of the Attainment of Knowledge of the Hidden Meaning of the Great Mantra," in the Third Section, the Dvāpara Age, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
