Listen, O Nārāyaṇī Śrī, to the expansion of the manifestation of the three-quarters (tripādvibhūti). Indeed, there are innumerable abodes consisting of pure sattva.
Indeed, those [worlds] are eternal, rich with the bliss of the joy of Brahman, entirely free from modification, and devoid of anything to be rejected or otherwise. || 2 ||
They are indeed divine, made of gold, pure, and radiant,
truly served by those possessed of devotion to the lotus feet of the incarnations.
They were inhabited by men and women of divine form who are eternally liberated,
and they contained forests, gardens, lakes, and cities.
The abodes of those who serve the imperishable Brahman are to be enjoyed;
they become palaces consisting of the bliss of the joy of one's own Self. || 5 ||
Indeed, those states of supreme bliss, such as Nirvāṇa and Kaivalya,
are truly endowed with the enjoyment of the singular essence of devotion and service to the feet of Śrī Śaṅkara.
Eternally liberated, most divine, and eternal, these attendants who serve me dwell within these very [lotuses], devotedly serving my feet.
Those who know the mantras indeed go to those supreme abodes;
they truly bestow the bliss of Brahman and grant me yoga.
Abiding in various places, I possess the nature of an incarnation;
yet as the one who incarnates, I truly exist in the imperishable, supreme abode.
Mahāmāyā, who is primordial nature (prakṛti), praises me again and again: "Salutations to you, the dweller in the imperishable; salutations to you, the Supreme Lord. (3.71.10)
Salutations to You, who are both the essence of the incarnations and the one who descends;
O Lord, I am Your power (māyā), and the worlds are Your māyā.
The abodes of the lords are indeed your very stages;
all the principles (tattvas) are truly your effects.
You are indeed the Ancient Puruṣa, the cause of all causes;
O Lord of Śrī, Bhū, Līlā, and Ramā, O Consort of Māṇikī and Muktikā!
O beloved of Prajñāpadmāvatī, homage to you, O Lord who bestows happiness!
Homage indeed to you, Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of Lakṣmī and Padmā! 14.
Salutations to the one whose nature is that of the Lord of All, whose self is the soul of all deities;
salutations, O Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, O Hari, to you of infinite forms! 15.
Salutations to you, the Immovable, the Beloved, the Supreme Lord;
salutations to you, the Omniscient, the All-pervading, the Son of Gopāla. || 16 ||
Salutations to you, the Supreme Self, whose essence is the creation of all;
salutations to you, the Brahman, the light, possessed of pure radiance. || 17 ||
Salutation to the progenitor, the father, the cause of creation, preservation, and dissolution;
and salutation to Nārāyaṇa, who dwells within the inner self of all.
Salutations to the one possessed of infinite divine qualities, who bestows the goals of human life;
salutations to the one in the form of the *vyūha*, whose nature consists of the five states.
Be gracious, O Blessed Viṣṇu, for the welfare of all the worlds;
indeed, these selves are devoid of knowledge, formless, and without senses.
They exist devoid of all ritual performance and without any support;
you ought indeed to grant me worlds and bodies for them.
O Śrī Kṛṣṇa, manifest Your playful opulence as before—the entire world of sentient and insentient beings, both stationary and moving. 22.
Behold, O Supreme Lord; awaken this illusory one who is dissolved and asleep within me;
indeed, together with me as Prakṛti, bring forth creation.
O Lord, having contemplated merit and demerit, pleasure and pain within me,
you ought indeed to empower me and perform your divine play through your splendor.
O Lakṣmī, having been thus requested by her through her power of illusion (māyā), I indeed proceeded to create the universe within that very illusion. (25)
Indeed, the person who was liberated from his abode by his own will became united with her;
therefore he is called Prakṛtipuruṣa, and thus Pradhānapuruṣa.

The primary principle (pradhāna) is indeed the Great Principle (mahattattva), which is the intellect (buddhi) and thus the Sovereign (īśvarī). From that [intellect], the personified primary principle (pradhānapuruṣa), the ego-sense (ahaṃkāra) is born. ||27||
This very Hiraṇyagarbha is indeed called Mahāviṣṇu;
from him the mind, the subtle elements (tanmātras), and the sense organs originate.
This group of sixteen is that Puruṣa named Vairāja;
from the Vairāja were born the Lords Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara. (29)
Brahmā became the earth and water, Viṣṇu the most exalted fire, Rudra the vital breath and wind, and from his heart the sky and space were born.
From these were created the sages, the ancestors, the gods, the spirits, and human beings;
as well as the asuras, dānavas, daityas, nāgas, and serpents. ||3.1||
All creatures of the animal realm were born according to their respective natures; all are joined to appropriate wombs in accordance with their past actions. (32)
For they always abide in their essential nature, yet they manifest by the will of Hari;
thus, O Lakṣmī, contemplate my play as consisting of Māyā.
You alone are that Great Illusion (Mahāmāyā), divine, having resorted to my yoga; you are my very own nature, my will itself, my power, and the one who possesses all forms.
And my half-woman is Brāhmī, Nārāyaṇī, Maheśvarī, Mahālakṣmī, Vāsudevī, Vaiṣṇavī, Kamalā, and Ramā. (35)
You are Rādhā, Lakṣmī, Priyā, Kāntā, and Śrī; you are the eternal bestower of happiness, the one who ordains the birth and other states of all living beings existing within the creation. (36)
Without my power, there is no manifestation of creation anywhere;
therefore, O Supreme Goddess, you are the very life-breath of the universe. (37)
I am the vital breaths, my form is Prāṇa; you are my Lord, the Supreme Ishvara.
I am full of all excellent qualities, the Supreme Ishana, the Supreme Ruler. (38)
I indeed become Śrī Kṛṣṇa for the sake of fulfilling the desires of Rādhā;
I indeed become Nārāyaṇa for the sake of fulfilling the desires of Lakṣmī. (39)
I indeed become Vāsudeva, complete and assuming three forms;
from that, there arises the form of Pradyumna, endowed with all sovereign powers.
He is the Lord of the abundant ones, the lords of lords, and the source of all;
he is the ruler even of Time, and indeed he brings about the divine creation. (41)
Having attained the state of the Inner Controller (Antaryāmin) and being entered by Mahākāla, he who assumes the form of Mahākāla possesses the powerful sovereignty of Hari. 42.
My resolve is powerful, and sovereignty is caused by time;
indeed, the son of Mahākāla is known as Kāla.
Having attained absorption within that, Aniruddha became the creator of the world;
in ancient times, he was granted by me the knowledge consisting of the eternal Vedas.
Indeed, Brahmās arise as partial manifestations of Aniruddha;
from Vāsudeva, moreover, another was born, namely Pradyumna. (45)
Endowed with my own power, splendor, and sovereignty, he performs the work of protection;
he protects the Īśa-creation and sets in motion the state of stability.
Then Viṣṇu, whose nature consists of those portions, repeatedly protects the entire world;
from Vāsudeva is born Saṃkarṣaṇa, the cause of destruction.

When those born from his portions, such as Rudra and others, are endowed with the power of knowledge, missiles, weapons, and so forth, they perform acts of destruction and bring about the dissolution of creation. (48)
Thus, O Lakṣmī, these portions of mine always exist;
and by my will, their portions likewise become their wives. 49.
The Fish, the Tortoise, the Boar, Narasiṃha, Vāmana,
Rāma, Paraśurāma, Kṛṣṇa, Buddha, and Kalki— these are the ten.
O Lakṣmī, my incarnations are born throughout all creations;
these performers of my work are those who necessarily manifest. (51)
I am the Avatārī, accompanied by you according to my own will;
I am the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama. ||52||
Through devotion to me, they indeed go to my abode, the imperishable state;
through devotion to the forms of my incarnations, they indeed go to Goloka and other realms.
Having gone among them, they indeed do not return without being liberated;
all of them possess happiness equal to mine, just as you are happy.
By my will, they are born for the sake of the welfare of the world;
for those liberated by me, there is no birth on earth bound by karma.
Indeed, for me, the state of being a follower is liberation itself and nothing else;
my servitude is truly bondage, yet it is eternal bliss and eternally imperishable.

Furthermore, those beloved of Brahmā, the great liberated ones, the servants of Hari who are free from all affliction, will return by their own will to my abode, remaining established in that very abode. (57)

If others also, having obtained my mantra which severs the bonds of karma, should abandon even the worldly happiness of eating food mixed with poison and devote themselves [to me], then indeed [they shall succeed]. (58)
They take refuge in me alone through the chanting of my names and worship;
with undivided devotion, they should worship me, the abode of compassion. 59.
The Supreme Self, a treasure-trove of affection for His devotees, protects them and leads them to the abode of Viṣṇu, which is as radiant as the rays of a thousand suns.
Having placed her in that celestial chariot, the Blessed Lord Śrī Hari himself [honored] those who had chanted my mantra and were solely devoted to me.
For me, here, the recitation of the mantra of Śrīpati, Śrī Hari, is supreme;
it is a divine medicine consisting entirely of nectar, the highest of medicines.
This supreme, divine elixir pacifies all agitation and the like, removes the noose of *māyā*, and is auspicious in dispelling the disease of *māyā*. (63)
While this great medicinal herb, the Kṛṣṇa-mantra, exists here on the surface of the earth,
that men do not take hold of it is considered a great loss.
Those fools who do not drink the elixir of Hari’s name remain within the delusion of their own past accumulated sins. 65.
Through the ritual service of worshiping Hari, through meditation, through service,
through truthful speech, and through giving, the purification of the body and the self arises for me.
Therefore, my dwelling is in my heart and likewise incessantly within my own self;
having made the heart of the devotee my temple, I lead them to my own abode.
O Lakṣmī, all you beloveds of Brahmā, and likewise the others who are beloved of Hari—may Līlā and the rest listen to me, and may they enjoy me, their dear husband. (68)
May they proceed upon the excellent path, having offered up all their dispositions,
as well as their services, their theoretical and practical knowledge, their meditations, and even their ascetic penances.
"Let them worship me, their beloved husband, through vows, sacrifices, gifts, and fragrant unguents such as sandalwood, as well as with gestures, expressions, and amorous charms. (3.71.70)
And let them see me everywhere— at all times in both dry and moist things, in stationary and moving beings, on the earth and in the clouds, in all embodied forms.
In their own affairs, even in the palaces of others, let them offer various kinds of gifts while addressing me, the Supreme Person. (72)
Chant me, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, always;
worship me, remember my mantra, and remember me as the one who makes it meaningful. (73)
Let them indeed drink the Vaiṣṇava nectar; let them drink the nectar of the mantra, and let them drink the nectar of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa.
May they drink the nectar of the command, the essence of love, and the essence of service;
and may all the beloveds drink the essence of liberation and the essence of the Beloved. 75.
May they drink the nectar of devotion, the nectar of yoga, and the nectar of the Self;
may they drink the nectar of Brahman, the nectar of service, and the nectar of the Beloved. ||76||
May they drink the essence of affection, the essence of truth, and all essences;
may they always worship their beloved and meditate upon Madhusūdana.
Let them sing of me, Mahākṛṣṇa; let them constantly chant the name of Śrī Hari;
for the sake of my pleasure, let them perform austerities, being devoted to me and intent on meditation upon me. 78.
Thus, all those humans and others on earth who shall perform devotion for my sake are indeed the supreme Bhāgavatas. (79)
O Lakṣmī, by my power, those who recite this hymn of praise for worship shall indeed become free from mental anguish; of this there is no doubt. (3.71.80)
They shall be free from sorrow, meritorious, and free from disease;
they shall be endowed with all sovereign powers and devoid of all ailments and the like. ||81||
By my supreme grace, even the immortals and the gods (nirjaras) shall possess abundance of wealth and grain, adorned with sons, grandsons, and their progeny.
In the section of my temple, in my heart, and in my mind, he who bestows all jewels always dwells as one whose vow is truth. (83)
At the doorways of the houses of those devotees who are engaged in the practice of mantras, wish-fulfilling trees (kalpadrumas) will always appear, bestowing the fruits of all desires. ||84||
Cows that yield all desires, as well as wish-fulfilling gems, wish-granting creepers, and wish-granting vessels, reside in the devotee's house. (85)
By my grace, O Lakṣmī, those immortals become endowed with all prosperity, auspiciousness, and splendor. ||86||
Devoted to generosity, wisdom, and meditation, and filled with bliss, there shall be neither famine, nor disease, nor untimely death. (87)
O Lakṣmī, where my Vaiṣṇava devotees dwell—those who are devoted to my vows, intent on meditation upon me, engaged in my recitation, and dedicated to my being—there [I abide]. ||88||
Their divine, meritorious houses, which even bestow liberation, have indeed become sacred pilgrimage sites resembling my own imperishable form. ||89||
In whose houses there are maces, discuses, banners, and bows; and in whose [houses] there are the emblems of the trident, the fish, the arrow, and the svastika—those are mine. (3.71.90)
And let my images appear on all the surfaces of the walls, at all the doors of the house, and in every manner upon all sacred sites. (9.1)
I possess divine paintings of my playful exploits, along with images of Tulasī, Rādhikā, Lakṣmī, and Māṇikī. ||92||
Wherever I am depicted within the house on all sides, endowed with the lotus-like Śrī who bestows the bliss of Prajñāpadmāvatī; ||93||
On all sides, the Vaiṣṇava sentiment is present and many auspicious sights are seen;
likewise, auspicious women who are devotees of Viṣṇu are depicted in paintings upon the walls. (94)
Those palaces wherein sacred bathing-places (tīrthas) exist are my homes; they contain statues for water-sports and the circular pavilion of Rādhārāsa. 95.
Images of the marriage of Brahmapriyā are painted in my house;
that house of mine, for my devotee, is of divine form and a sacred ford for liberation. 96.
And my form joined with cows, wonderful with the study of knowledge;
and my wonderful form seated in a celestial chariot, wonderful with the initiation for sacrifice and other rites. 97.
It was wonderful, featuring Kuṅkumavāpikā along with Aśvapaṭṭasara, graced by the hermitage of Lomaśa, and adorned with the illustrious Kambharā. 98.
The painting of Gopāla-Kṛṣṇa, worshipped by all the gods and others, and my auspicious images which provide a refuge and protect their devotees. (99)
O Lakṣmī, every sacred ford that bestows liberation is my own form and my abode;
likewise, the fifty-three forms of mine who have descended are accompanied by you.
O Lotus-born One, all those in whose houses these [images] reside are granters of liberation;
for their lineage, and the lineages of their lineages, liberation arises as a certainty.

Thus ends the seventy-first chapter, titled "The Description of Divinity and Other Attributes within the Single-Legged Līlā-vibhūti Created at the Request of Māyā," in the section on the Tripāda-vibhūti within the third period (Dvāpara-santāna) of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Puruṣottama said: Listen, O Nārāyaṇī Śrī, to my worship which bestows liberation:
"Kṛṣṇa, Viṣṇu, Hare, Rāma, Mukunda, Madhusūdana. (1)
O Nārāyaṇa, O Hṛṣīkeśa, O Puruṣottama, O Keśava!
O Anādi-Śrīkṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, O Lord of Lakṣmī, O Master! || 2 ||
O you who abide in the syllable Padmanābha, O one who delights in the Self, O treasure-house of compassion!
O Vāsudeva, O Lord of liberation, O Śrīdhara, O Lord of Śrī, O All-pervading One! 3.
O Lord of Rādhā and Ramā; O Victorious One; O Lord of Prajñā and Padmāvatī; O Giver of Prosperity; O Lord of Śrī; O Abode of Śrī; O Bestower of Liberation; O Lord of Māṇikī! || 4 ||
O delighter of Kambharā, beloved of Brahmapriyā, Janārdana;
O child Gopāla, Lord of the Universe, giver of happiness, Lord of Śrī, Sovereign! 5.
"O Lord of Life, O Beloved of the Goddess of Beauty, O Supreme Lord, O Mādhava!"—
thus indeed did the women on earth utter my names.
Even men, though advanced in age, as well as children, the elderly, and youths, go indeed to my abode when they are devoted solely to my name.
Even those who are devoted to household duties bow to me, Hari; for they indeed worship me as their Lord while sitting, lying down, traveling, meditating, and acquiring knowledge.
Playing, they offer salutations and go to my imperishable abode,
where they sweetly chant your name day and night.
In whichever house on the surface of the earth the presence of Kṛṣṇa is perceived,
it attains equality with the world of Viṣṇu and is equal to my own abode.
The fortune of that house is eternal; there is no need for deliberation on this point. I see no difference between that devotee’s home and the abode of the Imperishable (Akṣaralaya). || 11 ||
They constantly utter my name in my imperishable abode; likewise, wherever they chant my name upon this earth, that is my home.
The divine abode is imperishable and to be realized; no distinction exists therein.
The state of both worlds is entirely equal in its totality.
There is no fear of old age or disease, for the people there are free from death;
and there, my name is sung and likewise my mantra is recited.
What more indeed shall I say? By my resorting to them, my illusory powers become divine; for the cows of my devotee become divine, as do his auspicious buffaloes.
His divine gardens and his auspicious, celestial home were always magnificent;
his household utensils and even his foods were divine.
The courtyard of the house is always divine for the devotee, as are his sons, grandsons, and others;
indeed, his vessels and his wealth are always divine.
May divine trees, creepers, celestial garments such as those from Kāśī, coverings, caskets, clothes, ornaments, and other such divine things always belong to me, his devotee. || 18 ||
The dust, the particles, the waters, and even the divine grains of the devotee’s house belong to me, the Supreme Lord, wherever I am present.
Even the birds and animals that dwell in that house, as well as divine guests, are purified by my grace. (3.72.20)
All those sacred fords (tīrthas) are in every way to be enjoyed by devotees;
indeed, objects of enjoyment are purifying even for sinners.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, there exists that which purifies by virtue of my dwelling within it:
the home and so forth of a devotee, which is beyond qualities (nirguṇa), bestows merit, and grants liberation.
Listen, O Lakṣmī, to the narrative of Yayāti, the son of Nahuṣa.
For my devotee in this world, it is purifying and bestows liberation from the world.
Yayāti, a devotee of the Blessed One and a follower of Viṣṇu, performed a hundred Aśvamedhas as well as a hundred Vājapeyas, O lord of the earth.
With faith, the king gave gifts of many forms,
including hundreds of thousands of lakhs of cows, as well as hundreds of crores.
He also performed ten million fire-sacrifices (koṭihoma) and gave gifts such as land;
indeed, he lived for eighty thousand years.
Yayāti indeed lamented: "This body is bound by karma;
it will end as ashes, or as excrement, or as earth. (27)
By this [action], sin is acquired, and from that, hell is the fruit;
by this [other action], merit is acquired, and heaven and sovereignty again and again.
And by this, devotion is cultivated, through which liberation becomes certain;
therefore, that alone should be accomplished here by a discerning person while remaining in the kingdom. (29)
Having reflected thus, the king began the worship of the names of Hari:
"Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Viṣṇu, Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, O Lord! (3.72.30)
"O Anādi-Śrī-Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, Dāmodara, Acyuta!
Thus worshipping Him, He gave these auspicious words as an instruction to His own messengers. (3.1)
"Let my messengers go throughout the realm, as far as the edge of the ocean;
let them instruct the subjects and cause them to perform devotion to Hari. (32)
May they behold the Supreme Self, may they chant the glorification of His names;
may they worship Hari constantly and devote themselves to the Supreme Lord. ||33||
I shall certainly not accept taxes from my subjects;
let the people always chant the nectar of Hari’s name alone. (34)
Commanded by the messengers, the subjects likewise performed worship;
they meditated upon Hari-Kṛṣṇa and sang the praises of Janārdana. (35)
They always recited my mantras, performed austerities, and offered sacrifices to me; they were absorbed in meditation on me, resolved upon me, and devoted to my worship. (36)
Then the entire circle of the earth became Vaiṣṇava;
by my prowess, human beings were born free from all mental afflictions.
Free from sorrow and meritorious, they are devoid of all diseases;
endowed with every sovereignty, they are possessed of wealth and grain.
With noble lineages of sons, grandsons, and others, free from disease and calamities, may there be wish-fulfilling trees at their doorways, bestowing the fruits of all desires. (39)
Cows that yielded all desires and wish-fulfilling gems indeed appeared, as did unforeseen prosperities such as the increase of the kingdom. (3.72.40)
All the subjects were endowed with every auspicious fortune, devoted to knowledge and meditation, highly meritorious, and dedicated to devotion and worship. ||41||
There shall be no famine, nor disease, nor untimely death for men;
all human beings shall be devotees of Viṣṇu, intent upon meditation on me. 42.
Those who drink wine, yet are devoted to my worship, service, and the chanting of my names;
in whom there is a Vaiṣṇava disposition everywhere—even toward their home, trees, and animals. (43)
In every house there were radiant temples dedicated to me,
and upon the walls of those houses were paintings of me together with you.
Songs of mine are sung by women who are my devotees;
and the people—children, the elderly, and youths alike—worship me. 45.
Women devoted to household duties worship me, the Supreme Lord, while on their seats, beds, vehicles, during drinking, standing, and eating. (46)
In play, in festival, and in desire, they worship me, the Lord Hari;
they utter the name of Śrī Hari and honor that which bestows liberation.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, the entire surface of the earth became equal to Vaikuṇṭha;
everyone was devoted to me and intent upon my affection.
Having been instructed by Yayāti, they indeed became Vaiṣṇavas on earth; and by my grace, they became free from old age and death. 49.
Those Vaiṣṇavas who are long-lived do not go to my world;
rather, those who travel by celestial chariot (vimāna) go to my abode, the realm of Viṣṇu.
Even those men and women whose bodies have endured hundreds of thousands of years appear, by my grace, as if they were all only twenty-five years of age. (51)
With steady bodies, happy, and free from old age, disease, and other afflictions—all those devotees were attended by the messengers of Viṣṇu, the servants of Hari. (52)
Seeing the attendants of Yama, they wander about and strike out;
being beaten and weeping, those followers of Yama went toward Yama. (53)
They spoke thus on the earth regarding the conduct of the king:
"The entire surface of the earth has indeed become immortal and entirely Vaiṣṇava."
O Yama, by Yayāti’s great devotion, that place was indeed made to resemble Vaikuṇṭha;
there, the messengers of Yama were struck down by the messengers of Viṣṇu upon the earth.
"O Dharmarāja, what shall we do? We will certainly not go to the surface of the earth.
Upon hearing this, Dharmarāja reflected for a moment.
I must certainly act in such a way that this king comes to an end;
for upon the destruction of the king, all the subjects will fall onto the wrong path.
"The path to Yama will likewise be accompanied by its lunar days.
Having reflected thus, he went to Viṣṇu in Vaikuṇṭha and entreated the Lord.
He prostrated like a staff and worshipped the Supreme Lord; Dharmarāja then informed Hari that he had acted contrary to the conduct of Yayāti.
O Blessed One, by your devotee, the path of Yama has been blocked for me;
indeed, all human beings on the surface of the earth have been made Vaiṣṇavas by him.
Therefore, O Hara, quickly summon your own devotee here;
by that, even the obstruction of punishment for sinners shall be removed.
But now, through the yoga of devotion, even sinners go to that abode;
having shaken off their sins, my house in the realm of Yama becomes empty. (62)
Thus requested, Hari said: "That is indeed true for me;
for through contact with my devotees, even sinners are purified. (63)
They certainly do so, there is no doubt; for that earth is indeed equal to Vaikuṇṭha.
However, O Yama, I am subject only to my devotees and not otherwise.
I never act in opposition to the will of my devotee;
may it be well with you, worship me, and do not create an obstacle to devotion.
Or else, go to Parameṣṭhin in the true world of Brahmā and report the matter as it truly is; he will grant you his wisdom.
Thus addressed, O Lakṣmī, King Yama went toward Aja;
he bowed, worshipped him, and reported everything exactly as it had happened. (67)
Having heard this, Brahmā said to Yama: "This king is indeed a devotee of Viṣṇu;
he must certainly not be defeated. Therefore, you must truly exert effort in that regard."
But they possess hearts inclined toward the path of Yama;
therefore, exert yourself in such a way that you may go to heaven, O Indra of Dharma.
"Offer half of Mahendra's seat to the king for his gift;
when this is done, the king shall always dwell in heaven and not upon the earth."
O Yama, devotion will become weak among the subjects;
consequently, dharma will be weak, and thus your path will become full [of travelers]. ||71||
Thus addressed, Dharmarāja departed toward heaven for Indra;
the king of the gods quickly beheld Dharmarāja as he was approaching. 72.
Having risen, he offered him half his seat and inquired about his arrival;
Dharmarāja then related the entire auspicious life-story of Yayāti.
Even by Yayāti, the son of Nahuṣa, all those on the surface of the earth were indeed made Vaiṣṇavas and righteous through his Vaiṣṇava power.
The circle of the earth indeed shone with a form equal to Vaikuṇṭha;
men became immortal, free from old age and disease.
Free from evil, devoted to truth, and devoid of defects such as anger, those who are characterized by devotion and dedicated to dharma worship Nārāyaṇa. (76)
Just as blades of dūrvā grass growing from a root-sprout spread across the earth,
so too does progeny expand through sons, grandsons, and great-grandsons.
They do not go upon the path of Yama, but go instead to Vaikuṇṭha;
I have become devoid of purpose, stripped of all activity.
Having understood this, O Mahendra, you must indeed act for the welfare of my subjects as well,
regarding the flow of established conduct and the course of the creation of the Vedhas.
Having spoken thus, Dharmarāja then departed for his own abode;
Mahendra then said to his charioteer Mātali, "Go to the earth."
Speak my words to King Yayāti, the son of Nahuṣa, who is devoted [to me]:
"Mahendra will indeed grant you half of his own throne. (8.1)
By these [merits], O lord of the earth, enjoy happiness in heaven until the end of the kalpa;
for thousands of years, O king, you have enjoyed sovereignty.
"Enjoy heaven once more, and thereafter [attain] that supreme and eternal state.
You have four sons: Ruru, Puru, Kuru, and Yadu. (83)
Having entrusted the kingdom to them, come to heaven by means of a celestial chariot;
[there you shall find] Ila, Purūravas, Vipracitti, Śivi, and Manu.
Sagara, Nahuṣa, their father, and other lords of men rejoice there in heaven; come there yourself as one such. (85)
Established in the virtues of heaven, rejoice together with Śakra;
eighty thousand kings [shall remain] on the surface of the earth for as many years as you [have lived]. (86)
Indeed, having performed the abandonment of the five-element body upon the earth, his auspicious deeds—consisting of charity, sacrifice, and devotion to Viṣṇu—have departed [to heaven]. (87)
"Assuming a divine form, enjoy the pleasures of heaven.
Having heard this, Yayāti said, "O Mātali, listen to my words. (88)
Since it is by means of this body that one may achieve the well-performed means to liberation, and since devotion to Kṛṣṇa arises through it, how can this physical frame be abandoned? (89)
Why would a person abandon that body by which he accumulates merit consisting of truth and dharma, as well as liberation? (3.72.90)
Both the self and the body are like two friends;
therefore, one should never abandon one's own body. 91.
Having heard this, Mātali said: "O King, what you have spoken is true;
however, the body, nourished by karma, remains here subject to the power of time. (92)
And this form, consisting of the five elements, is specifically of the nature of earth;
indeed, upon the exhaustion of the karma that sustains life, it must be forcibly abandoned. (93)
This condition indeed always exists among people;
after he has grown old, he surely perishes—of this there is no doubt. (94)
"Therefore, having abandoned this body which is by nature subject to abandonment, go to heaven.
Having heard this, Yayāti indeed said, "Mātali, is that old age [not mine]? (95)
"Tell me truly, when did it arise and how does it cause suffering?
Having heard this, Mātali said: "Listen, O King, to that which is born of its own nature. (96)
Mahākāla is the power (śakti) of Hari, the Supreme Soul, the Lord of Śrī;
Mṛtyu is indeed the daughter of Mahākāla, and Jarā is her daughter. 97.

That [power], which exists together with the arising of the principles created by Māyā, enters into those principles once they have arisen and their duration has been determined, bringing about their destruction. (98)
For the primary nature (pradhāna) indeed perishes, as does the principle of the Great One (mahat-tattva) which is subject to destruction;
the ego-sense (ahaṃkāra) also perishes, and the mind (manas) likewise perishes. 99.
The Vairāja [self] is also exhausted, as are the senses and their objects;
even the elements and elemental things are repeatedly exhausted by it. (3.72.100)
The tastes, which are the nourishers residing within the body, become diminished;
indeed, all bodies shine forth when they are well-nourished by those tastes. || 101 ||
The *rasas* are indeed of the nature of semen; when there is an abundance of *rasa*, youth prevails.
However, O King, from excessive indulgence with women, even the loss of the sense of taste may occur.
For a woman, attachment to men indeed causes the loss of her vitality;
vitality consists of vigor and desire, and when that is lost, there is complete senility.
Upon the destruction of the semen and blood, the body becomes empty;
it then becomes discolored, tormented by suffering, and pervaded by old age. (104)
By that [process], gray hair arises, and from it the feverish heat is produced;
when they have become worn out, they go to destruction, and death likewise follows as a certainty.
"O King, having reflected thus, abandon your body and go to heaven;
a celestial chariot of Indra's splendor has been brought by me for your sake. (106)

Thus ends the seventy-second chapter, titled "The Description of how all the Subjects became Vaiṣṇavas through the Power of King Yayāti’s Devotion to the Mantra of the Lord’s Name," in the Third Section (Dvāpara-santāna) of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Puruṣottama said: Listen, O Śrī Nārāyaṇī, to the further words concerning Yayāti;
indeed, there is no difference whatsoever between dying in the world of Manu, in heaven, or in the realm of truth.
Therefore, having abandoned this body, I shall not go to heaven;
for the body does not exist without the vital breath, nor do the vital breaths exist without the living soul.
For the individual soul does not exist without the Self, and the Self does not exist without Hari;
having abandoned all this here, heaven does not please me at all.
Having abandoned those by whose grace I enjoy happiness on this earth, I shall by no means at all enjoy the pleasures of heaven.
Behold my body today, through the power of my merit and devotion, as if it were twenty years of age;
though I am decrepit at eighty years, I experience this body as if it were new.
There is no illness for me, no decline, no confusion, and no diseases;
through my devotion to the Dharma, my body alone grows ever stronger.
This divine medicine, consisting entirely of nectar, is joined with devotion.
And here, that which is called Dharma is performed, which destroys evil and disease.
Indeed, my body has been purified by the chanting of the glories of Śrī Hari;
I constantly drink and digest this elixir.
Therefore, by the power of that [name], old age and death do not exist for me;
nor indeed for those great devotees who drink the elixir of the nectar of Kṛṣṇa’s name.
Their bodies indeed become divine in form, just like mine,
through meditation on Hari, as well as through devotion, worship, and service.
O Mātali, by virtue of truth, the merit of giving, the recitation of mantras,
and the establishment of devotion, my body remains free from disease.
Through the blessings of the virtuous, I have become fearless of Māyā, Time, and the like; by the power of Hari’s grace, my state here is indeed heaven upon heaven.
Through the ritual services of worship to Hari, through devotion, meditation, and hymns of praise,
and through truthfulness, charity, and observances, my body has attained a divine state.
"I shall not go to heaven; rather, I am making heaven right here.
Go and report to Indra exactly what I have said."
Having heard this, Mātali went quickly and informed Indra;
Indra, too, having reflected, then prepared another [chariot] from among those already fashioned.
They devised a plan to delude the king and said to Mātali:
"Listen, O Mātali, this king is indeed a firm devotee of Viṣṇu."
But he, having abandoned devotion, will never go to heaven; rather, he must be respectfully invited while still in his physical body. 17.
He was to be informed by Mātali through various means, such as the gods, according to the principles of creation;
then, having received the command, Mātali went toward the king.
The king showed him honor, and Mātali spoke clearly:
"O King, Indra, Varuṇa, Yama, Kubera, and Agni—"
Īśāna, Anila, Nirvṛta, Guru, and Kavi—
all of them honored you, each according to the dignity of their own station.

There they quickly remembered Viṣṇu, Īśāna, and Brahmā;

By following our instructions, there is liberation, true liberation, and an auspicious state;

Through indulgence in sensual pleasures, that very king indeed reached old age;

The king grieved for her day and night;
then, one night, she beheld the king with feelings of love toward him.
"You appear to be old, O King; you are certainly not fit for my sake.

Afflicted by passion, the king summoned his sons and spoke these words;

My mind is extremely tormented, attached to women, and very fickle; moreover, whatever son I may have will bring about the onset of old age.

Having heard this, his sons said to him: "O King, you are devoted to dharma;

"Knowing this, my dear sons, you should do that which brings me happiness.

The kingdom, the bow, the parasol, the elephant, the horse, wealth, the earth, the treasury, the harem, the entire army, the fly-whisk, the fan, and the palace—[all these he gave]. (94)

Thus ends the seventy-third chapter, titled "Description of the Power of Devotion," in the third section (the Dvāpara cycle) of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, concerning how Yayāti, after departing from heaven, attained superior devotion and other virtues upon returning to earth; how Indra bestowed Bindumatī upon him for the sake of his renunciation of the world; how he regained youth through his son; and finally, his departure for Vaikuṇṭha. || 73 ||
Śrī Puruṣottama said: Listen, O Śrī Nārāyaṇī, to my supreme majesty, which bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation, as well as the divine state beyond the three qualities (nirguṇya). || 1 ||
By what means might I have joy, and how may I become satisfied?
When I am satisfied, a divine follower shall quickly be created by me.
I shall speak in brief; listen, O Supreme Goddess, to how the protection of subjects was accomplished by whom and service was rendered by whom.
By him my worship and other honors were performed for the sake of the virtuous, and by him liberation was opened up through the teaching and proclamation of knowledge. || 4 ||
O Kamalā, I am pleased with them; I am present within the assembly of the virtuous.
O Lakṣmī, my beloved, by pleasing the virtuous, I am always pleased.
Censure of the virtuous is a great source of enmity for me;
by honoring the virtuous, I am honored myself—of this there is no doubt. (6)
The virtuous are to be constantly saluted and fed without interruption;
those holy ones are to be served, for they are my very own forms.
I am pleased with those devotees who have performed service to the virtuous;
for them, no inauspiciousness or even the slightest stain exists.
One who is ever eager should constantly worship the virtuous man, the virtuous woman, the chaste wife, and the deity;
for by him the entire world, including gods, asuras, and humans, is worshipped.
"In that form, I, the Lord, always accept worship;
this alone is my worship and no other, for I abide among virtuous and good women. (3.74.10)
Leaving aside those in whom my own foundation resides, other people— those who are best among the ignorant and full of pride— worship another in vain and with haste.
I do not accept that gift, for it does not bring me satisfaction;

My discus is indeed to be worshipped, and my two feet are always to be worshipped;

The Daityas were slain by the discus, the earth was traversed with his feet, and indeed,
the asuras were struck down through incarnations such as the Boar.
I also grant the gift of liberation to people through those of virtuous form;

For that which causes distress to the virtuous is unrighteousness; this is my view.

Whatever brings contentment to the virtuous is indeed my true wealth;

Cows, clarified butter, curd, mustard seeds, and likewise *sādhikās*—these should be touched upon rising in the morning by one who desires the destruction of sin. (24)

The finest rice-pudding (paramānna) should be given as the best food for them;

Even after performing hundreds of sacrifices, that sacrificial offering perishes;

For in this world, humans are generally full of impurities and many flaws; the piśācas enter those who have abandoned virtuous conduct and proper behavior. (3.74.40)
Those men who are devoted to the service of the virtuous, who take refuge in what is auspicious—those faithful and meritorious people, the piśācas do not enter. 41.

The virtuous Hari, as Dattātreya, bestowed the attributeless Brahman upon his disciples.

Hari also went to his own abode, the source of all happiness;

Having given land to Śāṇḍilya, Sumanyu went to my abode;

Having bestowed gifts upon the virtuous, they shall go to the supreme state;
O Lakṣmī, all your companions, the lords of creatures, having given [these gifts] to me. (68)
Those who are devoted to Nārāyaṇa have gone to my abode and shall go there;

Whether it be small or great, that which is always given out of regard for dharma, for wealth, out of fear, from desire, or out of compassion to a virtuous person, indeed conduces to liberation. (71)
For the sake of Dharma, for the sake of the heavenly world, and for the sake of happiness and fame, one should give;

Thus, one who seeks their own welfare should give to the virtuous, for it yields infinite and excellent fruit:
when misfortune occurs, when fear has arrived, and when the loss of one's possessions is imminent. (73)
One who desires no fruit should give away all one's possessions to a virtuous person;
for the sake of what is dear, one should give with desire to one who is the very embodiment of virtue.
One should give with compassion to the distressed and the poor; likewise, one should give what is most auspicious to the virtuous, to my devotee, and even to the Brahmin. 75.
Indeed, for the sake of Hari’s grace, that which bestows liberation must be given;
having reflected thus, "This must be done by me," one should offer it.
One should give this which is devoid of qualities to a virtuous person, to Nārāyaṇa, and even to me; for this belongs to Nārāyaṇa, it does not belong to me—it is devoid of qualities.
That indeed bestows infinite fruit and shall grant great bliss;
I shall give that fruit in my own abode, and I give it even here upon the earth.
I bestow upon the giver an ocean of innumerable bliss in the supreme, imperishable state;
thus, O Lakṣmī, the highest station belongs to me, who serves the virtuous.
Whatever sovereignty and other riches I possess, whether eternal or acquired in the future— whether small or very great— I bestow them all upon the abode of the Imperishable.
Śrī Nārāyaṇī said:
O Hari, O Kṛṣṇa, O Supreme Lord, show me by your grace what kind of fruit you grant for even a very small gift; have mercy upon me. (8.1)
Śrī Puruṣottama said: "Behold, Lakṣmī, this devotee, a brāhmaṇa, approaching my presence;
indeed, with a very small gift, I shall bestow upon him that which is infinite. (82)
When this was said, a brahmin named Paraśucandraka, who was miserly, approached like a wretched man,
bringing with him the entirety of his household wealth.
Deprived indeed of wife and son, he muttered the name of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa while carrying on his shoulder a small basket containing a cooking pot, a water-jar, and a sacrificial ladle.
Having tied a worn-out cloth around his waist, holding a staff in his hand, and carrying a prastha measure of rice as well as a small vessel and a cloak; ||85||
Wearing a helmet upon his head, endowed with only this much wealth—Nārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇa, Puruṣottama, Mādhava! (86)
Then, proclaiming the multitude of objects before him and grasping his feet, [the devotee said]:
"O Kṛṣṇa, you who are worthy of refuge, protect me! Grant me liberation in your state. (87)
Thus he entreated for rice;
he gave him roasted grains, and there he prostrated himself like a staff, rolling on the ground while touching his head to the ground.
Closing his eyes for a moment, he slept upon the ground before him;
I am the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, who is affectionate toward His devotees. (89)
"What shall I do for this devotee? I am the protector of those who have come for refuge. Tell me, Lakṣmī; he is dying and is giving up his life-breaths in my presence. (3.74.90)
Having said this, I placed a few grains of rice in my mouth and indeed ate them; behold the fruit of this, and I grant him the imperishable abode. ||9.1||
Just then, a celestial chariot accompanied by attendants arrived there;
that brahmin, endowed with a divine body and filled with compassion, ascended it.
The opulent celestial chariot traveled through the path of the sky toward my imperishable abode.
Behold, Lakṣmī, this palace in my abode was built by me for his sake. (93)
It has been prepared, endowed with prosperity, and provided with various kinds of food, both solid and liquid, as well as drinks;
behold all this abundant fruit offered by me with divine vision. (94)
Indeed, a celestial chariot that moves at will has been offered by me for his sake;
likewise, the infinite nectar of Brahman, along with rice and fruit, has been offered. (95)
All kinds of drinks, as well as golden garments, were indeed offered for the enjoyment of the devotee who had come for refuge. (96)
Then, beholding him, the gracious Śrī Lakṣmī rejoiced within her heart; by the will of Kṛṣṇa, the body of the brahmin sank into the lake as if it were his own. 97.
Having himself become endowed with movement, he indeed attained dissolution therein;
and Lakṣmī spoke this most wonderful thing to all of them.
All of them, beginning with Brahmapriyā, gazed indeed upon that majesty of mine, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, with their divine vision. 99.
Behold, such is my greatness; there is a great fruit for everyone, and likewise, there is the highest fruit for those who recite or even listen to this.

Thus ends the seventy-fourth chapter, titled "The Description of the Means for Pleasing Hari and the Attainment of Infinite Fruit from a Small Gift by the Miserly Brāhmaṇa Paraśucandraka," within the narration of the greatness of an eternal devotee of Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, in the third section (the Dvāpara-santāna) of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇī said:
O Kṛṣṇa, having seen this great wonder, I am indeed satisfied;
tell me further of your majesty and reveal it to me. (1)
Śrī Puruṣottama said: "Behold, O Lakṣmī, this great wonder! Fire has been born from my mouth.
When he had spoken thus, fire arose and spread throughout the forest on all sides.
Enveloped in garlands of flames, he consumed the tiger-forest in an instant—
along with its trees, its grass, and its abundance of sprouts, creepers, crops, and the like.
Having thus completely consumed the forest, along with its multitudes of flocks of birds, its beasts of prey, and its reptiles, the fire of great flames [subsided].
Then he arrived before Hari in embodied form like a disciple;
he bowed at Hari's feet and indeed vanished from sight.
Then, seeing the forest completely consumed by fire, I, Hari,
restored it to its natural state with my gentle glances.
In that very same way, the forest once again became filled with flowering creepers and trees,
resounded with flocks of birds, and teeming with beasts of prey and reptiles.
"Behold, Lakṣmī, how it has become as it was before, exactly as it stood.
Having seen this marvel, Lakṣmī questioned her beloved Nārāyaṇa. (8)
"Who is this fire, O Kṛṣṇa, and how does it abide within you always?
Having heard this, Nārāyaṇa said: "Listen, for this is indeed my own splendor. (9)
Indeed, that which consists of Saṃkarṣaṇa exists in many forms within the material body;
likewise, it also consists of Rudra and consists of Śaṃkara as well.
That indeed is the nature of Mahākāla, the performer of universal withdrawal;
and my entire form of sovereignty exists within me at all times.
Whenever the dissolutions of the world-dwellers occur,
then this very sovereignty of mine proceeds throughout the creations.
I indeed withdraw that entire [universe] by that very same means;
and I create it again through my power, exactly as it was fashioned by conceptualization.
I possess the sovereignty of creation, by which this forest was created again;
you ladies, being of the nature of Brahman, were created by me from my own portion.
Indeed, this entire world was created by me in such a way from a portion of myself,
through my engagement in worldly conduct and through my service to the virtuous.
The fire of Time does not burn me, who am engaged in chanting [the Lord's names].
Behold this Lomaśa; leave him behind and likewise leave that hermitage.
Just as fire, having left the hermitages of the sages, does not pervade those very hermitages,
so too am I unable to bring about any misfortune for those who are devoted to my devotees.
For those people who worship me, time does not exist;
for them, illusion does not exist, nor does any agitation exist.
For them, indeed, there are no three-fold torments, nor does suffering exist for them;
I consume all their hardships, of this there is no doubt. 19.
I alone am the death of death; I give life to those who have taken refuge in me. I indeed command Time itself to grant eternal enjoyments to my devotee.
"Do not ever withdraw [your grace], and never let them encounter old age"—in this way, I always remain for the protection of my devotees. (21)
Thus, O Lakṣmī, this power and my dignity have been shown;
my greatness and the great strength of my devotee have been demonstrated to you. 22.
Non-violence, truthful speech, compassion toward all beings, religious observance, charity, and tranquility—these indeed are the dharmas rooted in devotion. ||23||
Indeed, even fasting becomes effective through devotion alone;
and celibacy likewise becomes effective toward me through devotion alone. (24)
The Vedic vow, the fire-ritual, the fulfillment of the teacher's service, and self-study—these are the duties that, once mastered, bring about devotion. ||25||

I am devoted to the practice of hospitality toward guests, and my food consists of what remains after being graciously offered; I eat only after my dependents have eaten, and I share the same conduct as they do. (26)
Only for the householder couple is there the offering of food to the gods;
likewise, constant service to the virtuous is the purpose for those who practice devotion. (27)
Protection, charity, diligence, sacrifice, and likewise sustenance, as well as service to one's father and service to one's master—these are the goals attained by those who practice devotion. (28)

Tending cattle and the like, performing the Agnihotra sacrifice, walking the path of the righteous, renunciation, self-restraint, and hospitality—these are the goals attained by those who practice devotion. (29)

Service, virtuous conduct, humility, and the state of being a servant or the like—whether as a female or male slave—are the ways for those who practice devotion; their purpose is already understood. (3.75.30)
The virtuous, who are indeed the essence of the world and preceded by Sanatkumāra, were created of old by the Creator in this world for the sake of the welfare of the world. (31)
O Lakṣmī, I have created many virtuous and devoted people here in this world who make known my greatness. (32)
Indeed, on this earth, the deities are capable of delivering all the worlds;
these are the knowledge of Brahman, devotion, my stories, meditation, and the festival. (33)
This group of six activities—bestowing my mantra, the protection of those who have come for refuge, liberation, and the destruction of sin—is always [the duty] of the virtuous. (34)

Devotion, charity, the practice of Brahman, the five duties of the virtuous, scholarship, adherence to the scriptures, self-study, silent recitation, and sacred learning—[these constitute the path]. (35)
Indeed, this group of six—proper conduct, tranquility, cessation [of worldly activity], affection for the virtuous, and hospitality—is natural to the good. (36)

Constant remembrance of Hari is the abiding in Brahman; it is the great virtue of the virtuous, characterized by freedom from pride, anger, and the like, and by affectionate speech and inner composure. (37)
Delighting in guests, eating only what remains after others have been served, forgiveness, contentment, and satisfaction—these virtues of the virtuous are innate. (38)
Service to the elders, to cows, and to Hari who dwells in the day;
abstention from delicious things—this dharma leads to liberation. 39.
The liberation from the bonds of hope, inward reflection free from attachment, the state of being devoid of the fetters of affection, and the surrendering of the self to the Self. (3.75.40)
The virtuous one who wanders as a mendicant through actions seen from the perspective of liberation indeed roams everywhere liberated; he should always remain steadfast in me. 41.
This is the dharma of those who know liberation for one who practices devotion;
there is nothing higher than devotion for one who upholds the dharma of eternal bliss. (42)
The state of liberation—free from suffering, supreme bliss, ageless, immortal, and immutable—belongs to the virtuous one who practices devotion, and it exists together with him. 43.
Devoted to devotion, compassion, and righteousness, their sins burnt away by austerity, they attain equality with the gods and illuminate the three worlds. 44.
Peaceful, virtuous, and auspicious, they move through my world as bearers of the discus;
wearing garlands and bearing the discus, they destroy the sins of the wicked upon the earth. (45)

Those who perform devotion wear a necklace upon their necks, hold a garland in their hands, bear my image in their hearts, apply the sectarian mark upon their foreheads, and maintain virtuous conduct throughout their bodies. (46)
In their minds they are bearers of forbearance; in their disposition they are sustainers of affection, with conduct rooted in love;
in their intellect they are lovers of liberation; and in their very self, they are always sustainers of Brahman. 47.

They possess affection for those who depend on them, they are steadfast in their wisdom regarding discernment, they maintain the savor of my teachings, and they maintain equanimity toward all living beings. (48)

Free from attachment to objects of enjoyment, like those who possess only the bare necessities for their journey, they have attained identity with me; clad in the sky as their garment, they are purifiers of the world.
Devoted to the path of worship, always fostering the company of the virtuous, and ever content with those who have sought refuge in them, the holy ones are the ornaments of the righteous.
O Lakṣmī, by relying upon these, the means to liberation have been fully realized;
for those who abide in the sacred abodes, nothing further remains to be done through their coming together.
The dharma of the sages and the dharma of the virtuous consist in constant delight in truth and moral conduct;
one should be neither arrogant nor conceited, neither displeased nor filled with wonder.
He is always intent on worshipping the ancestors and gods at night while it is day, considers himself awake while he is actually asleep, and thinks himself inferior to his most excellent guru. (53)
One who considers darkness to be light, the most excellent flavor to be something vile, great prosperity to be laughter, and pride to be dejection; 54.
Regarding prosperity as calamity, regarding life as death, regarding dharma as the association with Hari, and regarding delight within the heart as [the goal]. (55)
Thinking himself superior among the devoted, thinking himself superior among people in the forests and other places,
and thinking himself superior in the lineage of Acyuta, the virtuous man indeed delivers others.
O Lakṣmī, the virtuous man is considered a savior, and the virtuous woman is likewise regarded as a savior.
For me, there is no price for renunciation; indeed, in my house, the price is devotion.
I always worship the feet of the virtuous who possess devotion;
I also bestow honor upon devoted women. (58)
Then indeed there will be devotion toward me, when there is cessation from everything else;
when there is delight in tranquility, sleep in me, and even the playfulness of my sport is in me.
Those sages are virtuous, and those female sages are likewise;
they are completely immersed in the flood of the mass of bliss born from my devotion.
In my abodes throughout the lands, in rivers and mountain cascades, in the groves along flowing streams, and upon the mountains and in the forests; ||6.1||
My virtuous yogins dwell in the abodes of devotees;
they are devoted to the practice of yoga and likewise sleep upon the open sky as their bed.
Constantly feeding on what they find clinging to trees, always having the forest as their retinue,
clothed in rags and bark, they are solely devoted to me.
Established in goodness and having renounced everything, they dwell happily without obstacle alongside the hosts of virtuous gods, being initiated into me, Mādhava.
Men and women who are of such virtuous conduct, possessed of good character, and who take refuge in Me—these indeed are dear to Me; for them, there are eternal worlds. (65)
Those who, having abandoned evil while remaining [in the world], perform virtuous deeds with devotion,
even they indeed attain the state of the righteous.
Abiding by the dharma of those most devoted to Brahman, one attains the state of a Brāhmaṇa;
whoever, through my yoga, goes to the state of becoming Brahman.
The forest, which is the ultimate state of the inner self, is resorted to by the virtuous who desire Brahman; and I am Nārāyaṇa, the eternal abode for the righteous within me.
The forest is the guru, and likewise, awakening is the guru; dwelling with the virtuous is always my abode.
My fire-offering is the food offering, and I, Śrī Narāyaṇa, am the sacrifice itself.
I am the four-monthly sacrifice of the virtuous, and I am always the vows of the virtuous;
those who possess such conduct are indeed the righteous ones, adorned by righteousness.
Freed from all sins, those virtuous ones move within me; being saintly and ever-abiding on the true path, they attain the supreme goal. ||7 1||
O Lakṣmī, the perfected sages who take refuge at my feet go to the Brahma-world, which is of great merit, possessed of divine power, and most eternal. (72)
The virtuous, who are themselves fearless and adorned with goodness, constantly bestow the gift of fearlessness here, being ever intent on devotion and spiritual attainment.
They have compassion for all beings, they observe the vow of straightforwardness toward all beings, they have become the very self of all beings—these are the virtuous ones, adorned with virtue. (74)
Those for whom there is bathing in all the Vedas, beholding all beings as themselves, and equanimity toward all souls—they are the virtuous, adorned with goodness. (75)
Straightforwardness is indeed the dharma of the virtuous, for crookedness is unrighteousness;
through straightforwardness, the deities of the world become accessible.

Free from deceit, with a heart devoted [to the Buddha], having taken refuge in the true path out of love, and being supremely dedicated to virtuous conduct, the awakened one is fit for becoming Brahman. //77//
Listen, Lakṣmī: even if one performs virtuous deeds while abandoning me, their fruit in this world will indeed be perishable, for it exists without devotion. (78)
By means of the vows of fasting, they go to the supreme world of the Gandharvas;
indeed, one who sleeps in water like a frog goes to the world of the Nāgas.
One who feeds on young grass, leaves, and the like goes to Amarāvatī;
one who feeds on moss and leaves attains the world of Varuṇa.
One who subsists on fruits, roots, and air goes to the world of the Yakṣas;
a king devoted to the austerity of fire becomes a lord of life. ||81||
The king who delights in fasting rejoices in heaven in the celestial realm;
by casting his body into water or the ocean, he attains the world of Varuṇa.
Having pierced his feet with a stone, he dies and becomes a Guhyaka;
having cast off his body in fire, he is born in the world of Vahni.
Having gone to the world by way of the heroic mode (vīrarīti), he who is empowered finds himself rejoicing with the gods and others in a celestial chariot that moves at will. ||84||
Having received initiation from a yogin, he goes to the world of Rudra;
and by giving gifts of wealth, he reaches the abode of Kubera.
Having given gifts of gold, he goes to the world of the Sun;
and having given gifts of beverages, he goes to the world of the Moon. (86)
Having given gifts of clothing, he goes to the worlds of the planets;
having given gifts of maidens in marriage, he attains the world of the Apsarases. ||87||
Having given gifts of vehicles here, one goes to a celestial mansion;
having given gifts of food here, he goes to the world of the ancestors.
Having bestowed gifts of sacred knowledge here, he goes to Satyaloka;
indeed, by bestowing sovereignty and other such boons, he goes to the abodes of the lords.
Through devotion and the gift of all one's possessions, he goes to my world;
if he remembers me there, he proceeds otherwise, to the realm of light.
Through devotion to me, this very state of Vairāja becomes my own state;
all those gifts are offered to me there, within the inner self.
If one gives with devotion after recollecting [Me], I lead them to the eternal Brahman;
such is My majesty, O Lakṣmī, which is accessible through mere contemplation.
I am the devourer of meditative cultivation, bound by the threads of meditative cultivation;
and by means of the leaf of the form of meditative cultivation, I stand in close proximity.
The virtuous are saintly, rich in contemplation, and therefore their forms consist of me; they follow my conduct, they are my very bodies, and they are always the saviors of sinners.
Between them and me, in the application toward all goals, there is not even an atom’s worth of difference.
They are I, and I am they; this, O Hārda, has been told to you by me. (95)
All of you ladies are devoted to me; you are all women beloved by Brahmā.
You are indeed virtuous, ever-present here, auspicious ferrymen who bestow liberation. 96.
Indeed, your dwelling here is that very same imperishable abode;
your presence is eternal association with the virtuous.
Service to you is the supreme service to one's own self; the sight and other forms of contact with you always bestow auspicious liberation. 98.
Through my yoga, all your actions shall be designated as Brahman;
indeed, your bodies shall possess the Supreme Person.
I, Śrī Puruṣottama, am the entire possession of you all;
therefore, you are in every way the beloveds of Śrī Puruṣottama.
I have not the slightest difference from you, both in this world and in the next;
you are I and I am you—everything has been made by me into "you. (10.1)
Thinking thus, when another woman becomes endowed with devotion to me,
then she shall indeed attain equality with you.
From reciting this, from hearing it, and even from hearing about this knowledge,
the arising of the state of a virtuous wife occurs, and she attains the status of a beloved of Brahman.
Through devotion, one becomes equal to Rādhā and Lakṣmī; of this there is no doubt.
Through devotion, one becomes equal to Brahmā and the liberated souls; of this there is no doubt.

Thus ends the seventy-fifth chapter, titled "The Manifestation and Disappearance of Fire, the Prowess of the Holy Man, the Attainment of Various Fruits, and My Own Attainment through Association with the Holy Man," in the Third Section on the Lineage of the Dvāpara Age within the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
Listen, O Śrī Nārāyaṇī, to my greatness which is even greater than yours;
for I dwell among children who are free from sin, yet are without protectors.
The heart of children is pure, free from the crookedness of illusion;
in this state, devoid of latent impressions and the like, I dwell like a holy man. (2)
All children are my forms, as clear as a mirror;
therefore, children are in the state of Brahman, while people are in the state of yoga.
And my forms are young boys and girls up to eight years of age;
all these are indeed holy beings, just like Sanaka and the others of old.
The virtuous ones possess the dharma of the good; in youth, they possess the dharma of householders;
but those who are free from the state of youth are the virtuous celibates.
Virtue consists in the practice of moral conduct while remaining in the state of a householder through attachment to sensual desires;
for indeed, even for one who possesses desire, virtue arises when those desires are conquered.

Even for those who have no desire for sexual enjoyment, that very state of household life exists for the sake of desire; yet, neither union with a woman nor union with a man should be considered the defining cause of the householder's life.
The practice of sexual union, the state of householdership, and the excellence that depends upon it—
these exist in both woman and man when there is a disposition free from desire.
One who is free from desire, yet truly desirous, is born possessing all desires;
he alone is to be known as Brahman, endowed with the true nature of a Brāhmaṇa and goodness.
The state of being most devoted to Brahman is difficult to attain, O Śrī, and likewise, goodness is difficult to attain;
yet through my grace, both devotion to Brahman and goodness surely come to pass.
By my grace, this auspicious state of being a virtuous wife arises, which bestows liberation and effects the upliftment of one's lineage, just as it has in you.
Virtuous women devoted to truth and dharma, as well as holy men intent on Brahman, content with whatever comes by chance and free from forceful ostentation; || 1-2 ||
They enjoy wealth obtained through righteousness, offer it to the Supreme Lord, are free from obstinacy, possess pure hearts, are virtuous, and are adorned by goodness. (1.3)
By means of virtues, actions, and austerities, a man becomes as glorious as Nārāyaṇa; having completely cast off impurity, even a lowly person becomes most exalted.
Just as a Śūdra in another birth, having accumulated merit through his actions, is born as a Brāhmaṇa in a subsequent birth due to the conjunction of his virtue. || 15 ||
Likewise, even within a single lifetime, a Brāhmaṇa may become a non-Brāhmaṇa through violations of Vedic conduct,
and even a learned man (vipra) may descend to the status of a Śūdra.
The power of merit and demerit arising from attachment to auspicious and inauspicious actions is indeed great;
yet the Brahmin, who is preeminent among beings, can truly overturn those very dharmas. 17.
One in whom rajas predominates becomes a king; one in whom tamas predominates becomes a śūdra;
and one touched by both sattva and rajas becomes a splendid vaiśya. || 18 ||
Touched by both rajas and tamas, a Vaiśya becomes ignoble;
but one in whom tamas alone predominates becomes a murderer or a dog-eater (outcaste).
A Brahmin who abounds in the quality of sattva becomes a virtuous woman;
one who abounds in the yoga of Brahman indeed becomes liberated on this earth.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, this excellence which brings auspiciousness has been described;
even Nārāyaṇa himself becomes intent on yoga here.
Through union with that [power], others likewise become Nārāyaṇas;
thus, by my yoga, there is a succession of Nārāyaṇas. (22)
By my power alone, through the attainment of sovereignty and other such qualities, all men become Nārāyaṇas, and likewise all women become Nārāyaṇīs. (23)
Through worship, they are born from me alone, the Supreme Self;
the Vasus, Rudras, and likewise the Viṣṇus are born. ||24||
Through worship, O Rame, Brahmās and Īśvaras are born, as well as Īśvarīs;
they are all born through my worship.
Those who are free from passion are liberated from actions and the bonds of karma;
and by those very actions, when properly performed, they become Nārāyaṇas.
Indeed, all those actions consist of my worship;
for without worship of me, there is truly no performance of sacrifice.
Worship performed by those with desires shall fulfill their longings;
for those free from desire, I, when remembered, am truly the bestower of prosperity by my very nature.
Indeed, the devoted one who worships me through action, mind, and speech does not incur bondage even when performing what is beneficial for others. (29)

Those practitioners of ethical discipline who have desisted from taking life for the sake of sustaining their own existence, who are equal toward both the hateful and the dear, and who are self-controlled, are liberated from the bonds of karma. (3.76.30)
Those who possess compassion for all beings, who are trustworthy to all embodied beings, and who have performed the practice of devotion—such people go to the divine abode. 3.1
Those people who are devoid of self-interest, who assist others in their undertakings, who are free from expectations,
and who are content with what is obtained through righteousness, go to the celestial abode.
They look upon groups of women as they would their mother’s sisters or daughters;
they look upon groups of men as they would their father, mother, or good sons. (33)
Those people who are enriched by serving the virtuous as described, who are devoted to me, who are free from theft, and whose lives are sustained by good fortune, go to my abode. (34)
Those who delight in their own enjoyments, who pursue dharma at the proper time, who long for refined pleasures, and who are endowed with the splendor of heart and eyes; ||35||
Those who follow the path of Indra, who have established themselves through mastery over the senses, and who have made their dwelling in devotion to me—those people go to my abode. (36)
The path created by Akaṣāya consists of charity, righteousness, and austerity;
it is rich in ethical conduct, purity, and compassion, and is endowed with devotion, service, and self-surrender. ||37||

The state of being gracious through the granting of blessings, which increases the fruits of association with the virtuous and is enriched by the excellence of a pure intellect, should always be cultivated by the wise. 38.
Whether for their own sake or for the sake of others, or even out of playful jest, those who are free from false speech proceed upon the excellent path that is devoid of the defilements. (39)
Those people who speak untruth for the sake of their livelihood, for the sake of dharma, or out of personal whim, indeed go upon the straight path free from passion.
Those who speak sweet words that are free from harshness, devoid of even a trace of sin, and full of heartfelt affection, proceed upon the path of the virtuous which is free from all impurities. (41)

Those who delight in freedom from backbiting, who act to prevent the alienation of friends, who are free from malice and possess truth and friendliness, proceed along the excellent path that is free from passion.
Free from deceit, gentle in speech, and devoid of any trace of anger,
those who are free from the desire to tear at the hearts of others proceed upon the true path that is untainted by passions.
O Lakṣmī, virtuous men who speak beneficial words with gentleness, who possess the quality of truth, and who take refuge in Hari, proceed along the true path free from all impurities. 44.
Those who do not desire even in their minds the wealth of others, whether it be left behind or encountered in a secluded place, proceed along the true path free from defilements.
Those who do not desire anything belonging to others, whether in a village or even in their own home,
and who have no enemies, proceed upon the true path free from all impurities.
Those who are learned in the scriptures, full of devotion, protectors of truth and compassion,
eternally contented, and free from passion— they proceed upon the true path that is free from all impurities.

Those who delight in a mind of loving-kindness, who are characterized by faith, affection, and gratitude, and who understand the ripening of karmic fruits, proceed upon the true path free from defilement. (48)
Those who hold to what is right, whose nature is heavenward, who are devoted to exertion, established in the self, and intent on me—they proceed along the path of the stainless truth. 49.

Those of great wisdom who are devoted to Brahman, who cultivate knowledge and discernment, and who are intent upon the treatises of logic, proceed along the true path that is free from all impurities.
Those who are possessed by a dread of sin, intent upon the means of attaining the highest good, and desirous of discharging their debt, proceed along the path of the stainless and the virtuous. (51)
But those who belong to the pure class, who avoid self-harm, who cause no terror to living beings, and who bestow the gift of fearlessness; 52.
Possessing an affection for themselves like that for a deity, they are auspicious and easy to serve;
following divine conduct and gentle in disposition, they proceed upon the stainless path of the virtuous. (53)
Those who are well-behaved, performers of virtuous deeds, and free from malice toward living beings,
become long-lived in this world and proceed along the stainless path of the righteous.

He was a giver to the virtuous and a respectful host to the good; he bestowed food, drink, and edibles upon the poor, the afflicted, and the destitute, and he was a donor of garments and other gifts. ||55||
One who has made his dwelling in the yoga of devotion, who bestows the gift of knowledge, and who protects those who have come for refuge, proceeds along the stainless path of the virtuous. (56)
One should construct shelters, assembly halls, wells, lotus ponds, and water-stations;
[one should provide] a seat, a bed, a vehicle, a house, jewels, wealth, and a [generous] mind. (57)
All kinds of grain, cows, fields, and maidens—whosoever, with a joyful mind, bestows these as gifts upon a worthy recipient; //58//
Indeed, one who offers all his possessions goes upon the stainless, true path;
likewise, one who honors deities, the twice-born, the virtuous, and faithful wives.
He was one who paid homage and was humble, doing what was pleasing to all, pure,
beneficial to everyone, pleasant-faced, and devoted to performing honors according to what was appropriate.
Beholding the true path and honoring the guru, he proceeds along the stainless, virtuous way;
esteemed by all beings, he is saluted by the entire world. (61)
Born of a noble family and of noble lineage, possessing a vision of loving-kindness, equal toward his father, and trustworthy among all living beings. (62)
The one possessed of devotion to me, being greatly meritorious, proceeds along the path of the truly stainless;
such a person, O Lakṣmī, always prospers in unimpeded happiness.
This is the supreme path of the virtuous, wherein no affliction exists;
it belongs indeed to the holy ones who know the Vedas, the perfected ones, and likewise those endowed with devotion.
For those who, endowed with devotion, always cultivate [virtue] and avoid that which is inauspicious,
there is a path rich in eternal happiness that leads to the state of Brahman.
O Lakṣmī, through the conjunctions of these, auspicious things indeed come to pass:
all forms of excellence and countless heavenly realms. (66)
Indeed, those who abide in the dharma of the virtuous proceed correctly in this matter;
for the sake of the welfare of men, I have proclaimed this to you here.
One who abides in discernment knows within oneself one's own true welfare;
yet, without taking refuge in a true guru, one is unable to accomplish that which is supreme.
O beloved, human beings always desire to acquire merit;
yet, despite possessing great wealth, these fools do not perform the causes of merit.
From association with the virtuous, from my own company, and from the company of saintly women, the highest auspiciousness arises;
indeed, supreme welfare surely comes to pass, and you know this to be so.
Nevertheless, the rivers of logic are constantly afflicted by the torments of evil and have entered the mouths of the great,
wicked crocodiles of conceit.
They do not serve the virtuous nor do they honor me;
being excessively attached to sense-objects, they fall into hells and other such realms.
Those who are evil and corrupt, the nihilists, those devoid of generosity, those empty of virtuous intent, and the malicious do not cross the enchanting river of illusion. (73)
Devoid of the spirit of devotion and lacking divine sentiment,
they are constantly possessed of wicked dispositions and always maintain a focus on the physical body.
Delighting in base actions, devoted solely to their own self-interest,
they are satisfied with the belly and the senses, their vision fixed upon external pleasures.
Those who delight solely in what is non-self go only to hell;
whereas those servants who delight in the self alone and delight in the virtuous Dharma [attain liberation]. //76//
O Lakṣmī, those who carry out the commands [of the Lord] proceed along the stainless path—be they members of the castes or stages of life, and whoever they may be, whether men or women. (77)
Those women—whether brides, daughters, maidens, or mistresses accompanied by their sons—who possess the good fortune of receiving blessings from the elders, go indeed to heaven. (78)
Whether they be childless, or elders standing to receive blessings, or even prominent kings, or servants living in misery, they all go to that world. (79)

Whether they possess worldly attachments or are free from them, those who constantly serve their elders—being upright and having humility as their essence—go to heaven; of this there is no doubt. (3.76.80)
Those servants in this world who possess fame and share in heaven shall go to the higher state by virtue of my grace. (81)
Those of virtuous character, noble conduct, and patience, who likewise serve others and grant happiness through their service, go to my state when they depart for the celestial realm. (82)
Those in whose mouths is the name of Hari, in whose hearts is Śrī Hari himself, and who follow the words of the elders—they indeed take refuge at my feet. (83)
Those who give garments, food, and drink, as well as gardens, fields, and palaces, and those who give waistbands, thighs, and ornaments, go to my abode when they depart for heaven. (84)
I gave a cow to a Brahmin, a daughter to a youth, and a son to a virtuous man;
a garden to a deity, a field to me, and a mansion to a householder-yogi. (85)
Having given their hips to the weary, strength to the frightened, their thighs to the distressed, and their lap along with their wealth to the poor, people go to heaven. (86)
Then, having attained devotion toward me and offering everything to me,
those very same virtuous ones go to my abode, which rests upon the lotus.
Those who give hair, lips, cheeks, and teeth; those who give the chest, the back, and the hands; and those who give the neck, the shanks, and the feet, go to heaven and to my own abode. (88)
Having offered their hair to Brahmā, Īśa, and Viṣṇu, those who have taken refuge in saṃnyāsa—my devotees—go from heaven to the immortal state. (89)

Having received the sacred syllables (oṃ) and the initiation mantras, those devoted to me who have taken refuge at the feet of the preceptor go from there to heaven and then to the imperishable abode.
Having bestowed upon me those two cheeks—the affectionate and tender states of heart characterized by devotion—my devotees attain prosperity, and from that, they go to the imperishable state. 9.1.
Having even granted me his chest and having placed it upon me,
one who is thus confident indeed goes to heaven, and from there to my imperishable state.
Having first offered their backs as assistance for the auspicious attainment of the next world, they go to heaven; thereafter, through devotion, they proceed to my supreme abode.
Having performed service and servitude, and having offered everything to me, he goes to heaven; thereafter, through devotion, he proceeds to my abode.
Having given me his neck, or even his entire possessions, or else the gift of life,
or the gift of his vital breath, he goes from here to heaven and then to the imperishable state.
Having given both his calves and his entire family to me, he indeed departs for heaven;
then, having surrendered everything, he proceeds to my abode. (96)
He who gives feet, wealth, and a livelihood to the Great-Souled One goes to heaven through his devotion to me and proceeds to the imperishable abode. (97)
