"O wise one, having abandoned your discernment, why do you fear a woman so?
This Lalitā has been discovered by my spies to be devoid of strength. (59)
"Having created a multitude of women through her illusory power (māyā) and brought them forth, she has arrived;
indeed, I have no fear of her, so seize her and bring her before me."
By whom can Bhaṇḍa, whose greatness is unsurpassed in the three worlds, be conquered?
By me the gods have been so severely punished that they are not even able to breathe.
They dwell indeed hidden in the netherworld, in the ocean, and in deep caverns;
these foolish women, whose daring is in vain, do not know [this]. (62)
For those who are arrogant because they have performed no meritorious deeds surely pursue their own destruction;
or else, it may be that the gods come here having placed them at their head. (63)
"Even if Śambhu and all the others were to join together, I am capable of crushing them—Malaka, Kuraṇḍa, Karaṭaka, and Balāhaka. (64)
Vikaṭa, Karkaṭaka, Humbaka, Halamalluca, Karkaśa, Kukkura, Jṛmbhaṇa, and likewise Ghoṣaka. ||65||
Śirālaka, Kūpaka, Laḍuna, Māraka, Viṣeṇa, Parūṣa, Draghaṇa, and likewise Kollaṭa. ||66||
Dāsera, Mūṣaka, Mahāṇḍa, and Kubhāṇḍaka—
these were the Daityas, headed by Hiraṇyākṣa and Hiraṇyakaśipu.
In their presence, thousands of akṣauhiṇī armies would be reduced to ashes;
yet the playful illusions of women would appear as mere trifles on the field of battle.
Therefore, let them seize her by her mass of hair and bring her before me;
and let all the others seize each their own respective prey as it falls to them.
"Kuṭilākṣa, arise! Equip the army on all sides!"—thus he addressed the commander of the host, the lord of three thousand troops.
Bhaṇḍa went to the inner apartments to inform the crooked-eyed Mahāsattva;
then the Dānavas, making a great clamor, prepared their armor.
With spears, mallets, bhiṃdipālas, bhiṇḍipālakas, druhaṇas, bhūśuṇḍīs, axes, and even clubs.
With maces and *śataghnīs*, with three-pointed arrows and shafts as well, with half-moons and great discuses, and with bows and those bearing the *śārṅga* bow; ||73||
With clubs, sling-weapons, thunderbolt-arrows, excellent stones, daggers, fangs of serpents, shafts, and likewise with discus-fragments; ||74||
Armed with nooses, maces, fire-balls, and swords—
with such weapons as these, the Daityas went forth, fully prepared.
Tens of millions of Daityas, clad in armor with their own hands bound with straps,
were mounted on horses, elephants, and even donkeys.
They were riders of camels, riders of wolves, and likewise riders of dogs;
they were riders of crows, riders of vultures, and riders of tigers and other beasts. (77)
Some were mounted on lions, some on śarabhas, and likewise some on rhinoceroses; some were mounted on boars, some on serpents, and others had ghosts as their vehicles.
Those traveling in vehicles and celestial chariots also set out toward Lalitā,
as well as the crooked leader of the army, the Dānava Durmada.
Accompanied by ten akṣauhiṇīs,
Kuṭilākṣa, Tālajaṅgha, Tālabhuja, and Tālakaṭi were sent against Lalitā.
These formidable forces, accompanied by forty akṣauhiṇīs, indeed guarded the four gates of Bhaṇḍapura itself and remained stationed there. ||81||
Viśukra stationed one akṣauhiṇī of his own forces around his palace and dispatched the messenger Kapiśīrṣaka.
At the command of King Bhaṇḍāsura, he went quickly and announced:
"O beautiful one, become the wife of the great king Bhaṇḍa! (83)
"Otherwise, your death will surely come; do as you wish, O beautiful lady.
Having heard this from Mahālakṣmī, Durgā, the beloved of Hara, replied:
Abandon your jesting, you base one; go quickly to the netherworld!
Otherwise, your destruction here will be brought about by a woman. (85)
The messenger spoke those words exactly as they were; Bhaṇḍa, while Viśukra was listening, immediately replied in a state of great wrath.
Then Bhaṇḍāsura gave the command for battle to those generals and all the Daityas who were exultant in combat.
Uttering shouts of "kilakila," thousands of warriors,
intoxicated with the frenzy of battle, fell upon Lalitā’s army from all sides.
"Kill! Slay! Destroy! they cried out;
with their swords brandished, they fell into that great ocean of women. (89)
Then the goddesses, too, with their uplifted weapons, fought against the Dānavas;
with their unhindered arms, the goddesses crushed the army of the Dānavas.
The earth became crimson with the blood of the Dānavas being struck down by the Śaktis; heaps of the severed heads of the Daityas fell [upon it]. (9.1)
Here and there, the Dānavas were pierced by missiles and weapons and fell dead;
meanwhile, showers of arrows continued to fall in the battle.
The sky became completely covered and dense with arrows on all sides;
Durgā released fire and set ablaze that mass of shafts.
The fire, augmented by the power of Hariṇī, consumed the Daityas;
Durmada died there, and Viśukra too was torn apart.
All the guards of the rampart were struck down with divine weapons, as were the forty guardians of the gate-towers at that time. (95)
Those entire akṣauhiṇī divisions, separated from the armies of Lakṣmī,
were precisely the forces intended for the protection of Bhaṇḍāsura’s palace.
That army consisting of ten akṣauhiṇīs was destroyed by the goddesses;
Bhaṇḍa’s city became like a void, resembling the abode of hungry ghosts.
All the leaders of the army have been destroyed because of Bhaṇḍa;
this is something that could not even be imagined in a dream, nor had it ever been heard of before.
And that calamity which had not been suspected by the Daityas then arrived;
having reflected thus, he dispatched a hundred akṣauhiṇīs.
Day and night, a great battle, incited by the power of weapons and missiles,
raged against the Asuras for the sake of the divine women who were the embodiments of Fortune.
And in a single day, a hundred akṣauhiṇīs fell;
the entire city was shattered and drenched in blood.
Then Bhaṇḍa prepared an army of three hundred akṣauhiṇīs and dispatched the entire host of goddesses to destroy them.
Then, beholding that army of sixty crores belonging to the goddess Lalitā, he became enraged and rushed forward, intent on making it free of demons.
They hold nooses, maces, and discs, and carry spears;
they wield clubs, battle-axes, bows, and tridents.
As if drinking up the ocean of the Daityas, they indeed gathered by the millions;
untouched by the weapons of others, those divine beings pierced the Asuras.
The two armies entered into each other's interior and became helpless; indeed, those two oceans of troops attained a state of total confusion.
Those three hundred akṣauhiṇī divisions were indeed cut down by the goddesses;
by the grace of Mahālakṣmī, the women themselves were not pierced at all.
No blows were even inflicted, nor did weapons touch them;
victory belonged to Mahālakṣmī, while Bhaṇḍa indeed grieved at that time.
"How might victory be mine? How might I remain alive?
Thus he thought again and again as he had entered the cavity in the earth.
Then Bhaṇḍaka indeed remembered the Kaikasas, the sons of Diti,
who had previously obtained a boon from the Sun and were capable of victory in a great battle.

Thus ends the one hundred and sixteenth chapter, titled "The Description of Mahālakṣmī’s Armies Setting Out for the Destruction of Bhaṇḍa, the Counsel of Bhaṇḍāsura, the Annihilation of Bhaṇḍa’s Forces, and Bhaṇḍa’s Remembrance of Kaikasā and Others," in the third section, the Dvāpara Cycle, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇī-Śrī said: How did the Daityas named Kaikasas formerly obtain a boon, by virtue of which they might achieve victory in the world even in battle against Nārāyaṇī?
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
Listen, O Lakṣmī, I shall tell you that nowhere else does victory exist apart from Nārāyaṇī; at the end, one who has taken refuge in Hari attains victory, and no other.
But for those who have properly prepared themselves through austerity, O Lakṣmī, in the great battle victory appears for a moment as the cause of destruction.
The seven brothers, the sons of Kaikasa, first performed austerities for a hundred years without water, directed toward the Sun-god.
When the sun had risen, they became almost withered; he then spoke to the sons of Kaikasī: "By your ascetic power now... (5)
"I am well-pleased; may prosperity be yours! Choose a boon, O Dānavas.
Thus addressed, they chose this boon: "Whoever is our enemy in combat..."
Then, whether they be women, men, humans, gods, or others born of Brahmā’s creation—
even animals— their eyes shall indeed gaze [upon him].
O Sun, you must certainly remain within our eyes to blind us,
while you burn our adversaries with your terrible splendors.
Likewise, let every object of the eye then become motionless;
let those enemies, deprived of the power of sight, fall into blindness. (9)
"Those whose weapons have become stiff and who are motionless must be slain, and thus victory shall be ours.
When addressed thus, Ravi said to the Kaikasas, "So be it."
He said, "When I see Adharma, I shall go to his abode;
I will undoubtedly be your ally in the battle of Dharma. || 11 ||
Thus addressed by Kaikasā, those who considered themselves victorious through Śrī,
having been urged by Bhaṇḍa for the sake of victory through the power of the Sun, arrived there.
By the very power of the boon they had received, they moved about in battle, arrogant with pride;
then, they were gazed upon by those [enemies] whose eyes were possessed by the sun.
The deities, their eyes fixed and their enthusiasm rendered fruitless, were overcome by the defect of blindness; their powers remained silent.
The Daityas crushed the army of Śakti with unrighteous combatants;
the Lakṣmīs were rendered motionless, paralyzed, blind, and deprived of their functions.
They were unable to see that battle, which was not worthy of one born of dharma;
for an enemy who has laid down his weapons or is defenseless must not be slain in combat.
One who drinks [the Soma], one who is fleeing, one who has fallen, one who is bound, or one who has come for refuge—
indeed, unrighteousness oppresses those who employ weapons against such persons.
The Kaikaseyas struck the virtuous goddesses with arrows and other weapons, irresistible [to them];
at that time, their limbs were touched by the floods of the Daityas' missiles.
Then, raising a cry of "Alas! Alas!", they remembered Laliteśvarī;
at that moment, Lalitāśrī quickly spoke to Sūrya regarding his unrighteousness.
"Behold this unrighteousness, O Sūrya: the striking of warriors who are not fighting, perpetrated by the Daityas; why do you stand indifferent toward your enemies? (3.117.20)
Out of fear of the curse, the Sun indeed departed from the eyes of the Daityas;
then the Śaktis, their blindness gone, fought with great speed.
Roaring with lion-like cries, they discharged fierce arrows;
the Daityas could not endure those shafts which resembled serpents in the form of Kṛṣṇa.
Being crushed here and there, they found no stability;
and the Sāvitra weapon, discharged by Sāvitrī, fell upon the crores of Daityas.
The seven Kākaseyas and likewise ten million soldiers were then slain by the force of his weapons; from that, rivers of blood arose.
A few survivors who had escaped slaughter, being very dear to Bhaṇḍa, went to him and reported their own destruction; Bhaṇḍa then fell into despair.
The hosts of deities proclaimed that Sāvitrī had achieved victory;
meanwhile, Bhaṇḍa also held counsel with his remaining followers.
"Alas! The destruction of the Daitya clans has indeed occurred;
the powerful Fate has now begun to practice indifference. (27)
The denizens of heaven flee at the mere mention of my servants' names;
for such as we are, this reversal has now come upon us. (28)
It makes the strong weak, the wealthy destitute, the long-lived short-lived, and a king a servant of beggars. (29)
Where is the strength of our arms, and where is this wayward young woman, by whom even the highly arrogant army commanders have been struck down like mere maidservants? (3.117.30)
For she must indeed be seized alive; she must be enjoyed by force.
Only then will my appeasement occur; let them seize her while she yet lives! 3.11
"Either by you in female attire, or by the Daitya women likewise, let Jīvayoginī be captured through deceitful means as you gather together. (32)
Or rather, let a most formidable and supreme battle be waged first;
let our armies be drawn up at the very front of their host.
"Being on her back with little assistance, she will be easy for me to seize;
therefore, assuming the dress of a woman, I shall go right there where she is. (34)
Having seized her by force, devoured her, and then killed her, and having destroyed all others as well, I shall return to my own abode. (35)
That very [power] is the most exalted, being the root of all powers without exception;
by its destruction at the root, the entire multitude of powers perishes. (36)
"Having dragged her away and conquered her, I shall either enjoy her or take her home"—
thus was the counsel of this evil-minded minister, the Dānava Bhaṇḍa.
Having led the generals and the armies, he went to the field of battle;
evening had fallen and profound darkness had set in.
For the wicked asuras, the night alone provides strength;
indeed, their army, active during that time, stood at the front of the goddesses' army.
They fought with blows from weapons in the darkness that destroys life;
there, millions of Daityas were struck down and killed by the goddesses.
Indeed, blows that grant life and blows that destroy life occurred;
for the secret practices of Bhaṇḍa followed wherever the Goddess of the Suras went.
There they waged war, engaging in a great battle both from behind and from the front. Then there were those spears, headed by Kālī, which were as radiant as the night.
The Bhairavīs, the Bhairavas, the hosts of Rudras, the Rudrāṇīs, and the Īśikās struck down the Dānavas and Daityas; and the Bhūtyas likewise slew the Dānavas. (43)
That army of Dānavas, consisting of ten akṣauhiṇīs, was entirely destroyed during the night; Bhaṇḍa alone fled. ||44||
The night turned into dawn, and the quarters of the sky became clear;
Lalitā attained great satisfaction at the sight of the victorious goddesses. 45.
Then Bhaṇḍa, having consulted together with his own sons,
again dispatched his four sons, who had four arms and faces, into the battle.
Those thirty arrogant ones fought day and night;
an army of two hundred akṣauhiṇīs marched forth with the greatest speed.
Śrībālā, the daughter of Mahālakṣmī named Santoṣikā, was that maiden who then became ready to fight in the battle. (48)
Accompanied by a retinue of one hundred crores, bearing all types of weapons, and endowed with eighteen arms, she rushed toward Bhaṇḍa’s army. 49.
Then a battle commenced of exceedingly exalted prowess;
Śrī Bālā, intoxicated by the fight, assumed ten million forms.
And Lalitā’s daughter displayed her heroism in the battle;
by discharging weapon after counter-weapon, she shattered them all in an instant. ||51||
By the discharge of the Nārāyaṇa weapon, that illustrious young maiden, Śrībālā,
reduced an army of two hundred akṣauhiṇīs to ashes in a single day.
That young girl, your sister-in-law Santoshā, the daughter of Bhaṇḍa, simultaneously dispatched thirty arrows to the abode of Yama. (53)
He suddenly dispatched [the weapons], indeed piercing through their heads;
and the Śaktis there repeatedly uttered cries of "Well done! (sādhuvāda).
Then other Daityas, whose hope for life was very slight, fled;
having reached their own homes, they voiced their grief to Bhaṇḍa.
Then, having heard that his sons were lost, Bhaṇḍa, overwhelmed by the fire of grief and perceiving the destruction of his lineage to have occurred, lamented aloud.
"Alas! I am ruined, I am destroyed, and indeed today I am truly ill-fated;
for even now, there exists with me a woman who brings about the destruction of her family. (57)
Thus, with his vision obscured by a swoon, he fell to the surface of the earth;
then, having risen and drawn forth his fierce sword, he spoke.
Right now, having cut that Fortune into pieces with this sword in battle, I shall attain eternal peace. (59)
Thus brandishing his sword and uttering these words, he advanced into the battle, crying out: "I shall drink them all; I shall make them my own beloveds! (3.117.60)
"I shall now cut down all the gods, shatter the abodes of the gods, and crush their armies"—thus she went forth in battle, filled with rage. (61)
All my brothers were slain, as were all the commanders of the army;
thus, for three days, the entire battle took place for the sake of my destruction. (62)
Either destruction or victory may occur, for there is no strength without one's own power;
I shall either regain that lovely Lalitā or bring about her end.
Speaking repeatedly, brandishing and shaking his sword,
he stood at the head of the army of women like the enraged Fire of Time.
Beholding him, Lalitā, possessing exquisite beauty, proceeded to fight with him;
her royal chariot, the Cakrarāja, shone brightly as it advanced toward him.
He is the great fear for the four Vedas, the Great Wheel, and the goals of human endeavor.
Resplendent with the banner of bliss, it is endowed with the nine stages.
Accompanied by goddesses dwelling on the nine stages who had drawn their heavy bows, and by divine and non-divine assistants numbering more than a parārdha; ||67||
It was ten yojanas in height and four yojanas in width;
the mounts of the other goddesses were likewise in numbers reaching into the parārdha.
Likewise, there are those with the faces of lions, camels, men, predatory beasts, deer, birds, and horses;
as well as elephants, bheruṇḍas, śarabhas, tigers, vātamṛgas, and so forth. ||69||
Assuming divine forms, they always roared for the sake of destroying Bhaṇḍa;
celestial drums resounded, and showers of flowers fell.
Then auspicious omens appeared in the army of Lakṣmī;
at that time, battle commenced between both armies. (71)
The hosts of Dānavas were incessantly being slain by throngs of women;
at that time, the earth became filled with dancing headless trunks of Daityas,
and it was strewn with coconuts formed from the heads of Daityas, abounding in thousands of their hair.
The villages whose elephants were cut down by the discus, and the abodes of the asuras destroyed by the spear.
Filled with the faces of the heroic Daityas and exceedingly muddy with the flow of blood, even as I beheld that [river], a terror of death arose within me. (74)
Then, on the fourth day, the destruction of the Daitya army occurred;
thereafter, a battle took place between Lalitāśrī and Bhaṇḍāsura.
Through the agitation caused by missiles and counter-missiles, and by life-taking arrows,
the single arrow released by Mahālakṣmī indeed became tenfold.
Then, upon contact with the bodies of the Daityas, those arrows reached a count of one hundred thousand, appearing tenfold, a hundredfold,
and a thousandfold in the sky amidst the Daitya host.
She thoroughly pierced Bhaṇḍa’s vital points with her arrows;
Bhaṇḍa then released a terrifying weapon named Andhatāmisra.
Mahālakṣmī repelled it with the Mahābhāskara arrow.
Then, in that battle, the demon Bhaṇḍa discharged the weapon of heresy.
She released the Gāyatrī weapon, and Lakṣmī repelled it;
then Bhaṇḍa discharged the Andha weapon, which obstructs all vision.
Then Mahālakṣmī released the great weapon of Cākṣuṣmata;
thereafter, Bhaṇḍa discharged the Aśakti weapon against the host of women.
Lakṣmī discharged a fierce Great Śakti weapon against him,
while the demon Bhaṇḍa released the Antaka weapon, which destroys all things.
Lakṣmī discharged the great weapon Mahāmṛtyuñjaya against him;
then Bhaṇḍa indeed released the weapon that destroys all learning. (83)
I discharged the *dhāraṇā* weapon which bestows fortune and intelligence upon my own [followers];
then Bhaṇḍa discharged the *bhaya* (fear) weapon, and Kamalā discharged the *abhaya* (fearlessness) weapon.
Bhaṇḍa possesses the Mahāmāyā weapon, and Lakṣmī possesses the Nirāmaya weapon;
Bhaṇḍa possesses the Āyurnāśana weapon, and Lakṣmī possesses the Yoga weapon. Thus it is said. (89)
Then Bhaṇḍaka [discharged] the Āsura weapon, and Lakṣmī [discharged] the Durgā weapon;
[against] hundreds of thousands of Asuras and hundreds of thousands of Durgā-yoginīs.
And armies appeared in the sky and fought with great speed;
[they hurled] spears, discuses, maces, javelins, bows, swords, arrows, and thunderbolts. (87)
Grasping sticks, nooses, and balls one after another, they struck them excessively,
yet they did not touch the goddesses at all.
There the Asuras were slain on all sides by the hosts of goddesses;
likewise, Durgā, having mounted her lion-vehicle, engaged in battle.
Nārāyaṇī Mahālakṣmī indeed attained victory;
thereafter, Bhaṇḍa released the ocean-weapon upon the host of women.
Then Mahālakṣmī released the Śoṣaṇa weapon into the sky;
thereupon, the Daitya Bhaṇḍa became enraged and uttered a roar of defiance.
Thousands of Daityas were born; Durgā led them to Yama.
Then Bhaṇḍa discharged the deer-weapon, and Lakṣmī unleashed the lion-weapon.
Bhaṇḍa discharged the Balya weapon, Lakṣmī the Vāmana weapon, Bhaṇḍaka the Haihaya weapon, and Īśvarī the Paraśurāma weapon. (93)
Then Bhaṇḍa discharged the weapon of Rāvaṇa, while Lakṣmī discharged the weapon of Rāma;
Bhaṇḍa unleashed the weapon of the King, and Lakṣmī deployed the weapon of Kṛṣṇa. ||94||
The demon Bhaṇḍa discharged the Brahmāṇḍa weapon, and Kamalā discharged the Vyūha weapon; the demon Bhaṇḍa discharged the Kalpa weapon, and Lakṣmī deployed the Kalki weapon.
Having all performed the destruction of the asuras, those ten incarnations stood with palms joined in reverence, having paid homage to Lalitā Śrī. ||96||
By the command of Mahālakṣmī, they went to Vaikuṇṭha;
Bhaṇḍa discharged the weapon of delusion (mohāstra), and Lakṣmī deployed the weapon of knowledge (jñānāstra).
Lakṣmī reduced the Daityas to ashes with the weapon of Nārāyaṇa,
and she likewise reduced all the commanders of the armies to ashes with fire.
He reduced Bhaṇḍa to ashes by the splendor of the weapon of the Supreme Brahman;
he turned the city to ashes, leaving nothing but its foundation.
Then Bhaṇḍa died, and the three worlds became filled with the sound of joyful celebration;
by reciting or hearing this, fear of the Daityas is destroyed. (3.117.100)
Fear of enemies and calamities perish without a doubt;
they also attain enjoyment, liberation, good fortune, and supreme prosperity. || 10 1 ||

Thus ends the one hundred and seventeenth chapter, titled "The Destruction of Bhaṇḍāsura’s Armies by Mahālakṣmī’s Forces and the Subsequent Slaying of Bhaṇḍāsura," in the Third Section (Dvāpara-santāna) of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇī Śrī said: O Blessed One, O Lord of the lords of the gods, O Sovereign of sovereigns,
what occurred after the destruction of Bhaṇḍa at dawn on the fourth day?
Śrī Puruṣottama said: After the battle, the Great Lakṣmī, Lalitāramā, dispelled the exhaustion of all the goddesses with her glances that were like nectar and ambrosia.
Then Mahālakṣmī gave divine foods along with honors such as gifts of respect, rewards, and other highly precious offerings.
Then she bestowed all the divine ornaments;
having placed within her own heart all those forms numbering in the millions, billions, and hundreds of millions.
At that same time, Mahāramā, overflowing with affection, embraced them all;
she said, "They are my daughters," while Muktā, Brāhmī, and Īśikā were released.
I bestow upon all of you indeed the imperishable, eternal abode;
for you are the eternal beloveds of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa.
"May you be the queens of the wielder of the Śārṅga bow, always possessing the right to receive his gifts," he said to all of them, and placed moon-crests upon their foreheads.
Vyadhā fashioned a garland and gave it to them so that they might place it around my neck;
then all those beloved women there offered the garland upon my neck.
Those billions of billions of lotus-maidens are the goddesses of Brahmā, born from my own portion;
they are all my beloveds, who now exist as mine.
O Lakṣmī, it was indeed in your presence that I married those who are your beloveds at that time in the sacred field of Kuṅkumavāpikā.
"Indeed, your sisters, born of divided lineages, have become my co-wives for my sake;
they were commanded by me—those who are human, those who are divine, and others who are of the ancestors. (11)
"These are my wives, who possess many bodies;
listen, Lakṣmī, at the fourth hour, at midday, the hosts of deities—
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Mahendra, and Bṛhaspati— "
The Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, Maruts, and Sādhyadevatās. ||13||
The Siddhas, Kimpuruṣas, Yakṣas, the guardians of the quarters, the protectors of the worlds, the devoted Daityas and Dānavas, and those Nāgas who are Vaiṣṇavas—[all these were present]. || 14 ||

Those on the side of the gods and those belonging to the asuras, who were characterized by the qualities of darkness (tamas) and passion (rajas), all heard of Śrī Vijaya’s victory and likewise beheld the happiness of the gods. ||15||
Assembled there in the assembly hall, adorned by the entire race of women, they,
along with the Gandharvas and Apsaras, praised the Great Ramā.
Salutations, salutations to you, O Supreme Goddess, whose form is the crest-jewel upon the heads of the gods, whose nature is half that of Hari;
O Great Imperishable One, who dwells in the abode of the imperishable, O Mother of the three creations, salutations, salutations to you! 17.

Homage to you who dwell with all the [goddesses] beginning with Āvāhā; homage to you who dwell as the abode of ten million lords; homage to you who are the dwelling place of all the Īśvarīs; homage to you who are the supreme abode of the hosts of both the liberated and those seeking liberation. || 18 ||

Salutations to you, O Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa; salutations to you, the limb [of all], the perfected sage, the true father, and the auspicious one. Salutations to you, who are well-served by the multitude of goddesses; salutations be to you in the form of the illustrious Mānavī.
Obeisance to you, O Mother Santoṣikā, in Śrī Kambhara, O consort of Śrī Laliteśa;
O Gajānanā, O Mother whose form is like that of Ananta, obeisance to you who possess the nature of a doe.
O Sovereign of all, O Mistress of all beauty, O Śrīmāṇikī, Pāśavatī, and Pramodā;
O You who are the essence of the great ocean of Lakṣmī, O Abode of the beloved of Brahman—salutations to You constantly! 21.

O Mistress of the realm of desire, skilled in granting the requests of those who seek, wish-fulfilling gem that gives birth to the manifold world, bestower of liberation, whose eyes are the sun and the moon, and who possesses a gentle smile—to you, O Yoginī, let there be homage! 22.
Homage, homage to you, O Mother, slayer of the great asura Bhaṇḍa, wielder of the sword that brings an end to all the Daityas;
homage to you, sovereign of mudrās, whose form is the excellent yantra, and who gives rise to all sacred learning! 23.
O Kṛṣṇā, supreme one, stationed in the six-spoked wheel, destroyer of the six waves [of worldly existence], dispeller of fatigue;
O Mother, devoid of the six states of being, the locus of the eightfold qualities, salutations to you, the foremost sovereign of all! 24.
O beloved mistress of the Lord of Kamalā, O most stainless one, O sovereign of the world, O dear one,
O elixir dwelling in all essences!
And salutations be repeatedly offered to you of divine form. ||25||

O Mother of the world, O Creatrix, O Goddess supreme among gods, salutations to you; salutations to you who dwell upon the couch whose essence is Gopāla-Kṛṣṇa, and who are to be served by the eightfold powers beginning with *aṇimā*. 26.
O beloved of Brahmā, delighting in Brahmā, O Śrī Hari, whose essence is Brahmā, O Śrī Lalitā, salutations to you!
O stream of the nectar of Brahman, destroyer of rebirth, O Sovereign of Brahmā, O Śrī Lalitā, salutations to you! 27.
Salutations to you, O Lalitā, who possess an auspicious abode, who bestow auspiciousness, who are called the Imperishable, who have destroyed the host of enemies, and who are charming;
salutations to you, O Śrī Lalitā, who are supreme over all, who pervade all, and who grant all accomplishments. 28.
O Śrī Lalitā, who fulfills the desires of all the immortals, bestower of boons, salutations to you!
O Śrī, who abides in the Bindu and possesses the beautiful form of the Bindu!
Upon her broad breasts, where lotus-like blossoms sway, her necklace trembles.
Salutations to you, O graceful one with a lotus-face, who shines like the sun upon the trembling creeper that yields fruit;
O Puruṣottamī, the sole ground of essence, whose nature is Śrī, Bhū, Padmākā, and Kamalā.
O treasure-house of compassion, engaged in the work of the gods, illustrious Vaiṣṇavī, you who manifest all glories;
O charming one with eyes like a young deer, grant me [your grace].
O Mother, salutations to you, O Lalitā, O exceedingly beautiful one! ||31||
O Śrī Mahālakṣmī, bestower of prosperity, remover of calamities, most ancient and immeasurable one,
by you the entire world is well protected.
Having slain Bhaṇḍāsura and the others in battle.
By Śrī Śambhu, Manmatha was indeed reduced to ashes;
yet even Bhaṇḍa, who arose from those ashes, was slain by you again,
because even the ashes of Kāma were well-reduced to ash by you.
Freedom from desire and freedom from attachment have been demonstrated. ||33||
The gross body of Madana was burnt by Śambhu, and his subtle body was subsequently consumed by you; thus,
my husband is now deprived of both bodies.
Beholding that life, Rati made this request: ||34||
Then again, that which was the body of the cause, consisting of conceptualization and composed of many latent impressions (vāsanās),
from that indeed arose the invisible body of Rāma.
Having made it vast and pervasive, he gave it to the woman Rati.
Having beheld her own beloved, supreme and the sustainer of all the worlds, abiding within her heart in an invisible form, Rati was filled with passion.
With a heart full of serene joy, she embraced her husband. ||36||
For even though Kāma is by nature bodiless, he was ordained by you to perform the work of one possessing a body;
therefore, by your command, he attained pervasion over the Lord of Śivā.
Skanda came into being through his union with the daughter of the mountain. ||37||
It should be understood that one who is the conqueror of gross desire becomes the very nature of Śambhu;
[likewise] one who is the conqueror of subtle desire.
It should be understood that one becomes the very embodiment of Lakṣmī. ||38||
Nārāyaṇa, the conqueror of the limbs of evil tendencies, should indeed be understood as one who has attained the upward path;
thus, O Īśvarī, Supreme Lord of all, this which has been explained by You leads to our liberation from everything. 39.
Having thus praised and worshipped him, they sat down with joyful minds;
and they all celebrated a festival on that account upon the field of battle.
Lalitā-lakṣmī gave that kingdom to Ratīśvara;
Kāma himself, assuming a form at will, took up the reign of the kingdom.
He was born as the lord of nine hundred thousand [villages], a master of desire and the lord of Rati;
he was full of joy, a devotee of the illustrious Mahālakṣmī, and a follower of Nārāyaṇa. ||42||
O Lakṣmī, he has been held by me today for the satisfaction of you all;
indeed, this divine devotee of mine exists as one who is truly liberated from the qualities (guṇas). ||43||
He is the embodiment of true desire, the bestower of the bliss of the beloved of Brahman; though possessing attributes within the three worlds, he has assumed infinite forms.
O Lakṣmī, by your grace, the Lord of Rati (Kāmadeva) exists as all-pervading;
so too do the gods, the ancestors, the great-souled ones, and the great sages. ||45||
They all departed for their own worlds, while Mahālakṣmī remained forever seated;
she dwelt eternally in the city of Kāñcī, which is the very form of Mahāvaikuṇṭha.
In his second form, he went to the abode of Mahāviṣṇu;
in his third form, indeed, Śrī Kaṃbhārā exists.
In her fourth form as Gajānanā, she will manifest;
this very one, known by the name Śrī Lalitā, will experience [her presence] in Saurāṣṭra.
For thereafter there will be infinite incarnations—divine, always bestowing liberation, inaccessible, and beyond description. (49)
The beginningless Great Power, the divine Śrī Puruṣottamī, is known as my mother Kambharā; she exists as Mahālakṣmī. (3.118.50)
O Lakṣmī, serve that mother-in-law who always bestows liberation and grants emancipation;
I too shall always serve her and bow repeatedly to my mother. (51)
For those devoted to the service of their mothers, no ill fate shall ever occur;
service to one's mother brings about the destruction of even the great obstacle-demons.
Listen, Lakṣmī, and likewise elsewhere; I shall describe to you my auspicious temples, as well as those of Mahālakṣmī, my mother Lalitā. (53)
There, she who is divided sixteenfold makes her dwelling; all [the structures] therein were fashioned by Maya Viśvakarman. (54)
On Mount Meru, as well as on Niṣadha, Hemakūṭa, Himācala, Gandhamādana, Nīlādri, Meṣādri, and Śṛṅgaparvata; ||55||
Indeed, these auspicious temples on earth at Mahendra—these nine sacred sites (tīrthas)—are truly bestowers of liberation. ||56||
Furthermore, there are other waters flowing from the seven rivers, located in the oceans of salt, sugarcane juice, wine, clarified butter, curd, and milk-rice. (57)
Indeed, on the ocean Miṣṭa there are palaces, which are truly adorned with jewels, diamonds, and gems. (58)
Indeed, there were vast and lofty [cities] filled with great gardens;
and beyond them were thousands of trees that always bore flowers and always bore fruit.
Abundantly rich with the beauty of ever-present foliage, perpetually filled with fragrance, and endowed with the characteristics of all seasons, they serve as the causes of Lakṣmī’s adornment.
Nectar shall be his sweet juice, and flowers his ornaments;
divine yellow garments shall be his, and those very [garments] shall be coral.
Such wish-fulfilling trees stand before the temple,
as do wish-fulfilling ponds, wish-fulfilling halls, and groves of yellow sandalwood.
There are groves of Mandāra trees, gardens of Pārijāta and other celestial blossoms,
and groves of Kadamba trees, all made of divine sugar.
Indeed, O Lakṣmī, the dwellings of Mahālakṣmī are composed of wish-fulfilling gems;
formerly, O Lakṣmī, there was a great sage named Mātaṅga who was devoted to her service.
Adhering to the dharma of an ascetic, he performed the worship of Mahālakṣmī;
Mahālakṣmī, being pleased with him, granted him the fulfillment of his every resolve.
Overwhelmed with joy and overflowing with devotion, he praised Lakṣmī, the goddess who dwells within his range of perception:
"O Mother, by the mere remembrance of you, all my spiritual accomplishments [shall be attained]. (66)
The powers such as atomization (aṇimā) and all other such manifestations have already arisen;
indeed, there is nothing whatsoever remaining in the three worlds that I must attain.
"But act in such a way that I may have a constant vision [of you].
Having been addressed thus, Mahālakṣmī appeared in a dream to the female elephant.
She took a single cluster of *tāpiccha* blossoms from her ear-ornament and gave it to her;
thereafter, that wife Siddhimatī became pregnant. (69)
That daughter was named Viṣṇuśyāmā;
she was Śyāmā by name, for she was born from the womb of Siddhimatī.
Then Śyāmā, having worshipped Mahālakṣmī, shines forth;
indeed, she is always a companion in service in the presence of Mahālakṣmī. (71)
Being served by her, she is considered Vaiṣṇavī, who is dark-complexioned;
likewise, there is a second attendant named Ghanashyāmā.
And Meghaputrī indeed serves Mahālakṣmī from the sky;
they are devoted to the worship of Lalitā, meditation, recitation, and praise. (73)
Madhuśrī and Mādhava attend upon the Supreme Goddess;
Śukraśrī and Śuciśrī also attend upon the Supreme Goddess. (74)
The splendor of Nabhas and the splendor of Nabhasya wait upon the Supreme Goddess;
likewise, the splendor of Iṣa and the splendor of Ūrja wait upon the Supreme Goddess. (75)
Sahaḥ-Śrī and Sahasya-Śrī attend upon the Supreme Goddess;
Tapaḥ-Śrī and Tapasya-Śrī attend upon the Supreme Goddess.
The powers and fortunes of spring serve the Supreme Goddess, being devoted to the worship, meditation, recitation, and hymns of Lalitā. (77)
In Lalitā, divine women abide endowed with devotion;
there are also most celestial birds, who are attendants served by the Siddhas. (78)
Those who recite the Lalitā-mantra and are always devoted to the command of Lalitā—crores of deities exist among them as both forest-dwellers and wandering minstrels. (79)
The hosts of Gandharvas and Apsarases repeatedly sing the compositions of songs for Lalitādevī, singing with the sounds of their lutes.
They were of delicate form and endowed with devotion to Śrī Lakṣmī;
they were both male and female yogis, Vaiṣṇavas filled with devotion. ||81||
They enjoy the charming splendor of Lalitā and meditate upon her according to the prescribed rules;
for the sake of increasing their own good fortune, they also recite her mantra.
Kinnaras and Kimpuruṣas, always accompanied by Kinnarīs and others, serve Puruṣottamī while dancing and singing. (83)
Those supreme men who are devotees of Lalitāparameśvarī, possessing divine bodies, always serve their mother, Śrī Lakṣmī. (84)
Those who dwell in the netherworld (pātāla) and are practitioners of the worship of Śrī Lakṣmī—having attained perfection in form—they reside there, enjoying happiness. ||85||
Indeed, there exist in those Śrīnagaras those who have muttered the Lalitā-mantra, who have been initiated into the Lalitā-śāstra, and who are worshippers of Lalitā. (86)
In that regard, those who possess knowledge, who are devoted, who are dedicated to Mahālakṣmī, who are rich in devotion, and who are of the nature of Brahman—they enter the imperishable state. ||87||
Jayā, Ākhyā, Lalitā, Jyeṣṭhā, and Naya lead one indeed to the imperishable state;
they dwell together before Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. 88.
And those who dwell in the world of the gods, together with their wives, reside in the glorious Purottama; endowed with devotion, they are constant reciters of the name of Śrī Lakṣmī. (89)
The Siddhas, the divine ṛṣis, and others who practice the mastery of the vital winds (pavana),
as well as the Maruts who have attained liberation, worship the Supreme Goddess.
The treasures, the supernatural powers, the prosperities, and the manifestations—all these divine beings dwell right there and serve Puruṣottamī. ||91||
And indeed, many wish-fulfilling cows, proud of their flow of milk and devoted to the pleasure of Lalitā, serve the Mistress of Lalitā. (92)
The Rudrāṇīs as well as the Rudras, adorned with all ornaments, and the attendants of Rudra, serve Laliteśvarī. (93)
All of them were great-souled beings with the supreme forms of Viṣṇu;
they were experts in the meditation on the Goddess Śrī and were reciters of the mantra of Śrī Lakṣmī. ||94||
Great devotees of Śrī Lakṣmī serve Puruṣottamī;
the hundred Rudras, endowed with devotion, serve the divine Vaiṣṇavas. (95)
Aryaman, the creator of the universe, joined by all the sages, serves her;
Marīci and the others serve Lalitāśrī, the supreme sovereign. 96.
All the sciences and all the auxiliary sciences serve her by the thousands;
and all the arts and young maidens serve me, the Supreme Sovereign. 97.
The eternal Lord Viṣṇu, the husband of Śrī, likewise serves her;
the Master manifests in four ways, ten ways, and twelve ways.
Mādhava, assuming various forms, constantly and eternally serves her;
and the deities of the ten incarnations likewise serve her in the ruby pavilion.
Bearing the conch, discus, mace, and lotus, they serve the Supreme Goddess—
Nārāyaṇa, Keśava, Govinda, and likewise Mādhava.
The personified scriptures serve the auspicious Mahālakṣmī, the graceful and virtuous Mother;
they serve the glorious Supreme Sovereign.
The omniscient Mahādeva dwells together with Satī;
so too do all the planets, the groups of zodiac signs, the lunar mansions, and the stars.
The powers belonging to the Taijasa state also worship the Supreme Goddess;
and the Moon, together with the constellations, worships the Supreme Goddess.
Through the recitations, meditations, hymns, and even hundreds of worship-rites dedicated to Lalitā,
the Moon, joined by the stars beginning with Aśvinī, serves the Supreme Goddess.
And other women, adorned with various ornaments and possessing the beauty of the erotic sentiment,
wait upon Mahālakṣmī, who is lovely and glorious, remaining submissive to her will.
Agni, joined with his own wife, serves the Supreme Goddess;
[his wives are] Dhūmrārcis, Uṣṇā, Jvalinī, Jvālinī, and Visphulliṅginī.
Women who are auspicious, beautiful, tawny-hued, and carriers of oblations to the gods and ancestors,
endowed with the power of fire, serve Mahālakṣmī, the Supreme Sovereign.
Sūryā, Tapinī, Tāpī, Dhūmrā, Jvālā, Ruci, Kṣamā, Suṣumṇā, Bodhinī, Bhogā, Marīci, and likewise Dhāriṇī. (108)
Accompanied by the twelve powers beginning with Viśvā, he serves her:
Candrakalā, Amṛtā, Mānadā, Pūṣā, Rati, and Dhṛti. || 109 ||
Tuṣṭi, Puṣṭi, Candrikā, Śrī, Kānti, Jyotsnā, Aṅgadā, Śaśā, Prīti, Pūrṇāmṛtā, and Pūrṇā serve the Supreme Goddess. (3.118.1–10)
Nourishment, prosperity, stability, intelligence, loveliness, fortune, splendor, fortitude,
old age, and accomplishment— these digits of Brahmā serve the Sovereign Goddess.
Sthiti, Pālinī, Śānti, Īśvarī, Kāmikā, Tati, Varadā, Hlādinī, Prīti, and Dīrghā are the digits (kalās) of Hari. || 1.12 ||
Together with Viṣṇu, they always serve the beautiful Śrī Lakṣmī;
[the others are] Tīkṣṇā, Raudrī, Bhayā, Nidrā, Tandrā, Kṣut, Krodhinī, and Trapā.
Utkārī and Mṛtyu—these fierce digits (kalās), accompanied by Hara, serve the auspicious Mahālakṣmī, Lalitā, and the virtuous Kambharā. 1.14.
Nivṛtti, Pratiṣṭhā, Vidyā, Śānti, Dīpikā, Indirā, Rocikā, Muktā, Parā, Sūkṣmā, Amṛtā, and Kalā. (1.15)
Jñānā, Vyāptā, Vyomikā, and Vyādhinī— these sixteen attendants serve that Great Lakṣmī, the Mother Puruṣottamī.
Thus have the attendants of the Mother in Śrīpura been described to you;
by the mere hearing of their names, the destruction of sin occurs, and for the devotee, liberation shall come to pass.

Thus ends the one hundred and eighteenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Worship for the Victory of Śrī Lalitā Mahālakṣmī, the Hymn to Mahālakṣmī, the Rewards for the Victors, the Assumption of Desired Forms, the Sixteen Temples of Mahālakṣmī, the Splendor therein, and the Service of the Śaktis," in the Third Section on the Continuation of the Dvāpara Age of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*. || 118 ||
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
In that same way, Śrī Lalitā Lakṣmī is always worshipped by the Śaktis;
she is constantly served by the Śaktis, Śakta-s, and others, and I delight in her presence on all sides. || 1 ||
Those female servants and female disciples constantly perform worship;
all of them, being like daughters to him, abide in various distinct forms. (2)
Gāyatrī, Gaṇeśa, and likewise Mahāgaṇapati;
Sampadeśī, as well as Kālasaṃkarṣiṇī and Mahāramā. (3)
Śrī Mahāśambhunātha worships the Supreme Mother (Parāmbikā), as well as Annapūrṇā, Pādukāśrī, Mahāpadmā, and Varāhiṇī. || 4 ||
Tiraskaraṇī, Śrīpūrti, and Śrīpādā worship [her]; Raśmimālā, Mantrinātha, and Daṇḍanātha indeed worship [her].
In the palace of the wish-fulfilling gem, all the Lalitāśrīs worship;
there too are Aṇimā, Mahimā, Laghimā, and Garimā.
Lordship, mastery, liberation, as well as the power of irresistible will,
the attainment of desires, and the fulfillment of all wishes— these attend upon the Great Ramā.

The accomplishment of alchemy (rasasiddhi), the accomplishment of invisibility (mākṣasiddhi), the auspicious accomplishment of strength (balasiddhi), as well as the accomplishment of the sword (khaḍgasiddhi), the accomplishment of the feet (pādasiddhi), and the accomplishment of collyrium (añjanāsiddhi). || 8 ||
Mastery of speech, mastery of the world, and mastery of the body attend upon him;
likewise, millions of other such accomplishments and those that are proximate also remain near.
Brāhmī, Māheśvarī, Kaumārī, Vaiṣṇavī,
Vārāhī, Māhendrī, Cāmuṇḍā, and Śrī likewise worship her.
Kṣobhiṇī, Drāviṇī, Ākarṣiṇī, Saṃvaśinī, as well as Unmādinī, Mahāṅkuśā, Khecarī, and Bījikā. || 11 ||
And Trikhaṇḍā, Mahālakṣmī, Tripurā, Nāyikā, Pālinī, and likewise Kṣobhaṇā worship her with well-sealed [mudrās]. || 12 ||
The attractor of desires, the attractor of the intellect, and likewise another, the attractor of tastes, and yet another, the attractor of fragrances. (1.3)
Likewise, there is the art of attracting the mind, as well as that of attracting fortitude, that of attracting mindfulness, and the art of attracting names. (14)
Likewise, there is the Attractor of Seeds, as well as the Attractor of Wealth;
also the Showerer of Nectar, and similarly the Attractor of the Body. || 15 ||
These indeed are the divine Yoginīs, auspicious and fulfillers of all desires:
Pālikā, Drāvikā, and Mudrā, proud of their fresh youth. (16)
Deities possessing divine splendor and exceedingly beautiful forms wait upon Mahālakṣmī, the supreme sovereign Lalitā. (17)
Kusumā, Mekhalā, and Madanā, who was afflicted by passion; Rekhā, Veginī, Aṅkuśā, Mālinī, and Sundarī likewise. (18)
Hlādinī, Jṛmbhiṇī, Vaśaṅkarī, Rañjanakāriṇī, Unmādinī, Arthakarī, Sampatpūrā, and Mantriṇī. (19)
The protectors of the tradition serve the Supreme Goddess;
she is the bestower of perfection, the giver of prosperity, the one who fulfills desires, and the auspicious one.
She is the bestower of desires, the destroyer of suffering, the remover of death, and likewise the remover of obstacles;
she is the giver of good fortune, the all-knowing, the Śaktinī, and the embodiment of knowledge. ||21||

The [streams] are Aiśvaryadā (Bestower of Sovereignty), Vyādhihā (Destroyer of Disease), Mahādhārā (Great Stream), Pāpahā (Destroyer of Sin), Ānandinī (Delighting), Rakṣiṇī (Protectress), Ipsitadā (Bestower of Desires), and likewise Garvahā (Remover of Arrogance). ||22||
And Mālinī—all these serve Laliteśvarī;
likewise Vaśinī, Kāminīśā, Modinī, and Vimalā. (23)
Vāgdhārā, Jayinī, Kaulinī, and likewise Īśvarī—all these Sarasvatīs worship the Supreme Goddess. ||24||
And Siddhā, Khecarī, Kāmeśvarī, and likewise Bāṇeśvarī;
Vajrikā, Śataghnī, Bhūśuṇḍī, and Muśalī as well. ||25||
The small sword, the spear, the mallet, and the javelin—these goddesses of weaponry attend upon the Supreme Goddess. (26)
Kāmeśī, Vajreśī, Bhagamālā, Mitrikā, Ṣoḍaśikā, and Gocaryā serve the Supreme Goddess. 27.
Bheruṇḍā, Vahnivāsā, Vajrīśā, Kulasundarī, Vijayā, Nīlapatākā, Jvālāmālā, and Sumaṅgalā. ||28||
For the prosperity of the worlds, he serves Lalitā, whose nature is consciousness,
as well as the goddess of the heart, the goddess of the head, and likewise the goddess of the crest-lock.
The goddesses of armor, the goddesses of rain, and the goddesses of weapons—possessing beautiful forms, born from the *bindu* and *nāda*, and carrying out the command of Lalitā—serve her. (3.119.30)
Now, on the couch consisting of the five Brahmans belonging to the illustrious Goddess Lalitā, her four feet indeed become the forms of the [four] Vyūhas. (3.1)
By the grace of Mahālakṣmī, they attained the state of divinity,
becoming united with the forms of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa, and Īśvara.
These feet are embodied forms of Puruṣas bearing weapons;
their eyes are closed in meditation on Śrī, and their limbs are rendered motionless by that meditation on Śrī. ||33||
There Mahālakṣmī, Brahmeśī, and Laliteśvarī lie;
indeed, the stairs of this couch have truly become personified.
Earth, water, fire, air, and space; as well as smell, taste, form, touch, sound, and the organs of generation and excretion. (35)
The hands, speech, nose, tongue, skin, eye, and ear, as well as ego, intellect, mind, primordial nature (prakṛti), and the individual soul (puruṣa). ||36||
Niyati, Kāla, Rāga, Kalā, Vidyā, Māyinī, and Pūṣā serve the supreme goddess Lalitā. (37)
Now, on the couch there lies indeed a bed with swan-down pillows, provided with a head-cushion from the crest of a supreme swan, and serving as an auspicious support. (38)
Rich with the pillow of service at her feet, provided with the upper cover of joy, adorned with the ropes of all the Vedāṅgas, and possessing the side-pillow of peace. (39)
In this [city], the illustrious Mahālakṣmī, accompanied by Mahāviṣṇu, shines forth; the enchanting Mistress serves her own Lord. (3.119.40)
Compassionate, sixteen years of age, adorned with the attire of love, possessing a splendor equal to the rising sun, and fragrant with the scent of the finest sandalwood. ||41||
Adorned with necklaces, armlets, crowns, bracelets, and other ornaments,
he possesses a lovely smile, a face filled with moonlight, and is most beautiful.
Serving Mahālakṣmī, she was youthful, radiant as the sun, eternally fourteen years of age, and proud of her fresh youth. (43)
Possessing the luster of polished rubies, with sandalwood and lotus-like nails as its arrows,
the beauty of her lac-dye flows forth toward the redness of his feet without regard for herself.
She was enchanting with her anklets and falling bracelets that produced sweet sounds;
her shapely calves were like the pride-destroying quivers of the god of love.
Her thighs were as beautiful as the trunk of an elephant or the stem of a plantain tree;
she was enriched by the splendor of her waist and girdle, and radiant with the fullness of her hips. (46)
Adorned with a jeweled girdle, she is graced by a deep navel and the three folds [of skin];
her chest is endowed with the swelling buds of breasts like pearls. ||47||
Exceedingly radiant, beautified by her two arms skillful with red lac, and adorned with armlets, bracelets, finger-rings, and other ornaments; ||48||
Her chin was round like a mirror for her face; she possessed lips as red as the lower lip of a Lāṭa woman; and she displayed her smile with teeth possessing the beauty of jasmine buds. (49)
Her eyes, with corners as broad as lotuses, possess the luster of red lotuses;
on her forehead, charming with its fine lines, a mass of curls is perfectly arranged. (3.119.50)
Her ears were adorned with earrings of rubies set in full-blown flower-shaped ornaments,
and her betel-roll was perpetually fragrant with fresh camphor and musk.
Her face is as sweet as the orb of the autumn moon moving gracefully through the night;
her beautiful crown is fashioned from the very essence of wish-fulfilling gems.
She is resplendent with the crescent moon upon her forehead situated in the center of a shimmering tilaka, and she possesses a mass of curved, swaying, thick, and slender locks of hair. ||52||
Adorned with a line of vermilion applied to the parting of her hair,
she is enriched with every kind of elegant attire and decorated with all ornaments.
She whose limbs are divine and super-divine, who increases the joy of Hari, she is Mahālakṣmī, the Mother of all the worlds and the Supreme Sovereign. 55.
She serves her own husband upon the couch and is served by all the powers;
by the mere act of serving her, one gains the merit of worshipping all the gods. (56)
O Rame, it is indeed impossible to describe the virtues of that Goddess Lalitā even in thousands of millions of kalpas.
O Rame, such is the city of Śrīpura belonging to Lalitā;
those who hear of it, speak of it, or go there attain the supreme goal.
Having had a divine and magnificent temple for Mahālakṣmī constructed by artisans—one endowed with every power—the devotee goes to that supreme state. (59)
In this way, there are other cities where goddesses and deities dwell and also serve Lalitā, the Supreme Goddess. (3.119.60)
To the beginningless Śrī Mahālakṣmī, the supreme sovereign Kambharā-Śrī, the virtuous beloved of the illustrious Gopāla-Kṛṣṇa, the Great Viṣṇu. ||61||
My mother, your mother-in-law, the auspicious daughter who is an ocean of love, the performer of all welfare, the illustrious mistress of Kuṅkumavāpikā. (62)
O Śrī Nārāyaṇī, consort of Śiva, worship my mother—the auspicious, divine desire of the Supreme Lord, who has attained the state of the Supreme Brahman. 63.
O Kṛṣṇeśī, you who are formless, being embodied yourself, chant that supreme mantra and worship the yantra which bestows enjoyment, prosperity, and liberation.
Śrī Nārāyaṇī said:
O Blessed One, tell me this which is desired by all the worlds: of what mantra is its recitation [to be performed], and what is its ritual procedure? 65.
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
Listen, O Śrī Nārāyaṇī; the categories of objects are indicated by words.
The Veda consists eternally of the nature of sound, and among those, the mantras are considered the most excellent. (66)
Among those, the mantras of Hari are the most excellent, and the mantras of Lakṣmī are always supreme;
so too are those of Durgā, Gaṇeśa, Ravi, Śambhu, and Vibhāvasu.
Indeed, the supreme mantras among all mantras belong to Mahālakṣmī;
I shall tell you those of Śyāmā and Kambharā—listen to me.
Having risen early in the morning, bowed to me, and bathed, sit upon an auspicious seat and remember, O Lakṣmī, the divine and radiant lotus upon your own head. (69)
Having meditated there upon the glorious true Guru—radiant with a thousand petals, complete with filaments and a pericarp, gracious and full of compassion. (3.119.70)
Having sipped water (ācamana) and then applied the vertical mark (ūrdhvapuṇḍra) with its crescent moon, one should [worship] the supreme true guru, his father, known as Śrīmad Gopālakṛṣṇa. ||71||
Placing [the image] upon your shoulder and holding the *paṭṭaka* of the Supreme Goddess to your heart, become inwardly pure and perform the twilight worship (*saṃdhyāvandana*). //72//
Offer that arghya, consisting of kuśa grass, unbroken rice, flowers, and sandalwood, in a vessel shaped like a pipal leaf to Mahālakṣmī.
Having offered the arghya three times and having gratified [the deities] with water,
one should proceed to the site of the fire-oblation (homabhūmi), which is adorned with every kind of ornament.

O Lakṣmī, established upon your seat and accompanied by all the requisites for worship and so forth, perform the ritual placements on the limbs (aṅganyāsa); listen to them as they are proclaimed by me. 75.
Salutation to Omanādiparabrahmeśvarī on my head;
salutation to Omanādikṛṣṇanārāyaṇī on my forehead. (76)
Salutation to Omanādīvāsudevī Lakṣmī; salutation to you in my two eyes.
Salutation again and again to Omanādibrahma Lakṣmī; salutation to you in my mouth. (77)
Salutations to Omana-Ādikambharā-Lakṣmī; may she be in my throat. And salutations to you, Omana-Ādi-Mahālakṣmī; may you be in my heart. (78)
Salutations to you, O Śrī Narāyaṇī, beginningless with *Oṃ*, within my belly; salutations again and again to you, O Vaiṣṇavī, beginningless with *Oṃ*, at my navel.
Salutations to Omana-ādi-lalitā on your hips and mine;
and let there always be salutations to Omana-ādi-śrī on my two thighs.
Omanādikamalā, salutations to you; may you be at my knees. Omanādiramā, salutations to you; may you be at my feet.
Obeisance be to you, O Hariṇī who begins with *oma*; obeisance be to you in my two hands.
O Great Minister (*mahāmātra*) who begins with *oma*, obeisance after obeisance to you from every side. (82)
Salutations to you, Oṃ-manādi-padmā, on the palms of your two hands; salutations again and again to you, Oṃ-manādi-rakṣitrī, on the region of your back. ||83||
Salutations to you, Omanādi-hiraṇyā, upon your beautiful limbs; salutations to you, Omanādi-suvarṇā, upon the lines of fortune on your palms. ||84||
Homage again and again to you, Oṃmanādikumārī, in your virtue and dharma; homage again and again to you, Oṃmanādijananī, in all your limbs. ||85||
Having thus performed the ritual placements (nyāsa), meditate upon the Sovereign of Śrīpura;
meditate also upon Śrīpura itself, and upon me, the Lord of the Sovereign of Śrīpura. 86.
Thereafter, invoke the form fashioned of gold;
then offer a seat, followed by water for the feet and the guest-offering (arghya). (87)
Perform the ritual sipping of water (ācamana) and the bathing with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta); rub the Supreme Goddess with fragrant oils, essences, and the like. (88)
Having caused the consecration to be performed, offer garments and ornaments;
[present] every kind of finery, the highest auspiciousness, incense, and a lamp. (89)
He performed prostrations like a staff, circumambulations with reverence, and clockwise circumambulations;
he offered various kinds of food offerings, including items to be eaten, chewed, sucked, and licked.
Water, vegetables and the like should indeed be drunk, as well as milk-essence and milk-rice (pāyasa); likewise, the drinking of water, betel leaves, betel nut, and fruit [are permitted]. 91.
Offer this to Śrī Mahālakṣmī; choose forgiveness for your transgression.
Having performed the offering of a handful of flowers as an atonement, carry out your own endeavor. 92.
Then, O beloved Lakṣmī, having worn a garland of tulasī, chant the mantra;
chant the great mantra of Mahālakṣmī, which is dear to me. (93)
Facing north or facing east, one should always remain in the presence of the glory of recitation (japa-śrī), which accomplishes all goals and destroys all misfortunes, for it is the Lord himself. 94.
Oṃ, we know Mahālakṣmī; we meditate upon the consort of Mahāviṣṇu;
may that Mahālakṣmī inspire us.
Oṃ śrīṃ, salutation to Mahālakṣmī; oṃ hrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ phaṭ svāhā. ||95||
By reciting [the mantra] thirty-six hundred thousand times, success will be attained;
the fire-oblation (homa) should be one-tenth of that number, and the libation (tarpaṇa) should be one-tenth of that. (96)
Offer food to the devotees equal to one-tenth of that amount;
in this way, the mantra will become perfected, and thereafter perform the recitations for specific desires.
Having recited it one hundred thousand times, one may bring humans under control; by two hundred thousand recitations, women; and likewise by three hundred thousand, kings. (98)
With four hundred thousand [recitations], one obtains the Nāga maidens; with five hundred thousand, the women of Pātāla;
with six hundred thousand, the Bhūsundarīs; and with seven hundred thousand, the celestial women (surāṅganās). ||99||
With eight hundred thousand [recitations], one pleases the deities; with nine hundred thousand, the Gīrvāṇas;
with ten hundred thousand, the ancestors (pitṛs); and with eleven hundred thousand, the lords of the gods (sureśvaras).
And by twelve hundred thousand recitations, one may likewise bring the powers (siddhis) under control;
thus one shall become possessed of fortune, wealthy, and prosperous.
They obtain all sovereignty and divine power according to their desire;
meditating upon her and chanting her name, they attain great prosperity.
This perfection is attained, but never by the unworthy;
it is attained by those people who have performed intense austerity.
Whosoever’s lineage a person born as a reciter (jāpaka) may belong to, all those of that lineage shall become liberated, satisfied, and yogis. 104.
This very Lalitā Rame is the Supreme Self, accompanied by the mantra;
she alone is the great sacred ford (tīrtha), which the virtuous always meditate upon.
Kāmākṣī, Vaiṣṇavī, Mahālakṣmī, and Śrī Laliteśvarī are not attained by those of bad conduct, by revilers, or by those devoid of devotion. 106.
Because she caresses the Supreme Brahman, Lalitā is truly the playful one; she who caresses Mahāviṣṇu, my mother, is ever victorious. 107.

Thus ends the one hundred and nineteenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Service Rendered by the Divine Brāhmī Attendants Residing in the Cintāmaṇi House during the Dvāpara Age, as well as the Mahālakṣmī Mantra and the Fruits of its Recitation," in the Third Section (Dvāpara-santāna) of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
Listen, O Lakṣmī; I shall tell you another mantra of Mahālakṣmī, by the worship of which the practitioner shall attain both worldly enjoyment and liberation.

Oṃ, salutation to Mahālakṣmī, the Great Māyā, the Great Nārāyaṇī, the dweller in the lotus, the beloved of Mahāviṣṇu; Oṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Ṇīṃ Mlīṃ Ṣṇīṃ, salutation to the Great Sovereign who showers the goals of human existence, Svāhā. || 2 ||
One should always recite the divine fifty-syllable great mantra;
I am the seer Nārāyaṇa, and Mahālakṣmī is indeed the deity. (3)
She possesses the luster and form of a golden campaka flower, adorned with every ornament; her face is bright with a compassionate smile, and she is intent upon bestowing grace upon her devotees.
She is complete with all sovereign powers and other perfections, resplendent in every garment,
as beautiful as ten million suns and moons, and wearing jeweled necklaces and other ornaments.
One should meditate upon the Mother Ramā, the glorious Śrī Mahālakṣmī, who takes the form of the illustrious Gopālā, the great power (mahāśakti) of Mahāviṣṇu.
One should recite the mantra ten thousand times, or one hundred thousand times, or else a tenth part of that;

another [wife] is born anywhere at all, impelled by his true merit.
A girl indeed remains a girl, and likewise a boy remains a boy until otherwise;
their marriage in this world occurs when she becomes his wife according to the prescribed rite.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, the birth of a daughter occurs through the merit of the husband;
it may be the debt of the husband, the father-in-law, or the mother-in-law from a previous existence.
By that debt, the girl becomes increased and is then given away;
thus, even though she is another's wealth, she is called "kanyā" (debt).
"O Rame, this daughter of yours is said to be bound by a debt;
for generally, daughters indeed become a debt to their husbands."
The fruit of the gift shall indeed belong to the giver; that [fruit] belongs to the husband who was previously offered [the gift].
Since the giver alone is the enjoyer of the fruit, the giver was formerly considered the enjoyer.
O Lakṣmī, for by that king, indeed, gifts of maidens are bestowed with noble expenditures upon the auspicious wedding days of whichever girls it may be.
For by means of expenditures of wealth, they cause [the bridegroom] to act and cause [the bride] to be given;
indeed, those kings in this world become possessors of many wives. (15)
Or rather, in heaven, he indeed becomes a great deity possessing many wives, and being attended by numerous apsarases, he rejoices. (16)
One who gives a maiden finds a wife, but never otherwise;
for as many maidens as are given away without a bride-price, so many wives shall he obtain. || 17 ||
For as many wives endowed with such virtues as those are obtained;
he who gives a wife obtains a wife when the gift of a wife is performed in the Kṛta Yuga.
In the Tretā and Dvāpara ages, righteousness is not superior nor anywhere excellent; however, devotion to one's husband is the highest dharma, and having a single husband is supreme. 1.9

The vow of celibacy (brahmacarya) is declared to be the supreme state of having only one's own wife; its violation occurs through the taking of another's body. Therefore, the giving away of a woman [in marriage] is certainly not [the same as] giving.
In some cases, when a man is endowed with great capability and possesses a fiery temperament, the gift of a wife may be given without hindrance; indeed, it should be given as a beneficial act. ||21||
He whose dharma is not violated and who remains in the state of a maiden—even if he has many wives—by him indeed should a wife be given [in marriage]. (22)
In that regard, the fruit of giving away one's wife is that she becomes [one's] wife in another life;
this dharma is intended for one who is childless, with the hope of obtaining the fruit of a son. (23)
The best course, however, is the giving away of another's daughter; he should provide assistance with wealth like a father, and by that act, he shall obtain the fruit of having a wife.
This very rule is the most excellent; the gift of a wife is not the highest.
Yet, the fruit of giving a daughter in marriage is that one obtains wives—thus it has been established by all. (25)
Service to one's father and the performance of śrāddha rites are traditionally held to have the son as their fruit;
the Putreṣṭi sacrifice bestows the fruit of a son, while the Putrīṣṭi sacrifice bestows a daughter.
The gift of a son should be given auspiciously, never inauspiciously;
indeed, a gift accompanied by the taking of wealth yields no fruit.
A beautiful girl, adorned and free from the habit of taking others' property, or another maiden who is well-suited and devoid of all defects, should be given [in marriage]. (28)
Having brought about a union between the parents and having given them great wealth,
he then made [the child] his own, bathed him, and gave him ornaments and garments.
Having adorned it with ornaments, one should worship it with perfumes and garlands;
then, having observed the auspicious omens, as well as the lineage, the lunar mansion, the time, and so forth.

Having sought out an excellent groom worthy of the maiden and possessed of suitable qualities and other attributes, and having observed that the hearts of both are filled with mutual love known as *prema*... (31)
Having honored both according to the prescribed rite in the marriage festival pavilion,
she should be given to a worthy bridegroom who is most devoted to Brahman and an ascetic.
One should offer male and female servants, wealth, ornaments, garments, and vehicles to a learned man who is rich in virtuous qualities and capable of protecting a daughter. //33//
One should assign fields, gardens, wealth, grain, and groves;
one should likewise assign houses and utensils, and cause them to be given.
One should bestow a wish-fulfilling cow, a buffalo, elephants, horses, and bulls;
one should grant every means of livelihood that is appropriate for supporting a family.
Thus, for the giver of a daughter, as well as for the wealthy man who provides the dowry,
there shall indeed be innumerable enjoyments born of merit, even in heaven.
As many hairs as there are on the body of the maiden and her offspring,
for that many thousands of years he is honored in the heavenly world.
In that very pavilion, the unsurpassed gift of Lakṣmī should be performed;
it bestows all prosperity, happiness, and increases great sovereignty. ||38||
Having fashioned the incomparable Śrī-Lakṣmī out of gold according to the prescribed rite—
using a thousand [units], or half of that, or again half of that— ‍39.
Even with one hundred and eight [verses], she is endowed with all auspicious marks,
adorned with every ornament, the very personification of Fortune (Lakṣmī), and beautified by all her finery.
Having placed the auspicious four-armed Lakṣmī, or the eight-armed Mahālakṣmī,
within the maṇḍala, one should likewise place Viṣṇu Hari to her right.
Having worshipped Śrī and Hari with services such as offerings of royal enjoyments,
and having honored them after the fire-oblation, one should feed them and cause them to drink [the remains].
Then, having offered betel-leaf and performed the lustration ceremony (nīrājana) with prostrations,
one should thereafter offer a handful of flowers while prostrate like a staff.

One should bestow wealth upon a worthy recipient, a virtuous person, or a celibate student (brahmacārin), whether in the presence of water, in the presence of fire, or in the presence of Brahmins, making it publicly known.
In the presence of the Guru, in the presence of the Sun, in the presence of the gods, and before Hari, as well as before Lakṣmī—for one who performs such a gift, all prosperity is produced. ||45||
As the fruit of that, one's wives come to possess the luster of the color of the golden campaka flower;
likewise, daughters, excellent sons, and even sisters [are obtained]. (46)
They become male and female servants, as well as attendants;
in heaven they shall be the master of the apsarases, and in liberation they shall be the powerful lord of the Śaktis.
By the gift of Mahālakṣmī, one becomes a sovereign emperor and the husband of beautiful women;
by the gift of Kambharāśrī, one becomes an independent ruler endowed with all happiness. 48.
By the gift of a pair, one is born with a dual nature;
in ancient times, all the great sages were born as pairs.
Then, indeed, creation became manifold, enriched by the state of pairs;
for in the beginning, there was a conjugal union between the two Ṛṣis who were born together.
In the course of time, marriage between those of different lineages and castes occurs for the sake of benefiting all creation and for the purpose of consolidating affection. (51)

All the great sages performed [these acts] for the sake of obtaining woven garments and other such things; indeed, what were considered dharmas became adharmas, while those that were adharmas became dharma once again. (52)
In the course of time, beings are born even among gods, humans, and animals; through the passage of time, humans likewise adopt the nature of beasts and the nature of birds. (53)
In another age, humans will follow the dharma of the ṛṣis and the dharma of the gods;
and in another age, humans will follow the dharma of the Daityas and the Dānavas. ||54||
Yet those very same things become perverted again and again;
therefore, the fruit of giving is obtained there and there according to one's conduct. (55)
That which is to be obtained becomes already given; it is never the case that it is not given.
Thus, the auspicious fruit of giving away one's daughter is the attainment of a husband. (56)
In Ketumāla, the mothers give gifts to the youths; by that, they surely obtain husbands who are of beautiful form. (57)
By the gift of a sister, beautiful and auspicious sisters are adorned at the end;
the fruit of serving one's mother is supreme—one shall have birth with a virtuous mother on one's lap. (58)
Thus these phenomena remain hidden within the lotus of the earth;
those who do not know the reality do not perceive them, and they become deluded here and there. //59//
They indeed encounter supreme suffering and undergo affliction;
for they consider righteousness to be unrighteousness and do not practice charity at all.
"O ladies, even though you are my wives, that fruit was indeed given previously.
Listen, Lakṣmī, to that and also to the other cause for the attainment of a daughter."
The vow is called the Putrīvratam; indeed, that is the Kambharāśrī-vrata.
For when there is equality in the world regarding one's portion and even one's authority— (62)
In former times, the inheritance was equal for both sons and daughters;
at that time, the mother performed the vow for a daughter and the father performed the sacrifice for a son. (63)
In all worlds and everywhere, this became the supreme law:
my mother, Kambharāśrī, undertook the Putrikā-vrata for the sake of obtaining a daughter.
From that [act], a daughter named Santoṣā was born;
Vāsudevī herself, the goddess Lakṣmī, manifested in the form of a daughter,
who is called the virtuous sister of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa.
Śrī Nārāyaṇī said:
What kind of vow is that which is called the Putrī-vrata, consisting of a sacrifice?
Tell me its procedure, beginning from the start until the end, so that it may be fruitful.
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
Listen, O son, to the vow of the daughter which Kambharā, the mother, performed;
she then became Mahālakṣmī, Lalitā, and Śrī, possessed of a daughter.
On the first day of the dark fortnight of Phālguna, on the fifth lunar day (pañcamī),
the Putrīvrata should be performed by a mother endowed with the wealth of conjugal felicity.
On the fourth night, she should indeed be intent on drinking milk;
she should be devoted to celibacy and sleep upon the ground.
Having indeed fallen asleep in such a way that no evil dream might occur, and having risen after remembering Lalitā-Śrī-Mahālakṣmī for a moment, he [remained there]. (3.122.70)
Having meditated upon the four-armed Lakṣmī, who is the luster of golden campaka flowers and yellow pigment (rocanā), a young woman clad in green garments and adorned with golden ornaments; ||71||
Anointed with sandalwood and other unguents, fragrant with the scent of sārī musk,
her face serene, and her hands as delicate and radiant as the interior of a lotus.
Her limbs were proportioned to her form, her face was graced by a splendor like that of the moon,
and she shone with the beauty of lips reddened from chewing betel.
Having meditated upon her whose body is radiant with the fullness of youth and who possesses a robust form,
the virtuous woman should then bathe and worship her in a golden image.
O Mahālakṣmī, he should make this resolve: "Today I shall observe the Pañcamī vow for the sake of obtaining a daughter; may it be free from obstacles and reach completion for me. (75)
O Mother, for that reason I perform this beautiful worship for you;
please come, sit upon this seat, and accept the water for the feet and the auspicious arghya offering.
Then perform the ritual sipping of water (ācamana) and the bath with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta);
perform the consecration (abhiṣeka) with fragrant waters mixed with the essence of sandalwood.
Wear garments, ornaments, decorations, and finery;
apply auspicious substances, vermilion, and flower garlands. (78)
Enjoy incense, lamps, food offerings, the essence of milk, and milk-rice; enjoy various kinds of sweet foods as well as vegetables and fruits. (79)
Then accept the drinking water and the excellent betel leaf;
accept the waving of lights, the flower garland, and the constant prayer.
Then perform circumambulations and prostrations like a staff;
give me your daughter, who resembles you and is endowed with all auspicious fortune. (81)
She was beautiful in all her limbs, delightful, a lotus-like woman with a languid gait, a devoted servant who caused joy, possessing divine splendor, and like the moonlight of peace. (82)
Long-lived, healthy, a mistress of prosperity, virtuous, the ornament of her lineage, blessed with the fortune of husband and sons, and endowed with excellent qualities—[may she be so]. (83)
"Grant me a virtuous daughter who is devoted to you and devoted to the Supreme Lord.
Having thus prayed, one should then perform devotion in the form of kīrtana (sacred chanting). 84.
With a devoted mind, one should rotate the rosary according to one's capacity;
at midday as well, one should offer excellent food offerings, water, and betel.
Then one should cause [the deity] to sleep, cause [it] to rise, and offer the fruit;
one should offer water at night, along with the ārātrika lamp and excellent worship. ||86||
Then, having caused [the deity] to be honored with saffron, liquor, musk, camphor, flowers, and so forth, as well as an offering of milk-rice and other foods, one should perform a dance. 87.
She should perform chanting and singing, and keep a vigil at night;
then, the observer of the vow, having bathed in the morning and bathed her mother, [should proceed].
Having worshipped Mahālakṣmī and offered her a meal, followed by the waving of lights (ārātrika), he should say:
"Grant me a daughter; the vow has been completed, O Vrata, please grant me forgiveness. (89)
"O Supreme Goddess, by your majesty, may that which is incomplete attain completeness.
Having thus prayed and offered salutations, one should thereafter dismiss her.
Having fed her own husband and drunk the nectar-like water from his big toe, accompanied by the grace of Lakṣmī, she should then partake of her meal. (91)

One should give gifts according to the prescribed rule, according to one's ability and according to one's wealth—including everything such as suitable garments, ornaments, and cosmetics for the maiden. (92)
O Lakṣmī, one should feed eight maidens as a minimum and give them excellent sacrificial fees;
in this way, one should perform the vow that bestows the attainment of a daughter. 93.
Just as on the dark fortnight, so too on the bright fortnight, the observant woman, bestowing sons, should perform the twenty-fourth and fifth days according to the form described.
Then, in a dream, Mahālakṣmī shall come to you and say, "O virtuous one, after the conclusion of your year-long vow, a beautiful daughter shall be born to you. (95)
One should perform the concluding rite (udyāpana) accompanied by the gift of a bed,
and one should have the worship of Mahālakṣmī performed during the Sarvabhadraka festival.
One should cause a great festival to be held and give away a cow together with its calf;
one should also cause the gift of a maiden to be given according to one's capacity and wealth.
Homage to Lakṣmī, homage to Dhiṣṇyā, homage to Putrī, homage to Śrī;
homage be to you, Ramā, Lalitā, and Mahālakṣmī. ||98||
May Mahālakṣmī be pleased with these seasonal flower garlands and other offerings, as well as with the juices of seasonal fruits; and may she grant me a daughter. (99)
In this manner, one should always propitiate the goddess Kambharāśrī while observing the vow;
one should certainly not practice stinginess regarding wealth, for a daughter shall never become deceitful.

A pregnant woman, a woman who has recently given birth, a sick woman, or one who is impure may have [the rite] performed by another; otherwise, a woman who is in distress should perform it herself with great care.
For one endowed with extreme misfortune, the attainment of a daughter will surely occur through vows observed for three years, by a mere drop of the grace of Lalitā’s splendor. 102.
Upon seeing the birth of a daughter, one should offer the vow to the Goddess;
indeed, the vow must be performed for a long time until the fruit of a daughter is attained.
The commencement of this vow, dedicated to the worship of the clay image of Śrī Mahālakṣmī, was made on the dark fortnight of Phālguna, and its completion was performed by Kambharā. 104.
The daughter born from him was Lakṣmī, known as Santoṣā, the consort of Vāsudeva.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, has this most purifying vow been described. 105.
By performing the Putrīvrata, a man or a woman shall obtain a daughter;
Samudra performed this very rite and he obtained Lakṣmī as his daughter.
Sadāśiva performed his vow and obtained Jayā as his daughter;
Brahmā likewise performed his vow and obtained Lalitā as his daughter.
The quarters of the sky performed a vow and obtained Padmāvatī as their daughter;
Sūrya also performed a vow and indeed obtained Prabhā as his daughter.
Having performed the Kalpadruma vow, those very [trees] attained a daughter, Śrī;
having performed this very [vow], Divyavibhūti obtained a daughter, Māṇikī.
And Vairājī, having performed this vow, obtained Kamalā as her daughter;
and Khyāti, having performed this same vow, obtained Śrī Bhārgavī as her daughter.
Having performed that vow, Dharaṇī obtained Padmāvatī as her daughter;
thus it is, and not otherwise—what was undertaken by her has certainly borne fruit.
One desiring a daughter should indeed unite with his wife on the fifth,
or else on the seventh, ninth, eleventh, or thirteenth day.
When fifteen auspicious days have passed in the night,
by the depositing of the seed, that girl is born from the conception of a womb.
At the giving of the seed, Vāyudeva is on the left side, bestowing movement;
then indeed Kanyā is on the right side, bestowing a son.
Thus it is; there is no doubt. Therefore, having understood this, one should approach during the proper season.
From reciting or hearing this, there shall arise the excellent fruit that perpetuates one's lineage.
