Having performed a fire oblation with Varuṇa mantras, one should worship the gods with all the most excellent grains and whatever articles for giving there may be.
Having circumambulated me three times to the right, you oceans, together with the seas, should always pray to me: "O Oceans, may you always produce all flavors."
Just as you bring happiness to all creation, so likewise make me happy;
by your waters, all sins go to their complete destruction.
May my perfections increase; grant me, too, prosperity! And you, when given as a gift, may you augment my fortune.
May my treasuries, made of gold and silver, be like the oceans;
and may my happiness be inexhaustible both in this world and in the next. (15)
"O you who possess divine bodies, may you all be offered here for my sake;
may you all bestow both worldly enjoyment and liberation, and grant the great imperial sovereignty. (16)
At the end, they bestow heaven and truth;
they grant the earthly realm, the world of Virāj, the city of Śrī, the abode of nectar, the unmanifest, and the imperishable.
O sons of Rādhā, you must indeed grant us Goloka,
and may you always grant me oceans of bliss.
May they also bring satisfaction to the ancestors and act as their deliverers;
may they be the bestowers of happiness upon all those born within the lineage. (19)
Having thus entreated him, those seven oceans of gold should be given to the Guru, to the virtuous one, and likewise to Hari, the Lord. (3.132.20)
To the poor, the blind, and the wretched, various things should be given—
food, jewels, clothing, vessels, and wealth— as is appropriate.
One should feed Brahmins and virtuous men, as well as chaste and noble women;
one should also give gifts in every way to boys and girls.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, the giver of gifts goes indeed to the abode of Vairāja, then to Śrīpura, the immortal abode, and thereafter to the imperishable Goloka. (23)
He proceeds to the supreme world of Brahmā, the eternal state, being attended by Apsarases in a golden-colored celestial chariot. ||24||
Honored by my attendants, he goes to my eternal and beloved abode;
there, in that great ocean of bliss, he rejoices and is highly exalted.
Listen, Lakṣmī, to another unsurpassed great gift:
the jewel-cow, which bestows the world of cows and grants happiness. (26)
Having reached the day of purification (pavitradina), one should have an auspicious pavilion constructed;
one should likewise have an altar and a sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) made, and deposit gems there.
A wise man should place all the gifts to be given, as well as the jewels suitable for the gift of a cow, upon a black antelope skin.
Then, upon a heap of salt, a pile of *droṇa* measure, and upon a deer skin,
one should place a gem-encrusted cow together with her calf, both well-adorned.
The king should indeed fashion a great cow that grants all desires and purposes;
he should place eighty-one rubies in the mouth of the cow.
One should also place a hundred topazes on the snout,
a golden tilaka on the forehead, and a hundred pearls on the two eyes.
On his two eyebrows were two hundred corals, and likewise on his ears were two mother-of-pearl shells;
his horns were made of gold, and his head was fashioned from diamond gems.
On the neck, there was also a cloth made from a hundred pieces of go-meda stone and other gems; on the back, there were a hundred sapphire stones, and the sides were adorned with cat's-eye gems.
Its belly was made of crystal, its waist of a hundred saugandhika flowers,
its hooves of silver, and its tail fashioned from strings of pearls.
One should cause the sun-gem and moon-gem to be placed at the two nostrils, camphor and sandalwood at the nose, saffron-colored hair, and a silver navel.
One should place a hundred *gārutmata* gems at the base of the tail and excellent jewels on the breasts;
likewise, one should arrange other gems according to one's capacity. (36)
He saw his tongue as sugar, molasses as cow dung, clarified butter as urine, and both curd and milk in their true forms. (37)
At the tip of the handle, there was also a chowrie, and nearby a copper milking vessel;
he also had golden earrings and ornaments according to his wealth.
One should keep fodder, mouthfuls of grass, and grains for them nearby;
one should set aside a fourth part for the cow and store all the grains there. (39)
One should have sugarcanes made as well as a five-colored *jhullarī* (swing),
and likewise place various beautiful fruits within the pavilion.
Having performed the fire-oblation (homa) in the fire, one should likewise cause the invocation of the deities;
and according to the prescribed rite, one should worship me and the gods, and circumambulate the cow.
Having performed [the rite], the donor should request [blessings] after bowing to the Brahmins, to Hari, and to the Cow:
"O Goddess, you are the savior who takes the form of all the gods. (42)
Salutations to you, who are like a wish-fulfilling cow for all people;
O beloved Mother dwelling in Goloka, bestower of all desires! 43.
O Mother, who bestows merit, removes evil, and grants liberation, salutations to you;
O you who are Lakṣmī herself, deliver me in every way from this ocean. 44.
O bestower of all prosperity, O beloved of Kṛṣṇa, deliver me from the ocean!
Grant me the Vairāja heaven, as well as Śrīpura and immortality. 45.
"O Kamalā, grant me indeed Goloka, the imperishable abode";
having thus prayed, she should be given to a virtuous guru. 46.
These, as well as other jewels, grains, and whatever objects are fit to be given, should indeed be bestowed upon a Brahmin who is a worthy recipient and a devotee of Viṣṇu. (47)
All those things should be given to the mendicants with great devotion;
likewise, virtuous brāhmaṇas, as well as boys and girls, should be fed. 48.
Thus, by the giving of gifts, one shall partake of heaven as well as liberation;
one is always born endowed with worldly enjoyment, liberation, and great liberation. (49)
He is the savior of the ancestors and the savior of his family members;
indeed, he becomes a worthy recipient of all merit, consisting of the bliss of Brahman. (3.132.50)
Now I shall describe another great gift with which I likewise delight;
it is known as the Vase of the Great Elements, supreme and the accomplisher of all aims. (591)
Having reached an auspicious lunar day and having constructed an excellent pavilion,
one should then have the recitation of the Svasti-vāca and the Puṇyāha-vācana performed.
In the vicinity of the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), one should place clarified butter, rice, and other materials,
as well as the requisites for the gift, ornaments, clothing, food, fruits, and so forth.
Having established the guardians of the world, he should perform my invocation;
he should worship them all according to the prescribed rite and place a golden pitcher there.
Adorned with great jewels and the like, beautified by five sprouts, and measuring from one span up to a hundred finger-breadths in size. ||55||
One should place [the vessel] filled with milk and clarified butter, provided with garments, flowers, and other [offerings] appropriate for the ritual;
one should worship it there and also invoke the sacred bathing places (tīrthas). ||56||
One should place the Earth, accompanied by Varāha and adorned with Kamalā and others,
in that pavilion, and there one should worship Vināyaka.
One should worship Indra, Agni, Yama, Rakṣas, Varuṇa, as well as Anila, Kubera, and Maheśāna upon a heap of grain. (58)
There, one should likewise worship the Ṛgveda accompanied by a rosary,
the Yajurveda accompanied by a lotus, and the Sāmaveda accompanied by a lute.
Likewise, one should worship Atharvan, who is enriched by the *sruk* and *sruva* ladles and adorned with lotuses;
thereafter, one should fully worship Brahmā, Rudra, and Viṣṇu as well.
One should worship me, the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, together with the ruby (māṇikya) with a spirit of devotion, and thereafter perform the ārātrika ceremony. ||61||
All kinds of grains, ornaments, and various jewels; sandals, wooden shoes, umbrellas, chowries, seats, and mirrors. ||62||
Having prepared a bed, water-pots, lamps, and various articles intended for distribution as gifts, they circumambulated me three times.
One should give according to the ritual; then one should request the water-pot [with this mantra]:
"Obeisance to the Creator who has the form of the universe and is clothed in black. (64)
Salutations to You who are Rudra in form, who are peaceful, who are Viṣṇu, and who are the water-pot;
salutations to the abode of all, the giver of liberation—salutations again and again.
Salutations to you who are the abode of nectar and the bestower of the golden heaven;
salutations to you, O golden pitcher, the giver of the imperishable Śrīpura.
You are the abode of all gods, you are the refuge of all goddesses;
endowed with all supernatural powers, prosperity, and wealth—to you, we offer salutation after salutation. ||67||
You are the very form of the self consisting of the five elements; I give you as the embodiment of charity.
Grant me sovereignty here, and thereafter liberation in the hereafter.
Having thus prayed to the virtuous guru, who is likewise a yogi, [I say:
"This auspicious golden pitcher must be given by me to Hari. (69)
Other gifts, such as all kinds of donations, should be given as appropriate;
and food should be provided to everyone near the pavilion.
Whoever performs such a great festival consisting of the offering of the jar, his kingdom and great sovereignty shall certainly be attained on earth and in heaven. (71)
In the world of truth, in the realm of Vairāja, in the Vaiṣṇava city of Śrīpura, in the immortal Vaikuṇṭha, in the unmanifest abode, and also in the imperishable Goloka; ||72||
Having enjoyed the most excellent of enjoyments, he shall attain great liberation;
he shall liberate all his ancestors and always travel by means of a celestial chariot.
One should make a gift of even a very small water-pot according to one's wealth; likewise, the offering of a large jar, a pitcher, a wooden trough, or a cow-milking vessel. (74)
One should perform the offering of a water-pot and the offering of a treasury;
by that, there shall be enjoyment and liberation, bestowing happiness. (75)
By reciting, hearing, remembering, or even rejoicing in this, one shall indeed obtain the fruit of gifting a water-jar, which destroys all sins. (76)
Now I shall declare another gift to you; listen to me, O Lakṣmī!
One who desires prosperity should perform this great gift, the Lakṣmī-dāna.
One should cause an excellent pavilion to be constructed, adorned with jewels, gems, and the like, and beautified by pillars of plantain trees and arches made of all kinds of sprouts. (78)
Adorned with variegated garments and mirrors, beautified by golden jars, possessing a banner and an altar, and resplendent with sacrificial pits and seats. ||79||
It was resplendent with grain, ornaments, garments, jewels, gems, and rubies;
it was fully supplied with articles to be given away, and the sacrificial ground had been prepared by the officiating priests and others.
Accompanied by a water-pot and provided with the necessary materials for worship, one should [install] the great and virtuous Lakṣmī there in the center upon a golden seat. (81)
One should establish a beautiful golden image, fashioned according to one's wealth,
endowed with all ornaments and graced by every mark of beauty.
Adorned with all ornaments and garments, accompanied by Nārāyaṇa, one should [place] a golden image of Nārāyaṇa, four-armed and decorated with ornaments. (83)
One should establish the bridegroom-elect and perform the recitation for well-being (svastivācana);
likewise, one should worship Nārāyaṇa and Lakṣmī according to the prescribed rite.
Beginning with the ritual bathing, one should indeed perform the worship up to the final handful of flowers;
one should carry out the entire procedure according to the marriage rite as is appropriate. (85)
One should have the garland of choice placed upon the neck of Hari by the hands of Śrī;
one should also offer the food offering, water, betel, and perform the waving of lights (ārātrika).
Having performed the circumambulation, one should offer oblations of ghee and other excellent substances such as milk-rice;
thereafter, one should indeed give a gift to Mahālakṣmī and to Nārāyaṇa.
One should seek Lakṣmī and the supreme Lord Nārāyaṇa according to the prescribed rite, [saying]:
"You two are my mother and father; you are my protectors, guardians, and lords. (88)
O Blessed One, by this gift of Lakṣmī, may my prosperity increase;
and may there certainly be the dissolution of all portions of my sins. (89)
"By this offering to you, may I attain great sovereignty and supreme lordship;
may there be liberation for my ancestors, and likewise may there be the increase of my lineage."
May I attain the realm of Vaikuṇṭha, and from that, may I reach the imperishable state;
by the power of Your grace, may all kinds of prosperity dwell in my home. (91)
Having thus prayed, Lakṣmī should indeed be given to Nārāyaṇa;
thereafter, the image of Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa should be given to a virtuous seeker.
It should be given to the virtuous guru, to the temple seeking auspicious purposes, and all other jewels and such should be bestowed upon the community of monks. (93)
The virtuous woman should feed the holy ones, the Brahmins, children, the destitute, and young girls;
she should also feed the helpless, the blind, devoted twice-born men, and yogis. 94.
One should perform the giving of food and so forth, as well as the giving of clothing and so forth;
one should perform the giving of wealth and so forth according to one's faith and according to one's means. (95)
Thus, by the gift of Lakṣmī, one obtains the fruit of the gift of Lakṣmī;
one also attains the fruit of the gift of a daughter and the fruit of the gift of a wife. (96)

One shall attain the fruit of vows and sacrifices, the fruit arising from sacrificial sessions (satra), the fruit of iṣṭāpūrta rites, the fruit of all forms of giving, and the fruit of the Cāturmāsya observances. ||97||
Having enjoyed sovereignty even in this world through the grace of Lakṣmī, he shall attain the kingdom of heaven, the kingdom of truth, and the station of Vairāja. ||98||
Then, having enjoyed the kingdom of Śrīpura, he shall attain Goloka;
and having enjoyed the supreme Vaikuṇṭha, he thereafter goes to the imperishable abode (Akṣara-pada). ||99||
Immersed in the lake of the bliss of Brahman, he is glorified in the world of Brahman;
likewise, the giver of gifts obtains enjoyment and liberation according to his desire.
O Lakṣmī, these great gifts have thus been described to you;
likewise, there are other various kinds of gifts as well in this world. (101)
The gift to Sūrya, the gift to Candra, and also the gift to Mahendra;
likewise, the supreme gift to Brahmā, the gift to Viṣṇu, and the gift to Śambhu. (102)
The gift of Kubera, the gift of Yama which is a source of auspiciousness, the gift of life, the gift of the senses and so forth, and the gift of a golden image; || 103 ||
In all those cases, one should appropriately give the gift of a yantra, as well as the gift of the imperishable Brahman and the gift of Goloka. 104.
The gift of Vaikuṇṭha as well as the offering of Śrīpura,
and likewise other gifts that one may personally desire.
One should give all of these for the sake of attaining powers in another birth, or one should give the most excellent gift of devotion for the sake of liberation. 106.
From reciting, hearing, remembering, or rejoicing in this, one shall obtain the entire merit of giving, according to one's faith and purity. (107)

Thus ends the one hundred and thirty-second chapter, titled "The Description of the Rituals for the Great Gift of the Seven Oceans, the Great Gift of the Jewel-Cow, the Great Gift of the Vessel of the Great Elements, the Great Gift of Lakṣmī, and Other Such Great Gifts," in the Third Section on the Continuation of the Dvāpara Age of the Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā. || 132 ||
Śrī Nārāyaṇī Śrī said: O Kṛṣṇakānta, my beloved, I have heard about the great fruit of giving,
which was stated by you, O Lord, that it should be bestowed on an auspicious day.
All auspicious days have been described by you and understood by me; I wish to know which among them is the most meritorious day—please tell me that.
Śrī Puruṣottama said: That day on which my manifestation occurred upon this earth as the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa is indeed the most meritorious of days.
This very eighth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Kārttika is the most excellent for making gifts;
it is also considered the best day for a donor, serving as the donor's own birthday.
Even the days known as Kalpas become most excellent;
the months and days of Brahmā are likewise superior for the purpose of giving gifts.
I shall declare the thirty names of the months; learn them from me, for by the mere recitation of which one becomes endowed with the merit of the Vedas.
The first is the Śvetakalpa, while the second is Nīlalohita;
the third is Vāmadeva, and the fourth is named Rāthantara. || 7 ||
The fifth is named Raurava, and the sixth is called Devadina;
the seventh is named Bṛhat, and the eighth is called Kandarpa.
The ninth is named Sadya, while Īśāna is considered the tenth;
the eleventh is named Tamas, and the twelfth is Sārasvata.
The thirteenth is called Udāna, while the fourteenth is Gāruḍa;
the fifteenth is Kaumārya, and the sixteenth is Nārasiṃhaka.
The seventeenth is named Samāna; the eighteenth consists of the Āgneya hymns;
the nineteenth is named Soma; and the twentieth is considered to be Mānava.
That is remembered as the twenty-first day of Brahmā;
Vaikuṇṭha is the twenty-second, and Lakṣmī is likewise the twenty-third.
The twenty-fourth is Sāvitrī, the twenty-fifth is Aghoraka;
the twenty-sixth is Vārāha, and the twenty-seventh is Vairāja. || 13 ||
The twenty-eighth is Gaurī, the twenty-ninth is Maheśvara,
and the thirtieth is indeed the Pitṛkalpa, which is considered by Brahmā to be the new moon (Kuhū).

Among these, those days which are the "days of the Blessed One" (bhagavaddināni) and the "days of Śrī" (śrīdināni), as well as the auspicious lunar days named after Śiva and others, are meritorious for those who perform acts of giving.
O Rame, the days of Hari’s birth and the zodiac signs of Hariṇī’s birth are always meritorious, suitable for vows, and fit for the giving of gifts.
Indeed, all people of narrow hearts are not capable of performing those noble acts of giving which are prescribed for those of magnanimous mind. (17)
Whenever a person's mind becomes intent upon the duty of giving,
on that very day the donor should swiftly perform the act of giving.
Faith has departed, time has passed, and enthusiasm too;
the worthy recipient has gone and the object [of merit] is lost—it will never return again. (19)
All prosperities are transitory, and likewise life itself is transitory;
even one's intentions are transitory—one should employ them toward virtuous deeds.
One should fully satisfy Nārāyaṇa, Hari, Kṛṣṇa, my Lord who is the Master of the Imperishable, as well as the incarnations, the lords, the gods, and the sages. || 2.1 ||
O Lakṣmī, one should satisfy the planets with gifts, for they are my own forms;
for the attainment of all desires, one should always cause the pacification of the planets to be performed. 22.

One who desires prosperity, or one who desires peace, or one who desires the nourishment of his own life-span, or one who longs for a lineage, or one who seeks happiness, should perform the sacrifice to the planets (grahayajña). ||23||

On an auspicious day as declared by the Brahmins, having performed the recitation by the Brahmins (brāhmaṇavācana) and having installed the planets and the deities presiding over the planets, one should perform the fire-oblation (homa).
The planetary sacrifice (grahayajña) is considered to be the ten-thousand oblation (ayutahoma), the hundred-thousand oblation (lakṣahoma),
and likewise the ten-million oblation (koṭihoma), according to the requirements of the task and one's capacity.
The sacrifice to the nine planets (navagrahamakha) is considered to consist of ten thousand oblations;
[one should prepare] an area two spans wide to the northeast of the sacrificial pit.
Having made the altar square, facing north, adorned with the height of the sacrificial grass and surrounded by two Brahmins, one should then perform the fire-rite.
One should invoke the deities therein: Sūrya, Soma, Maṅgala, Budha, Guru, Kavi, Śanaiścara, Rāhu, and Ketu. 28.
One should place the Sun in the center, Mars in the south, Jupiter likewise in the north, Mercury in the northeast, and Venus in the east. (29)
To the southeast he placed the Moon, and likewise Saturn to the west;
Rāhu to the southwest, and Ketu to the northwest.
Or one should place the auspicious subordinate deities upon rice grains:
Īśa for the Sun, and Pārvatī as the subordinate deity for the Moon. (3.1)
[One should worship] Skanda as the deity of Mars, Hari as the subordinate deity of Mercury, Brahmā as that of Jupiter, and Indra as the subordinate deity of Venus. ||32||
One should install Yama as the attendant deity of Śani, Kāla as that of Rāhu,
and Citragupta as the attendant deity of Ketu.
Then, one should establish the respective deities in their various places in due order: Agni, Jala, Pṛthvī, Viṣṇu, Indra, and likewise Śacī.
One should also establish Prajāpati, the Bhogins, and Brahmā;
as well as Vināyaka, Durgā, Vāyu, and Ākāśa. (35)
One should invoke the two, Aśvin and Kumāraka, with the *vyāhṛti* mantras;
one should likewise meditate upon Ravi as being red in color, and Maṅgala also as red.
One should then recollect Soma and Śukra as white in color, Budha and Guru as tawny, Śani and Rāhu as black, and Ketu as smoke-colored. (37)
Garments and flowers of the colors of the planets should be offered, as well as fragrant incense and likewise a canopy above. (38)
One should offer everything worthy of worship, such as fruits and flowers, in the act of honoring;
specifically, one should offer rice with jaggery to Sūrya and milk-porridge with ghee to Soma.
One should offer sacrificial porridge (saṃyāva) to Maṅgala, a milk-pudding (kṣīrakullarī) to Budha,
rice with curd (dadhyodana) to Guru, and rice with jaggery (guḍaudana) to Śukra.
One should offer *kṛsarā* to Śanaiścara, beans to Rāhu, and rice mixed with various colors to the Ketus; thereafter, one should worship the gods.
To the northeast, he should place a water-pot provided with curd and unbroken rice,
joined with mango sprouts, and accompanied by a pair of fruits and garments.
One should place [the vessel] joined with the five jewels and install Varuṇa;
one should indeed invoke the sacred fords and the oceans there in the water.
And having brought earth from an elephant, a horse, a carriage-track, an anthill, a crossroads, a pool, and a cow-pen, together with water containing all medicinal herbs. ||44||
There, the Brahmin should place [the materials] for the purpose of bathing the patron;
he should perform the fire-oblation (homa) with clarified butter, barley, rice, sesame seeds, and so forth. 45.
The sacrificial fuel sticks (samidh) are, in order: Arka, Pālāśa, Khadira, Apāmārga, Pippala, Audumbara, Śamī, Durvā, and Kuśa. ||46||
For each [deity], one hundred and eight or twenty-eight oblations should be offered with honey, clarified butter, curd, and likewise with fuel-sticks.
There, one should prepare sacrificial fuel-sticks (samidh) from those branches, a span in length, without leaves; one should offer them there with the mantras of the deities. ||48||
Having offered ten oblations of cooked sacrificial porridge (caru), fuel-sticks smeared with ghee, and various kinds of edible foods, he should likewise offer oblations with the Vyāhṛtis.
One should offer the consecrated sacrificial oblation (caru) to each respective deity;
then one should give the final oblation (pūrṇāhuti) and bathe the patron of the sacrifice.
May all the gods who are worshipped here protect you;
likewise, may others who are worthy of worship guard you on every side. (5.1)
Thus, having been bathed along with his wife, the sacrificer gave sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā) both to the Brahmins and also to the households, according to their merit.
One should offer a tawny cow to the Sun, a conch to the Moon,
a red bull to Mars, and gold to Mercury.
One should give yellow cloth to Jupiter, a white horse to Venus,
a black cow to Saturn, and likewise iron to Rahu.
One should give a goat to Keśava, or as many cows as there are [syllables], or one should give gold, so that the Guru may be fully satisfied. (55)
O Rame, when a gift is given by Your Majesty regarding an object worthy of being given, preceded by my propitiation, it becomes the bestower of the most excellent merit. 56.
O Mother, you are the earth-formed cow, affectionate toward Kṛṣṇa;
may you be my merit-bestowing and sin-removing cow, and grant me eternal peace. (57)
You are the conch of multitudes of merits, the personified form of auspiciousness;
residing eternally in the hand of Kṛṣṇa, grant me peace incessantly. (58)
O Bull, whose nature is Dharma, you are established within the form of Kṛṣṇa;
may you grant me a foundation for all bliss and joy. (59)
O Gold, son of Fire, seed of gold for the radiant one;
grant me peace and prosperity, you who bestow the fruit of infinite merit.
O yellow-robed one, eternally supreme, divine, and beloved of Śrī Kṛṣṇa—grant me peace and prosperity, and make me dear to Kṛṣṇa. (61)
You are Hayagrīva, you are Viṣṇu, the drinker of the potency of the nectar-herbs;
O Lord, Master of the Ruby-Horse, grant me nectar and peace.
O Kṛṣṇā, you possess the nature of a cow; you are the consort of Kṛṣṇa, the daughter of Kṛṣṇa, and a noble woman.
You are the sustainer of Kṛṣṇa and you remain so; nourish me always.
Among the elements, you are the iron servant who performs every menial task; O Lord, white as an autumnal arrow, grant me eternal peace. (64)
O Goat, you are the very form of Time; seen in a dream, you are terrifying.
O Carrier of Agni, being duly worshipped, grant me perpetual peace.
May cows, who are indeed the very form of Kṛṣṇa, who are the refuge of all lords and gods, and who are capable of uplifting everyone, be present for my prosperity in every way. (66)
O bed, you have been enjoyed by Kṛṣṇa; you are purifying and bestow sons. May you always grant me prosperity, and may my wife never be empty [of you]. (67)
"Since all the jewels of the gods are indeed composed of cloth,
let them be offered here and fashioned into jeweled garments within my house."
The gift of land is the supreme gift, as is the gift of gold; may both the prosperity of food and the prosperity of wealth be brought about for me through this offering. (69)
Having thus entreated and made a formal request, one should especially give in charity;
one attains all desires and is glorified in heaven after death.
But whichever planet constantly causes affliction to one of meager wealth, that one should be worshipped with great effort and propitiated with the remaining offerings. (71)
Just as with armor, the pacification of afflictions occurs through worship;
one should give a complete sacrificial fee and avoid stinginess regarding wealth.

During marriages, festivals, sacrifices, consecrations, and other such rites, one should perform [this practice] which grants relief from agitation, for the sake of removing obstacles and for the sake of pacification. (73)
The devotee performed the auspicious sacrifice to the nine planets (*navagrahamakha*), consisting of ten thousand oblations (*ayutahoma*),
which was a great ritual centered upon the primordial Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa.
There, the sacrificer should pray to me and to the divine, sovereign goddesses;
the sacrificer, having been bathed with the waters of sacred fords by those learned in the Vedas.
The officiating brahmins, acting as protectors of the gods, should bestow benedictions:
"May Anādi-Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, joined by Nārāyaṇī, [grant them]. (76)
May Śrī Kṛṣṇa, joined with Rādhikā, and Nārāyaṇa, together with Śrī, who are eternally united with their respective hosts of liberated souls, protect you steadfastly at all times. 77.
May the emanations beginning with Vāsudeva protect you, the worshiper;
as well as Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa, and the lords of the directions beginning with Mahendra. (78)
The lawful wives, all together, and the nine planets beginning with the Sun;
the Vasus, the treasures, the Rudras, the seers, the sages, and the bulls.
Gods, Dānavas, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and Pannagas;
the wives of the gods, trees, Nāgas, Daityas, and the hosts of Apsarases. || 3.133.80 ||
The bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, and others; the Rudras, the Gaṇas, and the lords of the Gaṇas; all the Yoginīs and Śaktis; and the weapons, missiles, and vehicles. ||81||
Jewels and medicinal herbs, obstacles and time, those born of the lineage of Time—all these, as well as all sacred fords (tīrthas), are indeed limbs of Time. 82.
"May these [deities] consecrate you, protect you, and cause you to flourish. Having been thus increased by blessings, he, wearing white garments, should offer [the oblation]. (83)
He should give all kinds of various sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā) to the Brahmins and to his preceptor;
he should feed the Brahmins in many ways, as well as virtuous men and virtuous women.
He [should satisfy] boys and girls, as well as the poor, the blind, and the wretched, along with beggars who live by fate, with sweet foods, milk-rice (pāyasa), and other such delicacies. ||85||
One should have ten thousand oblations performed by the most eminent of Brahmins, or else one may perform them oneself, endowed with Vedic learning, good character, and vows. (86)
Therefore, one should by all means perform the expiation for the planetary sacrifice;
by that, there shall be pacification of the planets, the affliction shall perish, and one shall become happy.

Thus ends the one hundred and thirty-third chapter, titled "The Description of the Most Meritorious Days and the Demonstration of Rite for Appeasing the Planets and Worship," in the third section, the Dvāpara Age, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Puruṣottama said: Listen, O Śrī Nārāyaṇī, to this Lakṣahoma,
a sacrifice for the planets that grants all desires, pacifies all obstacles, and brings happiness.

Having observed the strength of the planets and stars and having performed the recitation by Brahmins, [one should perform this rite] which is dear to the ancestors, most excellent, and bestows the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation. || 2 ||
To the north-east of the house, one should have a new pavilion constructed;
it should be twelve cubits in width, square in shape, and facing north.
One should cause it to be surrounded by a wall ten cubits or eight cubits high;
one should have the ground made to slope toward the east and north, providing complete protection.
One should construct a square pit (kuṇḍa) with a girdle (mekhalā), provided with a womb (yoni),
located in the north-eastern part below the pavilion (maṇḍapa), and colored with pigments and other materials.
The girdle should likewise be four fingers in width and four fingers in height;
it should be auspicious, measuring two cubits in width and four cubits in length.
For a Lakṣahoma, one should indeed construct a beautiful sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) to its northeast,
measuring three spans (vitasti).
That sacrificial mound (sthaṇḍila) should be constructed by means of craftsmanship, sloping toward the northeast, square on all sides, and raised to a height equal to its width.
For the establishment of the gods, the three embankments (vapras) should share the same measurement;
the first embankment should be made two finger-breadths high, which brings auspiciousness.
Each of the two embankments (vapra) above is likewise one finger-breadth high;
the wall above that is ten fingers high, and the sacrificial mound (sthaṇḍila) is likewise above that.
There, one should invoke the deities upon a seat of flowers and rice:
the Sun and others, as well as the presiding deities (adhidevas) and the secondary deities (pratyadhidevatās). || 11 ||
One desiring prosperity should worship Garuḍa there as supreme:
"O devotee of Viṣṇu, O great devotee, you are indeed the remover of poison and sin. (1-2)
"O bestower of happiness upon the devotees of Viṣṇu, grant me peace and prosperity.
Having thus addressed the water-pot according to the prescribed rite, one should perform one hundred thousand fire-oblations (lakṣahoma).
One should perform oblations exceeding the number of fuel-sticks for the sake of pacification;
one should cause a stream of clarified butter from a vessel to fall upon the fire.
One should offer oblations with a ladle made of Udumbara wood and as long as a forearm;
one should cause [the officiant] to recite the hymns dedicated to Agni, Viṣṇu, Rudra, and Indra. 15.
One should cause [the officiant] to recite the Mahāvaiśvānara Sāman and the Jyeṣṭhasāman;
one should cause the sacrificer to bathe and should perform the recitation of the Svastivācana.
With a tranquil mind, he should also give abundant sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇās);
he should bestow these fees upon either four officiating priests (ṛtvij) or two.
He should likewise offer gifts of various foods to be chewed and eaten, as well as cows and precious gems.
Beds with their coverings, and golden bracelets. || 18 ||
One should give sacrificial grains, finger-rings for purification, golden necklaces, ornaments, and wealth; one should not practice stinginess regarding one's possessions.
One should perform the gift of food, which bestows abundance and a good harvest;
one should feed virtuous Brahmins and children with various kinds of food. (3.134.20)
A sacrifice lacking food burns the kingdom; one lacking mantras burns the officiating priests;
and one lacking sacrificial fees burns the patron. There is no enemy equal to a sacrifice [performed] without these.
One who possesses desires, having performed a hundred thousand oblations (lakṣahoma), shall obtain his heart's desire;
one seeking a son obtains sons, and one seeking wealth obtains wealth.
One desiring a wife shall obtain a beautiful wife; one desiring a husband shall obtain a beloved husband;
likewise, one who has lost his kingdom shall regain his kingdom, and one desiring prosperity shall attain prosperity. (23)
One who desires honor obtains honor, and one who desires preeminence obtains preeminence praised by the world;
likewise, one who desires victory obtains perpetual victory. ||24||
Whatever desire he prays for— whether it be sovereignty or even supernatural power—
he obtains that very thing through sacrifice by virtue of the favor of the planets.
He who performs sacrifice without desire goes to the Supreme Brahman;
there he enjoys supreme pleasures and attains infinite happiness. ||26||
Now, O Nārāyaṇīśrī, listen to that sacrifice which is superior to this:
the Koṭihoma sacrifice, which is a hundred times greater than this, comes into being. ||27||
With oblations, faith, sacrificial fees, and the fruit [of the rite],
one should invoke the planetary deities and the secondary deities in the pavilion.
Having invoked the secondary deities (pratyupadevas), one should perform the purification bath and other rites;
for a crore-fold homa, [the altar] should be four cubits square on all sides.
One should construct a sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) provided with two curved openings at the base and three tiers (mekhalā);
the first tier is two finger-breadths high, while the second is three finger-breadths high.
The third [measurement] is four finger-breadths in both height and width;
the vulva (yoni) is one span (vitasti) in length and six or seven finger-breadths in width. ||31||
Raised in the middle like the back of a tortoise, elevated by one finger-breadth at the sides,
resembling the trunk-tip of an elephant, and likewise elongated and adorned with a hole.
The altar (vedī) should be four vitastis in measure, square, and provided with three trenches (vapra); it is adorned with lines and other features having a luster like that of an aśvattha leaf.
The measurement of the embankment is as previously stated, and the height of the altar (vedi) is likewise.
The pavilion (maṇḍapa) should be sixteen cubits in size, four-faced, and beautifully adorned. ||34||
In the pavilion, one should station a twice-born Brāhmaṇa learned in the Ṛgveda at the eastern door;
one who knows the Yajurveda at the southern door; and one who knows the Sāmaveda at the western door. (35)
In the north, one who knows the Atharva Veda, and likewise eight others seeking to perform the fire oblations—
thus, filled with devotion, one should worship these twelve learned men.
With saffron, unbroken grains of rice, ornaments, and the like, as well as garments, garlands, and ointments,
[one should recite] the Rātrisūkta, the Rudrasūkta, and the most auspicious Pavamāna hymn.
First, one should have the Bahvṛcas recite the Śāntipāṭha from the beginning:
the Śānti, the Śākra, the Saumya, the Kauṣmāṇḍa, and the Śānti itself. (38)
Then, he should cause the learned Brahmins who know the Yajurveda to recite the Suparṇa,
the Vairāja, the Āgneya, and the Rudrasaṃhitā, while providing them with sacrificial fees.
Likewise, the westernmost twice-born man should recite the Jyeṣṭha Sāman,
the Śānti hymn, the Saura Sūkta, and the supreme Śākunaka hymn.
A twice-born man situated in the north should recite for the sake of nourishment and great sovereignty;
in this case, an oblation (homa) should be performed by the best of the twice-born using five or seven [mantras]. 41.
And the ritual for the stream of wealth (vasordhārā) consists of ten more [oblations] than the previous;
by performing the koṭi-homas in this manner, one shall attain all desires. ||42||
He shall go to the station of Viṣṇu and attain the station of Indra;
having attained the Vairāja station, he goes to my imperishable abode.
Whatever fruit one obtains by performing eighteen thousand horse-sacrifices, that one enjoys from a *koṭi-homa*.
Thousands of killings of Brahmins and billions of killings of embryos are destroyed by my yoga alone through the Koṭihoma sacrifice. (45)
Whoever, desiring my favor, should perform the three graha-yajñas, shall also attain peace from afflictions through my power. (46)
Whoever should hear this, or cause it to be heard, or even remember it, shall not suffer affliction from the planets; indeed, any such affliction currently occurring shall perish.
In whose house these three planetary sacrifices are kept written, there shall be no affliction for children, nor disease, nor captivity. (48)
Listen, Lakṣmī, to how the forms of the planets should be fashioned from gold:
[the form of the Sun] seated upon a lotus, with hands holding lotuses, possessing a luster like the interior of a lotus. (49)
The Sun should be depicted as possessing seven horses and seven reins, with two arms, wearing a crown, adorned with earrings, encircled by a halo, and endowed with radiance.
Śaśin should be depicted as white, wearing white garments, with white horses and a white vehicle; he has two arms, holds a mace in his hand, and bestows boons. 51.
Wearing red garlands and garments, holding a spear, a trident, a mace, and other weapons, four-armed and with white body hair, Maṅgala is considered the bestower of boons. 52.
Wearing yellow garlands and garments, with a luster like that of the Karṇikāra flower, holding a sword, shield, and mace in his hands, and seated upon a lion, the planet Mercury bestows boons. 53.
Bṛhaspati and Śukra are yellow and white respectively;
both have four arms and hold a staff, a rosary, and a water-pot.
Śanaiścara should be depicted with the luster of sapphire, holding a trident and granting boons, mounted upon a vulture, and bearing a bow and arrow. 55.
And Rāhu is considered to be seated upon a blue lion-throne, possessing a black luster;
all [the others] are smoke-colored, two-armed, equipped with maces, and filled with wrath.
Their banners should be made in the form of vultures and likewise as bestowers of boons;
all should be depicted wearing crowns and measuring one hundred and eight finger-breadths in height.
Listen, Lakṣmī! Formerly, in the land of Mālava, there was a Vaiśya named Lohāṅgāra who possessed great abundance of wealth and grain. (58)

Through his business activities, the great merchant became the protector of the royal treasury, as well as the guardian of the country’s subjects and wealth, and likewise a provider of resources. (59)
In whose house there were horses and elephants,
as well as gardens, various parks, and auspicious mansions.
There were golden lion-thrones and water-pots made of gold and silver;
and women richly adorned with golden ornaments and wearing strings of jewel necklaces.
Others dwell in the sky in celestial palaces as radiant as the sun,
each having a hundred male servants, a hundred female servants, and a constant retinue of a hundred thousand attendants.
His officials become intent upon the acquisition of wealth;
among the subjects, the king, and the circle of ministers, his opinion and judgment are held in high esteem. (63)
Although all the months were auspicious, since the planets were malevolent for him, Śani and the others were situated in inauspicious places; indeed, he was afflicted by them. (64)
He became ill, nearly dying; his wealth and all his possessions were plundered by the king, and his sons were cast into prison. (65)
At that time, he indeed perceived his palaces as if consumed by fire;
all these activities then became almost entirely lost.
Due to this stain, his reputation has suffered even among his subjects;
he now experiences great suffering that has come upon him from all sides. (67)
Now, his preceptor was a brahmin, a great sage named Amṛṣāyana;
he was a yogi who perceived the three periods of time, a knower of the Vedas, and a worshiper of the planets.

He was a devotee of Nārāyaṇa, adorned with the practice of vows; he was a virtuous man, rich in the quality of goodness (sattva), firm in his commitment to truth, and possessed of great learning. ||69||
Having heard that his disciple Lauhāṅgāra was submerged in suffering,
he then came to his house to see him, impelled by compassion.
Seeing his disciple submerged in distress—deprived of his wealth and reputation, and likewise afflicted by the punishment of his son and disease—he was moved to supreme compassion. (71)
He said to that Lohāṅgāraka: "Perform propitiation for this planet;
through domestic rites of propitiation and planetary sacrifices, the affliction will surely depart. (72)
Worship the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama, with an undistracted mind; you shall attain supreme bliss.
Thus addressed, he too, suddenly filled with a spirit of devotion,
accepted the command saying "So be it," and had a pavilion constructed.
On the eighth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, he fashioned a beautiful pool,
as well as golden images of the planets and a golden image of myself.
Together with you and Lakṣmī, he made her exceedingly beautiful,
her form adorned with garments, ornaments, cosmetics, and the like.
Then, in the pavilion, he invoked the presiding deities and their respective secondary deities upon their seats and worshipped them according to the prescribed rites.
He chose one hundred and eight Brahmins for the purpose of recitation;
he had them perform ten million recitations in every way, as they were knowers of the Vedas.
At the conclusion of the worship, he gave a secret gift from a deep pit in the earth,
having extracted one hundred thousand gold coins, excluding the final one.
Whatever was not manifest, that he gave as gifts to the Brahmins— gems, rubies, and diamonds, as well as cows, elephants, horses, and so forth.
She offered the prescribed food offerings and whatever drinks were appropriate;
likewise, she presented pure, sattvic bali-offerings to the gods.
He fed the Brahmins and virtuous men, as well as virtuous women, boys and girls, and those who were wretched, miserable, and suffering. (82)
He devotedly fed those who were without support, those without wealth, the crippled, the poor, the virtuous, and even the people of Puṇyajanapura. ||83||
They performed my worship according to the prescribed rites, and they too [performed theirs];
through the merit of the sacrifice for the pacification of the planets, and by my grace, both they and I [attained success]. ||84||
Then, indeed, the disease quickly vanished from the body of Lohāṅgāra;
consequently, the king became healthy and was filled with compassion for him. ||85||
Having summoned him, the lord of the gods bestowed upon him great honor, exceeding even his former status,
and granted him the position of chief minister.
The subjects also bowed down and honored him with respect;
then the king himself released his sons from prison.
Then the thieves, their hopes shattered and terrified by the fear of the king,
threw everything they had stolen into the courtyard during the night.
The light was revealed through his offspring, and what was seen at dawn was reported to him;
all wealth was obtained, and then I rejoiced because of the pacification of the planetary affliction.
Thus, having obtained all of that, she prepared it for the act of giving:
gold, gems, rubies, diamonds, and silver.
He commenced the great Vaiṣṇava sacrifice with the twice-born;
he gave away all the materials that had been gathered as auspicious sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇās).
O Lakṣmī, I was indeed pleased with each of those gurus and granted them my own vision at their final ablution ceremony along with you.
Requested for a boon, he chose instead the status of a servant.
I said to him, "Build a beautiful mansion for me and place me within that mansion. (93)
"Having established yourself, always perform service and be a servant in every way.
Having done so quickly, he indeed became a householder and performed that very servitude. 94.
Having become a supreme Vaiṣṇava, he offered himself to King Devala by name and served me, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama). 95.
He also made the sacrifice Vaiṣṇava and likewise made the subjects Vaiṣṇava;
by means of his own yoga, he rendered them devoted and engaged in auspicious deeds.
Having remained on earth for a hundred thousand years and enjoyed heaven for eight yugas,
he dwells in Satyaloka for ten million years and in Vairāja for a parārdha.
Having eaten, he went even to Vaikuṇṭha, my imperishable abode;
O Mahālakṣmī, this story was set forth in a previous kalpa. (98)
"Today, my attendant together with his family resides in my abode;
by thus performing this sacrifice to the planets, one shall attain heaven and liberation. (99)
Upon the destruction of suffering, he obtains daily happiness, joy, and supreme delight;
he attains the disappearance of what is undesirable and the persistence of what is desired. (3.134.1) 100.
O King, for one who worships [it] constantly, there is indeed eternal peace;
affliction from the planets shall not arise, nor that born of yakṣas or rākṣasas.
Neither created by thieves nor by Time, nor even by the gods—when a planet [is adverse], I, the bestower of power, protect my Vaiṣṇava devotee. 102.
From hearing, reciting, remembering, and rejoicing in this, one obtains a peace equal to the pacification of planetary afflictions; there is no doubt in this matter.

Thus ends the one hundred and thirty-fourth chapter, titled "The Description of the Rules for the Lakṣa-japa, Homas, Koṭi-japa, and Homas in the Planetary Sacrifice (Graha-makha) within the Second Dvāpara Age of the Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā; and the Account of how Lohāṅgāraka, a Vaiśya, regained all his lost property through the pacification of the planets (graha-śānti) after its total loss. || 134 ||
Śrī Puruṣottama said: Listen, O Śrī Nārāyaṇī; formerly you were praised by Dakṣa, and you yourself spoke of the manifestations of Lalitā and Lakṣmī.
Dakṣa asked his mother: "Tell me which manifestations of yours exist here on earth, where they are located, and which ones will appear in the future."
By the power of this worship, may I always destroy obstacles;
and by honoring you, may I destroy the afflictions of the planets and the defects of past actions.
Then you spoke of the auspicious fruit of your own worship, and indeed of the misfortunes that befall the worshipper of the Great Lakṣmī known as Lalitā. (4)
Those who perform my worship will undoubtedly perish;
whatever forms they may have and wherever they may be. (5)
I shall describe them to you; listen, O Dakṣa Prajāpati.
I am Śrī Devī, abiding in the abode of the Imperishable, together with Puruṣottama.
The beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇī, the illustrious Supreme Goddess;
the Brahmī, the Muktānikā, the Brāhmī, the Kārṣṇī, the Nārāyaṇī, and Ramā.
Vāsudevī, Vairājī, Hiraṇyā, Hariṇī, Prabhā, Mahālakṣmī, Kambharāśrī, Lalitā, Kamalā, and Calā. || 8 ||
She is the sovereign goddess, the power of Viṣṇu, the lunar goddess, and the golden deity;
she is the seer’s wife, the perfected one, the yoginī, the virtuous, the true, and the devoted wife.
Prabhvī, Dhāmā, Jayā, Bhaumī, Maheśī, Bhūrnarāyaṇī, Pāśavatī, Māṇikyā, Mārūpā, and Śrīharipriyā. (3.135.10)
The remover of suffering, the auspicious Queen Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇī Satī;
the beloved of Brahmā in the abode of Brahmā, and Mahālakṣmī in Śrīpura. 11.
Lakṣmī is at Kuṅkumavāpī, while Mahālakṣmī is on Mount Raivata;
Vyāghreśvarī is at Māhiṣa, and Dhenukarṇikā is at Gokarṇa.
Mādhavī is in the field of Akṣara and Camatkāra;
Viśālākṣī is in Vārāṇasī, and Liṅgadhāriṇī is in Naimiṣa. ||13||
I am Lalitā at Prayāga, Kāmākṣī on Gandhamādana; I am the goddess Kumudā at Mānasa, and Viśvakāyā in Cidambaram.
In Gomanta she is named Gomatī; on Mount Mandara she is Kāmagā; in Caitraratha she is Madotkaṭā; and in the place called Vāraha she is Jayantī. (15)
Named Gaurī in Kānyakubja, Raṃbhā on Mount Malaya, Kīrtimatī in Ekāmraka, and Viśvā here in Viśveśvara. (1.6)
In Puṣkara I am Puruhūtā, and in Kedāra I am Mārgadā;
on Himācala I am Nandā, and in Bilvaka I am Bilvapatrikā.
I am Bhavānī in Sthāneśvara, Padminī always on Śrīśaila,
Bhadrā in Bhadreśvara, and Jayā on the Vārāha mountain.
I am Kāmalā in Kamalābhūmi, Raudrī in Rudrakoṭika; I am Kālī in Kālañjara, and Mukuṭeśvarī in Markoṭa. (19)
I am Kapilā in Mahāliṅga; I am Jalapriyā at Śiva-liṅga; I am Mahādevī at Śālagrāma; and I am Kumārikā in Māyāpurī. ||3.135.20||
In the lineage of Kāñcikāpura she is Lalitā; in Durgapattana she is Utpalākṣī; in Sahasrākṣa she is Mahotpalā; and in Kalamākṣa she is likewise Mahotpalā.
Maṅgalā is in the Gaṅgā, Durgā is in Puruṣottama, Vimalā is in the Vipāśā, and Amoghākṣī is in Puṇḍravardhana. ||22||
On Supārśva I am Nārāyaṇī; on Vikūṭa, Bhadrasundarī;
on Vipula, I am named Vipulā; and on the Malaya mountain, Kalyāṇī. (23)
I am Koṭavī at Koṭitīrtha, Sugandhā in the Mādhava forest, Trisaṃdhyā at Kubjāmraka, and Ratipriyā at Gaṅgādvāra.
At Śivakuṇḍa I am Sunandā; on the banks of the Devikā I am Nandinī; at Dvāravatī I am Rukmavarṇā, and in Vṛndāvana I am Rādhā.
In Madhurā I am Devakanyā; in Pātāla I am Parameśvarī; in Citrakūṭa I am Sītā; and likewise on the Vindhya mountains I am Vindhyācalī. ||26||
On Mount Sahya I am Ekavīrā; on Harmacandra I am Candrikā;
at Rāmatīrtha I am Ramaṇā; and on the Yamunā I am Mṛgāvatī. ||27||
I am Mahālakṣmī in Karavīra, Rumādevī in Vināyaka;
I am Aromā in Vaijanātha and Maheśvarī in Mahākāla.
I am Abhayā at Uṣṇatīrtha and Amṛtā in the cave of the Vindhya;
I am named Māṇḍavī at Māṇḍavya and Svāhā in the city of Māheśvara.
I am Pracaṇḍā in Chāgala, Caṇḍikā in Makarandaka; I am Varārohā in Someśvara and Puṣkarāvatī in Prabhāsa.
Devamātā is on the Sarasvatī; I am Pārā on the bank of the Pārā;
the highly fortunate Piṅgaleśvarī is at Mahālaya on the Payoṣṇī. (3.1)
In Siṃhāraṇya I am Siṃhikā; in Kārtikeya I am Yaśaskarī; in Utpalāvartaka I am Lolā; and at the confluence of the Śoṇa I am Subhadrā. (32)
Mātā Lakṣmī is in Siddhapura; Aṅganā is in Pulahāśrama; Viśvamukhī is in Jālandhara; and Tārā is on Kiṣkindha Mountain. ||33||
Puṣṭi is in the Devadāru forest, Medhā in the region of Kashmir, Bhīmikādevī on the Himālaya, and Puṣṭi is also in me, Viśveśvara. (34)
At Kapālamocana, the mother is Śuddhi; at Kāyāvarohaṇa, she is Dharādevī; and at Piṇḍāraka, she is Dhṛti. (35)
I am Nārāyaṇīśrī in Māṇikyānartaka; I am Nāgarī in Nāgara;
I am Kālā in Candrabhāgā; and I am Śivakāriṇī in Acchoda. (36)
In Veṇā she is named Amṛtā, and likewise Urvaśī in Badarī;
she is Oṣadhī in Uttarakuru and Kuśodakā in Kuśadvīpa. (37)
I am Manmathā on Hemakūṭa, Satyavādinī on Mukuṭa;
I am Vandanīyā on the Aśvattha tree, and I am Nidhi in the temple of Śravaṇa. (38)
I am Gāyatrī together with Brahmā, Pārvatī in the presence of Śiva, Indrāṇī in the world of the gods, and Sarasvatī within the mouth of Brahmā. (39)
In the solar orb she is Prabhā; in steadfastness she is Pāśavatī Vaiṣṇavī;
and in me, Anādi-Śrī-Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, she is Ramā, the bestower of happiness. (3.135.40)
I am Arundhatī among chaste women, Tilottamā among the host of Apsarases; I am the digit of Brahman in the mind, and the beloved among all who are dear. (41)
I am Bhaṅgā on Mount Nīla; I am Vijayā on the surface of the earth at Sāma; I am Kāmākṣī in Kāmarūpa; and I am Irā in the land of Brahmā. (42)
Among the Khāsīs, she is the Brahmaputrī; falling upon their bodies, she is purifying.
In this ancient Śyāma region, she is Śyāmā, the daughter of Menakā. 43.
In Uccīna, Yāgaśikṣāṅgī; in the three Aṅgulas, Kāramī;
in Kārākāra, Kṛṣṇavarṇā; and in Eluna, Khanirā. 44.
I am a mute among the Maṅgalakas, and a Mañchikā among the Khiṅgas;
I am a Pāraśavī in the dwelling of thieves, but a Rāśiputrī in the Rāśana [country]. (45)
I am Uralā on Mount Coralā, Raktā on the ground of Cāraktabhū, Nārāyaṇī in Sudāna, and Alpā on Mount Alpa. (46)
In Ketumāla I am Iṅgitajñā, and in Balāyata I am Parī;
in Piṅgala I am Hāritī, and in Kiṃpuruṣa I am Amarī. (47)
Rākarī is at Mānakaṅga; Parī is in Dakṣaka;
Saṃhārā is on Mount Najara; and Kāmarūpā is in Kamāraṇa. ||48||
I am Māsāmbā on Mount Sāmba; I am Kalihārā in Mitrapa; I am Hotriṇī in Trihotra; and I am Māṃjhāmbikā in Jhamba. ||49||
In Navadeśa she is Maṇikāntā; in Uṣṭrālaya she is Mahordhvikā; in Kalagaralī she is Śvānāyā; and on Mount Kātha she is Cāliśī. (3.135.50)
O Dakṣa, I dwell upon the earth in such forms as these; everywhere perform my worship, which bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation. 51.
Thus spoke the illustrious Mahālakṣmī to Dakṣa, the Prajāpati;
therefore, the worship of Mahālakṣmī brings about all peace. (52)
If one should recite these two hundred names of yours during worship, may all accomplishments, which grant whatever is desired, attend upon him. (53)
May the afflictions of the planets, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and likewise of enemies,
go to destruction through your peaceful sacrifices and other rites.
Having caused an excellent pavilion, auspicious on all sides and shaped like a lotus, to be constructed as circular, and likewise having a sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) in the form of a lotus; ||55||
Having recollected you, the Supreme Goddess, by means of these two hundred names, one should invoke you into grains of rice and worship you with lotuses and other offerings. 56.
By my boon, all his afflictions shall indeed come to an end after he has performed eight oblations, each accompanied by the respective name.
Then one should offer the great oblation with ghee, milk-rice, and sweet foods;
likewise, with streams of ghee, fruits, rice, and other grains.
Whoever [worships] with coconut fruits and the like, with sacrificial fuel-sticks, with sugar and so forth—
whatever is desired in his mind, all that shall indeed come to pass.
For him, there shall be sovereignty, heaven, and liberation—indeed, everything;
he shall obtain wives, sons, husbands, and so forth, as well as wealth and fame. (3.135.60)
I shall describe the proper arrangement for that Lakṣmī-sacrifice as it truly is:
its circumference is one hundred and twenty cubits.
One should take ten auspicious pillars for the sake of the pavilion;
one should construct the pavilion there, beautifully adorned with four doors.
It was adorned with gateways, a well-constructed canopy, a circular pinnacle,
golden jars, and a resplendent banner.
One should cause it to be made auspicious, adorned even with a banner of red cloth;
likewise, one should have weapons depicted all around upon the archways.
The eighteen distinct [weapons] are, from the east in a clockwise direction:
the sword, the shield, the scimitar, the staff, the noose, the thunderbolt, and the bow. (65)
A battle-axe, an arrow, a discus, a mace, a conch, a great goad,
a lotus, a garland, a spear, a missile, and likewise the gesture of fearlessness.
In this manner, one should have these weapons placed upon the archways;
and at every pillar, one should likewise have water-pots and banners installed.
One should install the eight goddesses as the limb-deities upon the door-frames;
likewise, one should install Śrī and Māṇikyā upon the two eastern frames.
And likewise, one should establish Ramā holding a noose in the south;
and likewise, one should establish Maṅgalā and Amṛtā in the west.
Furthermore, one should likewise establish Vijayā and Jayā in the north;
and upon the central pillars, one should install Durgā and Satī in the northeast.
Likewise, one should cause Svāhā and Svadhā to dwell in the two fire-pillars;
and in the southwest (Nairṛta), one should likewise establish Saṃhāriṇī and Vaśinī.
In the northwest, one should install the beautiful and auspicious Śāradā Vāṇī,
as well as Sāvitrī, Gāyatrī, Sarasvatī, and Yamī.
Vaiṣṇavī, Varāhī, Caṇḍikā, Aindrī, Vāruṇī, Bhūmi, Saṃjñā, Kaumudī, Nandā, Nārāyaṇī, and Ramā. (73)
One should install the sixteen Śaktis, who are contented and adorned with exquisite grace, upon the canopy at the locations of the pillars and the sacrificial pits (carusthāna).
One should worship those two-armed figures, adorned with all ornaments, with waters from sacred fords (tīrtha),
along with saffron, unbroken rice grains, oil, and other fragrant substances such as sandalwood.
The sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) should indeed be circular and ten cubits in size;
likewise, one should have it fashioned in the form of a lotus with sixteen petals.
One should have the sacrificial pit (sayoni) prepared there, as well as three girdles (mekhalā);
one should also perform Lakṣa-homas and Koṭi-homas, which bestow the attainment of desired goals.
One should invoke and worship two hundred forms of yours—the exalted form of Mahālakṣmī with her auspicious face. (78)
Fifty-six finger-breadths in height, adorned with a crown and shining with necklaces, she is seated upon a golden lion-throne, fashioned from gold or another metal. (79)
One should have it performed by her friends, arranging it as is appropriate;
having bathed the Supreme Goddess with the five nectars and waters from sacred fords.
With fragrant perfumes, ornaments, and garments of pure consciousness, and with flower-garlands that beautifully adorned the limbs of her body; ||81||
Having worshipped with sandalwood, unbroken rice, tulasī, musk, and fragrant essences, one should offer various kinds of food offerings (naivedya). ||82||
One should indeed offer as an oblation all kinds of sweet foods, including milk-rice (pāyasa),
as well as sweet juices and vegetable dishes.
One should offer water and betel-leaf, and then perform the ārātrika rite;
having performed circumambulation, one should likewise pray and prostrate.
O destroyer of birth, O destroyer of worldly existence, O destroyer of disease, O Supreme Goddess!
O Vāsudevī, O Kṛṣṇadevī, O Mahālakṣmī, salutations be unto you! ||85||

O Supreme Brahmanī, who dwells in the hearts of all beings, O Thou who art higher than the highest, O Thou whose very nature is all the goddesses; to Thee, the Protectress, be repeated salutations! (86)

For me, your devotee, whatever suffering there may be—whether caused by fate or by humans, born of past actions or born of time, arising from the force of destiny (prārabdha), or produced by malevolent planets—[may it be removed]. 87.
Whatever mental distress there is that arises from one's own nature, or whatever has already arisen, or is yet to arise, whether from a curse, malice, or negligence; [all this is removed]. (88)
Whatever ill-conceived undertaking I may have undertaken out of ignorance, as well as my lack of lineage, childlessness, lack of a wife, and dishonor—[may all this be removed]. (89)
May all fear of disease also go to destruction for me;
by your very grace, may there be happiness and constant joy for you.
May there be for me the eternal Śrīpura, heaven, and the immortal state; at the end, may the imperishable supreme abode be my highest goal. ||91||
Having thus entreated her, one should then offer a handful of flowers, propitiating the Great Holy One (Mahāsati) so that she may forgive all transgressions. 92.
One should dismiss the female servants and likewise dismiss the subordinate deities;
and one should bestow the goddess Lakṣmī upon the Guru, who is the embodiment of Brahman.
Or one may install Mahālakṣmī in a temple that is stable and firm,
either alone or accompanied by Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa.
One should install [the image] together with the illustrious Gopālakṛṣṇa, who is one with the essence of Mahāviṣṇu, in a temple of the gods adorned with golden pinnacles.
One should likewise offer gifts of gold coins and silver, as well as rubies, diamonds, gems, ornaments, and garments. ||96||
One should also distribute sweet foods and present garments for women;
one should also present beautiful ornaments and various articles of utility. ||97||
One should cause all gifts of wealth, grain, and houses to be made;
having thus performed the rite of expiation, one should then partake of food.
One should feed virtuous Brahmins, as well as the poor, the blind, and the wretched; also children, young maidens, and women who are helpless or destitute. (99)
One should feed and likewise honor virtuous, chaste, and noble women;
one should also constantly worship Lakṣmī and feed her according to the prescribed rite.
Thus, for the performer, there shall never be suffering or remorse;
there shall always be enjoyment, perfect great liberation, and universal sovereignty.
May there be the enjoyment of unbroken bliss, the state of being more beloved than the host of goddesses, and equality with Kṛṣṇa, O Lord of Śrī, through the grace of Śrī. 102.
Thus has this worship, O Lakṣmī, which bestows tranquility, been described to you;
by reading or hearing it, great happiness shall always arise.

Thus ends the one hundred and thirty-fifth chapter, titled "The Description of the Two Hundred Names and Forms Spoken by Mahālakṣmī to Dakṣa Prajāpati, as well as the Peace-Offering Worship (*śāntipūjā*), the Image of Mahālakṣmī, and Her Mandala," in the Third Section on the Lineage of Dvāpara within the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
Listen, O Śrī Nārāyaṇī, to these two hundred names of Lakṣmī;
formerly, having performed penance for your sake, [I attained this] by chanting them and propitiating you.
The auspicious maiden of the Pitṛs, born from their mind, named Acchodā,
then obtained the powerful Amāvasu as her husband.
She received the blessing of the ancestors and of Mahālakṣmī:
"Born from the womb of a fish, you shall be born of the great heroism of King Vasu."
O maiden, you shall be supported by a fisherman and will become fertile;
through the seed of Parāśara, you will obtain one son.
On an island abounding in jujube trees, Viṣṇu’s mother herself became Bādarāyaṇa, the infallible one, and was subsequently married.
By King Śāntanu, a portion of the ocean,
you shall become the mother of two sons, Citrāṅgada and Vicitravīrya.
And having brought [this] forth, you will then swiftly go to the world of the ancestors;
in the world of the ancestors, you shall exist in the form of the Aṣṭakā of the month of Prauṣṭhapada.
In this world she is known by the name Satyavatī, and likewise as Aṣṭakā in the world of the ancestors;
she constantly bestows long life and health, and grants the fruit of all desires.
Thereafter, you shall also become a river;
by the name Acchodā, you will eternally effect the liberation of your ancestors.
Thus, by means of the Lakṣmī-Śānti vow, that daughter of the Pitṛs,
the mother of Vyāsa, became renowned and indeed obtained a boon.
He by whom these two hundred names are sung during worship on the eighth lunar day, or at the giving of a cow, or at the performance of a śrāddha, shall indeed have many sons. (11)
O Lakṣmī, there are likewise two hundred sacred fords (tīrthas) in those three worlds; by bathing there, one attains Brahman.
His ancestors, being fully satisfied, cross over and even attain Brahman;
furthermore, others, the Barhiṣads, the sons of Pulastya, dwell in heaven.
There are hundreds of ancestors, but among them, there is one daughter born of their mind;
she is a virtuous woman named Pīvarī, who has performed your vow, O Lakṣmī. (14)
Having performed vows and severe austerities that brought peace to Lakṣmī,
you obtained me as your divine wife in the forest, united with Hari-Kṛṣṇa.
And right there you obtained a boon from me: "Become one who possesses a husband;
your husband shall indeed be Śukradeva, a great yogi. (16)
The son of Vyāsa will have you as his wife; and you shall obtain a daughter born of his mind, named Kṛtī, who will be a yoginī of divine beauty.
Then you shall indeed give your daughter to the king, the lord of the Pañcālas;
and your four sons as well, O great lords, will follow after her.
Kṛṣṇa, Gaura, Prabhu, and Śambhu will be the bestowers of liberation;
accompanied by your husband, sons, and others, you shall attain emancipation after a long time. (19)
Thus Pīvarī obtained this boon through your vow;
and there were also other ancestors named Marīcigarbha.
The auspicious mental daughter of these [gods], named Yaśodā, having performed a vow for you, O Lakṣmī, indeed became the wife of Aṃśumat. ||21||
Then that beautiful woman, though she had attained liberation and gone to heaven, was born as the mother of Dilīpa and the grandmother of Bhagīratha. (22)
Furthermore, in former times, a daughter of the Ājyapās named Virajā,
having performed the Lakṣmī-Śānti vow, became the beloved wife of Nahuṣa.
And she, the mother of Yayāti, became known as Aikāṣṭakā;
having gone to the world of Brahmā, she rejoices there for eternal years.
Then the virtuous Narmadā, the daughter of the mental Pitṛs,
having performed the Lakṣmī-Śānti vow, rejoices in the form of a river.
She always rejoices in heaven and also delights in the world of the ancestors;
she is honored in the three worlds as the companion who provides amusement for Hari.
Then Gaurī, though the daughter of the Pitṛs, indeed shines forth as the beloved wife of Śukra and the mother of the Sādhyas by virtue of her vow of Lakṣmī-Śānti. ||27||
Thus, in heaven, as well as in truth and on every spot of the earth,
people rejoice with the abundance of prosperity solely through the Lakṣmī-Śānti vow.
Then Lakṣmī, having been made a Yoginī by the name Śukaputrī,
was formerly the daughter of Pīvarī, the maiden of her father’s mind.
For the sake of a son, the king, the lord of Pañcāla, performed the Lakṣmī-Śānti vow together with Nārāyaṇa and his wife.
The son of Vibhrāja named Anagha then indeed gratified Hari Nārāyaṇa and Ramā by means of the Lakṣmī-Śānti vow.
Lakṣmī and Janārdana, being pleased, spoke to them for the sake of a boon;
they then chose as their boon a son equal to Nārāyaṇa.
He was a master of all scriptures, righteous, and the best among yogis;
he understood the cries of all living beings and possessed great strength and prowess. ||33||
Having granted the boon with the words "So be it," he vanished;
then that very Nārāyaṇa himself became his son.
There was indeed one named Brahmadatta, compassionate and possessed of the true strength of virtuous beings;
his wife was Lakṣmī, who was also known by the name Sannati. (35)
Her son was Viṣvaksena, who was the Blessed Lord himself.
Thus, the merit of the Lakṣmī-vow always bestows great fruit.
Then she who was formerly Sinīvālī, the wife of Kardama,
having performed the Lakṣmī-Śānti vow, thereafter became Devahūtī.
By virtue of your vow, Dyuti, having performed penance and observed the Lakṣmī-Śānti-vrata in the past, obtained Kapila Śrīhari as her son.
Tuṣṭi obtained Vibhāvasu as her husband and gave birth to sons beginning with Pavamāna;
she also performed austerities and observed the Lakṣmī-Śānti vow.
For Prabhā, having performed her vow, obtained as her husband Dhātṛ, who is honored by all the worlds; she attained Hari, the maker of light, as her lord.
Having observed her vow, Kuhū obtained as her husband the auspicious Haviṣyanta;
Kīrti obtained Jayanta as her husband; and Vasu obtained Mārīca Kaśyapa.
Urvaśī obtained Purūravas as her husband, who was a source of joy;
once, indeed, Urvaśī danced at the svayaṃvara of Lakṣmī.
She performed the Lakṣmī-Śānti vow and gave birth to eight sons:
Āyu, Dṛḍhāyu, Aśvāyu, Dhanāyu, Sadhṛti, and Vasu. (42)
Having given birth to Śucividya and Śatāyu, she then indeed ascended to heaven.
Now, O Lakṣmī, there was the auspicious Śarmiṣṭhikā, the daughter of Vṛṣaparvan. 44.
Having performed the Lakṣmī-Śānti vow, Devayānī, the daughter of Śukra, obtained Yayāti as her virtuous husband; thereafter, she performed the Lakṣmī-vow once again.
He restored Kaca, the son of his guru, who had been devoured by the beasts of the Daityas;
and he caused Kaca, who had been ground up by the Daityas and drunk in wine, to be drunk once again.
And Śukra gave that Sañjīvanī to Kaca;
out of his devotion to the welfare of Devayānī, he gave it even though she was still in her womb.
Having performed the Lakṣmī-Śānti vow, Kaca went to his father’s house;
by its power, he taught the Sañjīvanī mantra to his own disciples.
Then indeed, Jyāmagha’s wife Caitrā, by means of the Lakṣmī-vrata,
obtained a son named Vidarbha, who was endowed with excellent qualities.
For a daughter-in-law indeed obtained her husband through the Lakṣmī-vrata;
likewise, she who was conquered in the heat of battle by Jyāmagha was made his daughter-in-law.
She indeed performed the Lakṣmī-Śānti vow from Uśīnara on the Dṛśadvatī river, and she obtained Śibi, the son of Uśīnara, as a universal emperor (cakravartin). ||51||
And Bali’s wife Sudeṣṇā, having previously performed the Lakṣmī-vrata, obtained five auspicious sons: Aṅga, Vaṅga, Kaliṅga, Puṇḍra, and Suhma.
Dīrghatamas obtained Brahmins who enjoyed the kingdom;
Śakuntalā, having performed a vow, obtained Bharata as her son.
Mamatā, however, having made a vow, obtained the auspicious son Bharadvāja from Bṛhaspati and gave him to Bharata.
Then Kṛtāyana, the disciple of the high-souled Kauśalya Hiraṇyanābha,
having performed his vow, [attained success] through the grace of Lakṣmī.
The divine collections of Sāman were indeed arranged in twenty-four ways;
Ahalyā, however, was the sister of Divodāsa, born from Śaradvat.
It is said that through the Lakṣmī-vrata, Kāverī, Kṛṣṇaveṇī, Narmadā, and Yamunā likewise obtained Śatānanda as their son, the sage.
The Godāvarī, the Vitastā, the Candrabhāgā, the Irāvatī, the Vipāśā, the Kauśikī, as well as the Śatadrū and the Sarayū. ||58||
The high-minded Sītā, the river Hradinī, and the purifying river Pāvanā likewise obtained sons as their celestial abodes after performing the Lakṣmī-Śānti vow.
In this way, other women as well, having performed this Lakṣmī-vrata,
obtained wealth, daughters, sons, heaven, and liberation.
Listen, Lakṣmī, to this most excellent vow, the Saubhāgyaśayana, which was performed by you in the past and which bestows the fruit of all desires. (61)
Formerly, when the worlds of Bhūr, Bhuvas, Svar, and Mahas had been consumed by fire,
the collective good fortune of all living beings then became condensed into a single mass.
Having reached that Vaikuṇṭha situated upon the chest of Viṣṇu,
it desires to go once again to that state of auspiciousness among the subjects during the new creation.
From the chest of Hari, the form of Lakṣmī manifested;
and by the command of Hari, she became the bestower of all happiness.
Having abandoned their forms as Lakṣmī, they assumed the form of aesthetic essence (rasa) consisting of nectar;
these were Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra, who are indeed the sustainers of creation.
There, accompanied by the goddesses, they drank that auspicious nectar which increases beauty,
charm, fortune, splendor, strength, and other such qualities.
The remainder, which contained all abundant objects, was divided into eight parts;
from the essence (rasa), seven delights (modas) arose that bestow good fortune.
Sugarcane, lumps of molasses, flat beans, and cumin seeds;
cow's milk and the like, safflower, vermilion, and likewise saffron. ||68||
Including salt—these increase one's good fortune through that vow;
even by himself, Nārāyaṇa has protected this essence of good fortune.
From her being cherished, there was born to him a beautiful daughter named Lalitā;
she always cherishes the worlds with her auspicious beauty. (3.136.70)
Because she attained all the worlds through her grace, she is called Lalitāśrī;
the Great Lord married this Trailokyasundarī. (71)
O Lakṣmī, you alone have become Mahālakṣmī, the bestower of good fortune, who is composed of auspiciousness in the world and grants the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation. 72.
By worshipping you with devotion, what may a man or a woman not obtain?
I shall now describe here that worship and vow of yours which brings about welfare.
Having reached the month of Vasanta, on the third day of the bright fortnight,
the sacrificer should perform a bath with sesame seeds in the forenoon.
Then the goddess Lalitā, endowed with good fortune, chose Nārāyaṇa;
one should worship me, Nārāyaṇa, together with her at dawn.
On the third day, one should bathe Śrī with fruits, flowers, incense, lamps, food offerings, the five products of the cow (pañcagavya), and water from sacred fords.
Salutation to Lakṣmī, to Mahālakṣmī, and to Lalitā on the head;
salutation to the Goddess, to Mahādevī, and to Lalitā on the face. (77)
Homage to Brāhmī, to Mahābrāhmī, and to Vaiṣṇavī in the heart;
homage to Mātṛ, to Mahāmātṛ, and likewise to Nārāyaṇī in the belly. (78)
Salutations to Śrī, Mahāśrī, and Vāsudevī at the waist;
salutations to Bhāgyā, Mahābhāgyā, and Saubhāgyā on the thighs.
Salutations at the feet to Bhūmi, the Great Void, and the Pervasive One;
salutations on all sides to the wife of Anādikṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa.
Salutations to you, the abode of good fortune; salutations to you, the manifestation of beauty;
salutations to you who possess a dual form; salutations again and again to you, the divine couple.
"Salutations again and again to Lalitā, who is endowed with all auspiciousness.
Having thus bathed her according to the prescribed rite, one should offer garments and ornaments.
One should offer all the ornaments and articles of adornment, as well as ghee, vermilion, milk, saffron, and likewise salt. (83)
Cumin, collyrium, sandalwood, red sandalwood, turmeric, camphor, musk, and bracelets; ||84||
A chain, a natthika, a string, together with anklets and rings;
niṣpāva beans, a leaf, a betel nut, and likewise betel leaf. 85.
One should place sugar, cloves, and cardamom before [the deity];
one should offer incense, a lamp, food offerings, and fragrant water. (86)
One should indeed perform the ārātrika rite, circumambulate Lalitā, offer prostrations once more, and present an añjali of flowers. ||87||
One should pray for Lalitā and Kṛṣṇa; may supreme fortune be granted, even in the form of a husband and wife, which brings unbroken happiness. 88.
In the house there were always foods such as juices, grains, and other edibles, including sweetmeats, soups, boiled rice, vegetables, and curd-rice. (89)
All things produced from milk and those produced from sugarcane,
as well as seasoned meat preparations (veśavāra) and other such items for perfuming the mouth.
Beds, coverlets, and vehicles; garments and ornaments; all kinds of clothing and various types of jewelry. ||91||
Vehicles, carriages, chariots, cows, horses, elephants, and excellent bulls;
male and female slaves, servants, groups of female friends, and likewise golden dwellings. (92)
Various mansions, fields, and groves;
all great gardens, as well as the lineage, sons, and daughters. (93)
Daughters-in-law and kinsmen, as well as fame, renown, and riches;
prosperity, peace, precious elephants, health, and supreme Dharma. (94)
"May devotion and knowledge be granted, and thereafter the imperishable abode of Kṛṣṇa.
Having thus worshipped them there, he should then install them in the pavilion. 95.
One should indeed perform the oblation consisting of one hundred and eight [offerings], and thereafter give the sacrificial fee and feed the virtuous Brahmins. (96)
One should feed the poor and the helpless and indeed bestow gifts; then, at midday, one should perform the ritual dismissal once again.
One should feed various kinds of food and offer water and betel-leaf;
one should cause Kṛṣṇa and Nārāyaṇa to sleep for one ghaṭikā and then awaken them.
One should offer water and fruit, and worship [the deity] in the evening at night;
one should perform the waving of lamps (ārātrika) with great festivity, and thereafter provide a feast.
One should cause those two Blessed Ones to sleep upon a soft and auspicious bed;
this sleeping together is the vow known as the Saubhāgya-śayana.
Having risen in the morning, one should awaken the two deities and then worship them according to the prescribed rite;
likewise, one should honor a Brahmin couple with garments and ornaments.
Then, one should give to a virtuous Brahmin two golden feet endowed with the eight marks of good fortune, and likewise a set of four for each of the other two.
One should give Lalitā to the Guru, and one should give Kṛṣṇa to a virtuous person;
one should give the couple to a virtuous person for the attainment of good fortune and long-lasting happiness.
In this manner, one should perform the rite on the third lunar day for as long as a year;
at the end of the year, one should perform the most excellent concluding ceremony (udyāpana).
In Caitra, one should offer a *śṛṅgāṭaka* (water-chestnut); in Vaiśākha, ghee and milk-rice (*pāyasa*);
in Jyeṣṭha, a *mandāra* flower; and likewise, a *vṛndā* leaf in Śuci (Āṣāḍha).
In the month of Śrāvaṇa one should give curd, and in Nabhasya, water with Kuśa grass;
in the month of Āśvayuja, milk, and in Kārttika, fresh butter.
In the month of Mārgaśīrṣa one should give split pulses; in Pauṣa, ghee with sugar;
in Māgha, black sesame seeds; and in Phālguna, the five products of the cow (pañcagavya).
Tulasī, lotuses, and other such items are indeed prescribed for every month;
having performed the vow in this manner, whether she be a woman, a maiden, or even a widow—108.
At the conclusion of the vow, one should donate a bed equipped with all necessary furnishings;
then, one should place golden images of Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa upon that bed.
One should give gifts to a virtuous Brāhmaṇa who is well-honored;
one should bestow grain, ornaments, cows, and wealth upon the twice-born. (3.136.1) 1 0.
He who thus correctly performs this Saubhāgya-śayana-vrata attains all desires and reaches the infinite state.
Whether it be a woman or a man, whoever performs the Saubhāgyaśayana vow for twelve years shall be cherished by the grace of the Goddess.
