and seeing Viṣṇu ready for his journey, she bowed at his feet.
She again offered a welcome and other courtesies to Śambhu; having presented fruits and roots to him, she gave them to him and asked, "From where have you come? (3.206.20)
"Where are you going, O Great King? If it is your desire, dwell in my house.
Upon hearing this, Śaṅkara said, "My arrival here was for the sake of your devotee."
Wherever there is a devotee, that place is a sacred ford (tīrtha) dear to me in every respect;
wherever devotees dwell, there I reside like a virtuous sage.
"You are a devotee who always offers hospitality to the virtuous in the forest;
having purified your home, I shall go to another excellent sacred site. (23)
Having heard this, the forest guardian also questioned him once more:
"O holy man, where is that purifying sacred site (tīrtha) to which you are going? (24)
Then the matted-haired ascetic said to the devotee: "The assembly of the virtuous is a sacred place;
wherever the company of the good is most excellent, there indeed I go.
There are many holy men who grant liberation from the cycle of worldly existence."
They were also intent on the meditation of Viṣṇu and dedicated [all their actions] to Śrī Kṛṣṇa. ||26||
They were renunciants endowed with austerity, devoted to self-restraint and discipline, intent on service and devotion, and dwellers in forests and wildernesses. ||27||
That house in which Viṣṇu, Śambhu, or the illustrious Narāyaṇa resides—whether it be Vāsudeva or Bālakṛṣṇa—that house is the most excellent sacred site (tīrtha). ||28||
Where the Lord Śrī Hari, golden-hued, with golden hair, the all-encompassing one whose form is entirely of gold, eternally shines forth. (29)
O devotee, that sacred ford is purifying; I dwell at that ford where the Lord, whose divine form is of immense splendor, shines forth.
O devotee, wherever there are devotees of Hari, as well as virtuous women and holy men,
I indeed go to that purifying sacred place.
I dwell here in that which is the form of truth, consciousness, and bliss, the full Brahman that is the source of illumination; from which great splendor this entire world shines forth.
Having meditated upon that very lotus-eyed Nārāyaṇa, the supreme person, the divine Supreme Lord who is higher than the highest, I shall attain him. 33.
Therefore, this entire world is indeed filled by that full Puruṣa;
I take refuge in that Śyāmasundara Kṛṣṇa, the Bālakṛṣṇa.
I approach the Lord of lords of living beings, the bestower of the fruits of karma, the Sovereign of liberation, who possesses a divine form and is the Lord of Lakṣmī. (35)
I take refuge in that Lord of Śrī, whose form possesses exceedingly great splendor, which is all-pervasive, upward-moving, present everywhere, and known as Brahman. 36.
I approach that radiant one, through whose lineage a supreme glory shines everywhere and who remains as if embodied, bestowing its fruit. (37)
I approach that Śrī Kṛṣṇa of divine form, by whose majesty the Mādhavas become lords, deities, and perfected beings. 38.
I go to him, the divine yogin, who has attained meditative absorption in his own form, wherein there is the dissolution of Māyā and its effects, as well as the principles (tattvas). (39)
The sky of consciousness is exceedingly blissful and eternally filled with great joy; I approach that Supreme Lord, whose form abides as the essence of purity.
I take refuge in that Lord Hari, who is the imperishable abode of Brahman, the divine ether, the great light, and bliss; he who bestows all happiness. 41.
I approach that Lord who abides as the imperishable within all things—within illusion, within the products of illusion, and even within the principles of the self. 42.
I take refuge in that Kṛṣṇa, whose power, through its persistence within the person, primordial nature, and time, effects all undertakings. 43.
Since it is from Him that the threefold creation indeed shines forth and into Him it goes to dissolution, I approach that Hari who abides within the threefold creation. 44.
I take refuge in that beloved of Māṇikī, by whose grace even a human or a god, possessing divine vision, perceives all as Brahman. 45.
I take refuge in that Supreme Lord, from whom infinite powers and millions of infinite sovereignities arise, and by whom Rudra and the other gods are brought forth. 46.
I approach that Lord Hari, whom the virtuous practitioners of the eightfold yoga and the gods to be attained behold in meditative absorption. 47.
I go to that [state] in which the channels, vital breaths, and spaces of embodied beings within the body become entirely contracted and withdrawn. 48.
The lords such as Brahmā and Rudra, as well as holy men like me, and indeed innumerable Nārāyaṇas, have become possessed of sovereignty by taking refuge in Him. 49.
The Blessed Ones are indeed male Nārāyaṇas, and they are also female Nārāyaṇīs;
I approach that Supreme Lord who is both the source of incarnations and the incarnations themselves.
Worship in every way that Lord, the husband of Śrī, the Sovereign, the Lord of all, the sustainer of all powers, and the husband of Rādhikā. (51)
I worship that god Viṣṇu, the supreme lord Śrī;
others, having worshipped that god, went to the highest state in the past. (52)
"Others have gone and others will go as well; therefore, worship that Supreme Lord.
Having spoken thus, Rudra, who is truly affectionate toward his devotees, became peaceful.
Then Lakṣmī, Śikhādevī, and Tilakarangaka, recognizing him to be a holy man established in Brahman and equal to Rudra, paid him homage. (54)
"Oh, virtuous one! How truly blessed is our fortune as householders, since today we have obtained such knowledge from you, a holy man! (55)
Indeed, the sight of a holy man such as you is difficult to obtain here in this world;
how then can the company of the virtuous grant liberation even to forest-dwellers? (56)
"You remain a devotee of Viṣṇu, while we are devotees of Hara; tell us, why would there be a meeting with Hara? That would be wonderful. (57)
Having heard that, Śambhu then said: "The vision of Śambhu shall be yours right here once you have restrained your mental fluctuations; of this there is no doubt. (58)
"Having composed your inner faculties, behold me within your heart;
for you shall indeed have a vision of Hara within this virtuous form. (59)
Thus addressed by the ocean-born one, Tilaka and the other forest-keepers then turned their thoughts inward and meditated within their hearts for as long as they could.
At that moment, the virtuous Rudra himself manifested, bearing a trident,
three-eyed, clad in a tiger skin, the lord of Satī, Śrī Pārvatī.
Immersed in the Hari-lake, he was seen as one who brings supreme bliss, possessing a gentle form and radiant splendor;
the great yogi appeared accompanied by Gaṇeśa and the other attendants.
Then, there within the heart of Hara, was my auspicious and supremely divine four-armed form of Hari, together with Lakṣmī.
It appeared, filled with great bliss and worshipped by Śaṅkara;
that beautiful [liṅga] had emerged from the heart of Śambhu to the outside. 64.
And it was seen being worshipped by Śambhu, bestowing happiness.
Having thus granted this vision, Śaṅkara appeared in the form of a holy man.
He, indeed, concealing his own form as Viṣṇu, quickly assumed the appearance of a virtuous man; thereafter, he likewise did so within the heart.
He caused all the oil-pressers and others who were outside to be brought in;
when they rose, they saw the holy man wearing matted hair just as before.
And all those wise ones prostrated at the feet of Śambhu, their own chosen deity and the husband of Satī, and they performed the massaging of Śambhu’s feet.
They begged for forgiveness for their offense and requested liberation;
Śambhu said, "I am always a Vaiṣṇava and affectionate toward my devotees."
I have come here to cause my devotees to practice devotion toward Śrī Hari;
I always protect Lord Nārāyaṇa within my heart.
I meditate upon that Supreme Brahman, Bālakṛṣṇa, the Lord of Śrī;
may you, my devotees, also worship the Supreme Lord. (71)
Having spoken thus, Hara himself bestowed the mantra of Lakṣmī upon them:
"Oṃ namaḥ śrīkṛṣṇanārāyaṇāya svāmine svāhā. (72)
Then, having instructed them in the worship and devotion of Nārāyaṇa for the sake of liberation, he suddenly vanished after speaking these words. ||73||
Then, by the command of Śambhu, Tilakaraṅga also took refuge with me,
Lord Bālakṛṣṇa, together with his wife and family at all times.
From that time forward, he has been constantly summoning both men and women from the forest and from among the human inhabitants of the woods, and is indeed causing them to perform kīrtana. (75)
Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, Bāla-Kṛṣṇa, Lord of Ramā! O Hari, Viṣṇu, Jiṣṇu, Anādi-Kṛṣṇa, Lord of Śrī! ||76||
Thus he constantly performs the chanting of praises and causes it to be performed as well;
he always worships Janārdana in the forest and upon the altar.
Having performed the lustration ceremony (nīrājana), he indeed pleases me—Kṛṣṇa, Nārāyaṇa, Hari—with fruits, flowers, and other offerings. (78)
He dances indeed with music out of love at evening and the arrival of night;
Hara abides only among the virtuous, and Hari shines forth in Hara. (79)
Realizing this, he always serves the virtuous even in the midst of the forest,
through action, mind, speech, body, and wealth.
He serves with leaves, flowers, fruits, water, and the offering of his own self;
having surrendered all his possessions for the sake of the virtuous, he practices the direct service of the holy ones.
One who has direct perceptual certainty serves the virtuous with perfect dedication;
a wife seeking pleasure serves her husband, while one devoid of passion abandons all for the sake of bliss.
In whatever way he may be, the virtuous woman seeking the supreme goal serves him;
and his sons, daughters, and others likewise serve that noble lord. (83)
Everything indeed proceeds from the virtuous; Hara, Hari, and Nārāyaṇa, as well as Brahman, liberation, and supreme bliss—the eternal happiness resides in the virtuous. (84)
The virtuous alone is the Supreme Brahman; the virtuous is the supreme God and the supreme Guru.
The virtuous person is an embodiment of Hari; indeed, service to the virtuous bestows liberation. (85)
In this manner, those forest-dwellers subsisted upon wild provisions;
then, once upon a time, on the eighth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Kārttika, they— ||86||
They indeed celebrated a great festival in the wooden grove within the forest, [using] swings constructed from tree branches and adorned with flowering vines and sprouts. (87)
Having thus beautifully adorned me, they seated me facing Kṛṣṇa;
and they performed my ritual waving, chanting, and worship. (88)
Then, at night, accompanied by the beloved of Brahmā, I celebrated my birth-festival, which is beginningless, with an abundance of dance and song.
I quickly became manifest in the form of a divine youth,
endowed with a most divine, exceedingly beautiful form, adorned with ornaments and garments.
The youthful Lord of Māṇikī appeared upon a beautiful swing, possessing a true radiance encircled by light, with a face of serene smiles. 91.
The Lord of Rādhā and Lakṣmī, the Master of Wisdom, and the Consort of Śrī-Kamalā—all were filled with wonder at him, and for a moment they gazed upon his vision. (92)
Then I immediately became embodied in form;
immersed in joy, they all eagerly made this request: |||93||
O Hare Kṛṣṇa, ocean of mercy, deliver us, Your own people, from this ocean of worldly existence; grant us Your abode. 94.
"So be it," I said, and at that time, O Rame, I granted them the boon;
having received what was offered by them, I bestowed the granting of the boon from the mouth of my own form. 95.
I became invisible, and they performed a rite of avoidance;
then, after some time had passed, [the turn] of the yogi Tilakaraṅga arrived.
Then, moved by compassion for Śikhādevī and the other forest-dwellers,
I became the bestower of liberation and appeared in the forest upon a celestial chariot.
Having fashioned them with divine bodies, I established them in celestial chariots;
I went to my own supreme, imperishable, and divine abode above.
Thus he indeed granted liberation—the supreme state—to the forest-dwellers;
others who were forest-guardians there also worshiped me, the Lord Hari. 99.
And they go to the imperishable abode when their life has reached its limit—
those people who, by the command of Śambhu, worship me, Janārdana.
O Lakṣmī, I lead them to my own abode, the imperishable and supreme beyond the supreme;
by reciting or hearing this, both worldly enjoyment and liberation shall be attained.

Thus ends the two hundred and sixth chapter, titled "The Description of the Attainment of Supreme Liberation by the Forest-Dweller Tilakaraṅga, a Devotee of Śiva, through the Worship of Nārāyaṇa and the Devotion Taught by Sādhurūpa Śiva," in the Third Section (Dvāpara-santāna) of the glorious *Lakṣmīnārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Puruṣottama said:
Listen, O Śrī Nārāyaṇī, to the auspicious story of the guardian of the field (kṣetrapa) named Nāñjakadeva, which brings about my devotee’s liberation. 1.
The brave Nāñjabhakta was the protector of the Sīma fields;
he was highly powerful and skilled in weapons and missiles at the field of Kuṃkume Laumaśa.
He dwells constantly within the boundary, goes to the city, and attends festivals; he is a protector of the crops and a guardian of the gardens. (3)
He is that very same person who was once a guard over a granary of grain-particles in a threshing floor;
he wanders all around the earth day and night for the sake of protection. (4)
And he provides protection in every way against thieves and plunderers, as well as for farmers, the wealthy, and the prosperity of citizens and others. (5)
And at the boundaries of the collections of leaves, stalks, and other such things,
Śrī Kṛṣṇa Śrī Narāyaṇa constantly attends to me by name.
She indeed turns her garland along the paths and at the boundary lands;
upon merely hearing the name "Añjasyā," thieves do not come toward that direction.
He is devoted and exceedingly skillful in devotion toward me, as well as in dharma, worship, service, chanting my praises, and meditation; he always remains diligent in these practices.
He was a hero in the protection of the virtuous, of cows, and of distressed women; likewise, he was a protector of chaste wives, faithful women, and the elderly.
He is a faithful servant, always free from pride like a slave, dedicated to the protection of the gods, the divine trees, and the celestial abodes. (3.207.10)
"O Lakṣmī, such is this devotee of mine who, having always performed my worship every morning, has gone toward the forest for the sake of seeing me."
He indeed travels in all directions for the sake of subduing the wicked;
once, in the eastern region, he traveled two krośas at dawn.
Far from Amarāpura, in the vicinity of Mṛdaṅgapura,
robbers arrived there by the command of Śatruñjaya.
Many horsemen, equipped with weapons and carrying food,
set out for the threshing floors in order to seize the grain from the threshing grounds of the farmers.
But the farmers, overcome with fear, entered the garden area;
finding no protector, they cried out while scattering heaps of grain. || 15 ||
Having abandoned [the field], they went far away; Nāñja did not come there.
Why are you dejected? You did not ask Nāñja about the farmers. 1.6.
The farmers, along with the plunderers who steal their food, said to him:
"Now they are forcibly seizing our grains from the threshing floor."
"O protector, provide protection for your strength against these plunderers;
having heard this, quickly remember Hari-Kṛṣṇa, me, the Supreme Person. (18)
The horseman himself ran swiftly toward that spot where those plunderers were indeed carrying off stores of food.
Having loaded food upon horses and camels, they indeed carried it;
seeing them, Añjaka did not roar with heroic shouts.
"You are powerful plunderers, born of noble mothers and fathers, and true to your word; having conquered me, you may depart, for otherwise you would be defeated and deprived of food. (21)
Hearing that sound produced by Bala, those warriors skilled in combat stood face-to-face,
equipped with their weapons, yet they were indeed not for the sake of achieving victory.
The sudden discharge of weapons occurred in their presence;
then the battle proceeded with arrows, missiles, and iron clubs.
Standing in the midst of twenty, he fights alone and not with another;
though wounded in many ways by weapons, remembering me, he fights valiantly. (24)
Ten thieves were pierced in the chests by the arrows of Añja and indeed died;
then, by the repeated blows of swords from the other thieves, [the rest] likewise perished. ||286||
Another man fell to the ground in a swoon, repeatedly calling out my name;
then I, the hero, quickly stood at his side with sword in hand. (26)
Manifesting with a massive body, his limbs like adamant and skilled in combat,
he pierced the remaining thieves who were armed with swords, without any hesitation.
All twenty thieves there quickly met their death;
however, the twenty-first thief, crying out "Rāma, Rāma," remained alive.
Having fallen into a swoon, he quickly lost consciousness and went toward death;
then, moved by compassion, I touched him who was solely devoted to the name of Rāma.
Reviving that devoted man, I made him free from disease;
then that devotee, known by the name Mahāmaya, rose up.
But out of compassion, he did not directly touch me with his hands as I prayed for my life;
instead, he repeatedly touched me with both palms.
Having dispelled his fainting, I raised him up, filled with happiness;
and then, having seen Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, those two [were likewise restored].
Filled with devotion, they both praised him for the sake of restoring the life of the deceased:
"Aho! You are indeed Nārāyaṇa; you are Rāma, the deliverer from the Rākṣasa. (33)
Oh, you are the Lord Nṛsiṃha, the destroyer of the Daityas!
Oh, Kṛṣṇa, Hari, Rāma, you are the one who rescued the elephant! 34.
You alone, who are affectionate toward your devotees, exist for the purpose of destroying the asuras;
even the sins of the wicked are destroyed by the sight of you. (35)
Indeed, even sinners cross over here by merely touching or remembering [you];
you, O Viśvaṃbhara, abide as both the nourisher and the protector.
"O Rudra, you manifest as Saṃkarṣaṇa, as Time, and as the Destroyer!
Protect us, protect us, O ocean of mercy; indeed, restore those who have died to life here! (37)
Even one who is a devotee becomes a thief through association with thieves;
I am a devotee of Mahāmaya, yet I am intent upon the work of theft. (38)
Nevertheless, you have protected this devotee here by means of the name "Rāma";
you did not protect Añjaneya here, for my protection arises from that [name]. (39)
O Blessed One, O Kṛṣṇa, fulfiller of the desires of Your devotees; these who have attained the yoga of devotion are to be protected by You, the Compassionate One. (3.207.40)
If they have died, let them be restored to life; they shall then worship Nārāyaṇa.
Or, if it pleases you, act accordingly to effect their liberation.
Thus addressed by me at that time, O Lakṣmī, for the sake of the liberation of the deceased, I first ordained a residence in heaven out of compassion. (42)
Because of their devotion to me and my yoga, I destroyed all the sufferings of Yama for those others who were sinful; I annihilated them from their very heads.
Having remembered the celestial chariots and fashioned those divine forms for them, I swiftly dispatched the twenty who had died in battle to heaven. (44)
Likewise, having repeatedly touched Mahāmaya’s food with my hand,
I indeed rendered him free from disease, just as he was before.
At that time, when they were nourished and freed from suffering, I awakened them [to this truth]:
"Indeed, this saṃsāra is impermanent; the body, the home, and so forth are impermanent. (46)
All things arising from illusion are impermanent and subject to decay;
nevertheless, ignorant people abandon right conduct and follow wrong paths. (47)
They constantly engage in violence, theft, and destruction;
they do not cultivate the company of the virtuous, nor do they worship the Supreme Lord. (48)
They do not listen to the discourse of the scriptures and they commit evil deeds without hesitation;
therefore, being punished, they experience the great sufferings of Yama.
Sinful people take birth even among animals and birds; those who act contrary to dharma encounter suffering upon suffering. (3.207.50)
By stealing another's food, one is born as a mouse;
by stealing ghee, milk, and the like, one becomes a cat.
By stealing vegetables, roots, and the like, one attains birth as a peacock;
by cutting off clothing or utensils, birth as a buffalo occurs.
By stealing fruits, leaves, and the like, one is born as a monkey;
by stealing gold, jewels, and the like, one is born as a bear. ||53||
By stealing water for drinking and such, one becomes a preta in a waterless forest;
by abducting a wife, son, or others, one becomes a eunuch and is born as a prostitute.
For those who play musical instruments and carry weapons, there is the state of being a common actor;
likewise, for those who betray trust, there is the state of a wolf or a chameleon. ||55||
Those who commit theft are born as horses; those who live by means of vehicles become oxen; debtors become mute, and those who revile others become dumb.
One becomes a eunuch or a bull among those who lust; a woman becomes a female demon (piśācinī);
and a mendicant becomes a deceiver, suffering from the misery of poverty. //57//
One who consumes the food and wealth of the gods becomes a dog, a crow, or a mouse;
one who destroys a family becomes a mongoose, while one who kills a woman becomes a rākṣasa.
A destroyer of the Dharma who is devoid of fortune is born as a wild boar in the forest;
a destroyer of devotion becomes a denizen of hell, childless, and a messenger of Yama. ||59||
A drinker of intoxicants becomes a urine-insect; one who consumes poison becomes a scorpion;
and when enraged, he may even become a serpent or a blue monkey.
Thus, having understood that births arise from karma, one should avoid them;
with this human body, one should perform what is auspicious and never anything inauspicious. (61)
One should cultivate auspicious Dharma, auspicious knowledge, and auspicious detachment;
one should also practice auspicious devotion and seek the company of the virtuous, which bestows liberation.
One should always perform sincere service for Hari and for the virtuous;
one should cause the temple of Kṛṣṇa, its courtyard, and so forth, to be plastered and swept.
One should perform the massaging of the feet and the rubbing of the body for the virtuous;
one should offer food offerings, meals, and the drinking of water to the wielder of the Śārṅga bow.
One should immediately give as desired and serve the circle of gurus; one should constantly listen to the sacred narrative and perform the chanting of the Name. 65.
One should abide in self-realization through the self whose nature is Brahman;
one should know me as the divine Hari, devoid of all defects. (66)
He should carry news of me and always maintain affection for me;
likewise, he should remain free from passion regarding illusory things and their effects. (67)
One should always perform auspicious service to the virtuous and keep the company of the good; one should cultivate a distaste for sense objects, and thus the mind will become tranquil.
One should make one's mind firm in the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa;
one should never, at any time, direct the mind toward anything else.
One should cause [these] to be made, or perform service for Me, as well as My adornment, out of love alone;
and one should bear My form, whether human or divine.
One should indeed cultivate affection for my devotees and nowhere else;
one should always avoid attachment and the bonds of affection toward wife, sons, and other such ties. (71)
One should remain engaged only in activities connected with Kṛṣṇa, and with a concentrated mind, one should desist from those devoid of connection with Kṛṣṇa. (72)
One should perform worship of me constantly and pray for one's own welfare, saying:
"Nārāyaṇa, Hare, Kṛṣṇa, Viṣṇu, O Lord, O Supreme Sovereign! (73)
Protect me from the world that follows the path of unrighteousness, as well as from atheism;
grant your assembly to your devotees and always bestow what is auspicious. (74)
May there be no association with the wicked; protect me always in such a way. Do not grant me the company of thieves, sinners, or revilers. (75)
I have no association with those who consume liquor and meat, those who are sexually promiscuous, those who deface my image, or those who destroy my worship. (76)
O Kṛṣṇa, you who are compassionate toward those who have sought refuge, grant me devotion;
act in such a way that no day passes for me in vain without it. (77)
O Lord, cause my mental activity to abide always in Kṛṣṇa;
likewise, act so that my mind may feel detachment toward worldly things. (78)
O Kṛṣṇa, grant us the company of the virtuous, the meeting with Your very form, and the long-lasting sight of You; dwell within the abode of our hearts.
Whether external or internal, let that vision of yours be truly divine;
likewise, O Kṛṣṇa, grant me the auspicious inner sight.
O Kṛṣṇa, grant me that imperishable abode which shines with Your own form; likewise, I pray for liberation consisting of service to You. (81)
Thus, you two should always pray to me, the Blessed Lord Hari, because of your devotion;
for that reason, I have come within the range of your vision.
"May there be well-being for you both; I am departing for my own abode.
Having spoken thus and having granted courage to the farmers, the Blessed Lord then [departed]. (83)
"Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Master; svāhā!
Having bestowed this mantra upon the farmers and the two devotees, He vanished from sight. (84)
Seeing that miracle, those farmers made me their refuge, performing worship and devotion; and the guardian of the field did so even more especially. (85)
O Lakṣmī, even Mahāmaya suddenly became free from disease through his union with Nārāyaṇa; likewise, even Añjana became free from collyrium. ||86||
They all constantly worshipped me, the husband of Śrī Rādhā and Ramā—performing my worship, feeding me, meditating upon me, sporting with me, and remembering me. (87)
They performed constant recitation, and at the end of their bodies, thereafter,
I arrived in a celestial chariot as resplendent as a chariot of Viṣṇu.
Then, accompanied by his attendants, he quickly led the farmers to his own world at the border of Aśvapaṭṭa, bestowing upon them divine bodies.
He did not bring any other food; instead, he brought that which is free from disease.
Thus, my devotees, as well as the guardians of the field, have attained the imperishable abode.
O Lakṣmī, one should offer me fresh grain produced from the field.
One should also offer a cucumber, a fly, a leaf, and a flower. ||91||
May he offer me the bulbous root, the fruit, the stalk, sweet vegetables, the flower-cluster, the tuft, the stem, the joint, or the branch. ||92||
Whether it be a grain of rice, a jujube fruit, or even a particle of purifying clay—whosoever offers these to me with devotion, I uplift that very offerer. (93)
Whoever offers me fuel-sticks, tulasī leaves, sandalwood trees, fruit-bearing trees, grass, darbhā grass, or sprouts, shall become a partaker of liberation.
Whether it be cotton, or a tuft of wool, or a pod, or even a sheath;
or a cluster, or a water-pot—if one should offer these to me, he shall attain liberation. (95)
One should offer sesame seeds, wheat, chickpeas, or split pulses; or wild rice, śālika rice, or dates. ||96||
Sugar or turmeric, salt or fresh ginger, various kinds of sour gruel, citron, and betel nut; ||97||
If one should offer me cardamom or even saffron, one shall partake in liberation;
or likewise, if one offers a seat, a bowl, a creeper, or even a cane. (98)
One should offer me a vehicle, clothing, food, oil, and the finest fragrance; adorned thus, he indeed becomes a partaker of liberation. 99.
One who would offer me milk, juice, cooked food, cool sweet drinks, a fan, or even side dishes shall become a partaker of liberation. (3.207.1) 100.
"By the surrender of their very selves, all indeed go to my abode, O Kamalā;
through reading, hearing, or even remembering this, one partakes in liberation.

Thus ends the two hundred and seventh chapter, titled "The Description of how the Blessed Lord protected the Kṣetrapa, the devotee Nāñja, the great devotee Mahāmaya, and the farmers from the thieves," in the third section, the Dvāpara Cycle, of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Puruṣottama said: Listen, O Śrī Nārāyaṇī, to the story of my auspicious devotee born of the Kirāta caste, named Sāgara, who dwells in the city of Mahāśāṭī.
Accompanied by his family, he wanders in the forest on the bank of the Mahī river for the sake of maintaining his bodily existence, while he makes accumulations at home.
Of wild tubers and roots, as well as grains, pulses, fruits, seeds, and likewise succulent plants; || 3 ||
In some places he eats food, fruit, or leaves; in others, he consumes tubers.
Thus he maintains his bodily existence and worships me.
Even for those wealthy enough to own gardens, he becomes a porter;
and sometimes the Bhilaka even enters into the service of merchants. || 5 ||
Acting in this manner, he does not obtain sustenance or food anywhere;
then, intent on fasting, he worships me with joy.
O Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa, he also performs the garland-twisting rite;
considering that vow to be natural, he indeed keeps a vigil at night.
Afflicted by hunger and thirst, he indeed performs the chanting at night;
his wife, sons, and daughters—all of them perform the vow as well.
Once, during the bright fortnight, on the eleventh day of the month of Kamala (Kārttika), not even the slightest amount of food was available for them to eat.
They performed for me the vow that is innate and born of the eleventh day, along with the night vigil,
the waterless fast, worship, and chanting of my praises.
Then in the morning, O Rame, they all offered me vegetables;
having offered water to me as well, they indeed ate those very vegetables. || 11 ||
"O Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, O Lord! they cried as they joyfully drank the water, O Lakṣmī; then I, the abode of compassion, spoke.
In their presence, he went along with a cart full of wheat;
they all, perceiving me to be a merchant of the highest rank, thought me a seller of goods. (13)
They bowed, offered water, and sang for a moment for the sake of rest;
and I, having understood their words, [placed] the female elephant in the courtyard of that house.
Having made the two bulls stand still and having bound them to the seat prepared by him,
they all sat down and massaged my feet.
And with their minds immersed [in grief], they cried out, "Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa!
Then, I asked them all: "What were their occupations? How did they earn their livelihood? (1.6)
They said: "Kṛṣṇa grants us life, and thus we live.
Today, let the worship of Kṛṣṇa be performed with water. (17)
"O merchant, we have eaten our greens and drunk water; indeed, peace always dwells with us, bestowing happiness. What need is there for wealth in the hundreds of thousands or tens of millions? (18)
We worship Śrī Hari constantly; He indeed provides our food, and we offer everything to Hari, who is beyond the material qualities.
"Today you are our honored guest in this house;
however, there is no great food suitable for you to prepare a welcome offering. (3.208.20)
"Then he said to me, 'I am giving this potherb; if it pleases you, take it.
Thus addressed, O Lakṣmī, I then ate that potherb with affection. (1)
He drank water and attained the satisfaction born of devotion. Then I gave them a full measure of wheat and bestowed upon them a thousand silver rings as wealth.
Then they questioned me regarding my name, my village, and my family.
I am Hari-Kṛṣṇa; I am Bāla-Kṛṣṇa.
My village is the imperishable abode (Akṣara-dhāma), and my family is the circle of devotees.
In their homes, I shall manifest my processions and grand ceremonies;
for you have performed the vow of Ekādaśī along with the ritual vigil.
Having been gratified by you with water for sipping, I arrived for the sake of protection;
out of compassion, I have come here to give you all the wheat.
"Once touched by my hand, these grains of wheat shall become inexhaustible;
they will remain so even when placed in a granary and covered over. (27)
Having made [a hole], they must be extracted through the opening and not otherwise;
indeed, by my power, they shall become inexhaustible. ||28||
May my devotees, born in successive generations of my lineage, be happy,
even when there shall be no worship of me here in this house.
"Then those wheat grains offered by me shall reach their end," having said this,
he gave them all and also revealed his divine vision.
And he gave me a four-armed form, endowed with splendor and captivating;
they all praised me and fell at my feet.
Overwhelmed by love, they all shed tears;
they chose protection and liberation, and finally, the supreme state.
O Lakṣmī, having spoken these words of encouragement, I then quickly vanished from that place along with the cart and the two bulls.
"For as long as I live, this Kirāta has been my devotee;
having had wheat cakes prepared by his own wife along with ghee, he offered them to me. (34)
Ascetics, other virtuous men, truthful women, and female mendicants—whoever comes here, they receive wheat flour cakes as their portion. (35)
A continuous feast of food was maintained for the ocean;
indeed, even those who had merely come as pilgrims to his house attained peace. (36)
Sāgara always obtains the great benefit of serving the virtuous;
endowed with much merit, Sāgara has become like the ocean itself. (28)
To whose house do the sages come, subsisting on food granted by the grace of the gods, and where do the deities in the guise of holy men come to eat wheat cakes? (38)
Perceiving his divine grace, mendicants indeed come [to him];
the wheat cakes given by Śrī Kṛṣṇa are equal to nectar. (29)
The meritorious *polikās* are enjoyed by the deities and by the ancestors in the form of mendicants, as well as by the *siddhas* with their divine bodies. (3.208.40)
For from morning until evening, the *polikā* cakes continue to be produced;
all the wheat is inexhaustible, increasing within the belly of the granary. (41)
The house of Sāgara became a sacred ford (tīrtha) renowned throughout the world;
it became famous even in the three worlds and was then rendered purifying. ||42||
Then, having heard that the food-sacrifice was inexhaustible, Durvāsas suddenly arrived in the morning accompanied by ten thousand disciples.
Honored by Sāgara and welcomed with respect,
he then arranged rows for the meal so that they were all simultaneous.
Terrified, Sāgara reflected upon the Lord, the Consort of Śrī;
then I appeared within his house together with Śrī.
Sāgara rejoiced greatly upon seeing me and Śrī likewise;
then Lakṣmī was commanded by me to quickly prepare the *polikās*.
Then Ramā suddenly fashioned five very small cakes;
she was cooked on the fire of the hearth by me and held in my hand. 47.
These five [dishes] are indeed inexhaustible and never diminish;
they were served by Sāgara, who held the vessel in his hand.
Ten thousand [polikās] were served to each individual;
thus, ten thousand polikās were distributed. ||49||
The vessel was given from the cooking pot and served to everyone;
it was touched by me, and it was delicious—both the vessel and the cakes. (3.208.50)
And all those followers of Durvāsas ate;
having become satiated by taking a mere handful, they indeed considered it a great wonder.
Then, seeing that exactly five cakes remained in the pot,
Durvāsas, struck by this great wonder, went to the house.
For the sake of a matter beyond my sight, Hari and I, together with Lakṣmī, vanished;
Durvāsas, having bowed again and again to the devotee Sāgara, [departed] with his grain-basket.
Having bestowed his most excellent blessing upon her, whose name was Sārikā, he said:
"May your wealth be inexhaustible, and may your grain be inexhaustible. (54)
May your vessel be inexhaustible, and may your faith likewise be inexhaustible;
may your food-offering be inexhaustible, and may your merit likewise be inexhaustible.
May your liberation be imperishable, may your devotion also be imperishable, and may your merit from the practice of giving be likewise imperishable; with these words, I shall now depart. (56)
Having spoken thus, being honored and exceedingly pleased, he departed for the forest.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, was the ocean protected by me there. (57)
Then, having heard this, eighty-eight thousand Vālakhilyas— the sons of Brahmā and great sages who were of dwarf stature— arrived there.
On the new moon day, Sāgara indeed provided them with prasādapolikās to eat in the very early morning, and likewise offered them hospitality and honor. (59)
Then, for the purpose of a meal, there arose a most excellent row [of guests] through the invitation;
at that time, Sāgara remembered Nārāyaṇa Viṣṇu and me as well. (3.208.60)
And immediately Janārdana arrived there along with Lakṣmī;
he became a brahmin there, and Lakṣmī likewise became a brahmin woman.
Having suddenly made ten *polikā* cakes the size of the palm of a hand, he gave ten to each of the eighty-eight thousand [monks]. (62)
Dividing [the food] together, they gave it to me, and they ate with great joy;
having become truly satiated, they took a mouthful and departed.
Praising the devotion to the ocean and the graciousness of Hari, O Lakṣmī, in this manner that ocean was [honored] by me there along with you. (64)
Protected by his excellent companion, he fed all the sages;
then Śaṅkara, realizing that his home was supremely sanctified, [departed].
Together with ten million followers, they arrived at midday;
all of them indeed possessed the appearance of holy men, wearing matted hair and animal skins.
Knowing that the food-offering was supreme and inexhaustible, they requested it;
they asked for the meal of *polikās* (fried cakes) and the vessels that purify even Kṛṣṇa.
There, Sārika and Sāgara, filled with fear, remembered me;
I then quickly arrived at their home along with Lakṣmī.
Having prepared a hundred *polikās*, I gave them to each virtuous ascetic;
indeed, I myself gave ten lakhs to the renunciants.
The wearer of many forms said, "Only a hundred of you remain at the end.
Having eaten those *polikā* cakes from the vessel, they were satisfied and praised the Ocean.
They indeed went to their own Kailāsa, while Śaṅkara practiced meditation;
there he beheld the cause, Viṣṇu, as Bālakṛṣṇa, endowed with splendor.
"Seeing me as one who is subservient to my devotees, he attained supreme wonder.
It was in this manner, O Lakṣmī, that the ocean was churned by me at that time.
Then, having heard this, Brahmā himself approached for the sake of a *polikā* offering; accompanied by ten million *siddhas*, he went quickly to obtain his grace. (73)
And Sāgara, by way of the celestial path, again requested Hari for the favor arising from the *polikā*, for the sake of satisfying ten million perfected ones (*siddhas*). (74)
He remembered me as his protector, and I then appeared before him,
accompanied by Lakṣmī, Śrī, and Rādhā.
Then he was together with Lalitā, as well as with Māṇikī and Ramā,
along with Padmāvatī and indeed with the beloved wives of Brahmā.
I remained in the sky with my wives, numbering in the hundreds of billions;
having had a thousand *polikā* cakes made, I was accompanied by ten million beloveds.
I gave a thousand *polikās* to each of the Siddhas, yet a thousand remained; thus the Creator of the Universe was struck with wonder. (78)
Then Sāgara, likewise perceiving his own supreme good fortune, conducted himself by making everything dependent upon Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. (79)
He performs the welcoming rites for guests day and night;
his inexhaustible granary attained fame throughout the three worlds.
Great lords come and depart from the three worlds;
casting aside all supreme exertion, the ocean serves him with joy. (8.1)
He did not beg for assistance from another or from divine power;
rather, when he felt fear, that devotee remembered me alone. ||82||
Thus, having observed the devotion and the disposition of that devotee who has surrendered his very self, I then became pleased with him, who serves the living beings of the three worlds. (83)
In particular, I reflected there for the sake of my devotees:
"I must give him this wish-fulfilling vessel, in which there shall be countless *polikā* cakes. (84)
Likewise, another vessel for the bhājā may constantly appear, wherein infinite well-cooked bhājās may also manifest. (85)
Having reflected thus, he gave him two vessels of excellent luster;
in them, he had prepared well-cooked *polikās* and *bhājikās* right at dawn.
He constantly protects both of his vessels by covering them;
I have said that there, either you or your wife is devoted to her husband.
Indeed, as many full vessels as you desire— even infinite ones— as many as you imagine, so many shall they be, filled and auspicious.
Delightful things will emerge from these two through mere volition; there will be no effort required for serving food, nor even the act of offering vessels. (89)
"They shall have no duties to perform; they will indeed go of their own accord into the [divine] ranks.
Having spoken thus, I was honored and given a vessel of water.
Such was that inexhaustible and full vessel, the cause of the full jar;
then, having vanished from that place, the ocean rejoiced exceedingly.
Then, on the auspicious new moon day of the month of Bhādra, having realized this great marvel,
the ancestors dwelling in the realms of Mahas, Jana, Tapa, and Satya arrived by the hundreds of millions and tens of billions.
Then all those embodied beings, eager for the sake of satisfaction, arrived by the will of Suprasāda and stood arranged in rows. 93.
Having purified herself by bathing and prepared various foods and cakes, Sārikā placed milk-porridge fit for a *śrāddha* rite into those two vessels. (94)
Having covered it and offered it to Viṣṇu, he prepared everything as prescribed;
Sāgara, too, having performed his ablutions, approached the presence of the recipient.
At that time, he thought: "Indeed, crores, ayutas, and arbudas of vessels—countless and full—have emerged from this pair of bowls. (96)
O Rame, for each individual ancestral deity, a vessel has been presented, filled with *polikās* and likewise with milk-rice (*pāyasa*). 97.
Likewise, with vessels and water-jars, they were satiated; having eaten, the ancestors—numbering in the millions, billions, and hundreds of millions—departed, fully satisfied. (98)
Empty vessels returned to their dissolution by their very nature;
in this way, that ocean was consumed by me during the sacrifice of parched grain.
Just as he who welcomes all increases his merit through supreme compassion,
so indeed did Kirāta experience everything through devotion to Devarāta.
Then, after some time, accompanied by divine attendants, I brought the couple together with a magnificent celestial chariot to my imperishable abode.
O Lakṣmī, thereafter there was the city of Mahīśāṭī, and then the one known by the name Godhumabhājikā, as well as Godhumasārikā.
Then the earth was called Godhūmarā, a purifying ground;
thus was that great tīrtha created by me, the compassionate one.
Afterwards, when the king had liberated the couple, the sage Godhara made that *kusūla* subject to his own control; meanwhile, the wheat was [consumed]. (104)
They became invisible, and the three vessels also became invisible;
the food-distribution hall was completed, and Camatkāra attained dissolution.
Thus, having observed that act of fate—the *kusūla* granary being perpetually empty—the wise Godhara honored Hari while remembering him. (106)
Nevertheless, that wonder which has departed has indeed departed;
yet, O Lakṣmī, by reading or hearing this, one shall attain a divine state.

Thus ends the two hundred and eighth chapter, titled "The Description of how Śrī Hari, pleased by the devotion of the Kirāta devotee named Sāgara, granted him a heap of wheat in the form of a merchant, made the grain in his granary inexhaustible, made his bread-pans, vessels, and water-jars inexhaustible, and bestowed liberation upon him," in the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, within the third section, the Dvāpara Cycle.
Śrī Puruṣottama said: Listen, O Śrī Nārāyaṇī, to the virtuous story of the devotee of the Hūṇas named Sāraṅga, a resident of the village of Bhūdharī.
In the forest village of Bhūdharī in Saurāṣṭra, O Rame,
there dwells a devotee of mine belonging to the Hūṇa caste, together with his family.
Having first performed his ablutions and worshipped me thereafter,
he leads the queen to a grassy meadow in order to graze her.
He goes to the grassy forest and likewise returns home at evening;
for in that forest there are lions, tigers, and even bears.
Moreover, wolves, leopards, and other predatory creatures—
tigers and lions— sometimes attack cows, buffaloes, and bulls.
Having killed them, they devour them; for they are indeed givers of terror and givers of suffering.
There was a Hūṇa named Sāraṅga, who possessed fifty female buffalo-cows as his wealth.
He grazes his buffaloes upon the most excellent and beloved pastures;
then, at the time of midday, from within a grove of trees by his side— || 7 ||
Five lions arrived by way of the forest path of karma upon the herd of female buffaloes, whose livelihood consists of grazing for fodder. (8)
Suddenly and unexpectedly, five roaring lions fell [upon him]— powerful, exceedingly well-fed, invincible, and possessed of great ferocity.
Suddenly, those queens also formed a protective circle with their backs,
guarding their faces all around while keeping their children in the center.
Out of anger and for the sake of protecting their lives, they formed themselves into a circle out of fear;
having gathered together and constructed a village-like enclosure, they offered prostration.
Upon seeing the village of Mahiṣī, the lions were quickly seized with fear;
turning back, they repeatedly discharged their urine from a distance.
If, having become separate from his own circle, he should flee for the sake of causing fear to the beasts amidst the masses of foul-smelling winds, then [the following occurs]. 13.
The lions, having seized them, would have devoured and killed them for their own food;
thus they acted, roaring and displaying their ferocity.
Nevertheless, those female buffaloes did not emerge from the caravan;
likewise, the lions remained just as they were, roaring most terrifyingly.
Having heard this, ten other lions also arrived for the sake of food;
those fifteen lions circled around Cakraka on all sides.
But all those queens, remaining as they were, did not run away, nor did they flee, nor could they reach him. || 17 ||
In this very way, it became evening; the lions were no longer far away.
Then the fire blazed forth, consuming the Sāraṅga and the Hūṇas. (18)
And on all sides of the female buffaloes, as they gathered fuel separately, the lions departed to a distance, fearing the fire. (19)
Nevertheless, those cruel times have not departed entirely;
they still wander all around and rush forth for the purpose of killing. || 3.209.20 ||
Nightfall has arrived and there is no assistance there;
moreover, in the shrouded darkness of night, the strength of lions becomes exceedingly great. (21)
There would be the destruction of the queens; what should be done on this ground of calamity?
Without Nārāyaṇa Kṛṣṇa, no helper is to be found. (22)
Thinking, "The Blessed One himself is the protector when the great time of calamity has arrived," he indeed obtained the mantra and, absorbed in it, recited it. (23)
That excellent mantra which was obtained from Lomaśa by Aśvapaṭṭatīrthin was formerly recited by that king of the Hūṇa devotees.
Oṃ, salutations to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Master; svāhā!
Having recited this one hundred and eight times, he beheld Hari in the sky. (25)
O Anādi-Śrī-Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa Viṣṇu, O Teacher of the World!
O Bāla-Kṛṣṇa, O Hare-Kṛṣṇa, protect me, protect me here! 26.
O Lion, protect me here who have come to you for refuge;
O Kṛṣṇa, in this forest, no other protector exists apart from you. (27)
O Hare Kṛṣṇa, O Bālakṛṣṇa, come quickly and protect us!
As darkness increases, death will surely befall us; of this there is no doubt. (28)
O Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, I am Your devotee; protect me!
For living beings, death occurs somewhere or other—of this there is no doubt. (29)
But, O Kṛṣṇa, it is my opinion that an untimely death here for these queens by forcibly tearing their bodies with fingernails is not appropriate. (3.209.30)
O Blessed One, O Kṛṣṇa, it is the milk of these cows that is indeed drunk by you every day—at dawn during worship, as an offering, during the day, and at night. (31)
If you do not provide protection for those women for whom I cause lamps to be lit with ghee at the onset of night, are you then truly merciless? (32)
O Kṛṣṇa, why do you not protect those for whom there is excellent curd, both very sweet and thick? 33.
Come quickly for our protection; otherwise, I who am your devotee shall first give up my life for the sake of the sacrificial animal. (34)
The master must always first protect those who depend upon him;
for if the master perishes, their destruction follows, which is not considered to be the fault of the master. (35)
"O Kṛṣṇa, these queens are looking toward me as their protector;
O Kṛṣṇa, residing as you do within my heart, do you not see? (36)
Look, look, O Hare Kṛṣṇa! These great serpents have fallen;
let him be merely a devourer, or even let him be a protector. (37)
Having spoken thus, O Lakṣmī, Sāraṅgahūṇa, the foremost of my devotees, shed tears and indeed sighed deeply,
free from all worldly desire.
Thinking, "We have come to our death," they wept for a moment;
the lions exerted their strength while remaining at a distance out of fear of the fire. (39)
The powerful Sāraṅga bird, having ignited and thoroughly kindled firewood on all sides,
casts it down here and there upon the ground.
"One should exert effort to protect one's life to the full extent of one's intellectual power;
thinking thus, one makes such an effort, yet the will of Viṣṇu is more powerful. (41)
Then, taking a flaming piece of wood in his hand and wandering about on all sides,
he indeed performed intense worship for the protection of his queens.
Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, O Bālakṛṣṇa, Lord of Śrī!
Hare Viṣṇu, Hare Jiṣṇu, Kṛṣṇa-Kṛṣṇa, Lord of Ramā! ||43||
Thus, O Rame, with my throat uplifted, I performed this hymn of praise to you;
then, for his protection and for the protection of the queen, I spoke.
Instantly, he assumed the great form of Siṃharāja, the maned lion, complete with a trunk, by which [the enemy] was indeed quickly struck with fear. 45.
Lions, tigers, elephants, and even śarabhas—let alone ordinary beasts—[flee] from that which is exceedingly cruel, terrifying, and possesses a fresh trunk-staff. (46)
Assuming the form of the great lion-king, I went forth;
making a roar like that of a cloud, I caused the beasts of the forest to tremble. (47)
O lions, know me to be a great lion, a man with eyes possessing the brilliance of lightning, the terrifying king of all species of lions. 48.
Hearing that [the monkey] possessed a strength exceeding a hundred [elephants], they were struck with fear in the great forest;
then, I suddenly leaped from the forest into the sky itself.
Having torn through a garment of a hundred cubits, I fell into the presence of the lion;
meanwhile, the lions, their courage lost due to great fear, stood before me.
Suddenly, out of fear of me, all those lords of beasts fled from the mouth of that one who resembled Death itself and entered the forest. (51)
Having suddenly put those lords of beasts to flight, I, the king of lions, assuming the guise of a human being, quickly became their prey. (52)
With a serene countenance and tranquil, bearing the conch, discus, mace, and lotus,
he was consoling his devoted queen and likewise consoling his devotee.
Seeing both Hari and me, Sāraṅga also approached closely;
having regained his life, he rejoiced and offered praise with supreme joy.
He fell at the feet of the queens and awakened them all with fearless cries, even though the queens themselves were already free from fear.
They rejoiced and became full of happiness there due to those two men;
they attained composure, and then Sāraṅga, the king of devotees, appeared.
Then Lakṣmī, having milked the milk, caused it to be drunk by me;
and I drank the excellent milk of all the queens. (57)
Then, together with Sāraṅgabhaṭa and the queens,
I proceeded slowly toward that gate of the mountain fortress.
There I dwelt joyfully until dawn, honored with offerings by my devotees, served by their wife and her followers, and by other Hūṇas as well. (59)
He was fully gratified by the chanting of His names and other such acts, by massaging His feet and similar services, by offerings of water, and likewise by other great festivals.
Then, at dawn, when the sun had risen, I assumed a virtuous form and was served by all of them with foods fragrant with flowers.
Questioned by the devotees of the Hūṇas for their welfare, I likewise took delight [in teaching] and instructed them for the sake of destroying their sins.
Listen, all you who are my devotees, though you may all possess coarse intellects;
nevertheless, by making an effort toward the highest good, you shall become possessed of subtle intellect.
Sirs, you indeed possess the wisdom for liberation, for that is subtle wisdom;
those who are intent upon their own highest good truly possess most subtle intellects.
If they are skillful in worldly affairs for their own welfare,
they are indeed considered fools, as if asleep, possessing always but a dull intellect.
Those who are shrouded by illusion, being dull and foolish, are said to be like cattle—whether they be a king, a leader, a guru, or even a teacher. (66)
If one who has studied the sciences does not strive for his own liberation, he is indeed a person of dull intellect; such a fool shall go to the realm of Yama.
Those divine men and women who abide in devotion to me are truly human; however, those who are not devoted should be understood as being like beasts, dwelling in hell. 68.
My devotees obtain a vision of me with their own eyes;
for those eyes are non-material and are always sustained by my yoga.
Hari and I dwell within the heart of the devotee; that very heart is divine.
The body of the devotees is divine, and their senses are likewise divine.
My internal organ is divine, and my activities are likewise always divine;
established in the abode of the Imperishable, I dwell somewhere upon the surface of the earth.
In some places here I appear as one who is like a devotee;
nevertheless, I am truly divine, for you all possess divine forms.
All the celestial queens are my devotees, as are all the divine men and women;
I am the Self of all selves, independent, the Lord, and the Master of all powers.
I am Hari, the Lord of Rādhā and Lakṣmī, higher than the highest;
I am the form of the cause of all, yet distinct within my own abode.
I myself have become this virtuous form here, appearing in an excellent guise;
by my yoga, the cowherdesses and the Hūṇas have attained divinity.
And having attained identity with me, they directly behold me through all their external and internal organs, which have become divine. ||76||
I am to be seen through sincerity and never otherwise;
out of compassion, I am to be grasped by the devotee themselves, and certainly not by any other means.
All the principles of Māyā attain divinity through contact with me;
indeed, the twenty-fifth principle, the individual soul, becomes liberated by union with me. (78)
I am the twenty-sixth principle, and I am the Blessed One, Puruṣottama himself;
I, who am the cause of all incarnations, remain under the control of my devotee. (79)
I am devoid of the qualities of Māyā, yet adorned with divine and transcendental qualities; I am worshipped by Īśvara and others, and among my devotees I am likewise so. (3.209.80)
Having worshipped and served me, and having realized me as the divine Nārāyaṇa, my devotees go to the imperishable abode, which is attended by the divine pārṣadas. 8.1.
Women who have attained union with me possess divine forms;
cows, buffaloes, and bulls have attained divinity through union with me.
By my yoga, O sages, my virtuous daughters as well as the youths and cowherds have attained divinity equal to mine. (83)
Even the wives dear to Brahmā, as well as the trees and creepers,
were transformed by my yoga into divine beings equal to me.
May they worship me constantly thereafter, and may they offer me water, milk, fruit, roots, bulbs, sweet food, and even leaves. (85)
Let them perform devotion in the morning, at midday, and likewise in the evening; day and night, let them remember me, Kṛṣṇa, in all their actions. (86)
May they constantly serve the virtuous with food and water, and may they always worship and glorify me with great zeal. (87)
In this world of imperishable liberation, I am the Lord of the Gopīs;
but for those with desires, I bestow skillful enjoyments of heaven that bring happiness.
Having spoken thus, and having always blown the great conch from below so that the predatory beasts would flee far away, he received worship.
O Lakṣmī, those Sāraṅga-Hūṇakas vanished from the forest;
they became happy and in the end attained the imperishable abode.
Thus, whether they dwell in the forest or in villages, whether they live in separate houses, or even those who are wretched—men or women—whoever worship me, Hari; || 91 ||
As soon as I am remembered, I, the Lord, truly deliver them from distress;
I grant them enjoyment, liberation, and an eternal state of bliss.
From reading, hearing, or even remembering this, there shall be the destruction of the sins of the wicked, as well as liberation and eternal protection. (92)

Thus ends the two hundred and ninth chapter, titled "The Description of how Śrī Hari protected the Hūṇa devotee named Sāraṅga—who possessed cattle and wealth of buffaloes—from the calamity inflicted by a lion in the forest and granted him liberation," in the Dvāpara Cycle of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
Listen, O Nārāyaṇī Śrī, to another story of a devotee;
there was a Puṣkasa named Yajñarādha who resided in Virādhakheṭa.
In the land of Ānarta, on the shore of the Samudrakhāḍikā, there lived a devotee;
it was there that ships filled with merchandise arrived and likewise departed. (2)
Wherever [the ship] was constantly launched, there he was appointed for the work of cleaning by the superintendent of the great vessel, his livelihood being provided [by him].
He constantly performs the sweeping of boats, riverbanks, and refuse heaps, together with his wife, at every spot along the way.
Likewise, the ship captains, other merchants, and laborers—even those compassionate ones—gave him the remnants of their food. || 5 ||
They also give vegetables such as leaves and the like, flat cakes, milk, roasted grain, cooked food, clothing, and other such things.
Thus,
being well-provided with food as well as a fair wage, he who is always skilled in his own work indeed carries out his duties constantly.
Whatever is obtained there, it is most excellent to sprinkle it with water, and having held a Tulasī leaf and then remembered me; (8)
Having mentally offered [the fruit] to me, he eats it and protects it, and not otherwise;
every morning, at the foot of a Pippala tree, he worships both Hari and me.
Having remembered me, he indeed worships me with water, food, fruits, and leaves;
likewise, having remembered me at midday and in the evening, he eats his meal.
Having performed the kīrtana together at night and likewise remembering Me,
the devotee— whether a wife, a son, or a daughter— sleeps while rotating the rosary.
For such a devotee who always eats the remains of offerings,
after giving [portions] to a dog, a cow, crows, and a person of the Puṣkasa caste— || 12 ||
Having given [food] repeatedly to the ants, to the sky, and to the gods, he indeed eats as one who subsists on remnants (vighasa); likewise, having also given to the fish.
Even that Puṣkasa beholds Hari within all living beings;
he possesses the realization that Brahman is the Self of all, and likewise, as the king of devotees, he is endowed with knowledge.
Indeed, this body is a mere outcast, always a vessel for impurity;
likewise, all bodies in every respect are containers of filth. (15)
If they are not equal in mind because they are pure, then for one whose mind is pure, their status as a Puṣkasa dissolves. (16)
In the womb, the child is not pure, as he partakes of the impure channels;
likewise, birth is impure, and after birth, one remains possessed of impurity. (17)
One who is devoid of purity is thus eternally impure and possessed of defilement;
he is joined with the turbidity of the mind and burdened by the stains of desire, anger, and the like. || 18 ||
Possessing a nature of deceit regarding his own interests, defiled by latent impressions (*vāsanā*), impure and burdened by a body, he is filled with pride, envy, and malice. (19)
Possessed of the notions of "I" and "mine," dragged away by negligence and delusion,
he remains truly impure, bound by his attachment to wife, children, and retinue.
Defiled by ignorance, attachment, clinging, and obsession, and filled with egoism and the like, he is a sinner through his indulgence in worldly enjoyments. (21)
This body, subject to the great afflictions of disease, illness, old age, and death, is called a *puṣkasa*; I am the conscious Self, not a *puṣkasa*.
All bodies are indeed *puṣkasas*, but the Self is never a *puṣkasa*;
the Self is Brahman—stainless, peaceful, pure, devoted, and radiant. (23)
By the majesty of the Supreme Lord, possessed of the awakening of being, consciousness, and bliss, I am liberated and free from bondage; here, I am forever a partaker of liberation. 24.
O Lakṣmī, even a Puṣkasa understands this always as his own nature;
he constantly conducts himself like one who is liberated, being ever devoted to meditation upon Me. (25)
This supreme state is established solely in the Blessed One and likewise established in the Self;
for him there is no self-interest, nor even the slightest mental affliction.
O Lakṣmī, tell me, how could I not indeed provide protection, delight to the heart, and the fulfillment of desires for such a devotee? (27)
O Lakṣmī, living beings, gods, and likewise lords are always equal to me;
all embodied beings here exist within my very Māyā as my own sons. (28)
A Brahmin, a king, a wretched person, a Puṣkasa, a woman, a eunuch, an animal, a bird, an insect, one who is afflicted, a tree, a creeper, and even grass—[all these are eligible]. (29)
Everything—even the fish and the insects—is like a son to me;
however, those who are immersed in service to me, for them especially, I am theirs.
I am the father, the protector, the sustainer, the shelter, the leader, and the supreme goal; for others, however, I am the witness who bestows the fruit of what has been done.
Then, on one occasion, a thought even arose in Bhakta:
"How might Nārāyaṇa himself come within the range of my vision? (32)
Then Hari himself was heard by that virtuous man from the mouth of a saint;
through service to a holy person, he becomes accessible.
Then this Yajñarādha indeed seeks out service;
wherever a virtuous person is heard of, he surely goes to that place. (34)
Having heard [the news] in Camatkārapura, he went to the bank of the Nāgamatī on the pretext of visiting a sacred site; there, he bathed in the river with true devotion. ||35||
At the sacred ford of Nāganātha, he indeed beheld a virtuous ascetic who had mastered the three states of existence, who was divine, established in Brahman, and beloved of Hari.
Then he saw the great seer named Brahmāyana, a peaceful sage who had renounced all attachments,
absorbed in meditation upon his seat, contemplating the Brahman.
Having gone before him, he prostrated himself like a staff;
for the duration of a ghaṭī, he stood motionless in front of him with palms joined in reverence.
At the end of a ghaṭikā, the best of sages emerged from his meditation and saw before him a Puṣkasa devotee who was performing a sacrifice.
Having bowed down, Yajñarādha stood with palms joined in reverence;
being instructed by the saintly one, who said, "May it be well with you," he sat down.
With great devotion, he sat down before the virtuous one;
he did so for the sake of increasing his virtues and also for the sake of attaining the company of the good.
Having heard that the means for the direct attainment of the Supreme Lord are indeed [these], the sage Brahmāyana, who was established in the self and the supreme self, rejoiced. (42)
Having remembered me, Nārāyaṇa, he spoke and instructed him:
"Listen, O devotee, to the qualities of the virtuous, which people here indeed adopt. (43)
These virtuous ones indeed become oceans of excellence; they perceive the faults of the wicked, whereas those who are corrupt truly perceive the faults of the virtuous. 44.
In the constant assembly of the virtuous, future virtues arise;
through the perpetual grasping of the virtues of the good and the realization of their greatness, [excellence is attained]. 45.
One's own beautiful virtues, which are auspicious and bestow the state of perfection, flourish; however, the occasional physical defects of the virtuous are not to be grasped. 46.
Those who seize upon faults indeed become faulty themselves, even if they were previously virtuous;
through great sin, their virtues are destroyed from the root in no time at all.
Therefore, one should indeed accept the good qualities of the virtuous, but never their faults; for by grasping even a small, base fault, a great ruin may ensue. (48)
By the very company of the virtuous, millions of virtues increase;
likewise, the dharmas of the Bhāgavatas flourish through association with the good. 49.
By serving those who are exclusively virtuous, one indeed attains divinity;
for embodied beings in this world, association with the virtuous arises through affection. (3.210.50)
Realizing that the virtuous grant liberation, destroy all sins, and bestow one's desires, [one should approach] the presence of the virtuous. (5.1)
One should always behave like a servant toward such a person; one should seek the company of the virtuous.
All spiritual qualities flourish through association with the good. (52)
Dispassion arises, as does the knowledge of oneself and the Supreme Self;
thereafter, devotion toward Hari is born, accompanied by the knowledge of His majesty. (53)
The physical basis shall also be firm, all activities shall be for the sake of Kṛṣṇa, and the operations of both the external and internal senses shall be permeated by the Blessed Lord. (54)
For indeed, for the devotee, the door to liberation remains ever open;
it becomes the supreme abode that bestows splendor and grants the attainment of the Great Path. 55.
The great attachment to women, wealth, and the like, which is difficult for an embodied being to cast off, likewise, when directed toward the virtuous, grants liberation to the embodied being. (56)
Affection for the virtuous should always be cultivated, indeed even more so than for one's wife, children, and others;
for those who are attached to the virtuous through such affection, eternal liberation is attained. (57)
A woman and a man should cultivate great faith in the service of the virtuous;
service performed with one's whole being certainly delivers even a master of illusion.
Service performed through total self-surrender makes a person successful;
when the saints are pleased, they indeed bestow the imperishable abode and divine nature.
Auspicious place and time should be resorted to; likewise, auspicious company should be sought.
Auspicious actions should always be performed, and the most excellent, auspicious mantra should be maintained.
Meditation on Hari should be performed constantly; the virtuous should always be held in the heart;
the initiation of the Bhāgavatas should be received, and one should always take refuge in Hari. (61)
For one who conducts oneself in this manner, Nārāyaṇa will indeed become manifest;
however, through association with improper places and the like, the intellect becomes ruined and fallen.
When there is a conjunction of a good country and other such factors, the mind becomes excellent and pure;
through the power of a preeminent accumulation of merit, a person obtains a good country and the like. (63)
Association with the virtuous arises for him, and from that, divine nature is born;
his intellect becomes stainless, and he is no longer affected by defects such as those of place and the like.
For one in whom these [faults] arise, it should be understood that great evil committed in the past has arrived, by which he is impelled toward sin. (65)
Or rather, because he has committed an offense against these great and virtuous ones here,
the fruit of that is that his mind has indeed become sinful, bestowing upon him transgression.
One should perform service to destroy that [ignorance] with a sincere disposition;
furthermore, through the service of Hari, one shall attain the favor of the virtuous.
Now, he who is a sinner indeed commits treachery and speaks base words out of a disposition of atheism. (68)
What indeed would be the use of the assembly of the virtuous here on earth?
For there are rogues who pose as virtuous; let them not hold such an assembly.
Thus do the wicked indeed speak; they should always be avoided from afar.
Therefore, one should cultivate association with the virtuous, for association with the virtuous is indeed the medicine.
One must certainly not associate with the wicked; association with the wicked is supreme poison.
The suffering person resorts to Śrīnātha solely for the sake of destroying that suffering. (71)
One who desires wealth indeed worships for the sake of attaining wealth; one who desires sovereignty likewise does so;
even one whose goal is liberation always worships Hari for the sake of absolute isolation.
But the man of wisdom, being devoted to the Blessed One, serves the Supreme Lord;
surrendering himself and fixed in the Blessed One, he becomes dear to Hari. (73)
For one who is devoted to Hari on this earth, there shall be direct realization;
he will come to possess complete knowledge of the majesty of Hari. (74)
His affection for Hari persists incessantly in every way and in manifold forms;
indeed, all his latent impressions other than those of Kṛṣṇa have truly perished. (75)
Those whose latent impressions have been entirely destroyed through service to the single-minded [devotees] certainly become wise; therefore, one should cultivate the company of the virtuous. (76)
One should always, through the association of the virtuous, cultivate knowledge of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Lord of syllables, together with his majesty. (77)
Pride must always be uprooted through association with the virtuous;
for those possessed by pride, divine qualities never flourish. (78)
An arrogant person indeed does not perform service for the virtuous, even when they are at the lowest level;
he does not stand before the virtuous with palms joined in reverence, nor does he praise them with his speech.
One should not bow before men even while living like a pauper;
pride is a great defect, for the pillar of pride is the cause of destruction. (3.210.80)
Devotion, knowledge, detachment, and the like do not increase at all in one who is conceited; but for the devotee whose pride has dissolved, these great qualities continue to flourish. 8.1
Nārāyaṇa himself dwells directly within his heart, through constant service and attendance upon the virtuous and upon Hari. ||82||
The pride of one who is richly endowed with intense dispassion quickly dissolves;
through devotion to the contemplation of the Self as Brahman, Hari is pleased with him. (83)
Indeed, the form of Hari appears serene to one who is serene;
for the sweet form is seen both within the heart and externally as well. (84)
Free from pride, the king of devotees is considered the best and endowed with the power of the Lord;
having abandoned arrogance and being established in the Brahman of the Self, he worships Śrī Hari. (85)
O Blessed One, for one whose steadfastness in the Self and steadfastness in the Lord have indeed reached maturity,
every illusory affliction dissolves right here.
By listening even to this narrative, by serving the virtuous, and likewise through devotion to Nārāyaṇa and the worship of Hari; ||87||
They attain the state of a Siddha, as well as omniscience and lordship, according to the specific nature and strength of one's own chosen deity’s worship. 88.
For him, such a great, divine, and supreme happiness arises;
illusory suffering is utterly destroyed—of this there is no doubt. (89)
For those whose love for Lord Mādhava is equal to that of the women of Vraja, no duty remains to be performed beyond this limit. (3.210.90)
Through the service of the virtuous, firm conviction in the majesty of Kṛṣṇa arises;
and the perfection of one's worship shall quickly become firmly established on all sides. (91)
He who exists in the supreme imperishable abode, in the realm of Goloka, in Vaikuṇṭha, in the city of Śrī, and in the unmanifest, immortal realm; ||92||
The Lord of Brahmā, Hari, the Lord of Rādhā, the Lord of Kamalā, the Lord of Lalitā’s Śrī, the Lord of Ramā, the Lord of Śrī, and the Supreme Lord. ||93||
He alone is the Inner Controller and the Beloved; that very Lord himself is perceived within through devotion in meditative absorption, and from without through service. 94.
Hari Nārāyaṇa, assuming a human form, indeed meets with even ordinary people;
among men, he becomes equal to them. (95)
That Brahman which is the imperishable light, from which millions of liberated lords and luminous beings such as the sun and moon shine—that indeed is He. 96.
Indeed, assuming a human form, he is perceived by means of a lamp;
he becomes visible to men even in the light of the sun and moon. (97)
Even at the end of the body, by the swift recollection of his name, even a great sinner becomes pure and free from sin, and is fit for the path to liberation. ||98||
He alone becomes accessible through the devotion of a sincere devotee;
worship that Supreme Self, the Lord of Śrī, Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa. 99.
Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord; svāhā!
Recite this mantra and likewise meditate upon Bāla-Kṛṣṇa within your heart. (3.210.10)
Drink the ever-pleasing water and eat the offered food;
remember the Lord who is the beloved husband of Brahmā, and you shall attain liberation.
Having been addressed thus by that lotus-born Brahmā, the Puṣkasa attained knowledge,
and after honoring him, he then departed for his own home.
In the manner described, he honors, meditates upon, and serves [the Lord];
thus he indeed performs service to the virtuous, and beholds and remembers the Lord. 10.3.
Once, however, Yajñarādhā beheld near a pippala tree a virtuous man, rich in beauty, auspicious, and equal to Brahmā himself.
Seeing him suddenly, the virtuous man performed a prostration like a staff and offered words of welcome; filled with affection, he also inquired after his welfare.
The devotee said: "I am skilled, especially in obtaining virtuous persons.
O holy one, give me your command so that I, together with my family, may serve you. (106)
The saintly one said, "Indeed, I must depart from this place for the holy site of Aśvapaṭṭasara, where Kṛṣṇa Narāyaṇa resides. (107)
"Having become my companion, come indeed with me";
"So be it," the Puṣkasa agreed, and he went forth together with him.
Accompanied by his entire family and young children,
just then a divine celestial chariot swiftly arrived from the sky.
O Lakṣmī, out of the power of my compassion, I myself became the bestower of liberation upon him;
indeed, having made them my own attendants (pārṣadas), I took them away in celestial chariots.
Having caused them to cast off their elemental bodies, I led them to my own imperishable state;
my devotees have attained that eternal, divine form and station.
Having thus performed what is beneficial for them through the company of the virtuous, all living beings who become like them worship me. 1.12.
From reciting this, hearing it, remembering it, or even causing others to hear it, there shall surely arise enjoyment, liberation, a divine state, and prosperity. (11.3)

Thus ends the two hundred and tenth chapter, titled "The Attainment of Liberation through Devotion to Śrī Hari by the Puṣkasa named Yajñarādhana and his family, following their meeting with the saintly Ṛṣi Brahmayāna," in the Third Section on the Continuation of the Dvāpara Age within the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
Listen, O Nārāyaṇī Śrī, to the story of a Caṇḍāla as well;
he indeed resided at the foot of a Rāyaṇa tree in a place known as Kapikṣaya.
Indeed, there was a Cāṇḍāla named Kapikṣaya who, together with his family, lived near Mount Raivata at Rāyaṇā; he was very wise. || 2 ||
First, due to the fault of his birth, he became a violent creature while wandering in the forest;
having killed the red wild monkeys, he would devour them. (3)
Therefore, having been informed by the forest-dwellers that he was a monkey (kapikṣaya),
he became famous in the forest by the very name Vānaramāra.
Then, on one occasion, seeing a large troop of monkeys situated in a grove of trees in the forest, he took up an arrow to slay them. (45)
Before the arrow was even released, that best of monkeys addressed him with a divine voice: "Listen, O best of outcastes! (6)
Having heard this, act as you desire for the sake of your journey; listen to me.
Formerly, you were a twice-born man who went to a low-caste woman and was devoted to courtesans.
There lived a Brahmin named Prājñeśvara, who was devoted to the performance of dharma and other duties;
he resided in the village of Śṛṅkhalā, where even the people were non-violent.
And by associating with them, by preparing their food, and through giving, honoring, and living together with them, their minds indeed became violent. || 9 ||
Due to the absence of proper place, time, action, speech, and companions, the heart gradually became devoid of goodness and inclined toward sin. (3.211.10)
The auspicious body of this Brahmin has been brought into contact with unrighteousness by you through union with a courtesan, as well as by [partaking of] things unfit for food and drink. (11)
Devoted to trivial activities and intent upon liquor and meat, you eventually met your death; thereafter, you— || 12 ||
He went to the city of Yama and there underwent the torments of Yama;
by the remainder of his sin, he now exists here as a Cāṇḍāla.
That prostitute, that low-caste woman, is indeed your wife who accompanies you here; likewise, your sinful friends and your sons and kinsmen are all here with you.
These sinners, bound by their evil deeds, exist in the womb of a caṇḍāla;
having committed sins in the past, you too have attained the state of a caṇḍāla.
Formerly, you defiled the state of a Brahmin with impurity like filth;
you destroyed great merit, as well as heaven and liberation.
