Beggars, travelers, virtuous women, and the poor eat their food—
curds that are indeed thick and sweet milks as well.
They partake of clarified butters endowed with nourishment, as well as sugar, molasses, honey, and the most excellent, sweet, and finest foods. || 15 ||
"Day after day they offer me ripe foods for Hari;
thus, through the practice of dharma, his prosperity increases. (16)
For they did not diminish, even as they were being enjoyed by the virtuous through the power of merit;
indeed, his fortune itself became exceedingly prosperous.
In whose house the five sacrifices are always performed by the twice-born,
a virtuous guest named Caitanyakāyani arrived at that sacrifice.
The great devotee, the best of worshippers, possessed of renunciation and dispassion, arrived; Jīrṇodbhava offered him a welcome.
Bowing down, he offered water, an auspicious seat, and sweet madhuparka;
he provided him with lodging in the cowshed and performed service for him.
Having performed the worship of the deity at night and having eaten, Caitanyakāyani engaged in the chanting of the pastimes and other deeds of Anādikṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. ||21||
In fifty-three years of this Brahmā, he proclaimed here and there the birth of Hari and the liberating divine sports performed therein.
Then he offered a hymn of praise which all the farmers heard:
"He who is the Supreme Brahman, the Blessed Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Beloved, the Sovereign. (23)
He shines in the supreme, imperishable ether, served by the liberated;
from him, indeed, manifold manifestations come forth during creation. (24)
This very son of Śrī Kambharā, the cowherd boy, resides in Saurāṣṭra at the sacred site of Aśvapaṭṭasāra in the field of Kuṅkumavāpī.
Where Śrī Lomaśa resides and the beloved of Brahmā dwell,
there are all the sacred fords (tīrthas), the gods, the lords, and the manifestations of prosperity.
Lakṣmī, Rādhā, Ramā, Padmāvatī, Śrī, Māṇikī, Pradhī, and Haripriyā—these wives of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Brahmā reside here. (27)
Wherein dwell countless holy ones whose nature is self-luminous, and where divine sages reside and take refuge. ||28||
Salutations to that Lord who performs the human dance, salutations to the inner controller of all; salutations to Hari, who bestows protection upon those virtuous ones within.
Salutations to that Supreme Soul, Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa,
[who delivers one] from spiritual afflictions as well as those caused by the divine powers.
Salutations again and again to the protector from the hardships of elemental beings and the like;
[salutations] to Vanacandraka for [protecting] from the cruel plunderer Sāmantavikrama. ||31||
And his wife Sukhādevī, by whom the merchants were protected,
was liberated through her reunion with the virtuous Sāyanāyana.
Salutations again and again to that Kṛṣṇa who abides as the protector;
to the Brahmin Dhaniṣṭhakaṣa, who was devoted to courtesans;
to his wife Snehalatā, and likewise to the preceptor Somāyana.
He protected King Mālavasiṃha and granted him liberation. ||34||
Salutations to that Supreme Lord, the beloved of Śrī, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow;
[salutations] to King Rājīva and the virtuous queen Kunda-nadevikā.
Salutations again and again to him who protected and likewise liberated;
he who provided protection for Devaviśrāma and the liberation of Kāṇḍikā. (36)
Salutations again and again to that Śrī Hari by whom this was performed;
and to his wife, Vidrumavallakī, who wore a joyful garland. (37)
Salutations again and again to that Hari, the Lord of Śrī, who rescued Śāṇadhara, Pitṛhan, and Karṣuka. (38)
Salutations to that Kṛṣṇa, who is Vṛṣahan and Nimbadeva; salutations to him, the vessel, the son of Kālindī, through his union with the lotus-abode of the virtuous. 39.
Salutations to that Kṛṣṇa who did not grant liberation to Rāyaṇadeva, the dancer, despite the yoga of Bodhāyana. ||3.235.40||
Salutations to him who rescued the singer named Nākirāla, as well as King Puṇḍravarmā, on the day of his vow in the city called Nākirālākhyapura. ||41||
Salutations again and again to that Lord who rescued the weaver known as Tūlavāya, as well as the wood-gatherer Jaṅgaladeva. 42.
Salutations again and again to you, who made the merchant Vātsalyadhīra and his wife Mañjulikā virtuous and chaste. ||43||
May that Hari, who rescued Tilakaraṅga, Vanapa, and their beloved wife Śikhādevī—even though he dwells within the heart—protect us. 44.
Salutations indeed to that Kṛṣṇa, who rescued Kṣetrapa, Nāñjakadeva, as well as Stena and Mahāmaya. ||45||
Salutations to that Lord of Śrī, who rescued the Kirāta named Sāgara and his wife Sārikā. 46.
Salutations to you who protected the Hūṇa named Sāraṅga,
as well as Yajñarādha and the Puṣkasa, through the intervention of Brahmāyana.
Salutations again and again to Kṛṣṇa, who liberated the one accompanied by his family;
and likewise to Him who [saved] the outcaste Kapikṣaya and the wise lord of the twice-born.
Salutations to that Kṛṣṇa, Hari, who liberated Nālīkara the blacksmith, as well as his wife Kundanikā. (49)
Salutations to that Śrī Viṣṇu, who liberated from the bonds of worldly existence the cobbler named Maṅgala and his wife Vibhāvarī.
Salutations again and again to that Blessed One who protected [them] from poison;
he who [protected] Haridāsa the chariot-maker and his wife Śrīmānavī.
O Lord, you liberated them again and again; salutations upon salutations to You!
[You liberated] Śilāhāra, Dāmaśilādaka, and his wife named Kalā.
Salutations to that Kṛṣṇa who liberated his servants,
as well as the artisan Sañjayadeva and his wife Keśavatī.
Hari rescued King Khaḍgavarman as well as other artisans;
salutations indeed to that Bālakṛṣṇa. ||94||
Salutations again and again to him who liberated Citrakṛt, Saṃbhara-deva, Citra, Saritāmpriyā, and other painters. ||55||
Salutations to him who protected the charcoal-carrier with pearl-like hair who had sought his refuge, as well as other laborers. (56)
Salutations to that Kṛṣṇa, who, through the instruction of Pautimāṣya, indeed liberated the hunter Cakradhara from the cycle of worldly existence. ||57||
Salutations again and again to him who, on the occasion of the construction of the Ghaṭīyaṇa temple, liberated even the treacherous Vāṭadhara from King Sutārasiṃhaka. 98.
Salutations again and again to that Kṛṣṇa who protected Vāṭadhāna along with his people and the queen of the King of the Dvīpas, and who liberated them. ||59||
Salutations to that Śrī Hari, Kṛṣṇa, who, on the occasion of the festival of Vṛṣaparvan, liberated Gṛhakāra by chanting "Śiva-jaya."
And Hari liberated Yaśodā’s son from the snare-maker by serving the sage Śuklāyana, and [he restored] his wife Rūpāvatī.
Likewise, he who rescued Bharavāṭa, named Udyamaśrīti, by his very birth,
as well as his wife Satīśvarī and the cowherdesses.
I bow to that Lord, the beloved Hari, who, on the occasion of the Rāmāyaṇa, rescued the camel-herder Dīrghabāhu.
Through the grace of Lord Nṛsiṃha, Hari-Nārāyaṇa rescued Kharapāla, who was like a jewel; I bow down to him.
I bow to that Lord of Lakṣmī, who liberated Gadārdaneśvara, the physician, and his wife Mukundinī from the cycle of worldly existence.
I bow indeed to him who brought about the liberation of Kīśanakulapāla and Deśyāvana, as well as his wife Purikā.
He [beheld] the barber named Harṣadharman and his wife Nigamikā;
the king Svarṇadhanvan and the queen Pañcadevikā.
By meeting with that virtuous abode of auspiciousness, Lord Hari Nārāyaṇa rescued them; indeed, I bow down to him.
And he who protected the goddess Rūḍāṇakī, the daughter of the Ābhīras, who had been oppressed by the Daityas—the beloved of Brahmā and the mistress of beauty—among those [who were present]. (69)
The Blessed Lord likewise created Mandārakalikā and others of divine form as his wives; I bow to that Janārdana.
Having made the fisherman Dhīraparvan pure through the yoga leading to Nirvāṇa, Kṛṣṇa liberated him; I bow down to him.
He rescued Tārakādarśaka from being impaled on a stake, restored King Supathānaka to his kingdom, and freed Śūlyaṅganā from the stake upon which she was fixed.
Having become one with matted hair, the son of Hari and Śrī Kṛṣṇa rescued him;
I bow down to that beloved Kṛṣṇa, the delighter of the cowherds. 73.
I bow to him who, through the yoga of Nārāyaṇāyana, liberated Jvālāprasāda by name, Agnida, and Prabhāvatī.

The illustrious [king] appointed Lavādāna as the superintendent of the royal palace, Garada as the lord of the realm, Śānteśvara as the crown prince, and Sūryakānta as the commander-in-chief of the army. (75)
I bow to that Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Teacher who dwells within the hearts of devotees, who rescued [the world] by means of the Kiṃśuka-āyana. 76.
Salutations to you who, through the yoga of the *nirmohana* weapon, liberated Indra from his captor and recovered his wife, the virtuous Satī.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, the virtuous Caitanyakāyani performed this hymn of praise to Hari, who is present everywhere and all around, at that time. 78.
Having heard and seen this, those farmers were struck with supreme wonder;
Jīrṇodbhava, the leader of the farmers, bowed down and questioned that sage.
O embodiment of consciousness, tell me the reason why protection as well as liberation was granted by the glorious Supreme Soul to those [trees]. (3.235.80)
Having heard them, the sage spoke that mantra of Nārāyaṇa to me:
"Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord; svāhā. (8.1)
Let other seekers of liberation constantly recite this mantra;
indeed, enjoyment and liberation shall surely be attained, and one shall become Nārāyaṇa himself. ||82||
"In times of calamity, the Supreme Lord shall provide great protection.
Having spoken thus, he ceased speaking and fell asleep while remembering me. (83)
The farmers were asleep, muttering that very mantra;
then, having risen in the morning and bathed, the practitioner, after worshipping me, [proceeded]. (84)
Having eaten the offered food and received worship, he departed for the forest;
those farmers constantly recite this supreme mantra. (85)
They worship me and Hari, and they even perform great festivals;
during the four months of Cāturmāsya, they have observed various vows dedicated to me.
Then, in the gardens, fields, forest lands, and in the wilds and thickets, there were stalks, grain, and grasses. (87)
When all the fruit-bearing trees became ears of grain, entirely filled with an abundance of grain and almost fully ripened in every way. (88)
That earth, extending for four yojanas, is indeed rich with crops; it shines with a golden hue due to its ripe leaves and medicinal herbs. (89)
Then, indeed, by the power of destiny and with the speed of the wind,
fire was drawn from the region above the boundary toward the farmer's hearth.
And having been cast down by the wind, it suddenly rose up over the fields of grain;
it spread over the dry grass and then pervaded the crops on all sides.
Then, in the fields filled everywhere with grain and ears of corn, he pervaded half a krośa like a forest fire and spread forth. 92.
Then a cry of "Alas! Alas! arose among the wife of the farmer;
indeed, thousands of men ran forth to extinguish the fire. ||93||
But, having flown up again and again by the force of the wind, he traveled far;
having become [light as] the sky, he moved through another enclosure and into another field.
It could not be extinguished at all; indeed, that terrifying fire spread forth, consuming all the grass and other vegetation for the sake of destroying the arisen sprouts.
A form that brought about famine spread everywhere;
at that time, all people, despite their efforts, became hopeless. (96)
They recited the protective mantra obtained from Caitanya;
they repeated it one by one for as long as they remained steadfast. 97.
While they were remembering me, the protector of the heart and destroyer of suffering, I too quickly contemplated their protection in the sky. (98)
Having manifested a cloud accompanied by lightning and thunder, I brought about rain at the end of a ghaṭikā; thus the fire that threatened the crops was extinguished. 99.
Within the distance of a single krośa, everything there was indeed reduced to ashes;
however, for the sake of the abundance of crops, I specifically brought down rain.
Furthermore, there, the crops, grasses,
and ears of grain indeed sprouted as before, following their respective seasons.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, at that time the fire of the rain was indeed extinguished by me;
thereafter, all the farmers created a new heap of grain.
In the ninth year, all desired foods, whatever vegetables there may be, boiled rice, pulses, alkaline foods, and other such items— 10.3.
Roasted grains that are succulent, delicious, and most excellent;
cooked foods smeared with nectar, and the finest milk-rice preparations.
All these offerings were presented to me in the vast temple;
there, I became manifest in person together with Lakṣmī before the image.
He enjoyed all kinds of foods— those to be chewed, those to be swallowed, those to be licked, and those to be sucked— as well as drinks and betel leaves.
The four-armed Lord himself, having partaken of the offering and bestowed his grace,
vanished instantly after receiving the lustration rite (nīrājanā) and worship.
All those Vaiṣṇavas attained a wonder born of my grace;
they enjoyed divine [bliss] and became purified. || 108 ||
All those members of my family constantly offered me devotion;
then, when the time arrived, they acted in due order and as was appropriate.
O Ramā, I shall draw you toward my own divine, imperishable state, which is free from suffering;
for all these hundred maidens are devoted to their husband as their sole vow.
Having worshipped me, these women—Brahmapriyā and the others who have taken refuge in you—have indeed given birth;
they are here in your abode, beginning with Devamaṇikā.
The cowherd girls of Kṛṣṇa exist in every way with divine bodies;
others have become liberated through my worship, O Rame.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, those farmers were liberated by me at that time through the recitation, hearing, remembrance, and even the mere practice of this [text]. (1.13)
They are born resembling liberated beings, enjoying my bliss;
they fulfill all desires, are not inferior to me, and have me as their very self. 1.14
Śrī Nārāyaṇī Śrī said:
O Hari, O Lord, O Husband, O Giver of all happiness, I am your devoted wife and a vessel of affection; for the sake of your satisfaction, how may I become beautiful? (1.15)
Śrī Puruṣottama said: To become beautiful in all her limbs, she should perform for me this supreme vow called Janmajayantī on the eighth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Kārttika.
She should dwell near [the deity] or consume fruits, milk, curds, and so forth;
with whatever offerings she obtains, the virtuous woman should worship me, endowed with prosperity.
For the sake of obtaining a face like the moon, one should give a golden moon;
for the sake of the beauty of the eyes, eyebrows, and forehead, one should give three golden leaves.
For the sake of the excellence of the cheeks, ears, nose, and lips, one should indeed offer golden leaves, ear-rings,
fine flowers, and bimba-fruit ornaments made of gold.
Likewise, for the sake of having teeth with a beautiful luster and fragrance, one should give golden kunda flowers during the vow;
furthermore, one should give sugar, kesaraka, keśara, and other such items.
For the sake of nourishment, one should give gold in the form of pomegranates and other fruits during the vow;
and for the sake of making the hands beautifully adorned, one should offer a stalk of sugarcane made of gold.
One should provide golden pitcher-panels for the sake of the beauty of the flanks, belly, and chest, as well as plates of gold and silver; these indeed bestow physical beauty.
One should give two jars for the sake of a slender waist and for the sake of the hips;
and for the sake of the delicacy of the vulva, one should give golden rings and pearls.
One should likewise give a gold coin, a conch-shell ring, or a pearl-oyster shell;
for the sake of a hairless vulva, one should give a vessel made of gold.
One should give musk, diamonds, and the like for the sake of health of the womb;
one should give two silver plantain trees for the sake of beautiful thighs.
One should offer plantain fruit for the sake of the feet, shanks, and beautiful form of one's chosen deity; sandals for the vehicle; and pearls for the sake of removing dust.
By propitiating Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa, a virtuous woman shall obtain everything;
on the day following the vow, she should feed the holy men and thereby obtain the fruit. || 127 ||
Thus I have told you everything that fulfills all desires; may all women obtain their wishes through this vow or through giving.
Thus have these deeds of mine been truly recounted to you—
deeds performed for the protection of my devotees during my sixteenth year.
Indeed, you have heard all those things desired by the mind,
which are endowed with the greatness of the virtuous and grant supreme liberation.
Out of compassion alone, O Rāmā, I have spoken these for the welfare of those who remember them,
for the liberation of those who meditate upon them, and for the removal of the sins of those who recite them.
For those who practice the yoga of identity, these indeed bestow great bliss;
and for women who have surrendered their all, they grant the state of being beloved by Brahman.
For those who have surrendered their very selves, they bestow the liberation of Brahman;
for those with desires, they fulfill all desires and grant happiness.
O Lakṣmī, by my grace, these divine pastimes of mine bestow upon those free from desire a state equal to my own; divine indeed are my yogi-devotees.
My entire divine field on earth consists of the supreme abode;
sixteen years have passed there, overflowing with great bliss.
"Indeed, on my seventeenth birthday,
a great festival will soon take place here, as initiated by Lomaśa and others."
I desist from all [other] wives even for the sake of exhaustion.
Om, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord; Svāhā! || 1.37 ||

Thus ends the two hundred and thirty-fifth chapter, titled "The Description of the Vision of the Lord and Liberation of the Farmer named Jīrṇodbhava through his Union with the Saint Caitanyakāyani, and the Narration of the Vow that Grants Beauty to Women," in the third section, the Dvāpara-santāna, of the glorious Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā.
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
Listen, O Śrī Nārāyaṇī, to the great festival of the seventeenth day;
on the day of my birth, the Caturvyūha shall perform it.
Vāsudeva, as well as Saṃkarṣaṇa, Aniruddha,
and Pradyumna— all these were likewise lords and great seers.
Having arrived tomorrow at the divine and greatly renowned imperishable field of Kuṅkumavāpikā, they will dwell there; let the female attendants be ready.
On the seventh day of the dark fortnight of the month of Caitra,
all the Lakṣmīs, the wives of Brahmā, were impelled and commenced their undertaking.
The goddesses of the assembly halls suddenly created the assembly halls themselves, as well as those specific locations within them, wherein the reflection of creation was manifested.
The Śṛṅgāradevis created divine ornaments;
the Dhāmadevis manifested radiant lights, and the Vanadevis manifested forests.
The goddesses of the groves created illusory trees;
the goddesses of flavors produced all kinds of tastes, and the goddesses of fragrance produced exquisite scents.
The Sarasvatīs produced songs, and Niśā created heavens; Annapūrṇā prepared the most excellent and sweet foods. || 8 ||
The Kalpa-creeper trees produced flowers, leaves, and petals; the wish-fulfilling gems (kalpamaṇi) created ornaments, and the fire produced gold.
The Earth-goddess, delightful couches, the wind as vehicles, the Rasa-halls beginning with Kamala, and the Vāruṇī drinking-halls; 3.236.10.
Lalitāśrī Mahālakṣmī brought her maidservants, who were like lotuses,
while Viṣṇu brought his own attendants, who were liberated souls.
Yajñanārāyaṇa quickly constructed the sacrificial pavilions;
all kinds of medicinal herbs and sacrificial fuel were swiftly brought forth.
The Gandharvas brought forth singers accompanied by musical instruments;
and the Kinnarīs and Apsarases, as well as female dancers, arrived swiftly. 1.3.
Then the lords of lords, the sovereigns who have attained liberation, such as Śaṅkara and others— the great commanders of the army— arrived for the purpose of welcoming him.
And the great seers returned with enthusiasm;
the hosts of Vāsudeva and others, as well as the Nārāyaṇas, likewise arrived.
The Rudras, the unborn Siddhas, and the Viṣṇus arrived there; likewise, the female lords, the liberated women, and all the Ramās came together.
The friends of Rādhā, the friends of Ramā, and the friends of Brāhmī arrived; and the Vairājas, the Hiraṇyagarbhas, and the Māyātattvas also came. (17)
The gods, goddesses, and ancestors, the guardians of the quarters and the protectors of the worlds, the sages, humans, and the devoted descendants of Kaśyapa all arrived. || 18 ||
Virtuous, righteous, and truthful ones, whose conduct was that of Brahman, arrived;
and the Ṛg, Yajur, Sāma, and Atharva Vedas, as well as the most excellent sacred fords, arrived.
Īti, Dhṛti, Śivā, and Śakti—the wives of the Vedas—arrived;
the oceans, the wives of Kṛṣṇa, and Rādhā and the others also arrived.
All the Yoginīs belonging to Śaṅkara and all the Gaṇas also arrived there;
Nara, Nārāyaṇa, and other ascetics likewise came to that place.
The forest regions and the very woods arrived as terrestrial globes; the sacred shrines, the seasons, the times, and the years and so forth also arrived. ||22||
The month of Puruṣottama also arrived at the imperishable field (Akṣetra), sounding the great drum—auspicious and the performer of all blessings. (23)
Yogis arrived; sacrifices accompanied by sons of devotion arrived.
There was no end to the celestial chariots, nor likewise to the elephants and birds.
There was no end to the mounts, nor to the bodies of the charioteers, bards,
and panegyrists of many forms who provided entertainment for the mind.
On the night of the seventh day of the month of Ūrja, all embodied beings arrived;
the goddesses and gods offered them a most excellent welcome. (26)
The virtuous attendants, who were dear to Brahmā, also acted as his father, mother, sister, and brothers. ||27||
Likewise, all the disciples, the sages such as Lomaśa and others who are themselves lords, and the virtuous ones such as Lālāyana and others; ||28||
They offered a welcome and provided food and drink;
then all the wish-fulfilling cows gave their milk.
All the female and male servants also performed acts of honor and service there at midnight; indeed, nothing was lacking whatsoever.
Having risen early in the morning, O Lakṣmī, I, Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, performed my ablutions, adorned myself with ornaments, and was accompanied by my beloved wives. ||31||
Nourished by my mother and father, I went quickly to the assembly hall;
at that time, musical instruments were played, as were those of Vāsudeva and the others.
The incarnations and the male lords, as well as all the female goddesses, and the liberated gopīs and gopas, all came to my pavilion. (33)
Having performed my worship while I was seated upon the divine throne,
they all offered the waving of lights (ārātrika) along with unbroken grains of rice, saffron, and moon-shaped offerings.
The brahmins and great sages uttered words of blessing; crores of abodes, crores of lords, and crores of celestial rishis and ancestors likewise sang praises. (35)
His wives likewise honored me with unbroken grains and flowers;
for human beings are all sacred pilgrimage sites, and the Vedas and their auxiliary sciences are the ultimate principles. (36)
The Sarasvatīs, the Śāradās, and all the Lakṣmīs offered me worship and presented me with every kind of divine gift in the assembly hall. (37)
Thus, until midday, my worship was most magnificent;
everything that came there, I gave away as a gift. (38)
Then, meals were indeed given to the honored guests,
an exemption was granted, and auspicious sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇās) were bestowed.
Rewards were given according to their merit,
such as instrumental music, great songs, dancing, and entertainment during the night.
It continued until midnight, and then there was a cessation;
on the ninth day, the great lords of the earth were honored and likewise fed. ||41||
Honored and dispatched, they departed for their own abodes;
thus, on the eighteenth lunar day, the first day of the seventeenth year.
O Kṛṣṇā, I shall celebrate the festival of my birth-day (Janmāṣṭamī) in the month of Kārttika;
and may this fame of yours shine throughout the three worlds. ||43||
Indeed, my wondrous deeds during my sixteenth year have been described by me here in this third lineage of the Dvāpara age. 44.
I am the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Lord; I am the ordainer, the creator, the speaker, and the recorder of these life stories. 45.
Whoever performs the recitation of this third section shall possess manifold prosperity, and his lineage shall become extensive. ||46||
Having placed a golden Garuḍa, one should give the book of the Dvāpara age;
by that, indeed, the gift of the entire earth is given—of this there is no doubt. ||47||
Whatever is offered at the moment of this discourse, even if it be very little,
shall become multiplied infinitely and shall become a bestower of the great heaven.
The gift of a cow, the gift of a garden, the bestowing of gold and jewels, the gift of a daughter, the gift of a house, and the offering of an elephant at a sacrifice. ||49||
The fruit of all his giving arises through this very gift:
the gift of celestial palaces, the gift of cities, and likewise the offering of groves.
Through this gift, the surrender of all one's possessions truly comes to pass;
it is the gift of Brahman, the gift of the Vedas, and the supreme gift of liberation. 51.
Through this gift, the offering of oneself arises;
the ancestors also cross over and become dwellers in the divine abode. ||52||
By means of this gift, the bestowal of sovereignty itself is accomplished for him;
diseases and obstacles perish, and misfortunes diminish. (53)
Misfortunes are destroyed by the gift of the Dvāparakhaṇḍa;
one should have it recited for seven days, or for a fortnight, or even for a month. (54)
One should feed virtuous Brahmins, as well as listeners and speakers, according to one's wealth;
likewise, one should feed virtuous, chaste women who are destitute and the poor in their entirety.
The women should cause the reciter to be paraded through the city in a choice vehicle,
as well as the Brahmins, the kings, the merchants, and the common people.
Likewise, maidens, well-attired, should cause [the deity] to be circumambulated with jars filled with water made from coconut shells, as well as with pearls and *āsīnī* flowers. ||57||
Unmarried women should worship and honor [the deity] with songs, unbroken grains, flowers, and saffron; they should also cause [the image] to be carried in procession through the city.
They should also bestow great gifts upon the high-souled reciter;
indeed, they should give whatever is necessary so that the virtuous one may be well-pleased. ||59||
Through hearing this, one attains enjoyment and liberation, as well as divinity;
there shall be the destruction of latent impressions and the dissolution of all impurities.
The destruction of the threefold suffering and eternal peace shall come to pass for those desiring a son or a daughter by giving this Dvāparakhaṇḍa. (61)
One should perform [this rite] together with a new cloth-wrap and accompanied by gold coins;
by that, one is indeed freed from enemies and no fear of the king arises.
Through this gift given with sincere devotion, he shall be liberated from prison;
moreover, even that which is impossible shall become possible for him through his hearing of this here.
Through hearing about him in many ways, omniscience arises;
he is the beloved noble Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Lord, the Great Master. (64)
May the Lord of Rādhā and Lakṣmī, the Lord of Padmāvatī and Śrīmāṇikī, and the eternal Lord of Prajñāmuktā, shine forth within his own heart through hearing [this teaching]. 65.
At the end of the year, one shall indeed meet Him face-to-face; one should listen to Him constantly.
The Soul of the Universe will meet one in secret, and one will meet Him even in dreams—of this there is no doubt.
In times of adversity, one should protect this *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa-Saṃhitā*, for it is my very image as remembered in the Dvāpara age. (67)
This fragmentary lineage of the Dvāpara age resides within my belly;
by touching, meditating upon, and serving my form, one attains the Imperishable.
Whoever—whether men or women—should have a desire for Me, who am truly worthy, in their hearts, they should listen to this discourse and my mantra should be chanted by them. (69)
Oṃ, salutations to Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Lord; svāhā!
Having arrived, I shall indeed grant you happiness as desired and grant my vision.
By reciting this mantra named after me one hundred thousand times, it shall indeed be perfected;
a fire-offering (homa) consisting of one-tenth that number must be performed, and the inner visualization (bhāvanā) should be maintained within.
Adorned with the Kaustubha gem and a crown, decorated with all ornaments, with a gracious countenance, the beloved of Lakṣmī, he is as beautiful as Kandarpa. ||72||
There is no object in the three worlds that I do not give away;
there is nothing in the three realms that I do not bestow upon my devotee.
I grant to the reciter of the mantra the lion-throne, as well as the lap, the abode, the imperishable, and my own seat; indeed, I bestow all my sovereign powers upon him. (74)
O Lakṣmī, this is my heart, my compassion, and my grace;
I shall indeed grant everything as desired to one who recites the mantra of identity with Me. 75.
The wish-fulfilling trees, the cows that grant all desires, the creepers known as kalpavallīs, the kalpa-pillars, as well as the cintāmaṇi jewels and the inexhaustible vessels; ||76||
The lotus-mark, wonders, and all manner of supernatural powers arise in the heart of one who recites the mantra through identification with it. (77)
He who hears the lineage of Dvāpara recites my mantra;
for him there is eternal merit and perpetual accomplishment of the kalpa.
Indeed, by the accomplishment of the mantra through my will, his movement becomes unimpeded and his vision becomes unobstructed; of this there is no doubt. (79)
By merely hearing [this], one may attain the state of a deity, the state of a sage, the state of a perfected being (siddha), sovereignty, or even the status of an incarnation during the Dvāpara age.
By hearing [the name] of Dvāpara, one may attain the state of the earth, the state of auspiciousness, the golden state, or the abode of the Great Puruṣa. ||81||
One should listen while fixing the mind firmly on Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa;
one should listen with great festivity, and it shall bestow the four goals of human life. ||82||
One should constantly give fruits, grains, garments, and ornaments, as well as articles of daily necessity, and one should listen to the sacred narrative.
Having abandoned fear of revilers, likewise fear of atheists, and having abandoned fear of adversaries, one should indeed listen while taking refuge in me. 84.
Where I am, there is victory; where I am, there are festivals. Where I am, there is protection; for where I am absent, there is indeed fear. (85)
Having heard this again and again, may your intellects become perceivers of the aesthetic essence, for they are within the range of my own being, that of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. 86.
I, Kṛṣṇa, shall be the deliverer from the ocean of worldly existence for those men and women who, with concentrated minds, listen to even a single chapter or a single verse. (87)
Even those who are sinful, low-born, or performers of base deeds, and even those who are devoid of proper conduct, are purified in every way through association with the virtuous. (88)
Likewise, by hearing this, the wicked are purified; of this there is no doubt.
Indeed, through my yoga, all who hear it become free from the qualities (nirguṇa). 89.
In this regard, those who have assumed human form are considered liberated souls (muktas), and their consorts are considered liberated women (muktānikās).
However, my abode, which is the imperishable seat of the narrative, should be understood as non-illusory. || 3.236.90 ||
There is a speaker who possesses my form; I speak it, of this there is no doubt.
O Lakṣmī, in every verse here, I have showered down my grace. 91.
Even if they approach Hari, their beloved, with devotion only slightly,
I approach them every day with a hundredfold joy.
If, after performing all sacrifices, one encounters any misfortune,
one should remember me and repeatedly recite the mantra of my identity.
All calamities are destroyed; this is the promise proclaimed by me for one who merely hears this fragment of the lineage of the Dvāpara age. (94)
Or one might perform [other rites], yet the destruction of calamities would come from forming this resolve alone: on one side are all other discourses, and on the other side is my mantra. 95.
O Lakṣmī, Manu is distinguished; how much more so one who is engaged in his narration!
May there be welfare for you all through even a drop of the compassion of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. (96)
May the teacher Kambharāputra be auspicious; may Gopālanandana be well, he who is endowed with contentment, younger brothers, gentleness, glory, wisdom, and omniscience. (97)
May Hari—the omniscient, the all-knowing, the inner self of all, and the cause of all—beginning with Śvetavyāsa and ending with Vyāseśvara, grant you prosperity. (98)
The refuge of all phenomena, the abode of all, possessing the color of all objects;
may he who is enriched by all strata, the sovereign of all mines, and the foremost one, grant you prosperity. (99)
By whose very presence Saurāṣṭra indeed attains its status as Saurāṣṭra— he,
who is both manifest and unmanifest, may he grant you eternal well-being.
May Brahmeshvara, the Lord of the God of Gods, who resides in the field of Aksharakunkumavapi and is attended by Lomasha, always grant you prosperity and well-being. 101.

Thus ends the two hundred and thirty-sixth chapter, titled "The Description of the Celebration of the Seventeenth Birthday Anniversary of the Beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa and the Greatness of Hearing the Narratives of the Dvāpara Age, Giving Gifts, and Chanting Mantras," in the Third Section on the Lineage of Dvāpara within the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
The illustrious Śrī Nārāyaṇī-Śrī said: "O beloved of my heart, O life-breath, O ocean of bliss,
O merciful Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, I have been purified by you."
Indeed, by listening to the divine and glorious sacred narratives of your honor, all these beloved wives of Brahmā as well as the other beloved wives of Hari [have been purified]. || 2 ||
By hearing Your story, all the gopīs have attained the state of supreme purification; they are all liberated souls, embodiments of Ramā, Lakṣmī, Śrī, and the Goddess of Fortune.
The female lords, the perfected ones, the goddesses, and even those of human descent— those born of Kaśyapa and those dwelling in the depths— all became fulfilled in their purpose for Hari.
Oh, what fortune! Oh, what fortune for the Daityas, Dānavas, and Rākṣasas, that we here possess daughters whose very essence is the beloved Kṛṣṇa!
Oh, how great is the compassion and the grace of the glorious Supreme Soul!
The wives are the listeners, the husband is the speaker, and he himself is the illustrious Puruṣottama.
O Lord, for those whose fortunes have been severed or shattered,
there is indeed no moment for hearing the stories of Kṛṣṇa’s lotus-like face.
Many noble women and men shall hear the nectar of his story;
therefore, provide a concise summary of the narrative for those of limited intellect.
Puruṣottama said:
O Narāyaṇī, for the sake of those whose faith is acquired only for a brief moment, I shall relate the seeds of the stories of this section; listen attentively.
This section consists of two hundred and thirty-six chapters, and it contains twenty-five thousand verses in addition [to those already mentioned]. 3.237.10.
O Rame, there are twenty-six chapters for the Satya, Tretā, and Dvāpara ages;
likewise, O Ramā, they number one hundred thousand, bestowing liberation.
The verses of the three sections amount to one hundred thousand and twelve thousand one hundred, which bestow enjoyment and liberation. (12)
This enumeration is to be understood here in the world of humans, and not by others;
this extensive compendium was already explained to you previously.
Here, at the beginning of the Dvāpara cycle, Śrī performed a hymn of praise;
thereafter, the calculation of the time of creation was declared by Brahmā.
Then, for the purpose of destroying the asura Rohiṇa, the glorious Nārāyaṇa Hari appeared in the form of Dyumārāyaṇa; these periods, known as kalpas, are said to consist of fifty-two years.
Merudhara was proclaimed as Merunārāyaṇa, and thereafter Raveḥśātanakṛt was described as Viṣṇunārāyaṇa. ||16||
For the sake of destroying the demon Dhūmra, the Lord Devanārāyaṇa is celebrated as Yajñanārāyaṇa, the initiator of the sacrifice. ||17||
Then Rudra was instructed by Brahmā and Nārāyaṇa;
thereafter, for the purpose of regulating the abodes of the gods, Āditya and Nārāyaṇa were appointed. ||18||
The Teacher of the Nagas, Śrī Garuḍa, and Nārāyaṇa are described; thereafter, Ārṣa-Nārāyaṇa, who bestows stability and firmness, is also praised. || 19 ||
Then there was the venerable Prājñanārāyaṇa, the preceptor of Thurānanda;
he is described as the virtuous Naiṣṭhika Vīranārāyaṇa.
Then the bestower of liberation, Bhadranārāyaṇa, was also described,
as well as the marriage festival of Lakṣmī, the daughter of Tuṅgabhadrāsana.
The primordial incarnation of Śrī Harinārāyaṇa has been described;
after that follows Bījanārāyaṇa, the protector of the seed.
Born in the house of Dharmavrata as Hari, the excellent Nārāyaṇa, he was born from the curse of Sudarśanī as one who possesses the forms of all women. (23)
He who grants liberation from the curse is celebrated as Strīpuṃnārāyaṇa;
thereafter, for the sake of destroying the Mākara demon, he is known as Jalanārāyaṇa.
Then Śīlanārāyaṇa appeared for the sake of establishing the dharma of the virtuous,
and then Vārdhinārāyaṇa appeared for the sake of destroying the demon Vyāghra.
Then Kṛṣṇa, who possesses four faces and is like the Creator himself, became Śrī Puruṣottama in the house of Rādhanikā, who was a mass of merit. ||26||
And after that, this story was told by me to Rame;
Tīrthanārāyaṇa, who sanctifies the sacred fords (tīrthas), has been proclaimed. 27.
Then Jīvan-Nārāyaṇa was described as the promoter of devotion;
thereafter, O Rame, Ardha-Śrīśvara-Nārāyaṇa was extolled.
Then there was Ardhapitṛnārāyaṇa and Plakṣanarāyaṇa;
thereafter, in the Naramedha sacrifice, he was proclaimed as Puṃstvanārāyaṇa.
Then Śyāmanārāyaṇa was addressed by Vaṭaśrī along with Rājanārāyaṇa for the purpose of destroying the demon Māyūra.
After Kāmabhasmottara came Brahmacārinārāyaṇa;
then Śambhujīvaka was proclaimed, and after that Śivanārāyaṇa. ||31||
Kubera, Ujjīvaka, and Svarṇanārāyaṇa have been described;
thereafter is Svāminārāyaṇa, the performer of the burning away of the flames of affliction.
Then, in the house of Nirvāṇika, Śrīsāvananārāyaṇa and Sādhunārāyaṇa were born together with the virtuous Lakṣmī.
He was the restorer of the illustrious Manoruja, a devotee of Nārāyaṇa,
who once again became a horse to serve as armor for the protection of King Varma-dhara.
The Lord Medhanārāyaṇa arose together with Medhālakṣmī;
thereafter, Vahninārāyaṇa appeared for the sake of preventing destruction by fire.
Then Rasanārāyaṇa was proclaimed for the purpose of destroying Ilodara;
thereafter, Daityahā Śrīcakranārāyaṇa was described.
Then there is Satyanārāyaṇa, the establisher of truth and dharma;
then Hiraṇyanārāyaṇa, for the sake of stabilizing the mountains.
Then Nairañjaninārāyaṇa, together with Naiṣkiñcanīśrī, [became] Śāpanārāyaṇa for the sake of pacifying the curse of Puṇyavatī. || 38 ||
May Brahman-Nārāyaṇa be for the fulfillment of the minds of the Apsarases;
may Guru-Nārāyaṇa be for the illumination of the knowledge of Brahman. ||39||
Then the Lord Ācārya-Nārāyaṇa, together with the glory of his wife Ācāryāṇī, bestowed the auspicious initiation upon King Bṛhaddharma.
Then Vidyunnārāyaṇa appeared for the sake of destroying Vidyutsrāva and others;
then Madhunārāyaṇa appeared for the sake of destroying Madhubhakṣa and others. ||41||
The slayer of the Daityas, Śrīnātha Nārāyaṇa, was also extolled there,
together with Vibhvī and Śrī, as the Lord of Men, Nārāyaṇa, during the golden festival.
Then there is Mokṣanārāyaṇa, accompanied by Muktiśrī;
and then Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, joined with Śivarājīśrī. ||43||
The Lord, beloved of ten million billion lotuses, has been extolled;
[the hymn] consists of twelve thousand and five hundred verses on the pair Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa. 44.
The Dvandvanāmastava has been declared, which destroys all sins;
and [therein] is the manifestation of the Supreme Brahman in the form of Nara and Nārāyaṇa. 45.
Then follows a description of the duties of household women who are obedient;
likewise, the virtuous conduct of young wives and the bulls that are to be protected by the wives. (46)

The power of truthfulness and reality has been taught, as well as the yoga of devotion that is beyond the qualities (nirguṇa), and also the yoga of the Supreme Person (puruṣottama) regarding the Supreme Brahman. ||47||
The identity with that which transcends the syllables, the Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa vow, the greatness of the Guru, and thereafter the liberation of the divine goddess. 48.
The story of King Subāhu regarding the gift of food and water;
the story of Nahuṣa; and indeed the story of the parrot Kuñjala. ||49||
The story of Kāmodā was told, and then the story of Cyavana;
followed by the teacher’s disclosure of the secret doctrine and a description of right conduct and other virtues.
Through the application of the *ṛṣi-dharma-ṛṣi* method, the supreme state of being beloved by Brahmā was attained;
such is the narrative concerning Līlāvatī, Suśīlā, and her other female companions. (51)
Then follows the narration of the liberation of the Rākṣasa and the horse; thereafter, the Guru’s manifestation in the form of Hari and the hymn of total self-surrender (sarvārpaṇa-stava). ||52||
Then follows the illustration of Kauśika and others regarding the state of being the best of Vaiṣṇavas, and thereafter the instruction on singing by Nārada is told. (53)
Thereafter, the attainment of the state of Garuḍa by Ulūka is described;
following that, the marks of a great devotee of the Lord are indeed set forth. 544.
Thereafter, the examination by Queen Citrāmbārā was described, and then the protection performed for the queen by the goddess Gadā was narrated. 55.
The superior power of the sciences, mantras, and gurus has been declared;
then follow unobstructed service, the vow, and the *damanaka* [rite]. (56)
On the day of the lunar change (Bhinnatithi), the worship of Hari in His divided form is proclaimed;
it is the narration of the majesty of devotion, the secret of the devotee’s love for the Divine Spouse. 57.
Thereafter, the entire essence of Hari’s grace is described;
then follow the great secrets of the mantras along with their meaningful nyāsas.

The Gāyatrī, the vertical mark (ūrdhvapuṇḍra) and so forth, as well as the knowledge of the hidden meaning; the manifestation of the three quarters and the divinity of the single quarter—these are the desired goals. 59.
Then the power of Yayāti through devotion to the Name was described,
followed by a description of the means for attaining the grace of Hari.
The story of the miser, the fruit of division, association with the virtuous, the means for attaining the state of being most established in Brahman, and likewise the stories of chaste wives. 61.
Then follows the wonderful narrative of the cowherd woman Sucandrikā, and thereafter the story of Manu’s wife, Brahmaprathā, is told.
The means for attaining long life was taught as the liberation of a hundred vultures;
thereafter, the renunciation of a hundred sons by Vinodinī was proclaimed.
In the context of Vātsyāyana’s work, the liberation of courtesans has been discussed;
the causes for their virtuous conduct have been stated, and the means to their liberation have been proclaimed. (64)
The practice of Vṛṣāyana was described by Caraka; that which arose from Śyena was proclaimed; and the fruit of serving the virtuous for Citraketu and Mālatī has been declared. ||65||
The virtuous are declared superior to the Brahmins by the vision of Viṣṇu;
likewise, the example of Durgā has been cited, and those who share in her dharma have been described.
The hells have been described through the illustration of the farmer;
likewise, those going to heaven have been mentioned, as well as the executioners.
The virtuous are said to be a moving sacred ford that purifies all,
even one who is sonless, emaciated, and born of a Śūdra mother.
Through austerities and by a boon from Indra, he attained the state of being most devoted to Brahman and the nature of fire;
there are many such examples regarding the cycles of rebirth for living beings.
There is also the example of King Bhaṅgāsvana attaining womanhood, and the example of the yogi Viṣula through the power of Brahman-yoga. (3.237.70)
The destruction of the demon Lomaka-pardaka, the increase of Indra’s splendor and virility, his defeat by Indra, and the propitiation of his preceptor are described. (71)
Then follows the raising of the Gokarṇa Tīrtha submerged in the ocean;
thereafter, the story of Kuvalāśva and the narrative of Triśaṅku are told.
The discourse on Brahman was proclaimed by Praṇat; likewise, the story of Kaśyapa was told.
The means for attaining liberation are the strength found in the company of the virtuous. //73//
Through his association with the virtuous Ālambāyana, there was the liberation of a hundred thousand [prisoners],
as well as the release of the vulture, the outcaste, and the Śabara.
Therefore, Lakṣmīnivāsa and Śrīvāsa are said to have arisen;
likewise, the curse of Bhṛgu during the incarnation is declared to have been caused by his own will.
The gift of a cow (godāna) and the vow of propitiating the cows have been described,
as well as the rescue of the bhāruṇḍa birds, which is a cause for the liberation of the deceased.
And there is the illustration of Vṛṣādarbhi as a recipient of Sūrya’s gift, [given] by the virtuous Śrī Cakrabhāsa to Naraśaya, the thief. (77)
Liberation was granted to the wealthy, and they were awakened by the Brahma-sacrifice;
a wife was wedded, and the root of all dharma was demonstrated. (78)
In this regard, the illustration of Jāṅgalāmakhani has been described;
likewise, there are various sons, daughters, husbands, and wives. (79)
Then follows the liberation of Śambhalavārasūta, who was devoted to the virtuous, as well as the testing of Kalyāṇabhakta’s service.
The manifestation of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa upon the earth has been proclaimed; the Thousand Names of Śrī Puruṣottama have been described in the Sāman hymns. 8.1.
The fruit of the Puruṣottama-sāman is the attainment of the Imperishable (akṣara);
likewise, there is the fruit arising from the gift of land and so forth, as well as the fruit born from the gift of food and other such gifts.
Then, for the two—the theist Dīrgha and the atheist Śīlabhidha—liberation was declared through instruction by means of self-restraint (yama). 83.
The Brahmasatyā, however, is the illustration of a yoginī’s gift of her body;
she was reborn as Devarāta in the wife of King Vaivarta. (84)
Then the liberation of Romapāda Paśupa was told, as well as the protection of the thief named Nagnabhaṅga through association with the virtuous. 85.
Furthermore, Bhāgavatāyana’s skillful restoration was such that it produced a marvel, like the regrowth of a forest consumed by a forest fire. (86)
In the destruction of the demon Bhaṇḍāsura, who arose from the ashes of Kāmadeva,
there was also the battle of the armies of Lalitā, Śrī, and Mahālakṣmī.
Then follows the destruction of the demon Bhaṇḍāsura, the Lalitāśrīstava, the distribution of rewards, and the sixteen temples. (88)
The worship of Mahālakṣmī in Kāñcīpurī is said to be twofold in its manifestation: by means of female attendants residing in a wish-fulfilling gem palace, and [the deity herself]. (89)
The procedure for initiation and the dwelling of the three deities have likewise been declared;
[next are] the one hundred and thirty-five names of Lalitāśrī.
The gift that bestows the attainment of a son and the vow have been proclaimed;
thereafter, the vow of service to the virtuous is declared to be the supreme vow. (91)

The gift of the person on the scale (tulāpuruṣadāna), the gift of the golden womb (hiraṇyagarbhadāna), the gift of the cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍadāna), and the gift of the wish-fulfilling tree (kalpavṛkṣadāna) have been proclaimed. ||92||
The great gift of a thousand cows, the offering of a golden wish-fulfilling cow, the great gift of a golden horse, and the gift of a golden chariot. (93)
The gift of a golden elephant-chariot, the gift of five ploughs, the great gift of the golden earth, and the offering of the Viśvasudarśana [chariot]. ||94||
The gift of a garland and a wheel is proclaimed as the gift of ornaments;
the gift of a great wish-fulfilling creeper is the gift of a beloved of the gods. //95//
The gift of the end of the eon, the giving of teachers, deities, and so forth, the offering of a temple, and likewise the gift of the seven oceans; ||96||

The gift of the great elements and the gift of prosperity are proclaimed; as are the pacification of the planets, their worship, and so forth, as well as the recitation of mantras ten million times and more. (97)
The example regarding the Vaiśya Lohāṅgāra for the pacification of planetary afflictions is given;
thereafter, two hundred names of Mahālakṣmī are indeed recited. (98)
Likewise, there is an image of Mahālakṣmī and her maṇḍala; through the recitation of the names and praises, the daughters of the Pitṛs obtain their own desired fruits. (99)
The Lakṣmī-Saubhāgya-Śayana-vrata has been declared,
as well as the Ghaṭa-Lakṣmī-vrata and the Sarva-Maṅgala-vrata.
The Sāṃkhyayoga-vrata, the Rasakalyāṇa-lalitā-vrata, and the Ārdrānanda-ramā-nārāyaṇa-vrata are proclaimed. || 101 ||
The Śāradeya-vrata has been described, as well as the Kalyāṇī-kamalā-vrata;
likewise, the Viśoka-lalitā-dvādaśī-vrata has been proclaimed.
The vow consisting of the fondling of Kṛṣṇa by means of playful displays of opulence has been described,
along with the illustration of King Puṣkaravāhana.
The exposition of the sixty-one vows has also been proclaimed;
and the sacred ford (tīrtha) consisting of Kuṅkumavāpikā brings liberation to sinners.

For the sake of pacifying the power of untimely death, the performance of mantra-recitation, worship, and so forth has been taught; for the humans of the Dvāpara age, the practice of dharma, ritual action, and so forth has been demonstrated.

The differentiation of the duties of the ages (yuga-dharma) and so forth, the rite for pacifying portents (utpāta-śāntika-karman), the rite for pacifying bad dreams (duḥsvapna-śāntika-karman), and likewise the sacrifice to the planets (graha-yajña) have been proclaimed. ||106||
Auspicious dreams and omens, rites for pacification in the face of inauspiciousness, the mantra of Hanumān, and the description of consecrations and other such matters have been described.
Likewise, the means for the destruction of great sins and other evils have been proclaimed;
and after that follows the description of the lineages of dharma and adharma.
The dwelling place of Duḥsaha and so forth, the calamities of his lineage and so forth,
and the discernment between what should and should not be done regarding the lunar mansions and other matters have been proclaimed.
Sarojinī and Kumbhakartṛ attained fourfold widowhood; yet, through service to Satīśvarī, they also attained the state of Padminī and the state of Ramā.
Then follow the descendants of the fourteen Manus and, after that,
the narrative of the Prajāpati Ruci is also proclaimed.
Furthermore, the sporting of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, accompanied by Brahmapriyā and others, on the Himālayas has also been described. || 11.2 ||
The origin of excellent gems such as diamonds and others from the Rākṣasa Bala; and then, due to the curse of Bala’s attendant, his subsequent fall [from heaven]. (11.3)
The nature of the Daitya and the origin of gems from his body have been proclaimed; furthermore, the qualities and other characteristics of all types of jewels have been described.
The fourteen incarnations of Hari among human beings, the procedure for the *jīva-śrāddha*, and the cessation of worldly existence. 1.15.
Then follows the dispelling [of obstacles], the hymn of praise, the giving away of a maiden and other gifts in the sacrifice,
the destruction of the causes of death, and the demonstration of the path to higher existence.
And the investigation by the illustrious Asacidānandayogin is also presented;
in the *Muktidharma*, the causes for the attainment and dissolution of the body have been declared. (1.17)
The cause of that which is called Māyā, as well as the attainment of the supreme abode;
the inquiry and the answer regarding the state of actionlessness (naiṣkarmya) for the wife of Sadvidyāyana. 118.

The experience of the auspicious and inauspicious and so forth, as well as consciousness, have been proclaimed; likewise, the discernment of liberation and dharma, and the analysis of the internal self and other categories. || 11.9 ||
The state of being devoid of qualities (nirguṇātmatā) while in the householder stage of the great seer Bhikṣāyana is described;
likewise, the liberation of his son, who was eternally dependent [on him], through devotion is proclaimed. (3.237.1–20)
The destruction of leprosy for the leper named Vyāghra has been proclaimed; and the liberation of Uttama, the village priest, has been described. (121)
The destruction of tuberculosis for Virāla, as well as his liberation;
and the restoration of sight to Andha, the son of Pṛthūdharas. 1.22.
The health of the Śūdra Sāgara despite his broken feet, the restoration of the severed state of Vṛkṇadeva, and the liberation of Bhāva—[these were the wonders]. (1.23)
Then follows the story of the liberation from the curse of the Pāśupata Śiva-brahmin;
Bāṇāṅgaṇa, a seller of liquor, was liberated through the company of the virtuous.
The leather-worker Mṛtādana, who served a cow, attained liberation;
even Śaṅkudhara attained liberation through the yoga of Sumantukarṣi.
The community of Mahāsaurāṣṭra was protected from bandits;
the merchant Dhaniṣṭhaka was liberated from sexual misconduct. (126)
The liberation of the Rākṣasa through devotion by the king who was a slayer of a Brāhmaṇa;
and the liberation from the sin of killing a woman by Devaviśrāma through the Kāṇḍikā weapon. 1.27.
The resurrection of the deceased Harṣula, the son of Bhakta, was performed;
the leprosy of Śāṇadhara was destroyed, and he was protected. (1.28)
The prevention of the sin of killing a bull by the devotee named Nimbadeva, as well as the sovereignty and devotion to Brahman of the Ekāntikas, are narrated. 1.29.
The liberation of Kālīndara’s vessel through devotion has been declared;
while Rāyaṇadeva was in the womb, he became a knower of dance and accumulated a store of knowledge.
And liberation was likewise proclaimed through the instruction of Bodhāyana for Puṇḍravarman, the king who was learned in the *vrata*, the directions, and the *gāyana*. (131)
The attainment of the state of Viṣṇu for the progeny and their subsequent liberation have been proclaimed; likewise, the liberation of the cotton-carder and the weaver has been described. || 1.32 ||
The release of the wood-carriers, headed by Jaṅgala and Deva;
and the virtuous conduct of Bhakta, steadfast in his affection, together with his wife. 13.3.
Liberation is proclaimed for the forest-guardian Tilaka-raṅga; there is neither devotion to Añja nor protection for the devotee of Mahāmaya.
The protection of farmers from plunderers was proclaimed;
and an inexhaustible granary was established for the Kirāta named Sāgara. (1.35)
The protection of the queen was performed for Sāraṅga, who was devoted to the Hūṇas;
and furthermore, liberation was attained by Yajñarādhapuṣkasa.
Then, the liberation of the outcaste named Kapikṣaya was told, and the release of the Nālīka, the blacksmith, and his family was described. || 1.37 ||
The protection against poison by Maṅgaladeva, the leather-worker, was proclaimed;
thereafter, the liberation of Haridāsa, the chariot-maker, was described.
Protection was afforded to Śilāhṛd, Dāmaśilā, and the Bhṛtyas;
likewise, the artisan Sañjayadeva was protected from the elephant. || 139 ||
Then the liberation of the painter Saṃbhara-deva was narrated,
followed by the liberation of the masters of the pearl-oyster, the stone, the charcoal, and the mine.
The destruction of the sins and other evils of the hunter named Cakradhara, and the liberation of the treacherous Khaśa, the keeper of the enclosure. || 141 ||
The liberation of the daughter of Queen Dvaipī from the punishment of King Siṃhabhūpa, and the release of Śivajaya, the builder of the temple. (142)
Then follows the sight of Kṛṣṇa as he cuts through the net of Aṅgāraka,
and subsequently the liberation of Udyamabha, Śrībha, Vāṭa, and the others.
By means of skillful application, Dīrgharava was liberated from the camel-herders;
likewise, by means of skillful application, the liberation of Ratnaprabha is also declared. (144)
The liberation of Gadārdaneśa Vaidya and Mukundī, as well as the release of Deśyāvana and Kīśasvāmin. || 145 ||
Hari assumed the form of another, a courtesan’s son, and thus performed service for the queen of King Svarṇadhanvan. (146)
Furthermore, their liberation was proclaimed thereafter;
in a previous birth, Hari [rescued] the daughter of a cowherd from a Daitya. (147)
He performed the protection and liberation of Ruṭāṇakya,
as well as the torments of Yama for Matsya, Māra, Dhīra, Parva, and others.
Then the liberation of Naupatija is told;
after that, the liberation of Śūlīpradatārakādarśaka. || 149 ||
The liberation of Aṅgāraka, known as Jvālāprasāda;
and the liberation of Garada, the chief of those who administer poison. || 3.237.150 ||
Then, the liberation of the one who wields the weapon known as Vikhaṇḍala was described;
likewise, the liberation of Jīrṇodbhava, who had been turned into a ploughman, through the proper application of yoga. 151.
For me, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Jayantī festival is celebrated on the seventeenth day from my birth. (152)
The greatness of listening to this section concerning the transition to the Dvāpara age, as well as the greatness of giving gifts and the recitation of mantras, has been declared. || 153 ||
Then, the essence of the narratives concerning the Dvāpara age was proclaimed:
"O Lakṣmī, Rādhā, Ramā, Kṛṣṇa, Padmāvatī, and Māṇikī! (154)
O Nārāyaṇī, O beloved of Brahmā, O Kamalā, O Amṛtā, O Ramā—may all you beloveds of Hari hear my soul as it is proclaimed by me. (155)
All discourses have me as their essence; you all are established within them.
The virtuous men are consciousness and the women are consciousness; I am the bliss even of those two.
And these three collections of narratives, whose nature is truth, consciousness, and bliss—
those who are Brahman, the virtuous, the followers of Brahmā, and those to be attained through meditation— are indeed you yourselves.
"O Ānanda, I am the Supreme Lord of those two principles;
these existing selves are indeed my power of consciousness (cicchakti) and my primordial nature (prakṛti). (158)
The primordial Māyā is the divine Rādhā, and I am that very bliss;
all the saints are my incarnations, and their wives are mine.
Of those two, I am Puruṣottama, the source of bliss and the auspicious one;
I am the existent, the truth, the entire cause, as well as consciousness and the object of consciousness, the effect. || 3.237.160 ||
I, the Lord of all, the Supreme Lord, am the giver of bliss to those two;
while existing as their distinct form, I also become the underlying continuity of consciousness.
And between those two dwells Ānandī, possessing the form of Śrī Kṛṣṇa; he is I myself, straightforward in all things, and though difficult to attain, I am present by the power of grace.
In all creations, throughout all the cosmic eggs (brahmāṇḍas), I myself become the object of experience for those devoted to me, assuming countless forms.
Neither for forms, nor for their own natures, nor for their effects, does there exist in any way an end, a number, or a measure, nor is there ever any [such thing] as "it exists. (164)
There is never any counting of my devotees, nor of their deeds, nor even any reckoning of my stories within the cosmic eggs (brahmāṇḍas). 165.
Whatever nectars there are, whatever elixirs,
and whatever ambrosias exist within this entire realm— all these are desired by everyone.
O Rame, all the various forms of love and affection directed toward devotees,
as well as all the divine favors of Hari, have been set forth here in this section.
All means of accomplishment, all reasons without exception, and all causes that bear fruit—indeed, their purposefulness resides here [in this very state]. 1.68.
Whatever fruits there are of efforts, whatever fruits there are of births,
and whatever fruits there are of devotion— all those have here borne fruit in every way.
That very purity which belongs to the liberated, that purity which belongs to the yogins, and that purity which belongs to his own devotees, belongs likewise to those who serve him. (3.237.170)
O Lakṣmī, just as Kṛṣṇa’s intensity is directed toward the destruction of the sins of the wicked,
so too is the intensity of the lineage of Dvāpara.
Devotees indeed cross over by devotion, the affectionate by affection for Mādhava;
sinners cross over by yoga, and [all] by compassion and service to the virtuous. || 172 ||
The wicked Asuras and Daityas, however, through direct contact with Śrī Kṛṣṇa, and then all of them through hearing the lineage of Dvāpara, [attained liberation]. 173.
Whatever accomplishments exist among the gods, the Daityas, the mantras, and the perfected yogis, they belong to this listener, speaker, and rejoicer.
The celestial chariots of liberation, the mounts such as elephants, the perfected goddesses, and the guides—all these come to resort to him. (175)
By merely hearing this, one obtains all the fruits of the Dharma of the Kṛta age, as well as the fruits of the Dharma of the Tretā and all the fruits of the Dharma of the Dvāpara age. (176)
By hearing of him, men indeed attain the state of Nārāyaṇa, women the state of Nārāyaṇī, and both attain his very form, ornaments, and so forth. (177)
The grace of Hari, the grace of the saintly, and the grace of Lakṣmī—these are firmly established in the embodied soul who takes refuge in the lineage of Dvāpara. (178)
Indeed, for this listener, all supreme merits, as well as all higher abodes, become masses of ever-increasing bliss.
That which is difficult to attain, difficult to traverse, and difficult to abide in— even that which is hopeless—
becomes indeed easy to attain, easy to traverse, secure, and full of hope through the hearing of this [teaching].
Salutations to the primordial Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the one who descends in incarnations; salutations to Him whose body consists of both consciousness and matter, the inner controller of all. 181.
Thus, by means of even a single verse, an embodied being— whether unwilling or even at the point of death— shall obtain the fruit born from the Dvāpara-khaṇḍa.
Or even he who does not have a single moment for hearing [the teaching] in the forest—he too is liberated by mere remembrance; how much more so, then, by hearing it? (183)
Thus, O Lakṣmī, I have described to you in every way the supreme greatness of the lineage of Dvāpara, which is indeed superior to all others.
Then a white man appeared, four-faced and four-armed;
having four feet, he bowed with a serene countenance to Puruṣottama.
He said, "I am the Satya-yuga; I have been made worthy of liberation by you.
Through the application of this progeny, people shall attain liberation. (186)
Then he who had drunk the male essence arrived— having three necks, three arms,
and three feet— and laughing, he bowed down to Śrī Puruṣottama.
I declared: "I am the Yuga and the Tretā; I have been made worthy of liberation by you.
Through the connection with the lineage of the Tretā, embodied beings shall attain liberation. (188)
Then there came a man with two feet, two arms, and two faces;
red in color and overflowing with joy, he did not bow to Śrī Puruṣottama.
Accompanied by a loud laugh, he said: "I am Dvāpara;
by you, who are a descendant of Dvāpara, I have been made a bestower of liberation."
"Embodied beings shall indeed attain liberation through my lineage.
Then, O Lakṣmī, a weak man arrived from there, appearing as if dejected. (191)
With a heart that did not blossom and devoid of happiness and joy,
he was dark-complexioned and sorrowful, like another man who was utterly wretched.
Suddenly shedding tears, he repeatedly prostrated himself like a staff,
like a sinful soul who is impure and has been banished by people.
Making himself known, he said: "I am a sinful man, born in the Kali age;
indeed, there is no place for me among the gods, nor likewise among the great sages."
"O Blessed One, as long as there are perfected beings and virtuous women, I shall never have a place here;
I am miserable in this creation of yours, so please deliver me. (195)
Just as the three brothers attained liberation through yoga, so too may embodied beings attain liberation through my yoga. 196.
O Mādhava, may you grant me a welcome among the gods and others through your compassion,
so that I, though a sinner, may become virtuous here by association with you.
"I am he; I bow here to my compassionate Lord. Thus addressed, I, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, overcome with grace, spoke: 198.
Having composed the Tiṣyasaṃtānaka-khaṇḍa for you as well, I shall make you equal to my three brothers; be joyful!
O Lakṣmī, having heard this and bowed down, the four brothers departed together;
therefore, from this point forward, there shall be a lineage of the Tiṣya age.
He who is the glorious Supreme Brahman, the Great Being beyond all, the Puruṣa who is saluted in the heart by all the incarnations, the great liberated ones, the lords, and all living beings;
And may that Puruṣottama protect you from the outside as well. 20.1.
He who is Bālakṛṣṇa, the son of Kambharā on earth, the beloved of all the sons of Gopālakṛṣṇa,
and the one who assumes incarnations for the sake of sustaining the creation and all else of the universal self;
May he who descends in all [forms] protect us constantly. ||202||
Twenty-five thousand, one hundred and sixty-two verses were composed by Śveta in the lineage of the Dvāpara age. (203)

Thus ends the two hundred and thirty-seventh chapter, titled "The Description of the Subject Matter of the Dvāpara Lineage, the Greatness of the Specific Dvāpara Lineage, the Direct Revelation of the Successions of the Four Yugas, the Prayer for the Eligibility for Liberation during the Kali Age, the Introduction to the Ātiṣya Lineage, and the Benediction," in the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, within the third section, the Dvāpara Cycle.
Thus ends the third section, the Dvāpara-santāna-khaṇḍa, of the glorious Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa-Saṃhitā.
Oṃ. May this be offered as an oblation unto the Blessed Lord, the Supreme Person.
The venerable Vyāsa Śvetāyana said: Oṃ, salutations to the one whose form is the Yuga; salutations to the liberator at the beginning of the Kali age (Tiṣya);
salutations to you, the Lord of the young Yoginīs; salutations to you, the youthful Yogin.
Salutations to the one of countless deeds, and salutations to the ocean of bliss!
Salutations to you, Bālakṛṣṇa; salutations to the inner self within the child. || 2 ||
Salutations again and again to the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa, whose body consists of both consciousness and matter;
salutations to the Lord of Badarikā, who is the very self of Nara and Nārāyaṇa. || 3 ||
Salutations to you, the bestower of all happiness, the sovereign of all dharmas, who dwells in your divine play, and who possesses the form of the virtuous.

Salutations to Him who is perfectly blended with the power of the virtuous one (Sādhvī-Śakti), who wears the matted locks of Svarṇarekhā, whose essential nature is of a single flavor, and who is the consort of the lotus-born goddess (Sarojanī). || 5 ||
In one way, ten ways, a thousand ways, and in ways numbering ten million, a billion, and a hundred billion;
you abide both united with your beloved and also separate from her—homage to you!
He who, for the sake of Rādhā, assumed his own form as Kṛṣṇa;
and he who, for the sake of Śrī, is Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of Nārāyaṇa.
And he who assumed the beautiful Vāsudeva array for the sake of creation,
and who also assumed the golden form, the form of Viṣṇu.
Likewise, for the sake of uplifting those afflicted by Tiṣya, the Blessed One assumed the body of an ascetic consisting of Nara and Nārāyaṇa through his own dharma.
I bow to that Supreme Lord, who is entirely filled with compassion, endowed with virtuous conduct, served by liberated sages, and peaceful. 4.1.10.
Beholding the form of her beloved, the wielder of the discus, as Nara-Nārāyaṇa,
she who was Māṇikyā became an ascetic woman, possessing the beauty of the Imperishable and disciplined in yoga.
She who is divine, possessed of divine power, and devoted to celibacy cannot endure even the slightest touch from anyone other than the illustrious Lord Hari.
She became Badarikā to serve her beloved ascetic;
she is Badrīśvarī, Māṇikī, Suprajñā, and the very essence of Pārvatī. (13)
The pure consciousness of Nanda shines forth, worshipped by Rādhā, Ramā, and others;
though consisting of three aspects, it exists eternally as a single form, in the likeness of the umbrella of Hari.
In whose leaves even goddesses and pearl-like women dwell,
and in whose jujube fruits sweet-souled pearls reside.
The supreme Brahman is the imperishable, which possesses form as Badarī;
it is composed of light, consisting of a divine abode, and here indeed takes the nature of a tree.
The invocation of Hari is embodied in service performed through letters;
here, celibacy shines forth in human form for the sake of Hari. (17)
The sages who are the Lord’s hairs shine there together;
and the other jujube trees there are indeed the very powers of Hari.
Here, the Gaṅgā exists as the wife of Nārāyaṇa, whose form is consciousness and intellect;
and in the forest of Badarī, the spiritual planes (bhūmis) exist in the form of bliss and sovereignty.
The white stones here are of the nature of existence, consuming the forest fire;
the leaf-huts are the dwellings, and the assembly hall consists of the vow of Brahman.

Concentration, retention, and meditation indeed dwell within the canopies; they shine upon the foreheads of the sages, and among the sages' foreheads, the state of "Upward-Stream" (ūrdhvasrotas) is supreme. //21//
Mastery over the senses shines forth in the bodily marks that are free from the flow of the humors,
and self-mastery shines within the hearts at Badarikāśrama.
Where there is no dwelling of the Kali age, Truth always resides;
there exist those whose nature is truth, who are truly virtuous, and who follow the dharma of the Kṛta age. (23)
As long as the Earth-goddess shall endure, and likewise as long as the Himālaya mountain shall remain,
so long shall the illustrious Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa remain as an ascetic.
The supreme Lord, known by the names Nara and Nārāyaṇa, resides as Badrīśvara;
indeed, the dharma established by Him shall endure in the forest of Badarī.
Blessed is this world of men, for whose sake the Supreme Person,
the Lord of Kuṅkumavāpikā, has appeared in the form of Nara and Nārāyaṇa.
He shines eternally as this very Badarīnātha;
Māṇikyā is his divine Aśvinī, and this tree is his vehicle in the form of a tree. (27)
Having become Badrī with a Brahmanic body, she shines resplendent along with him;
for she is indeed Lakṣmī, the consort of Nārāyaṇa, who serves Bālakṛṣṇa. 28.
To those people by whom [he] has been meditated upon, saluted, and likewise known, and by whom service has been rendered, he bestows the yoga of Kṛṣṇa. (29)
Through the grace of Māṇikya, all those men and women on earth,
even if they were previously devoid of virtue, become endowed with virtue and partakers of liberation.
Oh, what fortune for the worlds that the Badarī forest stands in their midst!
Oh, what fortune for those humans who dwell all around the forest! (31)
Those regions where the cool breezes from Badarī touch the dwellings of people become pure and meritorious, becoming equal to Badarī itself. (32)
Blessed is this Goddess Badarī, who puts the Pārijāta tree to shame;
for the Pārijāta indeed resided for a year in the abode of Kṛṣṇa.
This Goddess Badarī, however, shines like a parasol over Hari until the end of the kalpa, eternally united with Him through her yoga of liberation. 34.
Even before her, the wish-fulfilling tree does not attain its status as supreme;
for that [tree] is possessed of desire, whereas this Śrī Narāyaṇī is free from desire. 35.
Although Tulasī is fortunate, she remains in forest after forest without Hari; since she dwells without her manifest husband, she is therefore not equal to Badarī.
This Badrikeyī, however, is the housewife of the Blessed One, appearing in the form of a home;
it is after her name that the abode of Śrī Nārāyaṇa becomes renowned.
Leaving Vṛndā behind, Kṛṣṇa went to the western region of Vṛndāvana;
because of him, that Vṛndā remained in separation, taking the form of trees.
The Lord, the Sovereign, never abandons this Badarī at any time;
however, restriction within Vṛndāvana and Tulasī is considered to be of a passionate (rājasa) nature. ||39||
In Badarī, the essence of Brahman indeed always attained a state of pure goodness;
and Ketakī, having performed austerity, ascended to the heights of the sky.
But she, due to the fault of her deceit, sank down into the lower regions;
having given false testimony to the Creator, she indeed attained a state of unworthiness.
This Badarī is Mahāmuktānikā, the obedient servant of Hari;
she is the maidservant Muktānikā, possessing the color of a great ruby.
Unable to endure the separation from the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, she, full of remorse, [longed for] her beloved Nara-Nārāyaṇa, the ascetic. 43.
Having become the goddess Nārāyaṇī, she followed after Bālakṛṣṇa;
indeed, Badarī, the young yoginī, always possesses the nature of a child. 44.
The most excellent [cow] exists here, the eternally devoted companion of Kṛṣṇa;
indeed, all the wish-fulfilling cows are found by going to the sacred grove of Badarī. 45.
Having bowed to Nārāyaṇī at Badarī, they sit together in its shade;
and having caused Nārāyaṇa to drink milk, they depart after him toward that heaven.
They consider themselves blessed and fortunate to have been joined with Badarī by Kṛṣṇa;
even the wish-fulfilling creepers and the celestial vines grieve at their separation from Hari.
Having occasionally obtained the nectar-like fruit of Badarī, which is constantly offered there, the gods praise its great fortune, desiring the bath in the Gaṅgā. 48.
They rejoice in the essence of the fruit and hold even nectar in contempt;
for the gods, though they constantly drink nectar, never attain true satisfaction.
Having obtained the jujube fruit, the great seers were satisfied for a year;
the Bodhi tree was left in the forest by the virtuous Nārāyaṇa. 4.1.50
Even that [other place] does not possess such prosperity as Badarī possesses;
the staff of the illustrious Vāmana has dissolved into it once its task was accomplished. (51)
Without service, she remains in the world of Brahmā as one separated from her beloved;
this Badarī is fortunate and great compared to Yaṣṭikā and the others. ||52||
Kṛṣṇa, who is Nārāyaṇa in the form of sacrifice, fashioned auspicious trees for the sake of sacrificial fuel;
likewise, in former times, he himself offered them into the fire at the sacrifice.
Nevertheless, they were not as fortunate as Badarī,
because at the conclusion of the sacrifice, they were abandoned in the forest by Nārāyaṇa, the performer of the sacrifice.
This Badarī has always been placed upon the head by Nārāyaṇa;
blessed are you, O Goddess Māṇikī, blessed are you, O Sovereign Lady of Badarī! (55)
You, who were not abandoned by Kṛṣṇa even at the end, like Satyabhāmā and others—
blessed indeed are millions of women who have attained union with Kṛṣṇa.
O Badarī, those [other trees] are never truly blessed as you are;
for while they have all subsequently gone to their destruction, you alone continue to shine.
Indeed, O Badrikā, from you as their source flow all sacred fords and rivers;
you are Lakṣmī, you are Ramā, you are Śrī, you are Kamalā, the beloved of Hari. (58)
Through your dwelling as Nārāyaṇa, you are Nārāyaṇī;
Rādhā, Virajā, Hariṇī, and Sarasvatī all have you as their refuge. (59)
All of them go to behold you constantly by the command of Nārāyaṇa;
but Gaṅgā, having bathed your feet, then proceeds to another place.
The Narmadā indeed lasts for seven kalpas, while the Godāvarī lasts for ten kalpas;
Badarī, however, lasts for all kalpas, having been created by Nārāyaṇa.
As long as the remaining [portion] of Lakṣmī dwells in the Ocean of Milk residing in Śveta-dvīpa,
and as long as she remains in Vaikuṇṭha, so long indeed shall Badarī be eternal.
Among all species of trees and plants that possess roots, the divine Badarī is the purifier; she is Nārāyaṇī, the Supreme Sovereign.
In Plakṣadvīpa, at the abode of the Plakṣa deity during the great festival of the Plakṣa tree,
species born from sprouts arrived from other continents.

The trees that sprout from the earth (kalpodbhijja) arise from heaven; those that sprout from merit (puṇyodbhijja) arise from truth; those that sprout from ancestral rites (śrāddhodbhijja) arise from people and so forth; and the divine trees arise from the earth itself.

There were sacred trees, fuel-trees, sprouts, and various kinds of *darbha* grass; likewise, there were trees with succulent stalks, those with leafy branches, those bearing fruit, and those in flower.
Those who give their names to the continents, such as Jambū and others, arrived;
likewise, medicinal herbs that neutralize poison and bestow life arrived.
Pregnant women, those who had recently given birth, and those in their lineage arrived; those with milk in their udders, celibate women, and women in pairs also arrived. ||68||
Then, following the worship of the Plakṣa tree, in the pavilion of ten million medicinal herbs,
the Kalpavṛkṣa spoke to these trees known as the "divine" ones.
This Plakṣa festival has been completed; it is meritorious for all trees.
I have one inquiry, which I shall set forth before you. (4.1.70)
We are all trees, bearing fruit upon the tips of our branches;
others enjoy our fruits, while we ourselves are always like ascetics.
Those who consume the earth’s womb while being devoid of offerings to the gods shall become eaters of sin, thereby becoming joined with the guilt of the slaughter of Vṛtra.
