elsewhere, he laughs with loud bursts, making the sky resound with great thundering.
In some places, having become a Brahmin, he wanders in the midst of a village at midnight or thereafter, suffering exceedingly.
O Goddess Badrīprabhā, such was the destiny of Śrīśīla:
he had wives, sons, daughters, and likewise a wife. (54)
Having received royal honor and attained great happiness,
they dwelt there continuously by the command of their eldest brother.
Young Brahmin maidens, equal in beauty to celestial nymphs, were then married through good fortune into the royal family. (56)
The mother became very happy, as did the queens;
and the sons, too, were renowned, being joined with royal households. (57)
They then became the husbands of the daughters of the king’s household;
for the devotion of the virtuous indeed bears fruit, and service also bears fruit. (28)
Generosity, merit, assistance, and blessings also bear fruit through the power of the elder brother's merit, just as in the case of the royal family. (99)
He was born into a vehicle, food, wives, and sovereign power—wherever Fortune is gracious and where Nārāyaṇa himself resides. (4.6.60)
Where the gods are well-pleased, there no deficiency is found;
what is performed bears fruit in due time, but what is not performed is never attained anywhere.
O Badrīprabhā, through devotion to me, through narration, through hymns of praise, and through acts of giving and worship, this Suśīla became like a lord of subjects.
Then one day, his father, who had become a ghost, approached his own wife;
having entered her with a powerful possession, he wept in many ways.
"Who are you that has been made manifest by all with clear syllables?
He replied, "I am your father; my name is Śrīśīla, and I am dead. (64)
Then, overcome with grief, they all wept according to worldly custom;
subsequently, having received the king's command, those people performed the funeral rites.
He went to that place of death for the sake of worldly affairs and for the purpose of performing the *śrāddha* rites;
they prepared the city of Muktikahāra and performed the *śrāddha* and other ceremonies.
For the sake of their father's funeral rites, they gave many gifts there;
indeed, the sons performed various meritorious acts of liberation in that place.
They performed the annual rite of depositing bones in the Gaṇḍakī river; and whatever wealth had been earned by their father and buried in the earth as well, [they took]. (68)
O sons, you gave everything in gifts, yet it was defiled by stinginess;
nevertheless, the good state of the deceased brahmin was not attained.

O Lord of Badarī, even when a sacrifice has been performed, there is no liberation for one possessed of latent desires; how much less can acts such as giving lead to liberation for one with latent desires? (4.6.70)
He did not attain liberation; instead, he returned to his wife.
Trembling and letting out a great cry, he spoke to his own sons: ||71||
"Indeed, my liberation has not yet arisen, for latent impressions (vāsanā) afflict me—those of food, fine clothing and the like, greed, and wealth. (72)
For the sake of abandoning latent impressions (vāsanā), let them go to Badarikāśrama,
the abode of Nara and Nārāyaṇa, frequented by hosts of great sages.
Let them perform the śrāddha rite for my sake right there on the Badarī plateau;
let them also offer me a divine jujube fruit for my meal. (74)
Water offered to Nārāyaṇa, a large jujube fruit (badara), as well as bark, clothing, or a woolen blanket, as is appropriate. (75)
"May one who offers a vessel made of jujube wood and even the juice of the jujube fruit at my śrāddha ceremony grant me eternal satisfaction. (76)
There will be the destruction of hunger; there will be the destruction of thirst.
My latent impressions (vāsanā) shall perish before the presence of Badrīśa-Nārāyaṇa. 77.
"Entering my wife, I shall indeed come with you;
let them perform my rites in the divine Badarikāśrama. (78)
By the gift of even a single jujube fruit, my satisfaction shall be attained;
it will grant me liberation and eternal contentment—of this there is no doubt. (79)
Otherwise, there is truly no liberation for me here even by the gift of ten million;
indeed, there is no liberation for misers even when ten thousand sacred fords have been visited.
Then they all set out on foot for Badarikāśrama;
having bathed there in the primordial Gaṅgā, they bowed down to Nara and Nārāyaṇa.
They bowed down to Badrīprabhā and likewise honored the virtuous sages;
having performed their ablutions at all the sacred fords, they performed the ancestral rites (śrāddha) with concentrated minds.
The eldest son offered funeral cakes (piṇḍas) as well as the fruit known as badara,
and the water of the Gaṅgā, which is born from the grace of Nārāyaṇa’s feet.
He gave gifts of gold and likewise bark-garments to the brahmin;
he also gave the gift of a cow and other supreme gifts, such as the gift of land.
They indeed gave gifts of fresh milk and other dairy products, sweet foods, clarified butter, and various garments befitting kings. (85)
The illustrious Brahmin Śīla, having come in person, took hold of his hand and [gave him] a jujube fruit,
lovely water, bark-cloth, and likewise sugar.
Having obtained everything else that was excellent, he attained satisfaction;
entering his wife right there, he said, "I am completely satisfied."
Now the eternal worlds have presented themselves for my sake;
having departed from this state of a preta, I shall indeed go to the supreme state. (88)
At that time, my latent impressions were destroyed, and the illusion leading to the end of suffering was destroyed;
my sins were destroyed, and merit conducive to liberation arose. (89)
And for my sake, a celestial chariot of supreme splendor, endowed with great luster and graced by the attendants of Nara, Nārāyaṇa, and Kṛṣṇa, has indeed arrived.
May all my sons and daughters be happy and dear to me;
with a single jujube fruit, I have attained eternal satisfaction.
"Here I go; may it be well with you; having been delivered, I am indeed departing.
Having spoken thus, he ascended a celestial chariot in that divine abode.
Indeed, he was honored by the attendants and devotees of Viṣṇu while all his sons, daughters, and wives looked on. (93)
While the great sages looked on, he departed for the Imperishable by means of a celestial chariot;
everyone present at the hermitage of Nara and Nārāyaṇa was struck with great wonder. (94)
Having secured the liberation of their father and having worshipped Badarīśī and Narāyaṇa, the Lord of Badarī, the sons and others returned. 95.
Having worshipped Nara and obtained a jujube fruit along with its seed,
they then descended from the Himalayas and quickly went to their own abode.
Having obtained a pearl necklace and having given a gift of a house,
and having bestowed gifts of all household utensils and the like, ||97||
They arrived at that place of happiness, the city known as Dārābhāgya, [to see] their father-in-law, the king, the lord of their wives, and likewise the subjects. 98.
The male devotees and the female devotees as well told that very account;
they had attained a supreme wonder born from the majesty of Badarīśa.
Thus, O Badrikā, the supreme greatness of the gift of jujube fruits— which bestows liberation and wards off all calamities— has indeed been told to you.
Then, having heard this, the king named Dārābhāgya, along with the multitudes of people and his subjects gathered in groups, went forth accompanied by their families. || 101 ||
Indeed, for the purpose of a pilgrimage to Badarī, they went to the hermitage of Nara and Nārāyaṇa,
fully equipped with all necessary provisions, their minds fixed solely on devotion.
Worshipping the Lord of Śrī-Badrī and meditating upon the Goddess of Badarī,
they reached Badarikāśrama on Mount Himālaya, which possesses the splendor of Badarī.

Thus ends the sixth chapter, titled "The Description of the Royal Honors Bestowed upon the Sons of Śrīśīla at Dārābhāgyapura, the Death of Śrīśīla, His State as a Preta, and the Liberation of that Preta through the Performance of Śrāddha and the Offering of Badara Fruits and Other Gifts at Badarikāśrama," in the Tiṣya lineage within the fourth section of the *Śrī-Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
The illustrious Badarīśvarī said:
O beloved Nārāyaṇa-Kṛṣṇa, my husband was indeed a king who possessed the fortune of a wife;
tell me, what did he do upon reaching the abode of Badarī?
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said:
Beginning from Ṛṣīkeśa,
that king prostrated like a staff at every krośa before the Lord of Badarī and bestowed gifts.
Indeed, he went slowly on foot together with all my subjects;
for the entire expenditure on food for those thousand embodied beings was truly his own.
The king, together with his subjects, undertook the vow of eating only at midday;
every day, the monarch performed the turning of a thousand garlands.
And the subjects likewise performed the chanting of the names "Mālāvartana" and "Kīrtana":
"Hare Kṛṣṇa, Bālakṛṣṇa, Badrīnātha, Īśa, Mādhava! (5)
"O eternal Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, husband of Padmāvatī!"—
thus they joined together and performed vocal worship on the road.
All of them, full of zeal, observed the vows pertaining to sacred fords (tīrtha-vrata),
as well as sleeping on the ground, celibacy, and eating only once a day.
The mutual avoidance of physical contact between women and men, truthful speech, freedom from malice, and the refraining from other [inappropriate] songs. || 8 ||
Non-stealing, living according to the will of the Lord, self-study, eating only the fruits [of one's labor], service to the virtuous, service to Hari, and likewise service to saintly women. || 9 ||
In the evening, there shall be the hearing of sacred narratives and their recitation accompanied by musical instruments;
in the morning, there shall be the salutation of elders and the worship of the gods at dawn.
He practiced non-violence toward living beings and did not cut down even grasses or trees;
he also performed ritual bathing, meditation, recitation, fire-offerings, and libations for the ancestors.
Service to one's parents, service to one's husband, service to the virtuous, constant giving, service to cows, and honoring and worshipping Brahmins. || 12 ||
The pilgrims on the road indeed performed such vows as the giving of food and clothing, and the offering of incense and lamps. || 13 ||
All these thousand men, together with their wives, are unfortunate and destitute;
O Lord of Badarī, victory to you, O Viṣṇu, O Lord Nara-Nārāyaṇa! (14)
"Victory to Gaṅgā! Victory to the Lord of Badarī! And victory also to Himālaya!
With such words of "victory" and the like, they ascended the mountain full of enthusiasm.
Then, observing the peaks which are black like collyrium and gradually white, they proceed very slowly, immersed in devotion.
Then Nārāyaṇasvāmī became a saintly being, as did Nara;
likewise, the illustrious Badarī became a virtuous woman, possessing the splendor of the Bhāgavata.
Wearing the garb of mendicants and joined by the community,
the three of them met at night and performed a sweet-sounding hymn of praise.
They all act with affection toward Nara-Nārāyaṇa alone;
they listen together in groups and bow down as if to three gurus.
Some feed them, while others serve them;
indeed, those who have but a mere pittance for their journey frequently offer as much as they desire to these three.
And the threefold divine form of the Lord, appearing here and there, indicates the proper path as well as the provisions for the journey. (21)
Assuming the form of a seller and placing mountain fruits and other goods as if in a marketplace, he indeed stands before one on the road.
Thus the Blessed Lord dwells together with the assembly at Badarī, so that his devotees may become gracious through service and be freed from suffering. (23)
Hari-Kṛṣṇa cannot endure the separation from His own devotees, even when they have departed for that realm; yet the devotees themselves do not endure it at all.
Likewise, O Lord of Badarī, by my own will, I became Nārāyaṇa together with you, joined with Nara, when the assembly was convened. ||25||
For I am the bestower of liberation to my devotees, the son of Pārvatī, and the destroyer of sins;
impelled by compassion, I wandered among the assembly of the faithful, assuming the guise of a holy man.
O Badarī, by serving the virtuous, by serving Kṛṣṇa, and by visiting sacred pilgrimage sites, as well as by beholding and circumambulating [the deity], one's journey becomes fruitful. (27)
Then, O Badrī, for the sake of testing the king and the Saṅgha, I manifested at that time a sickly appearance, overcome by a fever. (28)
At that time, I was unable to move due to the fire of fever;
then my brother also suddenly became possessed by fever. (29)
My wife, a virtuous and faithful woman, wept bitterly:
"How can two men overcome by fever be served on this road? (4.7.30)
"How shall these two, who are ill, dependent on others, and deeply distressed, be protected on the road by a single virtuous woman amidst this cold and snowy path? (31)
Those who pride themselves on their wealth do not come into her presence;
yet the female mendicant sits down in solitude and cries out in their presence. (32)
All the young men established in the Saṃgha were endowed with compassion, as were the followers of other sects; whoever came into their presence remained there filled with compassion. (33)
They attend upon her for the sake of curing her fever, they even massage her body; they speak words of encouragement to the woman and even grant her whatever she desires. (34)
Gradually, a thousand men indeed gathered around the sick man, blocking his path;
though they met together, they were unable to abandon him.
As the king was departing on his way, he saw you both on the road—
those two most excellent holy men who were afflicted, and his beloved virtuous wife who was suffering.
He stood there suddenly and sat down before the two of them;
he asked what they desired, granted them fortitude, and gave them wealth.
The king gave this auspicious word to those two virtuous ones:
"Until your illness has been cured, for that long [you shall remain here]. (38)
"I shall not depart from this place; I will take you both with me to Badarikāśrama. Do not feel distressed. (39)
"We shall all dwell right here until our well-being is restored,
carrying you on our shoulders by your command."
"We shall go to the Badarītīrtha, for the virtuous are indeed the heart of Hari;
once attained, the virtuous must never be abandoned by those seeking liberation. (41)
"Let this virtuous woman not fall into grief; we shall remain as her companions.
May the Lord of Badarī quickly restore these two to health here. (42)
Having thus resolved, both the king and the subjects, who were dear to Hari, all abandoned their journey and remained on the road for the sake of the virtuous purpose. ||43||
Then they prepared food, drink, and fruit; and they gave to the two virtuous ones cooked mung beans, cakes, and other delicacies. (44)
The two of them fell happily; the virtuous woman prepared the meal.
They all ate, and then the arrival of night occurred.
At night, all of them, their throats filled with passion, performed kīrtana; they chanted the name of Śrī Nara-Nārāyaṇa accompanied by musical instruments. 46.
Then, indeed, as the middle of the night passed away, a rain of snow fell;
a cold fire pervaded everywhere upon the surface of the earth throughout the assembly.
Having abandoned their lives at dawn, the two who were afflicted fell dead;
that virtuous woman, now having a protector, wept, and the king and his subjects wept as well. 48.
When the departure of the cold had occurred and following the dawning of morning,
the king, addressing all those set out on the journey, spoke.
"As long as they do not live until death, so long shall I renounce food;
I consider death together with the virtuous to be the bestower of liberation for me. (4.7.50)
Upon hearing this, all the people—men, women, and even children—who were traveling there made such a vow: "We shall not take any food."
"As long as these two do not survive, we shall die here without water;
for the sake of the virtuous, we shall go to the abode of Brahmā, restraining our breath."
What is the use of traveling here for those who, having abandoned the virtuous, seek only their own interest at the expense of others?
His life is fruitless; he lives only by abandoning the virtuous. (553)
One should always protect the virtuous even at the cost of one's own life—
for the sake of cows, for the sake of Brahmins, for the sake of the righteous, and for the sake of a chaste wife.
For that person who provides protection even at the cost of their own life,
both heaven and liberation are considered certain, for he is a true refuge.
Even one who is addicted to the five great sins, if he gives up his life for the sake of the virtuous in order to protect them, is liberated from all sin. (56)
The Lord Hari provides protection for those who protect the virtuous;
Hari dwells only among the virtuous, for the virtuous person is indeed Hari himself.

Having directed toward the virtuous that same affection which one feels for one's own sons, for one's wife, for one's parents, and for one's kinsmen, one is here released from the bondage of birth. (58)
If the effort that is extended for the sake of maintaining one's own family is instead applied for the sake of the virtuous, then that person, being diligent, is indeed released from evil. (59)
Just as partiality is shown by people toward their own family members, so too is that which is done for the sake of the virtuous; indeed, what is performed for them carries one across.
Just as the oil inherent in a person's own body exists within their physical frame, if it likewise arises toward the virtuous, one is liberated from the ocean of worldly existence. //61//
Just as a man who has exerted himself for his own sake does not perceive his fatigue,
so too, out of affection, the virtuous do not perceive their own fatigue when acting for the sake of others.
He does not consider anything as belonging to another, nor does he regard the hardships of liberation as such;
he alone attains the lotus feet of Nārāyaṇa in the divine abode.
But that embodied being who, filled with pride, abandons a virtuous person who is afflicted by illness and departs,
goes indeed to the world of Yama, and experiences here [in this world] suffering resembling that of Yama.
Through service, one obtains the fruit of serving one's mother, the fruit of serving one's father, as well as the eternal fruit of serving one's beloved, according to the wise. (65)
All sacred fords always reside within the person of the virtuous;
one who treats the virtuous—the true ford—contemptuously does not obtain the fruit born of sacred fords.
For these two virtuous ones who have come upon this path, abandoning them would indeed be a sin;
for their sake, by giving up my life, there shall be merit, heaven, and liberation. (67)
Having thus resolved, both the king and the subjects abandoned all worldly affairs; even forsaking food and water, they sat down in the presence of the corpse.
There they made their dwelling and constantly engaged in the chanting of the Name;
then that virtuous and faithful woman desired to give up her life.
Having gathered the wood in one place and placed the two corpses there,
just as he was going to set fire to them, the king himself arrived.
Leaping up, he fell before the woman upon the heap of wood;
thereupon the queen, the other women, and the subjects were all overwhelmed with grief.
They suddenly fell upon the wooden funeral pyre for the sake of death,
even as the woman, having kindled the fire, lay there.
The mountains and other [elements] lay down and did not emerge from the fire;
seeing such supreme devotion, the Blessed One himself—
From the funeral pyre whose fire had been extinguished, Hari arose alive as a man, laughing, with a divine body endowed with four arms. (74)
Holding a conch, a discus, a mace, and a lotus, and graced by Nara, he was likewise accompanied by the virtuous Lakṣmī; smiling, he spoke to the kings and others.
"Gentlemen, you are my devotees who have offered me everything; you are endowed with noble affection, purified by sacred pilgrimage sites, and equal to my own self. (76)
All of you, having surrendered yourselves and being freed from all sins,
are worthy of Vaikuṇṭha, endowed as you are with my grace.
I have examined them all; they have exerted themselves for my sake, they have given their very lives for my sake, and they have made their existence meaningful for my sake.
Having abandoned attachment to worldly life, children, and kin, and being devoted to the virtuous, you have become fit for the divine abode and fit for liberation here in the Himalayas. (79)
"By my grace, may you all possess divine bodies here, fragrant and moving through the sky; indeed, let everyone become entirely free from suffering."
"O sinless ones, Badarikāśrama is not far from here for me;
come quickly with me by way of the sky. (8.1)
Having spoken thus, the Blessed Lord Nārāyaṇa and Nara led them all through the path of the sky to the hermitage of Badarikā.
Devoted to the Blessed One, they remained there all around Badarī; they dwelt for a fortnight, serving Nara and Satī, the lords of Badarī. 83.
Those of superior knowledge beheld the sages, gods, and divine hosts of ancestors who had assembled from heaven; and they became as if liberated.
Then they beheld there a certain brahmin, an ascetic sage performing austerities at the tip of the Badarī tree, absorbed in the recitation of the name of Nārāyaṇa.
And I beheld a beautiful maiden approaching before the twice-born one, who was without food, absorbed in meditation, possessed of a divine form, and endowed with matted locks.
Having given a jujube fruit to the brahmin from the base of the Badarī tree, that divine and wonderful radiance suddenly vanished.
In Badarī, that Nārāyaṇī entered into a state of absorption;
seeing that supreme wonder, those men and humans were filled with amazement. ||88||
Then they performed the ritual for the sacred ford and the worship of Nārāyaṇa;
at that time, they bathed in the Gaṅgā and subsisted on a diet of jujube fruits.
With their life-breaths focused on Nārāyaṇa, they chanted his names;
they performed the lustration ceremony for Hari and, full of longing, partook of his grace.
Their minds became one-pointed and filled with the melting flow of affection for Kṛṣṇa;
at that moment, their bodies indeed became divine and refulgent.
O Badrī, they were born in an instant, and then a celestial chariot arrived;
established in unwavering meditative absorption, they possessed divine senses and forms.
With those very same divine bodies, they all ascended the celestial chariot—the men, women, and children, all divine and four-armed. (93)
Having bowed to Hari along with his radiant attendants, they beheld the stainless and uninterrupted path to Vaikuṇṭha in the sky.
Then, O Badrī, shouts of victory went forth toward the abode of Vaikuṇṭha; auspicious sounds arose among the gods and the great sages in the heavens.
At that time, all men became Nārāyaṇas and the women became Nārāyaṇīs;
being divine and worthy of Vaikuṇṭha, they entered Vaikuṇṭha in an instant. (96)
Indeed, the fruit of service to Kṛṣṇa, who possesses a beautiful form, is liberation;
the subjects saw those [troubles], such as misfortune regarding their wives and kings, in their dreams. (97)
They celebrated great festivals with celestial chariots for those who had attained liberation;
thus [was it] through the pilgrimage to Śrīmāṇikībadri and Badarikāśrama. 98.
Indeed, by reading, hearing, remembering, or even praising this, human beings attain liberation, possessing divine bodies and traveling in celestial chariots. 99.
Those who speak thus of the splendor of Badrī indeed obtain both worldly enjoyment and liberation;
for where you are, O Splendid Badrī, there Nārāyaṇa himself is present.
Where the divine great sages dwell, where the Gaṅgā is, and where Pārvatī is—
there Vaikuṇṭha itself resides as the fifth, endowed with austerity.

Thus ends the seventh chapter, titled "The Description of King Dārābhāgya’s Journey to Badarikāśrama with Ten Thousand Men, His Vision of Badarī-Nara-Nārāyaṇa in the Form of Sādhus and Sādhvīs, His Testing, His Offering of Life for the Sake of Nārāyaṇa, Their Graciousness, His Transport to Badarikāśrama through the Sky, His Attainment of a Divine Body, and His Liberation," in the fourth section, the Tiṣya-santāna, of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmīnārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
The illustrious Badrīśvarī said: Who was that brahmin there, the ascetic in the grove of Badarī, to whom she gave the jujube fruit? O Hari, tell me the story.
Śrī Nara-Nārāyaṇa said: There was a brāhmaṇa named Brahmadeva who resided in the village of Lūnī;
he was an expert in the Vedas and their auxiliary sciences (vedāṅgas) in Saurāṣṭra and was devoted to the performance of sacrifices.
Having bathed in the morning and having worshipped Kṛṣṇa and the five deities,
he would indeed go for alms to the good houses where people reside in the village.
Having obtained enough to fill its belly, it returns to its own home;
even without obtaining a full meal, it goes as far as the courtyard of its dwelling.
Having obtained enough, he goes home with his wife, whose name was Viśadākṣī; having cooked the food, he eats it after first offering it to the gods. ||5||
As he lived in this manner, a thousand years passed;
yet no offspring was born, and his wife became overcome with grief.
For one who is childless, there are no worlds that grant happiness;
likewise, there can be no liberation for one who is bound by debts.
Even a fool who belongs to the lineage uplifts his ancestors;
for one without a son there is no destination, and for a barren woman there is no liberation.
"Therefore, one must indeed strive for the sake of a son through austerities and other means. Having reflected thus, the radiant and large-eyed woman spoke to her husband.
Indeed, a thousand years have passed, yet there is no son born of my mind;
neither one born of the womb, nor one born of the body, nor one given, nor one protected.
Without a son there is no way [to salvation]; therefore, a son must be desired.
Indeed, among all sons, the one born from the womb is the most venerable.
An excellent son born of the womb—one who is our own legitimate offspring, endowed with virtues, and a reflection of both his parents—must be produced by us two. (12)
"Conceive a child after meditating upon Hari, so that I may have fulfilled my purpose.
Having heard these words of the woman, the Brahmin said, "I have no son. (13)
"It is written upon your forehead that you shall have no son;
therefore, we two, being childless, must remain in the ocean of worldly existence."
Having heard this, the woman said: "Fortune increases through austerity.
For the sake of desiring a son, penance must be performed here either by you or by me."
"The death of those who have no son indeed leads to hell;
having discharged the three debts, one should fix the mind on liberation. (16)
"O beloved, for a Brahmin ascetic, especially, there is nothing that cannot be accomplished;
therefore, you must by all means perform supreme austerity for the sake of a son. (17)
Having spoken thus, the brahmin ceased and fell into reflection:
"The words of my wife are indeed true; for one who is childless, there is no attainment of the supreme goal. (18)
The divine Badarikāśrama is a field that fulfills all intentions;
one should go there for the purpose of pilgrimage, for the sake of a son, and also for the sake of ascetic penance. (19)
Either the attainment of a son will occur, or the perfection of liberation will come to pass;
therefore, for the sake of accomplishing both, one must go to the Badarī forest.
Having thus reached a decision, he went with his wife to Badarikāśrama; there, having performed the rites for the sacred ford, he took his seat in the light.
That Brahmin performed penance day and night together with his wife;
for one month, he subsisted solely on the fruit of the jujube tree.
He remained without food for one month, subsisting on the cold wind;
at the end of two months, having remembered Badarī, he performed a hymn of praise.
May Nārāyaṇī, Satī, Sādhvī, Māṇikī, Śrī, Ramā, Rati, Hariṇī, Kamalā, Lakṣmī, and Mādhavī be ever victorious! 24.
May the goddess Mādhavī—possessing roots, leaves, and branches, originating from the Himalayas, rich in jujube fruits, and having men as her seed—be ever victorious! 25.
May the virtuous Brāhmaṇī Bālayoginī, who holds a trident and a goad, the Śrī who is the dwelling place of all ṛṣis and gods, the consort of Mādhava, be ever victorious! 26.
May Mādhavī ever be victorious—she who is dark-hued, beloved of Kṛṣṇa, cooling, golden, and a quencher of fire; she who is the consort of Hari, possesses the character of Brahman, and is eternal. 27.

May the daughter of Madhu, who consists of pure being, whose nature is that of Bālakṛṣṇa, who is the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama), and who is Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa in the form of primordial wisdom, be victorious! 28.
May Pārvatī, the mother of the universe who has descended as Brahmā’s daughter and others, the beloved of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and his protectress, the consort of Mādhava, be ever victorious! 29.
May the Goddess Mādhavī—the ascetic Parameśvarī who abides in wonder, who fulfills the desires of her devotees, and who belongs to the Moon—be ever victorious! 4.8.30
Having thus offered praise and paid homage, that Brahmin withdrew;
then, having gone to Viśadākṣa, he worshipped Badarīśvarī.
Water, as well as unbroken grains, excellent flowers, and sugar;
incense, a lamp, sandalwood, saffron, and likewise fine cloth. (32)
Having offered [the oblation] to Goddess Badrikā, she performed the lustration rite (nīrājana);
with clear eyes, she also entreated her for forgiveness for her transgressions.
Then, O fair-eyed one, a celestial voice was heard there above Badarī, saying: "Perform the Badarī vow."
Every morning, you must sprinkle water at the root of the Badarī tree;
furthermore, sleep beneath the Badarī and take your seat beneath the Badarī. (35)
Water purified by *badarī* leaves, a diet consisting of *badarī* fruits, and residing for one month having reached the shade of the *badarī* tree. (36)
Likewise, bathing in water mixed with the juice of Badarī fruit is most excellent;
so too is the constant wearing of a garland of Badarī fruits around the neck. (37)
Wearing a garland of jujube leaves and fruits on the forearm; wearing a girdle of jujube leaves around the waist. (38)
Likewise, there is the taking of a cluster of jujube flowers with their fragrance, and similarly, the wearing of a cluster of jujube flowers in the hair-braid. || 39 ||
The evening worship consists of the chanting of hymns to the illusory power of Badrī, the cleansing of the ground of Badrī, and the consumption of the Badrī-gundra plant. 4.8.40.
One should also drink water mixed with the powder of *badarī* bark;
furthermore, at the end of the month, one should plant the sprouts of *badarī* seeds. (41)
The concluding rite, worship, and the offering of jujube fruits;
as well as the gift of gold, silver, ornaments, and gems according to one's capacity.
The giving of food, clothing, and so forth, as well as the bestowing of wealth and sovereignty, the offering of gifts according to one's means, worship, and the ritual dismissal (visarjana). ||43||
There was also food for the virtuous men, as well as food for the virtuous women;
there was food for the maidens and food for the young boys as well. ||44||
He also provided food for the young brides and food for the pregnant women, as well as shawls,
necklaces, bodices, and breast-binders.
One should give to the women who have shown me favor a gift that brings pleasure;
one should give wealth as a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) and then perform the ritual circumambulation.
In this manner, one should observe the month-long vow; by doing so, a son shall be born to her, or even a daughter who will be equal to me—of this there is no doubt. (47)
Having heard this celestial voice, she performed the Śrī-Badarī-vrata for a month exactly as prescribed, and the brahmin also practiced penance.
At the conclusion of her vow, the goddess Badarī, known as Māṇikīramā, became manifest in the form of a maiden herself and emerged from within the tree. 49.
Holding a jujube fruit in her hand, she gave it to the Brahmin’s wife;
the large-eyed woman did not bow, nor did she bow to that Badarīśvarī.
She strove within her heart for the sake of the husband's attainment of the fruit;
and Badarī, suddenly perceiving his intention, gave it to the Brahmin.
First, she gave that divine jujube fruit with its seed which bestows a son;
then she gave a second jujube fruit to that Brāhmaṇī.
The goddess Badarī said to the brahmin: "Eat this with its seed;
you shall have a son through your wife in due time. (53)
Then he spoke to Viśadākṣī, and after that, to his son:
"Merely by the resolve of your daughter-in-law, you shall possess a daughter."
"O young yoginī, that girl shall suddenly become my mind-born daughter;
equal to me, she will be a devotee of Śrī Hari and become Nārāyaṇī. (55)
Therefore, for the sake of your daughter-in-law, protect this second jujube fruit so that it remains imperishable.
O Brāhmī, I am pleased with you; may you be one who causes the expansion of the lineage. (56)
"Your lineage shall be known as Bādarāyaṇa, and you shall be a singer of the Pautrīvaṃśa"—thus did he offer this blessing to that Brāhmaṇa woman and likewise to the Brāhmaṇa. (57)
Having given [it], the queen Bādrīnārāyaṇī vanished;
the brahmin had accomplished his purpose, and the brahmin woman’s heart was fulfilled.
Having worshipped Nārāyaṇa, Badarīśa, and Badrī with devotion, and having performed the entire concluding rite (udyāpana) according to one's capacity, [one attains the fruit]. ||59||
Having completed his journey and performed his full course of austerities,
and having honored the sages and the gods, he then indeed plunged into the Gaṅgā.
Having bowed slowly and remembered Hari, both of them returned to Ṛṣikeśa,
Haridvāra, Puṣkara, and Siddhapattana.
Having joyfully visited the sacred fords (tīrthas) for four months, the two of them arrived in Saurāṣṭra at the holy site of Kuṅkumavāpikā.
Having performed the rites for the sacred ford and beheld the sage Śrī Lomaśa,
both of them worshipped Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa.
With serene minds, they reached their own home in the village of Lūnī;
honored with offerings, those two householders took up residence there.
The large-eyed woman also displayed the signs of pregnancy for her husband;
in due time, she gave birth to a son endowed with auspicious marks.
The Brahmin gave gifts and performed the birth rites and other ceremonies;
she, whose eyes were bright and who possessed a son, was indeed counted among the virtuous mothers.
By the grace of the goddess Pārvatī, the consort of Badrī, she became endowed with offspring; blessed with good fortune, she was a successful housewife. (67)
Then, as time passed and his son became a youth,
he attained renown even among the subjects by the name Nikāmadeva.
He was married by his father in the auspicious abode of Dhūnī village to Sureśvarī, the virtuous daughter of the Brahmin Girīśvara. (69)
He took the maiden in marriage according to the prescribed rites in the pavilion;
she too [wedded] him who was equal to Mahendra, born from the grace of Badarī.
Having obtained a husband named Nikāmadeva, she rejoiced;
and Nikāmadeva’s mother, for her daughter-in-law, [offered] a jujube fruit.
Having protected it for a long time, Sureśvarī joyfully gave her daughter-in-law the fruit, together with its narrative, as the deity of Badarī.
She became possessed of divine knowledge and endowed with the power of true resolve; whatever that Queen of the Gods imagined in her mind, she brought into being.
All that indeed comes to pass just as Lakṣmī and Sarasvatī did;
thus, O Badrikā, has this narrative of the Goddess of the Gods been told to you. (74)
Now, O Bālayoginī, I shall tell you another story:
you yourself have been born as Badarī, my daughter Bālayoginī. (75)

Thus ends the eighth chapter, titled "The Description of how the Childless Brahmin Brahmadeva of Lūnī Village obtained sons and daughters through the granting of a boon received by his asceticism at Badarikāśrama," in the Tiṣya lineage within the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Goddess Badrīrāmā, to this purifying story of a devotee named Nikāmadeva, who dwelt in Dhūni in Saurāṣṭra.
The brahmin lived in the auspicious house of his father-in-law in Dhūnigrāma;
for he was the preceptor of those dwelling in the forests of Mount Raivata.

He was a follower of the Vedas, established in the dharma of ritual action, devoted to the performance of rites, intent on the worship of the five deities, and a bringer of happiness to the sacrificers.
There, the ritual acts were rooted in sacred refinement (saṃskāra),
consisting of marriage and other ceremonies, including the recitation of the seven-day vow.
There, the festivals of the gods and the festivals of the year proceed as soon as they are summoned by the people,
preceded by great honor.
He accomplished all his tasks according to the prescribed rules,
and there were thousands of patrons for him in every village.
Wherever he goes, from that place he obtains excellent and abundant wealth, which he brings home with great eagerness.
He obtains food, many garments, ornaments,
as well as vehicles, mounts, vessels, and even various utensils.
Having taken it, he indeed goes to his own home, being preoccupied with greed;
nor does he give it even to other brahmins who are destitute.
He constantly accumulates wealth in his mansion;
yet, for the sake of his own kinsmen and others, he does not even give anything away when it is needed.
Within the house, things indeed become worn out by the onset of autumn and other seasons; they are destroyed by the rains and are further decayed by the heat of the sun and so forth. || 11 ||
Insects devour garments as well as many kinds of food; yet even so, the greedy person does not give anything at all to those in need.
The wife of the brahmin Nikāmadeva was named Sureśvarī;
she was devoted to acts of giving and possessed great generosity.
He gives to the mendicants such that they do not even know it;
he bestows food, clothing, and alms-bowls upon the destitute and the homeless.
"May the Supreme Lord be gracious, and may Hari, the Master, be the inner self";
having uttered this, he indeed bestows [the offering] upon the embodied Brahmins.
By the method of offering everything to Kṛṣṇa, the practitioner of devotion gives;
consequently, her merit constantly arises as eternal and abundant. (16)
Indeed, her inner self and Lord are exceedingly pleased with whatever she offers to the Wielder of the Śārṅga bow at the time of worship for the Brahmins. (17)
In that form, Hari, possessing a divine appearance—the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa himself, the Beloved of Śrī—assumes all of that. 18.
Desiring a daughter, she ate a jujube fruit offered by her mother-in-law;
meanwhile, in a certain house, there lived the wife of a brahmin who was likewise longing for a daughter.
A certain girl, nine years of age and possessing the form of Badrī, arrived;
she said, "I have no protector, for I am bereft of mother and father. (4.9.20)
"My household does not function; protect me, O wife of Brahmā!
Thus did the maiden Sureśvarī entreat her repeatedly. (21)
Then Sureśvarī, devoted to affection, protected her like Badrī;
"Perform all the duties of the household as my own daughter. ||2||
"I shall always protect you; you are indeed my mind-born daughter.
Having thus asked her husband for refuge, she protected him.
The maiden also served them, regarding them as her mother and father;
then, as time passed and she reached youth, she became a young female yoginī.
Even upon attaining her youth, she did not undergo any transformation of her senses;
when questioned regarding marriage by the two Brahmins, she replied, "No."
Having previously practiced yoga, she spoke to her mother regarding the supreme self:
"O Mother, this human body has been primarily acquired for the sake of liberation. (26)
One who seeks liberation should not employ [the senses] for the sake of sense-objects or for the sake of worldly existence;
many lifetimes have already passed away in pursuit of those objects and their pleasures. (27)
There, although all things have been enjoyed, the end of craving has not been seen;
for regarding enjoyments, a craving arises that is ever-increasing and does not cease. (28)
For me, there is no craving for that which has not been eaten, nor does it arise;
and for that which has not been consumed or has already been released, liberation is within the palm of my hand. (29)
Brahmā is indeed to be won over, and Nārāyaṇa is the one to be wedded;
however, you yourself must go there, to the abode of the glorious Nārāyaṇa.
Indeed, association with Hari is true association (satsaṅga), while any other is bad association (kusaṅga).
Having attained the rare satsaṅga, the Supreme Lord must be realized. ||3 1||
In the world of mortals, this living soul has been born many times as women;
he has also been born as a man, for he has not abandoned his desires. (32)

When, through association with the virtuous, one attains discernment—both as higher realization (*vijñāna*) and as knowledge (*jñāna*)—one gains discrimination (*viveka*), which is the cognition of difference, and attains devotion (*bhakti*). ||33||
When the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the treasury of power, is directly perceived, the devotee then indeed crosses to the further shore of saṃsāra with joy. (34)
O Mother, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama, exists on the surface of the earth as the young cowherd boy Kṛṣṇa. (35)
The divine Śrī Parameśvara, the husband of the beloved Anantabrahmā—by worshipping him, there is no fear of time, māyā, or evil deeds. (36)
Those who worship the Supreme Self, having abandoned all worldly attachments, are indeed called true saints; and those women as well are called saintly wives.
Those in whom desire, anger, and the like never exist at any time—should even desire for their devotees ever be observed, it does not constitute a bond. (38)
For one who has attained union with the Blessed One, divine desires and the like are always present;
and through the power of Kṛṣṇa’s majesty, even Māyā attains a state of divinity. (39)
Therefore, in Kṛṣṇa and in His devotee, even a bad quality becomes the highest of virtues;
it truly becomes divine, bestowing liberation and destroying sin.
Wherever Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa is, and wherever his beloveds are, those who know true devotion desire a body greyed by the dust from that place. ||41||
Even the trees, grasses, shrubs, creepers, beasts, and birds—all who entered into a relationship with Kṛṣṇa attained divinity. ||42||
Even they become worthy of worship by the gods; through association with them, one attains liberation. How much more so, then, for devoted humans who are solely intent on the service of Kṛṣṇa? ||43||
O Mother, you always perform meditation, worship, chanting of names, remembrance, and so forth of Kṛṣṇa; you worship Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of Śrī, the Supreme Person.
Then, through my constant service to you, I attained divinity;
I desire no other husband than the beloved Śrī Kṛṣṇa. (45)
In all matters, austerity is declared to be the cause of pleasing the Blessed One;
even Hari was formerly propitiated by the Creator through the power of austerities. 46.
He was propitiated by Sanaka and others through states of selfless dedication;
likewise, other discerning ones also [practiced] for the sake of pleasing Viṣṇu. (47)
They perform various kinds of austerities and restraints;
they abide in self-restraint, desiring to please the Blessed One. (48)
In Badarī, at the White Abode, the saintly perform austerities for the sake of attaining divine love and also for the sake of obtaining service [to the Lord]. (49)
"Whether in this life or in other births, O Supreme Person, I shall indeed perform austerities until you are pleased. 4.9.50
"By the power of service to Hari, through devotion to Hari, and also by your grace, O Mother, I shall become equal to Śivā, Brāhmī, and Ramā. (51)
Having propitiated Śrī Hari, my beloved, husband, master, and Lord, with garlands, sandalwood paste, fine garments, ornaments, food offerings, and services, I shall attain Him. (52)
Indeed, that service to the high-souled Śrī Kṛṣṇa, whose very nature is austerity, brings about the supreme good in both this world and the next for all beings. (53)
For one who is thus engaged there, no floods of obstacles shall ever arise;
rather, there will be various kinds of enjoyments and riches consisting of golden ornaments. (54)
Food, drink, flavors, and the like do not arise for the sake of bondage;
O Mother, this worldly flow is like the path of the blind following those who are blind.
It flows on indeed even without knowledge, its further shore never to be reached—by passionate women and by widows who are agitated by the thirst of desire. (56)
Even young women who possess exclusive devotion to Kṛṣṇa do not mourn their deceased husbands nor take refuge with another man, even while they are still married. (57)
Yet even they enjoy sensual pleasure while regarding Śrī Hari as their husband;
therein, desire, latent impression, and lack of discrimination constitute bondage. (58)
Divinity, meditative cultivation, and self-knowledge bestow the supreme good;
therefore, for the pleasure of Kṛṣṇa, one should perform austerity joined with loving devotion. (59)
"O Mother, I must perform here in your presence that which bestows liberation;
O Mother, I must cultivate love for Kṛṣṇa, who is most dear to me. (4.9.60)
Whatever task is dear to him, that I shall always perform;
likewise, I shall always conduct myself in accordance with his pleasure.
Whether far away or nearby, one should always abide by His command;
for Kṛṣṇa never does anything unpleasant to His own devotee anywhere.
Wherever the devoted woman dwells by his command,
there Hari goes, being completely under the sway of the devotee's love.
Therefore, there can never be a separation for Him from His devotee;
indeed, Kṛṣṇa is never able to endure separation from His devotee.
O Mother, this body is illusory and a binder of the living soul;
Māyā is the cause of birth, as well as darkness, ignorance, and delusion.
Having established association with the virtuous, one should destroy illusion, delusion, and the like;
with love, one should meditate upon the Supreme Brahman, Hari himself, the Lord of Ramā.

One should meditate upon Bālakṛṣṇa, the Lord of the world, the Knower of the Field (kṣetrajña), the Supreme Lord, who dwells in the heart, the beloved, the captivating one, and the bestower of divine bliss. 67.
One should listen with both ears to his playful deeds out of great joy;
for the pastimes of Hari are most weighty and superior even to asceticism and charity.
O Mother, through union with Hari, one shall always possess freedom from desire;
through union with Him whose desires are fulfilled, one shall always possess the state of having all desires fulfilled.
Whether seeing a man who is a child, a youth, or even an old man, a woman may undergo a transformation of state; for she is considered to be possessed of illusion (māyā). 4.9.70.
Even when the three types of men behold her limbs, she undergoes only a slight transformation; yet even that [transformation] is illusory. (71)
Just as she would feel upon seeing a beast, so too, upon seeing a man, she would not undergo any transformation;
such a woman would be one who has conquered her senses and is free from passion.
She who experiences transformation in secret is indeed called one of middling passion;
but she who undergoes no change even during union with a man is a sovereign mistress (īśvarī). //73//
She is Brāhmī, Muktānikā, Bodhyā, Brahmapriyā, and Haripriyā; she is endowed with great dispassion and is fond of divine garlands. ||74||
But such a woman, regarding that divine Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Lord, always perceives desire, pride, and anger as divine. (75)
The meditation upon that object of knowledge is indeed as immovable as Mount Meru;
by means of it, one shall attain the supreme great accomplishment (mahāsiddhi) in this very birth. //76//
O Lord, for one whose heart has been scorched by the defects of illusion and the sensual pleasures of women,
there can be no sense of fulfillment even upon attaining sovereignty.
The defects of *māyā* (illusion/delusion) are to be destroyed by serving those who are free from *māyā*;
Hari himself is manifestly free from *māyā*, and his true devotees are likewise free from *māyā*.
Through union with them, one should abandon illusion and all that pertains to illusion;
indeed, by means of the state of being Brahman, one should serve Kṛṣṇa as his female servant.
One should not remain for even a moment without the company of Kṛṣṇa;
one should abide in Hari in human form, the Lord who bestows all bliss. 4.9.80
Having gathered the words of the virtuous regarding conduct toward the glorious Supreme Lord, I must live in Hari, having completely abandoned the notions of "I" and "mine. 81.
For even harsh words, if they are true, should always be accepted;
through the grace of the Supreme Self, those devoid of virtue are utterly destroyed.
Furthermore, through the propitiation of the virtuous, one's evil qualities perish;
therefore, one should live before them with a mind, body, and senses that are free from deceit. (83)
In every way, one should perform what is pleasing to them; one must never commit an offense.
Should an offense ever occur, they should be propitiated through services.
For her with whom the virtuous are pleased, there is no fear of time;
for her, supreme and certain welfare shall come—of this there is no doubt. (85)
Possessing knowledge and having the nature of Brahman, she fears nothing from any quarter;
O Mother, through union with Kṛṣṇa, that beautiful woman becomes one who has accomplished her purpose.
Having full confidence in Śrī Hari, she does not fear anything from anyone among the virtuous;
she is certain that "I belong to the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. (87)
Affectionate and full of love for Kṛṣṇa, she fears nothing from anyone;
Kṛṣṇa alone is her supreme boon, and her devotion as a devoted wife is ever fixed on Hari. (88)
In her heart there is no fear, for she is Śrī, who has attained her goal through Hari;
indeed, for the sake of the joy of Kṛṣṇa and the virtuous, she would renounce all that is illusory.
Neither kingdom, nor husband, nor enjoyments, nor home, nor wife, nor family—nothing whatsoever anywhere causes her fear; rather, something else arises. (4.9.90)
Just as an elephant of the quarters is intoxicated with rut, so too should she be;
with her soul possessed by the planet Kṛṣṇa, she should never desire anything else.
Indeed, with this very body she shall go to the supreme goal;
whether consecrated or unconsecrated, she goes to the abode of the Blessed One.
Kṛṣṇa, the lord of the abode of Brahman, comes here for the sake of the happiness of those who cannot endure separation; having granted them joy, he leads them to the imperishable state. 93.
Thus, for the happiness of his devotees, he manifests within all the cosmic eggs (caṇḍas);
having brought joy to his friends, he leads them to the imperishable abode (akṣaradhāma). ||94||
Kṛṣṇa is born among the gods, sometimes among the ṛṣis and the ancestors; sometimes among men, women, aquatic creatures, beasts, and birds. ||95||
Having accomplished his purpose to the full extent, he returns to his original form;
indeed, his own form is two-armed, human in appearance, and served by the liberated.
Whether by the will of his devotee or even by his own will, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama) may become a householder or one devoid of passion, possessing many arms. 97.
O Mother, that Supreme Lord exists as the very embodiment of the highest good in every respect; O Mother, the storehouse of compassion, His sovereignty is manifold in form. (98)
Only the maidservants, and no others, know Kṛṣṇa as their inner self;
that excellent Lord dwells everywhere in the form of the inner controller (antaryāmin). 99.
O Mother, I have been surrendered in every way to Kṛṣṇa;
by the power of taking refuge in Kṛṣṇa, I shall certainly not choose another husband.
O Hare Kṛṣṇa, O Bālakṛṣṇa, O Śrīkānta, O Puruṣottama!
You alone are my eternal husband; I have come to you for refuge. 10.1.
Having spoken thus, O Badrikā, that young female yoginī fell silent;
and Sureśvarī, her mother, was filled with great wonder.

Thus ends the ninth chapter, titled "The Description of the Instruction on the State of Brahman and Other Matters Concerning the Liberation of the Child-Yoginī Badarī—who had taken the form of a daughter for the sake of the Brāhmaṇī Sureśvarī—in the *Bālayoginīgītā* within the fourth section, the *Tiṣyasantāna*, of the *Śrī-Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*."
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said: Then the mother, the Queen of the Gods, questioned the maiden again:
"Tell me once more in detail, how may the Blessed One be obtained by me? (1)
Thus addressed, that delighted young yoginī spoke again:
"I shall tell you all of that; listen, O Badrī, for your own benefit. (2)
O Mother, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa becomes attainable through intense service,
through servitude, through a flood of love, and through acts dedicated to His sake.
For its sake the body must be maintained, and for that purpose the sense organs as well;
for that purpose the mind, the ego, and the intellect exist, all having that as their aim.
Desire, joy, delight, festivity, and greatness have those [objects] as their purpose;
pleasure, sleep, play, touch, and the bed have those [objects] as their purpose. (5)
Whether internal or external, secret or intended for that purpose; whether hidden, manifest, or everything—all that is for that purpose should be performed directly.
"By that, the Lord who is the beloved of Kamalā might be won through his loveliness;
for that purpose, indeed, I have performed everything day and night."
"The Lord will come," [thinking thus,] the Blessed One is bound by the cords of affection for his devotee;
I behold the Blessed One within my heart and remember him. (8)
O Mother, whether on my bed, at my meal, or while traveling, I see that beloved one for a moment, sometimes smiling and sometimes calling me toward him.
While he is enjoying himself, I shall delight him, for as I rejoice, I am absorbed in him;
thus, in all my states, he is perceived by me as being joined with me.
O Mother, day after day, whether eating, drinking, moving, standing, lying down, or hearing, I do not remember anyone else apart from you.
By the grace of the Lord of Ramā and of the virtuous, I have likewise become such a one, and together with my yoginī companion, I serve that very Śrīprabhākānta. (12)
Having attained restraint over food in Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Self,
they have attained self-control in Mālatīśa, the Supreme Self.
Such steadfast and exclusive devotion to Kṛṣṇa must always be cultivated;
then, for all women as well, liberation will be held in the palm of their hand. || 14 ||
The vow of celibacy is indeed that which consists of desire for Brahman;
by the very vow of celibacy, all dharmas are accomplished in every respect. || 15 ||
The primary duty for women is the yoga with Kṛṣṇa, which is supreme at all times;
O Mother, through that, liberation which bestows divinity is produced.
That conduct toward the beloved which is directed toward Śrī Kṛṣṇa should never be altered; indeed, it must be diligently nurtured by women through the company of the virtuous. 17.
That which causes displeasure to Kṛṣṇa must indeed be quickly turned away; for a disposition that does not produce favor should be abandoned, even if it is innate. (18)
A virtuous woman should always conduct herself in accordance with her husband's will;
she thus becomes worthy of union and bestows divine liberation. 19.
One should always abandon identification with the body or pride in the presence of Kṛṣṇa;
for a devotee of such a nature, the attainment of the highest good shall come to pass in this very world. 4.10.20.
One should cultivate association with such noble women who bestow the highest good;
she who affectionately unites one with Kṛṣṇa is indeed mother, father, and lord. (21)
That which does not cause one to remember Kṛṣṇa, nor unites one with the Supreme Lord, nor awakens one to the cause of the highest good, but rather shows laxity toward Hari. (22)
She who reveals faults among the virtuous, as well as wicked qualities in Śrī Kṛṣṇa, causes one to fall from the yoga of the Blessed Lord; she is not at all worthy of association.
Her word is not to be respected, nor should one remain with her;
she who bestows hells is no mother who brings auspiciousness.
Kṛṣṇa would fall from his station if her word were not held in honor;
for even if fallacious arguments should arise in the heart, they would be obstacles to Kṛṣṇa. (25)
At that time, one should constantly perform the auspicious chanting (kīrtana) of Kṛṣṇa;
the Lord, the friend of the distressed and an ocean of mercy, should also be entreated. 26.
O Hare, O Nārāyaṇa, O Kṛṣṇa, I am yours; protect me here!
Indeed, the divine names of the virtuous are likewise to be glorified. (27)
One should always maintain firm devotion to the Self as well as to Kṛṣṇa;
thus, supreme divinity shall arise, which destroys fallacious arguments. (28)
Whatever serves to manifest the form of Kṛṣṇa must indeed be performed;
however, that form in which Kṛṣṇa is not truly present should not be viewed as a form at all.
Where there is no fragrance, Kṛṣṇa is indeed not to be smelled, for there is no fragrance at all;
where there is no touch, Kṛṣṇa is indeed not to be touched, for there is no touch at all.
In that bliss, O Kṛṣṇa, there is indeed no one to be gladdened;
in that relish, O Kṛṣṇa, there is indeed nothing to be relished at all. 3.1
Where Kṛṣṇa does not sleep, there indeed one must not sleep;
and in whatever place Kṛṣṇa does not stay, there indeed one must never stay.
Where Hari is not present in a particular attire, that attire becomes poison to me; where Kṛṣṇa is not present in the true essence of things, everything becomes a source of suffering for me.
Through the perfect accomplishment of such states of being and so forth, Kṛṣṇa becomes like a lover;
O Mother, through union with such Śrī Kṛṣṇa, I shall become liberated.
And by me, being liberated, the Supreme Lord is eternally served;
one who knows Brahman in this manner attains the Supreme Spouse. (35)
O Mother, through exclusive devotion, the beloved of Kṛṣṇa attains the Supreme Brahman, the manifest Puruṣottama, who is the refuge of devotion. (36)
The earth is always to be understood as the woman, and the Lord who bestows the seed is the husband;
all women are the wives of Kṛṣṇa, the daughters of the earth, and the consorts of Mādhava. (37)
The syllable (akṣara), the incarnations (avatāras), the liberated ones (muktas) and likewise the female liberated ones (muktānikās);
the lords (īśvaras), the gods (surās), Māyā, the principles (tattvas), and likewise consciousness (cetanā). ||38||
He whose body, that of Kṛṣṇa, consists of women—that Kṛṣṇa is the Lord, the soul of all principles, and the master of all forms. (39)
He, the Lord of the City of Brahman, is the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama) in form;
endowed with infinite sovereignty, our Master is directly worthy of our service.
Thus, this knowledge is supreme knowledge, the highest means for liberation;
she who possesses such perfect knowledge is indeed the beloved of Kṛṣṇa. 41.
It should be entirely free from flickering toward anything other than Kṛṣṇa;
the eye should be fixed on Kṛṣṇa, and the skin [should find] its beauty in the Lord of Lakṣmī. 42.
Likewise, O Kṛṣṇā, the hands and feet should be yoked to Mādhavīśvara;
all the sense organs should be yoked to Rameśvara. (43)
The restlessness [of the mind] attached to Kṛṣṇa will become entirely and most firmly fixed, depending on the degree of one's faith and the resulting slackening of effort. (44)
Even though Hari is unchanging, a gradation of devotion may arise in the devotee;
for one who possesses supreme faith in service to the virtuous, that same faith exists toward Hari as well. (45)
It certainly comes to pass, there is no doubt; that divine [state] arises quickly through the repeated hearing of the excellent narrative of the Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa-Saṃhitā. 46.
By listening to them, the arising of devotion and affection occurs;
one becomes as affectionate toward Hari as a doe is toward a deer, and thus becomes truly Nārāyaṇī. 47.
That woman in whom there arises for Hari a deep affection characterized by an inability to endure even momentary separation, she [is one who] [suffers] when separated from her own beloved. (48)
Without Kṛṣṇa she would give up her life; everything becomes poison to her.
Without Kṛṣṇa she becomes distressed and finds no happiness. ||45||
Since all embodied beings are filled with blood, bones, impurities, flesh, and so forth, one who has attained a state of detachment does not find stability anywhere at all. (4.10.50)
Such men are indeed rare; they are not merely obstacles on the path to the highest good, but are givers of wandering in saṃsāra and bestowers of suffering both in this world and the next. (51)
Those men who have insatiable desires, who seize all one's possessions, and who are not beneficial to others, have been experienced through many births; they repeatedly bestow further birth upon one.
Indeed, association with the virtuous alone—Śrī Kṛṣṇa—is the giver of liberation to me; without him, everything is but a puppet. How can I take refuge in a mere puppet? (53)
A woman who is established in the Self is not deluded by the sight of men;
being disciplined in spirit, that divine beloved of Kṛṣṇa is never agitated anywhere.
That Lord of Mādhavī, who is the Self of selves and possesses eternal bliss, is to be attained;
I am the Self, I am of the nature of Brahman, and I am indeed the servant of the Lord of Light. (55)
I am the beloved of that Kṛṣṇa, who is served by countless female companions whose very selves are Brahman; that Kṛṣṇa exists in human form—he is my refuge. (56)
In such a devotee, divine vision increases;
therefore, no desire for the enjoyments of heaven arises in her. (57)
Then, how much more so would there be a thirst for enjoyment regarding worldly bodies?
For such a yoginī, who is eternally chaste, there is supreme bliss. (58)
Illusion (māyā), however, always exists in the form of suffering for one who is not a devotee;
but for the sake of a devotee, O Kṛṣṇa, she indeed bestows nourishment through service. ||59||
She bestows happiness upon the devotee, grants union with Kṛṣṇa, and confers divinity; she indeed grants liberation as well, bestowing the grace of Kṛṣṇa. (4.10.60)
That very Māyā which is indeed considered a binder for those who are not devotees, is regarded as the nourisher of devotion for women who are devotees. (61)
Those who serve Kṛṣṇa through their body, mind, speech, offerings, desires, and so forth— in that state, even the body and other such factors become bestowers of liberation.
Therefore, the female form is the means for attaining Kṛṣṇa’s grace;
thus, the Lord of Mādhavī, being propitiated by the cowherd girls, became the bestower of liberation.
In this manner, I must propitiate this Ramā-Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa,
the soul of all, the imperishable Lord, and the sovereign of the lords of time.
In that state which is the beloved of Kṛṣṇācārya, where no other conceptualization arises—
that non-conceptual state indeed must be realized by the woman.
If a lord were to act among the states of desire like an ordinary man, then even one who is superior would act [like him], and consequently, one even more superior would act [likewise]. ||66||
He may engage in the enjoyment of all sense objects and transcend them;
likewise, he may even engage in those things censured by the whole world, provided he remains under the Lord Mādhava.
Doubt does not arise for one in whom divine nature has been born;
indeed, it is entirely fitting that [divinity] resides in Kṛṣṇa, the doer of all and the cause of all.
She who knows and serves all things as they truly are is the beloved of Hari;
but Hari, like fire and like space, is free from all taint.
Though he is the enjoyer of millions of Śrīs and the lord of millions of Muktānikās, he should always be understood as the Lord of Rādhā’s wisdom-Śrī within his own abode. (4.10.70)
In that divine abode of the Blessed One, which is Brahman, immortal and imperishable, there I must reach my beloved, dear husband, Kṛṣṇa. (71)
May such wisdom as this—valid and free from conceptual construction—always abide in Śrī Kṛṣṇa, my lord, the beloved of the illustrious Mati. (72)
Thus, the disciples, enriched by the certainty of non-conceptualization, have reached Hari;
having accomplished their purpose and being fearless, they are considered followers of Kṛṣṇa and Nārāyaṇa. (73)
Indeed, from a guru endowed with the perfections of Kṛṣṇa, the accomplishment of one's own desired goals arises;
therefore, the guru who abides as Nārāyaṇa is to be served. (74)
By the power of the guru, even the disciple attains superiority over the junior;
she whose state is free from conceptual construction has directly realized the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa. (75)
She is not drawn away by other waves that are empty of Kṛṣṇa;
for she has taken refuge in the Blessed Lord and her mind is never directed toward anyone else.
She has reached the perfection of illusion (māyā) and is beloved by Brahmā; of this there is no doubt.
When her body is drawn forth into Kṛṣṇa, she becomes Puruṣottamī. 77.
Having become the wife of Kṛṣṇa in the bliss of Kṛṣṇa, she fulfills her great desires;
having attained the service of Kṛṣṇa, she rejoices in the beloved of Kṛṣṇa. (78)
Thus, O Mother, I worship Kṛṣṇa, the Great Nārāyaṇa;
having become His maidservant in the form of a woman, I serve the Lord, the Beloved of Śrī. 79.
I have a great distaste for any object devoid of Kṛṣṇa;
therefore, my pleasure always lies in renouncing that which is illusory.
I have a natural affection for the virtuous and a love for Hari;
I possess a longing for Śrī Kṛṣṇa, my beloved and the Lord of all. (81)
Lord Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa is indeed the eternal embodiment of auspiciousness;
he is the Supreme Lord, the source of all incarnations.
"Whether within, without, or in between, this beloved one is seen by me—divine, an abode of divine qualities, possessing a form, and adorned with divine ornaments. (83)
He is beloved by rows of pearls reaching the millions, filled with supreme splendor, and endowed with divine loveliness, sweetness, brilliance, and coolness. ||84||
Worshipped with divine sandalwood paste, flowers, and other offerings by the powers of Brahmā, he gazed at me with side-long glances out of great affection, causing me joy. (85)
And at every moment this Lord Hari is seen as ever-new;
therein, O Mother, my devotion is always desireless and unwavering. (86)
My affection for Hari is like that for a son, wealth, a wife, or a beloved;
likewise, my love for the virtuous is also natural toward Hari. (87)
At the time of their glorification, my mind runs toward them—toward Śrī Kṛṣṇa, toward Vallabhācārya, and toward the Lord who is the beloved of the gopīs. (88)
O Tārābhā, O you who shine like lightning, O you with the luster of fire, O you who resemble the submarine fire, O you who possess great splendor—my husband is within my own heart! 89.
He remains the bestower of bliss upon me, raining down the bliss of Brahman;
he remains the giver of all bliss within me through eternal identity. 4.10.90
With my nature free from obscuration, I behold my Lord within me;
I behold Him who bestows great bliss, pure, perfect, and supreme to me. 9.1
O Mother, such as I am, there exists no passion born of illusion;
for one who abides in the state beyond qualities, how indeed could there be any staining by qualities? (92)
Whence, then, could there be latent impressions here, and whence the storehouse of karma? Whence the physical sheaths, and whence attachment to things that are perishable? (93)
Whence can there be malice toward devotees, whence the perception of faults in the virtuous?
Whence the touch of egoism and possessiveness, and whence the defilement of dualism and the like? (94)
O Mother, while you, the sovereign of the virtuous, are the lord, whence can there be pride—the heap of all defects—when everything has become divine through union with the Beloved of Rādhā? 95.
I possess a body, and my physical self is a devoted servant;
[so too am I] for these other liberated wives of Kṛṣṇa who are like her. (96)
O Mother, I become the mother of leaves, grey with dust, pollen, and the like; I am a servant, a slave, one whose nature is that of a messenger, and even a wretched handmaid. (97)
Thus, the intellect of one who drinks in such majesty shall never waver from Kṛṣṇa;
her status as a servant does not cause her defilement, for she knows the compassion of Hari. 98.
There is never any falling away for her from servitude to Kṛṣṇa, the Beloved;
she is that supreme power of Brahmā, the beloved of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa. 99.
Out of fear of her the wind blows; out of fear of her the sun also shines;
out of fear of her the clouds always take refuge in the sky according to the seasons.
Out of fear of him, Dhruva remains steadfast at the shore of the ocean;
likewise, the world-protectors, death, time, and illusion remain so out of fear of him.
They proceed in their respective duties, each according to its proper application;
such a great power arises, which is rooted in Hari. 102.
I have attained Anādi-Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the son of the cowherd Nanda, the beginningless Beloved, the Lord of Śrī, who is cherished by the beloved of Śrī.
A woman who conducts herself in such a manner shall obtain that husband as her lord;
O mother, may you obtain that beloved Kṛṣṇa, who is served by Śrī.
Having spoken thus, that maiden, a young yoginī, became silent;
Sureśvarī also held [the words] in her heart, O Badarīśvarī.

Thus ends the tenth chapter, titled "The Description of how the Attainment, Abiding, and Other States of the Blessed Lord were Explained by Bālayoginī to Sureśvarī," within the *Bālayoginīgītā* in the fourth section, the *Tiṣyasantāna*, of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said:
O beloved of Badarī, listen; then the goddess Sureśvarī asked about the nature of the service to be rendered to the maiden, which I shall now tell you. || 1 ||
All service consisting of material gifts is inferior; the gift of oneself is far greater.
Indeed, the gift of happiness, the gift of one's mind, and the gift of one's intellect should be offered to the wielder of the Śārṅga bow.
The gift of the mind, the gift of honor, the offering of all the senses, the gift of life, the gift of the body, and servitude—these constitute the gift of everything. || 3 ||
O Mother, she who is dear to Brahmā is considered a maidservant;
such a supreme maidservant as this, whether a human or even an immortal, [is honored]. 4.
No one is capable of diverting him from the path of Kṛṣṇa’s beloved;
furthermore, there is not even the slightest fear of such a maidservant.
Just as she was a maidservant of the God of gods, the Lord of Śrī, the Lord of the Lotus, so too was this young female yogi a maidservant of the wise, endowed with wisdom.
Blessed is she who attains union with the virtuous and union with Hari; this young yoginī serves the beloved youth Kṛṣṇa.
The task shall be accomplished. O Mother, there is servitude to you within the sky of consciousness;
that which is being experienced here unfolds within the imperishable state.
This very nature of the Supreme Self is likewise established by itself;
both of these forms lead to the highest good, as do all other infinite forms that exist.
They were of the nature of truth, consciousness, and bliss, filled with loveliness,
endowed with divine sovereignty, and adorned with every ornament.
Indeed, they possess forms of infinite beauty and infinite splendor;
they are endowed with many powers and portions, and they are the internal controllers of all. || 1.1 ||
The supreme bliss of beholding the primordial Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa exists indeed for Rādhā, who possesses infinite crores of fortunes and the splendor of Lakṣmī. (12)
For the sake of his task, the Lord Mādhava assumes many forms;
having employed them as required, he causes them to vanish.

The embodied soul is perceived as consisting of the senses, the gods, and the objects of the senses—by those who are illusory, and not by those who are divine and have attained the state of service. || 14 ||
For that pastime of Nārāyaṇa exists indeed by the will of his illusory power (māyā);
it is entirely auspicious in nature and bestows the divine abode. 15.
That divine meditation upon those in human form is the awakening to the state of a servant;
among those who are truly human, that divine meditation is the supreme practice.

In every respect, one should act like Kṛṣṇa, realizing that one is a servant of Kṛṣṇa; and even among women, including those who are virtuous, that divine and supreme contemplation should be practiced.
O Mother, she should always be made aware of her state as a servant;
furthermore, by that [state] which is highest of all, she shall thereafter attain the status of being beloved by Brahmā.
In this way, through such cultivation, the perfection of service shines forth;
having thus accomplished it, one attains the supreme beloved Kṛṣṇa, and not otherwise. (19)
O Kṛṣṇa, he indeed bestows divine senses upon the maidservant;
through union with Kṛṣṇa, a divine fragrance arises within her body. (4.11.20)
Through the yoga of Kṛṣṇa, there shall be constant freedom from obscuration;
through the yoga of Kṛṣṇa, there shall be a state of being filled with bliss day and night. ||21||
O Mother, through union with Kṛṣṇa, all objects become supreme like Kṛṣṇa himself; they arise for the sake of peace, being likewise free from harm and imperishable. 22.
Above the bliss of the Lord of innumerable creations is the imperishable bliss;
beyond that is the supreme bliss of Kṛṣṇa, the Beloved, which possesses infinite qualities. (23)
O Mother, Brahmā and the other lords become like beggars in his presence in every respect; one should hold that Kṛṣṇa within one's heart. 24.
In the treasure-trove of Pūrṇānanda alone is all happiness fully contained;
such a state is not far off, therefore one should offer oneself to Kṛṣṇa.
Thus, O Mother, by your grace I have become overwhelmed with abundant bliss through the glorious form of Kṛṣṇa; and here I shall devote myself to your service.
Through the very experience of identity, Kṛṣṇakānta is enjoyed;
but she who has attained the state of being devoid of qualities (nirguṇya) serves as a maidservant. ||27||
She obtains that very Lord, the beloved of Kṛṣṇa, who is accompanied by her own [consort], the bestower of great bliss and the provider of satisfaction in all enjoyments. (28)
Even if slight, that intellect and action whose object is the beloved Kṛṣṇa is divine, known as the power of Brahman, and it showers down all perfections. (29)
Through her connection with Kṛṣṇa, she is devoid of material qualities and is designated as divine, imperishable, and immutable;
[she is the source of] seeing, touching, smelling, tasting, hearing, and so forth.
O Mother, for a maidservant, sleeping, sporting, serving, and embracing should always be performed solely for Lord Hari, Kṛṣṇa, and nothing else. (31)
The body and senses must never be directed elsewhere;
for if they are left unguarded, they will surely cause the yoginī to fall through the power of Kṛṣṇa.
"Hare Kṛṣṇa! O Beloved of Kṛṣṇa, O Mādhava! Protect me, Your maidservant who serves Kṛṣṇa; and let her pray to the Supreme Lord for others. (33)
Thus entreated, Kṛṣṇakānta protects his maidservant;
there is no one like Kṛṣṇasadvara in the entire universe.
The Lord who shines here within His own imperishable Brahman, served by divine powers and divine attendants, is present there. ||35||
The Supreme Person is served with devotion by Rādhā, Ramā, and others;
He is entreated by the lords of the cosmic eggs to enter the egg. (36)
Out of compassion, that Bālakṛṣṇa manifests himself there indeed; he performs activities identical with those of gods, humans, animals, and so forth. ||37||
The Supreme Lord bestows a lifespan corresponding to the age, as well as strength, capability, and even the physical body, according to that particular age. (38)
Both virtues and faults are seen as truly divine in Hari;
he conducts himself on earth in such a way that it may be for the benefit of human beings. (39)
Becoming thus, he indeed brings about a consequence of his own kind;
having withdrawn his radiance, he proceeds as a human being. (4.11.40)
In that divine realm, human beings do not find excessive pleasure, for the worlds cannot endure such splendors and thus fail to attain a state of mental composure.
O Mother, by the power of his purpose, he sometimes assumes great sovereignty;
he displays it to his devotees and then again makes it dissolve away.
O Mother, He is indeed the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa Ārya, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama), the son of Gopāla, and the sustainer of all incarnations. 43.
In its support, there shall be a row of devotees who are always free from fear from any quarter,
just as a single essential form might consist of the essence of sugar-candy.
Likewise, O Mother, I now possess identity with the Supreme Brahman, the auspicious Consort, the abode of Being-Consciousness-Bliss, who is the single Reality. (45)
Just as fire, having entered an iron ball, is perceived [as the ball], yet the iron ball itself is not perceived [as distinct from the fire], so it is with the Lord within me, O Mother. 46.
Behold, O Lord of All! I am indeed not within the range of vision;
all this has that as its essence, and I am pervaded by the Great Self. 47.
Where there is nothing to be abandoned by Kṛṣṇa, who is consciousness and bliss—she who knows this thus is to be known as the supreme Brāhmī, the most excellent among those who know Brahman. 48.
Having attained the state of non-conceptuality, she whose wisdom is established is utterly fearless;
having reached the state of absolute certainty, she has entered into cessation within Kṛṣṇa.
Having conceived a firm and continuous bond of affection for Hari in his human form, that friend is considered to be ever devoted, consisting of love, and free from doubt. 4.11.50.
She whose mind is firmly fixed on Kṛṣṇa is a daughter of Kṛṣṇa; she has accomplished her liberation.
One should always fight against conceptual constructions with a desire that is free from conceptual construction. (51)
Even one who does not fight is dragged away by the sense-objects and may even fall;
likewise, though he has known the Lord of all, he may even abandon the Lord of lords.
She would be a traitor toward her husband Kṛṣṇa, her beloved lord and master;
indeed, Kṛṣṇa is never pleased with one who commits such treachery.
If she regards time, karma, inherent nature, or illusion as the cause, while excluding Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, she becomes an offender against Hari. (54)
The liberated souls reside in Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa; Brahman resides in Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa;
