indeed, countless incarnations exist within Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa. 55.
All powers and austerities, as well as sovereign glories, sacrifices, and wonders, reside in Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa; [all] reside in Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa. (56)
The gods, the worlds, and the states of existence reside in Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa;
indeed, all creations reside in Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa. (57)

She who knows the supreme reality, the beloved and charming one, and who is an ocean of knowledge—she is the knower, the servant of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, she is the embodiment of Brahman, and she is the most excellent among those who know Brahman. 58.
When devotion is of such a kind, there arises the grace of Kṛṣṇa;
for indeed, when it has attained an excess of affection, all virtues dwell therein.
A devotee endowed with knowledge of the Lord’s majesty becomes single-mindedly devoted to the Master;
through the practice of serving the virtuous, devotion to Kṛṣṇa arises. (4.11.60)
The virtuous, who are the very embodiment of Kṛṣṇa, should be served with mind, speech, and body;
indeed, by means of the practice of dharma consisting of service.
Everything that was to be done here has been accomplished; nothing remains to be performed.
Through union with the virtuous, the Blessed One shines forth both externally and internally. (62)
Like a moth, Kṛṣṇa himself becomes absorbed in her activity;
O Mother, for by that means she attains the supreme bliss of Hari.
The Māyā of Hari, in the form of affection, brings only happiness to that virtuous woman who is held within the heart and the imperishable self, which are pure and radiant.
When the Lord, who is the beloved, becomes directly manifest, she becomes absorbed in rasa;
embracing her beloved, she rejoices in the bliss of Brahman. (65)
She immerses herself in the supreme Brahman, the Lord, who is the great bliss beyond all qualities;
she also drinks the nectar of love within that great bliss.
Having attained the Lord who transcends Māyā, she herself becomes one who transcends Māyā;
fixed upon Hari, she goes to Hari, and Hari indeed liberates her.
Thus, for one who has taken refuge in Kṛṣṇa, the state of being a lotus arises;
whatever desired happiness she may have, he rains down all of it.
Indeed, for one who has surrendered, surrender arises mutually between Hari and her;
and there likewise arises mutual single-minded devotion between the devotee and Acyuta. (69)
Indeed, for such a devotee, O Mother, all actions toward both [the teacher and the deity] become equal to those of the Satya Yuga. (4.11.70)
All phenomena proceed from volitions accumulated through truth;
indeed, all mental creations therein bestow the desired results.
When their purpose is accomplished through union with Kṛṣṇa, they become like Kṛṣṇa himself;
moreover, the compassionate Lord Kṛṣṇa bestows upon them even His own magnanimity.
"I must bring about the highest welfare for all those possessing bodies—men, women, and eunuchs alike—having thus exercised supreme compassion. (73)
The bestower of yoga indeed uplifts animals, trees, and birds;
he even uplifts enemies, as well as Rākṣasas and Daityas.
He even rescues groups of women situated in evil by means of enjoyment;
for indeed, even the wicked, having attained [his] company, become liberated as divine beings. (75)
Through the swift penetration of Kṛṣṇa, all principles quickly attain the state of Brahman, and even Māyā attains the nature of the Imperishable.
The function of the eye, which consists of gross forms and is composed of light in the form of rays, though material in nature,
attains the state of Brahman when fixed upon Hari.
Therefore, having become devoid of qualities (nirguṇā), she becomes the illuminator of Brahman;
she takes the form of Kṛṣṇa, overflowing with the joy of the bliss of great ecstasy.
She merges into that divine Kṛṣṇa, and her self experiences that bliss;
having thus become the very form of Kṛṣṇa, she partakes in the joy of Kṛṣṇa. (79)
O Mother, the great devotee attains happiness from Kṛṣṇa;
he beholds the auspicious vision of Kṛṣṇa, obtained through his divine eyes in meditative absorption.
Even that bliss which lasts for but a moment may be as if it were performed for a thousand years—bliss consisting of the undivided, attributeless, and perfect bliss of Brahman. (81)
Through devotion, the eternal [Lord] is experienced within various states—whether in the Lord Kṛṣṇa in human form, or in a king, or in one who has assumed the form of a saintly person. ||82||
Whether that bliss is experienced while remaining within or in a divine form, may the virtuous ones, who are abodes of compassion, meet with him daily. (83)
Such happiness is attained even through service characterized by affection;
however, the supreme, divine happiness of the Guru’s form is attained through [devotional] service alone. //84//
Betrayal of the guru, betrayal of the virtuous, and betrayal of Kṛṣṇa bring about destruction;
service to the guru, service to the virtuous, and service to Kṛṣṇa bestow the Imperishable. (85)
One who commits an act of malice may become a worm, an insect, a stone, a piece of wood, a mountain, or a worldly being;
since there is no yoga for the sake of liberation in such states, one should therefore avoid malice.
One should also avoid pride in the presence of Kṛṣṇa before his devotees;
for pride is indeed the cause of attaining the status of a great asura. (87)
The state of being an asura arises from the practice of hatred for the sake of hell;
by that, one is led entirely onto the path to hell. (88)
But those who are conceited repeatedly impute faults to Hari, the virtuous one, for the sake of proclaiming their own superiority; consequently, they go to the lowest state.
Indeed, virtuous persons (sādhus) should be served for the sake of destroying pride, hatred, and other such afflictions;
those sādhus who are non-different from Kṛṣṇa purify even those who are defiled. 4.11.90.
One should cultivate supreme affection for the virtuous, so that no fault may arise;
toward one who is affectionate, no fault ever occurs, and one will always perceive their virtues. (9.1)
By perceiving the virtues of the virtuous alone, one perceives the virtues of Kṛṣṇa;
through that, there is the direct vision of the Self as Brahman and the direct vision of Hari himself.
She always experiences a state of union with Hari;
for this friend, there is no deficiency resulting from her acquisition of a male friend as a husband. (93)
That female companion attains Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, who abides in the Imperishable and possesses a radiance equal to infinite millions of suns, moons, fires, and lightning bolts. 94.
That female companion obtains the beloved Bālakṛṣṇa, who stands upon the earth, possessed of great heroism, great beauty, and filled with great power. (95)
That dear friend obtains a great ocean of bliss;
she receives from the beloved Kṛṣṇa all the seeds of liberation.
Divinely intoxicated, she exists in a state of self-satisfaction;
yet for those who behold her, and even for those who hear her words, [there is no such satisfaction]. 97.
Liberation occurs in the abode of the divine Imperishable, for they go indeed to that Imperishable;
O Mother, thus [worship] Bālakṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, as your husband. 98.
I have attained the heart of all; I am in every way one who has accomplished her purpose.
No worldly existence is worthy of my regard except for Kṛṣṇa. 99.
Any woman like me who worships Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of Śrī, the venerable Badarīśvara,
shall become a devoted and liberated soul.
Having spoken thus, that young yoginī paused for a moment;
O beloved of Badrī, she then spoke again to her mother: "I shall say this. (101)

Thus ends the eleventh chapter, titled "The Description of Attaining the Nature of Nārāyaṇī through Service," within the *Bālayoginīgītā* of the fourth section, the *Tiṣyasantāna*, in the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said:
O Pārvatī, beloved of Badarī, and O young Yoginī, listen; she told her mother about the righteous conduct of virtuous women.

She who, being virtuous, dwells having obtained the Lord of Śrī as her husband is called a bride; indeed, she whose nature is devoted to Kṛṣṇa is considered one who has the disposition to offer her all possessions.
Having unified her own body, which is as lovely as Kṛṣṇa, as well as all her senses with her internal organs, she becomes eternally non-different from Him. (3)
Just as a clod of earth is constantly drawn toward a magnet,
so too does she become immersed and sink deeply into meditative absorption (samādhi).
There, that ascetic woman, perfected in yoga and whose true nature is non-different from Kṛṣṇa, beholds the beloved Kṛṣṇa pervaded by the radiance of ten million suns.
Assuming many forms, the divine young yoginī is born;
she hears the sounds of the abodes and beholds the cosmic eggs.
Thus, she is always born endowed with innate and infinite sovereignty;
wherever she desires by her own will to grant her vision, there she appears.
In each and every place she manifests like Kṛṣṇa;
as is Kṛṣṇa, so is the daughter of Kṛṣṇa—the supreme, all-pervading one who comes into being.
By union with her, even a woman who is an unworthy vessel and indifferent to Kṛṣṇa becomes instantly established in samādhi through the power of her compassion.
One is liberated immediately by serving the women of Kṛṣṇa;
even one devoted to serving virtuous women is released from great sin.
Extremely meritorious and worthy of being known as an awakening, she is indeed a virtuous woman in the form of a sacred ford;
having attained union with a virtuous man, that virtuous woman becomes a true *satī*.
By divine destiny, the virtuous Muktānikā became divine;
for a noble woman, even when she becomes a wicked wife, her divinity is the cause of her grace.
In this world, virtuous people should always be propitiated through service;
they should always be pleased with all kinds of gifts, for they are the bestowers of liberation.
For the intoxication of the virtuous consists of Kṛṣṇa, as well as the intoxication of the affection of devotion;
indeed, through that intoxication, the virtuous intoxicate the noble woman who has taken refuge in them.
With their hearts solely intent on meditation upon Kṛṣṇa, they are devoted to Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa;
they cause others to dwell in Kṛṣṇa and make them followers of Kṛṣṇa in every way.
The virtuous do not desire any happiness other than that which arises from Kṛṣṇa, the creator of all; O Mother, even for me, the happiness of Kṛṣṇa is what is pleasing day after day.
Everything else appears like hell, a terrible suffering where there is no one of radiant splendor; for in such a place, suffering is indeed illusory.
Wherever Lord Mādhava resides, there indeed is eternal bliss;
O Mother, that mastery over the senses is found in Kṛṣṇa, wherein all the senses find their true abiding. (18)
One who has conquered the senses should serve Kṛṣṇa as much as desired;
indeed, her days pass away with manifold devotion to Kṛṣṇa. (19)
Devoted to the dharma of renunciation and intent upon the goal of Kṛṣṇa, that woman remains free from attachment; she is not bound, for there is nothing apart from Hari.

By Hari’s command, although she was engaged in ritual action, she remained devoid of qualities (nirguṇā) and free from transformation; though appearing inert in outward form, she possessed perfect wisdom within. ||21||
For she is indeed intent upon the activities related to Kṛṣṇa and His devotees;
she possesses the nature of renunciation, is endowed with devotion, and leads to liberation. (22)
Without Kṛṣṇa, every ritual action leads to a downward state;
however, that which renounces everything for the sake of Kṛṣṇa is indeed the supreme [action]. (23)
For the virtuous, an action performed for the sake of Kṛṣṇa while engaged in worldly activity, and which makes one a recipient of Hari’s grace, does not bestow bondage. 24.
The beloved Lord is the Blessed Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Hari; he is the husband of Rādhā, Prajñā, Pāśavatī, Badrī, Lakṣmī, and Ramā. (25)
And in Akṣara, Goloka, Vaikuṇṭha, and Badarīvana, the Lord Śrī Mahārāja Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa resides. ||26||
He alone is the agent of the creation, maintenance, and dissolution of infinite millions of cosmic eggs;
he assumes forms such as Vāsudeva and bears the essential nature of Keśava and others.
Manifest in human form, possessing the power of ten million billion lotuses,
Bālakṛṣṇa indeed shines resplendent in the sacred field at Kuṅkumavāpī.
In Badarī, that very Śrī Nara-Nārāyaṇa also shines forth;
his power is the virtuous Śīlā, who is indeed Bālayoginī herself. (29)
"O Mother, know that her virtues are my own virtues, always auspicious;
for the divine sports of the Blessed One in human form are indeed worthy of being heard and grant liberation. (4.12.30)

Indeed, those who have attained Kṛṣṇa—even if they were devoid of spiritual qualities—did so through some state such as desire or anger, or through fear and the like, or through affection, or through a sense of self-interest. (3.1)
The birth, activities, and other deeds of the Lord, the Consort of Śrī, are devoid of the material qualities (nirguṇa);
even the touch of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa is devoid of the material qualities.
Having realized that Nārāyaṇa is devoid of attributes, one goes to the imperishable state;
[so too do] the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa, which have attained divinity through those devoted to Kṛṣṇa who have been drawn [to Him]. 33.

They should be established for the purpose of remembrance—those which do not cause affliction to embodied beings—and indeed for the purpose of being seen by the worlds and for the manifestation [of grace] for those possessed of devotion. (34)

For the destruction of the sins of sinners, for the sake of meditation by those who are affectionate, and likewise for the purpose of remembering the sense of "this-ness" [of the Lord], the pastimes of Hari should be performed. (35)
One should compose dramas and other works that increase devotion to Kṛṣṇa;
in whatever way possible, devotion to Kṛṣṇa shall arise among living beings. (36)
For the sake of awakening reverence for the Guru, one should maintain a beautiful appearance;
likewise, even in relation to Hari, one should adopt a demeanor that inspires obedience.
In this way, indeed, there shall be liberation for those whose minds are fixed on Śrī Kṛṣṇa;
likewise, there shall be the fulfillment of the purpose of human bodies upon this earth, as well as that of women. (38)
It is said that by beholding the divine play (līlā) of Kṛṣṇa, spiritual welfare arises; for those who possess devotion to him are his devotees, and they are indeed the bringers of welfare. (39)
People on earth should perform divine and wondrous pastimes for them, so that the devotion of those seeking liberation may increase especially.
So that through discernment there may arise freedom from desire for the body and so forth, and so that one's own self may become attached to the one Lord of Fortune, who is the essence itself. (41)
So that there may be service to Hari, whose nature is truth, consciousness, and bliss, and so that renunciation, devotion, and divinity may always arise; 42.
Thus, the deeds of Kṛṣṇa should be emulated and not otherwise, because through seeing, touching, and internalizing them, embodied beings may attain liberation. (43)
Having become one with Brahman and possessing divine limbs, they do not return to rebirth;
yet, by the will of Hari, they may manifest in the world independently.
But their objects of experience become divine and consist of the Blessed One;
they proceed having utterly abandoned the cultivation of the three bodies. 45.
They meditate upon Hari as their own husband, whose nature is existence, consciousness, and bliss;
indeed, by the power of Hari, death ceases for them and they abide in peace.
Therefore, objects of the senses are not able to enter there;
but those who come [there], O Blessed One, become divine and identical with me. ||47||
And for Kṛṣṇa, she becomes divine, devoted to the service of the virtuous;
she always attains a state of stability known as tranquility with the Lord of Śrī.
Indeed, they take exceeding pleasure in her who is discerning and devoted as a maidservant. 48.
Indeed, because she pleases the virtuous through her excellence, no calamities befall her;
and knowing her own divine nature, that Narayani rejoices. (49)
O Mother, devotion to the Self and likewise devotion to Kṛṣṇa are the two wings by which embodied beings, endowed with consciousness, may travel through the sky of the Intellect. (4.12.50)
Consciousness and affection—these two lead one toward the Supreme Lord;
affection leads to the dream state and deep sleep, while [discrimination] joins one to Kṛṣṇa in the fourth state (turyā). ||51||
O Mother, without devotion to her husband, Kṛṣṇa does not attach himself;
indeed, without service, Kṛṣṇa does not take a maidservant onto his chest.
But servitude is in every way the carrying out of orders for one's own sake;
whereas devotion to the husband (pātivratya) is for the sake of Kṛṣṇa, devoid of self-interest. ||53||
The highest form of service is the devotion of a wife, which consists of total self-surrender for the sake of her husband;
this very state of dependence is what constitutes the bond of a householder’s life, just like that of a wife. (54)
As long as the mind is immersed [in the world], service proceeds out of affection;
if the mind is separated from servitude, the state of being a servant vanishes. (55)
Therefore, for a woman, the state of being a wife and devotion to her husband are praised;
the vow of fidelity to one's lord is praised as the foremost of all spiritual means. (56)
To attain the grace of Hari and to attain Hari himself, that woman by whom an inner [offering] is given to the Lord of Lakṣmī [attains her goal]. 57.
The beloved Hari was indeed attained, accomplished, and made one's own; subsequently, the internal gift secured his status as lord in every respect. (58)
O Mother, lordship over Kṛṣṇa is difficult for ordinary women to attain;
but the status of being His mistress is even more impossible for one who lacks merit. (59)
The state of being Māṇikī, the state of being Rādhā, the state of being Lakṣmī, and the state of being Badarī—
these exist in Akṣara, in Goloka, in Vaikuṇṭha, and in the Badarī forest.
Through great affection and supreme compassion for Kṛṣṇa,
devotion is earned by embodied beings even toward the God who is beyond their perception.
Likewise, when a woman acts toward the beloved Lord Hari as toward her own Guru, all her eternal goals, beginning with the divine, will indeed be accomplished. (62)

Through association with the virtuous, through association with Hari, and again and again through association with the guru, everything that is to be attained is obtained: the supreme state and the fulfillment of one's purpose.
Affection for Kṛṣṇa, when cultivated, is like honey; it bestows liberation.
Through union with Kṛṣṇa, even for a passionate woman, Brahman as pure existence shines forth.
The self attains the state of Brahman; no desire remains.
Through the power of practice, one reaches the state of Brahman within Kṛṣṇa, who is Brahman. (65)
But for his wife, who had become one with Brahman, there arose daily toward Kṛṣṇa and the sons of Kṛṣṇa a flow of affection, friendship, and joy.
Śrī Lakṣmī, whose mind is drawn by the qualities of Hari; Mādhavī, the beloved; Māṇikyā; Rādhikā; and Badrī—all of them bring satisfaction to Hari. (67)
Through the grace of Hari, the ocean of compassion, they always became like female deer;
and by serving Hari, the best of beings, they forever became like Nārāyaṇīs.
Nothing other than Kṛṣṇa is pleasing to them, nor does anything else appear fearful;
everything proceeds under the control of all these Nārāyaṇīs.
But those women who, devoted to the beloved of Kṛṣṇa, attained tranquility, reached the supreme goal through the firmness of their union with Kṛṣṇa. (4.12.70)
Even ordinary women go to that supreme, imperishable abode which fulfills all desires;
how much more so those who are beautiful as maidservants and the like?
Within the body, the Supreme Person, the Lord of Śrī, dwells as the Self within the self;
yet, seeing the supreme devotion of His devotee, He manifests externally.
He bestows supreme bliss arising from his own union;
he delights and causes delight, embracing his very own form. 73.
Service pervaded by the greatness of affection is never thwarted by obstacles;
how could even firm devotion to one's husband ever overcome that which is eternally dependent [on such affection]? (74)

From the remembrance of his name, from the chanting of his praise, from the recollection of him, from bowing down to him, from association with him, from touching him, and from marking oneself with his sign; ||75||
By bearing a portion of him, by dwelling in his bed, by following in his lineage,
by seeing him, and by sporting with him, even a dog becomes like a performer of the Soma sacrifice.
Even a courtesan is counted among those liberated through association with him;
how much more so a wife who is a servant and handmaid through her devotion to her husband? (77)
Oh, how great is the power of the Name, O Kṛṣṇa, which draws away even the dog-eaters!
Oh, how insignificant are penances, sacrifices, holy places, and vows! (78)
The names of Kṛṣṇakānta alone fulfill all purposes in every respect;
through the name of Hari, the Lord of All, fearlessness arises. (79)
For embodied beings who cry out "Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa! in fear, their terror ceases;
indeed, through service at the soles of His feet, they enter that state which is free from all fear.
Through service to the great, O Mother, even a moment is obtained for entering into Kṛṣṇa; compared to those with desires, there is greater happiness for one who is free from desire. 81.
For the sake of Kṛṣṇa, even though she possesses desire, she is proclaimed to be free from desire;
this virtuous woman, devoted to no other, does not long for anything other than Kṛṣṇa. (82)
For the sake of the highest good, she attained Hari; therefore, Hari is pleased with her.
Śrī Hari quickly becomes gracious toward one who seeks the highest good with pure devotion. 83.
When Kṛṣṇa is directly propitiated, all desires are fulfilled;
Kṛṣṇa alone bestows happiness upon his own devotees, not others. (84)
Therefore, one should always maintain the thought of oneself in Kṛṣṇa and in all His followers;
one should seek His side in every way, just as one would firmly protect one's own self. (85)
The protector at one's side must endure insults and the like, or even death;
therefore, one should show them special affection, regarding them as more important than one's own body. (86)
O Mother, one should never perceive their non-existence;
for a devotee such as this, there is no fear arising from Yama or others. (87)
Indeed, even Mahākāla and the other [deities] are not able to overcome her;
therefore, one’s mind should be fixed upon Kṛṣṇa like a diamond-stake set in ground of diamond. (88)
Thus, while the body exists as a dwelling place, that friendship which one has for Kṛṣṇa, for those who belong to Kṛṣṇa, and for Kṛṣṇa’s mind, is what motivates the Imperishable One. 89.
There is a separation from the devotees of Kṛṣṇa, and therein lies a very great obstacle; living without affection leads to being cast far away from the Divine Splendor. (4.12.90)
Knowledge of the self, knowledge of Hari, and the knowledge of the devotees—these three gateways alone exist for entry into the abode of Hari. (9.1)
The saintly and virtuous always remain eager within the three types of knowledge; affection, service, and devotion—these three grant entry into the inner state.

The virtuous and chaste women, having attained these three—total self-surrender, devotion to their husband, and trust—indeed go to the abode of Kṛṣṇa; for these three constitute the bed [of union]. (93)
The virtuous and saintly women go to the bed of Śrī Hari by means of these three;
having reached that bed, they indeed experience the singular flavor of identity with Him.
Through direct experience, they perceive Him directly as the essence of existence; absorbed in Him, they experience the beloved Kṛṣṇa, the great bliss. 95.
What can saṃsāra do to devotees of this kind?
Even all their actions arising from the body become divine. 96.
The universe goes to destruction, but the devotees do not meet their end;
such divine devotees rejoice in the imperishable abode.
Vṛndāvana is eternally divine, and the grove of Tulasī is divine;
likewise, Badarīvana is divine, as is the divine Kuṅkumavāpikā.
Divine is that city of Sāketa; divine indeed is the Rāsa-maṇḍapa;
divine are the gopīs, the wives of Brahmā, who are eternally the beloveds of Hari. 99.
They are divine in the imperishable world, and they exist here as well, inseparable from it;
beloved of Brahman, they are eternally divine, possessing divinity through their divine splendor.
Kṛṣṇa is divine, and His abode is likewise divine, all-pervading, and present here as well;
therein are whatever servants, dwellings, enjoyments, and manifestations there may be. || 10.1 ||
Therefore, O Mother, she is truly divine; this young yoginī is divine.
You are eternally divine; do not conceive of yourself as material.
Embodied beings who have attained refuge in Śrī Kṛṣṇa become divine;
they indeed become one with Brahman and even attain the status of His companions. 103.
The female servants of Kṛṣṇa attain the state of Nārāyaṇī and the state of Śakti;
the male servants of Kṛṣṇa attain the state of Viṣṇu and the state of Nara.
"Thus, O Mother, this yoga of Śrī Kṛṣṇa has been told to you by me.
Having spoken thus, O Badrī, that young female yoginī indeed became silent.

Thus ends the twelfth chapter, titled "The Description of Women Possessing the Qualities of Great Bhāgavatas and Other Virtues," within the *Bālayoginīgītā* of the fourth section, the *Tiṣyasantāna*, in the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nara-Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Goddess beloved of Badarī; then that young yoginī spoke again to her mother concerning the auspicious bulls of youthful yoga.
O Mother, infancy is indeed the primordial state for all embodied beings here;
therein there is neither desire, nor anger, nor self-interest, nor even passion.
Day by day, clarity increased in the boy; he did not perceive faults in himself, nor in the internal organ, nor in the senses, nor in the body, nor even in the subtle elements.
Like a clear mirror, childhood must always be protected by one seeking liberation;
she whose youth is not touched is the ever-constant *bālayoginī*.
Desire is the mode of conduct in youth; it causes shame and acts such as theft. It brings about many misfortunes and increases the mountain of latent impressions (*vāsanā*). (46)
Indeed, in youth, all modifications, inherent natures, actions, and likewise deeds of a different kind proceed as mere restless impulses.
Indeed, all those very faults never arise at any time for her who,
having taken refuge in Śrī Kṛṣṇa as her beloved, is a young yoginī.
Austerity, righteousness, dispassion, as well as observance and restraint,
are the causes for the conquest of the senses and also for the conquest of the mind.
Childhood, which is innate like the yoga of a child, brings about total victory;
indeed, the yoga of Bālakṛṣṇa bestows mastery over all the senses.
Friendship with the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa brings happiness and effects victory over Māyā, Time, and the rest; what need is there to count one's religious merits? 4.13.10.
O Mother, absolute great power shall always reside in Kṛṣṇa;
through love for Kṛṣṇa and through love for the descendants of Kṛṣṇa, supreme peace shall arise. (11)
Indeed, for a lowly devotee, peace comes through affection like that of a servant;
however, for one possessing devotion to Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, peace is indeed eternal.
One should worship the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa by perceiving his qualities in this way: as one's teacher when he is venerable, and as a friend when he is equal to oneself. || 13 ||
Wandering here and there, bound by the fetters of karma,
the individual soul sometimes becomes a woman, sometimes a eunuch, and even sometimes a man.
Whether independent or dependent, whether suffering or happy, in some place—be it in a forest, a wilderness, a city, a house, outside, or even on a battlefield—[he remains thus]. (15)
Whether in prison, in the world of Yama, in heaven, or among humans anywhere,
for one who follows the course of karma, attainment of Kṛṣṇa is indeed difficult to obtain.
If that [desire] has arisen, then another should not be sought by the embodied being here;
for the fortune of a universal monarch is like impurity, like mud and the like. (17)
Through awakening, even the supernatural powers (siddhis) are like grass or clay;
the self should be joined to Kṛṣṇa, remaining as firm as a mountain. 18.
O Mother, I am bound to the Beloved of Kamalā and always to the virtuous;
indeed, by Hari, with the noose of affection, I have been brought under his control.
Therefore, I am unable to ever abandon the company of Nārāyaṇa, the company of the virtuous, and their service; I have already made the gift of my head.
Such am I toward Hari; my heart is moved by love for his devotees. Indeed, apart from him, there is no other inclination of my mind to which it is attached. ||1||
O Mother, through the chanting of Kṛṣṇa’s names, intoxication arises within me;
in my state of agitation for Kṛṣṇa, I experience a forgetting of the body. (22)
Nevertheless, endowed with power, I abide within the body like one who is wise;
I exist as a servant to Hari, and Hari exists as my master within me.
Therefore, may Lord Hari indeed lead me according to His own will,
whether to a celestial chariot, an elephant, a swan, to Vaikuṇṭha, or even to this very earth.
Whether in heaven, in Badarīvana, or in Śvetadvīpa; in the Ocean of Milk, or in Goloka, or even in Śrīpura, or in the supreme, imperishable world of Brahmā (Brahmaloka); ||25||
Whether it be indeterminate or even immortal, may Hari lead my friend [to that state];
let Him fashion me exactly according to whatever His own pleasure may be.
Indeed, I possess no personal beloved distinct from the beloved of Kṛṣṇa;
that which is dear to Kṛṣṇa alone is my most excellent beloved. (27)
Nor has my livelihood ever been contrary to the will of Kṛṣṇa;
nor does my other karma (prārabdha) arise from the will of Nārāyaṇa. ||28||
I have always attained a state of attachment to Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of all and the Sovereign;
therefore, in all circumstances, my state is indeed that of Brahman.
Relying upon whom a supreme woman may attain exclusive devotion to Kṛṣṇa, by her grace there is indeed no fear for her arising from obstacles. (4.13.30)
There is no essence other than Kṛṣṇa; there is no fear [of anything else].
In one devoid of virtue there is no essence, for Kṛṣṇa does not abide therein. (3.1)
Hari resides within one established in moral conduct; thus the Bālayoginī is born.
Indeed, the bliss of Kṛṣṇa is divine, supreme, and difficult to attain, being distinct from that which is illusory. 32.
"By her, all this supreme sovereignty was attained;
through the very grace of the Lord of Creatures, it has now been obtained by me. (33)
Born as Brāhmī, beloved of Brahmā, Nārāyaṇī, and the Supreme Sovereign,
O Mistress of Badarī, I have attained once again the highest and most supreme joy.
"Whether she be such or even otherwise, I have united with the beloved of Kṛṣṇa;
I have obtained supreme love for Hari, which is like the juice of sugarcane and like nectar. (35)
O Mother, I cast far away that which creates obstacles in the dark path;
for I grasp only that which brings about attachment to the goal. (36)
I am eternally full of faith in Hari, the destroyer of worldly existence;
though longing for Kṛṣṇa, I remain unattached even to the other world.
Through providing food, drink, and massage for the head, hands, and feet, I am devoted to serving the virtuous; indeed, I am engaged in the service of Kṛṣṇa. (38)
I indeed offer everything most dear to me to Mādhava;
having offered it to the virtuous women and also to the holy men in every way. (39)
Then I put that object to use; having bestowed it out of compassion, I consume the remainder by his command. (4.13.40)
I perform the worship of Śrī Hari himself, whose form is divine;
I also perform mental worship in accordance with the seasonal rites.
Placing devotion to my husband foremost, I perform service to Hari;
for one devoted to her husband, there is no regard for another man even in a dream. (42)
In the same way, I always maintain my affection for Kṛṣṇa alone, as well as for the devotees of Kṛṣṇa because of their connection to him. (43)
May there always be exclusive devotion to Hari Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa within me;
may all my activities be for the sake of the Lord, free from desire and liberated from bondage. 44.
Just as seeds that have been parched and sown in a field do not produce sprouts,
so too are karmas [rendered fruitless] in the month of Mādhava.
Indeed, those devoid of qualities do not simply undergo birth and so forth;
rather, through association with Śrī Kṛṣṇa, they truly become worn away. 46.
Latent impressions are pacified and conceptual constructions no longer arise; all seeking directed toward the sphere of sense objects is destroyed. (47)
All my actions consist of Hari’s commands; indeed, there is nothing else for me anywhere.
By them the entire world has been renounced, and by them love for Kṛṣṇa has been established. (48)
O Mother, she has no home other than Kṛṣṇa;
for the sake of Kṛṣṇa she became a Yoginī, and so am I, that daughter of Kṛṣṇa. (49)
Dharma is considered the sustainer of the world; that Dharma is Kṛṣṇa for me, and no other. Knowledge is self-realization; that realization for me is [finding] Hari. (4.13.50)
My affection and drawn-out devotion is for Kṛṣṇa alone and nowhere else;
my devotion and service are in every way for Kṛṣṇa himself, and not for anyone other. 51.
That service of mine toward Kṛṣ�ṇanārāyaṇa is the supreme renunciation; however, religious duty devoid of a connection to Hari bestows another birth. (52)
Whether it be engagement or withdrawal, that which is well-yoked to Nārāyaṇa should be understood as the great Bhāgavata path; for that indeed is the righteous and virtuous action.
That which is worthy of service for the sake of Kṛṣṇa and for the sake of performing righteous acts for Kṛṣṇa is indeed divine;
that alone is fit for love, while everything else is to be abandoned in every respect. (54)
Even in the crush of countless men, I desire to dwell for the sake of Hari;
otherwise, I would not wish to dwell even in the forest.
For the sake of Kṛṣṇa and for the sake of performing righteous deeds for Kṛṣṇa, this forest of mine acts like a city;
for wherever Kṛṣṇa is, there swans are always seen by me.
Where Kṛṣṇa does not dwell, even the twice-born act like tigers;
even Badarīvana is cold, for it is not a city of Nārāyaṇa.
"O Mother, I possess a prosperous empire, and nothing else;
yet that place where Kṛṣṇa is not worshipped is, for me, full of thorns. (58)
Without Kṛṣṇa, my bed of arrows is like a bed of flowers; but with him, even that is a bed of flowers.
Indeed, without Kṛṣṇa, neither water nor food is pleasing to me, for I am not a devotee [of anyone else]. (59)
I have no pleasure in that which is not black; Hari is the lamp of my mind;
Kṛṣṇa is the necklace upon my heart; Keśava is the jewel in the dwelling of my hair.
For aeons, Kṛṣṇa—the beloved Lord of the secret—has dwelt in my mind;
those women in whom devotion to Hari resides are truly dear to Kṛṣṇa. (61)
O Mother, they alone are dear to me, and certainly no others anywhere;
their conduct is that of Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s beloveds, and their activity is the activity of Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s beloveds.
She whose magnanimity is dear to Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who dwells within Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s beloved, and for whom Śrī Kṛṣṇa is the beloved—that virtuous lady is Badarīśvarī. (63)
In the syllable-dwelling of Māṇikya, you are Bālayoginī;
in the wonder of Nārāyaṇī, you are Rādhā in the mind of Kṛṣṇa.
Lakṣmī is by the side of Kṛṣṇa; on the Himālaya mountain, I am Badarīśvarī;
and in the house of Sureśvarī, I exist as a maiden, the Supreme Goddess.
She who is Pārvatī, the wife of Hara, is I myself as Badrikā, the mistress;
I am Badarī, the abode of Nara and Nārāyaṇa, the young Yoginī. (66)
Those goddesses who are Kārṣṇyas and Vaiṣṇavīs are always my kinswomen;
dwelling with them forever, whether here or in the other world, is what pleases me.
In the human state of existence, those who are affectionate and truthful are indeed rare;
they are filled with love and devotion, and always desire the welfare of Kṛṣṇa.

Whether by becoming female servants or by becoming virtuous wives, those who have taken refuge in Kṛṣṇa become of the nature of consciousness (cidrūpa) through the attainment of the virtuous person whose nature is consciousness; such are those women and men. 69.
Having attained the supreme abode of the Bhāgavatas within the imperishable realm (akṣaradhāman),
they indeed propitiate their beloved Lord Nārāyaṇa with love.
One should cultivate affectionate devotion toward Kṛṣṇa with joy and a connoisseur’s relish;
for through such sincere service, Kṛṣṇa indeed bestows his grace.
Indeed, through compliance, the virtuous become gracious;
those who are honorable and saintly must be propitiated again and again with prostrations and other such gestures.
In whatever way they may become serene, it should be arranged accordingly;
for the great state is considered to be attainable through their favor. (73)
The holy Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa Svāmī should always be worshipped with joy;
mental worship should be performed with excellent offerings appropriate to each season. (74)
O Mother, every morning I always perform the worship of Hari;
indeed, during the hot season, I offer fragrant cold water.
I bathe him with cool waters and massage him with love,
using cool, fragrant oils and the finest essences of fragrant substances.
I cleanse all the limbs of Hari with a fine cloth, as well as His subtle, beautiful, and new garments. (77)
And I clothe him with garlands of fragrant flowers, with ornaments, decorations, and the splendors of a sovereign king of kings. (78)
Having applied a tilaka and a crescent moon-mark with sandalwood paste upon the forehead of Hari, as well as a mark with saffron, one should perform worship with the palms and soles of the hands.
O Mother, I perform the worship of your chest and belly with sandalwood;
thereafter, I perform the worship of your thighs, knees, and the tips of your hoods.
I offer incense, lamps, excellent food offerings, sandalwood and other items according to my preference, cool water, and fried cakes to the Wielder of the Discus. ||81||
Having offered the *uttarāpośana* water and likewise betel-leaf, and having performed the *ārārtrika* ceremony, I shall embrace Hari again and again. (82)
I bear the footprints of Hari upon my head, forehead, and breasts;
indeed, my limbs become smeared with the saffron clinging to them. (83)
Upon embracing him, I beheld my entire divine body marked with auspicious signs by the sandalwood paste and other substances remaining on his limbs, as if it had been anointed by them.
In a flower garden, I delight my lord Hari in a bower; I serve him as he wanders and sports with a serene mind. (85)
Upon a soft bed, beautiful and adorned with flower petals,
I shall lay my beloved lord and desire him according to my wish.
I massage his limbs and awaken him in the morning; during the rainy season, I perform the worship of my own beloved as is appropriate. (87)
But I shall act in such a way that the cold of the rainy season does not afflict him;
I shall bathe my beloved in the sky with slightly warm waters. 88.
Likewise, I wear other auspicious ornaments that are somewhat costly;
and at that time, during the worship, I offer sandalwood anointed with saffron.
I worship my Lord with the finest flowers and other offerings available at that time,
as well as foods that are balanced in temperature— neither too hot nor too cold— and even those of incomparable quality.
O Mother, I offer Lord Hari, who has come to my bed, to my master;
in the cold season, I provide him with extremely hot water in every way. (91)
I offer all warm garments as well as warm foods—warm, desirable cooked grains and prepared dishes—to the wielder of the Śārṅga bow. (92)
I remain pressed against the side of Bālakṛṣṇa on his bed,
acting in such a way that the cold does not afflict him in the morning.
Thus I recognize my own great good fortune in the service of Kṛṣṇa;
indeed, I always attain the bliss of Brahman, the supreme bliss of Hari. 94.
Even regarding the attainment of service to the supreme abode that is the Imperishable, the causes are:
possessing a constant and innate desire for the realization of the Imperishable. (95)
Knowledge consists in being established in the Self; devotion consists in the contemplation of the Lord, and indeed in devotion to the Blessed One, Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa. 96.
The constant avoidance of illusion, the contemplation of one's own divine self, the dissolution of false knowledge and the like, and likewise the arising of valid knowledge. (97)
Affection for the Lord of the Meat-beans (Śiva), likewise devotion to the husband in the case of Harī, association with the virtuous, service to the holy, and constant worship of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. 98.
By such reasons as these, the imperishable abode is attained;
therein, having become a vessel for affection toward Kṛṣṇa, one receives His service. (99)
She who always possesses firmness in her own purpose upon attaining Kṛṣṇa indeed attains Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa as her beloved and never leaves him. (4.13.10)
By knowing the greatness of Hari, one indeed becomes dear to Hari;
a wife who possesses love for Hari increases exceedingly in excellent virtues. || 10.1 ||
Having heard the qualities of Kṛṣṇa, she who desires Kṛṣṇa should meditate upon Kṛṣṇa;
she should resolve within her heart that Narāyaṇa is the Lord of Pārvatī.
One should constantly enjoy that which is divine and has become manifest;
that alone is to be understood as the grace of Śrī Hari, known by the name of enjoyment (bhoga). 103.
Hari’s favor is equal toward both a pauper and one like a king;
indeed, Kṛṣṇa is quickly pleased by the offering of leaves, flowers, and the like.
"Through faith, affection, love, devotion, and so forth, she quickly becomes gracious"—
thus spoke the young Yoginī to her mother, O Badrikā.
Having spoken many times about his own state, he paused for a moment before Hari;
then, coming outside once more, he sang aloud, "O Lord Kṛṣṇa! (106)

Thus ends the thirteenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Duties of Bālayoga as Spoken by Bālayoginī," within the *Bālayoginīgītā* of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, in the fourth section concerning the lineage of the Tiṣya age. || 13 ||
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said:
Then, O Goddess, beloved of Badarī, to her mother Śrī Bālayoginī he spoke of the supreme Vaiṣṇava yoga; I shall relate that to you as well.
O Mother, those who possess the form of Kṛṣṇa are to be honored by all Vaiṣṇavas like Viṣṇu himself, and especially so by Vaiṣṇava women, like Kṛṣṇa himself. || 2 ||
For they were devoted in every way solely to activities related to Viṣṇu,
and their inner senses were under the control of their own selves.

Those devotees whose celibacy is directed toward Hari, and whose state of being Brahman is centered on the Lord as their Master— those whose minds are fixed solely on Kṛṣṇa are to be honored and worshipped just like Hari himself.
These are neither equal to humans nor even equal to gods;
they are not mere female devotees, nor are they human women—for they are indeed Kamalās in every respect.
Women should by all means serve those women who are devoted to Viṣṇu; for they have reached the further shore of dharma and conduct themselves entirely according to the portion of Kṛṣṇa.
For the sake of Hari, they are free from the veils of worldly shame and the like,
yet they remain fully shielded by the fear of the faults inherent in enjoying things other than Kṛṣṇa.
In their service to Kṛṣṇa and the Vaiṣṇavas, they possess greatness equal to that of Kṛṣṇa himself;
free from the bonds of Māyā, they enjoy divine nectar and fragrances.

They gave their bodies for the sake of Kṛṣṇa, they were engaged in the service of Vaiṣṇavas, they brought joy to the family of Kṛṣṇa’s devotees, and they consorted with women who were themselves devoted to Viṣṇu.

Adorned with the splendor of the Vaiṣṇava maṇḍala and beautifully colored by the Vaiṣṇava dyes—those women who possess the Vaiṣṇava [deity] within their hearts should always be served like Kṛṣṇa himself. (4.14.10)
They are to be served like Rādhā and Kamalāvattā, and like Māṇikī; they are to be attended upon like Badrikā, and like the virtuous Śrībhūlīlā. (11)
Just as Lakṣmī and Padmāvatī are to be served by their lord,
so too are those beloved of Hari to be served like Lalitā and Mahālakṣmī.
But those auspicious and inauspicious activities and actions do not touch [the Self] at all;
they exist for the welfare of embodied beings, for the dissolution of defects, and for liberation.
Hari is born in the world; through union with Him, those [energies] become free from bondage.
They are always like Kṛṣṇa, like the son of Kṛṣṇa (Kārṣṇa), and like the daughter of Kṛṣṇa (Kārṣṇī).
The divine ones are to be served, gratified, and attended upon through services and internal offerings, with uncontracted dispositions and by following them without obstruction. || 15 ||
She who, in service, would never display pride, arrogance, egoism, or self-importance, nor shame or concealment—she is a true companion (sakhī) dear to Hari. 16.
Always dear to Brahmā, she contemplates the maṇḍala of Brahmā within her heart;
she also serves Kṛṣṇa with the honoring gift of all her possessions.
Disciplined and entirely stainless in the presence of the Vaiṣṇavīs, devoid of self-conceit, she is always most excellent and beloved by Brahmā. (18)
Within Śrī Kṛṣṇa, whose very form is bliss, divine oceans of bliss exist in every single pore and in every single atom throughout his entire being. 1.9.
Abandoning pride, one should serve the blisses of the divine wheel-bearer;
all other blisses are entirely subordinate to this Supreme Self.
For when [the Lord] is well-pleased by service, the virtuous indeed become gracious;
and in this way, all the desires of those who serve are fulfilled. (21)
One should always desire the pleasure of the virtuous and of Kṛṣṇa;
and one should abandon whatever is displeasing to Him, as it creates an obstacle to His favor. (22)
No other knots should be tied except for the Lord Kṛṣṇa;
however, those that lead to the propitiation of Kṛṣṇa should be worn for the sake of attaining Him. 23.
The Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa-granthi is the supreme knot that brings about marriage;
when one is bound and strung together by it, she is called a Brahmarṣiṇī. (24)
She alone is the beloved, she alone is the wife, she alone is the consort, the companion in dharma;
she alone is the mistress, the beloved, the yogini who is the knot of the Lord. 25.
Having reached the knot formed at the edge of the garment of love belonging to the Supreme Self, the most excellent woman becomes a Brahmā-rohiṇī. ||26||
With a dark mount, dark flanks, and a heart centered on Śrī Kṛṣṇa, this friend has taken her rest upon Kṛṣṇa and immerses herself in the bliss of Kṛṣṇa. 27.
Through association with her, other female friends also obtain happiness from their husbands;
because of their longing and devotion, they likewise become so as well. (28)
O Mother, through the process of union with darkness, those who move in darkness become dark;
yet they are born without effort as those who have attained the yoga of Brahman.
Precisely through that union with Hari, those very Bālayoginīs are born as Nārāyaṇīs, possessing bodies that are half-Nārāyaṇa.
Through compassion and cooperation, they become dear to Hari;
through self-surrender, they become dear to Brahman and ever beloved. ||3 1 ||
Those with parched hearts, who perceive faults, are not born as beloveds of Hari;
for the Blessed One is eternally one whose desires are fulfilled and who is filled with perfect bliss.
Indeed, the activities of Kṛṣṇa, the Beloved, bestow happiness upon his devotees and grant them liberation;
moreover, through portions of His perfect bliss, the other creation is endowed with happiness. (33)
For Kṛṣṇa, who delights in his own self, there is no garden that depends on anything else;
those whose gardens depend on others are eternal portions of Kṛṣṇa’s beloveds.
For those who harbor such thoughts, ignorance becomes intense:
"By my enjoyment, this Kṛṣṇa experiences pleasure and bliss. (35)
O Mother, she who knows her husband’s nature as the sustainer of all incarnations shall never be possessed of such faults; she is truly beloved by Mādhava. (36)
The beautiful woman knows that Kṛṣṇa is the bestower of all happiness;
free from the fault of pride, she becomes his beloved in his presence. (37)
Indeed, by the constant companionship of one such as this with the wielder of the Śārṅga bow, there shall always be the abundant favor of Hari toward her who serves him. (38)
The life of a fish is in the waters, and the life of a servant is in Hari;
indeed, divine happiness exists within the life of a servant of the Lord of the Bhāgavatas. (39)
Life is in Prāṇadā, O beloved; happiness also is in Mādhavī;
and magnetic attraction is in the radiant Prāṇapradā, O beloved, the sovereign mistress.
O Mother, the maidservant belongs entirely to the illustrious Mādhavīśvara;
she possesses full ownership over Hari, and Hari likewise possesses full ownership over her. (41)
Whether she be a renunciant or a householder, O Kṛṣṇa, her intensity is supreme;
for her, whose essence is such, there is both the state of being Brāhmī and the state of being Śrī. 42.
Her virtuous conduct, vows, and celibacy remain entirely unimpaired; her detachment, her self-abidance, and even her status as a chaste wife belong to her alone. (43)
Her state as Nyāsinī, her liberation, her divine nature, her identity as Nārāyaṇī, and her abiding in the lotus within the eternal (Sadākṣara) [are all hers]. 44.
First comes the hearing of this majesty of Hari;
from that arises affection, then love, and thereafter the activities of meeting. 45.
Attraction, vibration, and the functioning of one's own nature in that form;
then the desire for the bliss and joy of the gods, and from that, the application [of effort]. (46)
Then follows the attainment of that which is beyond the senses, or [the vision] of one in a dream who possesses a virtuous form;
thereafter, there occurs the direct attainment of the treasure-trove of great bliss. 47.
Embracing, the bliss arising from the touch of one-pointed joy, and the happiness of all sensory objects—all this is obtained then through the Lord, the Master. (48)
In this way, one who formerly delighted in Kṛṣṇa and was dear to Kṛṣṇa shall, through service to the virtuous, gradually attain identity with Kṛṣṇa by means of devotion. ||49||
Through service to the virtuous and through great love, everything is accomplished for a woman;
it is by means of that very great love for Kṛṣṇa that they become those whose conduct is pleasing.
That divine activity, which consists of renunciation, is offered to Nārāyaṇa;
it is devoid of the sense of "I" regarding the body even in all bodily actions. //51//
The adorable Nārāyaṇa Kṛṣṇa has been won by me as my beloved husband;
all my meditations are fixed upon the beloved Śrī Hari, and none others. (52)
And likewise, there exist mental dispositions residing within my own support;
from dwelling in those very states comes joy, whereas elsewhere, wretchedness ensues. (53)
Having attained such a state, my mind rejoices exceedingly;
for that Lord, the beloved of Śrī, who shines in the Imperishable, is truly my beloved. 54.
Indeed, many incarnations of him exist for the sake of the highest good;
he alone is the Lord, the manifest Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, the Sovereign. (55)
With his lotus feet served by liberated women who have transcended the syllables of speech,
he is within the range of our vision in the sacred field of Kuṅkumavāpikā.
Filled with ultimate compassion, the glorious son of Gopālānanda, Kṛṣṇa, the son of Śrī Kaṃbharā, is the Lord Bālakṛṣṇa, the Master and Protector. 57.
He is eternally youthful in form, transcending all desires;
he is the beloved who fulfills every wish, the purifier, and the Lord of all. ||58||
With a pure heart, she beholds that Lord within the sky of her own heart,
endowed with color, youth, radiance, nourishment, tranquility, and strength.
The Lord of Mādhavī is worthy of all beautiful women and is capable;
she who lies within the snare of his hand knows this through experience.
The young wife, pressed closely against his chest in an embrace, perceives directly the divine bliss of her beloved Kṛṣṇa, which is beyond the reach of words.
O beloved, mothers indeed become brides with various dispositions;
some, being delighted by their lover's laughter, have their minds fixed upon him. (62)
Some were exceedingly devoted to the playful words of their beloveds, while others were intensely devoted to their beloveds' eyes filled with love. ||63||

Some [women] were excessively captivated by the beauty of their beloved, his erotic charm, and his youth; others were so by his emotional states, his gestures, his praise, and his playful dalliances. (64)
Some find delight in solitude, some in wandering abroad;
some become joyful at the victory or defeat in gambling. (65)
Some [were employed] in the granting of honors, some in touch and in eating together;
some in sharing a seat, and others likewise in the execution of commands.
Some [women] become joyful during water-sports and the like, some during the adorning with flowers, and some become cheerful upon seeing him again and again. (67)
Some have their conduct drawn toward a vehicle, a celestial chariot, a bed, or a bower; others have it drawn toward solitude or toward a crowd of people. (68)
Some [loved ones] were intent on embracing the chest, some on arranging the hair and so forth;
some on drinking fragrant scents, and some on betel.
Thus, some functions that occur during quarrels or dejection are rajasic or tamasic, having been drawn away from their natural course. (4.14.70)
In this way, by the power of their inner disposition, wives become devoted to the conduct of their beloveds;
and the Lord, the Beloved, too, having discerned their dispositions, brings them joy.
Abiding within yet remaining outside, he draws his own beloved toward himself according to her true nature and bestows upon her great bliss. //72//
Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, whose form is the embodiment of divine bliss, who is an ocean of all joy, and who is the very personification of perceptible beauty, protects [us]. 73.
The Mahāmuktas, the Mahāmuktānikā women, the Avatāras, the Vyūhas, the Īśvaras, and the Īśanī women constitute that boundary.
The gods, the Siddhas, groups of chaste women, virtuous wives, and stainless holy men;
all the Yoginīs and ascetics—these great lords protect [it]. (75)
Therefore, for His pleasure, I must always maintain that auspicious boundary;
He alone is the savior of the living beings of the world, the leader of the imperishable. (76)
Kṛṣṇa-svāmī is the deliverer from the lowest state and the purifier of the fallen;
he is such a one for the sake of fulfilling the mental disposition of his devotee. (77)
Concealing its own nature, it indeed assumes the state of being dependent;
oh, how great is its compassion, for it desires to be the refuge of those who take refuge in it! 78.
Even regarding his own wife, he rejoices by perceiving her true nature;
blessed indeed is that woman who thus finds the Lord. (79)
She whose faith and taste find no delight in anyone other than her beloved,
and whose mind is struck down by the illusory pleasures of sons, wealth, and the like.
She who has no faith in other mantras and the like for the sake of her husband, and for whom no night is delightful except with Lord Kṛṣṇa; 81.
For one who feels no respect or faith toward a person capable of displaying supernatural feats such as magic, except for Hari, [he is lost]. (82)
Hari shines within me alone, in my own self whose nature is pure consciousness;
therein indeed reside the wonders and the supernatural powers for my sake. (83)
For all the goals to be attained by me exist within my beloved Lord;
by him, no other delusion arises regarding anything other than Nārāyaṇa. (84)
The Lord, like a sovereign, should show favor toward such a wife who possesses supreme intelligence;
for the virtuous, the great, and the excellent are as meritorious as the Lord himself. (85)
Those in whom the devotees of Hari, established on the true path, find a gracious disposition, possess great divine fortune; by them the essence has been acquired. (86)
Then, having sat upon the lap of the beloved Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, she no longer desires the status of being the sovereign of millions of oceans other than Śrī Kṛṣṇa. ||87||
There is no delusion in one who is distinct from the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa;
just as with Nara-Nārāyaṇa, there is no delusion regarding a woman or a man. 88.
My husband is the sage Nara-Nārāyaṇa, a powerful ascetic who observes vows of virtuous conduct and dwells on the far shore of the Great Illusion (Māyā) in the Himalayas. (89)
O Mother, Nirmoha dwells upon the ground of the Badarī forest;
likewise, O Mother, I am the female ascetic Badrikā, the mistress of Badarī.
I, a young yoginī, dwell here in this house of yours which is empty of liberation;
I am a maiden always devoted to moral conduct and vows, bringing welfare to the world. (9.1)
By means of my fruits, the sages go forth with the millions of their sins completely shaken off;
my syllable is the supreme abode, the imperishable state of me, their Lord.
"O Mother, a calamity has befallen me because of Hari; without him, not even a single moment exists for me.
Only that which is distinct from him truly exists. (93)
O Mother, through my essential identity with Your affection, there is always a state of absorption in You, my Lord; without that, I do not exist as a formed being.
How can I abandon my beloved and charming Lord Kṛṣṇa, who bestows happiness in all states and protects me in all worlds, now that he is so distressed? 95.
He is Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the support of the self and the abode of bliss;
he is served by Śrī Lakṣmī and Māṇikī, and is the supreme husband of Lalitā. (96)
The Lord, the Master, Badarīśa, the husband of Pāśavatī, Hari—who is always served and likewise worshipped by Śrī Mahālakṣmī. ||97||
"O Mother, tell me with your wisdom: how can I abandon that which was meditated upon by the illustrious Kambharā-Īśvarī, cherished and protected by her, and which I have now obtained? (98)
I have no laxity toward Hari, nor do I engage in deceit;
I have no delight in another's body—what generous person could I possibly seek? 99.
Having spoken thus, O Lord of Badrī, that young female yoginī ceased;
the virtuous mistress of the gods considered her own fortune to be blessed.
He reflected upon the means for attaining Hari through his daughter;
and having recognized her as the mistress of Badarī, he bestowed blessings upon his daughter.

Thus ends the fourteenth chapter, titled "The Discernment of the Yoga of the Supreme Vaiṣṇava," within the *Bālayoginīgītā* of the illustrious *Lakṣmīnārāyaṇīyasaṃhitā*, in the fourth section concerning the lineage of the Tiṣya age. || 14 ||
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Goddess beloved of Badrī, to that which Śrī Bālayoginī then spoke to her own mother regarding the essence of supreme Brahman-love.
The contemplation of Vāsudeva should always abide in the heart of the mother;
there should be firm affection, great magnanimity, and abundant faith in Hari. (2)
Great bliss, joy, happiness, and cessation [of suffering] reside entirely within the Lord, the Sovereign Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa; peace abides in that Master in every way. (3)
She who possesses this becomes a knower of the essence of Brahman, and no other;
when she encounters dire adversity, her steadfastness remains fixed upon Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa.
For one who has followed Kṛṣṇa, who takes refuge in Kṛṣṇa,
and who is devoted to the service of the saintly, the nectar of love for Brahman shall surely manifest.
The means for attaining the highest good arises from the nectar of love for Brahman;
yet this cannot occur without the vision of one’s own Self, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. (6)
Peace would not come to anyone even through direct means without yoga;
and yoga [is attained] only through meditation, worship, and devotion unto Śrī Hari.
To obtain that wine of the desired flavor, one's labor is as futile as [trying to extract oil from] chaff;
yet out of compassion, Śrī Hari bestows yoga upon the woman who is devotion.
His limbs are exceedingly beautiful, a collection of all splendor;
he is eternally enriched with divine qualities and captivates the hearts of all embodied beings.
Lord Kṛṣṇa and His maidservants, the Muktānikās, worship and serve the Supreme Person; they possess identical forms and identical desires. (4.15.10)
Through union with Him, embodied beings rich in qualities attain freedom from those qualities,
for He is the Wielder of the Discus who abides within all as the Inner Controller.
He is the life-force of all conscious and unconscious beings, the creator, the enjoyer, the lord, and the master;
likewise, he is a treasure-house of the many arts of his own self-established, vast sovereignty.
The union with that Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa is always bestowing happiness here in this imperishable realm to the liberated one, whose nature is existence, consciousness, and bliss.
Lord Kṛṣṇa, the creator of supreme bliss, being served with love,
absorbs His own devotee into His own form through that very nectar.
Whether today or at some other time, when she attains absorption into Kṛṣṇa,
then and there the female friend shall taste the nectar of love for Kṛṣṇa.
Having attained both the power of self-abidance and the glorious surrender to Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, O beloved one, one should indeed achieve absorption in Him forever.
One shall obtain great joy in Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the king of all kings;
one shall understand His majesty and partake of the essence of Brahman. || 17 ||
The cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa), inhabited by fourteen regions and protected by Brahmā, exists;
there are innumerable such eggs, and their king is Virāṭ, the Supreme Person (supūruṣa). || 18 ||
For those Vairājas are indeed innumerable, the excellent sons of Mahāviṣṇu;
and in this way, even the Mahāviṣṇus are born from Pradhāna and Puruṣa.
Those countless lords of Pradhāna arise from Prakṛti and Puruṣa;
that Māyā and that Puruṣa are both considered to be merged in the Imperishable (Akṣara) during the dissolution.
When it attains manifestation again and again at the beginning of creation,
it is thus flooded with the mere measure of bliss belonging to such a portion of the Imperishable.

The entire creation experiences happiness, yet the Imperishable (akṣara) possesses happiness like that of Hari; and the infinite liberated ones who possess the Imperishable have infinite abodes among those who dwell in such abodes.
The incarnations are innumerable, as are the liberated ones and their consorts;
likewise, all sovereign powers, energies, and attendants. ||23||
And all those who are the attendants of that form which partakes in bliss—of that Supreme Self, the beginningless Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa. ||24||
In every single limb, within every pore, there exists bliss;
before that [bliss], the lords and living beings appear like sparks before the sun. (25)
Even the guardians of the universe are utterly insignificant;
they all merely enjoy that which has been bestowed by Anādikṛṣṇanārāyaṇa. ||26||
They enjoy a tiny portion of pleasure that is residual, illusory, and perishable;
for such a purpose, they strive through austerity with a longing for heaven. (27)
Even those of a rajasic nature, whose conduct is deluded, consider that [the Bhāgavata] difficult to attain;
how then can the bliss of the Kārṣṇa-Bhāgavata be described? 28.
Therein lies the innate, eternal, and supreme non-worldly bliss, in a portion of which yogis attain absorption during the samādhi of yoga. (29)
There they remain for thousands of years, rejoicing in the unmanifest;
others become blissful in the great deep sleep of the fourth state (turyā).
They experience happiness in desire and even in sexual pleasure;
likewise, they rejoice in the pleasures produced by the other sense organs. (3.1)
Such is the ocean of bliss, the Blessed Lord, the Master, the illustrious Vallabha, the Sovereign;
the glorious Lord of Mādhavī, who assumes forms such as Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, and others. (32)
The Lord of Syllables (Akṣareśa) has descended, worshipped by all the liberated;
Bālakṛṣṇa is the Supreme of All, an ocean of the infinite nectar of Brahman. ||33||
He is cherished by all those dear to Brahmā and is hailed by the beloved of Hari;
the dust of whose feet is [revered] by Rādhā, Lakṣmī, Badarī, and Śakti.
It is always borne by Brahmā, Virāṭ, Mahāviṣṇu, and Puruṣa;
therein the term "Śrī Bhagavat" exists as the Supreme Brahman itself. (35)
He who is the sole Lord of all, to whom none other is equal or superior, and through whose service and worship people attain His very same nature. (36)
Nevertheless, all those powers—both those with form and those without form—behave before him like servants, remaining entirely subject to his will. (37)
Time, Māyā, Puruṣa, and the others, who are like servants out of fear of Him, always carry out the creation, maintenance, and dissolution of the universe upon receiving His command. (38)
Thus is Janārdana, the Lord of Badarī, of inconceivable power;
he is the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the delight of the cowherds. 39.
Today a man dwells in the temple of Kuṅkumavāpikā,
by whom the swans, peacocks, and parrots have been made variegated from a mere portion of water.
Men, birds, insects, and animals were created as their own respective species through the most wondrous and playful manifestation of his power. 41.
"Nothing that has been done by him can be made otherwise by anyone here," said that wielder of the Śārṅga bow, who is endowed with all such powers. (42)
Having fashioned the living beings of creation, He bestowed His own portion of bliss upon them;
through that essence, all created things become full of flavor.
Having recognized him as the son of Kambharā, the Lord Śrī Kamalāpati, the Lord of Badarī, the Lord of Mādhavī, the Lord of Bhārgavī, and the Sovereign Master; ||44||
To that Lord Mādhava, Śrī Lakṣmīnātha, the husband of the virtuous Satī, Kṛṣṇa the lord of rubies, the beloved Hari, the master of Māyā; ||45||
The Lord who is the protector of the multitude of liberated souls, the sovereign of the abode of Brahman, the master of Rādhā and Ramā, and the cause of Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, and others. ||46||
Therein, O Mother, one should cultivate delight, affection, love, infatuation, and great festivity; through blissful play, one shall attain the essence of Brahman. 47.
For such a Badarī, how could she be bound by illusion?
Even when bound, she is liberated in Kṛṣṇa; being liberated, she does not cling elsewhere. (48)
It becomes stainless and divine, and it binds one’s devotion to Śrī Hari;
O Mother, this very contemplation nourishes all the limbs like milk. 49.
O Mother, this verse containing the essence of Brahman is filled with all meaningful purposes; by whomsoever it is drunk, by them the fresh nectar of the essence of Brahman has been drunk.
Any virtuous woman who forms an association with such a devoted lady will undoubtedly become filled with the essence of Brahman, becoming one with Kṛṣṇa. 51.
Exclusive devotion to Kṛṣṇa is perfected through this very realization, by means of union with this very Śrī Hari, and by avoiding attachment to anything else. 52.
Listen, O Mother, I shall tell you the story of a divine woman from the forest;
by name she was the goddess Nāgamukhī, but by birth she was a Cāraṇī. (53)
To the west of Mount Raivata, in the city of Halamādana,
that virtuous woman became the protector of the female buffalo herd in the forest on its slopes.
Deprived of her husband and sons, she remained alone and abandoned by people; yet, subsisting on curds, milk, ghee, rice, and other provisions, she remained established in righteousness. ||55||
She thought: "My husband is lost, and my five sons are indeed lost;
I have no daughter and no family; my very lineage does not endure. (56)
Even those who have renounced the world become many here who resort to the life of a householder;
they die and are born again without that devotion. (57)
Many husbands have been obtained by them, yet no end is seen;
for those daughters of Suta, there is no end even to their illusory power over their husbands. (58)
There is no end to desire, nor even the dissolution of sense objects;
there is certainly no cessation of karmas—how, then, can there be the destruction of birth? (59)
Every day, new latent impressions (vāsanās) arise from the occurrence of enjoyments;
in that state, there is no liberation for the self through the flavor of desire for women.
Therefore, having obtained this body which is so difficult to find and which bestows liberation,
one may attain that eternal, healthy essence of Brahman which is to be gained through it.
The Supreme Self and the holy ones became embodied on the surface of the earth as human beings; both men and women were his very powers.
They wander for the welfare of embodied beings as the very embodiment of renunciation—those who possess the form of humans, who are Śrī Hari himself in the form of holy men. 63.
Indeed, the essence of Brahman is attained through service to the virtuous, through their grace, and by the conduct of a servant; it cannot be attained in any other way whatsoever.
Whether it be Hari, or a female deer, or virtuous devotees of Hari who abide in the ocean of the nectar of the Supreme Brahman, they cause even others to drink [of that nectar]. ||65||
Therefore, I must always serve saintly persons who are the very form of Kṛṣṇa, and saintly women who are the very embodiment of Lakṣmī, consisting of Rādhā and Ramā. (66)
In connection with that, the Blessed One, the husband of his beloved, will meet [you];
without the gift of your head, sovereignty cannot be obtained.
Indeed, without the gift of all one's possessions, mastery is difficult to attain;
in this world of karma, which is built by action, one reaps the fruit of what has been done.
"I shall give my entire possession to Kṛṣṇa, the servant of Kṛṣṇa;
then Kṛṣṇa will certainly give his own entire possession to me. (69)
"I have no obstacle from my family; I have no teacher other than my husband. I have no bond even to the king; I am independent and endowed with happiness. (4.15.70)
A great rise of fortune has occurred, since that which was once bound by Māyā has now attained bondage even to Kṛṣṇa, who is the beloved of the virtuous. (71)
"By serving the Lord of Śrī, I shall attain the great bliss of Brahman-bliss. Having reflected thus, Nāgamukhī, the wandering mendicant, remained a celibate student.
In his own residence, he performed service for the holy ones dwelling at the sacred site;
he constantly and joyfully served the virtuous women with milk and other offerings.
Having heard of the sincere devotion of the chief Nāgas, virtuous men come;
they dwell in her house, and she serves them with joy. (74)
Performing her vows with excellence, this supreme servant attends to him;
she bathes him with warm water and massages his limbs with oil and other unguents. (75)
And the chaste Cāraṇī causes the virtuous to drink warm milk, freshly drawn in the morning, mixed with sugar and cardamom, enriched with saffron filaments. (76)
She performs worship with sandalwood paste on the foreheads, chests, thighs, and feet of the virtuous,
as well as with the offering of flower garlands.
Then, having performed the evening lamp-offering and the midday meal,
she causes sweet and savory foods to be cooked and feeds the bards.
Even the virtuous perform their worship of Hari only after first eating;
in the evening, Cāraṇī would feed the virtuous and then eat herself.
The virtuous Satī undoubtedly performs the massaging of the feet for the holy ones; and Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, appearing in a beautiful form, remains present and even meets with them. 4.15.80.
Thinking that service to the virtuous is devoid of worldly qualities, divine, destructive of sin, and a bestower of liberation, she rejoices greatly upon her bed. (81)
Thus that goddess Cāraṇī indeed performs her virtuous vow;
with faith, she constantly chants the name of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. (82)
Considering the bliss of the self arising from service to the virtuous, as well as bodily pleasures and the like, to be the essence of the Supreme Brahman, she is satisfied and rejoices therein. (83)
Thinking, "Whether this person be a saint, another, or someone else, Lord Hari himself will become pleased with me through my service and grant me his company," one serves him. (84)
Then once, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Lord of Śrī, having assumed the form of a holy man (sādhu) and accompanied by many other holy men, [appeared]. ||85||
O Mother, assuming the form of Bālakṛṣṇa—distinguished by his beauty, qualities, body, and splendor—he went to her house. (86)
The forest-dwellers, however, had their minds fixed there upon Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa;
they fed all the holy men and served them with massages for their bodies. (87)
But at every moment, that extraordinary being was constantly throbbing;
at the end of the night's half-watch, he went to sleep, encircled by a halo of light. (88)

It possesses the fullness of the bliss of Brahman, the quality of coolness, and is even more cooling than the moon; it is an ocean of nectar, exceedingly pleasant, beautiful, and endowed with the vigor of youth. ||89||
Having embraced him first, Cāraṇī experienced the pleasure of touch; meanwhile, she experienced the pleasure arising from all her senses from the form of Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa. (4.15.90)
She attained the great bliss arising from all the sense faculties—a sea of the joy of the flowing stream, fully nourished by [practices such as] attraction and so forth. //9.1//
Absorbed, she was as if inert, devoid of the perception of her body and so forth;
she became merged within the form of Kṛṣṇa, like one who has reached the further shore of saṃsāra. (92)
Until dawn, she remained attached to Hari, delighting in the touch of his entire body; she did not rise from the bed embraced by Kṛṣṇa, like the fire-drill wood [which does not release its heat]. 93.
Having attained the nectar of the essence of Brahman produced over ten thousand yugas, she became satisfied; yet, by the will of Kṛṣṇa, she remained a lifelong celibate.
From her, who was as dark as Kṛṣṇa and remained unblemished, the divine daughter of Kṛṣṇa (Kārṣṇī) was born.
Then, at dawn, Kṛṣṇa said: "Behold my sovereign form."
Having spoken thus, he revealed his own most beautiful form, the supreme abode beyond the highest, which is infinite and inhabited by the liberated. 96.
Then [he saw] the Lord of Badarī, served by Anantarādhā, Lakṣmī, and others;
thereafter, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa of the beginningless [time], who resides at Kuṅkumavāpī.
He revealed his beautiful form as Bālakṛṣṇa,
and then, quickly vanishing from sight, he spoke to that virtuous Cāraṇī.
"What do you desire? I shall grant it here; the virtuous have been satisfied by you.
I, your husband, have come to bestow a fruit upon you. (99)
Cāraṇī said: "O Blessed One, together with the circle of queens, I shall indeed go to your imperishable abode; grant me that."
"So be it," the Lord said; at that very moment, the celestial chariot arrived.
With that same divine body, he went to Cāraṇī, the daughter of Nagnakesarin.
Having performed the naming ceremony and taken them into his celestial chariot, the Supreme Lord caused even those queens to cast off their animal bodies.
Having fashioned celestial bodies for the female attendants of Nagnakaisarī,
her beloved led them to the supreme, imperishable abode.
Having bathed them in the Brahma-lake and having made them free from worldly bonds,
he bestowed upon them the essence of Brahman-bliss and protected them in the state of liberation.
Thus, O Mother, that divine Cāraṇī, through her love and service to the virtuous, attained the essence of the Supreme Brahman and became liberated. 105.
Thus, this glorious Bālakṛṣṇa, the Lord of Śrī, shines as the Protector in the sacred field of Kuṅkumavāpikā, near the hermitage of Lomaśa.
The Blessed One, the King of Kings, who wields the power of ten million billion lotuses—
that Lord has been chosen by me as well, and I too obtain the essence of Brahman.
Having spoken thus, O Goddess of Badarī, that young yoginī ceased speaking for a moment,
her heart joined with her beloved husband.

Thus ends the fifteenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Essence of Love for the Supreme Brahman, the Attainment of Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa through the Service of the Holy by Nāmamukhī of the Forest, the Attainment of the Essence of Brahman, and Liberation," in the *Bālayoginīgītā* within the fourth section, the *Tiṣyasantāna*, of the glorious *Lakṣmīnārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O beloved of Badarī, to that which the illustrious Bālayoginī spoke— this narrative concerning the playful activities of her mother, who was seated upon the Brahma-throne.
I shall tell you that [account] of Kṛṣṇa which bestows the essence of Brahman;
by hearing it, even men and women attain liberation through that method. || 2 ||
In the village of Kāmayāna, there lived a man named Devalaka;
his wife was a virtuous woman, skilled in the art of jesting.
Even for one who has attained indifference, or who is beset by great suffering,
or who is devoid of laughter and amusement, she nevertheless produces laughter.
With words full of charm appropriate for that occasion, as well as others,
and through various applications of aesthetic flavor, he quickly produces mirth.
People who come to his house indeed become exceedingly pleased in mind by that news,
and they present him with gifts.
Wealth, ornaments, garments, sweet foods, auspicious items,
grains, and even household utensils— all these they offer.
And during the great festival of the royal assembly, as well as his own personal festival, the king also imparts a sense of humor to her through the superior poetry of the Sūri. (8)
The assembly becomes delighted and the people indeed rejoice greatly;
the king also bestows a great reward upon him.
Thus that virtuous wife of Devala, Vinodinī by name,
was born well-known in the auspicious land of Saurāṣṭra.
Women and men come to her in order to practice the arts of comedy;
she teaches them all of those skills, in every way and according to their respective needs.
Then, on one occasion, there arrived at her house an assembly of virtuous men and an assembly of saintly women who practice devotion to the Blessed Lord.
Having all been fed and honored in the house with rites of welcome,
and having been served by her as well, they performed auspicious recitations during the night.
Having heard the glorification of the virtuous as well as the songs of the virtuous women,
her mind became fixed on the Supreme Lord, and she became devoted to the dharma of devotion.
Through her diversion, Hari himself became engaged in reflection;
he was as well-pleased by the praises of the virtuous and saintly women as he is by such diversions. 15.
The supreme Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa becomes satisfied;
