I shall act in such a way that He may likewise be eternally and perfectly satisfied. 16.
Having reflected thus, she received from that virtuous man named Brahmarasāyana the Vaiṣṇava mantra, which bestows liberation, as well as a garland of *tulasī*.
"Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Lord, svāhā!
He repeated this supreme mantra and took hold of the image made of variegated jewels. 18.
She worshipped that image of Hari daily and served it with joy;
having become a pure devotee of Hari, she became delightful and playful. (19)
She questioned the virtuous Guru, who was known as Brahmarasāyana,
regarding the means for attaining the great, most desired nectar of bliss that is the bliss of Brahman.
With great reverence, the one whose essence is the nectar of Brahman spoke to that disciple:
"In that supreme nectar, all other essences become unified. (21)
In the glorious incarnation of Svāmī Bālakṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, the Lord himself is the means for attaining Him and for attaining the essence of His nectar. 22.
She who has offered her very self and all possessions through loving devotion is dear to Hari;
by this self-surrender, one attains Śrī Kṛṣṇa. (23)
The surrendering of oneself, filled with affection, love, and devotion, and free from defects such as opposition, laziness, and lack of faith. (24)
Unobstructed by any other mental state, it is the constant sphere of manifestation, rich with the wealth of divine and immediate perception, and takes refuge in the beloved Śrī Kṛṣṇa. ||25||
The entry of Kṛṣṇa into this body composed of the five elements occurs in every way;
his very form and its qualities reside within the objects of the senses.
That is its object; that is its sweetness, its bliss, and its delight.
Its taste, its touch, its form, and likewise its sound. ||27||

The scent of that, the taking up of it, dwelling in it, and the relinquishing of it; the bliss therein, the pondering of it, the thorough reflection upon it, and the intellect [are all absorbed in Him]. ||28||
Its measurement, its determination, its valid cognition, its memory, as well as its mental impressions and its volition—these are to be known as the summary of cognition. (29)
In manifestation, in appearance, and in cessation, He alone is always the object of perception;
both within and without, He alone is the Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa. (4.16.30)
Whether in secret or in public, in the heart or in solitude, even among people;
whether in ritual action or personal conduct, in laughter or in joy—he [is present]. (3.1)
In every way—whether in ornaments and the like, or even in the erotic sentiment—he is indeed Hari;
whether in bathing, sleeping, amidst dust and such, in play, or even in religious observance, he is he.
May the Lord of Māyā protect me in ownership and in the state of belonging to another, in the act of offering and in receiving,
in taking and in giving back, and even in exchange.
He is present all around, in front, behind, in the middle, below, and even in the half;
He is the correlate (*anuyogin*) and the counter-correlate (*pratiyogin*), for Hari indeed exists even in conjunction.

Mādhava is present in that which is to be tasted, in savory transformations, in satiety, in that which is to be drunk, in what is exceedingly cool, in the desirable, in attraction, in the assembly hall, and even in recreation. (35)
He was in the house, in the forest, in the courtyard, on the terrace, and even on the couch; he was on the swing, in the celestial chariot, in the carriage, and even upon the mount.
And even when that which is distinct from Him is desired, Hari, whose nature is great bliss, remains the Lord who must be concealed within the flow of favorability. (37)
Thus, in every respect, for her to whom Śrī Kṛṣṇa alone is everything, that devotion full of love is the means for attaining Kṛṣṇa. 38.
Upon attaining Kṛṣṇa, there is the attainment of His rasa, which is eternal and irreversible;
born from union with Him, it becomes divine, arising from the rasa of self-surrender and other such means. (39)
Otherwise, Kṛṣṇa is not attained, nor is His rasa attained;
eternal bliss is not attained without the grace of the playful one. 4.16.40.
One should win his grace through service, his mind through affection, Kṛṣṇa through self-surrender, and the great nectar of that [surrender] through Kṛṣṇa. 41.
"Having attained the fruit that is the essence of Brahman, nothing further remains to be attained.
Thus was the virtuous Devalī, who brought delight, addressed by her teacher. 42.
He served his guru in such a manner that he acquired complete instruction;
Kṛṣṇa himself is Nārāyaṇa, and the guru is Nārāyaṇa himself. (43)
The Guru is manifest, bestowing all fruits, and acts in accordance with the devotion [of his disciples].
The Guru is Brahmā; the Guru is Kṛṣṇa; the Guru is the Lord Hari, the destroyer of worldly existence. 44.
He himself, the performer of all human dramas, was thus properly gratified;
by her, Narāyaṇa, the sovereign lord of the gods, was fully propitiated. ||45||
Realizing this, that beautiful woman, devoted to celibacy, righteousness, and service, satisfied her guru with devotion. (46)
The peaceful Guru dwelt for a long time in her house;
then, on one occasion, he indeed assumed the form of a temple-priest.
Then, recognizing him as her handsome, beloved, husband, and master, she spoke with supreme affection: "I am blessed, seeking your grace."
O divine Guru, you who assume the form of my master, please serve me as you wish;
regarding me as your own, grant me the drinking of the nectar of Brahman. 449
Devotion to a husband is dependent upon the master; you are now my master.
You are the very form of Nārāyaṇa; you are the embodiment of the Master—accept me.
Then the king of gurus, perceiving that all her intentions were pure, became pleased;
having accepted her, he then joyfully bestowed his blessing from the depths of his heart. (51)
Become the maidservant of Hari, his supreme and exclusive devotee, equal to divine Lakṣmī, a disciple, a woman of Nārāyaṇa, and the most excellent of women. 52.
"Delighted by your service, I grant you supreme sovereignty;
O possessor of a wondrous divine form, be happy! (53)
Having spoken thus, the venerable Guru, who is the elixir of the essence of Brahman,
touched Vinodinī with his hand alone and made her drink water.
Then Rādhā, divine, of supreme form, equal to Lakṣmī, virtuous, with an unveiled body, appeared as a source of delight. (55)
Thus born, the divine goddess performed superhuman rites;
and the Guru, having accepted the worship, offered it in turn as worship to Kṛṣṇa. (56)
Having thus witnessed this supreme and most excellent marvel even in his guru, he suddenly vanished like a flash of lightning in the sky.
Delighted and intent upon a great wonder, she stood motionless for a moment;
she reflected in many ways: "Who is this one who has assumed the form of my guru? (58)
Is he Nārāyaṇa himself, or is it Nara, the younger brother of Nārāyaṇa;
or is he the Lord, the Inner Self, the Supreme Brahman, or the Sovereign? (59)
By whose grace and by whose touch divinity was attained;
yet even so, this Guru is not perceived by me with divine vision. (4.16.60)
Therefore, let my teacher Nārāyaṇa abide in the exceedingly divine realm;
meanwhile, the worlds of Māyā remain within the range of my vision now.
"The Guru is not seen there; therefore, this must be Brahman.
Oh! The Creator of Amusement has been found by Vinodinī through her own amusement. (62)
Nevertheless, I am truly blessed; I shall worship this image of Kṛṣṇa, which was offered by my guru and is free from deceit, and I shall strive again to attain it.
Thus, considering him to be the Great Peace (Mahāśānti), she meditated upon the Imperishable One;
meanwhile, the other male and female practitioners vanished from sight.
They all attained dissolution into the form of Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa;
then she reached the certainty that this was indeed the form of the Guru.
All have gone here to dissolution into Kṛṣṇa, who is Nārāyaṇa himself;
and having bestowed his own form upon me as my guru, he vanished and is no longer seen.
Then, this very Lord Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa appeared today;
thus, being exceedingly pleased, she spoke to her husband, the temple-priest: 67.
This form is itself virtuous and consists of the elixir of Brahman; though sentient, it stands as a mere image. O Lord, even you are blessed! (68)
It is our supreme good fortune that the Inner Self, being pleased by this diversion for embodied beings, has come to our home. (69)
"I shall constantly entertain that Supreme Person in person;
O Blessed One, O Lord, you too should always perform service for him. (4.16.70)
Then, filled with joy, the two of them served that living image of the Lord of Gods according to the prescribed method, honoring him with due respect.
Devalaka constantly worshipped Acyuta with great zeal;
however, Vinodinī served her husband as if he were visibly present before her. 72.
Nevertheless, Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, who possesses a conscious form and knows the inner disposition of beings, does not manifest from his physical form anywhere for a long time. (73)
He desired to test the instability of Vinodinī;
therefore, after a year had passed, he [acted] by means of serving Mūrti.
In the presence of the Mūrti, he undertook a vow of fasting with the desire for a vision;
he performed that month-long vow before the Mūrti seated upon a lotus throne.
With her mind fully absorbed, she held a rosary in her hand and chanted the name of Keśava;
with her two eyes she beheld his form, and in her mind she meditated upon Hari. (76)
He perceived his own manifestation as an image of Hari in dreams and the like;
indeed, he perceived nothing else, for he had performed the touching [of the image] during worship.
She directed her sensory functions inward toward Hari;
though she possessed external splendor, that beautiful woman fixed them upon Hari as their external object.
Having attained the unity of the internal and external, she became a devoted and joyful Satī, single-mindedly intent upon the supreme Acyuta.
Then the Blessed One, longing for the flavor of her laughter,
did not manifest his true form, but waited for her amusement.
A period of time exceeding one month passed while she remained on a single seat;
then, she also began to divert herself with her physical form.
You appear with a single face, yet you are indeed turned away;
though placed within a cage of two faces, you shall become faceless within. (82)
You are devoid of outflow, yet you are fixed upon an unmanifest flow;
you shall become eternally without outflow—become possessed of outflow for my sake. (83)
Thus, in the presence of Kṛṣṇa, the proud woman constantly uttered these playful words aloud to provoke laughter from his form. (84)
Then she spoke these playful words to Hari thereafter:
"You are eternally of great form, yet you have assumed the shape of a span. (85)
"And do as you wish to enter Hiraṇyagarbha.
Having spoken thus, she rose from her seat and danced.
Lord Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, having attained such great clarity, suddenly manifested his form, his body pervaded by splendor. (87)
Smiling, he became a youthful youth standing before her;
he embraced his devoted consort and caused her to drink his own essence. 88.
He bestowed upon that embodied form pleasure within the range of all the senses and so forth;
thereafter, he caused it to become absorbed, becoming one with the Embodiment (Mūrti). ||89||
The Lord gave her all his own divine happiness;
she, the divine Muktānikā, quickly became satisfied.
She became devoid of her illusory power and remained as if established in the world of Brahmā;
meanwhile, Devala also arrived there due to his great merits.

Having beheld his beloved Kṛṣṇa and the virtuous daughter of Kṛṣṇa (Satyabhāmā) who was so full of delight, he likewise desired for himself that same state; thus, he attained a state of melting love toward Kṛṣṇa.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa, having perceived the supreme disposition within the temple priestess,
transformed that woman into the form of a female companion, just like Vinodinī;
and she, abandoning her male form, became the female companion Devalikā.
In every way, through the compassion of Hari, she is equal to Vinodinī in beauty. ||94||
Just as Lakṣmī is dear to Rādhā, so too did Devalikā become;
both were born as Muktānikās, divine and adorned with celestial ornaments.
When Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, who is rich with the divine nectar of Brahman and possesses a divine dark form, has become absorbed and established within that body, [then... //96//
Thus, the two of them were indeed led by their beloved Śrī Kṛṣṇa to his abode;
they immersed themselves in the eternal bliss of the supreme Brahman. 97.
O Mother, for one who is a devotee of Kṛṣṇa, there is always such a drinking and eating of the great nectar of Brahman; and for me, it exists even now.
"I have no other abode or spiritual cultivation apart from Śrī Hari; the essence of Brahman resides in Hara," having said this, he observed a vow of silence. (99)
Thus, O Goddess Badarī, the imperishable essence of the Supreme Brahman is attained;
and how it is attained by those two, so has it been declared as attained.

Furthermore, by offering one's entire being to another person, even if that other is someone else entirely, one shall attain the essence of the bliss of the supreme Brahman according to the method described. 101.
In the attainment of the essence of the Supreme Brahman, the Supreme Brahman itself is the cause;
even service to one who possesses a virtuous form is a cause for attaining the Supreme Brahman. 102.

Thus ends the sixteenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Direct Attainment of the Blessed One by Vinodinī, the wife of a Devalaka, through her playful service; the Liberation and Befriending of the Devalaka by the Lord in the form of a virtuous alchemist for the sake of obtaining the nectar of the Supreme Brahman," within the *Bālayoginīgītā* in the fourth section, the Tiṣya lineage, of the glorious *Lakṣmīnārāyaṇīyasaṃhitā*.
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Goddess beloved of Badarī; I shall relate to you again what that young yoginī, Sureśvarī, spoke to her mother. (1)
In the auspicious coastal city of Saurāṣṭra known as Mahuvāsa, there was a Śūdra named Bahurūpa, who wore many different types of dress and assumed various names.
In form, however, he was equal to Indra; in his body, he was a youth sixteen years of age, with a woman’s face, wearing fine matted locks, and beautiful in his arrangement of hair.
In some places he is a Samaya-holder wearing earrings, a nose-ornament, and other finery;
in some places he is a king, in some places a queen, and likewise in some places a general.
In one place he was a merchant, in another a thief; in one place a maiden, in another a young boy;
in one place a bride, in another a queen; in one place a god, and in another an actor.
In one place he was a brahmin, in another a warrior; in one place a poor beggar, and in another a forest-dweller; in one place a boatman, and in another a farmer.
In one place he was a ghost and in another a monkey; in one place he assumed the form of a bear, and in another he was a husband with children; in one place he was a rider of mares.
In one place he was a virtuous ascetic, a master, a celibate student, and an anchorite; in another, a joker full of all manner of amorous charms; and in yet another, a villain.
Such is he through his dress, appearance, and refined conduct;
the people call him by the name Bāhulaketi. || 9 ||
People, having summoned him who is skilled in dancing, dress, singing, and the playing of musical instruments, hold festivals that delight the populace. (4.17.10)
Then, by the power of his past merit, he married a bride of similar character,
an auspicious maiden named Līlāvatī.
Like a Gandharva maiden, she was skilled in the arts and capable of assuming all manner of guises;
clever and wise, she was an expert in male attire.
Practice performed correctly in the past bears fruit even in another birth;
likewise, righteousness, the bestowing of wealth, service, and devotion bear fruit in due time.
Nothing unearned is obtained without the grace of Hari;
even the auspicious knowledge, women, prosperity, and pleasures bestowed in a previous life [are lost]. 14.
In another birth, virtues, fame, and wealth are obtained;
likewise, for those who have committed sins, mental afflictions arise.
The festivals of those who have performed good deeds increase day by day;
however, a wife who performs her own duties is not obtained by one of meager merit.
In virtue, beauty, essential nature, discernment, and the heart—these are equal; they are attained through great merit, as well as through cleverness and discrimination. (17)
Likewise, a husband who possesses a nature favorable to his wife cannot be obtained through small merit; indeed, he is obtained only through austerity.
Indeed, those who maintain an even mind in the face of loss, suffering, agitation, service, poverty,
disease, calamity, and pain are very rare to find.
If they possess an even mind toward loss and the like, heaven is within their grasp; but if they possess an even mind toward gain and the like, they will indeed find it in every house. (4.17.20)
The virtuous yogis, free from impurity, maintain an even mind toward both gain and loss;
so too do the highly awakened ones, such as Nārāyaṇa, or those householders who are meritorious.
Thus these two were joined together; but could there be two actions for one? Yet such as they were, those two who devoted themselves to drama and the like, were happy. (22)

And by acquiring wealth, food, clothing, and goods through the performance of drama, he successfully carries out his livelihood, which is difficult for the world to overcome, including the preservation of his very life. (23)
He set out on a pilgrimage to Somanātha, Raivata,
Dvāravatī, Camatkārapura, and Kuṅkumavāpikā.
There, having bathed in the auspicious syllable (Oṃ) and at the Aśvapaṭṭa lake, they went to the venerable Lomaśa and bowed to the true guru and the sages.
They both received the great mantra that destroys the noose of illusion:
*Oṃ namaḥ śrīkṛṣṇanārāyaṇāya svāmine svāhā*. (26)
Having become supreme Vaiṣṇavas and devoted practitioners who had exerted themselves in their practice,
they dwelt for a long time and worshipped Bālakṛṣṇa.
They constantly worshipped with love the divine child Gopāla, the Lord Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, the husband of Mādhavī. 28.
And they always maintained association with the virtuous there, attained knowledge, and both achieved divinity; they now abide, adorned by the beauty of service.
They repeatedly listened to the narrative of the *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa-Saṃhitā* and to the accounts of the incarnations occurring therein.
They both reflected upon the deeds of the gods and of noble kings,
as well as the conduct of liberated women and of devoted followers.
Having heard this and reflected upon it in his heart on the bank of the Aśvapaṭṭasara lake,
he [acted] according to everything he had heard through his dress, gestures, actions, and so forth.
Filled with great joy, they both brought them down and showed them to the people repeatedly during the night of the moonlight festival.
But when hundreds of thousands of people see them, they become truly amazed;
they praise the actress and the actor, who are masters of assuming many forms. (34)
These two are equal to gods, as if they were portions of Nārāyaṇa himself;
for they indeed manifest that ancient event and its very form.
Born in the field of Kuṅkumavāpī as two handsome youths worthy of honor, such a time has arrived for them that increases their fortune. (36)
On that occasion, the seventeenth festival of the birth of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa took place; there, the liberated gods arrived. || 37 ||
Gods, humans and others, bards, panegyrists, and heralds, as well as great sages, those from sacred fords, brahmins, and masters of the arts, all arrived there. (38)
The powers beginning with Ramā, as well as the progeny and the worlds, also arrived for the sake of the Supreme Soul, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. (39)
Relatives and the inhabitants of the worlds arrived on the eighth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Kārttika, the birth-tithi of Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa.
Having observed [the time], all beings, both stationary and moving, arrived during the night;
on the morning of the eighth day, this Śrī Kṛṣṇa Mādhava bathed.

Having performed the auspicious rites and worship, having adorned himself with the marriage-thread (kautuka), and having been honored and saluted by his wives numbering in the millions, billions, and hundreds of millions; ||42||

Having received the auspicious blessings of his mother, father, elders, mothers-in-law, fathers-in-law, and others, and having become beautiful through the attire they provided for him, [he set forth]. (43)
In the vast assembly hall on the shore of the Aśvapaṭṭasara lake—a place enriched by all created beings and joined by Lomaśa and others—[he spoke]. ||44||
Hearing the shouts of victory and the fame of Kṛṣṇa while seated upon his elephant-throne, he sat down after arriving; at that moment, musical instruments were sounded everywhere.
Musical instruments resounded for all the worlds and auspicious songs were sung;
the Vedic chants of the great seers became purifying to the ears. 46.
The glances of everyone became heavy with affection;
then joy, delight, and bliss appeared as if they had taken on physical form. ||47||
Lomaśa, the sages, the gods, the twice-born, the kings, the ancestors, the Siddhas, and millions of lords worshipped the Supreme Soul. ||48||
Apsarases and goddesses, humans and others, as well as those dwelling in the netherworlds (pātāla) and so forth, and sacred fords (tīrthas), both insentient and sentient; ||49||
All the perfected ones, the aged women, the goddesses beginning with Ramā,
and both the virtuous women and the virtuous men likewise worshipped the Supreme Lord.

They applied a tilaka-mark upon you with sandalwood paste and other substances, along with unbroken grains, saffron, and auspicious items; they fashioned a moon-design on your forehead and placed flower garlands around your neck.
They bestowed fragrant essences, the essence of sounds, the essence of mantras, auspicious blessings, and various gifts; indeed, they gave their very hearts as well. (52)
They gave him crowns, earrings, necklaces, bracelets, chains, rings, gems, and ornaments of gold and jewels.
There were songs of praise and likewise dances;
there was the offering of betel, drinks, and the like, as well as sweet foods and auspicious ceremonies.
At that time, there was even the shaking of hands within the assembly;
and at that moment, there were also acts of great honor and formal salutations in the hall.
The hosts of sages performed the *ārārtrika* rite for Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, and Muktā and others offered hymns of praise; thus a great festival took place.
On this festival, having found the opportunity, Bahurūpadhṛk and his wife Bāhulakā assumed beautiful forms and became exceedingly handsome.
Causing wonder and delighting the minds of the assembly, those two, beautiful in their female attire, arrived within the hall laughing. (58)

At that moment, because they were so exceedingly beautiful in form, those two could not be distinguished as "which is the woman" and "which is the man" by the members of the assembly, nor could they be discerned even by the gods.
With identical throat-voices and equal in their gestures, emotions, limbs, and expressions, even Hari himself, though omniscient, became bewildered for her sake. (4.17.60)
What need is there to speak of others whose eyes are merely the skin-bound flesh, enriched by illusion?
Thus, the assembly also suddenly beheld the two women on all sides.
Just as a wooden doll becomes motionless when enchanted,
so too did those two women there become transfixed by the song concerning the glory of Bālakṛṣṇa.
They both created [a realm] filled with the essence of bliss for all desires; the gracious Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa gave jewels to them.
She gave them jeweled necklaces, ornaments, and auspicious blessings;
then those two women performed a dance imbued with various emotional expressions.
Accompanied by songs concerning the life of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, you are the manifest Lord of Akṣara, the Supreme God in human form. 65.
But for those upon whose tongues, minds, intellects, and even within their very selves You are the dancer, for them there is indeed eternal liberation. (66)
"Be gracious, O Blessed One! Make our dance truly meaningful;
perform it yourself and grant us two women the touch of Your feet. (67)
"Om," said the serene son of Kṛṣṇa in the midst of the assembly;
immediately, the two women approached the presence of Śrī Kṛṣṇa's feet.
They likewise placed the dust of Kṛṣṇa’s feet upon their heads, then upon their chests, their bellies, and their entire bodies; thereafter, they again [placed it] on the feet of Hari.
With serene minds, they touched their breasts while the members of the assembly looked on, [the breasts] being now divested of their bodices.
The two youths quickly became endowed with male attire; they possessed male speech and were adorned with all the marks of a man. (71)
Upon seeing that she had attained womanhood, the Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa,
the assembly, and the gods, beginning with Īśvara, were struck with great wonder.
The members of the assembly there fell into doubt regarding whether they were two men or two women;
at that time, no one was able to reach a definitive conclusion.
At that time, the entire assembly and the spectators were struck with wonder as these two [heroes] made their footsteps heard through the jingling of their networks of small bells.
Performing in the midst of the stage, the two of them executed a great dance;
even Śaṅkara was then momentarily enchanted and deeply moved within his heart.
Then the Gandharvas and other dancers had their pride dissolved;
thus, having performed a dance for the great lord Bālakṛṣṇa, [they departed]. (76)
Having touched his feet and received gifts and rewards as tokens of appreciation—
such as gems, jewels, diamonds, and the like, as well as golden ornaments and garments— (77)
Having been cursed in the midst of the assembly, both of them quickly became deprived of their masculinity right there, while all embodied beings looked on. (78)

They were dressed as eunuchs and possessed the disposition of eunuchs; they sported with the playful charms of eunuchs, their hands joined in rhythmic clapping, and their eyes filled with radiant glances from the corners. (79)
Speaking in the speech of eunuchs, both of them caused laughter in the assembly;
then, at the end of that moment, one of them became a female dancer and danced.
Having become another actor there, he played a supreme musical instrument;
while the gods and others were looking on, the actress vanished from sight.
The actor also became a female dancer for the sake of continuous performance on the stage;
while she was dancing on the stage, that female dancer arrived.
Upon seeing the dancing actress, the man indeed became that very actress;
thus, having observed these many forms, she was greatly delighted in the assembly.
That assembly uttered words of great respect for those two;
then, at the end of a moment, the bride and groom were honored with a garland of choice flowers.
Manifested in the forms of a husband and wife, the two appeared in the midst of the assembly;
they both offered salutations to Hari and to the members of the assembly. ||85||
Filled with humility, they both offered a prayer for forgiveness for their offense;
then they stood in the midst of the assembly, assuming their true forms. (86)
Then the gods, beginning with Īśvara, as well as humans and the sages, became free from doubt and were indeed exceedingly delighted. (87)
The beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama, Śrīmat Gopāla Kṛṣṇa and others, and the virtuous mother Śrī Kaṃbharā. 88.
Other world-protectors and others as well, intent upon great wonder and motivated by joy, presented offerings to the two of them. (89)
Then the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, with a gracious mind, spoke auspiciously to the two of them in order to receive their boon.
They chose the bliss of the essence of the Supreme Brahman from Hari;
they attained a state of supreme immersion in the great ocean of the nectar of divine bliss and the Great Brahman. 9.1.
They both made a request of Kṛṣṇa, Nārāyaṇa, Keśava; Hari replied, "So be it," and from that time on, [He acted] for them accordingly.
And there arose a non-conceptual samādhi that bestowed joy upon Kṛṣṇa;
it was the manifestation of Hari within the functions of all beings, senses, and so forth. 93.
Thus, by the grace of Hari and through his own portion (kalā), those two always remained liberated, established as if within the syllable itself.

Then, through the contemplation of his manifold forms which effect the welfare of the world, he [perceived] that supreme state, the great bliss within the belly of the bliss of the Supreme Brahman. 95.
Endowed with divine bodies and senses, they always attained the celestial state;
the seventeenth great festival of their birth reached its full completion. (96)
Then there were various foods for the assemblies, as well as offerings, acts of satisfaction, and great gifts. ||97||
Thus her own mother spoke to the young Yoginī regarding the nectar of Hari;
those two who had obtained it were then devoted and dedicated to Mādhava. ||98||
Having thus attained the eternal nectar of Brahman through compassion, the young Yoginī, completely immersed in it, remembered the Lord and became silent. 99.
Thus, O beloved of Badarī, the supreme Brahman-essence has been described to you;
it is attained through the grace of Kṛṣṇa and never otherwise.
Many have attained the supreme essence of the bliss of Brahman through service;
many have attained it through grace, just like the beloveds of Brahmā here in this world.

Thus ends the seventeenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Means for Attaining the Essence of the Supreme Brahman through the Narration of the Devotional Conduct of the Couple named Bahulakalīlāvatī—who assumed many forms—and the Festival on the Seventeenth Birthday of Śrī Hari," within the *Bālayoginīgītā* of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, in the fourth section, the *Tiṣya-santāna*.
The illustrious Nara-Nārāyaṇa said:
"Listen, O Goddess beloved of Badrī; [I shall describe] the Mother Bālayoginī, and then she spoke further of the excellence of the essence of Brahman."
Formerly, in the village of Bhadragrāma, there was a gardener named Māliya;
Māliya’s wife was named Mallikāśrī.
Cultivating the garden for the purpose of selling fruits and the like, and fashioning flower garlands and such, those two became devoted [to their work]. (3)
Wherever they heard of the abodes of the gods, they traveled all around them;
having gone to Saurāṣṭra, they performed worship to the gods.
Sūrya, Dāmodara, Somanātha, Śrīgopanāthaka, Guptaprayāga, Aśvapaṭṭasara, and Raivata; || 5 ||
Filled with wonder, they went to Dvāravatī and worshipped [the Lord] with flowers,
garlands, fruits, and clusters of tulasī leaves.
With various kinds of lotuses, both land-lotuses and water-lilies, with flowers such as mālatī and others, and with blossoms like the pārijāta; || 7 ||
With *campaka* and *bakula* flowers, with climbing vines and flowers born of grass,
as well as with sweet plantains and the nine colors and so forth.
With cool sandalwood pastes well-blended with saffron and other ingredients, and with many varieties of flowers possessing abundant fragrance; (9)
Of those divine garments that were never worn, which captivated the heart,
he took the turban, the head-covering cloth, the four-cornered mantle, and the undergarment.
A suravāla cloak, a blanket, an arm-guard, a skirt, a ghargharī, a breast-binding cloth, and a kacalīnikā. || 11 ||
Having fashioned garments such as the *kucalī*, *karpaṭī*, *caulī*, *caula*, and likewise the *antaḥpaṭī* from flowers alone, those two—
In various auspicious sacred places (tīrthas), they both offered [their bodies] with love to the forms of those respective goddesses and gods, and held them within their hearts.
The two honored the God and the Goddess, as well as Mādhavī, Kṛṣṇa, Viṣṇu, Śrī, Nārāyaṇa, Arka, and Śaṅkara, who are dear to Rādhā and Ramā.
Having prepared all kinds of floral garments, they offered them to the Mūrti;
the deities and goddesses residing in the Mūrti, such as Gaṇeśa and others, as well as Hari. || 15 ||
Indeed, Devikā and the others become gracious when they behold devotion;
then, having fashioned all their ornaments out of flowers, those two [proceeded]. (16)
Full of devotion, the two of them constantly offered to the gods a crown woven with flowers, as well as earrings and ear-ornaments. (17)
Let him take the ball, the necklaces, the garlands, the two auspicious bracelets, the various chains, the girdles, and the waist-bands. (18)
He [took] the hair-remover, the breast-ornament, and the forehead-leaf, as well as the crest-jewel, the topknot-jewel, and the supreme Kaustubha gem. (19)
She also had anklets on her feet, as well as bangles and bracelets;
likewise, she wore leather sandals, hair-filling combs, and garlands for her braided locks.
A garland on the topknot, the moon at the navel, as well as moons on the hips, auspicious rows of thighs, leaf-patterns on the forearms, and flower-clusters [are all favorable]. (21)
With the sun behind them and leaf-patterns upon their necks, whatever ornaments they possessed, both of them wore them all in that manner. (22)
Having adorned the deities of the sacred fords with various flowers, those two, possessing skill in the arts, joyfully decorated them with affectionate devotion.
Day after day, having gone repeatedly to the abodes of the gods, those two performed their rites;
their faith increased constantly, and their happiness grew.
Divine renown increases, and imperishable merit grows for those two who perform worship with flowers; upon them, Hari bestows his grace. (25)
The favor of the gods who have been worshipped also increases;
thus those two indeed became very meritorious and likewise most beloved. 26.
By performing flower worship and other rites for all the gods, they became worthy recipients of blessings and attained the grace of the deities and others. (27)
Then one day, Hari himself desired to grant them a vision when they were worshipping him in the sacred field of Kuṅkumavāpikā.
On the banks of the Aśvapaṭṭa lake, there are those of divine form:
all the temples as well as auspicious shrines. (29)
In various places, Hari, through his manifested forms, showed him wonders and caused him to drink the nectar of Brahman, which shone like honey.
When Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa was in His golden abode, He desired to grant them a divine vision arising from the image. ||3 1||
In the morning, having been honored by those two with flowers, ornaments, and garments,
that man Kṛṣṇa then became one who has reached the imperishable abode.
He sat upon a divine elephant-throne in the abode of the Imperishable,
adorned with divine ornaments, garments, weapons, and the splendor of festive finery.
He is attended by innumerable liberated beings, worshipped by infinite hosts of emancipated souls,
and is indeed the source of countless incarnations and various embodied forms.
He is filled with the power of the wonder of infinite sovereignty and capability; he possesses the splendor of the king of kings and is the regulator of all principles. ||35||
With a form filled with infinite and profound splendors, the Lord, who is higher than the highest,
having become thus, indeed manifested the splendor of Brahman.
The imperishable Brahman transcends the qualities (guṇas), is the source of all splendor, is endowed with countless rays of light, is all-pervading, and has emerged from its form. ||37||
Having shown that abode to Māliyānā, the illustrious Mallikā,
he revealed there the divine realm of Akṣarī, which is radiant, peaceful, and cool.
She consists of great bliss, is auspicious with the waters of divine nectar,
is the very form of pure consciousness, and is born from the embodiment of the imperishable Brahman.
The Blessed Lord, the Lord of Abodes, Śrī Nārāyaṇa, revealed Himself;
Mādhava showed Him His own imperishable city.
Then he showed them the abode of infinite liberation;
having led them into divine samādhi, he showed them the garden.
The Blessed One showed him the auspicious village of Bhadrāyana and the great Kusuma garden, where Hari is worshipped with flowers.
In the city of Māliyāna, there is a supreme garden belonging to Mallikāśrī;
therein exists a tree consisting of fruits and flowers that is imperishable. (43)
He is eternal, the bestower of divine fruits, the giver of divine sweet nectar;
he is the provider of the desired honey-essence arising from divine flowers. ||44||
Having shown him that garden, Hari spoke these auspicious words:
"Whatever has been offered to me upon this earth, including all these groves and so forth—"
The flowers and such produced in the gardens, the fruits and such of the great groves—everything here is eternal for you both; perform your own [duties]. (46)
Indeed, here the wish-fulfilling trees are eternal and filled with essences;
they yield sweet fruits—drink that nectar of existence. 47.
"Partake of these sweet fruits which grant divine satisfaction," having said this, the Blessed One caused them both to drink that juice. (48)
At that very moment, the Lord graciously caused them to take food consisting of fruits,
and he presented them with an arrangement of floral ornaments.
The Lord himself bestowed upon them all his own divine, sweet, eternal, and joy-filled happiness, consisting entirely of supreme bliss. 4.18.50.
That rasa which does not exist in Śaṅkara, nor in Aja, nor even among the Īśvaras;
that rasa which is not in Viṣṇu, nor in his incarnations, nor even in the liberated ones; [that rasa exists here]. (51)
The essence which exists in that which consists solely of the state of identity with Kṛṣṇa, always resides in the form of Kṛṣṇa and exists as non-different from Kṛṣṇa. (52)
That rasa which exists in Kṛṣṇa’s consorts—such as Śrī Rādhā, Prajñā, Mādhavikā, and others—and in all the beloveds of Brahmā and the beloveds of Hari; ||53||
That essence which exists eternally within Śrī, Lakṣmī, Kamalā, Padmā, Māṇikyā, Lalitā, and others, is a great ocean of the bliss of perpetual love. ||54||
It is an ocean of the bliss of non-dual joy arising from the identity with the attraction of affection;
it is the supreme swoon that dissolves all appearances, radiance, and so forth. ||55||
He assumes a form that is a single mass drawn together by all the senses and the internal organ;
he causes the uninterrupted flow of a stream of singular, great bliss. ||56||
Placing those two devotees on his lap, Hari caused them to drink the nectar of the great bliss of the Supreme Brahman, which is born of his own form.
Then he caused him to drink the honey of the garden trees,
and he caused him to drink the fragrant nectar of the flowers.
He caused them both to attain satisfaction right there in the abode of the Imperishable;
then, rousing them from their meditative absorption, he showed them the world of beings.
The sacred field of Kuṅkumavāpikā, his own human form,
and the divine seven-storied temple of Bālakṛṣṇa made of gold.
Then, rising suddenly, the two of them bowed repeatedly to Hari,
who was filled with the nectar-like essence of priceless and unprecedented beauty.
Having praised, bowed to, and worshipped [Him], and having attained eternal satisfaction,
they were dismissed by Śrī Hari and went outside the palace.
Endowed with divine splendor and adorned with flower garlands and ornaments,
the two of them were on the shore of the Aśvapaṭṭa lake for the purpose of worshipping the gods.
From the western region, the two of them proceeded eagerly toward the northern direction;
there they worshipped Śaṅkara, Kṣetrapāla, and the Goddess.
In the three forms, Hari and Kṛṣṇa beheld Ramā,
who held in her hand a vessel filled with the essence of great nectar.
He caused them both to drink the supreme essence of the Parabrahman;
thereafter, Gaṇeśa, Kārtikeya, Durgā, and Rudra were worshipped.
Among those gods, the Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa,
having received worship consisting of flowers, caused the two of them to drink the nectar.
Then the two of them worshipped Kubera, Indra, Agni, Dharma, and the other deities;
among those gods was the Blessed Lord, the Master Śrī Naravallabha.
Having received worship, he of divine form caused them both to drink the nectar;
they, in turn, honored the gods, beginning with the Sun, the Moon, and Bṛhaspati.
Among those gods, the Blessed Lord, the Master Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa,
accepted their worship and caused them both there to drink that nectar.
The two of them performed the worship of the images of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa, and others;
yet among those deities, they [recognized] the Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa.
Having accepted the offerings there, he caused them both to drink that juice;
thereafter, they both performed the worship of the images of their ancestors.
Among them, the Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the son of Śrī Kṛṣṇa,
accepted their worship and caused those two devotees to drink that nectar.
When those two had worshipped the forms of the Siddhas and the Ṛṣis, the Lord of Creatures accepted their worship and caused them both to drink that divine essence.
In the forms of the lords and goddesses, the Lord of Mādhavī received supreme worship from their images, as well as offerings of flowers and their fragrance.
Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa caused Śrīkānta to drink from those two [breasts] among the Muktānikās, the liberated souls, the incarnations, and the divine forms. (76)
And among the attendants, the cowherds, and the cowherd women headed by Śāradā, as well as among all the deities of the holy fords and the consecrated images, [he offered worship]. (77)
Having attained his own abode, Svāmī Harikṛṣṇa— Bālakṛṣṇa, the Lord of Akṣara—
caused those two to drink the divine nectar of Brahman as if it were a beverage.
Holding in his hand a vessel filled with the essence of Brahman,
and placing his other hand upon [the disciple's] head, he touched those two as they sat upon his lap.
Placing the vessel to his lips,
Kṛṣṇa made him drink that essence— the eternal nectar of divine love— with cup after cup.
Abiding in his form, he caused those two to drink that which consisted of the fruit of their worship—
the deities who dwell at the holy site on the shore of the Aśvapaṭṭa lake.
The lords, the incarnations, the great seers, the virtuous ones, the perfected beings, the female perfected ones, the attendants, the powers, and the wives of Brahmā; ||82||
There, in every place, the Blessed Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa Hari,
having granted them his divine vision, caused the two of them to drink the nectar.
In this way, Hari himself out of compassion caused Mālyavān and Mallikāśrī to drink the nectar of his own supreme Brahman. 84.
By that, they attained divinity like those liberated from the abode of Brahmā;
indeed, they then became possessed of divine bodies, free from the portions of *māyā*.
Through the consumption of flowers, fruits, and other such things, they attained a divine fruit;
from drinking the essence of the Supreme Brahman, their bodies became transformed.
Then, the principles of the five elements dissolved into those two;
all the sense organs likewise became consciousness at that time. (87)
Indeed, even the internal organ (antaḥkaraṇa) became of the nature of eternal knowledge;
having undergone dissolution, its portion of *māyā* vanished and its portion of *brahman* was fully manifested. (88)
Then, having completely transformed all their constituent parts, they became portions of Brahman;
those two became eternally satisfied and filled with great bliss.
When their lifespan had reached seventy-eight thousand years,
those two, Māli and Mallika, having performed worship, attained a divine state.
They became possessed of divine bodies, sixteen years of age;
the pair became equal to Bālakṛṣṇa in beauty. (91)
Then, endowed with dispassion, those two, who had reached the further shore of Brahman, quickly requested Hari while they were in the earth, gardens, houses, and other such places.
Neither the city of Bhadrāyana, nor the earth, nor likewise heaven;
neither truth nor even the sattvic worlds such as those of the night pleased him. (93)
Without the pair of lotus feet of Your Majesty, there is no dwelling in the imperishable state;
therefore, O Kṛṣṇa, protect us both in Your desired imperishable abode. (94)
O Śrīkānta, my two feet are forever offered at Your feet here in this divine, imperishable field of Kuṅkumavāpikā, or wherever You may be. 95.
Having thus entreated him, they both observed silence for a moment; then Hari [spoke]: "Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord, svāhā! (96)
He gave this mantra to them and granted a beautiful celestial chariot;
he sent them off with his eternal attendants driving that divine vehicle. 97.
Then, by the grace of Śrī Hari, having drunk the nectar of the Supreme Brahman, they both indeed went to the imperishable abode in that very same body. 98.
Having bathed in the Brahma-lake at its boundary, they then entered the Imperishable;
remaining engaged in service at the feet [of the Lord], they became liberated. ||99||
Thus did that young female yoginī speak to her mother, Bṛndā,
concerning the greatness of the blissful nectar of the Supreme Brahman, which bestows divine liberation.
She too paused for a moment and reflected on the essence:
"Indeed, that which is to be attained through service comes from the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. (101)
Having recognized it as the supreme excellence, she held it in her heart—
that by performing which even a virtuous woman may attain the highest state.

Thus ends the eighteenth chapter, titled "The Description of how the Mother was told by the Child-Yoginī that the two florists, Māliyāna and Mallikāśrī, through their service with flowers, fruits, and other offerings, attained the eternal abode of the imperishable Brahman— the supreme divine state— by means of that very body, having realized the essence of the Supreme Brahman, and never to return again," from the *Śrī-Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*, in the fourth section, the Tiṣya lineage.
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Goddess beloved of Badarī, to that supreme essence of Brahman, attainable through knowledge, which the illustrious Bālayogin spoke to his own mother.
To whatever extent there is delusion regarding one's own body, even toward the sensory organs within it, even toward one's own heart, and likewise toward oneself, a wife, or a son— (2)
A living being experiences such delusion regarding a husband, wealth, or livelihood;
likewise, whether it be a woman or a man, one should direct that same delusion toward the form of Hari.
One should abandon all delusion toward anyone other than the sage Nārāyaṇa;
one should direct one's delusion [of devotion] toward Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of Śrī, who is the Knower of the Field (kṣetrajña) and Nārāyaṇa himself.
There, one should maintain one's livelihood through Hari, the glorious Puruṣottama;
one should not move the mind that is fixed upon Kṛṣṇa, who is most delightful.
While the Guru exists, one should cultivate affection for Hari and never elsewhere;
one should fix one's attachment on Śrī Hari and on His most purifying nectar.
One should firmly hold Hari Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa within one's very self;
for in Hari, all the pleasures of every sense-object are found together in one place in every way.
"Therefore, the essence of Brahman is obtained even through mere sight;
knowing this, O beautiful one, you should worship Kṛṣṇa with devotion as a wife. (8)
The Blessed One indeed becomes exceedingly gracious toward her through his compassion;
by serving him gradually and steadily, one should propitiate that Lord and Master.
Through service perfected by many cycles of practice, one may attain the *rasa*;
she who is always free from deceit toward the Supreme Beloved, the Lord of Rama, shall become the Unmeasured (*amāyā*).
For her, the stage of perfection shall come, along with eternal fulfillment;
at that time, she is considered fit for the essence of the bliss of the Supreme Brahman.
The ultimate good and the highest state of being a virtuous wife are to be attained;
by that virtuous wife who has achieved this, the nectar of Hari must be drunk.
Day and night, one should maintain mindfulness of the beloved Kṛṣṇa within one's own self;
one should hold the form of the Blessed Lord and serve Him with a divine body.
Like a full ocean, the bliss of that devotee is perpetually fulfilled;
for the connoisseur Kṛṣṇa, there is a plenitude of bliss within his connoisseuress.
Indeed, through devotion characterized by aesthetic relish, Kṛṣṇa bestows his own essence—the nectar of Brahman, great bliss, and the sentiment of being the Beloved—to the devotee. (15)

Indeed, through devotion that is free from fault, divine in nature, joined with the realization of Brahman as the inner controller, and offered to Him, Kṛṣṇa, the connoisseur of rasa, attains that very rasa.
The mistress should be served incessantly by the servant with the realization of oneness with Brahman;
and the servant, too, partakes of the nectar from Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who is the giver of nectar. 17.
Kṛṣṇa becomes beloved and gracious through devotion or even through service;
whether by his command or by following him, the virtuous woman should protect that dharma.
He whose mind possesses uninterrupted thought of Kṛṣṇa attains that most beloved of essences; no one else finds it.
That which is one-pointed concentration arises as a single flavor;
just as the Blessed One is seen, even a human being is no longer merely human.
There is no affliction for her by illusory objects, nor any defeat;
for a transcendental power shines forth in the beloved of Kṛṣṇa. 21.
Kṛṣṇa, the lord of countless women, bestows rasa even though he is untainted;
knowing the Lord thus, she who partakes of rasa worships him as her protector. 22.
She who possesses devotion to the Lord’s vows, heroism, total self-surrender, identification with Him, and whose side is affection for Kṛṣṇa, is a partaker of the aesthetic flavor (rasa). ||23||
Service to the virtuous, service to Hari, and service to saintly women—these are always [recommended], provided they consist of service to Padmāvatī-Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa. (24)
She who, even within this essence-less cycle of existence, is intent upon the essential truth—she, being truly virtuous, indeed abandons everything that creates obstacles. (25)
Service to the great and virtuous, as well as the command and grace of Hari, and total self-surrender, bestow the nectar of the divine Supreme Brahman in every way. (26)
O Kṛṣṇā, she whose food is always provided in every way for the body, the senses, and the inner self,
shall indeed be the partaker of the essence.
The sacrifice of self-surrender is the crest-jewel of all sacrifices;
it is the offering unto the Supreme Person, the Lord of Gods, who is the Supreme Brahman.
Internal giving and external giving in every way—all activity, such as vibration and so forth—exists as being related to Hari in every respect. (29)
Having attained the state of the Lord which is beyond the qualities (nirguṇa) and conduct free from qualities,
and having reached supreme great fortune and the stainless highest station.
That direct attainment of the Blessed One, born from the oblation of all the senses and so forth, is equal to Rādhā and Lakṣmī; by that virtuous woman, [the goal] is always produced. 3.11.
For the vast power of her form must indeed be protected in many ways, so that her affection for the Lord Hari, the most powerful one, may continue to increase. (32)
Through the powerful form of Hari, the state of actionlessness (naiṣkarmya) is perfectly accomplished;
for there can be no fear from this Māyā, nor even from Mahākāla. ||33||
For she indeed is one whose devotion is mature; she is truly a single-minded devotee.
For her who is mature in the state of being established in the true nature of Hari, there is the highest welfare.
For one who knows thus, there is the fulfillment of purpose, immersion in the essence of Brahman, and the attainment of that which is the essence of essences;
indeed, the state of being Śrī is accomplished here.
From the Lord of the Imperishable, those who are liberated become liberated, and others arise as incarnations—both male and female—including Rādhā, Ramā, and the rest. (36)
Even the lords and goddesses become cowherds and cowherdesses;
likewise, the male companions and female companions, as well as the male servants and female servants, also become so. (37)
The *ātivāhika* deities, as well as the presiding deities (*adhidevatāḥ*) and the gods (*surāḥ*), and the spiritual persons (*adhyātmānaḥ puruṣāḥ*), also arise as emanations (*vyūhāḥ*). ||38||
All elemental beings and all luminous entities arise from the form of Hari as the powers of Brahmā, who acts as the inner controller.
One should take refuge in the beloved Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa,
the source of all bliss and joy, the treasury of all delights, and the abode of the essence of Brahman.
He fulfills desires yet is free from desire; he bestows the essence of all bliss; he is both attached and unattached, and though an enjoyer, he is devoid of enjoyment.
It is both smeared and unsmeared, beautiful and devoid of beauty; it is the most excellent and the lowest, delightful and abandoned by delight; it is lying down and free from a bed.
He is both seized by the bride and yet separated from her; he is a householder and yet devoid of a home;
he is without a mark and yet possesses the divine mark; he has the scriptures as his source and yet is without a source.
Indra, as well as the one devoid of power, the powerful one, the instigator of power, the virtuous one, the one devoted to women, the black one, the white one, and the formless one. ||44||

Having thus perceived Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa as the supreme beloved—one who is both inactive and yet possesses divine activity, and who is endowed with every form of virtuous conduct—[she fell at his feet]. (45)
Having directly attained divine yoga, one may obtain the essence of Brahman;
indeed, nothing remains for the acquisition of the essence of love such as this. 46.
The worlds of the gods, the worlds of Brahmā, and all worlds are for the sake of Hari;
the worlds of the goddesses, the worlds of the supreme beings, and the worlds of Śrī are also for the sake of Hari. (47)
The worlds beginning with Guṇātīta, the worlds of the devotees of Hari, the worlds of the liberated and their consorts, and likewise the abodes of all auspicious things; ||48||
Moreover, all [temples] conceived as abodes of prosperity (sampad) become bestowers of liberation when presided over by a divine master. 49.
She who desires the grace of Hari through every kind of transformation, performance, knowledge, and service is the enjoyer of rasa. 4.19.50
Firmly rooted through one's own effort, governing the body, senses, and so forth, and having dedicated all one's possessions for the sake of Hari, one partakes of the nectar of Brahman. //51//
The divine juices of contemplation, the supreme and true flavors of activity, the experiences of bliss and joy, and the festivals of affection, love, and happiness. ||52||
Desire, volition, attachment, and so forth; passion, attraction, and intoxication; the drinking of all nectar and the like; betel-juice and wine; (53)
Having surrendered all her possessions, she enjoys the flavors arising from the union of touch, sweetness, and beauty,
as well as the flavors born of every erotic sentiment.
For her, by whom all is composed of Brahman, there is the consumption of the essence of Brahman;
she is dark as a rain cloud, radiant white, enchanting, and youthful. (55)
Having attained the form whose essence is Kṛṣṇa, which is cultivated through the meditative states of the Muktānikā, Mahāmaṇḍala, and so forth, one becomes a consumer of the nectar of Brahman.
Of one flavor, great splendor, and illuminating the imperishable Brahman; its own abode is full of essence, consisting of the essence of the Supreme Brahman. ||57||
The Blessed One, the Lord of Wisdom, the Supreme Person, the glorious Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, the Master who is replete with absolute liberation, brings this about. 58.
He remains that very same human being, yet he is also non-human;
his garments and ornaments are divine, as are his vehicles and female attendants. (59)
Divine servants, worthy of food, drink, and honor, were intent upon his service;
he is the sustainer of all incarnations and the cause of all incarnations. (4.19.60)
Although the Blessed One is supramundane, he conducts himself here in accordance with the world;
one who understands this will indeed find the state of liberation in the palm of their hand.
No duty remains to be performed for her, as she has reached the end of all means of attainment;
abiding in the bliss of Brahman, she feeds upon the essence of the Supreme Brahman.

And she remains established in the life-force of truth, possessing the true aesthetic flavor attained through devotion to the Lord; this is due to her union with those who are single-mindedly devoted to the Good, and because of her certain realization of identity with Him. (63)
Abiding in non-conceptual samādhi and possessing the form of the qualityless Brahman,
that very woman becomes one who tastes the essence of the Supreme Brahman.
That which is the distinguished, gross-form Māyā is Mādhavī, the essence of whom, though subtle, brings about procreation through union with Kṛṣṇa. (65)
She is always the consort of Kṛṣṇa, his object of enjoyment, and the power of illusion that binds;
though insentient, she becomes divine through her connection with Kṛṣṇa, being filled with the essence of his rasa.
She becomes the one who intoxicates countless worlds with the nectar of Kṛṣṇa;
Rādhā, Ramā, Priyā, and the others are drenched by the nectars of the Supreme Brahman.
In that same way, that Nārāyaṇī nourishes the entire world;
having attained association with the virtuous, she is invincible to those other than Hari.
He indeed relishes the eternal essence of the Supreme Brahman, which abides in innate bliss within his own self, is devoted to its Lord, and bestows supreme peace.
The virtuous woman who is devoted to Kṛṣ�ṇa, who longs for the very nature of Kṛṣṇa, and who upholds the dharma intended for Kṛṣṇa, swiftly attains peace. (4.19.70)
She who possesses intense faith in attaining Hari and in obtaining His nectar finds the nectar born of Kṛṣṇa, which is produced from wisdom. (71)
That passionate woman who always experiences a state of agitation upon seeing Kṛṣṇa and so forth should be understood as one who relies on intense and impetuous faith. (72)
From faith endowed with knowledge of the Great Self, sharpness [of perception] arises;
through the longing for the innumerable flavors, she becomes the beloved of Kṛṣṇa. (73)
Without distinction and without renunciation, she serves the Lord as her husband—the embodiment of Kṛṣṇa—possessing steady wisdom, free from conceptual construction, and firm in her discernment. (74)
He serves her who destroys all sins, bestows the divine essence, and grants fearlessness;
she too, in turn, serves him, her own supreme devotee, Puruṣottama. (75)
The singer sings of the Lord, who is changeless, the knower of all fields (kṣetrajña) in every way, and free from all taints, regardless of whether their conduct is worthy or unworthy. (76)
Considering it a great fortune, she remained with her wisdom fixed on Hari;
devoted to meditation and chanting, she attained the imperishable state.
Devoted to serenity through acts such as salutation, worship, and giving, she is worthy of service by all like a maidservant, just like the one liberated at Badarī. (78)
Resembling a resident of Śvetadvīpa, she was as if established in the city of Śrīpura;
she always took refuge in her chosen deity, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. (79)
Devoted to her husband, she [served] Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of Lords, with her mind, her body, her devotion, and through service to His forms and His devotees. (4.19.80)
Equal to Rādhā, Ramā, Pramā, and Padmāvatī, she remains propitiated;
here she partakes of the nectar of the Supreme Brahman. ||81||
When she abides in the ever-delightful union with the Primordial Black One (Anādi-Kṛṣṇa),
she indeed becomes the divine Brāhmī, the supreme companion of Māyā.
Having attained identity with the consciousness of the Self within Hari, she is filled with the exclusive union of the beginningless beloved Śrī Kṛṣṇa alone. (83)
Through her application toward the Supreme Brahman, she is likewise all-pervasive like Brahman itself,
bearing the countless wonders of the great power of universal sovereignty.
The Great Queen herself becomes like the All-Knowing One, a sovereign empress;
she is the consort of the state of accomplishment, just like Mahāmuktānikā. 85.
Having attained the supreme state of perfection, my beloved, by means of that very same body, went to Goloka, the imperishable divine realm, as well as Vaikuṇṭha and Śrīpura. ||86||
The Indeterminate, the Immortal, the Abode, and whatever others there may be—
there she goes through union with Hari, independent and perceiving the aesthetic flavor (rasa).
O beloved of Kṛṣṇa, even within the three worlds, a good rebirth is attained; for the consciousness of Hari always bestows auspiciousness and the power to accomplish all things. (88)
The deeds of Hari performed by the virtuous, whether they pertain to his physical body or are transcendental, may be either with desire or free from all desire. (89)
All these are indeed divine, always bestowing liberation, purifying, free from deceit, and directly manifest to the virtuous as Lord Hari himself.
The Blessed One is directly present here; you virtuous ones stand visibly upon the earth, possessing eternal natures established in the ancient, imperishable abode. (9.1)
Indeed, she who possesses here the knowledge of this very greatness has truly attained the eternal Cintāmaṇi jewel of the Supreme Brahman. 92.
The highest good arises for that woman who has wisdom as her consort; she whose goal is the imperishable abode and whose husband is the Lord to be attained. (93)

The kingdom is the attainment of the nectar of Kṛṣṇa, and the subjects are the hosts of Muktānikās; bliss is found in union with Śrī Kṛṣṇa—what, indeed, remains for her that has not already been attained? 94.
Apart from Hari, there is no greed for anything else—neither in another world nor in one's own self—not even for the splendors found throughout the realms of Brahmā. (95)
Since her mind is not attached [to worldly things] and she has reached the ultimate pinnacle of solitude, she has attained the virtuous path that is most excellent. (96)
The deities perform worship for that virtuous wife of Brahmā;
for through union with Hari, she has attained a supernatural wonder.
The wish-fulfilling gem, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, rests in her hand;
by means of it, she partakes of the essence of the nectar of love for the Blessed Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa. (98)
"O Mother, having thus eternally attained the nectar of the inner essence of Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, I remain seated upon His lap and partake of it. (99)
"I desire nothing other than the Lord of Rādhā, whether sentient or insentient," having said this, O Badrikā, the young yoginī fell silent.
O Prabhukṛṣṇa, Harikṛṣṇa, Bālakṛṣṇa, Lord of Ramā;
O Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Master, Lord of Mādhavī, Lord of the virtuous! || 101 ||
The young yoginī caused her mother to listen to her devotion; then, immersed in love for the Beloved, she danced for a moment, overwhelmed by the weight of emotion.

Thus ends the nineteenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Supreme Essence of Brahman, Attainable through Knowledge, as Taught by Bālayoginī to Her Mother," within the *Bālayoginīgītā* of the fourth section, the *Tiṣyasantāna*, in the glorious *Lakṣmīnārāyaṇīyasaṃhitā*.
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Goddess beloved of Badarī; then Śrī Bālayoginī spoke again to her own mother, which I shall relate to you accordingly.
Meditation bestows the savoring of the essence of the Supreme Brahman;
it is like the mind, the internal organ, being a ray of the Self.
Having fashioned a mental image, one should worship the Lord within the mind;
for that mind is indeed unmodified when it is ever-attuned to Kṛṣṇa.
That alone is to be understood as the mind of the most excellent devotees of the Lord,
which is eternally attached to Hari and free from the states of cold and heat.
Excellent is that mind to be known, O Kṛṣṇa, which is established unwaveringly in You;
rich with an unbroken stream of affection, it finds its rest in Kṛṣṇa. 5.
Just as the mind is [conceived] like a perfected being, or like a yogi, or like one who is liberated;
likewise, it is like a bride, like a beloved, and like that which is most desired by oneself.
Whatever the mind turns toward Kṛṣṇa, whatever it brings into manifestation,
whatever it is immersed in, and whatever is the cause of its remembrance— that one experiences as the nectar of Hari.

The mind is eternally free from latent impressions when it abides in Hari, who is himself free from impressions; and through service to Hari and the virtuous, one's latent impressions dissolve quickly. (8)
Even a queen who becomes a servant in service behaves like a maidservant dependent on gifts; she obtains the favor of her lord.
Whatever is outside the sphere of the Lord’s and the virtuous ones’ approval should not be done; whatever is pleasing to Kṛṣṇa, however, should be performed.
Even that which is desired in the service of Kṛṣṇa, if it creates an obstacle, must be abandoned by one who would attain the grace of Hari. || 1.1 ||
Like a guru, like a father, like a mother, and likewise like a king,
Hari becomes pleased with that disciple who is truly devoted.
That which always strives for the welfare of the virtuous and for their spiritual clarity—compassion and renunciation—become obstacles to the service and worship of Kṛṣṇa. (13)
Therefore, even if one's compassion and renunciation have become dull, one should worship Mādhava;
adorning oneself with flowers, ornaments, necklaces, and the like, one should propitiate the beloved Lord.
One should satisfy the Lord of Mādhavī with beds, food, drinks, and the like;
one should delight the Lord of Lalitā by offering all one's possessions and through gifts.
One should worship the Lord of Śrī with all the senses and the internal organ; one should propitiate the Lord of Victory with the body, virtues, duties, and so forth. 16.
She should also gladden her devotees through service and devoted attendance;
she who is herself a devotee of her devotees is one who partakes of the essence of Brahman.
Even service to devotees is the supreme cause for Hari’s grace;
the abundance of devotees and their grace, as well as service to devotees, bestow the divine rasa.

Even while remaining on earth, she who is devoted to the service of the virtuous and established in the Imperishable One— no diseases can create obstacles to her service when she is in the company of Śrī Hari.
Being attentive even while hearing the accounts of Hari’s names, one shall become filled with Kṛṣṇa through firm attachment and firm latent impressions. (4.20.20)
Having become Brāhmī, one should worship Kṛṣṇa, the beloved, the master, the lord, the Supreme Person beyond the imperishable, the cause of all causes. 21.
To the Blessed Vāsudeva, the Great Person among persons,
the father of all creations, and the Lord of all embodied beings.

The witness of those engaged in action, the inner illuminator of those whose nature consists of the qualities (guṇas), the supreme and the distinct from all beings, and the one who descends in every incarnation. ||23||
One should serve the Lord Bālakṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, whose lotus feet are worshipped by the divine personages of Brahmā, and who is the bliss of Kambharā. 24.
The Sañjīvanī creeper forms an excellent connection with Kṛṣṇa;
just as the Amṛtā creeper lives even when severed, provided it remains attached to it. 25.
O beloved of Śrī, one should apply oil like the banyan tree;
having produced its own matted roots, it lives even from the base of its branches. (26)

Likewise, even after forming an attachment to the objects of the senses and so forth during the month of Mādhava, she who lives having surrendered her very life-breath partakes of the nectar of Kṛṣṇa. ||27||
Knowing Kṛṣṇa to be his own family member, affectionate, and the fulfiller of all needs,
one should hold Him as the foremost and wander through the planes of Brahman.
Having meditated upon Bālakṛṣṇa as being truly present, having praised him by chanting his qualities,
and having served the Beloved within the heart, one should cultivate the nectar of the secret union.
One should always maintain mindfulness of the glorious Kṛṣṇa, the wielder of the discus, within one's inner heart;
through devoted service, one shall attain the supreme grace of Hari.
One who has resolved upon the goal of Kṛṣṇa should dissolve desirelessness itself;
for that total offering of all one's possessions is, in truth, the surrender of all desires unto Śrī Kṛṣṇa. 31.
Thus, having attained freedom from action, one should cultivate desirelessness toward Kṛṣṇa;
one should worship the Lord Kṛṣṇa through ritual action and serve Him with devotion.

Through affectionate devotion, through contemplation, through the practice of self-surrender, through attachment, through wisdom, through latent impressions, and through the thought of offering oneself to the Self. ||33||
One should acquire it by means of offering one's life-breath, by contemplating the desire for aesthetic flavor (rasa),
by the specific dharma of a virtuous woman, and likewise through practice.

One should acquire the divine nectar of Kṛṣṇa, the nectar of Kṛṣṇa’s essence, the true nectar of the company of the saintly for the sake of the virtuous, and the nectar of all those who belong to Kṛṣṇa. ||35||
She should cast all accumulated things together into the presence of the Lord; the virtuous woman should surrender her body, senses, and actions into Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
She becomes the agent of the vision of the Self, beholding the Supreme Self through the singing of the deeds of Hari and other such means of worship. (37)
One should cultivate the nectar of the Lord through constant mindfulness;
one should worship Hari directly and proclaim His deeds. (38)
One should perform the worship of the Name, protect the dharma of Kṛṣṇa, and, becoming one with the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa, drink the nectar of the Brahman that is Kṛṣṇa. ||39||
One should, through meditative absorption (samādhi), maintain an uninterrupted flow of consciousness toward Śrī Kṛṣṇa;
thus one becomes a heroic heroine (śūravorā) who is affectionate for Kṛṣṇa and knows His majesty. 4.20.40.
She would become an object of compassion through service and thus drink that nectar;
for attachment to anything other than Kṛṣṇa for trivial purposes is indeed illusion (māyā), which would conquer her.
One should carry Kṛṣṇa’s command upon one’s head; thus Māyā shall meet its dissolution.
In this world, one quickly gains the reputation of being a giver of wealth and a giver of sons. 42.
She who possesses such conviction in Hari Kṛṣṇa shall conquer her material nature;
having abandoned her own inherent disposition, she shall forever enter into Śrī Kṛṣṇa. 43.
In that state, the individual soul's identification with Hari is filled with affection;
indeed, this divine bond toward Kṛṣṇa consists of an ecstatic outburst.
Without Kṛṣṇa, one should pass days ruined by great suffering;
but in Kṛṣṇa—the beginningless, supreme Nārāyaṇa—one attains identity with him.
Whether at the end of the body or while still embodied, one should contemplate "Kṛṣṇa, the Beloved";
through inward vision upon the Beloved Hari, direct experience shall arise. (46)
By that, the blissful consciousness of the supreme essence of Brahman shall descend;
Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa himself will indeed bestow his own essential nectar.
She, whose left side is dark, always attains the supreme secret;
for the maintenance of the world and the satisfaction of devotees, Mādhava remains upon the earth. 48.
The beginningless Vāsudeva, Kṛṣṇa, the Lord Nārāyaṇa,
has performed and continues to perform the activities pertaining to dharma, artha, and kāma.
Living beings sing [of them] and hear them; they are indeed liberated from the bondage of illusion and from sin, and attain the supreme state. 4.20.50.
The birth, action, delight, desire, form, movement, and activity of Hari—His divine form grants liberation; everything pertaining to Kṛṣṇa brings about emancipation. (91)
She who performs the worship of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Brahman, endowed with firm conviction, shall become that supreme mistress, the young bride. 52.
Devoted to the service of the virtuous, she is the auspicious one who belongs to Kṛṣṇa and is the consort of Janārdana;
she is indifferent to the offenses of her devotees and looks toward Kṛṣṇa and the others.
Seeking the service of the virtuous and partaking in the nectar of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, she is immersed in the ocean of great bliss; she is worthy of honor, just like Ramā. (54)
She is indeed always full of service, intent on perceiving virtues and making requests;
she is devoted to prostrations like a staff and is endowed with noble respect. (55)
Intent on praying like one in distress for the sake of pacifying the unknown offense, she was deeply immersed in love for Kṛṣṇa and became a vessel for the auspicious blessings of the holy ones. 96.
One considers one's own greatest fortune to be service to the virtuous;
for the sake of pleasing Hari, that service is for the purpose of one's own ultimate welfare. (57)
Having bestowed His entire being, He enjoys the essence of Brahman;
appearing in the form of each individual gopī, He bestows His own supreme nectar.
He became the counterpart of tens of millions of billions of lotus-eyed women;
in marriage, in dalliance, and in private dwelling, he was the bestower of aesthetic delight.
The beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the son of Gopālā, the Lord of Akṣara, the Master, the Beloved, the Son of Śrī Kambharā. (4.20.60)
The Lord of Mādhavī, cherished by the Sovereign Śrī Mahālakṣmī, the Master of ten million liberated souls, the individual self within, and the inner Lord of that [self]. ||61||
Bestowing all desires upon him, he who is established in yoga experiences the essence;
the Lord never makes her—whether she be affectionate, innocent, or separated—[unhappy]. (62)

She experiences in Mādhava that love which transcends the qualities (guṇa), which consists solely of its own essential being, which has arisen, and which is devoid of qualities, being of the nature of Brahman. 63.
For her who has previously attained association with or the sight of the Blessed One among the virtuous,
there shall always arise a divine state, which is the state of Brahman.
For her there is neither illusion nor passion, nor even latent impressions, nor any other [affliction]; O Beloved of Badarīnātha, may she abide in every way [in this state]. (65)
That supreme devotion to Hari, which is equal to the experience of one who has fasted, having attained the grace of the Lord, is intent upon the highest state. 66.

The enjoyer of the bliss of existence, consciousness, and bliss (saccidānanda) belonging to the form of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, having obtained the grace of the virtuous, enjoys happiness in the imperishable abode (akṣara-dhāma). 67.
For the virtuous are indeed propitiated by fire, moon, sun, and lightning;
therefore, they always shine brightly and remain happy in heaven.
The virtuous should be propitiated with auspicious deeds for the sake of attaining the essence of Brahman;
they are filled with the nectar of the consciousness of Brahman and are established in Hari. 69.
Seeking the supreme bliss of the Brahman for one's own welfare, one should indeed acquire the grace of Hari and the virtuous through service in every way. (4.20.70)
He who, having seen the decline and prosperity of the worlds, does not grieve, but worships the divine Śrī Hari—that virtuous person is like Kṛṣṇa himself. (71)
She who has taken refuge in the Dharma of the great devotee, which is absolute, is like one who is dead when such [devotees] are no longer present. ||92||
How can she find her own happiness here, or how could she attain the bliss of Brahman—she who, though a woman of great sin, [yet perceives] the virtue and serenity of the virtuous? (73)
She accepts service and commands; though already pure, she shall attain the Imperishable.
Through association with the virtuous, sins are swiftly destroyed in this world. (74)
The sense organs, the body, the mind, the self, and likewise the intellect—all these are produced here as divine, even leading to supreme liberation. (75)
Then, in the assembly of the virtuous, a woman should remain and strive to attain the unbroken, eternal nature of Kṛṣṇa for the sake of obtaining the essence of the Supreme Brahman. (76)
Just as with Kṛṣṇa himself, devotees of Kṛṣṇa should mutually honor one another;
likewise, they should understand His majesty and practice service [to Him]. (77)
Through association with Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the male devotees and female devotees here become divine; they are Akṣara, liberated, and possessed of the realization of the Nirguṇa state. ||78||
Since they purify all the worlds and are to be served by one another, may those [sages] who grant liberation be pleased; Kṛṣṇa shines resplendently among them. (79)
Rādhā, Ramā, and the other goddesses always shine among the female devotees;
the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa shines among men. 4.20.80.
One should always be gracious toward others, just as the splendors of Kṛṣṇa are mutually radiant;
for it is through grace that the oceans of the nectar of the Supreme Brahman are attained. 8.1
Just as the worship of Hari is auspicious, so too should the worship of the virtuous always be performed by devotees; from that, the bliss of Brahman arises. (82)
The bride of Kṛṣṇa always enjoys the essence of her own bliss, the excellent flavor of innate bliss, the nectar of Lord Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa. (83)
That virtuous and beloved friend was constantly absorbed in uninterrupted contemplation of Kṛṣṇa’s form;
full of love, that chaste woman had attained oneness with the very nature of Bālakṛṣṇa. 84.
In that [place] which is completely filled with the nectar of Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa himself always dwells by force out of love, in order to bestow his own supreme nectar. (85)
Ramā dwells in the midst of the virtuous women, and the Blessed Lord also dwells within Ramā;
there, the essence of great bliss eternally shines forth in Kṛṣṇa.
The beloved friend resides within the aesthetic flavor (rasa), and likewise Hari resides within that beloved friend;
thus, there exists a state of absolute identity among the friend, Kṛṣṇa, and the essence of rasa.
Wherever that virtuous and beautiful lady, who is composed of Kṛṣṇa himself, takes birth—blessed are her mother, her home, and her family members and kinsmen. (88)
Through association with virtuous knowers of Brahman, this supreme news is known:
the direct manifestation of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. (89)
Contemplation and spiritual vibration arise for the virtuous through association with those who know Brahman;
there is no other gain from obtaining a human body except the attainment of Hari.
