When all the senses of the virtuous are always devoted to the service of Hari and intent upon that alone, she indeed becomes his exclusive devotee. 91.
Among all those devoted to Hari, Rādhā is the foremost, just as Lakṣmī is to the Lord;
she alone finds delight in the nectar of the one whose beloved is Kṛṣṇa. (92)
She whose form, being the very nature of Kṛṣṇa, is considered divine,
and who possesses the divinity of the virtuous, enjoys the nectar of Kṛṣṇa’s essence.
Just as rivers [merge] into the oceans, just as moths [fly] into the fire, so do heroes in battles, the truthful, and the Gopīs toward their husband Kṛṣṇa. (94)
For in that same way, all possessions and even sacrifices become absorbed in Hari, the Supreme Lord, who is the Brahman-soul, full and of a single flavor. 95.
She who is absorbed, imperishable, devoted, a divine woman for the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama), possessing unbroken and supreme affection, and joined with boundless love. ||96||
And she who is entirely devoted to Kṛṣṇa through every application of all her wealth obtains and enjoys the eternal nectar of the beloved Kṛṣṇa. ||97||
Existing as the very nature of its own being within the Lord of Light,
it attains aesthetic relish (rasa) upon reaching a state of identity that transcends all boundaries.
Having spoken thus, O Badrikā, she paused for a moment;
for by the power of her devotional practice, the mother had indeed become one who relishes the nectar of Brahman.
Having attained Bālayoginī, Bāleśa, Bālakṛṣṇa, Balīśvara,
and the essence of Bālarasa, one rejoices in the presence of the Mothers.

Thus ends the twentieth chapter, titled "The Description of Attaining the Divine Rasa through the Worship of Śrī Kṛṣṇakānta," within the *Bālayoginīgītā* of the fourth section, the *Tiṣyasantāna*, in the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Goddess beloved of Badarī, my constant companion;
then [the Lord] spoke to Śrīmātā regarding that dharma which the young Yoginī had taught.
Those who are the bulls among the renouncers, those who are the bulls among the yoginīs,
and those who are the bulls among the householders— they all follow after the Supreme Lord.

Whatever virtues are proclaimed for virtuous women, whatever virtues belong even to female servants, and whatever virtues belong to daughters-in-law and maidservants— all those follow after Janārdana.
All those bulls shine before Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of all Mādhavīs, the refuge of all dharmas, and the possessor of supreme righteousness. || 4 ||
All enjoyments, all luxuries, desires, and even riches, as well as powers,
women, and female servants, are joined to the Supreme Self.
Dwelling in the forest, exile, wearing matted hair, being humiliated,
and being clothed in saffron or black garments— these are appropriate even for the Supreme Self.
The stages of life and the social classes are also joined with the Lord of Śrī;
therefore, a woman endowed with faith should serve the Supreme Lord.
Having understood that the son of Kambharā, the beloved of Śrī, is the refuge of all phenomena,
one of small intelligence would instead embrace her own [wife], who fancies herself a scholar.
[They conceive] the Supreme Lord as faultless and omniscient, yet devoid of intellect;
and themselves as the creator of all, and the Supreme Goddess as the doer of all. (9)
[He saw] Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of Lakṣmī, the Lord of Badarī, the Lord of Lalitā, the servant [of the Lord], the one worshipped by Śeṣa and others, and likewise the one possessed of vain pride.
Having thus imputed such faults to Hari-Kṛṣṇa— who is worshiped by the Vedas and Agamas— yet who performs trivial actions and the like, one should speak with contempt.

She does not know the dharmas, she does not find the embodiment of Dharma; she does not recognize the Supreme Lord, but recognizes only the performer of ritual action. Being thus deluded, she does not find the essence of Brahman.
In the southern region, however, one surely experiences the bitter suffering brought about by Yama.
Through association with the virtuous, Lord Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa comes under one's influence;
and toward Hari, the virtuous, and saintly women, one’s self-perception is always auspicious.
That very passionate woman, whose constant production of pleasure gives rise to delight, brings Hari-Kṛṣṇa, her husband, under her control.
Just as the notion of "self" arises toward the body, toward one's wife, husband, and home, toward the mansion, the image, the water, and one's own kinsmen and others; || 16 ||
And likewise for her son, her domain, her own beloved, as well as her senses, her auspicious face, her beauty, her enjoyments, and her amusements—[all these belong] to the Lord Hari. (17)
That very woman protects and repeatedly drinks the nectar of Kṛṣṇa;
she alone brings Kṛṣṇa under her control, and no other.
Whatever the future beloved of Kṛṣṇa does, her very conduct is indeed Vaiṣṇava;
she goes to the temple daily and beholds Kṛṣṇa every day.

The supreme delight in the nectar of stories concerning the news of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, as well as the conduct of the virtuous in assembly and especially residence at sacred pilgrimage sites (tīrtha). 4.21.20.
Delighting in the devotees of Kṛṣṇa, passing one's time in their company, fearlessness toward those who are illusory, and likewise daily maintaining equanimity toward them. (21)

There is always equality among those who are not different from Kṛṣṇa, while Kṛṣṇa Himself possesses excellence. That which is the essential nature of Kṛṣṇa is one thing, whereas everything else is devoid of essence.
All activities and endeavors are for the sake of pleasing the virtuous;
likewise, they consist of contemplating the true nature of Hari and singing of Hari’s qualities. (23)

Everything he has done for the sake of Hari—his entire wealth for the sake of the horse, his very life and so forth for the sake of the horse, even his amorous form and beauty—all that is solely for the sake of Hari. (24)
She whose conduct is always thus is a fortunate woman, beloved of Hari;
she is a knower of the essence of the Supreme Brahman, a Nārāyaṇī, resembling Ramā. (25)
She whose love for Hari has reached its firm root through prior ripening and has entered the heart of the Supreme Brahman,
having attained rest therein, she is a consumer of aesthetic essence (rasa).
Where there is no obscuration whatsoever in the movement of the self that is the reality of Brahman, she becomes the unobscured Brahman-Nārāyaṇī through union with that. ||27||

She was a virtuous woman who had renounced everything else; she was the one who sent away her obstructor; she was the one who welcomed the arrival of the lord of her life; and she was the one who lay down upon the announcement of auspicious tidings. ||28||
She is one who strives to instruct her affectionate companions for their spiritual welfare, and she is both a singer and an instructor of the life stories of her beloved Lord. (29)
She understands her own supreme good to be service to the virtuous and to Hari;
she possesses virtuous ones who are superior, being even more excellent than Brahmā and the other gods.
Indeed, for the virtuous, there is no higher good than union with Hari;
he also brings about the yoga of service for those possessed of great merit.
Affection for the virtuous is like that which one has for a wife, a husband, a son, a mother, a uterine brother, a father, a teacher, one's own body, and wealth. ||32||
She who causes affection for Hari to arise among the virtuous is a vessel of aesthetic essence;
that passionate woman, being ever-attached and tender, becomes one who has achieved her life's purpose.
Through her previous births and other lives, she was devoted to the service of the virtuous Hari;
through her desire for union, she sought rebirth for the sake of His grace and for the sake of service. (34)
Distractions do not afflict her as she devotes herself to the worlds;
for the distractions of separation from Hari take the form of separation even for the virtuous. (35)

They indeed afflict that devotee who is solely intent on the essence of Brahman, having themselves heard of the insults and such directed toward their own beloved, even if those were from the virtuous. (36)
She does not experience agitation in her heart as if she were being insulted;
rather, upon hearing of the honor shown to the virtuous, that beloved of Hari rejoices. (37)
Unable to endure the offenses against her saintly lord, the beloved of Hari remained intent on pleasing her husband Kṛṣṇa, even at the cost of offering her own head. (38)
She who is devoted to Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa is never like a river;
for she is one who has arrived, beyond all doubt, for the sake of Hari’s work. (39)
Competing with her co-wives and friends in the display of affection, she has surrendered all her possessions for the sake of Hari; she would even give away her own head. (4.21.40)
Having received the command, she acts in every way exactly as instructed without any hesitation;
through the tasting of the nectar of the Supreme Brahman, that friend quickly becomes one who is melted with devotion. 41.
Indeed, by means of the body, senses, internal organ, self, and action,
when performed according to the rule of dedication to Kṛṣṇa, one quickly attains that essence.
Even if slightly joined with Kṛṣṇa, it attains divinity at that very moment;
one should indeed employ everything belonging to oneself in the service and other activities of Kṛṣṇa. 43.
She who conducts herself as one solely devoted to the beloved Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa becomes equal to Śrī Rādhā herself in this very month of Mādhava. 44.

And likewise, she who conducts herself in service with devotion to her husband, which is exceedingly beautiful through its self-abnegation, and even with the service of a maidservant, is dear to the Imperishable One. (45)
Constantly manifesting, resembling the imperishable Brahman, she perceives the Supreme Brahman within her own nature, which is the state of Brahman. 46.
Therefore, happiness other than Kṛṣṇa always appears like poison;
in union with Kṛṣṇa there is peace, but elsewhere there is only torment. (47)

Peace exists in the company and in the refuge of those who associate with Kṛṣṇa; through association with the virtuous, and especially through association with Hari, one attains the fulfillment of all goals. 48.
Even through service, the great liberation can be attained by ordinary women;
for noble women who possess the essence of Kṛṣṇa, there is truly no fear of Māyā or Time. 49.
For the noble ones who possess true being, there is indeed no bondage of latent impressions;
for the noble ones established in the Self, there is indeed no fear of rebirth. (4.21.50)
For noble women who possess love for Hari, the noose of death does not exist;
for noble women who serve their devotees, there is truly no fear of the hells.
For those who behold the virtuous, there is no fear of disease or mental affliction;
the virtuous exist as the very form of Brahman, the supreme embodiments of Brahman. (52)
There is no merit equal to serving them, nor is any other liberation known;
if one has the desire for strength, then indeed the virtuous should be served. (53)
The saintly ones are the very embodiments of Śrī Hari, the bestowers of all blessings;
the Supreme is the beginningless Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of Śrī Mādhavī. 54.
He is the Lord of all incarnations, as well as of the liberated souls and of Brahmā;
He is the cause of the mistresses, the Śaktis, and the sovereign goddesses.
The Vyūhas are Vāsudeva and the others; Śrī Kṛṣṇa and the others are the Pūrṇas;
Parśurāma and the others are the Āveśas; and likewise, Pṛthu and the others are the Aṃśas. (56)
Sanaka and the others are the *kalās*, while the sun and the other luminaries are the *vibhūtis*;
the Nārāyaṇas are the *vibhavas*, and the images are the *śaktimūrtis*.
All those auspicious bodies of Brahmā indeed arise from the Supreme Brahman;
they are equal to the Supreme Brahman and should be served for the attainment of the essence of the Supreme Brahman.
All these women bestow complete happiness, being filled with the essence of the true flavor of bliss; they grant the joy of the supreme Brahman and should be served by men and others. 59.
All of them are considered bestowers of liberation, as well as granters of all desires;
they all bestow divine bliss and likewise bring one across the ocean of Māyā.
The upholder of all those incarnations is Puruṣottama, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the son of Gopāla. 61.
The beloved son of Śrī Kambharā, who is dear to ten million billion lotuses, abides in his own syllable and the supreme abode, and is the commander of kings over kings. 62.
He grants his vision in creation wherever there is a desire that fulfills the devotee's longing;
he is enriched by all primordial perfections and is worshipped by all wonders.
The Lord of infinite wonders, who simultaneously assumes all forms,
whose essence consists of millions, billions, and hundreds of millions of bodies, and who is the treasury of the arts of all yoga.
He is the connoisseur among connoisseurs, the one whose conduct is renunciation among the renouncers, the giver of knowledge among the wise, and the fulfiller of the hearts of all. (65)
The author of the fruit of all powers, deceits, arts, and the net of māyā;
the Teacher who stands above all, the beginningless Lord Nārāyaṇa. ||66||
Free from delusion within the bodies of embodied beings, possessing extraordinary majesty, he was moved by compassion to accept the service of his devotees performed with love. (67)
Just as a husband enjoys the pleasures arising from sense-objects provided by his wife,
so too do the ignorant imagine faults in him and consider him to be truly attached.
Just as base men devoid of greatness are merely human,
so too is this delusion and illusion destroyed here by those such as Hara.
Indeed, there is no knowledge of Śrī Hari, but rather a perception of non-existence,
for those people who have attained the state of Brahman and are perceivers of the Self.
They are not deluded regarding Hari; they know the supreme nature [of all things].
Nor are they deluded by māyā; how then could there be delusion concerning Hari at that time?
The Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa is forever untainted;
though he is the enjoyer of all, he remains a non-enjoyer, as pure as a purifying fire.
Women become pure through enjoyment of him, just like the cowherd girls;
men likewise become pure in every way through association with him. 73.
Men who know this, as well as their female devotees, are in every respect considered to be exclusively devoted to knowledge and solely intent on service to the Lord. (74)
For the sake of such as these, Kṛṣṇa causes the eternal nectar of Brahman to rain down from his embodied form and makes those who have taken refuge in him drink it.
Compassion is indeed the primary means for attaining the essence of Brahman from Hari;
taking refuge is also a means, and *prapatti* (surrender) is the supreme means.
Exclusive meditation and steadfast worship are means of accomplishment;
likewise, the fulfillment of commands, service, and affection are means of accomplishment. (77)
Knowledge of his majesty, as well as constant remembrance, the offering of one's very self, trust, and what is called "entrustment" (nyāsa)—these too [are forms of surrender]. //78//
Servitude, service, devotion to her husband, and even goodness—these constitute the state of being a wife, the state of being a mistress, and the infusion of the sentiment of love. (79)
Following the gestures of Kṛṣṇa, the graciousness of the virtuous, and direct association with the truly good—which bestows the nectar of Brahman upon Hari—[are the means]. (4.21.80)
For those who have direct realization of the Blessed One here in this world, their time passes through the recollection of His stories and songs. (8.1)
Indeed, there shall be the direct vision of one's own self, which consists of consciousness transcending the three states and is of the nature of Brahman, as it is united with Kṛṣṇa. 82.
Just as it is with Kṛṣṇa, so it is without doubt in this world within the divine abode,
for one who takes refuge at the feet of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa.
In this world, in the next, and everywhere, Rādhikā dwells;
by the grace of Hari, she becomes the mistress there, while he becomes her servant. 84.
And whatever greatness he knows of the Supreme Self, by way of bliss, power, splendor, majesty, form, and excellent qualities; ||85||
To that extent, the dark-complexioned Nārāyaṇī becomes capable;
nevertheless, the power and other qualities of her husband, Śrī Hari, are limitless. (86)
O Blessed One, the boundlessness of Mādhava’s great sovereignty, beauty, and so forth is such that there exist countless millions of women like me who resemble him. (87)
They have obtained from the presence of Kṛṣṇa qualities, sovereignty, splendor, and the like;
nevertheless, the majesty of the Lord remains forever boundless.
Not even a slight deficiency exists in the Supreme Self;
[He possesses] the capacity, qualities, actions, and so forth, as well as beauty and the bestowing of bliss. (89)
And they become endowed with auspicious qualities in infinite numbers;
through those fragments of Hari’s attributes and through their worship of Hari, they become supreme.
Indeed, those who are devotees of Viṣṇu are born as infinite as the Haris;
nevertheless, they do not possess even an atom’s worth of the majesty and noble qualities of Śrī Hari.
Consequently, [all others] indeed fall into deficiency, whereas He is the most perfect;
He is devoid of depth, limitlessness, boundaries, and the like, as well as being free from the limitations of number.
Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama), remains present; by means of His worship, even women have gone to His abode, becoming equal to Him. 93.
Knowing it to be boundless, the female attendants always serve it;
the handmaidens are ever active and enjoy the essence of Brahman. (94)
Thus, what is the use of much speaking? By means of millions of spiritual practices, one attains the beloved Lord of Badarī, the Lord of Māṇikya, the protector of the virtuous. 95.
"I am [that]; nothing else remains for me to attain. Nothing further remains to be performed by me, who have been wedded by the Wielder of the Discus. (96)
O Mother, all my desires have been fulfilled in Śrī Bālamādhava;
therefore, I am forever the servant of Kṛṣṇa, a female yoginī. 97.
I am Badarīśī, the female ascetic, Brahmaśīlā, and the supreme sovereign;
I am one whose very soul consists of the nectar of love for my beloved Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. 98.
"Though born as your daughter, I experience the very same essence;
I have come here for the purpose of fulfilling the granting of that boon. (99)
I am the dark half [of the moon], the beloved of Kṛṣṇa, as Lalitā and Māṇikī are;
just as Rādhā, Lakṣmī, and Mādhavī are indeed the favorites of Kṛṣṇa.
"O mother, worship that Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa in such a manner.
Having spoken thus to her mother Sureśvarī, the maiden—
The remembrance of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa ceased for a long time;
then Sureśvarī spoke that to her beloved, the god Nikāma.
The goddess Badarī is the one who grants sons; she is Māṇikyā, established in the Imperishable (Akṣara), the supreme sovereign and the consort of Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. 103.
A daughter in the form of Narayani has been born in our home;
she desires no other object of sense-experience except for the beloved Sri Krishna. (104)
"Through union with them, our liberation will surely come to pass; of this there is no doubt.
Having understood this, the brahmin also rejoiced and took refuge in Hari. (105)
Because of her childhood, Bālayoginī became a lifelong celibate;
you are that very Śrī Badarīdevī, the dweller in the hermitage of Badarī.
O Badrīprabhā, you become Badrikā, the very embodiment of renunciation;
O Supreme Goddess, remember this entire account of yours.
You have indeed attained my eternal and constant nectar of love;
by means of this song, you bring about the liberation of women. 108.
Any woman who hears this song of Bālayoginī will indeed speak with affection for Hari and will act like a devoted wife.
She shall attain her lineage, wealth, fame, happiness, eternal life, and her beloved Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Brahman, in His abode.
The accomplishment of the four aims of human life shall be hers;
having received betel-leaf upon the lap of Kṛṣṇa, she shall enjoy its inexhaustible flavor.

Thus ends the twenty-first chapter, titled "The Description of the Eternal Child-Like Yoga, the Essence of Brahman, and the Dharmas that Bestow It," within the *Bālayoginīgītā* of the fourth section, the *Tiṣyasantāna*, in the glorious *Lakṣmīnārāyaṇīyasaṃhitā*.
Śrī Nara-Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Goddess beloved of Badarī; thereafter, that young yoginī, being completely absorbed in Hari, performed the entirety of kriyā-yoga.
She practiced the fourfold great yoga toward Mādhava,
and she entrusted her activities of every kind to her husband, Śrīdhava.
For instance, she made her own body subject to the bed of Śrī Kṛṣṇa;
she joined her own hands together for the purpose of embracing Hari’s neck. (3)
She employed her feet for visiting Kṛṣṇa and for circumambulating Kṛṣṇa and so forth; she employed her tongue for the sake of Kṛṣṇa by means of chanting the glories of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. || 4 ||
She gave her hips for the sake of Kṛṣṇa and provided a comfortable seat upon his lap;
she offered her pleasure, her love, her total devotion, and her desire to Hari.
She offered gestures, emotions, delights, and movements to Hari;
she performed symbolic signs, silent indications, and purposeful actions for Hari.
She provided food, bedding, drink, and recreation for Hari;
she fashioned for Hari a beautiful form, adorned with divine splendor.
She prepared collyrium, dye, cleansing, dressing of the hair,
attire, ornaments, fragrant scents, and decorative arrangements for Hari.
He offered a garland, a necklace, a jewel, a gem, oil, a bath, excellent sandalwood, saffron, vermilion, camphor, and betel leaves to Hari.
She offered lac-dye, hair-ornaments, a braided tuft, a topknot, a creeper-like braid, sesame seeds, a forehead mark, a woman adorned with such a mark, and moonlight to Hari.
She offered laughter, dance, gait, grace, dalliance, play,
physical well-being, and perfect purity to Nārāyaṇa.
He performed belching, breathing, sitting, stretching the limbs of his body,
snapping his fingers, and clapping his hands for Hari.
Singing with sweet voices, keeping time, playing instruments, massaging the limbs,
adjusting the joints, fetching water, and cooking vegetables.
She provided a bed-covering for Hari that was capable of withstanding heat and cold;
in this manner, along with her female friends and companions, she engaged in childhood play and other such activities. (14)
He also brought firewood, sacrificial fuel, fruits, flowers, and leaves for the sake of the primordial Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Beloved. 15.
The Sovereign Lady performed all her arts for Śrī Hari and not for her own sake;
thus she always engaged every limb of her activity for the sake of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
Then he performed the second limb of yoga, contemplation, upon Hari;
he offered all his insights and cognitions to Hari. (17)
All visual perceptions whatsoever, and all auditory perceptions; all tactile perceptions whatsoever, and all gustatory perceptions. || 18 ||
He placed all those [objects] born of the sense of smell— those produced in the waking and dreaming states,
as well as those arising from the states of fainting, deep sleep, the fourth state (turya), and so forth— within Hari.
All means of knowledge, such as perception and the rest, as well as all acts of recognition, all forms to be maintained, and all manifestations whatsoever—[all these are but the Self]. (4.22.20)
She also bestowed upon Hari inference, inferential cognition, and so forth;
as well as analogy, analogical cognition, similarity, and verbal testimony.
He presented to Hari cognitions arising from the association [of words] according to his desire,
as well as presumptive testimony (*arthāpatti*), reasoning (*tarka*), proof (*siddhi*), and final ascertainment (*nirṇaya*).
Non-perception itself, as well as expectation, curiosity, mental reflection, awakening, and likewise self-conceit; ||23||
One should also cultivate the enumeration of virtues and the auspicious dwelling of meditation, as well as affection,
happiness, joy, desire, effort, virtue, and sacred learning.
Impulse, worship, devotion, service, meditation, compassion, action, grasping, remembrance, joy, agitation, and the state of being overwhelmed. ||25||
In this way, her contemplation was always directed toward the meaning of Hari;
then she performed the third limb of yoga, the offering of her life, unto Hari.
The conscious self within the body that lives through the union with the vital breaths—its very life is the attainment of enjoyment, and it has offered that enjoyment unto Hari. (27)
Bliss, joy, consciousness, and light are the very nature of the Self;
indeed, the young yoginī offered that light unto Kṛṣṇa. 28.
She, that young girl, who was the embodiment of existence, consciousness, and bliss, and who was filled with eternal bliss, bestowed the state of existence, consciousness, and bliss upon Kṛṣṇa. 29.
The Yoginī, however, offered herself to Kṛṣṇa, her beloved;
she indeed offered her true being to the one whose nature is reality, and her consciousness to the eternal Consciousness.
One should recognize bliss in eternal bliss, the self in the supreme self,
as well as the state of Brahman, fullness, the state of being the knower, and one's own sovereignty.
O Kṛṣṇa, the child entrusted to you both the status of a teacher and the sovereignty of a king;
then, the fourth [state], which consists of the enjoyment of the essence of the Supreme Brahman, is bliss.

It is a limb of yoga, the extinction into Kṛṣṇa, an immersion in the aesthetic essence of bliss in Kṛṣṇa, the full enjoyment of the essence of the Supreme Brahman, and the arising of identity with Kṛṣṇa. ||33||

The supreme bliss of tasting the joy of unbroken, limitless enjoyment; the state of being absorbed in that very self through a swoon of one-pointed intent upon that taste; and the state of samādhi consisting of that.
It is a state of melting, an invisible essence, and a divine flavor;
it arises from the satisfaction of drinking the nectar of beauty, the sweetness of immortality, and the elixir of life.
She offered that peace, cool as nectar, unto the Supreme Self;
thus was that princess of Badarī, a young female yoginī. (36)
The mother Sureśvarī, seeing that he bestowed the four limbs of yoga upon the Supreme Self, was constantly filled with wonder.
Nowhere does her reality exist as something separate from Kṛṣṇa;
Kṛṣṇa is Kārṣṇī, and Kārṣṇī is Kṛṣṇa—she is that young Yoginī. (38)
Even in the speaker there is no distinction; even the difference in gender has dissolved.
Somewhere that Mātrā is seen, whose essence is Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa. (39)
Having become Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the young yoginī is seen; she is repeatedly seen as Lakṣmī, the Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇī of Badarī. 4.22.40.
Indeed, she attained from the Lord of Yogis the great four-limbed yoga, which consists of activity, contemplation, the individual soul, and the offering of the essence of Brahman. 41.
Then, having thus observed that maiden who was solely devoted to Nārāyaṇa, Sureśvarī said to her daughter: "O daughter, [this state exists] even without the performance of the purificatory rites."
For the body is indeed impure; therefore, marriage is desired.
Through marriage, the constant purification of maidens is brought about. (43)
When the dissolution of the assembly occurred for the maiden Dīrghikā while she was present in the assembly hall of Indra in heaven; 44.
Thereafter, an excellent seat is indeed provided for her;
for Indra, perceiving that she is impure, certainly causes her to undergo purification.
Having sprinkled [him] with water, the king of the gods performed purification;
having perceived that, the lord of the gods was then questioned by the oblong pond.
"Why, O Indra, is sprinkling performed daily upon my seat?
Indra gave this reply: "For you are indeed a young woman. (47)
"For you are an unmarried maiden and thus impure;
therefore, I shall now purify your impure seat here by sprinkling it with water. (48)
Or rather, O daughter, having become married, remain pure; for a woman who is devoid of a husband and permeated by the dust [of menstruation] is indeed impure. 49.
Having obtained a husband through marriage, you shall become pure;
for marriage is the sacramental rite that constitutes union with a husband.
It was created by Brahmā for the sake of purifying the bodies of maidens;
therefore, go there, O daughter, and having performed the purification, become one whose seat is pure.
Having been addressed thus by Mahendra, she performed her own marriage with the Ṛṣi who was suitable to her desire, and thereafter she became pure in her seat.
Therefore, O girl, O young maiden, you must obtain Kṛṣṇa as your husband and lord through a formal marriage ceremony in my house.
"In the presence of the fire and the Brahmins as witnesses, though you are already pure, you shall attain further purity;
honoring my mother's word, partake in the festival of marriage. (64)
Thus addressed, that mother, devoted to her son and knowing the purpose of all dharmas, said "Om" there; the mother attained great joy.
That maiden meditated upon Lord Hari, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the bridegroom who dwells in Kuṅkumavāpikā, the beloved husband of Pārvatī and Badrī. 56.
The glorious Lord, the son of Kaṃbhārā, the cowherd boy who is the supreme person and one's own chosen master, appearing in the form of Nara and Nārāyaṇa.
With her mind deeply immersed for the sake of accomplishing her mother’s heart's desire, she constantly meditated upon Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa during her states of samādhi. (58)
Standing in meditation day and night, there appeared the radiant form of the youthful Puṣṭiyuvanādi-Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the laughing Hari. 59.
The beloved Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, adorned with every ornament of amorous grace,
whose form is enriched by beauty corresponding to beauty itself, is the captivator of maidens.
He, whose limbs possessed a splendor shining like gold, arrived there alone and said to his own wife: "Tell me, my beloved, what do you desire? (61)
"I shall fulfill whatever desire you have; speak what is in your mind.
Then, rising quickly, that joyful young yoginī [spoke].
He fell at his feet and said, "Accept me according to the sacred rite; adorned with the garland of choice and honored in the sacrificial pavilion, I am yours. (63)
O Lord, perform my marriage ceremony in the presence of the deities;
O Lord Nārāyaṇa, make the words of my mother come true.
Having heard what was spoken by the boy, Hari himself, whose form is grace, said,
"Let it be so," and, eager for the wedding, accepted the proposal.
Then Bālā offered him the honey-mixture (madhuparka) as a mark of worship;
he accepted it from Bālā and led her to his mother.
The maiden said to her mother: "O Mother, Kṛṣṇa Narāyaṇa has arrived here out of compassion, fulfilling the desires of those who seek him according to your wish. (67)
O Mother, having worshipped Keśava, who has appeared before you out of compassion in his human form, make yourself fulfilled. (68)
His mother, filled with agitation, offered him a welcome and a seat;
she presented him with priceless water for his feet, and performed the ritual of worship.
He suddenly spoke to the infallible Nikāmadeva who had arrived;
he too, beholding Hari, the Supreme Lord and the lord of his daughter’s life.
Exceedingly delighted, he danced for a moment upon seeing his husband, the lord of the maiden's life, who was receiving the supreme honor from the Supreme Lord.
The Lord of all, an ocean of compassion, appearing in human form,
a guest at his home, gentle in appearance and adorned with every ornament.
Then the mother desired to behold the four-armed form—the divine Śrīsvāmī Kṛṣṇa, Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Lord. ||73||
Having suddenly perceived what was in his heart, the illustrious Bālakṛṣṇa quickly became four-armed, bearing the conch, the discus, and the mace.
Honored by Rādhā and Lakṣmī, and having received the worship of his attendants and others,
he revealed his divine form and once again became a human being.
Then Kṛṣṇa was honored, saluted, fed, and served by Sucandra; he was further adorned with a tilaka mark and garlands of flowers. ||76||
And having been delighted by the formal betrothal of the maiden according to the prescribed rites,
he was then requested to marry the girl according to the marriage ceremony.
Having been dispatched in various ways and entreated to return quickly,
he was honored with blessings and then swiftly vanished into the sky.
Then they all awaited the return of Nārāyaṇa for the wedding festival of Śrī, who had taken the form of a young yoginī.
Then Nārāyaṇa-Kṛṣṇa dispatched a brahmin named Yogīśvaradeva to relate the news.
The Brahmin, having arrived quickly at the temple of Nikāmadeva,
related the account told by Kṛṣṇa to Nikāmadeva.
He described the entire essence of the marriage,
which was to take place at the most excellent moment on the morning of the fourth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Āṣāḍha.
"I shall indeed come with my family for the sake of the marriage at the appointed auspicious moment";
having said this, the brahmin vanished and departed for his own home. (83)
Sureśvarī, her daughter, and the Brahmin Nikāmadeva were all delighted there,
rejoicing in the wedding of their daughter.
Then Nikāmadeva, having indeed written out the marriage contract, quickly dispatched it to Mādhava through the hand of a brahmin.
Having gone to the Kuṃkumavāpikā field, the brahmin Harīśvara presented the document of the auspicious moment that indicated the favorable time for the marriage.
The Blessed Lord Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa joyfully accepted that [gift]; he honored the brāhmaṇa with flowers and other offerings, as well as wealth, jewels, and riches. (87)
The illustrious Gopālakṛṣṇa respectfully bestowed [the gifts] upon the brāhmaṇa;
his mother, Śrī Kaṃbharā Lakṣmī, sang auspicious songs. ||88||
He gave many gifts, erected a pavilion, and distributed documents to his kinsmen that indeed informed them of that [fact]. (89)
Lord Hari Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, together with Lomaśa,
bathed at the holy site of Aśvapaṭṭasara and remained in his own abode.
The women dear to Hari massaged his body with fragrant pastes and bathed him thoroughly with well-ground sandalwood and other unguents.
On the night of the third day of the bright fortnight of Āṣāḍha, the Supreme Lord appeared,
adorned, youthful, robust, and marked with the insignia of a sovereign emperor.
Having had all auspicious rites performed for him by his parents, he was strengthened by the blessings of great sages and gladdened by all the members of his household.
He was accompanied by the deities of the sacred fords, by the liberated ones such as Brahmapriya and others,
and by the hosts of devotees from Saurāṣṭra, who were mounted upon divine horses and elephants.
Accompanied by more than a thousand women at an auspicious moment, he was joined by excellent holy men, all of whom were richly adorned with celestial splendor. (95)
Accompanied by all the people of Kuṅkumavāpikā, he departed;
and those who had received his command set out, joined by a magnificent procession of vehicles.
Women full of great enthusiasm and men endowed with good fortune arrived at the very dawn, during the Brahma-muhūrta, accompanied by excellent offerings. 97.
The village of Dhūnī was pervaded by great gardens and highly adorned;
it was a dwelling situated in a vast garden on the bank of the Karuṇāvārī river. 98.
There, Nikāmadevaka, together with his family and graced by the auspicious sounds of women's songs, found rest.
Accompanied by Brahmins and others, he quickly approached the beginningless Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa, the excellent one who had come for the sake of the maiden, in order to perform the worship.
Seeing him fully endowed with all sovereignty, Varavṛddha attained great joy,
as did his divine wife and his celestial kinsmen.
Then women and men came from Varavāhinī with celestial [attire], as did divine mounts, vehicles, and even divine utensils. || 10.2 ||
The divine gods, the deities, and the goddesses who are dear to Brahmā,
as well as the subjects dear to Hari, possess bodies of celestial splendor.
Having beheld all that was divine, he went forth in great wonder;
he then reflected upon all those ten thousand embodied beings.
For the sake of hospitality, there was sweet food, sweet water, a palace,
all kinds of beds and seats, and most excellent dwellings.
Possessing great fortitude, he performed worship with infinite vessels for food, along with substances, grains, juices, and sugar, while remembering the Lord Nārāyaṇa.
Having touched Hari— the Lord who is the husband of the daughter [of the mountain], who is served by all the Siddhas,
and who is like a wish-fulfilling gem— he reflected upon his own glories.
Honoring his daughter’s husband, he provided for all her needs— sufficient for the sake of Nārāyaṇa and splendid with the festivities of her wedding.
Having obtained her husband as a lord, she no longer experienced fear arising from poverty,
nor even from the power of her daughter at that time.
He reflected upon the riches of the great kings of kings;
meanwhile, in that forest region, there were magnificent gardens on all sides.
At that time, golden palaces filled with lotuses in water rich with the sweet fragrance of fruits and flowers stood all around there.
Then tens of thousands of male and female servants quickly became gods and goddesses,
performing the tasks for the faction of Nikāmadeva.
At that time, the kitchen, the stables for horses, the royal palaces, the women's quarters, and the pavilion were all beautifully constructed of gold.
There were great kitchens with foods, savory juices, honey, sugar,
all kinds of sweetmeats, and vegetables along with liquid dishes.
All the finest fragrances, all the finest milks, and various foods—those to be chewed, those to be licked, and those to be sucked—then became manifest before them. (115)
There were beds, seats, couches, and all things for enjoyment;
nothing was lacking there, and in every house stood wish-fulfilling trees (kalpavallīs).
Just as heaven and Vaikuṇṭha are, so did Dhūnī village become;
its women and men, its animals, its houses, and even the ground of its clay were like those celestial realms.
Everything there became equal to heaven by the power of Kṛṣṇa’s grace;
having honored the elders with boons and likewise treated the subjects with respect.
Having beheld his own abode, which resembled Vaikuṇṭha, Nikāmadeva rejoiced, considering all that divine splendor to have been born of Kṛṣṇa.
He had dwellings constructed, gave female slaves and servants,
caused musical instruments to be played, and had the sounds of the Vedas proclaimed.
Then he quickly had auspicious songs sung everywhere and dispatched various enjoyments, including flavorful foods and water.
He attended upon all the great lords without exception, offering them objects of desire that were exceedingly vast and divinely enchanting, as well as his own devoted services.

Thus ends the twenty-second chapter, titled "The Description of the Fourfold Great Yoga of Bālayoginī; the Arrival and Disappearance of the Beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa following the meditation upon Him for the sake of the marriage rites according to the Mother’s word; and the arrival at Dhūnī Village with Vāhinī for the wedding, the making of it like divine Vaikuṇṭha, and the performance of the *mahīmāna* honors," in the Tiṣya lineage of the fourth book of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nara-Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Goddess beloved of Badarī, to the midday meals as well; all these have been introduced and provide great satisfaction for everyone. (1)
Indeed, all divine nectars were deposited by the Wielder of the Discus;
before them, all illusory flavors became tasteless. || 2 ||
Through the mental resolves of the young Yoginī, all kinds of sweet foods, infused with the essence of Brahman, appeared at the time of the meal.
There, water arose from the Brahma-lake, produced from that Imperishable One;
and from Goloka, milk and other products were brought forth, including curd, clarified butter, and fresh butter.
From Vaikuṇṭha he brought divine vegetables and the like; from Śrīpura, meals; from the Ocean of Milk, milk-rice dishes; and from the Badarī-kṣetra, fruits.
From the world of the Sun, [he obtained] caṭanyas and the like; from the Moon, sandalwood; from the world of Hiraṇya, vessels; and from the world of Śrī, beds.
All kinds of ornaments came from the world of Viṣṇu;
there was nothing new that had been imagined which did not exist there.
Even that which had never been seen or heard suddenly became delightful; it appeared instantly and without delay in the presence of the enjoyer.
When the meal was completed, O Badrikā, mouth-perfumes such as betel-leaf and all other suitable items were then offered.
Then, on that middle day, they found rest within the palaces;
thereafter, following the end of the day, they became ready for their journey.
Then the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa was adorned;
endowed with splendor and beautifully attired, he appeared in the form of an excellent king.
It was inlaid with a thousand fine gems and likewise with a large gem in the center;
it was the most excellent, fashioned from soft gold.
The crown, together with its crest-jewel, was adorned with a halo of radiance;
it rested upon Kṛṣṇa’s head, and the moon was placed upon his forehead.
Collyrium was applied to her eyes, beautiful earrings were placed upon her ears,
and flower-ornaments were set all around, producing a most excellent awakening of her senses.
Garlands made of various fragrant flowers hang from their crowns;
there are golden necklaces set with jewels, accompanied by the Kaustubha gem.
A yellow-colored lotus-stalk is held at his throat,
and upon his chest is a yellow garment adorned with edges woven with gold and silver threads.
A cloth, bright with gold and radiant, was tied around her waist;
she wore reddish-yellow garments made of fine silk.
On his two shoulders he wore an excellent, most superior upper garment, adorned with golden borders and bearing rows of flower garlands. (18)
There were armlets, bracelets with chains on the forearms,
as well as bangles, rings for the fingers, and finger-rings.
For the wielder of the discus indeed wears divine ornaments rich with jewels,
including a girdle fashioned of gold and a sword of golden brilliance.
They indeed carried him, along with coconut fruits and other offerings, as well as a white-colored elephant with four tusks that resembled a mountain. ||21||

It is immensely pure, fashioned with beautiful forms, and possesses the luster of refined gold; it is accompanied by the Mother (Ambā), radiant like the sun, effulgent, and free from all karmic bonds.
Adorned with ornaments and having performed all auspicious rites, the illustrious Narayana was mounted [upon the elephant],
attended by those bearing the royal umbrella and fly-whisks.
The excellent river, frequented by gods, great sages, and humans,
shines like the celestial city, with its divine horses, Garuḍa, and other beings.
And there were lamps of medicinal herbs, clarified butter, and lightning, as well as jewels and divine gems; they provided comfort all around at that time. (25)
Thus, that army, rich in every splendor, adorned with elderly people,
and filled with the songs of groups of women, moved forward.
Then musical instruments were sounded and shouts of victory arose;
a rain of flowers and sandalwood powder was released by divine hands.
The Supreme Lord, honored with auspicious rites such as parched grain and unbroken rice,
proceeded on the back of the elephant toward the wedding pavilion.
It was vast, touching the sky, adorned with variegated cloths,
and exquisitely decorated with golden pillars, branching arches, gateways, and other ornaments.
It was augmented by natural lamps and the like, with golden jars,
pervaded by wish-fulfilling creepers and other ornaments, and resounded with the natural sounds of song.
It was adorned with auspicious shrines, deities,
and statues, and consecrated by the presence of fire-gods and brahmins with their ritual implements.
Having reached such a pavilion, which is honored by all sacrificial fuels, augmented by learned Vedic Brahmins, and is indeed equal to the divine abode, the bridegroom [enters]. (32)
Having dismounted from his elephant and paid homage to the lord of that pavilion,
Hari was hospitably received and honored by his father-in-law as well as his mother-in-law.
Refined by worldly customs such as water-libations and the like, and by garlands and other offerings;
and further honored with unbroken grains and similar items, as well as household utensils. (34)
The Lord of Lords, having been rendered free from obstacles, was led to his abode for rest, into the midst of a great palace within a magnificent golden mansion. (35)
Respectfully seated upon the lion-throne by his father-in-law and others, he was gratified with pearl necklaces, efforts of welcome, and offerings of food and water.
All the guests were honored and made comfortable by being presented with water, betel, sweet foods, and fruits.
There musical instruments are played and auspicious songs are sung;
Vedic mantras are proclaimed, and men and women rejoice. (38)

Then the women and maidens, as well as those wives endowed with good fortune, [adorned themselves] at that time with various divine garments and the like, and with erotic ornaments such as jewelry. ||39||
They adorned that young yoginī with ornaments and with waters purified by holy fords, such as the essence of fragrant oils.
Having bathed [the deity] with yellow sandalwood, saffron, and powdered gold-dust,
[he bathed] the *ghargharī* which was filled with gold, pearls, gems, and other such things.
They also took up a garment shimmering with gold,
a golden bodice made of fine threads, and likewise a waist-cloth.
They gave her a colī, a kucalī, and a golden-colored garment, as well as an auspicious undergarment, a red-colored one, and a fine shawl along with a companion cloth. (43)
Having fashioned the hair-arrangement, the braid, the coiled tresses, and the ornaments, they tied the knot with a *phulaka* and placed a beautiful crown upon it. ||44||
A forehead ornament, a lock of hair, a crest-jewel, and a chain;
a crest-jewel, an ear-ornament, and a small bell for the carriage. 45.
And [he gave] the *natthī*, the *candrikā*, the *phullī*, the *ṭippakī*, the *ratnacakrikā*, the *paṭṭapatrī*, the *phullamālā*, the *mudgamālā*, and the *māṣajā*. 46.
They placed necklaces of cane, necklaces of jewels, and necklaces of joints around their throats;
as well as bracelets, anklets, lion-claw armlets, and arm-bands. 47.
They wore finger-rings, bracelets for the fingers, and lotus-petal-shaped ornaments; they also wore girdles accompanied by jingling bells and small tinkling ornaments. 48.
They placed Kāmbīja bracelets rich with the sound of networks of small bells upon their wrists,
and likewise they placed toe-rings adorned with upward-pointing crescents upon their toes.
Necklaces, pendants, neck-ornaments, earrings,
pearl necklaces and other strings of gems, clusters of jewels, and garlands shaped like cow's udders.
Then she placed her bracelets, girdle, and anklets [upon him],
and applied red lac from her nails to his hands, the soles of his feet, and other parts.
The coloring of the lips, cheeks, temples, forehead, and breasts;
collyrium for the eyes; and gold powder and the like upon the body as part of the attire. (52)
The women placed those [ornaments] upon the girl in order to increase her beauty;
they also fastened auspicious flower garlands upon the bride’s crown.
The women displayed their slight modesty with fine silken garments;
they indulged in chewing betel, eating sweet foods, and drinking water.
Then, when the auspicious moment arrived, they led the bridegroom toward the pavilion,
and with eager anticipation, they brought the high officials and other dignitaries.
Then the aged brahmins, headed by Lomaśa, performed the rites of the conduct of the virtuous;
having washed her feet, the Queen of the Gods performed the *nīrājana* ceremony.
He honored him with parched grain, flowers, parched rice, and other offerings, and then increased his excellence through songs and the Vedas; he [the boy] then took up a clay skull-cup.
Having crushed [the obstacles] and bowed to the gods, his preceptor, and the fire, that king of sages sat down before the sacrificial pit in the pavilion upon the seat that had been shown to him. 58.
He was honored with unbroken grains and flowers by the eminent brahmins and their wives,
while he was drunk in by the thirsty eyes of the village women.
Having brought the divine one into his heart and offered him to himself as if to a beloved,
they then led the young female yoginī to the pavilion.
Accompanied by Sureśvarī, they sang auspicious wedding songs;
meanwhile, the Brahmins quickly honored the maiden with perfumes, unbroken rice grains, flowers, and other offerings.
They caused [the festivities] to increase greatly and sang auspicious songs repeatedly;
they designated the day [for the rite] and settled [the matter] in the presence of the gods.
They also had the maiden worship Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa on the left side, as well as perform the worship of Gaṇeśa and the other deities. ||63||
The binding of the fruit of desire, the worship of the pavilion and the fire, the worship of the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), and likewise the worship of the Brahmins, elders, and so forth. ||64||

Then, for the sake of purification, they performed expiatory rites (prāyaścitta), as well as the ancestral offerings (śrāddha), libations (tarpaṇa), and the worship of the family deities and others. ||65||
Having fashioned a garland of flowers with the hand of the maiden upon the neck of the bridegroom, they caused the offering of flowers, unbroken rice, and other auspicious substances.
O Brahmins, with their own hands they likewise placed a garland upon the neck of the maiden and tied a knot in her garment; thereafter, they performed the rite of giving the name.
They indeed caused these two to perform the circumambulation of the fire four times, as well as prostrations,
worship, and likewise the offering of oblations into the fire.
There, the father, a performer of great gifts, caused the taking of the hand;
he joyfully placed his own hand into the hand of the bridegroom for the sake of the maiden. (69)
Then the celestial sage Nikāmadeva bestowed blessings:
"O daughter, may you always be highly fortunate and ever devoted to Nārāyaṇa."
Bālakṛṣṇa took the hand offered by the girl in his own hand,
so that they might always practice their common duties and live in constant union.
The brahmins offered blessings, while other people gave gifts;
they also presented hand-held wealth consisting of many jewels and other riches.
The father bestowed gifts worthy of honor and sacrificial fees upon the Brahmins;
Śrī Gopāla, Kṛṣṇa, and others gave abundant gifts in great measure.
They indeed bestowed all the great gifts, beginning with the gift of cows;
and there, the bride and bridegroom took morsels of food from one another. (74)
There, in that pavilion, they affectionately placed each other's faces together and played with rings in a vessel of water.
Then the Brahmins offered consolation to the women in a beautiful and auspicious palace, accompanied by songs, as they were together with their husbands.
They laughed and made jokes, and they gave them excellent food;
likewise, they gave them water for drinking and betel-leaf in private.
There they gave a bed as a reward for the young bride;
having obtained it, she served her beloved, and likewise did the guests and the subjects.
Having eaten, the people then went to bed; then, on the fifth day of the bright fortnight of Āṣāḍha, having bathed and eaten, they became eager for what had occurred at dawn.
Then the two husbands, joined by their army, became ready to depart;
and their father, Anikāmadeva, gave them most excellent wealth.
There, she also gave her dowry, which was of many kinds and entirely divine in its excellence, to the glorious Kṛṣṇa-Narāyaṇa. (8.1)
The husband said: "O Kṛṣṇa, take my parents along with you;
in the village of Dhūnī, my parents are suffering due to separation from me. (82)
"Therefore, let them both become yours; O Kṛṣṇa, take them and show mercy.
Then, having approached, they grasped even the feet of Hari.
Nikāmadeva also said, "Lead us indeed to your own home. Hari said, "So be it," and likewise did Gopālakṛṣṇa.
Sureśvarī led those two, her son-in-law and father, to her own Kuṅkumavāpikā; likewise did Nikāmadeva and Bālayoginī. (85)
They went to Kuṅkumavāpikā along with Kṛṣṇa’s army;
and the other people of Dhūnī village who were devotees of Hari also went.
After their midday meal, they all set out;
divine musical instruments were sounded and a rain of flowers fell.
"Māyā has been conquered by Sureśvarī; Kṛṣṇa has been conquered by the offering of her son;
and even liberation has been conquered"—such were the words that arose among the gods in heaven. (88)
Then there was a village equal to heaven, with pavilions made of divine gold;
there were sacrificial halls, laboratories for elixirs, and even kitchens. (89)
As soon as the Supreme Lord had departed, everything vanished instantly;
the gods and others, full of longing, took away the sweet foods and delicacies as his grace.
The holy fords, the gods, and others were struck with wonder at Acyuta;
the male and female servants created by Hari quickly became invisible.
Having led his own army,
Bālakṛṣṇa, the husband of the young yoginīs, arrived at Kuṅkumavāpikā accompanied by his beloved.
All auspicious rites were performed there in Kṛṣṇa’s palace;
the father bestowed gifts, feasts, and honeyed drinks. (93)
He performed worship, beginning with prostrations, and likewise offered gifts;
thereafter, he bestowed wealth and other such things as was appropriate.
Then, full of honor and joy, they departed for their own homes;
and Bālakṛṣṇa gave a golden [ornament] to the father and mother of his bride.
He gave him a temple and all kinds of articles for his permanent residence; they both attained supreme bliss upon seeing their son-in-law, the Lord Hari. 96.

Having attained the great fortune of obtaining a daughter and beholding her joyfully, they both returned; then, having bestowed the girl according to the prescribed rites, he chose them as his bridegrooms.
Those two were joined day and night to the form of Hari for the sake of liberation;
then, on one occasion, Śrī Nikāmadeva questioned that Hari.

O Badrī, having observed that her father-in-law’s mind was indeed set on liberation, she then [taught] that which is the most excellent means for the highest good and brings about liberation right here.
His own son-in-law instructed him in every way in the yoga of liberation,
by attaining which even human beings may quickly obtain release.

Thus ends the twenty-third chapter, titled "The Description of the Feasting and Adornment of the Dignitaries, the Procession to the Pavilion, the Adornment and Procession to the Pavilion of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Ritual Marriage, and the Return to Kuṅkumavāpikā," in the fourth section, the Tiṣya lineage, of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nara-Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Goddess beloved of Badarī; for the sake of your welfare, your father-in-law questioned Hari regarding ultimate liberation—tell me here how that may be attained.
The son-in-law Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa, the incarnate Supreme Person, instructed Nikāmadeva in the means for attaining liberation.
O most worshipful father-in-law, I shall now declare the means for liberation—a yoga of liberation that is very easy to attain, yet difficult for the unfortunate to obtain. (3)
Through direct association with Kṛṣṇa, one is liberated from the bondage of worldly existence;
indeed, by giving everything to Kṛṣṇa, one becomes truly freed from the illusory world.
He who gives his daughter to Kṛṣṇa indeed goes to my supreme abode;
having attained identity with Kṛṣṇa, the daughter uplifts her entire family.
Through devotion to Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, human beings go to His abode; thereafter, they dwell in the imperishable realm (Akṣara), residing in the temple of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
Those who have placed their trust in Śrī Kṛṣṇa indeed attain eternal liberation;
for he whose daughter is Nārāyaṇī has surely attained liberation.
The holy site of Kuṅkumavāpikā certainly delivers the resident;
the company of the virtuous bestows liberation, provided that supreme devotion to Nārāyaṇa has been established.
The company of the virtuous is always the most excellent means for attaining the highest good; through association with faithful and chaste women, wives attain the supreme state.
Through service, the favor of the virtuous is obtained; through that, Hari is attained.
When Hari is attained, there remains no higher attainment for the sake of liberation.
O best of brahmins, this [knowledge] is easily obtained and has been acquired by you;
no other [attainment] remains to be gained, for I am the Supreme Lord.
Having meditated upon Nārāyaṇī Mahālakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Lord,
and having served them with affection, one is liberated from the bondage of karma.
Thus, I am Nārāyaṇa, and Lakṣmī is Bālayoginī;
she who is dear to Badrī and dwells in my beloved Badarikāśrama.
"That Badrikā, your daughter, has been given by you to me as my wife;
thus, by meditating upon her as myself, you shall become identical with my form. (14)
For the welfare of both you and me, direct service is the knowledge that benefits you;
by performing that here at this great sacred site, you yourself shall attain liberation.
Service to the guru, the god, and the ṛṣis and siddhas; association with the virtuous;
knowledge of Brahman as the Self; and devotion—these are the supreme means for attaining liberation. 16.
The yoga of liberation is great, the lord of all yogas, and blissful;
it is the form of Hari, the eternal yoga, the greatest yoga of liberation.
The root of the tree of saṃsāra is always "mine" and "I";
when that sense of "mine" and "I" is joined to the Supreme Kṛṣṇa within me, it brings about liberation.

I am to be understood as the sprout of illusion, and that latent impression (vāsanā) is its very root; the tree possessing the aggregates (skandhas) is the notion "mine," while the fields and houses are its branches. (19)
Wives are its friends, and leaves are wealth, grain, and so forth; it is pervaded by the flower-buds of evil and likewise bestows the filth of suffering and other afflictions.

To atone for that, one should acquire the supreme knowledge of Kṛṣṇa’s greatness through learning; for the tree of the ego must be cut down by the wise. Then, having drunk the supreme nectar of Brahman which bestows divine satisfaction, [one attains liberation].
The wise indeed proceed to the supreme Brahman, the highest state of liberation.
This body is not indeed a brāhmaṇa, nor is the self called a brāhmaṇa;
he who has attained knowledge of Hari is a brāhmaṇa, endowed with the knowledge of His majesty. (23)
The cycle of worldly existence, consisting of "you" and "I," is created by divergent latent impressions;
through the offering of all to me, Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of Brahmins, you and the primordial source dissolve into me.
House, wife, wealth, and lineage—his latent impressions (vāsanās) dissolve as well;
that is a true house where he dwells, and she is a true wife by whom he is liberated. (25)
That is wealth which serves as a companion; that is lineage which is eternal; Nārāyaṇa is the permanent home; and the intellect that seeks liberation is the wife.
Devotion is wealth on the distant path, a companion, and likewise imperishable;
that alone is the lineage of the liberated, and those are the lineages we recognize as such.
The essence of Brahman is the great object of enjoyment by which one always lives;
that which is performed for the sake of liberation is indeed proclaimed as the supreme human goal (puruṣārtha). || 28 ||
He who meditates upon Hari in his own head, throat, forehead, heart,
and as abiding within the self, shall be liberated from bondage.
When there is the dissolution of all desires within me, the Lord,
then one attains desirelessness and enjoys the essence of Brahman.
Just as fire increases through wood and becomes many-fold in its brilliance,
so it is only by providing fuel that it is reduced to the form of ashes, and not otherwise.
In this way, the self increases through merits and becomes brilliantly luminous;
having reduced merits to ashes, it partakes of the essence of Brahman.
Whether it be merit or whether it be evil, that great forest leads to existence;
having surrendered both merit and evil to me, one attains great liberation.
Having known me as the Supreme Self, residing within one's own self, the Lord, the Master,
the Sovereign, and the abode of divine qualities, one is liberated and partakes in the nature of Brahman.
I am Brahman, fixed in the Supreme Brahman, free from the gross; I am Brahman, fixed in the Supreme Brahman, free from the subtle. || 35 ||
I am Brahman, fixed in the Supreme Brahman, free from causes;
I am Brahman, fixed in the Supreme Brahman, free from the ether. ||36||
I am Brahman, fixed in the Supreme Brahman, devoid of place;
I am Brahman, fixed in the Supreme Brahman, devoid of measure. ||37||
I am Brahman, fixed in the Supreme Brahman, devoid of the senses;
I am Brahman, fixed in the Supreme Brahman, devoid of the vital breaths. ||388||
I am Brahman, fixed in the Supreme Brahman, free from all objects;
I am Brahman, fixed in the Supreme Brahman, endowed with divinity. ||39||
I am Brahman, born from the Supreme Brahman, possessing the radiance of knowledge;
I am attached to the Supreme Brahman as His remnant, His servant, and His minister.
Among all creations perceived by my vision, nothing pleases me except Kṛṣṇa.
Thus, by knowing the Brahmic light of the self in this way, one is liberated from worldly existence.
Consequently, there is no suffering of death, no disease, and no hell;
the wise one is not joined with sins, nor is he cooked in the infernal realms.
Neither in the womb nor outside is his dwelling anywhere illusory;
for he is Śvetanārāyaṇa, who has attained Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa.
Indeed, through devotion, service, and worship, he attains me.
Through meditation, through glorification, through worship, and through the recitation of my [mantra];
through praise, through vows, through charity, and through sacrifice—
by means of everything offered unto me, one becomes pure in soul and is born as Brahman.
By means of the mantra "Nārāyaṇa" and by Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa— that is,
Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa— one attains liberation.
Even one who has been drawn out [from worldly existence] through devotion to me attains everything most excellent.
Or he even goes to heaven, the imperishable abode of eternal bliss.
(47) Just as I am pleased by devotion, service, and offering, so I am not pleased by anything else; I am pleased by the service of the virtuous. (48)
O twice-born one, the memory of you is always the root of great blessings, the source of a continuous stream of merit, and the sweet fruit of my life.
Out of intense joy, my hair stands on end as I shed tears of delight.
The people who have taken refuge in me sing the Sāman hymns;
singing of the Supreme Brahman, they abide in the form of Brahman.
Those Vaiṣṇavas who offer prostrations with devotion are purifiers upon the earth.

For those who have attained affection for the illustrious devotees of the Lord, rejoicing in the devotion to Kṛṣṇa, and delight in hearing the pastimes of Hari, their very existence has become fruitful. 52.
He by whom devotion is offered to Kṛṣṇa through the very surrender of everything, and whose being is fixed upon Kṛṣṇa—he indeed is a great devotee (mahābhāgavata). ||53||
He who constantly worships me, meditates on me, and even proclaims my name, being entirely free from all attachment—even if he be a barbarian—he is indeed the best of Brahmins. (54)
He who has set out for the path of liberation and who is truly an object of my compassion—he is a purifier of human beings; he is worthy of worship, just like Hari himself. ||55||
Even a Cāṇḍāla who is a devotee of Śrī Hari purifies others and is indeed holy;
for in his house dwells Śrī Hari, and in his heart resides Śrī Nārāyaṇa.
To him [the gift] should be given, and from him it should be received, for he is indeed the purifier of sinners;
having heard of another sinner, he praises me for the sake of that person's liberation from sin.
Show mercy to one who has sought refuge; show mercy to him who says, "I am yours.
For Kṛṣṇa indeed remains under the control of one who grants such fearlessness to all beings.
A devotee of Kṛṣṇa excels over thousands of Vedic mantrins, tens of thousands of those who have taken religious vows, and even ten million ascetics. (99)
The exclusive devotees of Hari, by means of their divine body, go to the Imperishable;
or else, by that very same body, they attain the supreme state through devotion.
Rich in exclusive knowledge and devotion, sustained by undivided intent,
he is eternally the most beloved of Hari, remaining unwavering in his devotion.
Even in times of adversity, he shall not abandon his unfailing affection for me;
remembering me and taking refuge in me, he shall not depart from my heart.
He who does not study the scriptures, nor performs sacrifices, nor observes vows, nor even possesses refined conduct—
but who bears devotion to Me— he indeed is considered by me to have accomplished all that is to be done.
Even those who have reached the further shore of austerities, sacrifices, and the Vedas do not attain that goal which the practitioners of the yoga of devotion reach without [such] devotion.
Whoever is a devotee of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, even if they are of improper conduct or belong to no stage of life (anāśramī),
nevertheless, like the risen sun of the worlds, they are purifying.
Even those people who are under the sway of their bodies and senses, and who engage in sinful practices,
go to the Imperishable if they are devoted to me and dedicated solely to Nārāyaṇa.
For those whose firm devotion to Nārāyaṇa is unwavering, the happiness of heaven is trivial; their devotion bestows eternal liberation.
In this world consisting of karma, the Lord accepts food, water, and betel from those who have approached him; being pleased, he becomes the bestower of liberation.
For one who does not feed, nor cause to drink, nor serve, nor even worship the Kṛṣṇa, all of that is utterly useless. ||69||
He who does not listen to the discourse is deaf, being shrouded by illusion;
he who does not perceive it at all is blind here, being enveloped by ignorance.
He who experiences no bristling of hair upon the recitation of my names here,
nor even a thrill in his heart, is indeed nothing but a corpse.
O Brahmin, for those possessed of devotion toward me, liberation waits like a maidservant;
but for one whose mind is focused on no other than me, there is the complete destruction of worldly existence in every way.
Yama also daily addresses his host of messengers at dawn:
"Avoiding the Vaiṣṇavas, go instead toward those who are not Vaiṣṇavas. (73)
"Even though I am the wielder of the rod of punishment, I am not the master of those who are devotees of Viṣṇu;
for even one who is ill-behaved or of wicked conduct is liberated if he is a devotee of Viṣṇu. (74)
Possessing exclusive devotion to Kṛṣṇa and graced by the excellence of certainty regarding Kṛṣṇa, he becomes supremely devoted to the dharma of the virtuous, divine, and indeed most excellent. (75)
For one whose devotion to Kṛṣṇa is firm and established in every atom of the body, all goals are within his grasp; liberation is already in his hand. (76)
The illusion created by me binds everyone;
yet for him, that very same illusion becomes favorable, bestowing both devotion and liberation. //77//
They cross over my illusion and take refuge in me with their intellect;
I, the Lord of Śrī, am pleased by their devotion and service, even unto their very selves.
I do not find satisfaction through other means as I do through the offering of my self; worldly existence is a poisonous tree, yet its fruit is auspicious in this age.
Devotion consisting of affection for me, as well as association with the virtuous—his ancestors are pleased by these, and his grandfathers dance for joy. 4.24.80.
O Brahmin, if there is a person in the family who practices association with the virtuous and likewise devotion, then water and food have been prepared by me for the sake of their peace. (8.1)
Nevertheless, people possessed by delusion do not worship me at all;
yet even the wicked who hate me, through the mere remembrance of me, go to my eternal abode.
Even those people on earth who are dull-witted, if they have come to me for refuge, they too transcend illusion and attain the supreme imperishable state. (83)
Even one who is intent on offering salutations to me becomes worthy of homage as an embodied soul, for I am the one dwelling within, beautifying the abode of the heart. (84)
Through my yoga, my devotee is divine and eternally liberated;
one should incessantly bow with the heart to that Kṛṣṇa, the witness of all. (82)
He who, though fully capable of offering salutation, does not salute me, is submerged here in this most terrible cycle of existence and shall not cross over. (86)
Even a single thought and prostration toward Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa within me instantly purifies even a Cāṇḍāla; how much more so, then, other people here? (87)
Whoever, having performed [this rite], bows down to me as Nārāyaṇa with a firm staff-like devotion, attains the most excellent state, intensified by a thousand sacrifices. (88)
For embodied beings running here in this world through the wicked wilderness of saṃsāra, a prostration to me, Kṛṣṇa, provides rest and is a means of deliverance. (89)
Whether sitting or lying down, whether eating or even while moving about, one should utter: "Obeisance to the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. (4.24.90)
"My name is indeed easy to obtain; my tongue was given for the sake of seeking it.
Yet these denizens of hell do not utter it—what a marvel that is! (91)
The Vyāsas born of infinite emanations and the Śeṣas of infinite forms do not reach the end of my playful deeds and names.
They turn back due to the exhaustion of their intellect, never because of a deficiency in my qualities.
O Kṛṣṇa, even one who speaks involuntarily is liberated from all bonds.
He has girded his loins for the sake of the Imperishable in every way;
even in his dreams he remembers me, and this twice-born man is fit for liberation. (94)
Salutations to Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa and to the auspicious Śrī Kṛṣṇa;
though he carries [the staff] with devotion, this devotee has certainly not been fashioned for Yama.
O Brahmin, just as the destruction of blinding darkness occurs at sunrise, so too does the destruction of sins arise through my recitation; and from that, liberation follows.
The great sound of the name of Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa is the provision for the journey;
it wards off all obstacles for those traveling through the intermediate worlds. (97)
Chanting "Śrīkṛṣṇa, Śrīkṛṣṇa, Nārāyaṇa, Śrīkṛṣṇa Mādhava," a person always and at all times attains the Imperishable throughout the ages. (98)
He on whose tongue [resides] Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa-Hara goes to liberation;
the worship of Hari is the essence of all essences for me. 99.
"You are worthy of worship; you are my father-in-law, and you are the father of Nārāyaṇī.
In every way you are to be favored, for you are established in liberation, O giver of honor."
Having obtained me as a son-in-law and having bestowed my daughter as a gift, what else remains for me to attain in liberation? O God who grants all desires, tell me! (101)
All your tasks have been accomplished; the auspicious liberation has been achieved.
O Blessed One, you have fulfilled your purpose; your secret has been declared to me.
Chanting "Prabhu-Kṛṣṇa, Jaya-Kṛṣṇa, Mādhavī-Kṛṣṇa," and chanting "Śrī-Kṛṣṇa,
Lalitā-Kṛṣṇa," go to my imperishable abode.
Chanting "Bālāyoginikākṛṣṇa, Bālākṛṣṇa," and reciting "Kṛṣṇa is my beloved lord; go to my imperishable state," go! 104.

Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter, titled "The Description of How Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, having been questioned by the one named Nikāmadeva regarding the yoga of liberation, instructed him in that yoga," in the Tiṣya lineage within the fourth book of the glorious *Lakṣmīnārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Goddess beloved of Badrī; thereafter Kṛṣṇanarāyaṇa again instructed his own true nature-yoga to that excellent devotee.
For one who exists by taking refuge in Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, whose own form is a human body, liberation is certain in every respect.
Shining in the supreme syllable, the king of kings, the lord of lords,
the source of all incarnations— I am indeed that very Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
Among all the Vāsudevas, I am the supreme Vāsudeva;
I am Ananta-Śrī-Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, the highest of Nārāyaṇas. || 4 ||
Among infinite Blessed Ones, the Blessed One is the most excellent of the excellent;
among infinite persons, I am the Supreme Person.
I am the teacher of the supreme syllable among infinite syllables;
I am the sovereign lord of the liberated among infinite liberated ones.
I am the lord of the attendants of countless attendants;
and I am the great lord of the powers of countless powers.
Among the divine pearl-women, I am the lord of the great pearl-women;
among all virtuous men and women, I am the most excellent and supreme of the virtuous.
I am the greatest of all manifestations, possessing countless riches;
I am the Supreme Person, the possessor of parts, whose forms consist of infinite portions.
I am the performer of infinite entries; I am the Lord of the Great Entry.
I am the Lord and Master of countless, transcendent powers (kalās).
I am the possessor of great majesty among countless majesties;
I am the supreme Lord of Māṇikya, Lalitā, Rādhā, Ramā, and the others.
He is the Lord of the virtuous, the Master of the Imperishable, and transcendent beyond the Imperishable;
He is the Protector of the Self and the Controller of all creators and guardians of the worlds. || 12 ||
I am of the nature of Truth, Consciousness, and Bliss; I am eternally divine and exceedingly beautiful.
I possess a divine form, consist of the single Reality, and am endowed with innumerable joys.
I am the great abode of joy, delight, and bliss;
I am the purifier and the illuminator of all festivals.
Among all the nectars that contain ambrosia, I am the ocean; among the most delicious of all sweet flavors, I am the treasure-trove.
Among divine powers of attraction, I am the embodiment of the Great Attraction;
and among the surges of bliss, I am eternally the surging bliss itself.
He is an ocean of grace, as it were, for all divine favors;
he possesses all beauty and happiness, and is replete with all sweetness.
I am Mādhava, the one who brings about all delightful associations; I am the fulfiller of all desires and the remover of thirst.
And among all forms of satisfaction, I am the giver of satisfaction during the libation;
and among all forms of contentment, being myself satisfied, I am the bestower of contentment.
Of all loves, I am the giver of love, the source of love, and the Lord; of all affections and tender dispositions, I become full of affection. (4.25.20)
I am the lord of all attachments;
I am the giver of nectar and honey among all sweet things, such as sugar. ||21||
Among cool and pleasant things, he is the one who grants the excellence of coolness and comfort;
and among hot things that bestow great bliss, he is the one who grants the comfort of heat. ||22||
Of countless varieties of the erotic, I am the essence of the erotic sentiment; and of all tastes, I am the weight of the supreme taste. ||23||
In the closing of the Āśleṣā [embrace], I am the weight of great bliss;
in all kisses, I am the giver of trembling joy. (24)
I am the bearer of tears of affection; I am the thrill of horripilation arising from love; and I am, in every way, one whose hair stands on end with various kinds of rapture.
I am filled with the stupor of all delusions,
yet I am the giver of rest and the end of all beds, deep sleeps, and states of repose.
Among gardens, I am the great garden; among those who delight, I am Rāma.
Among those with desire, I am the source of delight; and among those who long for love, I am Kāma himself.
I am the delight of those who take pleasure, and the peace of the perfected yogis;
I am the nourishment of the well-nourished, and the supreme strength of the strong. (28)
Among all those who possess strength, I am the fearless one;
among fragrant things, I am the cow Surabhi; and among flowering plants, I am the flower. (29)
I am the fruit among fruits, and I am the element among those possessing elements;
I am the gold among colors, and I am the form among all material forms.
Among those with beautiful throats, I am the sweet-throated; among those with melodious voices, I am the voice. Among songs, I am the sweet song; and among dances, I am the single-minded devotion.
I am the gesture, the emotion, as well as the movement and the sign present in all things; I am union, I am fortitude, and I am the bull of virtuous nature.
I am the desire of all, and I am the boundary for embodied beings;
among all wonders, I am the all-pervading wonder.
Of all curiosities, I am the supreme curiosity;
of women who have attained fulfillment, I am the fulfillment of their actions.
I am the possessor of skill in all kinds of sports, and the bestower of the yoga of eternal bliss among all yogas. (35)
Among all passions, I am the passion that creates the purpose of delight;
and among all beauties, I am the beautiful one, most radiant. (36)
Among intoxicants, I am the intoxicating one; among objects of enjoyment, I am the increaser of enjoyment;
and among those who possess great enjoyment, I am the very embodiment of supreme enjoyment.
Of all liquid substances, I am the Lord whose nature consists of oily moisture;
of all forms of affection, I am natural tenderness. 38.
Of all the magnetizers, I am the possessor of the mass-magnetizer;
of all internal ecstasies, I am the Great Ecstasy. ||39||
Among all those things to be abandoned, I shall become a mild smile;
among side-glances and gestures, I shall be the side-glance and the gesture. (4.25.40)
Among those who possess hearts and those who are heartless, I am the Great-Hearted One;
among all those who draw forth [all things], I am the Great-Drawer-Forth.
Among the most excellent and the most preeminent, I am the one who possesses the most excellent and venerable dharma;
among the most distinguished and the most choice, I am the most distinguished and the bestower of boons.
I possess the great pervasiveness of all-pervading spaces;
I am the playful one who moves within the waves and the sports, absorbed therein. (43)
He is the manifestation of exhilarations and graces, the creator of grace, and is endowed with great contemplation regarding both mental dispositions and aesthetic sentiments.
I am the one who dwells within dwellings, garments, and latent impressions;
