Whether ignorant or well-informed, whether learned or not, a devotee is dear to the Supreme Self; whether stainless or not stainless, a devotee is dear to the Supreme Self.
Whether a woman, a eunuch, or a man, whoever is devoted to the Supreme Self—be they a god, a demon, a rakshasa, a serpent, or even a bird—[is dear]. (3.1)
Whether possessing hooves or a tail, a living being who is devoted to the Supreme Self is dear to Him—
even if that embodied soul consists of illusion, provided he is intent on union with Māyā.
If he is a devotee who has no other object of devotion, he is dear to the Supreme Self;
through his practice toward Kṛṣṇa, the saintly one becomes dear to the illustrious Supreme Self.
He was elderly, free from greed, self-possessed, and without hypocrisy;
he was perfectly disciplined, straightforward, and dear to his master. (34)

To those who abide in the service of the compassionate, who are devoted to great austerity, who have entrusted themselves to me as a deposit, who are full of affection, and whose minds are under control; (35)

For those who are dispassionate and possessed of knowledge, who are self-controlled and likewise generous, who abide in truth and are free from greed, and who perceive the nature of Brahman as the Self; ||36||
The Supreme Lord is pleased with those whose actions are not opposed to devotion to Kṛṣṇa, provided they possess no indolence toward devotion and are entirely free from negligence. (37)
Faith exists toward that Kṛṣṇa, and thus Kṛṣṇa is pleased with him;
moreover, in him there is absolutely no dejection or atheism whatsoever. (38)
Kṛṣṇa is pleased with him who has no thought of self-interest, who possesses no pride in his devotion, and who has no doubt whatsoever regarding Him. 39.
Kṛṣṇa is pleased with a devotee who is ever endowed with enthusiasm, who remembers the Supreme Self, and who is intent upon service as His servant. 40.40.40.
Kṛṣṇa is pleased with one who is constantly endowed with all hearing, all seeing, and the awakening to the ultimate reality; who knows all touch, and is possessed of devotion. 41.

Kṛṣṇa is pleased with a devotee who possesses all-encompassing relish, whose consciousness is enriched by divine fragrances, tastes, and so forth, and who is endowed with sovereignty free from all obscurations. 42.
Whether dwelling in water, dwelling in fire, dwelling on the earth, staying in a cave, or even dwelling in the open sky—Kṛṣṇa is pleased with one who is devoted. 43.
O Meghadhārā, O Dṛḍhadhārā, O Svargadhārā, O Dharādhārā—even for one who possesses devotion, Kṛṣṇa is indeed pleased; it is not otherwise.
Kṛṣṇa is pleased with that devotee who possesses the power to produce fire from his body, who is free from the fear of heat, and who has the power to prevent burning. 45.

He is pleased with the devotee who possesses power even when water is turned into fire, who acts as a protector of fire within the midst of water, who seizes fire within water, and even when his own physical form has been reduced to ashes.
When one is capable of entering another's body and so forth, capable of supporting a mountain, and capable of obstructing the wind with both hands, [the Lord] is pleased with that devotee. (47)
Even when the earth trembles with the mere touch of his fingertip, and though he assumes a thousand forms, Kṛṣṇa is pleased with his devotee who possesses such power.
The Blessed One is pleased with the devotee who possesses the power to travel through space, the capacity to comprehend all sounds, and the ability to obtain whatever is desired. 49.
He is pleased with the devotee who is capable [of enduring] cutting, beating, binding, the revolutions of saṃsāra, the conquest of death, and even dissolution. 4.44.50
Even if one abides in freedom from craving, if one is not devoted to the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa,
and if one is devoid of devotion to Kṛṣṇa, then Kṛṣṇa does not become pleased with one here.
He who sports in the sky and perceives subtle matters attains knowledge of all sounds, provided he does not harbor malice toward him.
Kṛṣṇa is never pleased with that person who remains dry [in heart] toward him.
Even if one perceives all things as being of the nature of light; ||53||
He beholds many divine images and celestial palaces;
he beholds Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Indra, Yama, Agni, Varuṇa, and Īśvara.
Even the planets, constellations, and stars, as well as the subterranean realms, do not perceive themselves or the Supreme Self with such affection and devotion. (55)
If one is devoid of self-knowledge, likewise abandoned by the service of Kṛṣṇa, lacking the clarity of the sattva-guṇa, and deprived of the nectar of Kṛṣṇa’s grace; ||56||
If one is devoid of service to the virtuous, all of that is useless;
it is impermanent, a mere meal for the time being, and at its end, it is indeed worthless.
Lack of sovereignty, ignorance, unrighteousness, and passion—wherever these may exist, if that person is devoted, Kṛṣṇa is pleased with him. (58)
The Lord of All is pleased by devotion, but He is not pleased when devotion is lacking;
Kṛṣṇa is especially well-pleased with those intent on serving the virtuous. (59)
But toward a woman who is devoted to the service of virtuous wives, Nārāyaṇa— the radiant Kṛṣṇa, the compassionate and infallible— is always well-pleased.
Lust is the Paiśāca bond; women are the Rākṣasa bond;
and wealth is the Yākṣa bond. The Lord is pleased by the renunciation of these.
The Gāndharva bond is for dance, while the Māhendra bond is for temples;
the Saumya bond is for fame, and the Lord is pleased by its renunciation.
The solar bond is existence; the progenitor’s bond is lineage.
The bond of the Creator is the abode; the Lord is pleased by the renunciation of that.
The bondage of the Lord of Wealth (Kubera) is indeed prosperity; that of Viṣṇu is [the attainment of] wealth.
The bondage of Yama is latent desire (vāsanā); the Lord is pleased by its renunciation.
Greed is the bond of the Dānavas; craving is the bond of the Daityas;
the objects of the senses are the serpent’s bond; but the Lord rejoices in their renunciation.
Bondage related to fire is enmity; hatred is said to be that of Nirṛti.
Bondage pertaining to hell is sexual, while the womb is the bondage of procreation.
Attachment is bondage; pride is the Raurava hell;
arrogance is the Bhautika bondage, and the Lord is pleased by its renunciation. (67)
Having severed, loosened, worn away,
and destroyed all bonds, the Lord, free from attachment, finds satisfaction in that very state.

But merit is a bond lasting for a year; divine power is its capacity; and the power of Brahman consists in the excellence of the quality of goodness (sattva). When that [merit] is relinquished, the Lord is pleased.
Bondage to the qualityless is that of Kṛṣṇa; devotion is the bondage to liberation.
True bondage is service to the saintly, for the Lord is pleased by its acceptance.
For the virtuous are to be served with one's body, mind, and material possessions;
likewise, virtuous women, when propitiated, grant liberation and should be served by the total surrender of all things.
Hari dwells even in person among the virtuous and the chaste;
he who fulfills all desires is to be served by us, for he is intent upon them.
Oṃ, salutation to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord; Svāhā!
Thus should the Supreme Lord, whose essence is mantra, be constantly recited. (73)
This [mantra], which bestows the fruit of all desires, should be cherished in the heart;
it is the giver of the great bliss of the nectar of liberation and the performer of union with Kṛṣṇa. (74)
One must always remember Hari, thinking, "Lord Kṛṣṇa is my own";
for He is in every way the manifest bestower of all desired objects. (75)
Gifts should indeed be given to Hari; a vow should be observed for the sake of Hari;
penance should be performed for the sake of Kṛṣṇa; and yoga should be practiced for the sake of Hari. (76)
A sacrifice should be performed for the sake of Kṛṣṇa, and a pilgrimage should be undertaken for the sake of Hari;
chanting should be performed for the sake of Kṛṣṇa, and affection should be cultivated for the sake of Hari. (77)
All virtuous deeds should be performed for the sake of Hari;
one should always practice auspicious self-purification for the sake of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. (78)
One should adopt a divine disposition for the sake of liberation in the abode of Hari;
service to the virtuous should be performed like one's own self for the pleasure of Kṛṣṇa. (79)
The supreme imperishable field should be resorted to for the sake of liberation;
Kuṅkumavāpikā should be resorted to for the attainment of the beginningless Kṛṣṇa.
The red field is Kuṅkumakṣetra, the white is Aśvasarovara,
and the black field is Anādi-Śrī-Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, Hari.
These three should always be served with devotion, love, goodness, and faith:
the field of Kokāmukha for love, and the Aśvasaras lake for goodness. (82)
Faith in Kṛṣṇa is to be understood as consisting of three aspects, which is the means for attaining liberation:
love for Kṛṣṇa is constant attachment; goodness is one's own abiding state in Kṛṣṇa. (83)

Faith in Kṛṣṇa, the offering of one's own self consisting of the three qualities, and devotion to Kṛṣṇa—these are the means for liberation; redness is saffron, and whiteness is the essential flavor in Hari. (84)
Blackness, attraction, and the threefold means to liberation reside in Kṛṣṇa; Hari is attached to me, the field, while I am attached to Hari, the essence. (85)
In me, Hari was sown as the seed; therefore, I am indeed Hari.
Attaining identity with Hari, I experience myself as being of the nature of Hari.
To Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa Svāmī, the Lord who bestows all-bliss—thus should the supreme yoga be performed toward Nārāyaṇa Kṛṣṇa. (87)
O Supreme Lord, who carries one across the far shore of existence and the cycle of saṃsāra—may there be well-being for you, welcome to you, and may you also receive our leave. (88)
"The Blessed One should be asked for forgiveness now that worldly honor has been rendered.
Having said this, Lomaśa then brought the assembly to a close in the evening. (89)
Having eaten and drunk, and having received the command of Hari, they went to their own abodes;
for at night they had been properly honored, fed, and worshipped.
Having spent the night sleeping on the ground, they departed in the morning,
praising the name of Hari and the instruction of Lomaśa.
To the illustrious Gopālakṛṣṇa and his mother, the venerable Kambharā, as well as to the sacred field of Kuṅkumavāpikā and the Aśvasaras lake. (92)
Praising Hari, the lords of the gods departed for heaven and other realms;
such, O Badrikā, was the festival celebrating the anniversary of his birth. 93.
In his second form, as the Supreme Soul Śrī Kṛṣṇa, he was made charming and most excellent by the great sage Lomaśa. ||94||
Then, in the evening, the deities beginning with Brahmā quickly abandoned Saurāṣṭra from their celestial chariots and went to the regions of Sindhu. (95)
There, in the city of Śārkara situated in the land born of the Sindhu river, dwells Anādikṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, where the sage Lomaśa also resides. ||96||
Where the sage who recites the Saṃhitā dwells, self-luminous, and where the complete recitation (pārāyaṇa) of the Lakṣmīśa-saṃhitā takes place; 97.
Wherever the sacrifice was being performed and the sages were assembled, they came there, bowed to Hari, and worshipped Him who is beloved by the Vedas. 98.
They uttered shouts of victory, performing the custom of the Jayantī festival, and they again placed offerings at the feet of Kṛṣṇa.
They performed the *ārārtrika* ritual at night and rendered service that bestows happiness; honored with welcomes and the like, they were fed and spent the night there. (4.44.100)
All the deities were gratified by Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa;
having received the command of the Supreme Soul, they were pleased to depart in the morning.
Having offered blessings to the king and others, they departed for heaven.
In the morning, the Blessed Śrī Kṛṣṇa performed his ritual bath;
there were festivals, songs, hymns of praise, and the sounding of musical instruments.
Praises from bards, wandering minstrels, and captive singers resounded on all sides. || 103 ||
Thus, O Badrikā, everything is of the nature of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa;
just as the imperishable field [of salt] becomes like the salt of Saindhava, so did it become.

Thus ends the forty-fourth chapter, titled "The Description of the Presence of Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, the Instruction of Lomaśa, and the Celebration of the Great Festival by the Gods and Others," on the occasion of the twenty-first birthday festival in His second form at the sacred site of Kuṅkumavāpikā, within the Tiṣya lineage in the fourth section of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Badarīpriyā said: O Blessed One, ocean of compassion, after that, what did the Lord do in the land of Sindh? Tell me everything exactly as it happened.
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said: Having risen at dawn on the ninth day, the Blessed One performed his ablutions;
he donned all appropriate attire, ornaments, and finery.
Then musical instruments were sounded, songs of women arose, and the voices of panegyrists were heard uttering auspicious words. (3)
The sounds of Vedic mantras arose near the pavilion,
and the sounds of musical instruments resounded, signaling the awakening of Kṛṣṇa.
Sages, seers, and holy men arrived there for the purpose of worship;
they honored the Supreme Lord with whatever offerings they had at hand.
Then the noble women, the wives of kings, arrived there for the purpose of worship;
they worshipped Hari-Kṛṣṇa and placed that image within their hearts.
Then the king and others arrived there for the purpose of worship;
the lords of the earth honored him with offerings of great value.
The subjects, women, men, sages, and deities came there;
for the sake of worshiping the Blessed One, they honored him according to the prescribed rites.
Having worshipped Hari, all the worlds became fulfilled;
thereafter, the drinking of milk, eating, and other such activities commenced.
At the conclusion, the offering of betel-leaf served as the parting gift; then Rāyahari respectfully bestowed ten million coins upon his guests.
Eagerly, they each bestowed a most excellent reward;
then, those honored ones departed for their own lands by means of celestial chariots.
Having instructed his servant for the purpose of reciting the *Saṃhitā*,
and having arranged for his own illumination along with a lamp of a thousand wicks, he [departed].
Having performed the worship of the *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa-Saṃhitā*,
he became ready to go to his own field, Śrī-Kuṅkumākṣara.
Just then, the king born in the region of Kaccha, named Mādhavarāya, arrived there and entreated the Supreme Lord.
And he entreated the Lord to purify the marshy land on the shore of Lake Nārāyaṇa,
as well as to purify the city of the serpents.
Likewise, the great sages dwelling at the Nārāyaṇa lake,
as well as Dharmāyana, Mokṣāyana, and others, were praying to the Supreme Lord.
Hari said, "So be it," and then set out together with them;
he was thus dispatched by all those mountain kings who were his own virtuous friends.
Honored by his own celestial chariot as it sped along,
he quickly descended from the sky to the land of Kaccha.
The Supreme Lord descended from his celestial chariot onto the shore of Lake Nārāyaṇa;
having made it a supreme and purifying holy site, he bathed there.
Just as he sat down on the bank of the sacred ford, Śaṅkara arrived there,
wandering along the western marshland accompanied by Pārvatī.
Bearing a white form, he was accompanied by four mental disciples:
Sananda, Nandana, and Viśvanandanaka.
Accompanied by Upananda, Hara, known as Sadyojāta,
worshipped the primordial Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Person (Śrī Puruṣottama),
and prostrated himself there like a staff, bowing again and again.
He praised the Supreme Self, the bestower of liberation and the protector of the world.
O Nārāyaṇa, O Hari, O Kṛṣṇa, act in such a way that this Śrī-sarovara, purified by you,
may attain supreme renown.
Hari spoke to the Lord of the Universe, Śambhu:
"O Śambhu, that which was formerly known as Nārāyaṇasara and Śrīsara is now [called] Nārāyaṇasara. (21)
This place, purified by Urvaśī, shall indeed become famous as both the Urvaśī-tīrtha and the Caṭaka-tīrtha. (26)
Likewise, Śrītīrtha and Sadyojātatīrtha, which grants liberation, shall become the great Nārāyaṇatīrtha; of this there is no doubt.
"O Mahādeva Sadyojāta, let this be your dwelling here;
by your name, this great holy site shall be known as Sadyojāta. (28)
And in the course of time, your names shall indeed become other auspicious ones;
that sacred ford shall become Koṭīśvara.
Having spoken thus, the Blessed One gave the command for Śambhu to dwell on the shore of the lake; and there Śambhu made his permanent residence.
At that moment, a divine cow, white and red in hue, arrived there;
she had four horns, four faces, four feet, and four mouths.
Having four hands, four eyes, four fangs, and four breasts,
she quickly descended from the sky and bowed at his feet before him.
She licked the soles of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa’s feet with her tongue;
Hari gave water to her, and she quickly drank it from her tongue.
There, the maiden Sarasvatī, possessing a universal form, appeared;
she praised her own Supreme Self, the beloved of the Lord of Śrī.
Salutations to you, O Anādikṛṣṇakānta; salutations to you, O Ramākānta. Salutations to you, O Śrīmāṇikīkānta; salutations to you, O Lakṣmīkānta. (35)
Salutations to you, O beloved of Sarasvatī; salutations to you, O beloved of Rādhā.
Salutations to you, O bestower of happiness, beloved of Śrī; salutations to you, O beloved of Padmāvatī. ||36||
I am Śakti and you are the Śakta; I am Kṛṣṇā and you are Kṛṣṇa—salutations to you!
I am the divine Bhagavatī, the wife, and you are the divine Lord, the husband and master. ||37||
"Having performed penance, we have arrived from Goloka at your command;
having instructed me, the purifier, establish me here on the bank of the lake. (38)
"O Hari, O Kṛṣṇa, please establish a holy ford here under my name as well.
"So be it," Hari replied to that Sarasvatī, O Badrikā. (39)
On the shore of the Nārāyaṇa lake, he established the auspicious Sarasvata Tīrtha and the great cow Sarasvatī.
Merely by bathing there, it became a purifier for all the worlds, bestowing knowledge, granting self-realization and so forth, and providing the awakening to Brahman. ||41||
The Blessed One gave her purifying names:

Pradhānā, Śrī, Prakṛti, Viśvamātā, Nārāyaṇī, and Maheśvarī—white and red; these twelve are indeed auspicious. (43)

He has a thousand heads, is the soul of the universe, possesses a thousand eyes and a thousand feet;

Adorned with the Kaustubha gem and bearing weapons such as the conch, discus, mace, and lotus,

Salutations to you whose nature is infinite, who move as the cause of all; salutations to you, the supreme Lord, whose essential form is the highest Kṛṣṇa.
Salutations to You, Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Brahman, the Supreme Lord;

O Brahmeśa, Sarvamukteśa, Akṣareśa, salutations, salutations to you!
Salutations to you, the Supreme Self, the Lord of all abodes. 49.
Infinite Viṣṇus like me arise from my own portion;

O Blessed One, Lord of all gods, Lord of Time and Illusion, at all times,

"I desire to remain forever with the god Sadyojāta;

"So be it," Hari said; thus Viṣṇu always made his residence there.
Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa established [his presence] for him at the Pippala tree.
That supreme sacred ford (tīrtha) known as Sahasraśīrṣa-plakṣa indeed came into being;

Then Hiraṇyagarbha, the soul of all, the seed of all creation, arrived from the region of the sky, possessing a full-bodied form and a beard.
The sustainer, the destroyer, the creator of the universe, and the progenitor of all cosmic eggs— Brahmā bowed down and likewise fell at the feet of Nārāyaṇa-Kṛṣṇa.
Having arrived, he offered praise to the Lord of Śrī, Kṛṣṇa Keśava:
"O Hari-Kṛṣṇa! O Hari-Viṣṇu! O Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, O Lord! (57)
O Lord of all, abode of all, bestower of all powers, you who provide protection for all have come here as Nārāyaṇa. (58)
For the welfare of the worlds and for the purification of sacred fords,
Śambhu, Viṣṇu, and Sarasvatī are present here at this Nārāyaṇa lake.
Just as they have prepared their dwellings, so too do my own dwellings please me;
therefore, O Blessed One, command me to establish my residence here.
"So be it," Hari said thus to the Supreme Lord (Brahmā), O Badrikā;
Brahmā then made his dwelling there upon that Palāśa tree.
The tree became clothed in red garments and adorned with red flowers;
it was a purifier for all worlds and a benefactor of sacrifices.
Thus did the gods dwell there, performing what is beneficial for the world;
and then, O Badrikā, a most wonderful and marvelous marvel occurred there.
Listen to that beautiful and divine form which came into being;
in ancient times, Śabalāśva and Haryaśva were indeed the sons of the Creator.
Having attained dispassion through the instruction of Nārada,
seventeen thousand people remained there for the sake of performing austerities.
Having approached Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa there, they all stood before him—
ascetics with matted hair, emaciated, and adorned with rosaries of rudrākṣa beads.
Engaged in the chanting of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa-Svāminārāyaṇa, they were serene in mind and resplendent with an aura of divine luster. ||67||
Having withdrawn the impulses of their senses, they were devoted to celibacy;
peaceful, their minds were fixed on the remembrance of Lord Rādhā, who is beyond all qualities.
Even those who appeared as children, yet were well-nourished and possessed of youth,
performed congregational chanting (saṃkīrtana) while leaping about with great joy.
Clapping their hands and crying out, "Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇasvāmī!
they exclaimed, "Aho! Aho! O Hari, Kṛṣṇa, Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa! (4.45.70)
"O doer of good, O Great Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, O All-pervading Lord, O Master!"—thus crying out, they indeed approached Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. (71)
They prostrated themselves like staffs out of devotion and placed the dust upon their heads;

"You are the bestower of liberation; grant us release from the ocean of worldly existence.

Awaiting Śrī Kṛṣṇa, we dwell here engaged in silent recitation;

"I have come for the sake of liberation; grant me the supreme state of liberation.

Constantly devoted to Nārāyaṇa and dedicated to the service of the gods,

Having in every way made those people staying at the holy site like me,

When Hari indeed came out from the celestial chariot there,

At first, He remained for but a single ghaṭikā upon the tip of the palanquin. (4.45.90)

having honored Him with ritual offerings and ornaments such as crowns and the like.

They performed the nightly lamp-offering and praised the Supreme Lord:

At the Nārāyaṇa-tīrtha, the Śabalāśvas, the Haryaśvas, and the virtuous sons of Brahmā were protected by me; they took refuge in me. ||98||

Having prepared yourselves, performed the rites of the sacred ford, and bowed to those virtuous ones,

"Those who are ready must set forth for the sake of liberation, never turning back.

Having ascended his own celestial chariot, he went to Kuṅkumavāpikā;

Thus, O Badrikā, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Lord of Śrī,

Everything delightful, auspicious, and bestowing heaven and liberation has been told to you;

Even one who is sinful, mindless, and devoid of dharma—

What need is there to speak of others who serve Him as practitioners of devotion?
The compassionate Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa would grant whatever they desire.

Thus ends the forty-fifth chapter, titled "The Description of King Mādhavarāya of Kaccha Bringing Hari to Kaccha; Hari Establishing the Tīrthas of Śiva, Viṣṇu, Brahmā, and Sarasvatī at Nārāyaṇasaras; Causing the Two Forms of Śabalāśva and Haryaśva to Be Made and Granting Them Residence and Liberation at the Tīrtha; and Purifying the Family of King Mādhavarāya in Bhujaṅganagara before Proceeding to Kuṅkumavāpī," in the Tiṣya lineage within the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*. || 45 ||
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Goddess beloved of Badarī, to the purifying and auspicious story of the women of the Kusāra caste, which bestows liberation and is filled with devotion. 1.
Those devotees in the land of Sindh who had taken refuge in Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa then gathered together and formed certain organized communities.
During the auspicious recitation of the Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa-Saṃhitā,
on the morning of the eleventh day (Ekādaśī) of the bright fortnight of the month of Kārtika.
For the purpose of worshiping the Saṃhitā, Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, Śūdras, male servants, and female servants arrived bringing offerings. || 4 ||
To whatever extent they worshipped the Goddess of the Saṃhitā with flower garlands and the like, with saffron, unbroken grains, and sandalwood, with incense, lamps, and excellent food offerings— 5.

Likewise, by means of the *ārārtika* lamp, handfuls of fruit and flowers, the offering of gold, and with gems, jewels, diamonds, and the like, as well as golden ornaments, garments, and so forth; || 6 ||
They all likewise worshipped Vyāsa, who is self-effulgent, with divine and supreme offerings; thereafter, they performed the glorification of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
They performed music enriched with various instruments and filled with the sound of rhythmic clapping, chanting:
"Hare Kṛṣṇa! Bālakṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, O Lord! (8)

As their minds were one-pointed, a great wonder indeed occurred:
a divine celestial chariot arrived, possessing a splendor equal to ten million suns.
There, one named Dyotikā, a Kaṃsārī with a divine form,

The venerable Badrīpriyā said: "How did she who was named Dyotikā come to possess such a divine form?
By what merit did she go to that imperishable abode? Please tell me that. (12)
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Goddess beloved of Badrī; she was indeed a laborer, a servant or maidservant for hire in the service of King Rāyahari. 1.3.
By birth she was indeed a Śūdra woman, Kaṃsārī by name, a maker of vessels and an applicator of collyrium; there she was a servant to the queen of the king, devoted to sweeping and other such tasks.
Devoted to the worship of Kṛṣṇa, that enemy of Kaṃsa was indeed a destroyer of evil;
endowed with self-restraint, she constantly listened to the Lakṣmī-saṃhitā.
Having completely accomplished the duties of the queen and all the duties of the gods,
she performed every task pertaining to the royal residence.
Having performed her ablutions, recitations, and worship, and having assumed a posture of servitude with her body fully extended,
she stands before him with reverence, devoted to the sacred narrative.
Together with a garland of flowers, or with a flower-offering, he constantly worships the reciter with saffron, unbroken rice grains, and ritual seals (mudrās).
Then Karamālā, with a steady mind, having bowed to Vyāsa,
sat down in the assembly for the sake of hearing [the teaching], remaining indeed unwearied.
Her husband, Kusāra, also known as Kṛṣṇasāra, always comes quickly to hear the story and departs swiftly for his work.
Devoted to service of the king, he performs the remaining duties for his wife;
she, full of affection, listens to all his stories in every way.
Having heard and retained [the teaching] at night, she even tells it to her own husband;
such is her devotion, arising from the mere act of hearing the story. (22)
She became purified and was freed from all sins;
by her, the auspicious mantra of Hari was received there from Vyāsa. (23)
"Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Lord, svāhā!
She constantly chants this mantra and likewise performs its glorification. (24)
Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, Śrī Parameśvara;
Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, Śrī Puruṣottama. ||25||
In this way, he prepares his vessel and takes his food only once;

For those noble Kaṃsas who conduct themselves in this manner, there is liberation from sin, the arising of merit, and the grace of Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. (27)
Everything that has arisen by its own nature, he performs as service to the Guru:
sleeping, massaging the limbs, washing clothes, and so forth. (28)

She was further strengthened by the power of devotion arising from the great merit of serving Vyāsa, as well as by the arrangement of Vyāsa’s seat and so forth, and by the sweeping of the assembly hall and other areas. (29)
Through the power of her great merit, the exhaustion of her karma was brought about;

Having ascended a divine celestial chariot, the Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa himself arrived to lead him away; indeed, the Lord is within the range of vision of those who possess divine sight. 31.
Wearing a crown, earrings, and a discus, and clothed in garments, endowed with splendor,

Descending from the celestial chariot, Hari took her by the hand;

Having bowed again and again to his own divine Guru, who is self-luminous and an embodiment of Viṣṇu, as well as to the sage Lomaśa and other holy men; 34.
And having requested forgiveness, the auspicious Muktānikā, possessing a divine body—divine, dark-complexioned like Kṛṣṇa, equal to Rādhā, and captivating—[departed]. (35)
Having become so, she ascended a celestial chariot accompanied by Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa and went to the divine, imperishable abode while those with divine vision looked on. ||36||
O Badrī, that indeed became a supreme wonder—the true fruit of hearing this narrative—and it was likewise the ultimate bestower of great liberation. 37.
That Kaṃsārī, possessing beautiful stripes and appearing like a black antelope, shone forth as if she were the goddess Lakṣmī born within a divine splendor. ||38||
Thus, at that time, many indeed—both men and women who were purifying—having heard this story, became liberated while living in the world and dear to Hari. (39)
O Badrī, nectar is indeed the medicine that makes one free from disease;

Service to the virtuous, service to the guru, devotion, and worship of Hari indeed bring about the supreme divine state of the self and its final liberation. (41)
Listen, O Goddess beloved of Badarī: on the eleventh lunar day of the month of Kārttika at evening, another great marvel occurred there. (42)
The family of the potter indeed became entirely subservient;

Indeed, all the sons and daughters were devoted to the complete recitation of the scriptures;

Moment by moment, he gives exceedingly cool water to drink; he provides the breaking of vessels and the excellent gift of fanning with fans. (45)
The spreading of carpets and the like, the sweeping away of dust and so forth, and the clearing away of the carpets at the conclusion of the discourse when they have become empty. (46)
Protection [of the site], clearing away refuse and the like on suitable ground, listening to the discourse, as well as worship, viewing [the deity], and so forth. ||47||
The entire family of the potter indeed attends the assembly;

Thus, with his sins destroyed, he received the mantra from the true guru Vyāsa;

"Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord; svāhā!

O Hare Kṛṣṇa, O Lord Kṛṣṇa, O Lord Bālanārāyaṇa!

They performed the waving of lamps (mālāvartana) and cried out, "Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa!
They offered service in the assembly of Vyāsa, who possessed immeasurable splendor.

Where the Lord Nārāyaṇa-Kṛṣṇa, joined by Rādhā, descended from his celestial chariot, illuminating all the directions. (56)
There on the ground before the potter, while those with divine vision were looking on,

having attained a divine state through their service to the holy Guru, they became subtle. (5.9)
Through service to the Vaiṣṇavas, through devotion to the sacred narrative, and through the meditative contemplation of Kṛṣṇa with devotion, they then attained the state of being followers of Kṛṣṇa.
Indeed, hundreds of thousands of people there became immersed in wonder;
"Oh, the majesty of this narrative, O Badrikā, which bestows divine liberation! (6.1)
Listen, I shall tell you of a great wonder that occurred thereafter at night;

During the vigil on the eleventh day, they became single-mindedly devoted to Kṛṣṇa; indeed, immersed in love, they were absorbed in the kīrtana accompanied by musical instruments. 63.
Among them, one was a goldsmith’s wife and another was a smelter of metals;
the first was named Sumbālikā, and the other was known by the name Vinodinī.

Proclaiming [his name], they suddenly became absorbed in him; having attained a state of mental restraint and reached one-pointedness, they quickly entered into meditative absorption (samādhi). //65//
In front of those two appeared an eternal, radiant form of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, endowed with youth. (66)
Delightful, with a radiance equal to the sun, moon, fire, and lightning,
she was brilliantly shining, auspicious, well-nourished, and beautiful in every limb.
A celestial chariot, radiant with divine splendor and most wonderful,
was seen there at night upon the earth in the presence of Hari.
Accompanied by many attendants and adorned with pearl necklaces, it was worthy of being seen by those with sight and came within the range of vision for everyone. (69)
While all embodied beings were looking on, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa Viṣṇu touched those two women with his right hand.
At that moment, those two became white and radiant like lightning;
they possessed divine forms, wore divine ornaments, and had exquisitely beautiful bodies.
Their two material bodies, however, vanished right there;
they became divine, perfectly formed, auspicious bodies equal to those of Rādhā and Ramā.
Having bowed to Hari, the two young women ascended the celestial chariot;
then the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the laughing Hari, departed swiftly.
Having ascended his own celestial chariot and taken those two liberated women with him,
he went swiftly to the imperishable abode by way of the divine path through the sky.
Thus, that place became filled with such wonder and amazement;
for the fruit of narrating this story and the like is auspicious and bestows liberation. (75)
O Badrikā, at the time of dawn on the twelfth day, during the Brāhma-muhūrta, a supreme marvel occurred; listen, for I shall relate it to you. (76)
There was a playwright there, skilled in the art of delighting [the audience].
Having performed a vigil and bathed, he rose at dawn during the Brahma-muhūrta.
Having taken flowers, garlands, sandalwood, saffron, fruits, unbroken rice grains, darbha grass blades, sesame seeds, honey, and sugar; ||78||
Taking wheat, white cloth, a gold coin,
and a woolen blanket for the purpose of worshiping the Saṃhitā, he arrived at the pavilion.
Indeed, women circumambulate this collection of verses;
and men, having bowed to and honored it, proceed to worship their teachers. (4.46.8)
There, a skilled musician who had arrived for the purpose of worship began to sing;
he honored that Saṃhitā with flowers and other offerings with great reverence. ||8 1 ||
He performed a circumambulation and then offered the arati-lamp;
at that very moment, his mind being restrained, he entered the fourth state (turyāvasthā).
Deprived of its luster, his body fell right there upon the ground;
at that moment, a divine, radiant, and auspicious celestial chariot arrived.
Suddenly he descended from the sky to the earth like a flash of lightning;
there, Nārāyaṇa-Kṛṣṇa appeared in a divine form. (84)
The Lord, the husband of Ramā and Rādhā, is directly within the range of all;
Hari possesses a divine body free from illusion and is skilled in the art of enchanting.
Having led the liberated soul to his own celestial chariot, he went to the imperishable abode;
O Badrikā, a great marvel occurred there at that very dawn.
At that moment, a certain miserly Brahmin arrived there, bringing leaves, flowers, and water for the worship of the Saṃhitā. ||87||
He stood amidst the throng of women reciting this verse:
"Homage to the one whose form is the *Saṃhitā*, homage to the Lord of Mādhavī! (88)
Salutations to You who abide in the hearts of the stainless ones and who bestow liberation;
salutations again and again to You whose forms are Rādhā, Ramā, Lakṣmī, and Śrī.
Salutations to you, the giver of liberation, the divine mother, and the bestower of knowledge;
salutations to you, the beloved of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, and salutations to you, Māṇikyā.
Salutations to you, the embodiment of the knowledge of Brahman, and to you, the power of the abode;
salutations to the goddess Śrī Badarī, and salutations to you, the goddess Jayā. ||91||
Salutations to you, the beloved, the divine, and the one who has reached the further shore;
salutations to you, the Mother, Mahālakṣmī, and Lalitā. ||92||
"Salutations to you, the giver of Brahman and the giver of union with the Supreme Brahman"—in this manner he praised Harikṛṣṇa, the glory of the Saṃhitās. (93)
Meanwhile, the noble ones did not grant him the opportunity for supreme worship;
however, that stingy king of brahmins worshipped the Supreme Self. 94.
He honored the *saṃhitā*, as well as leaping, dancing,
clapping with the hands, playing the *tāla* rhythm, and making sounds with the thighs.
He blew the ghurghura horn and likewise performed hymns of praise;
at that moment, the human spectators indeed became motionless.
Then, immersed in such chanting with a one-pointed mind and free from all obscuration, he attained oneness with the image and entered through the aperture of Brahma (brahmarandhra). ||97||
From his *brahmarandhra*, a radiance resembling a thousand suns suddenly emerged, indeed blinding the three worlds. (98)
O Badrikā, all the men and women there fell into a swoon from the sight;
however, that [vision], which was like the moon, gradually became peaceful and visible once more. 99.
There, the Lord Anādikṛṣṇanārāyaṇa appeared,
holding by the hand that miserly one named Śrīrāmasundara.
At that moment, a celestial chariot indeed arrived there from the great sky;
Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, having taken Śrī Rāma Sundara with him, [ascended it].
The Lord of Śrī quickly went to His divine body, the imperishable abode;
it was a supreme wonder for all women resulting from the sight of Kṛṣṇa. 102.
Indeed, the men were filled with supreme enthusiasm,
and that body of the miser vanished right there.
Indeed, people who have attained this great wonder see it again through hearing this narrative, as well as through its recitation and worship. 104.
For the illustrious Kadarya, there arose an imperishable divine body;
it became an eternal abode for him to dwell in forever, belonging to the Lord.
Thus, O Badrikā, at the moment of the complete recitation (pārāyaṇa) in the land of Sindh,
liberations for embodied beings indeed arise constantly, perpetually.
From reciting, hearing, and proclaiming this marvel,
there shall be enjoyment, liberation, and even the divine state— the supreme goal.

Thus ends the forty-sixth chapter, titled "The Description of the Liberation by Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa of Vidyotā (named Kaṃsāriṇī) through the hearing and worship of the Saṃhitā, as well as the families of the potter Nararāja, the goldsmith’s wife Ambālikā, the metal-smelter’s wife Vinodinī, the actor Rañjanakovida, and the miserly Śrī Rāmasundara," in the Tiṣya lineage of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nara-Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Goddess beloved of Badarī, to this most purifying narrative;
for in the land of Sindh, there were those who constantly desired to hear the story of the Saṃhitā. || 1 ||
The lord of Kṣārapura arrives by means of a celestial chariot, along with his queen named Ruhāraṇi; he is known by the name Kṣīrodavīra.
Both of you, having honored the reciter in the assembly,
and having likewise honored the Saṃhitā, should bow down to the sages, the seers, and the gurus.
Seated upon thrones worthy of kings, their minds fixed on Kṛṣṇa, those two—
the king and the sage— became purified by that hearing.
For they both received the *mantra* from Vyāsa, their own illuminator:
"Oṃ namaḥ śrīkṛṣṇanārāyaṇāya pataye svāhā. (5)
"O beloved Kṛṣṇa! O Bālakṛṣṇa! O Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa!"—thus they both performed the chanting of Hari’s names by means of their rosaries.
Devoted to the worship of Kṛṣṇa, the two of them performed service for the virtuous, calling out, "O beloved of Kṛṣṇa!
O Hari-Kṛṣṇa! O Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa! (7).
They spoke thus constantly, and every morning they performed worship for Hari,
offering food, incense, a lamp, betel-leaf, and water.
The two highly devoted ones offered their meditation to the Lord of Mālatī;
thus they became endowed with divine qualities.
Always remaining humble like servants in the assembly hall,
they constantly bore the image of Kṛṣṇa, which was the very embodiment of sacred narrative.
The subjects of those two also come together seeking the discourse;
men and women become purified through listening and other such means. (11)
Many of them, having come for refuge, received the mantra of Hari on the twelfth day of the bright fortnight of Kārtika at the place where the narrative was being told.
King Kṣīrodavīra, together with Rūhāraṇyā and likewise with his subjects,
remained there engaged in conversation.
Having heard the narrative of the *Saṃhitā*, he then performed the *ārārtrika* rite;
having obtained the grace of Śrī Hari, he partook of the nectar-like water and tasted it.
There, in the assembly hall, he sat down while the people looked on;
and the queen also then sat down there in his presence.
At that moment, a celestial chariot of divine luster arrived there—
resplendent and presided over by the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa.
From that [lotus], the Lord Nārāyaṇa descended to the side of the assembly hall;
having arrived on the earth, he manifested those two divine forms.
Then the Lord, Śrī Puruṣottama, having taken the two kings in his celestial chariot,
went to the imperishable abode while everyone was looking on.
Beholding that supreme wonder, the people attained great joy; they realized that those two did not possess material bodies there, and thus it was truly magnificent.
Having observed the power of the two kings and the compassion of Nārāyaṇa,
Mādhava leads them to liberation with this very body.
O Badrī, having reflected thus, many eager men and women there became ready to go to the imperishable abode.
There, thousands of virtuous great seers were present,
thousands of elders, and also thousands of women who were without protectors.
Whether they be sinful or sinless, those who listen to this discourse are intensely devoted to going to the imperishable abode of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa. (23)
On the evening of the twelfth day, after the nīrājana ceremony and at the conclusion of the kīrtana, Hari, knowing the auspicious desires of his devotees, [appeared]. (24)

Kṛṣṇa arrived to lead away those devoted ones who had washed away their sins by hearing the sacred narratives, who were immersed in the refuge of surrender, and who had renounced all worldly desires. (25)
Then Hari, having made all those men and women who had received the mantra possess divine bodies, [endowed] them indeed with the nectar of his own body.
Having placed the Imperishable Abode within a truly vast celestial chariot, he departed;
O Badrī, this was a supreme marvel performed by Kṛṣṇa at that time.
Those who were without mantras and without gurus were not at all qualified;
the remaining ones, being unsteady, remained right there at that time. (28)
At the conclusion of hearing that discourse from Lomaśa, they all indeed received Manu there; being purified, they truly became ready for action.

Then the Blessed Lord, the Consort of Śrī, arrived at night, having placed those who were attached to worldly things— possessing divine bodies and accompanied by mantras— within a celestial chariot to lead them away.
Anādi-Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa led them to his own imperishable abode;
thousands of men and women, whether old or young, were freed from all latent impressions.
Devoted to love and affection for the form of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa,
they regard worldly existence as poison and have likewise renounced all desires for the worlds.
With their mental functions ceased, they attained supreme surrender to Kṛṣṇa; and by the grace and will of Viṣṇu, they went to the imperishable abode of Hari.
Oh, how powerful is their good fortune and how mighty is the compassion of Hari,
by which they have attained the imperishable state that is obtainable only through austerities performed for ten million kalpas!
That supreme state which even the sages seek by means of various austerities, both slight and great— that Hari they have attained.
For the sake of which kings even renounce their kingdoms and the earth to perform austerities, yet they do not attain it, even though they have obtained it through the grace of the Lord. (36)
The Lord of the Abode, who was difficult to attain, has now become easily accessible here on this earth;
through his grace toward all embodied beings, he who was invisible has come into the realm of visibility.
Hari is difficult to attain today, yet He is entirely attainable through compassion;
otherwise, how could Hari ever come within the range of vision of the sinful? (38)
The people said: "Oh, how auspicious and supreme is our fortune, that Hari himself has come here to his own home and grants us his personal vision! (39)
But those men who, having obtained such an easily accessible [opportunity], do not cultivate it—they alone are indeed devoid of merit and truly unfortunate. (4.47.40)
Their life becomes like that of cattle, yet it leads to liberation; a human body will not be obtained again, therefore, let them worship Him. ||41||
May they all accept the mantra of Śrī Hari and take refuge in Him in every way; with body, wealth, and intellect, may they serve Kṛṣṇa with great devotion. 42.
The home, the garden, the daughter, the wife, the husband, the sons, the horses, and all riches are flickering; through these, may they attain Kṛṣṇa in this world. (43)
Thus, O beloved of Badarī, the people there spoke to one another;
they took up the mantras of Kṛṣṇa and became Vaiṣṇavas at that time. 44.
Men and women took refuge in Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa and served the holy sages; having thereby attained supreme purity, they remained so forever. 45.
Having become great devotees of the Lord, they awaited Mādhava, wondering, "When will the Lord Nārāyaṇa-Kṛṣṇa lead us to His own abode? (46)
"When will the Lord, having made them his own in person, take their hand?
Thus were those devoted solely to Nārāyaṇa, longing for that very purpose. (47)

From that time on, O Badarī, the regions born of the Sindhu became filled with people, from children to the elderly, who were devoted to solitude and spiritual practice through the power of these stories. (48)
For the most part, having attained divinity, they were accompanied by devoted Bhāgavatas;
here and there, Bālakṛṣṇa granted his own vision from a celestial chariot.
Having given both food and devotees, he leads them to the abode of the Imperishable;
thus does this wonder occur there perpetually, day after day. 4.47.50.
O Badrikā, this news has spread throughout the region, the kingdom, the village, and the city—
that which is the ultimate refuge and the giver of liberation.
Having heard the *pārāyaṇa* of the Lord, meditations lead to liberation;
but having obtained a direct vision [of Him], they go to His abode traveling in celestial chariots.
The Blessed Lord Kṛṣṇa does not take account of the sins of the sinners here; having purified them through His very compassion, He leads them to the supreme, imperishable state. 53.
O Badrikā, having heard this, even others who have committed great sins, their minds terrified by sin,
come and, upon hearing the story, go to the supreme state.
Having heard of such a marvel, which was proclaimed with great honor, sinful and most wicked men arrived at the site of the *Saṃhitā*.
Violent ones, slayers, thieves, ungrateful persons, deceivers, betrayers of trust, drinkers of intoxicants, and even eaters of meat—[these are those who fall]. (56)
Then, impelled by the desire for liberation and terrified by their own past actions,
they took up the dharmas of steadfastness, faith, surrender, and trust in Hari.
Having heard this narrative, men and women attained supreme purity.
Listen, O Śrī Badrikā, to the story of a woman there who was a great sinner. (58)
Ultimately, she became a courtesan named Somikā, who was purifying and the destroyer of all sins, and a bestower of the yoga of Kṛṣṇa; she had five sons.

Those who eat meat and the like, those who drink liquor, those devoted to the injury of living beings, those who consume everything, those who keep poultry and the like, and those who eat the flesh of dogs—[these are the women]. (4.47.60)
The daughters and even the courtesans— all those women of the city—
were born from the mixture of seeds in the wombs of those who lived in the brothel for couples.
Having indeed heard from the leaders of the world the supreme majesty of Hari, and having also learned that the attainment of liberation arises from hearing his stories; ||62||
Desiring the destruction of the sins they had committed and for the sake of uplifting their own kinsmen,
those five daughters and their mother first went to Śarkarāpura.
Desirous of hearing the story of the Saṃhitā, they arrived equipped with the necessary means;
having bowed down to Lomaśa, they made their own request known to him. (64)
The compassionate Lomaśa bestowed upon them the nectar of compassion and strength;
he gave them the water, flowers, leaves, and fruits produced by the grace of Hari.
The vow of eating only once a day, daily bathing in the ocean, the thorough worship [of the Lord], and the constant, profound contemplation of the form of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. (66)
Lomaśa bestowed upon them the renunciation of liquor, meat, and the like, the daily service of virtuous people, and the chanting of the name of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa. (67)
O Badrī, they all remained exactly so, abiding by the words of their guru;
thus, established in their vows for a month, they listened to the narrations of the Saṃhitās.
Their sins were destroyed, their righteousness was purified, and through the grace of eating the fruits of the tree, their bodies became pure. (69)
Then Lomaśa gave them the supreme mantra of the Lord:
*Oṃ namaḥ śrīkṛṣṇanārāyaṇāya pataye svāhā*. (4.47.70)
Then Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇasvāmī gave the mantra "Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa" to them; from the full moon of the month of Kārttika, for that entire month, they all maintained pure-souled and divine contemplations.
Remaining engaged in the complete recitation until the full moon of Mārgaśīrṣa,
they heard the Supreme Self, the beloved of Lakṣmī, abiding within their hearts.
At the onset of night, they offered prayers to the Lord Nārāyaṇasvāmin, Kṛṣṇa;
then, suddenly, they beheld the Supreme Soul standing before them, smiling.
Through the grace of the guru, by the recitation of the mantra, by service to the virtuous, by hearing the sacred narratives, and through devotion, meditation, and steadfastness; ||74||
By the arising of merit, the Blessed Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa granted his vision; he was endowed with millions of desires, supreme beauty, charm, and youth. (75)
Hari is enriched by the ornamentation of all jewelry, beautiful with every kind of grace,
full of all affection and joy, and the bestower of great bliss.
Illuminating the surrounding regions with his splendor and smiling,
Hari spoke to those six for the sake of a boon, and they in turn chose Kṛṣṇa.
The women said: "May Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa be the giver of boons; may he be our supreme boon. And may the imperishable state be our eternal abode for the sake of our residence. (78)
Indeed, through your devotion, the destruction of all sins has not occurred here;
O pure, liberated, and divine one, take us to the supreme state. (79)
"O Badrikā, they thus chose [the boon] from Śrī Hari at that time;
'So be it,' Hari replied, and just then a celestial chariot arrived."
Indeed, there appeared the divine, auspicious Hari, the primordial Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, who possesses a golden complexion and bestows all prosperity. 8.1.
Accompanied by Rādhā and Lakṣmī, he descended from his celestial chariot;
standing before the assembly, he touched them with his hand.
At that moment, their elemental bodies fell to the earth, and they indeed became possessed of divine forms resembling Kamalā. 83.
While everyone looked on, eager and by the command of Kṛṣṇa, they all suddenly ascended that celestial chariot together with Bālakṛṣṇa. 84.
In the sky, however, there was a celestial vehicle that went toward the imperishable abode;
at that time, there were shouts of victory, and it was indeed a great marvel.
"Aha! Though they were of sinful conduct, by hearing [the name] of Hari they obtained Him as their husband and reached the imperishable abode; for such is the greatness of devotion. (86)
The compassionate Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the venerable Svāmivallabha, certainly leads those burdened with great sins and even more heinous crimes after purifying them. 87.
"The supreme, eternal state—indeed, there is no need for deliberation on this matter.
Having heard this, O Badrikā, the others were then struck with wonder.
They said to one another, "Oh friends, a story about our village courtesan has been told!
She who was named Somikā went there with her five sons to hear it."
She departed by means of a celestial chariot to the supreme abode, the realm of Hari;
blessed was that Somikā, and blessed were those five daughters.
Aruṇānī, Pāṭalānī, Dhavalānī, Mṛṇālinī, and Kiñjalkānī—these five daughters, having become goddesses, attained the Imperishable. (91)
"Oh, we shall go for refuge to the auspicious Śrī Kṛṣṇa;
having directly attained Hari as our husband, we shall effect our own liberation. (92)
Thus, having decided upon this conversation, thousands of courtesans, who were skilled in the arts of amorous dalliance, arrived there to listen to one another.
O Badarī, for those who perform the śrāddha rite, even during a pilgrimage, the fruit born of an Aśvamedha sacrifice arises at every step; such was the case for them. 94.
At that time, their sins were destroyed by visiting the sacred fords;
having bathed, stayed there, and heard the sacred narrative, they indeed received the mantra from Lomaśa.
On the eleventh day of the dark fortnight of Pauṣa, at the conclusion of those stories,
they beheld a golden celestial chariot that had arrived from the sky even at dawn.
Then Hari descended from that great vehicle, which was joined with the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, to the vicinity of the hall of stories. 97.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa repeatedly performed the sprinkling with water brought from his celestial chariot upon the assembly of courtesans. (98)
Having reached Kaṇva’s ears, they quickly cast off their material bodies and, becoming divine pearl-like maidens, stood in the presence of Kṛṣṇa.
While all the worlds were looking on, Kṛṣṇa, having taken [them] in his celestial chariot,
went to the Imperishable Abode accompanied by thousands of liberated souls.
And having bathed in the lake of Brahman, those pure women became equal to Śrī Kamalā;
by the grace of Kṛṣṇa through this narration, they became liberated souls in his abode.
Through faith one obtains the fruit; likewise, through devotion one attains clarity;
through service one attains the Self; and through grace, the Supreme Lord. || 10.2 ||
O Badarī, the power of the narrative of this Saṃhitā, which bestows liberation and destroys sin, suddenly spread throughout all the worlds.
Indeed, men and women in groups, having resolved upon liberation,
come from all directions for the purpose of hearing this discourse.
Chanting arises in every place, and services for the virtuous are carried out by providing various kinds of food and edibles. (105)
Marvels arise here and there day after day;
indeed, upon hearing them again and again, men and women become filled with joy.
They worship Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa, who dwells directly within their hearts;
they obtain the supreme gain, which is knowledge, purity, and the highest goal. 107.

Thus ends the forty-seventh chapter, titled "The Description of the Liberation of King Kṣīrodavīra and Queen Ruhāriṇī, along with their thousand subjects, the courtesan named Somikā accompanied by her five daughters, and the courtesans residing in Mithuna-kuṭṭa, through the hearing of the stories of the *Saṃhitā*," in the fourth section, the Tiṣya lineage, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Goddess beloved of Badarī, to the story of the woman named Liyārī, a resident of Bilvapattana who was a drinker of liquor.
At that time, in the city named Bilva, in the country of Markaṭāna,
there was a family of liquor-makers, rich in their business with intoxicating drinks.
There, the chief was a liquor-seller named Miṣṭāsava-dhvajin;
his wife, named Līlāryā, was accompanied by sons and daughters. (2)
Then, from the mouths of people, he heard a story of supreme power,
the narrative of the *Kṛṣṇasaṃhitā* in the city of Śarkarā.
That woman desired to hear it and then entreated her husband;
the husband said to his wife, "The place for this discourse is far away."
The road is long and the journey ahead is fraught with danger;
moreover, we are destitute of wealth and tormented by the suffering of poverty.
"How indeed shall we proceed on the road where bandits are present?
Having heard this, the wife said to her husband, "There is no destruction of the body [in this]. (7)
Or rather, since people in this world must inevitably die at some point or other—whether today or after many years—death is considered a certainty. (8)
By whatever cause death shall come to pass, we are sinful, performers of evil deeds, and devoted to wickedness. (9)
The death of sinners occurs within sin, and that indeed brings grief; however, if death occurs within non-sin or in meritorious action, [it does not bring such sorrow]. (4.48.10)
Whether such hardship arises or it is auspicious and brings gain, those who make meritorious resolves and those who desire to go on pilgrimage [attain their goal]. (11)
Indeed, even those who have not performed religious rites go to heaven when they die;
whereas we are all drinkers of liquor and perpetually great sinners.
If they die on account of a pilgrimage to sacred fords, they partake of heaven;
likewise, if they are plundered by robbers on the road, or if they subsequently live by begging.
Having prepared food as well, we shall go to the place of discourse;
by that, there will be the destruction of sins and the arising of good fortune. (14)
Or rather, there will be liberation from this world; of this there is no doubt.
In every way there is only gain; no loss is found therein. (15)
"Therefore, a sacred bathing place must be established, and one must go to the place where the story is told.
Thus addressed by his wife, the banner-bearer, together with his family, [acted accordingly].
Having made the house empty, she set out with sugar;
and just as she had previously intended, so it happened for her on the way. (17)
Robbers gathered on the road and plundered his vessels and other belongings,
as well as his provisions, the donkey, the load-bearing bull, and the mule.
The plunderers also seized their garments and bowls;
however, they considered this great hardship to be for the sake of the sacred pilgrimage site.
Although they had deliberated previously, they did not consider it too difficult;
for all of them, including even their eleven sons, had been stripped of all their possessions.
Then, your father, mother, and seventeen daughters gradually became devoted to Kṛṣṇa at the edge of the lake every evening.
Having made their dwelling on the ground thick with trees and respectfully waiting for the night to pass,
they drank water and remembered the Supreme Lord.
"Alas! We have encountered great hardship on the road; everything has been plundered by robbers.
This night may pass, but tomorrow there will be suffering from hunger. (23)
One may have to die, or beg for alms, or eat only leaves from a tree;
nevertheless, one must go to that place of discourse—of this there is no doubt. ||24||
Having thus resolved and having brought sacrificial fuel, they kindled the fire;
then, remaining supported by it, they all began the chanting.
O beloved Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, O purifier Nārāyaṇa, O Lord! O Consort of Śrī, O charming Kṛṣṇa, O Lord Bālakṛṣṇa, O All-pervading One! 26.
Thus they made the noise, preceded by the clapping of their palms;
meanwhile, half the night passed while he remained seated upon the camel.
A certain merchant, accompanied by his ten sons and provided with food and clothing, came along that path to the edge of the lake to drink water. (28)
He too, seeing the auspicious fire and the men stationed there, drank water, gave it to them to drink, and arrived for the sake of rest. (29)
Having cried out, "Victory to Nārāyaṇa-Kṛṣṇa!", he descended onto dry land;
having tied the camels to the base of a tree trunk, he reached the auspicious site of Vahnisthala.
Having gone there, he questioned them all regarding the news of his arrival and other matters;
becoming humble, Miṣṭāsava indeed related his journey to him.
Even when everything had been plundered by robbers, he spoke to him;
then the merchant, hearing of this great suffering, became filled with compassion.
He indeed gave them excellent food, such as dates and other delicacies;
he also gave them garments and then bestowed upon them the gift of fearlessness.
Filled with joy, he said to them, "I too shall go to that place to hear the story; therefore, you all mount my camels. ||34||
"We shall set out by this path and reach the settlement tomorrow at dawn;
there are camels that know the way, and I too am familiar with the route. (35)
"I have no victory; you must mount my camels," he said;
thus addressed, O Badrikā, they all mounted the camels. (36)
The swift camels, with long necks and long strides,
plunged into a rapid gallop and traversed the paths as they were urged on.
Just as Garuḍas, swans, celestial chariots, or elephants, they traversed the path like those who roam the sky. (38)
They set out with speed during the middle watch of the night for the journey that would take two days;
however, by morning, Śarkarāpura had already come into their sight.
They, however, beheld before them a place adorned with white palatial buildings,
shining with a story-telling pavilion and graced by celestial pitchers.
In the early morning, many virtuous sages, Vaiṣṇavas, and men with their wives were wandering about for the purpose of bathing, worshiping, and other such rites. 41.
It indicated the site of the assembly by the smoke of burnt offerings and by the proclamations [of the bards], and by the loud chanting of the sacred mantras from the mouths of the Brahmins. (42)
O Nārāyaṇaprabhu, O Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Lord of the universe!
O Bālakṛṣṇa, Harikṛṣṇa, Mādhavīramaṇaprabhu! ||43||
Thus, beholding Śarkarānagara pervaded by purifying sounds filled with such proclamations, they experienced supreme wonder. (44)
Having gone quickly to the bank of the Sindhu river, the merchant bathed repeatedly in the water;
then, having brought down all of them, he showed them the supreme path. ||45||
Having personally caused all the camels at the place of discourse to drink sweet water, he quickly vanished from sight. 46.
Beholding this, the charioteer holding the banner became filled with great wonder, thinking:
"Aha! Who could this be who acts as our protector in the midst of the forest? (47)
He is the bestower of happiness on the great path and the one who leads to its attainment at the conclusion of the excellent teaching;
he is surely Nārāyaṇa, or perhaps some lord of the gods. (48)
Otherwise, such an invisible movement would never occur anywhere;
there, that Lilārī indeed remembered Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa. 49.
Through a voice from the sky, the Blessed One said to her: "I am the Blessed One;
having taken up camels, I have come for the protection of my devotees. (4.48.50)
Come to hear the divine story; serve the sage Lomaśa and serve that which is self-luminous, and there shall be the highest goal.
Thus addressed, O Badrikā, they were all satisfied and gladdened by joy; taking flowers with great devotion, they went to the place of discourse. (52)
Having bowed from a distance and entered the assembly hall,
they then performed the worship of the Saṃhitā with flowers and other offerings.
They sat down for the sake of hearing as long as the recitation of the story continued;
at the conclusion of the story, they went to Lomaśa, bowed to him, and drank the water from his feet.
They related the account of the service performed for Kṛṣṇa on the road;
and he who was indeed that excellent camel-owner was Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa himself. ||55||
The Blessed Śrī Hari has brought us here to this place of discourse;
we desire His surrender—grant us the most purifying mantra. (56)
Thus requested, Lomaśa caused them to hear that auspicious mantra:
"Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord; svāhā. (57)
Likewise, at that very time, he gave him a name for the purpose of purification:
"Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Supreme Lord. (58)
Then, O Lord of Rama, Bālakṛṣṇa, Ādikṛṣṇa, and Nārāyaṇa gave them a vow to live free from the consumption of liquor. ||59||
And the venerable sage Lomaśa arranged for their meals and other provisions from the royal kitchen, while they resided constantly in a small hut.
Thus, O Badrikā, they lived there always in happiness;
they performed service for the virtuous there, as well as the cleaning of their vessels and other utensils. ||6 1||
They performed the sweeping, washing, and bringing of articles at the storytelling site,
as well as the massaging of the bodies of Mahimāna and the others.
Having heard this story and having served the holy ones,
one shakes off all sins through the nectar of their blessings and by partaking of the food that is the grace of Kṛṣṇa.
Indeed, they have all become stainless, devoted solely to Kṛṣṇa;
they are meritorious souls, supreme devotees who have offered themselves to Him.
They remember that Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who is their beloved soul, as the camel-herder;
for even in states such as dreaming and deep sleep, the camel-herder is perceived.

Their minds were fixed on that, they were immersed in that meditation, their sensory faculties were directed toward that; established in that yoga, remembering that, they became absorbed in that through divine contemplation. (66)
In a very short time, they became the most excellent of great devotees of the Lord;
O Badrikā, Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa appeared before them within the sphere of their dreams.
Having become an actual camel-herder, her beloved husband becomes Nārāyaṇa himself,
bearing the conch, the discus, the mace, and the lotus, at that very moment.
Thus, Kṛṣṇa—who constantly grants his vision to those bound by devotion and held fast by the noose of affection—approached them in order to lead them away. 69.
Having ascended a divine celestial chariot, the Lord, endowed with divine radiance,
descended from that chariot on the eleventh day of the month of Pauṣa.
For as many devoted embodied beings as behold [him] during the bright fortnight, there shall be sweet liquors, as well as wives, sons, and daughters. (71)
Beholding their beloved lord Kṛṣṇa who had arrived,
they rose suddenly, bowed at his feet, and prostrated themselves like a staff.
They licked his feet and held the dust with their tongues;
then, they sought Kṛṣṇa upon their bodies for the sake of attaining liberation.
The compassionate Blessed One said: "Be prepared indeed quickly;
I shall lead you, who possess divine bodies, to my imperishable abode. (74)
As soon as these words were spoken, they all cast themselves at the feet of Kṛṣṇa and fell upon the earth while all the worlds looked on.
Having abandoned their elemental bodies and having become divine by the will of Hari, they attained liberated forms with bodies equal to those of Kṛṣṇa. ||76||
At the command of Kṛṣṇa, they quickly descended from their divine celestial chariot;
bowing to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, they entered the auspicious assembly hall.
Accompanied by the utterance of the word "Victory," they, having attained their liberated nature, went by celestial chariot to the imperishable abode at Badarī together with Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
Those maidens became Muktānikās, and likewise their sons and father were liberated; they all went to the imperishable abode of Hari.
Thus, O Badrikā, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the teacher of the universe, is forever the deliverer of the wretched, the helpless, and the poor. (4.48.80)
The Lord is always intent upon protecting those who have come for refuge, disregarding the sins of the wicked as well as their evil qualities. (81)
The refuge for those who have come for shelter, he leads them—purified by listening to his stories—to the imperishable state through his grace and compassion. (82)
Having purified all those men and women who were addicted to drinking liquor, the Lord, out of compassion, led them to his own imperishable abode.
This Lord, an ocean of compassion, does not take account at all of the sins of sinners in this world; he leads them to the imperishable and immutable state. 84.
Having witnessed this marvel, the people attained supreme wonder, exclaiming:
"Oh, Kṛṣṇa, the friend of the distressed, himself rescues them! (85)
He grants his own vision and bestows the desired object upon those who have sought refuge, having purified them and destroyed their suffering in the realm of Yama. //86//
He himself leads them to his own abode by means of a divine celestial chariot;
oh, what fortune, what fortune for those who listen to this narrative! (87)
Within just one month, he effects liberation from the bonds of worldly existence;
this compendium (saṃhitā) is the very form of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, while its verbal expression is the form of Lakṣmī. 88.
By serving that image, one attains heaven and liberation;
by reading or hearing this, one becomes liberated—of this there is no doubt. (89)

Thus ends the forty-eighth chapter, titled "The Description of how Śrī Hari, appearing in the form of a merchant, protected and liberated a drunkard and his family—who were wine-sellers and encountered hardship from robbers on the road—by means of listening to the sacred narrative," in the fourth section, the Tiṣya lineage, of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Goddess beloved of Badarī, to the beautiful story of Cakriṇī. In the kingdom of Kālāntaka, there was a virtuous woman named Gaṇḍavātā.
She was the wife of Skavāda, a wheelwright and maker of machines;
she was a highly renowned housewife who had sons and daughters. || 2 ||
In whose house thousands of iron implements are produced—
sugar-cane pressing machines and sesame-crushing mills.
There are also seed-crushing machines and those for extracting juices;
such are the iron implements produced from metallic ores.
She constantly sells even base metals fashioned into artistic forms, as well as mechanical devices and oil-presses.
He likewise purchases seeds from all quarters for the sake of oil;
at that time, twenty machines are set in motion even within his own house.
There were twenty oil-mills and sugarcane-presses that revolved;
there was the constant sale of wheels and the mending again of those that were broken. (7)
That virtuous woman also effects the rejoining of things that have been broken;
indeed, thousands of servants of karma remain under her control.
Even thousands of laborers perform those tasks;
moreover, machines are operated by means of buffaloes, camels, donkeys, and so forth.
Ten thousand coins are obtained every day;
such indeed was that virtuous lady, O great king.
Abounding in wealth, abounding in honor, and abounding in goodness, that Paśupālinī,
known as Kalāvatī, was famous in Dīrgharāṣṭra as a wielder of the discus.
O Badrikā, she heard that supreme, liberation-granting majesty described by the people, arising from the narrative of the Saṃhitā.
She knows that the accumulation of sins is crushed by the great wheels.
In seeds and such, there arises for living beings the suffering produced by being crushed and so forth.
He truly knows the fruit of slaughterhouses— suffering experienced in the city of Yama, as well as the lowly hellish state that brings extreme torment.
Driven by a desire to know for the sake of pacifying those sins, she became filled with faith in hearing the story and developed a resolute mind. || 15 ||
The virtuous woman said to her husband:
"O Lord, in the city of Śarkarā, the recitation of the entire scripture (pārāyaṇa) takes place, which destroys all sins. (16)
Many wonders that destroy sins are heard of;
now, by his grace, the Lord who bestows liberation is seen there.
But we are eternally sinful, crushed by the wheel and ground by the wheel;
for the sinners, there is no auspicious destination—their course is said to be that of hell. (18)
Whether it be a kingdom, a nation, or whatever else exists within one's home—if there is residence in hell at the end of the body, all of that is utterly useless. (19)
Wealth consisting of an inexhaustible treasury, and even tens of thousands of male and female servants—
if these result in dwelling in hell at the end of the body's life, then all of it is utterly useless.
If there is residence in hell at the end of the body, then all these—enclosures, fields, groves, gardens, and even houses—are utterly useless. (21)
Palaces with golden domes, beautifully adorned with hoisted banners, and riches that are inexhaustible and beyond counting in every respect. (22)
If there is residence in hell at the end of the body, then all that is useless;
[so too are] buffaloes, cows, elephants, horses, camels, and female elephants. (23)
If, after the end of the body, there is residence in hell for the swans, garuḍas, menā birds, parrots, cranes, and cātakas, then all of that is useless.
There were many wives, as well as sons, daughters, and grandsons in the lineage;
there were sisters, elder brothers, kinsmen, mothers, and women. ||25||
If one's husbands, groups of male slaves, and female slaves by the thousands must dwell in hell at the end, then all of that is rendered meaningless. ||26||
There were also many activities involving a thousand carts, ten thousand machines, and a thousand vehicles. ||27||
Furthermore, even if there were infinity of enjoyments, fame, and festivals, they would be useless if one is destined for hell at the end of the body. (28)
Therefore, O Lord, for the sake of my own welfare, I reflect upon the destruction of sins through gifts as well as through service to the virtuous and other such means. (29)
From listening to these stories, there shall arise an emergence of merit;
for this prosperity does not bestow merit, as it is characterized by violence.
It is my opinion that this prosperity should be employed for the sake of meritorious deeds;
having obtained more than a hundred thousand coins, let us go to the place of discourse.
We shall constantly listen to the sacred discourse, we shall give money and other gifts, we shall perform purification of the self, and we shall attain what is beneficial for the soul. (32)
We shall behold Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of Śrī, and we shall attain the supreme state,
having made ourselves entirely subject to that foremost servant of the Primal Being.
"Or, taking immeasurable wealth, let us go indeed to the place of conversation;
there is no certainty in life, for this [wealth] will not accompany us. (34)
Dharma-action is a great gift; devotion to the virtuous is a vow;
devotion to Kṛṣṇa and the merit of hearing His stories provide companionship in the next world. (35)
Having performed that and having acquired in every way the wealth of an inexhaustible nature of merit, we shall proceed upon the path to liberation; do not undergo vain suffering. (36)
Thus addressed by his wife, her husband— though he was already self-realized and desirous of liberation—
gave his consent for her journey for the sake of her own liberation.
Then, with her cheeks glowing, she quickly became ready,
accompanied by her hundred sons and daughters and joined by her hundred maidservants.
She was accompanied by a hundred female slaves, endowed with two hundred grandsons, joined by her daughters-in-law, and likewise attended by young boys and girls. (39)
Accompanied by elderly women and joined by virtuous warriors who provide protection,
there were two hundred carts and likewise two hundred horses.
He also gave twenty camels, a hundred bulls, and a hundred milk-yielding cows for the purpose of carrying loads. (41)
Having brought forth an inexhaustible supply of food, an infinite quantity of garments,
and an incalculable number of bowls, he then became ready.
Yāska, too, being delighted for the sake of the journey and for the purpose of liberation,
became ready like a king, accompanied by ten million pieces of gold.
Equipped with all necessary articles and seated upon an excellent celestial chariot, he,
together with his wife, bowed to the Lord Gaṇeśa from that chariot.
Through the air, he went to the land of Śarkarā along with his family members,
as well as the caravan leaders, servants, herds of cattle, and riches.
Having arrived at Śarkarāpura in the evening by way of the terrestrial path,
he entered his own yoga-center in the garden on the bank of the Indus.
Endowed with all prosperity, Yāskavāda dwelt there with his householders;
then, having arranged his entire army and bathed, he [proceeded]. (47)
Accompanied by his wife, he went forth, eager to see the illustrious Lomaśa;
having arrived, he bowed, offered worship, and likewise expressed his heartfelt intentions.
Then Lomaśa also gave him encouragement with auspicious blessings;
he gave him the nectar-water of Kṛṣṇa and likewise bestowed his grace upon him.
Having brought him to the place of the *Saṃhitā*, the Discus-wielder caused him to appear;
he honored Vyāsa, who was seated upon the seat of Vyāsa, with excellent riches.
And there, with many formal ceremonies, he took a vow along with his wife: "I shall always take only one meal a day."
I shall serve the virtuous and listen to their discourses every day;
I will also constantly provide the holy ones with food, even if it be according to their specific desires.
There should always be gifts of gold and constant gifts of clothing; there should always be the offering of water for grace and other drinks, but no other house [for such purposes]. (53)
Thinking, "May drinking milk and all other such things come from me alone," he, Vyāsa— who is self-luminous— undertook those observances.
Constantly performing a hundred circumambulations with a garland, a hundred prostrations like a staff, and the recitation of the mantra one thousand times is the most excellent practice. (55)
Lomaśa indeed gave them such observances as these;
he gave them a mantra and garlands, and bestowed upon them names for the purpose of recitation.
Oṃ, salutation to Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Lord; Svāhā!
O Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Master, Lord, Nārāyaṇeśvara! ||57||
"O Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, Lord of Śrī Mādhavī!
Having thus bestowed these religious observances, Lomaśa departed for his own hermitage. (58)
Then Yāskavāda and all the others returned to their own dwellings;
they lived there happily, conducting themselves exactly according to their rules. (59)
They constantly listen to the discourse with great eagerness;
they all serve the virtuous with due respect.
Free from doubt, they indeed personally attend upon the holy ones.
The sins of such people were instantly destroyed by the wielder of the discus (Viṣṇu).
All those men and women quickly became free from sin;
their inner doors were burst open, and they swiftly attained wisdom.
Yāskavāda gave food daily to the virtuous;
he bestowed many gifts of clothing and gave gifts of fruit.
He likewise gave all kinds of desirable gifts and gifts of cows;
