The unsteady woman related the entire account exactly as it had occurred: that from birth there had been an exchange for the sake of protecting the princess.
"O son, I have already performed [the rites]; you are the daughter of the queen and my own son.
Therefore, regard me as your mother, who bore you in her womb and gave you birth. (14)
"Know me to be revealed, my child; make yourself well-known, and likewise make the maiden well-known, for when she is revealed, there will be no harm at all. (15)
Therefore, know me to be your mother, who must keep everything secret;
O Badrikā, a woman’s heart is cruel, like a door that has been broken open.
Sometimes it is surely broken through anger, and sometimes through affection;
therefore, an unbearable calamity may indeed arise from that.
That which is to be hidden from a woman must be kept secret; it should not be revealed in the presence of a woman.
Moreover, such excessive affection for her daughter exists even in the king’s mother. (18)
His daughter had become marriageable, auspicious and like unto a queen;
he then reflected, "To whom and where should this daughter be given? (19)
The queen herself became deeply anxious on account of her daughter, thinking:
"She must not be given to a slave; she is indeed to be given to a prince."
"The princess must be given to the prince; otherwise, she must be protected.
Thus the queen reflected, for the maiden was awaiting a husband. (21)
"When will my marriage take place? Why does my mother not speak of it?"—thinking thus, she questioned her mother in this way. (22)
"Why do you never consider my marriage, O mother?
Then that maidservant, the queen's mother, spoke this refusal.
"O daughter, she always performs it; therefore, I do not speak of it.
Then, on one occasion, the daughter became intent upon serving the queen's body.
In private, he questioned that queen: "O Mother, I bow to you repeatedly;
I ask you what is in my heart—do not impute any fault to me. (25)
I ask you a secret; you should tell it to me as it truly is:
how may I have an auspicious marriage for one who is fit for marriage? (26)
"You do not wish to do it; how can you be restrained? Having heard this, the mother, the queen-mother, [regarded] her own daughter as a slave-girl.
Having drawn her close and held her many times, he shed tears upon her breast;
then, summoning his fortitude, he spoke these beneficial words to his daughter.
"O child, you are born from my womb and are the auspicious daughter of a king;
yet, being of meager fortune, you were formerly surrendered by me to a maidservant. (29)
"I have obtained a son of a slave-girl born at the very moment of your sight;
if I do not act in this way, the King will surely put you to death. (4.54.30)
The king shall certainly not be anyone's maternal uncle, father-in-law, brother, or even another elder brother who is an heir to the royal inheritance. (3.1)
And how could that Śālaka have held authority over the kingdom?
Furthermore, how indeed could your father or your father-in-law have been anyone else’s [father or father-in-law]?
For when you were born as my daughter, you were protected by me; had it not been so... [the rest of the verse is omitted in the source].
For the sake of protecting the Aśvalāyana lineage and for the preservation of the status of being a son-in-law to an Aśva. ||33||
The king might destroy you quickly, and I would be left without my daughter;
for I have obtained this only daughter, who grants me the sight of her face. (34)
"How could I give [her] up to be killed, even at the cost of hundreds of my own lives?
My dear child, I then reflected thoroughly upon what would be for your ultimate welfare. (35)
And this young boy who was born as a son to a maidservant was quickly brought by me to my home from that maidservant, for I am bound to her by affection. (36)
O child, you were entrusted to her for the sake of protecting your life;
yet you, my daughter born from my own womb, remain here in my presence. (37)
How indeed could I bring myself to give you, that most excellent princess born from my own body, to just any servant? (38)
Therefore, my daughter, I am forbidding the maidservant from being given away;
for the gift of a slave is base, whereas that of a prince is praiseworthy. (39)
"Speak, my child; what can I do for you that was told to me in secret? Everything you asked has been told by me, O daughter of mine. (4.54.40)
"O princess, it would always be better for you to remain in maidenhood without a prince;
nevertheless, my daughter, I shall certainly strive for that which may bring you auspiciousness. (41)
Do not disclose this matter; through it, ruin will come.
My destruction and your destruction will come about by way of the king. ||42||
Thus the queen spoke to her own daughter while lying in bed;
and the daughter, having understood everything, became devoted to the service of her mother. (43)
Especially after the birth of the prince, even toward his mother,
such a reversal occurred within that natural affection.
Then, in their speech, their hearts, their bodies, and in all their actions, the feeling of affection for their respective mothers increased in both of them. (45)
Then once, the king was asleep upon his own bed;
at midnight, the king’s sleep vanished and he awoke.
The queen was sleeping on the king's bed, fast asleep in a dream;
impelled by destiny, she spoke in her dream while the king was listening. (47)
"O daughter, my daughter, do not inform the king!
You are the daughter of the queen, while the prince is the son of a slave-girl. (48)
"O slave girl! O slave girl! Do not tell this to anyone!
The prince is the son of a slave girl; the princess is the daughter of a king. (49)
Having heard this, the king was struck with great wonder and amazed by the truth of the matter;
bewildered by the realization of the words, he reflected upon the true meaning.
Once, however, for the sake of a decision, he gave a golden chain to his maidservant and questioned her, saying, "Tell me what else you desire."
"I am pleased with your service; what other wealth shall I give you?
Shall I give you a palace, a garden, a field, or a village?"
O Badrī, with a serene face, the maidservant, due to her limited intellect, did not at all ask for a garden, or a field, or a village, or wealth, or a house. (53)
"O King, nothing at all pleases me; I am entirely satisfied.
If a boon must be granted to me, let it be requested for the two princes. (54)
"O King, give the entire kingdom to the second prince;
or else, O Lord of Men, give half to him and grant the other half to the eldest. (55)
Having heard the arguments of both sides, the king then asked for the reason;
the maidservant, having been enticed with many jewels and other gifts, spoke the reason. (56)
That young boy exists as the son born from my womb;
that young girl exists as the daughter born of your wife. (57)
"O King, grant even half of your auspicious kingdom to my son.
Badrikā became a maidservant; though born a Kṣatriya, she performed the work of a servant. (58)
The queen was named Prabhāvatī; her son, born of the king, became a second Kṣatriya, and he requested the kingdom from Sāta. (59)
Everything that should not have been told was told by me, a servant, out of a greedy disposition;
yet, out of affection for my own son, the supreme secret was told in private. (4.54.60)
Then the king, having learned that the prince was the son of a maidservant, and that his own daughter, the princess, was likewise the daughter of a maidservant, [acted accordingly]. (61)
He was always utterly bewildered as to what ought to be done and extremely distraught; indeed, there should not have been such a state of mind in an eldest son.
"I must certainly not be the father-in-law of another king;
otherwise, this news will inevitably become widely known. (63)
"The eldest son holds the authority over the kingdom, or at least over half of it;
if I were to give [the kingdom] to the son of a slave-girl, there would be ill fortune for the realm. (64)
If it should result in what is undesirable for me, then that must certainly not be done;
in this matter, the dissolution of the lives of the girl and the boy is considered auspicious.
Through contact with poison and the like, the two will quickly pass away;
of this there is no doubt. Therefore, that which is best must be done in this matter.
Having reflected thus, the King of War secretly caused a fierce, life-destroying poison to be given to the maiden and to Kumāra.
There was a female servant of the king named Gupti, belonging to the Ghaṭamālā lineage, who was born of the Khaśa caste and served as his attendant.
Likewise, poison was administered to them at the time of the meal; neither the queen nor her maidservant mother knew of the administration of the poison. (69)
That for which death was written down occurs;
that for which life was written down also occurs. (4.54.70)
Having eaten the meal mixed with poison, the son and the grandson both became lifeless there; at that very moment, a brahmin arrived.
A virtuous ascetic, wondrous and possessing knowledge of the medicine for poison, arrived while wandering, carrying a pill composed of the essence of that medicine. 72.
Impelled by fate, a guest named Jīvanāyana arrived there, desiring only food. ||73||
Upon hearing that both had met an open death in the kingdom, the king then quickly dispatched them for cremation. (74)
When this had happened, the virtuous ascetic, having learned that his son was dead, departed by way of the royal cremation ground; he was indeed a Vaiṣṇava.
Having recognized that the two bodies were blue in color, he quickly extracted a medicinal pill and placed it between their lips, and then gave them water to drink.
"Oṃ namaḥ śrīkṛṣṇanārāyaṇāya svāmine svāhā.
He gave this mantra to the two of them right there in the cremation ground. (77)
Having risen, with their poison pacified, they became healthy and free from disease, O Lord Nārāyaṇasvāmin, O Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa! (78)
The ocean of compassion gave them the name Dhunya and restored them to life;
then, having learned of the king's cruel deed, he went toward the monarch. (79)
"O King, this evil, cruel, and sinful deed has been committed by you;
the murder of a maiden and the murder of a youth have been perpetrated by you. (4.54.80)
"I am a self-controlled ascetic, free from fear, yet I am the master who can punish you.
Alas! A cry of lamentation prevails today, for two have been killed by the king with poison. (81)
O King, what is the use of sovereignty to you, who have committed such exceedingly evil deeds?
O King, you are no longer worthy; your lifespan has reached its end. (82)
Your dwelling in the world of Yama will be long and painful;
behold the curse bestowed by Kanyā and Kumāra, which has now come within your range of vision. (83)
"Let this King of War die; let the Destroyer indeed kill us with poison.
This curse stands before you in embodied form, taking away your life right here. (84)
Now there is no refuge for you on earth other than death;
the sin of killing has arisen for you, and this Death has arrived. (85)
When this was said, a terrifying messenger of Yama arrived there,
holding a noose in his hand, hideous in appearance, and vomiting fire from his mouth.
Having bowed to that Vaiṣṇava ascetic, the protector of Kanyākumāra,
he bound the wicked and sinful king with a noose.
Then the king, his body rendered dependent on another, became unconscious;
struck by the mallet, he suddenly fell into a swoon while crying out. ||88||
And while he was bound by the snares of poison, the king went for refuge to that ascetic with his heart, in order to be separated from his body. (89)
Having thus remembered Nārāyaṇa and taken refuge in Śrī Kṛṣṇa,
he begged for forgiveness there within his own self, even though he was unconscious.
Bound by Yama and fallen under his control, he grieved in many ways;
thus was the messenger seen by the people, hideous and resembling a mountain.
And the subjects and the groups of kings, having heard and understood that great calamity concerning the maidens, the princes, and the lords of the earth, quickly assembled there. (92)
Realizing that this was the ultimate misfortune, they all gave way to grief;
yet the queen, knowing him to be virtuous and endowed with sovereignty, fell at his feet. (93)
The goddess Nārāyaṇī, by name, praised the virtuous Lord:
"O Lord of Mercy, O Embodiment of Compassion, O Compassionate One, you who are ever the benefactor! (94)
O great yoginī, who are like Hari, bring my husband back to health;
you have protected both my daughter and my son. (95)
"Out of compassion, protect this sinner, my husband as well;
for the wicked commit sin, while the virtuous bestow merit. (96)
Disregarding the sin of my master in this matter, create a forest so that there may be the destruction of his sin as well as his liberation. (97)
Therefore, O Blessed One, act here for our benefit;
I am your servant, so please carry out my request. (98)
Having spoken thus and grasped the feet of the saint, the queen became senseless.
Then that saint, the source of her life, took water in his hand. (99)
She placed it in the queen's mouth, and the queen became healthy and established in comfort;
then he went and gave water into the king's mouth as well.
Oṃ, salutation to Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Master; Svāhā!
O Lord Nārāyaṇa, O Lord Śrī Śarvarīnārāyaṇa! 101.
"O beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, O Lord of Śrī, O True Sovereign!"—
thus he then gave him the name-mantra along with water.
The messenger of Yama then quickly departed, leaving the king;
the king suddenly realized this and did not bow to the protector.
The virtuous one protected him from the southern direction against the one who harms maidens and the one who harms children;
and then, O Badrikā, everyone completely cast aside their grief.
With serene minds, they became devoted; thousands of men and women took up the *mantra* of the virtuous one and took up the churning of his name. (105)
That news spread through the city of war with the speed of the wind;
then, a peace equal to a cry of "Alas! arose once again. || 106 ||

Thus ends the fifty-fourth chapter, titled "The Description of King Yuddhapātana’s Death in Battle due to the Administration of Poison by King Yuddharāja; the Restoration to Life of the Daughter and the Prince through the Skillful Application of a Remedy despite their Having Died; the Arrival of the Messengers of Yama and the Death of King Yuddharāja through the Destruction of His Lifespan by a Curse as the Fruit of Sin; and the Protection Provided by the Holy Man," in the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, within the fourth section, the *Tiṣya-Santāna*.
Śrī Badarīpriyā said: O Lord Kṛṣṇa-Nara-Nārāyaṇa, what then happened there concerning the maidens, the princes, and the mountain? What was performed by the virtuous one? || 1 ||
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Goddess beloved of Badarī; indeed, thousands and hundreds of thousands of men, having heard of the death of the king, [then] heard of his life once again.
They indeed came together to behold the virtuous king Camatkṛti,
having seen that the monarch, the prince, and the princess were alive.
Therefore, people thereafter called that prince Sādhujīva by name,
and they likewise called that girl Sādhujīvinī right there.
Then the people praised the eldest boy as being free from dejection;
indeed, they quickly became renowned among the subjects by those respective names.
Whichever people, men and women alike, arrived there, they quickly took refuge with that virtuous man upon seeing his miraculous power.
The virtuous Sañjīvanāyana bestowed upon his subjects the initiation into the sacred mantras and the worship of the names of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa.
Oṃ, salutation to Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Lord; Svāhā!
Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Narāyaṇa! || 8 ||
"Bālakṛṣṇa, Ādikṛṣṇa, Nārāyaṇa, Narāyaṇa"—
thus the sage gave this mantra, a recitation of names, to them.
Those subjects were [found] in the city of war, in every house, on the ground, in the forest,
in the garden, in the grove, in the field, in the wilderness, and at the city gate.
At the crossroads, on the royal highway, in the streets, and even in the marketplaces:
"Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Nārāyaṇa! (11)
"Bālakṛṣṇa, Ādikṛṣṇa, Nārāyaṇa, Narāyaṇa!"—
thus they performed their worship, their minds enriched by His great majesty.
Hundreds of thousands of men and women were born as Vaiṣṇavas in that kingdom of war;
they worshipped their own virtuous guru, the ascetic Sañjīvanāyana.
They honored the Arhat with sandalwood, heaps of flowers, fruits, leaves, as well as garments, various kinds of food, and provisions for the journey.
They served the most excellent teacher and attained the destruction of their sins;
they acquired great merit and earned supreme purity. || 1 ||
The virtuous Sañjīvanāyana instructed them for their benefit:
"O people, this saṃsāra is essence-less and consists of passion and hatred. (16)
Indeed, for the sake of the body and for the sake of nourishing the body, attachment and aversion arise;
consequently, a person commits violence and destruction against other embodied beings. (17)
Time, conjoined with ignorance, attachment, or aversion,
is the destroyer of creation when it is joined with the illustrious Supreme Brahman.
Time creates everything; Time always ordains all things;
and by Time alone is this entire world carried along in its flow.
If one desires to go to the Imperishable only after casting off the noose of time,
let human beings always worship the Supreme Lord, the Death of Time.
Ignorance is the cause of saṃsāra, and saṃsāra consists of latent impressions (vāsanā);
having investigated this and completely abandoned it, may you acquire the cause of liberation. ||21||
May they obtain here in this world eternal knowledge, devotion, service to the virtuous with affection, a refuge in the auspicious, supreme bliss, and peace. 22.
May they practice the supreme meditation on the Supreme Lord, which consists of the Supreme Brahman, within Indra, Candra, Ravi, Vahni, Vighneśa, and Narāyaṇa.
Let them renounce the entire world of moving and non-moving beings, for that is what creates bondage;
let them grasp instead that which dwells within them, the mover of all moving and non-moving things.
Let them always worship Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Lord of Śrī, who dwells within, as well as the glorious Nārāyaṇa and those who have taken refuge in Him.
Having served the virtuous who have fixed their minds on Nārāyaṇa and are devoted solely to Nārāyaṇa, they go by the divine path to the imperishable state.
The inner priests, who are devoted to divine rites, are to be honored and served;
even if they are deformed or disfigured, those who dwell in the abode of Brahman must not be reviled. (27)
All the inner priests (ābhyantarārcakas) are never to be subjected to examination; however, those who revile them will surely become afflicted by suffering and short-lived. ||28||

Those who know Brahman are to be propitiated with service performed without the twenty-fold [distinctions], for they are liberated from the system of castes and stages of life by those who are well-established within that very system. (29)
Association with the virtuous is in every way divine, bestowing liberation and destroying sin;
it must certainly be practiced by the wise for the sake of pacifying the sins of killing and the like. 4.55.30.
Now, divine association with the virtuous exists in Śarkarāpura, consisting of the complete recitation of the Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa-Saṃhitā. (31)
There, Nārāyaṇa himself, bearing a form of self-luminous nature,
now causes all Vedic knowledge that bestows liberation to be heard.
He indeed proclaims eternally the supreme Brahman, supreme Lakṣmī, supreme liberation, supreme happiness, supreme dharma, and supreme knowledge. ||33||
I am departing for that place for the sake of attaining liberation for myself;
that attainment will not be possible for people on this earth again.
There, virtuous ones, sages, perfected beings, celestial bards, gods, gandharvas, ascetics, vidyādharas, and kinnaras were present. ||35||
Kimpuruṣas, Bhūdevas, great sages, men, and women; gods devoted to celibacy and divine liberated beings—all have assembled here. (36)
But by the sight of whom the destruction of evil occurs in every way, and by the service of whom the burning away of all latent impressions (vāsanās) may come to pass; ||37||
By obtaining whose grace one attains divinity and divine fortune;
by the mere company of whom supreme liberation is achieved. (38)
Through affection for whom there may be the constant attainment of the bliss of Brahman, and by taking refuge in whom alone there may be the journey to the abode of Brahman. (39)
Those who always worship Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Lord, and daily praise the glorious Lord Bālakṛṣṇa, their Master and Lord; || 4.55.40 ||
Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Narāyaṇa; Bālakṛṣṇa, Anādikṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Ramāyaṇa! ||41||
Thus do the virtuous ever proclaim that Supreme Lord;
by attaining the company of such as they, the four aims of human existence are attained. 42.
Repeated salutations again and again to all those holy ones;
salutations to the one whose very nature is the saintly, salutations to the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa. ||43||
Salutation to the Lord of All, the Foremost of All, the Wielder of the Discus;
salutation to Him who is worthy of worship at His descent, salutation to the Source of all creations. ||44||
Salutation to him who is the source of all knowledges and the source of all actions;
salutation to the instructor of the lords and the sovereign of the gods. (45)
Homage to the source of the sages, the planets, and the constellations;
homage to the source of lightning, radiant bodies, and clouds. ||46||
Salutations to the source of the rains, the mountains, and the rivers;
salutations to the source of all medicinal herbs, foods, and satisfactions. ||47||
Homage to the Supreme Self, the progenitor of the forms of Dharma and the rest;
homage to him, the source of the essences and the source of the jewels. (48)
Salutation to the source of the seasons and the source of the means of livelihood;
salutation to the source of all worlds and the source of all branches of knowledge. ||49||
Salutations to him, the source of vows; salutations to the source of mantras;
salutations to the source of all accomplishments and the source of all vital energies. ||4.55.50||
Salutations again and again to that Lord of fortunes, the illustrious Master;
salutations to that high-souled Lord of creatures, the bestower of boons. 51.
Salutations again and again to that subtle and great one who is omnipresent;
salutations to him whose nature is sacrifice, and salutations to him whose essence is worship.
Salutations to you who bear the stream of weapons and missiles, salutations to you, the beloved of Mādhava;
salutations to you, the divine one who is the sacred ford, salutations to you whose nature is the sacrificial altar.
Salutations to Vīrya, to Kāma, and to you who are eternal bliss;
salutations to Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa, and salutations to you, the giver of fearlessness. ||54||
Salutations to you, the giver of boons, the most excellent, and the peerless;
salutations to Viṣṇu, who is pure and whose form consists of the sacrificial offerings to gods and ancestors (havya-kavya). ||55||
Salutations to you, Nārāyaṇa, who are the sanctifier of the assembly;
salutations to you, the pure one, the awakened one, and the eye of all. ||56||
Salutations to you whose nature is both visible and invisible, who take the form of a divine couple;
salutations to you, the golden one who renounces all, and who possesses a gentle form. ||57||
Salutations to You, the Beloved, the Lord of Śrī, the Noble One who is cherished;
salutations to You, the affectionate, the one upon whom all depend for livelihood, and the slayer of death. ||58||
Salutations again and again to the immeasurable, the vast, the potter;
salutations to you, the slayer of demons, the destroyer of poison, who is to be known by your devotees. ||59||
Salutations to you who are without distinction, who are dear to the heart, and who bestow liberation;
salutations to the youth of the cowherds, and to the one who is the source of the glory of Yaśodā.
Salutations again and again to the giver of desires who is served by young women;
salutations to you, the ancient one, who is older than the old and exceedingly aged. ||61||
This earth is considered your body as the sustainer of the world; indeed, it is your divine form, for heaven is your head and the netherworld (pātāla) is designated as your feet. (62)
Salutations to that Kṛṣṇa within whose belly the creations reside;
salutations to the Supreme Self, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa.
Salutations to you, the youthful one dwelling in the sacred field of Kuṅkumavāpikā;
and salutations to you, the inner controller who dwells within the hearts of all. 64.
Those who thus praise the Lord of Souls with this Nārāyaṇa-stava,
and those who likewise listen to this hymn, shall experience the dawning of good fortune.
He is to be venerated, praised, and served; He is the beloved Lord, the Soul of the universe, the one to be loved, the dear husband in all undertakings. || 26 ||
The Lord of Life must be protected and guarded within the cave of the heart;
those who desire eternal bliss should never release him. 67.
"Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord; svāhā!
Having spoken thus, O Badrikā, the virtuous Jīvanāyana remained alone. (68)
Then the people, including the king and others, as well as the subjects, became ready to go together to Śarkarānagara. ||69||
Men and women, children and the elderly, as well as the young—all prepared themselves and went out quickly for the purpose of hearing the Saṃhitā. (4.55.70)
The procession of the Saṅgha was exceedingly long, consisting of over a hundred thousand people;
indeed, O Śrī Badrikā, their minds were fixed upon Śrī Kṛṣṇa. (71)
That maiden is Sādhujīvinī; that prince is Sādhujīvana.
The prince who is the eldest, possessing the prowess of a serpent, is free from despondency.
The crown prince himself, Queen Nārāyaṇī, the virtuous Satī, Queen Prabhāvatī, and another named Ghaṭamālā—[all these went forth]. (73)
A thousand male and female servants, and subjects numbering in the hundreds of thousands, went forth eager for liberation to hear the Saṃhitā. (74)
Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Nārāyaṇa; Bālakṛṣṇa, Ādikṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Ramāyaṇa. ||75||
O Badrikā, men and women, the elderly and children, all who travel along the path while chanting the praises of Dhunna become entirely devoted to Brahman.
Having reached Sindhughāṭa, they bathed in the sacred ford and drank its water;
then, resounding with the chanting of hymns, they went to the pavilion for the recitation of the Saṃhitā.
And they bowed like a staff to that self-luminous speaker;
they drank the water of grace, the nectar of Kṛṣṇa’s feet. (78)
They placed the sacrificial offerings before Him, purified the *saṃhitā* texts for Lord Hari, and received the mantra there in the presence of the Supreme Brahman. ||79||
"Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Lord; svāhā!
Thus they spoke, and they listened to the sacred narrative and worshiped the sage Lomaśa. (4.55.80)
Free from doubt, they performed service to the virtuous and service to the chaste women;
thus, for a month, they remained composed and engaged in the service of sacred discourse.
Whatever sin there was from the giving of poison by Yuddharāja, and that which arose from the killing of maidens and boys—that has been eradicated along with its very root. 82.
The sins of others as well were completely incinerated;
the king, his subjects, and all others became purified and sanctified. ||83||
Through hearing the auspicious stories and discourses, their latent impressions (vāsanās) dissolved;
and by serving the holy ones (sādhus), all divine states of being then arose within them. (84)
Abiding in dispassion, they await liberation from the illustrious Supreme Lord;
through concentration, the king attained meditation upon the Supreme Self. (85)
The queen also attained such meditation upon her beloved lord, and the maidservant attained meditation upon Nārāyaṇa, the husband of Mādhavī. (86)
Other men and women who were aged became practitioners of meditative yoga;
indeed, on the eleventh day of the bright fortnight of Phālguna, they were intent upon seeking liberation.
Then [the gods] were ready to go toward great liberation for the King, the foremost of the twice-born, the eldest prince, who was indeed named Nāgavikrama. 88.
Having written [the decree], he then bestowed the royal throne together with its crown;
having performed the formal resolve for a great sacrifice, the Sārvamedha.
Then the two, the maiden and the youth, became virtuous and noble;
they were ever-renouncing disciples of the self-luminous yogin.
Other women and men also took up the initiation of renunciation;
thousands of other devotees likewise entered the stage of life dedicated to renunciation.
Listen, O beloved of Badarī, to a most great marvel that occurred there:
golden celestial chariots arrived from the path of the sky. (92)
In them indeed reside Padmā, Lakṣmī, Ramārādhā, Māṇikyā, Mādhavī, the women, the pearl-like liberated souls (Muktamuktānikās), and the attendants (Pārṣadas). 93.
Then the beautiful Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa shone upon each of them,
and by that, their sky became equal to the abode of Brahmā.
Having made his own dependents worthy of being led to divine bodies, Kṛṣṇa placed more than a thousand men within celestial chariots.
He departed for his own imperishable abode while all embodied beings looked on;
not even a single body remained in the form of a corpse at that time.
Even those material bodies then became divine in form;
by means of those very bodies, they all departed, seated within celestial chariots.
Oh, the divine play of Hari in Badrī is indeed inaccessible and beyond the reach of logic;
he manifests his own abode through Māyā—what then can be said of other things? 98.
Now, as for other men and women, boys and girls alike, all those who abide in the stage of renunciation (tyāgāśrama), and others who abide in the householder stage (gṛhāśrama). 99.
Those who dwelt in the kingdom of war departed for their own auspicious lands;
thus, O beloved of Badrī, a great wonder occurred there.
King Nāgavikrama also gave gifts many times over:
various kinds of food, as well as ornaments and garments at that time. || 10.1 ||
Having performed the worship together with Śrī and likewise having bowed to the Guru and the Ṛṣi, and having paid homage to the virtuous ones,
he returned happily to his own kingdom by their command.
O Badarī, liberation was indeed granted to the killer of a maiden who had fallen for refuge,
as well as to the killer of a youth who was devoted to the service of the virtuous.
Liberation was bestowed by the compassionate Supreme Soul, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, through the sage Jīvana.
From reciting, hearing, remembering, or even reflecting upon this, as well as from appreciating its virtues, enjoyment and liberation shall come to pass; there is no doubt in this matter. ||105||

Thus ends the fifty-fifth chapter, titled "The Description of the National Subjects' Departure for the Seat of the Saṃhitā with Śrī Jīvanāyana and Yuddharāja, the Liberation of Yuddharāja and Others, the Renunciation of the Maidens, and the Return of the Others to the Kingdom with the Crown Prince," in the Tiṣya lineage within the fourth section of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nara-Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Goddess beloved of Badarī, to another most purifying story.
In that city of Śarkarā, there was a certain procuress who was a friend [of the king]. (1)
Abounding in friendliness toward courtesans, she incited those who engage in sexual intercourse;
she was the destroyer of the virtue of women, young maidens, and daughters.
She who was named Sānaṅgavallī was indeed extremely destitute;
she maintained her livelihood by means of engaging in sexual union.
That sinful woman, who was the very embodiment of evil, indeed knew medicinal herbs as well—
those that destroy fever, those that remove heat, and those that cure diseases.
That female friend knows the remedy for diseases of the private organs and other ailments; she even knows the remedy for miscarriage and the remedy for causing an abortion.
For this very reason, she was fearless even during sexual intercourse and other such acts; she bestowed yoga, was devoid of sinful knowledge, was simple-minded, and was exceedingly passionate.
Being wicked herself, she brings others to wickedness through her actions;
in this way, she gives rise to many husbands who are likewise devoid of dharma.
Embryos were repeatedly caused to fall and seeds were destroyed;
even those who were mature, young, or ready for birth were killed by means of medicines.
Thus that woman, who had committed the sin of killing a child, heard the narrative of the Saṃhitā; through it, she became aware of the great evil born from the murder of her child and other sins.
O friend, even for one possessed of knowledge, the suffering born of Yama is unbearable;
moreover, there is the terrible punishment of falling [into a womb] again and again in every successive birth.
Having realized this, she grieved in many ways and turned away from her sins;
thereafter, she sought to learn about expiation from a true guru.
Once, she went before Śrī Lomaśa to make her request; at the conclusion of the discourse, she approached Lomaśa and, having honored him like one in distress, spoke.
Having prostrated himself like a staff, he grasped the feet of the sage;
having performed the washing of the feet of the high-souled Lomaśa.
Placing his head at [the sage's] feet, he drank all the nectar of those feet and, having confessed all his sins and misdeeds, spoke without any deceit. (14)
The compassionate Lomaśa, having heard [his request], prescribed the Brahmakūrca vow,
as well as a decoction made from Palāśa leaves and other ingredients, along with the five products of the cow (pañcagavya).
He gave her the command to drink it, and she did exactly as he had said.
At the end of the month, her body purified, she received the mantra from Lomaśa.
Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Lord; svāhā!
O Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Narāyaṇa! || 17 ||
He received from the sage Lomaśa this mantra— "O Bālakṛṣṇa, Ādikṛṣṇa, Nārāyaṇa, Ramāyaṇa"— as well as the method of worship.
He also recited a hundred garlands of verses under the name Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa;
having bathed daily in the waters of the Indus river, he protected the nectar of his feet.
He always partakes of the grace of Kṛṣṇa with true devotion,
and he also eats the remnants from the vessels of the holy ones, which are purifying.

In the dwellings of the virtuous, she constantly performed cleaning, the polishing of bowls, and the application of ointments; having approached them, she served the holy ones by massaging their limbs.
And for the removal of sin, Anaṅgavallikā devoutly performs the smearing of her own body with dust that has been swept up. 22.
Remaining in the assembly, she constantly performs the ritual waving of incense and chanting;
she also gives fruits, flowers, and other offerings to the reciter of the Saṃhitā.
To Śrī Kṛṣṇa, to virtuous women, to the high-souled Lomaśa,
and to the wielder of the discus (Viṣṇu), he daily gives a gift of a single *ḍhabbuka* measure of wealth.
She constantly gave a handful of unbroken grains to the reciter;
thus did Sānaṅgavallikā act daily with devotion. (25)
He heard the discourse in its many forms, which purifies all sins,
removes all ignorance, destroys the deepest darkness, and bestows knowledge.
A month passed for her in activities such as conversing and attending to her duties;
then, she beheld in a dream the Lord Kṛṣṇa approaching her.
Touching his own [beloved], smiling at his own, making the Lord of Śrī smile, speaking to her saying "You are pure," and leading her back toward his own self. (28)
Having thus displayed himself for a mere moment, the Blessed Lord, the husband of Mādhavī, vanished from sight; she too awoke, filled with eager longing.
Rising suddenly in her own dwelling during the Brahma-muhūrta,
that beautiful woman quickly searched for Kṛṣṇa everywhere.
When she, having become overwhelmed with love, did not find him, then that innocent girl quickly bathed and performed worship of the Supreme Soul. ||31||
She went quickly for the purpose of worshipping with saffron and unbroken grains (akṣata) according to the Saṃhitā;
at the hour of Brahmā, there was a tumultuous stream of women in the early morning.
She was constantly engaged in the worship of the *Saṃhitā*;
in the midst of that, having meditated upon her beloved Lord as seen in a dream, she quickly departed. (33)
Then, having quickly worshipped Lomaśa,
her friend, being eager and with a serene mind, went to him and told him everything.
Having heard this, the venerable Lomaśa said: "You are pure and a practitioner of the yoga of devotion;
you have attained the favor of Kṛṣṇa and now abide like Ramā herself. (35)
Be ready to go to your abode; liberation shall be yours here, for all your sin has departed today since Kṛṣṇa has come within your range of vision. (36)
Then she also spoke quickly to her guru, O illustrious Badrikā:
"I am ready, O Blessed One; however, there is a reflection in my heart. (37)
By my yoga, those women who are young and deprived of husbands, as well as those burdened with faults such as causing abortions and likewise those guilty of foeticide—[may they be purified]. (38)
I desire their welfare, preceded by the destruction of their sins;
for you, O compassionate Guru, possess both the power and the command to do so here.
I bring all of them here for refuge unto you for their liberation;
for nowhere can they find it except through Nārāyaṇa Kṛṣṇa and the true Guru.
There can never be any deliverance for sinful women;
indeed, without the refuge of the devotees of Viṣṇu, there is no protection at all. ||41||
Without serving the devotees of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, there is no expiation for sin; without the grace of the virtuous, there is no destruction of the latent impressions of the wicked. 42.
Without the sacred ford of consciousness, there is no purification for those of sinful nature;
O Guru, in this illusory world, purity is difficult for women to attain. (43)
In the field of desire, however, service rendered by those free from desire indeed bestows purity;
for that woman who desires purity, liberation, and the supreme state of Brahman. (44)
Therefore, one should serve the saintly devotees of Hari, who are free from desire and are embodiments of Kṛṣṇa;
through service to the saintly, there is the destruction of lust, anger, greed, and other vices. (45)
O Guru, just as the destruction of my own latent impressions has occurred, so too do I desire the purification of my friends. (46)
When the divine Guru Kṛṣṇa is attained, self-liberation is considered foremost; yet by the grace of both Kṛṣṇa and the Guru, that liberation is also considered attainable for one's own people.
The merit gained from saving oneself is ten thousandfold when it comes to saving another;
however, the merit for saving women in that regard is considered to be ten millionfold.
Indeed, that which arises from the lifting up of the universe is for the sake of rescuing those who are without a protector;
O Guru, those women who are without a protector have fallen into my snare.
"As long as they have not been rescued, so long shall I remain in hell;
having caused the downfall of one who has risen, may he forgive this offense."
"Having made my own debt-free, I shall then go happily to heaven;
such, O Guru, is the thought in my mind as one who has liberated his wife. (51)
Having placed them all in darkness, how can my liberation come about?
For in this matter, true friendship consists precisely in that both parties share the same gain. (5.2)
O Lord, gain and other benefits consisting solely of self-interest lead to hell when accompanied by deceit;
therefore, I must by all means effect their liberation.
"O Sadguru, this moment will not come again;
O Badrikā, having spoken thus, Anaṅgavallarī fell silent. (54)
Lomaśa, considering it auspicious, spoke to her out of compassion: "O blessed lady, you speak what is fitting; you are reflecting upon what is most excellent. (55)
A living being who pursues only his own self-interest will become a denizen of hell; of this there is no doubt.
Such a person who seeks only his own ends becomes a crow, a serpent, or a pig.
You are a virtuous woman devoted to the welfare of others, bringing prosperity to both [yourself and others]. For one who effects the welfare of others, her own welfare naturally arises. (57)
"You have certainly conquered the next world, O benefactress;
for you, though most wicked and sinful, have lived according to your own will. (58)
If a virtuous woman attains heaven through the dharma of helping others, then helping others is for the sake of merit, whereas causing pain to others brings about sin. (59)
One who destroys the suffering of others is released from the bondage of misery;
one who bestows happiness upon others is honored in the heavenly world.
"O Anaṅgavallī, you must certainly bring the circle of friends;
I shall impart the mantra to them here, and likewise bestow the recitation of my name. (61)
I shall undertake the vow; I will perform the Brahmakūrca rite which destroys sin.
I shall make them pure, partakers of liberation, and attainers of purification.
Thus was it spoken, O Badrikā, by the great seer Lomaśa,
after he had quickly gone to Śarkarānagara and to whatever other places there were.
In that city, young women who were without husbands became intent on sexual intercourse, and they fell into the sins of causing miscarriages and killing fetuses. (64)
Those various Anaṅgavallarīs, united with Anaṅgavallī,
awakened them for the removal of sins and likewise for their ultimate welfare.
Having gained confidence and accompanied by Anaṅgavallikā,
they bathed, took the materials for worship, and arrived before their teacher.
O Badrī, those hundred young women were widows who caused miscarriages;
and there were also a hundred maidens in the prime of youth who were killers of embryos.
Having arrived before the venerable Lomaśa, filled with grief due to the fear of sin,
they approached the sage with shame, trusting the words of their own female companion.
Then they all drank the water from Lomaśa’s feet and listened to his discourse; thereafter, they undertook the Brahmakūrca vow.
They performed worship for the Saṃhitā and indeed for the reciter;
they circumambulated him, offered praise, and then begged for his forgiveness.
They received the mantra from the sage and took up the name-chanting:
"Oṃ namo śrīkṛṣṇanārāyaṇāya pataye svāhā. (71)
Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Nārāyaṇa; Bālakṛṣṇa, Ādikṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Ramāyaṇa! ||72||
Having thus obtained the mantra and performed worship accordingly,
they always bathed at the holy ford and listened to the narrative of the Saṃhitā.
Thus, O Badarī, while all those [rivers] were present—
purified, being born, and devoted to the service of the virtuous— (74)
Lomaśa was pleased with all those women who were intent on his command;
Lomaśa then bestowed upon them that which was born from Kṛṣṇa’s grace.

Having received the holy prasāda, which was like sweet food produced from their own vessels, they ate it with great devotion, even though it was the very fruit they had previously consumed themselves.
Then, from their bodies, black crows emerged;
they all became known as "slayers of embryos" (garbhahatyā) and likewise as "slayers of fetuses" (bhrūṇahatyā).
Flying up again and again into the sky, they fell into the ocean at the mouth of the Indus;
indeed, those sins in the form of crows suddenly met their destruction.
Those women, having attained purity, worshiped Nārāyaṇa;
let them listen with one-pointed minds to this Pārāyaṇa, distinguished by its inner sentiment.
Then, on the full moon day of the month of Phālguna, Kṛṣṇa Narāyaṇa arrived to lead the Anagha vine.
Seated upon his celestial chariot on the ground before the city of Anaṅgavallikā,
he spoke to her to come onto the chariot for the sake of liberation.
Then, out of compassion, she said: "O Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, these two hundred female companions of mine are also women who are vessels for sin. (82)
If there are those who have become sinless through the application of the Kathālomaśa [mantra], they should be led to your imperishable abode after you have made them divine. 83.
"O beloved Kṛṣṇa, I do not desire liberation alone;
rather, deliver all of them first, and then deliver me as well. (84)
Having heard this, the compassionate Lord Bālakṛṣṇa, the master of light, became exceedingly pleased and said, "O Anaṅgavallī, may it be well with you. (85)
I shall lead all those widows to my supreme imperishable state;
together with you, I will make them equal to Kamalā by means of a celestial chariot.
As for those who are indeed maidens, there is no liberation for them at present;
let all of them dwell fearlessly in their father's house. (87)
Purified and freed from sinful bodies, they were blessed by me with my grace;
having married them and experienced the life of a householder, thereafter— (88)
"At the end of my life, they shall come to my abode; of this there is no doubt.
Having spoken thus, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa touched them with his hand. (89)
At that time, all those hundred widows remained there listening to the Saṃhitās; having purified them all, they then [departed].
Having endowed her with a divine body, he caused her to ascend her own celestial chariot;
meanwhile, he commanded the maidens to remain in their father's house.
O Badrī, while everyone was looking on, Kṛṣṇa went by celestial chariot to his own great imperishable abode, as did Anaṅgavallikā herself. 92.
She quickly assumed a divine body, adorned with celestial ornaments; mounting a celestial chariot, she went to the imperishable abode of Hari.
There was a great cry of victory and a rain of flowers fell at that time;
for when Kṛṣṇa raised up the lowly, his majesty became truly incomparable. (94)
O Badrikā, by the mere hearing of this narrative, all those who had destroyed their embryos attained purification and were liberated from the power of their preceptor. 95.
Oh, how supreme is the power of the Guru! Even the Blessed Lord, becoming powerless in his presence, carries out the word of the true Guru. (96)
Having seen and heard of that greatness which destroys the faults of sexual misconduct, other women as well then joyfully took refuge in Kṛṣṇa. (97)
Devoted solely to exclusive devotion, they destroyed their own faults;
they recited the mantra and performed the chanting of the Name. (98)
They performed service to the virtuous, they practiced the merit of giving, they took up total surrender, and they attained purity. ||99||
Thereupon they became divine beings, devoted to moral conduct and firm in righteousness,
always endowed with devotion to the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa.
Thus, O Goddess Śrī Badrikā, the Lord Kṛṣṇa, Hari himself, that ocean of compassion, brought about their liberation when the time had arrived. || 101 ||
From reciting, hearing, remembering, and even reflecting upon this, as well as from grasping its virtues and putting it into practice, heaven and liberation will certainly be attained. (102)

Thus ends the fifty-sixth chapter, titled "The Description of the Liberation and Deliverance from Sin through the Hearing of the Saṃhitā and the Practice of Mantras and Vows of Anaṅgavallarī—who resided in Śarkarāpura, who caused sexual misconduct, and who was a destroyer of fetuses, embryos, and children—along with her two hundred female companions," in the Tiṣya lineage within the glorious *Lakṣmīnārāyaṇīya-saṃhitā*.
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Goddess, beloved of Badrī, to the story of the group of eunuchs. There was a eunuch named Ṣaṇḍhavraja in the city of Śrī Śarkarāpura. || 1 ||
This very one, who is the teacher of a hundred eunuchs and has received initiation many times, wears the dress of a woman; he is neither of the feminine gender nor of the masculine gender.
Even though he has abandoned the realm of desire, he remains filled with the latent impressions of desire;
the initiated eunuch always persists, endowed with the initiation of a eunuch.
He maintains his own livelihood entirely through begging for alms,
yet he can always sustain himself even by means of other forms of labor, including royal service.
There, they heard from the people and human beings that auspicious greatness of the narrative, which bestows liberation and destroys all sins.
Furthermore, by hearing this narrative, one shall no longer see rebirth;
all former sins are undoubtedly destroyed. (6)
Indeed, all other merits, even those earned in this very life, are reduced to ashes for that person born as a human who does not listen to this narrative at all.
He who does not strive for his own liberation is a eunuch; he is nothing but a beast, even if he be a king, a wealthy man, a merchant chief, a protector of subjects, or a leader of the people. (8)
Nevertheless, even a bull, a donkey, a eunuch, a beast, a bird, a woman, or even one who is intoxicated—one such as these would not seek liberation for their own sake. (9)
Even a dog-cooker or a rogue who acts for his own spiritual welfare is the best;
liberation is what must be achieved, for that indeed is the supreme goal of human endeavor.
Even if all means of accomplishment exist and are present, he by whom liberation has not been achieved is a mere insect; he is even a pig.
For indeed, dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa are the goals of human life;
having protected dharma, artha, and kāma as is appropriate, [one should seek liberation].
Having first abandoned their attachments, human beings desire liberation;
the great sages of old did likewise, and not otherwise.
Others who know the Self likewise proceed through the stages in succession;
however, virtuous renunciants, having abandoned those stages, desire liberation.
Even kings, having reached the forest and burned away their desires, become intent on austerity;
being free from desire, they truly attain liberation thereafter.
The element consists of defects and is the activator of latent impressions;
if that were not present in the body, that would indeed be the grace of the Lord. (16)
Thinking thus, having taken refuge in Hari, having bowed to the virtuous, having attained liberation, and having served holy men and propitiated the teacher with devotion; || 17 ||
Having offered his entire self to the Guru as well,
he makes himself free from the bonds of Māyā, stainless, and devoid of latent impressions (vāsanā).
Having made everything divine— possessing a divine nature and divine vision—
one should ascend the celestial chariot of Kṛṣṇa and proceed to the supreme abode.
Having become a servant of Hari, she became a maidservant of Kṛṣṇa in Vaikuṇṭha,
and likewise in Goloka, in the immortal realm, and in the unmanifest abode of Brahman.
In Śrīpura, the abode of the Blessed One, one should savor the nectar of Hari and ever partake of the grace of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa. (21)
Whether it be a man, a woman, a eunuch, or even an animal, one who has thus attained absolute liberation (kaivalya) is considered to be that very [supreme] Person (puruṣa). ||22||
Liberation is the great goal of man, which has been accomplished by him;
for in this world, a man is truly a man when he possesses his purpose, and that purpose is indeed the goal of man. (23)
The mutual association between these two is always meaningful;
yet, one does not understand the goals of human life in this way, nor does one expand them. ||24||
He who is full of pride in his manhood in vain is indeed a eunuch; there is no doubt about this.
That state of being a eunuch, created by Māyā in the past, must always be abandoned.
Indeed, [this world] causes living beings to fall from the path of liberation and is self-destructive;
therefore, the virtuous should be served, sacred stories should be heard, and the Lord Śrīpati should be attained. ||26||
Furthermore, rebirth known as "eunuch" (ṣaṇḍha), which is like a grove of trees, must be avoided;
for even one endowed with sons, grandsons, and so forth, may attain liberation. ||27||
"O Badrikā, having reflected thus—that he has the nature of a grove of trees, and though possessing testicles, he is actually a eunuch—those [disciples] along with their guru became eunuchs. (28)

Placing the group of eunuchs at their head, they arrived at the place where the auspicious stories were being told, having approached for the sake of spiritual welfare and being filled with a spirit of devotion. (29)
Taking offerings and articles for worship in their hands, having performed their ablutions and being purified, they worshipped the supreme Kṛṣṇa.
They were chanting the names of their Lord: Kṛṣṇa, Mādhava, Śrī Narāyaṇa, Nārīśvara, Narāvāsa, Bahucara, and Adhiṣāyaṇa. ||31||
Thus singing the seven-fold song, all those eunuchs went to the place of discourse;
from afar, they indeed bowed toward the pavilion.
Then, having arranged themselves in a circle, they all performed the rāsa dance; assuming the attire of women, they danced with rhythmic accompaniment.
They performed with leaping, singing, and whirling; they performed with instrumental music, graceful gestures, and excellent jesting. ||34||
In the midst of them was one dark-complexioned Nārāyaṇa holding a flute;
all the other women were gopīs [who joined] in the supreme rāsa dance. ||35||
Standing in a circle, they performed auspicious acts such as playful sports; seeing the *rāsa* dance of the eunuchs, the members of the assembly were struck with supreme wonder. (36)
The sages, the ascetics, the subjects, the king, the men, and the women all became filled with joy there during the bright fortnight of the month of Phālguna.
Then, on the evening of the full moon, at the conclusion of the discourse, Lomaśa became pleased, even though he is self-luminous. 38.
Those eunuchs, having bowed down repeatedly to Lomaśa, as well as to the Śrī-saṃhitā, and having also bowed to Brahmaprakāśa, then performed the most excellent worship. (39)
Then they gave golden necklaces set with jewels and beautiful garments; they also bestowed coins of gold, silver, and other metals, as well as clothes, vessels, and other articles. (4.57.40)
With saffron, unbroken grains of rice, flowers, and other offerings, they likewise worshipped the Saṃhitā; those eunuchs also worshipped Vyāsa and Lomaśa.
And they performed the *ārātrika* ceremony, preceded by the clapping of hands,
enriched with the sounds of mṛdaṅga drums and bronze cymbals, and graced by the whirring of *ghurghurā* bells and dancing.
And they offered excellent food offerings, including cooked grains and fruits;
that was presented to Hari by Vyāsa, who is the manifestation of Brahman. 43.
Graciousness, water, and likewise betel leaves—these were indeed given to them for the sake of refreshment, and they are truly purifying. (44)
Those eunuchs, having obtained the gracious favor of the Rasika, ate the fruit and drank the nectar of his feet. ||45||
Then they entreated the purifying sage Lomaśa for the sake of destroying the sin of impotence and for the removal of the misery born of impotence.
For the sake of removing their impotence, for the sake of liberation, and also for the sake of purification,
Lomaśa gave them a mantra as well as a means of worship.
Oṃ, salutation to Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Lord; svāhā!
Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Nārāyaṇa! ||48||
Having obtained even the mere mention of the names Bālakṛṣṇa, Ādikṛṣṇa, Nārāyaṇa, and Ramāyaṇa, they then became purified. 49.
They stayed right there for the night and performed the song of the *rāsa* dance;
on the first day of the dark fortnight of Phālguna, they held the festival of the flower-swinging.
They all celebrated a supreme festival following the narration, and hundreds of thousands of men also held a grand festival of flower-swinging. ||51||
They caused Kṛṣṇa, Lord Hari seated upon the swing, to be sprinkled with colored powders; hundreds of thousands of people bathed him profusely and rejoiced.
Men and women, having become separated, performed their play upon the stage;
thus, O Badarī, all those Vaiṣṇavas subsequently became eunuchs.
They constantly listen to and proclaim the stories of Nārāyaṇa;
they mutter mantras with rosaries and serve virtuous people. (54)
The Blessed One quickly becomes an object of perception for those possessed of intense spiritual urgency and devotion; however, he swiftly attains clarity even for eunuchs. (95)
In the dark fortnight of Caitra, those eunuchs observed the vow on the eleventh day;
they all kept a vigil and, having bathed in the morning, listened to the nectar of the sacred narrative.
They partook [of food] as usual in the morning, and then at midday;
having eaten, they went to the assembly hall and sat there happily. (57)
They performed meditation there upon Hari; meanwhile, Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of the beloved, arrived in a divine form seated within a celestial chariot. 98.
He said to them, "Indeed, let them be as you desire, possessing desired and beautiful forms;
likewise, let there be the form of Mukta and the form of Muktānikā according to your wish. (99)
"O Badarī, let whatever is desired by whichever men or women arise here by my will. When this was said, he who had been a eunuch among the women— ||4.57.60||
Muktānikā and the others attained divine forms entirely distinct [from their former selves],
while he among them who was a eunuch attained the state of liberation.
Thus, those auspicious liberated women, possessing divine forms,
suddenly became adorned with all ornaments there.
Then, having assumed a divine form, that multitude of eunuchs spoke there to those foremost men and enlightened them. (63)

Impotence arises for a woman who creates an obstacle at the moment of sexual union; likewise, it occurs for a co-wife who creates an obstacle, or for a wife who creates obstacles for her husband and his consort. (64)
For one who creates obstacles for her husband, as well as for domestic animals, birds,
or couples, the state of being a eunuch arises.
For a woman who abandons her husband to be attached to another,
or for one who cannot endure sexual pleasure and is full of hatred toward her husband, the state of being a eunuch arises.
[They are] women who practice malevolent magic, women who bind the private parts [of their husbands], women who cause the fall of the linga, and women who destroy the fertile season. ||67||
He is born as a eunuch in that very life and in future births;
and it is the same for a man who does not fulfill the desires of his wife.

[The same applies] to one who turns away from his own wife, to one who takes pleasure in the wives of others, to one who creates obstacles for couples, and to one who defiles virgins and the like. ||69||

Even for one who approaches those who should not be approached, for one who cuts off the testicles, and even for one who destroys the genitals and so forth of embodied beings such as cattle and birds; || 4.57.70 ||
Impotency arises for one who destroys an embryo and for one whose bodily constituents are depleted; generally, impotency occurs on this earth for those who perform evil deeds. (71)
For that is declared to be a great sin in a human birth;
being deprived of both masculinity and femininity is indeed the very form of hell.
Through our compassion for that [state] and by hearing this narrative today, we have attained both liberation and the supreme state of being liberated. (73)
The husband obtained is Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Brahman, the beloved Lord;
he is the Blessed One of unfailing power, the Sovereign who bestows the bliss of Brahman.
Let neither women nor men in this world commit the corruption of desire;
for those who create obstacles to desire, hell is indeed their destination here.
May those fortunate men and women, afflicted by fear, worship that Hari, the beloved of Śrī, without whom there can be no deliverance for them. (76)
Constantly remembering their own respective webs of evil deeds, let them go for refuge to Nārāyaṇa, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, and may they possess divine bodies. ||77||
And may those resting in His lap be born immersed in eternal bliss;
we, having bathed in the waters of the sacred ford and repeatedly drunk the nectar of Your story, [remain thus]. (78)
Having partaken of the remnants of Kṛṣṇa’s grace and attained the favor of our Guru, and having obtained Kṛṣṇa as our husband through devotion, let us go to the supreme, imperishable abode. (79)
Having assumed divine forms, worthy of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and abodes of happiness, may we become equal to Rādhikā, immersed in eternal bliss. (4.57.80)
Having spoken thus, O Badrikā, all those men and women, now liberated in form, sat upon a golden vehicle by Kṛṣṇa’s command and went to the Imperishable Abode. 81.
Indeed, by means of those very bodies of their own, those who were neuter, having transformed their bodies, then became liberated and divine. (82)
There was no falling of their bodies; rather, their bodies became transformed. By the mere touch of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, they were liberated and became eunuchs. ||83||
All the men and women were sixteen years of age and possessed the splendor of their sons;
they were all liberated souls, and Muktānikā was equal to Kṛṣṇa, Rādhā, and the Goddess Ramā.
Otherwise, that unimpeded power and sovereign will of Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of lords, would have been made manifest. (85)
This great wonder displayed by Kṛṣṇa in the narrative took up residence in the hearts of men and shone forth brilliantly. 86.
He could make the insentient sentient and make the sentient insentient;
he could turn a woman into a man and cause a man to become a woman. (87)
One may represent them as a man or a woman, or both as a hermaphrodite;
or one may depict the retinue as hermaphrodites, or as men and women.
One should cause the liberated soul (mukta) or the female liberated soul (muktānikā), as well as the divine insentient matter (jaḍa-divya), to be established;
he should make the imperishable Māyā, and he should indeed make the imperishable Prakṛti.
He should create the principles (tattvas) and the non-principles; he should make the Void (śūnya) consist of the nature of the principles.
He should produce one principle from another principle; these indeed are the powers of Hari.
The celestial chariot of Him who possesses infinite power is always difficult to attain;
yet there is nothing at all wonderful therein, since everything has Him as its essence. (91)
And then, having heard from Badrikā that eunuchs possess divine bodies, both women who were secretly eunuchs and men who were also secretly eunuchs [attained it]. 92.
Having gone to the place of the *saṃhitā*, they attained refuge; and with joy, they received from Lomaśa the mantra, the mode of worship, and the rhythmic chanting (*dhunyan*). ||93||

Having made each fortnight [of the lunar month] their own, they likewise performed worship, listening [to the teachings], meditation, service, adoration, and the eating of food granted as a favor. (94)
Having become free from sin, pure-souled, endowed with virtue, rich in great merit, and having attained mastery over their senses, they then became those [women]. 95.
Some, having meditated upon Śrī Hari and attained liberation, went to the imperishable realm;
thus, by the grace of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, even eunuchs [attained this] on earth. (96)
The men of truth and the noble women of truth became liberated through truth;
likewise, the female attendants of those liberated through truth also attained eternal bodies.
Oh, what is difficult to attain here where there is even a fragment of Kṛṣṇa’s grace?
Oh, how great is the majesty of this supreme Lord’s narrative, O Badarī! 98.
Everything has attained a state free from sin, such that the world is of the nature of liberation;
or else, all are either liberated while in the body or liberated beyond the body.
Born in Śarkarāpattana through hearing the narrative of the Śrīsaṃhitā, enjoyment and liberation shall come into one's hand by reading or hearing this [work]. (4.57.10)

Thus ends the fifty-seventh chapter, titled "The Description of the Liberation from Sin through Hearing the Saṃhitā by the Hermaphrodites of the Ṣaṇḍhavraja and others residing in Śarkarāpura within the Tiṣya lineage in the glorious Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā; and the attainment of the imperishable realm (Akṣara-pada) by those very bodies—consisting of divine female souls—through the vision of Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa; as well as the manifestation of masculinity, femininity, and so forth in other secret hermaphrodites through taking refuge [in Him]. || 57 ||
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Goddess beloved of Badarī, to this story that destroys all sins.
Long ago, it took place at Karāñcanīpura, on the shore of the ocean at the mouth of the Sindhu river.
A certain man named Yavasandha, a slayer of those who eat cows, lived there;
he was a great killer who delighted in meat, wine, and gambling.
Having killed hares, monkeys, boars, deer, forest birds, aquatic creatures, as well as gayals, goats, and antelopes; || 3 ||
Together with his family, he cooks, sells, and eats [meat];
thus, he is of sinful conduct and always devoted to evil. || 4 ||
The "Cock-eater" is one who consumes the fluid of a hen's egg;
having fallen from his body and fallen from his karma, he is born into the Yavasaṃdhīya caste.
Yavasaṃdhi heard news from the mouths of the sailors;
there, in Śarkarānagara, was the auspicious account of the Saṃhitā.
It arises as the bestower of liberation and the cleanser of all sins;
moreover, its listeners are born with divine bodies and go to the world of Brahmā.
The Blessed One, the refuge, who is affectionate toward his devotees, forgives all the sins of the devotee who has come for refuge and bestows heaven upon him.
Many violent beings, including women and men, were delivered by him;
and there dwells the seer Lomaśa, as well as the self-luminous Lord.
Likewise, there are those who are virtuous and righteous, as well as noble women and brahmin-sages; indeed, by the sight of them, by serving them, and by pleasing them, [one attains purity].
Eternal liberation is born, and there is a supreme journey by means of a celestial chariot;
indeed, an occasion such as this will not meet us again.
O Badrikā, Yavasaṃdha, who destroys sin, is pure, and bestows effortless liberation,
heard these auspicious words.
At that very moment, a desire for liberation arose in him instantly for the destruction of his sins:
"Indeed, infinite killings and sins have been committed by me. (1.3)
For them there would be no deliverance without taking refuge in divine beings;
all these supporters of the boat speak that very truth. (14)
I am going to Śarkarāpurī and shall destroy my sins;
if there is for me the destruction of evil, may there be the destruction of the sin of many killings. (15)
Then what remains for me here that would be superior to that, if there is indeed a turning back from actions performed upon this earth? (16)
What further goal remains for me to accomplish, or what duty is left for me? I must certainly go there, where nothing exists but mere life-breath.
One must necessarily dwell where there is peace for oneself;
one must necessarily give where what is sown becomes fruitful. (18)
One must necessarily sleep where there is fearlessness;
one must necessarily die where there is eternal bliss. (19)
If I go there as an expounder of the meaning of the Saṃhitā, my sins will be destroyed; therefore, I must certainly go for the sake of liberation.
I shall never again return to Karāñcanīpura; sinful action does not please me—not at all, not at all, not at all. (21)
Accompanied by my family, I shall go toward Śarkarānagara;
I will travel quickly by means of a large, engine-driven boat. (22)
Having reflected thus, Yavasaṃdha spoke to his wife, named Mājāvalī, regarding everything auspicious that he had intended in his mind. (23)
She too considered her own fortune to be blessed by the sight of the land,
as well as the sight of its sanctity and the witnessing of the great festival.
O Badarī, she considered the contemplation of liberation to be superior to violence and other such acts; her sons and daughters likewise held that same view. (25)
Then those twenty-one householders quickly [offered] wealth,
goods, ornaments, garments, and even foods.
Medicines suitable for the household, as well as perfumes, vessels for preparing the body and other requisites, and whatever else is necessary. (27)
Eagerly, they carried away everything—caskets, implements, the corpse, and so forth—as well as whatever else was suitable and beneficial for the funeral procession. (28)
Then, by means of a boat capable of reaching the shore of the ocean through the force of its engine,
they went first to the mouth of the river, and from there, by boat, into the river itself.
By that very [means], they all suddenly went forth with full joy;
having bathed in the waters of the Sindhu, they reached the illustrious land of Śarkarābhūmi.
Having presented their offerings, they went to the excellent pavilion of discourse;
there they heard the delightful narrative that destroys all sins.
At the conclusion of the discourse, they all honored the reciter with auspicious gifts; thereafter, they likewise bowed down to Lomaśa and the other holy men.
They offered prayers seeking liberation from sin that bring about auspiciousness;
and then Lomaśa bestowed upon them the Śrī-Brahmakūrca.
He gave him the vow, the five products of the cow (pañcagavya), as well as the name of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the mantra, the dhunyan, the devotional service, and likewise the nectar of his feet.
Out of grace, he gave them food for the purpose of destroying their sins;
they too, with great devotion, ate that excellent food.
They drank the water, observed the vow, and practiced listening to the sacred stories;
at the end of the month, they all became purified and freed from sin.
Thus their end of life occurred in accordance with their meditative cultivation;
having taken their meal at midday on the twelfth day of the dark fortnight of Caitra.
They all then sat down in the courtyard of the residence;
at that moment, a divine celestial chariot suddenly arrived from the sky.
Touched by the splendor of the celestial chariot, they all fell into a swoon;
even then, the four-armed Hari became visible to them.
The eternal Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Lord of Mādhavī,
having transformed them into divine bodies, caused their corpses to be cast away.
Having placed them upon celestial chariots, he led them to his own auspicious, imperishable abode;
even the great sages were filled with supreme wonder upon seeing that at that time.
They praised the compassionate treasure-house, the beloved Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa;
and they praised all those human beings who had come for refuge. ||42||
Filled with devotion, they praised those who were free from sin despite having committed great evils, saying:
"Oh! Even for those who have committed countless sins, the Blessed Lord Hari [is the refuge]. (43)
And by his irreversible compassion, he effects supreme liberation.
Blessed is Nārāyaṇa-Kṛṣṇa; blessed are those who partake in liberation. 44.
Blessed is the city of Śārkara; blessed is the narrative that bestows liberation.
O Badarī, in this very way, others indeed attained liberation there. (45)
From reciting, hearing, and reflecting upon this, there is liberation from evil;
there shall be both enjoyment and liberation, as well as the eternal state. ||46||

Thus ends the fifty-eighth chapter, titled "The Description of the Liberation through Hearing the Narratives of the Saṃhitā of Yavasaṃdha and his Family—who were constantly committing slaughter in Karāñcanīpura—within the Tiṣya lineage" in the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Goddess beloved of Badarī, to the story of Bhāṇḍa which bestows liberation.
In the city of Dvārāmṛta, there lived a man named Bhāṇḍa who had a family. || 1 ||
He was an elder among his kinsmen, possessed of supreme intelligence, and skilled in humor, jesting, and the like;
he was present at all royal festivals as well as those of the common people.
Being thus addressed, he departs quickly; at night he plays, and then indeed performs songs, playful verses, and amorous acts.
Having performed and displayed these things before the kings, he indeed makes their subjects laugh;
thus that skillful man remains and receives a reward.
He became well-known on earth by the name Bhaṇḍaśīlaka;
he too heard from the people about the great festival of the Pārāyaṇa.
Where an assembly of hundreds of thousands and millions of people gathers, divine stories indeed arise, along with ever-new diversions. (6)
There are indeed playful pastimes and even novel manifestations;
and through merely hearing this narrative, the destruction of evil occurs.
For those who possess supreme devotion, there arises both the company of the virtuous and the vision of the Supreme Self; indeed, a wondrous marvel occurs.
There, the most beautiful celestial chariot of Śrī Hari arrives;
having attained liberation, people go to the supreme abode of the Supreme Lord.
Men and women indeed go here to the imperishable abode of Hari;
there, liberation from sins is bestowed by the Supreme Self.
Having thus described all the vessels and the strength of Hari,
he himself, accompanied by all the vessels and joined by men and women, [proceeded].
Accompanied by young girls and boys, together with elders worthy of honor,
and joined by all the chariots along with provisions for the journey.
Having yoked his draft animals such as cattle, he prepared himself and set out with great eagerness, meditating upon Śrī Hari and bowing to the deity of the village. (13)
Taking wealth intended for charity, as well as ornaments, garments, clothing,
and his favorite implements and other items, he departed toward the place of the discourse.
Having bathed in the waters of the Indus near the city of Śarkarā, he,
together with his entire family and accompanied by three hundred men, [proceeded].
Having established his residence in the royal garden, he attained well-being,
equipped with the materials for worship and accompanied by elderly men.
He went to the pavilion of discourse for the purpose of worshipping Vyāsa;
having gone to the site of the Saṃhitā and having bowed to the members of the assembly as well.
Victory to you, Kṛṣṇa, the bestower of victory and liberation; O Vyāsa, live long!
May the sages, who are venerable elders and compassionate, be victorious here.
May these virtuous ones be victorious, and may the listeners here also be victorious;
may those who perform pilgrimages and dwell at sacred fords always be triumphant upon the earth.
May the wise women and virtuous men who bring about liberation be victorious;
may the Vaiṣṇava people, the removers of the sin of ignorance, be victorious.
Speaking thus, they indeed repeatedly struck them like sticks;
they cast the dust of the assembly hall upon their heads and bodies.
Then, having received the command of Vyāsadeva, they arrived for the purpose of worship,
setting down various offerings, flower garlands, sesame seeds, and unbroken grains of rice.
They placed fruits and betel leaves before the Saṃhitā,
and then they performed worship of Vyāsa with sandalwood paste and other offerings.
They performed the lustration ceremony and circumambulated him;
all the musicians and their attendants performed dances and songs.
Making people laugh with their eloquent speech and bowing within the assembly hall, they sat down, seeking to hear [the teaching], after having received his favor and drunk water. ||25||
Having heard the discourse, they received the mantra from the venerable sage Lomaśa:
"Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord, svāhā. (26)
Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Narāyaṇa; Bālakṛṣṇa, Ādikṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Ramāyaṇa. ||27||
Thus Dhunya gave them [the names] for the purpose of chanting their names;
then, having taken refuge in Hari, they went to their own abodes in well-being.
Everyone, from children to the elderly, constantly listen to the stories of Hari and sing his songs; they all serve holy yogis.
Thus, having maintained that constant association, the month passed quickly;
on the night of the eleventh day of the dark fortnight of Caitra, they performed a vigil.
On the twelfth day, having performed their ablutions and after listening to the sacred narratives,
they suddenly [beheld him] upon the assembly hall's throne, exceedingly radiant.
They beheld the smiling Śrīśa Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa,
while Vyāsa was manifesting the Lord before the gaze of the assembly members.
Hari quickly vanished, and Ramā entered the Saṃhitā;
seeing that supreme marvel, the sage Śrī Lomaśa [was struck with wonder].
In that assembly, he spoke of the rising fortune of the vessels;
and on the thirteenth day, he likewise revealed a further narrative.
Likewise, on the fourteenth day, the Pārameśvara [rite] was performed;
and at dawn on the new moon day, the vessels beheld the most excellent dream. (35)
They beheld them departing for the imperishable abode by means of celestial chariots;
then, with hearts full of joy, they quickly rose up toward the realm of Brahmā.
Having bathed and become ready, many of them went to the place of discourse; at the conclusion of the discourse, however, they openly declared what had come within the scope of their dreams.
But Lomaśa, having heard this, said: "Today shall indeed be your liberation; it will take place this evening at the conclusion of the discourse. Prepare yourselves for your release. (38)
Those vessels also became ready for departure as was appropriate;
then, at the conclusion of the evening discourse, the Lord, the Master Kṛṣṇanarāyaṇa, [spoke]. (39)
Having extracted them from their bodies and endowed them with divine forms, he came in a radiant golden celestial chariot to lead them away.
Having obtained a divine celestial chariot, he went to his own imperishable abode;
one hundred and fifty were liberated, as were the Muktānikās and the Bhāṇḍakas.
Having shattered the vessel of the universe, they attained the vessel of Brahman;
oh, how wondrous is the compassion of the supreme Self, the illustrious Mādhava! 42.
Having taken the vessels, Kṛṣṇa, the husband of Lakṣmī and Padmāvatī, departed.
Then, O Badrikā, the other remaining vessels were for his funeral rites. 43.
Having become supreme Vaiṣṇavas on the banks of the Siṅghu,
they indeed established their residence there for the purpose of hearing the sacred narrative.
They too constantly performed service to the virtuous and the holy with joy; they practiced the service of chaste women, celibate students, and ascetics. ||45||
Through service, worship, and the sight [of Him], they were born sinless;
they became great devotees (mahābhāgavatas), and their lineages became purifying. 46.
Men and women became devoted to the saintly and equal to them;
even in the practice of total self-surrender, they were knowers of the Self, free from doubt. (47)
O Badrikā, those among them whose lifespan came to an end also proceeded slowly to the imperishable abode by means of a divine vehicle.
Other boys, youths, and young women took refuge in Hari—the beloved Kṛṣṇa, the glorious Lord, the husband of Mādhavī—for as long as they lived. 49.
Through their association, many kinsmen and relatives also became devotees of the beloved Śrī Kṛṣṇa and attained the supreme abode. (4.59.50)
