Gāyatrī and the other wives of Brahmā fanned him with fans,
while Sāvitrī and the others there performed the service of serving food.
Hari was satisfied, as were the wives of Hari, the female servants, the male servants, the attendants, and the saintly associates;
they too were satisfied, and then they took a single handful of water.
They drank the water of immortality and took mouth-fresheners;
the Blessed One and all the beloved consorts of Śrī Hari partook of betel-leaf. 8.1.
They also took other mouth-perfumes, divine betel nuts, fragrant seeds, and cooling grains. (82)
Having eaten and risen, Hari-Kṛṣṇa sat down upon a great throne;
so too did Brahmā, the wives of Brahmā, and the sons of Brahmā and others.
All the sages, beginning with Sanaka, and the supreme lifelong celibates, beginning with Ṛbhu, partook of the prasāda of Śrī Hari with great devotion. (84)
The virtuous Satyas, headed by Śāradā, partook of the prasāda;
thereafter, the Blessed Lord respectfully [offered it] to the inhabitants of Satyaloka. ||85||
The protector granted his own mantra himself to those who had come for refuge:
"Oṃ namaḥ śrīkṛṣṇanārāyaṇāya svāmine svāhā. (86)
He likewise gave him this mantra: "Oṃ, let us know Bālakṛṣṇa; let us meditate upon Anādikṛṣṇa; may that Lord of Śrī inspire us. (89)
In the world of truth (satyaloka), there were millions of perfected ones (siddhas), those to be perfected (sādhyas), lifelong celibates (naiṣṭhikas),
and those who had dwelt as gods and others in previous and even earlier kalpas.
All those gods and goddesses indeed became Vaiṣṇavas, taking refuge in Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, and they all began to chant His name. 89.
Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Narāyaṇa!
O Lord Anādi-Śrī-Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Ramāyaṇa! || 4.93.90 ||
In this manner, Brahmā celebrated the festival of the mountain of food;
so too did Dakṣa and the other sons of Brahmā, as well as Nārada and the other great sages.
Those who had gone to Satyaloka joyfully received Kṛṣṇa’s grace;
Nārada and the other celestial musicians performed dances and songs of praise. ||92||
The Apsarases from the lake of Brahmā performed dances with great joy;
likewise did the yogins, ascetics, Siddhas, forest-dwellers, and celibate students. ||93||
The gods—truthful ones dwelling in truth who shall not die again—performed the name-chanting of the Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa. 94.
Having arrived at the abode of Brahmā, they performed the worship of Śrī Hari;
they received his divine grace and accepted the mantra of Hari. (95)
Then the glorious Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, having propitiated the Creator and being praised by Viṣṇu, departed from there for the abode of Nārāyaṇa.
Having indeed reached the vast realm of Viṣṇu in the abode of Viṣṇu, he is honored with the highest hospitality by Viṣṇu, Śrī, and all the attendants. (97)
On the full-moon day of the month of Kārttika, the Lord of Padmāvatī joyfully accepted the welcome, worship, and the offering of the divine Kaustubha gem and other gifts from Urja.
Having obtained auspicious food and drink, as well as worship performed with splendor,
the Lord departed for the city of Hara, which is composed of light, by means of a celestial chariot.
Hara, the leader of millions upon millions of hosts, with a joyful mind,
approached Hari and prostrated like a staff along with his millions of attendants.
Having caused Kṛṣṇa, who was traveling in a celestial chariot, to wander through the city composed of light,
he led him to his own golden abode and worshipped him with flowers and jewels.
Śaṅkara also performed the nightly lamp-offering and fed him ambrosia;
he served Kṛṣṇa together with all his attendants.
The Gaṇas, the Gaṇikās, and Satyas, together with Śrī Satī, performed service to Hari and to Lakṣmī and the others with exceeding devotion.
Hari gave the mantra to them and his own supreme mantra to those women;
having thus established the Vaiṣṇavas and received their worship thereafter, [he departed].
Requested by the self-born Manu who had come to him, the Lord Kṛṣṇa departed together with him;
he was honored, worshipped, and increased in prosperity with all kinds of wealth.
Attended by women such as Śatarūpā, the Lord of Śrī and Pramā pleased that Manu and departed for the abodes of the other Manus.
All those Manavas, having established their respective wives in their own palaces and having obtained the mantra, worshipped Hari with all their wealth.
The wives of the Manus, who were the wives of Kṛṣṇa, purified themselves with devotion;
they then performed the ritual waving of lamps (ārātrika) and likewise prepared meals.
Pleased with them, the Blessed One placed his feet upon their chests;
thereafter, Kṛṣṇa was sent away by means of his own celestial chariot.
Having completed his pilgrimage during the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, which is dear to Badrī, he went to the world of Tapas in Satyaloka, accompanied by all his kinsmen.

Thus ends the ninety-third chapter, titled "The Description of how the Blessed Lord, requested by Brahmā, departed for Satyaloka in a celestial chariot a hundred *yojanas* long accompanied by his millions and billions of wives and others, and after being worshipped there during the great festival of Dīpotsava, Annakūṭa, and so forth by Brahmā, Siddhayati, Manu, and others, Hari gladdened them and returned to Tapoloka," in the fourth section, the Tiṣya-santāna, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*. || 93 ||
Śrī Nara-Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O beloved of Badarī; Prajñāpārāvatīśvara went to the world of asceticism (tapoloka), the dwelling place of the practitioners of austerity. || 1 ||
The supreme celestial realm is the meritorious abode of the ancestors, beginning with Aryaman;
there dwell the gods who were appointed to their respective stations and constellations at the beginning of the previous kalpa.
Having completed their respective offices, it is there that the ṛṣis, the munis, the ancestors, and those who are the Śrāvaṇas dwell free from fear.
The years of Yama, the times, and those who are the presiding deities of time;
those lifelong celibates, ascetics, the elderly, and those devoted to meritorious endeavors.
Likewise, the Vairāja gods are entirely free from burning;
so too are the Prajāpati deities, the Saumyas, and the Barhiṣads.
The Agniṣvāttas, the Kāvyas, the Ṛtus, the Somapas,
the lords of the Aṣṭakās, the Lekhas, and also the Uṣmapas.
The Divākīrtyas are the Pitṛs, as are the Chhandajas;
the Śrāddhadevas are the Pitṛs, as well as the Yajvānas and the Ayonijas.
By means of celibacy, austerity, sacrifice, and likewise progeny;
by faith, knowledge, and gifts, as well as by action endowed with faith.
Those who have gone to the other world and dwell there, O ascetic—
whether they be the Vāruṇas, the Bhṛgus, the Āgneyas, or likewise the Āṅgirasas— [all these are present].
The Mārīcas, the Ātreyakas, the Paulastyas, the Paulahas,
the Vāsiṣṭhas, the Vasus, the Brahmās, and those Pitṛs.
These indeed belong to Prajāpati; King Yama is Prajāpati.
[They are] the Kārdamas, the Kāśyapas, the Śaiṣas, the Vikrāntas, Suśravas, and others. || 1 1 ||
Bahuputra, Kumāra, Vivasvat, Śuciśravas, Prācetasa, Ariṣṭanemi, Bahula, and Pitṛ— these are they.
The Kuśoccayas are the Pitṛs of Prajāpati;
likewise the Bālakhilyas, the Vaikhānasas, and both sons of the Aśvins.
All these dwellers in the world of austerity (tapoloka) enjoy the fruits of their merit;
there they beheld the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa who had arrived.
Having learned this, King Āryamā, accompanied by an army of ten million ascetics,
queens, and Mothers, went into the presence of Kṛṣṇa.
He caused Hari, accompanied by all the women in their celestial chariots, to enter his own city, Āryamṇī, which was adorned on all sides with ornaments.
In his own great palace, Aryaman seated him upon the lion-throne;
he worshipped Hari with jewels, flowers, and golden ornaments.
And he fed him with sandalwood and other unguents, with nectars and ambrosias, with unbroken grains and the like, as well as with various divine enjoyments and edible foods.
The two sinners also performed the nightly lamp-offering (ārārtrika) with the nectar-like water from her feet;
and Āryādevī, his queen, [performed it] for the sake of those who possess bodies of ancestors.
She worshipped the Supreme Soul as well as the beloved of Brahmā and the others;
indeed, the noble goddess Mātṛkā caused them all to be fed.
Then, in the month of Pauṣa, Kṛṣṇa, while residing in the palace of the Sun,
went repeatedly to the dwellings of those who inhabit the world of Tapas.
Mahāśveta, Vāmadeva, and other great sages joyfully brought Śrī Kṛṣṇa to their own excellent abodes. ||22||
Indeed, they honored him along with his entire caravan according to their wealth;
even the sages, such as Brahmasattva and Ayana, escorted Hari.
Just as they performed honors according to their wealth, so too did those who were devoted in spirit—
the ancestors beginning with Śravaṇa and the others— even though they were the rulers of the realm of the Pitṛs.
Together with their wives, they brought Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who was accompanied by his wife, to their own home;
there they worshiped, fed, and adorned the Lord.
Likewise, the ancestors of Yama, headed by Dharmadhana and others,
led Hari away by the thousands to their own abodes and worshipped him there.
Likewise, Samvatsara, Parivatsara, and the other Pitṛs, together with their respective families, led the Lord to their own abodes. (27)
They honored him according to their means, fed him with divine food, performed the *ārātrika* ceremony, and gave many gold coins and jewels. (28)
Likewise, the seasons, known as the presiding deities of time, along with the months and fortnights, and the ancestors, worshipped Śrī Hari and led him to their own abode. (29)
Then those lifelong ascetics who were aged, stores of merit,
known as the Pitṛs (Fathers) and Generators of Virtue— they too led Hari away.
In their respective abodes, they worshipped the Supreme Lord according to the prescribed rites;
then the Vairāja gods who dwell in the world of Tapas [did likewise].
Led by Svarṇadahana, they brought the Lord Nārāyaṇa to their respective abodes according to the prescribed rites, honoring the Lord like a sovereign king of kings.
They worshipped the Lord of Īśa and offered him precious gems;
then there were the Prajāpati gods, inhabitants of Tapoloka. ||33||
Yogins, Āhārakas, Abhidhyas, and others led the Lord of the Gods, the husband of Pārvatī, to their respective abodes and worshipped the Lord of Devas with the highest reverence.
They performed the *ārārtrika* and other rites and fed the Infallible One (Acyuta).
Then the gentle Pitṛs, known by names such as Cāndrāyaṇa and others, [also partook].
With devotion, they led the glorious Supreme Soul to their own abodes;
they honored Him with nectar and other offerings and fed Him the nectar.
And at the moment of worship, they gave him moonstones and other gems;
then the Barhiṣads, the Pitṛs such as Kuśika and others, also [gave].
Eagerly, they led the Lord to their respective dwellings and worshipped him; according to their means, they performed honors for him with food and other offerings. ||38||
Then the Pitṛs, such as the Agniṣvāttas and others like the Bhāsuras,
led Nārāyaṇa to their respective palaces and worshipped the Infallible One.
They indeed gave those purifying foods, such as milk-rice and other delicacies;
however, there were some ancestors of Kāvya who were fond of uncooked food.
They led the Supreme Soul to their respective abodes and worshipped him there.
Then Somāyana and others, who were drinkers of Soma and consumers of nectar, [approached].
They led Śrī Hari to their respective homes and, full of eagerness, worshipped him; they prepared delightful foods of nectar for Acyuta.
Then the lords of the Aṣṭakas, the ascetics, the ancestors, and those such as the descendants of Uttathya-Kāyana, led Hari to their own abodes. 42.
They worshipped him, fed him, and performed the *ārārtika* ceremony and other rites;
then the Lekhas, the Pitṛs, Vipralīpa, and the others [worshipped] Hari. (44)
They led him to their own hermitage with joy, honored him, and presented him with offerings; they fed him most abundantly and served the Lord with devotion.
Then the Uṣmapā Pitṛs, such as the Phenilehas and others, led Hari to their own hermitages and worshipped Śrī Puruṣottama there.
And they gave edible offerings such as fresh butter and other foods according to their wealth.
Now, as for those ancestors known as the Divākīrtis, such as the Ṛṣikas and others—
They too, being eager, led Hari to their own abodes and worshipped him;
and the Chandas-born ancestors, beginning with Anuṣṭubh, also led him there.
They worshipped Hari, the Lord and Supreme Controller, in their own abodes;
and the Pitṛs, the gods of the Śrāddha rites, led the Lord of Śrī to their own home. 49.
They honored him, fed him, and performed the waving of lights and other rites;
even the sacrificial kings and those who were universal emperors did likewise.
Those who were situated in the world of Tapas also brought Nārāyaṇa to their home and worshipped him with great respect using articles worthy of royalty.
The excellent Varuṇas, Bhārgavas, Āgneyas, and Pitṛs gave gifts and fed the Infallible One.
The Āṅgīrasas, the Mārīcas, the ascetics of the Ātreya lineage,
the Paulastyas, the Paulahas, the Vāsiṣṭhas, and those who are the Vasus.
Those stainless lords of creatures, belonging to various distinct stages of life (āśramas), each led the Lord of Śrī, the husband of Rādhikā, to their own respective hermitages. 54.
In the world of Tapas, they honored him with reverence and, full of eagerness, fed him;
Yama and Prajāpati also led the Lord to their own abodes.
The Kārdamas, the Kāśyapas, the Śaiṣas, the Vikrāntas, those beginning with Suśravas,
the Pitṛs known as Bahuputras, and also the Kumāra-pitṛs.
The Prācetasas, the Vivasvants, the Ariṣṭanemayas,
and the Kuśoccayas— these Pitṛs also led Nārāyaṇeśvara.
In their respective abodes, they worshipped with offerings, filled with joy; they fed them most abundantly and served them with eager devotion.
The Vālakhilya sages and those who are Vaikhānasas,
as well as the two divine physicians and others who have taken refuge in asceticism.
They led the Lord of the Goddesses together with his consort in celestial chariots to their respective abodes;
they worshipped him, performed the *ārārtika* lustration ceremony, and presented offerings.
In every house they fed him with excellent foods that were like nectar;
in every village and in every home, they caused the Lord of Lords to wander.
Those perfumers and garland-makers gave them beds, seats, and articles of enjoyment; they also presented ornaments, garments, and such things as necklaces of jewels and gems. ||62||
They gave him, according to his needs, alms-bowls, seats, priceless ornaments, and other such items;
they presented these new requisites to the Lord of Kamalā.
And they offered food and means of recreation to the Supreme Self in sacred gardens, groves, and in the regions of forests, wildernesses, and mountains. (64)
Having led the king of all around his own kingdoms, palaces, subjects, and dwellings, they, full of eagerness, purified him.
They drank the nectar from His feet, as did those various auspicious women;
having fed Hari, those women received His grace.
They considered their own good fortune to be supreme, blessed, and fortunate;
through the grace of Nārāyaṇa, they became fulfilled in all their aims. ||67||
They delighted the Lord of Īśas by bestowing their respective riches upon him,
and they served Śayaneśvara exceedingly according to his desire.
They fed the Lord of Life and presented him with excellent offerings:
fragrant substances, wealth, divine garments, and ornaments. (69)
Many women swung Kṛṣṇa on swings;
they massaged his feet and likewise rubbed his limbs.
They displayed their respective skills before him:
"Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord; svāhā! (7.1)
They also took up the two mantras: "We know Bālakṛṣṇa; we meditate upon Anādikṛṣṇa; may that Śrīśa impel us. (72)
Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Nārāyaṇa!
Anādi-Śrī-Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Beloved of Ramā! ||73||
Thus they took up the name Dhunya for the Lord of Śrīmādhavī;
they designated his mother as Śrī, Ramā, Lakṣmī, Prajñā, and Arhaṇā.
Likewise, the goddesses and the wives of the Brahmins honored him with offerings;
they held festivals of dance and song in their own dwellings where Janārdana was staying.
They offered everything as an oblation to Brahmā, the Supreme Self;
both men, women, and ascetics praised the beloved of Śrī Jayā.
Salutations to the Supreme Self who descends through all incarnations,
who dwells in the assembly of the liberated, yet also resides among human beings.
Salutations to you, the compassionate one who bestows the attainment of the world of truth;
salutations to you, the god of ascetics who has come from the world of austerity.
Homage to you, the bestower of liberation; homage to you, the deliverer of the ancestors;
homage to you whose nature is infinite and who are endowed with infinite power. (79)
Salutations to the Inner Self, whose essential nature is beloved by Brahmā;
salutations to you, Bālakṛṣṇa, who is served by the beloved of Hari.
The world of austerity (tapoloka) is attainable through austerity; when that austerity is exhausted, one goes to destruction.
And ascetics who have lost their sovereign power perish in the ocean of worldly existence.
"Without Hari, there is truly no liberation; he has now come to you.
Lift me up from this world of asceticism and from the ocean of worldly existence. (82)
We here are indeed partakers of the merit of former kalpas;
for by [your] grace we dwell here, even though we are always possessed of wealth. (83)
Nevertheless, your presence and the worship of your feet are never obtained by us; indeed, they could not be attained without your grace. (84)
For all those dwelling in the worlds of heaven, the truth, and the end, there certainly exist great merits that are indeed nothing but bonds. (85)
No other enjoyment arises from the fruit of merit except for this, O Hari: that you grant me the sight of yourself here out of compassion. (86)
Indeed, a birth upon the earth is better where Kṛṣṇa is truly found;
for there is no day anywhere on this earth that is without Kṛṣṇa being manifest. (87)
Out of respect, he will come once more to other worlds;
for the sake of accomplishing a multitude of great tasks, you shall not be seen at all.
It is better to be born as a spirit, a piśāca, or other such beings than among gods, sages, or ancestors;
for the latter may encounter liberation through yoga from Śrī Hari anywhere at all, whereas the former do not. 89.
Therefore, today the Blessed One, the inexhaustible treasure-house of compassion, has arrived;
grant us liberation in every way, for this is the boon we seek.
Listen, O Goddess beloved of Badarī, having heard their request for that purpose—the ancient multitudes of ancestors who subsist on the expectation of śrāddha offerings. (91)
O Badrikā, Śrī Hari quickly desired liberation for those most ancient of the ancient beings, and He caused them to drink the nectar of immortality.
Out of compassion, he kindly fed them the nectar of his feet and other gifts; feeling at ease, he placed his feet upon their chests, which remove all bondage.
They bestow divinity, are beautiful, are served by Rādhā, Lakṣmī, and others, possess upward-pointing lines, have red soles, and are exceedingly soft. (94)
The auspicious right foot is joined with an eight-pointed svastika, a vajra, a jambu fruit, a goad, a banner, a lotus, a fine wheel, and so forth. 95.
It is joined with two triangular pitchers, with the feet of a cow and a makara as ornaments, and with archers, fish, half-moons, and temple-circles. 96.
Even upon merely beholding his left foot, they attained supreme satisfaction;
Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa then placed both hands upon their heads.
It has tender soles with reddened palms, adorned with nails like moonbeams, and is graced by the signs of the fish, banner, bow, svastika, arrow, and trident. || 98 ||
Beholding Hari’s right hand, adorned with the four discs, the great mace, the conch, the sword, and other weapons, they indeed attained supreme bliss. (99)
The left side was exceedingly beautiful and charming, adorned with a parasol, a cow, and creepers;
it was joined by a wheel and graced by four wheels and a lotus.
Then, seeing the tip of his middle finger marked by Śaṅkha,
they were endowed with divine vision, and they beheld Lakṣmī upon his left thigh.
But beholding Rādhā at the hips, they attained great bliss, quickly casting aside their wooden puppets of fathers by the grace of Kṛṣṇa. (102)
At that time, many ancestors attained divine bodies;
the Pitṛs, Mātṛs, and the Gaṇas became liberated, indeed liberated. || 10.3 ||
And celestial chariots, impelled by liberation from their abode, arrived;
having stood and sat within them, they went to the imperishable abode of Hari.
Thus, O Badrikā, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, having granted liberation,
having graced them, and having spoken to those residing there, departed.
And the Lord Aryaman himself, having performed the worship, set out in his celestial chariot accompanied by his entire retinue and arrived at the people.

Thus ends the ninety-fourth chapter, titled "The Description of how Śrī Hari, having received worship performed by Aryaman and others in the abodes of the Pitṛs and other hosts of gods residing in Tapoloka, brought about the liberation of the Pitṛs, and returned to Janaloka," in the Tiṣya lineage of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nara-Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Goddess beloved of Badarī; in the month of Pauṣa, the Blessed Lord then proceeded to Janaloka, which is inhabited by the Sādhyas.
There, the gods known as Sādhyas, those called Jayas, the Pitṛs,
and the supreme deities who partake in the sacrifice, offered a welcome to Śrī Hari.
Those gods born from the mouth of Brahmā, desiring progeny,
all of whom have mantras as their bodies, offered a welcome to Hari.
The one called Darśa, the one called Pūrṇamāsa, the Bṛhat-sāman, the Rathantara, as well as Citi and Viciti, Ākūti and Kūti. || 4 ||
Vijñāta, Manas, and Yajña—these are the deities known as the Jayās;
they reside in the palace of Yajñanārāyaṇa, which is resplendent with the glory of the king of kings.
Yajñadeva established a residence for Hari there;
he worshipped him with supreme devotion and likewise performed the lustration ceremony (ārātrika).
He fed him ambrosia and served it with devotion;
then the gods named Tuṣitas led him to their own abode.
They worshipped with supreme affection and performed the lustration ceremony (*nīrājana*) for Hari;
thereafter, the monkey-gods led the Lord Nārāyaṇa away.
The gods named Vaikuṇṭhas, who dwell in Janaloka, honored Acyuta with great abundance and fed him.
They led Kṛṣṇa to their own palace and worshiped him with supreme reverence; Haṃsa, Prāṇa, and Prabhava performed the waving of lights (ārātrika) for Śrī Hari.
All eight Vasus also led Kṛṣṇa toward their own abode:
Dhara, Dhruva, Soma, Āpa, Anila, and Anala. (1)
Pratyūṣa and Prabhāsa worshipped Śrī Puruṣottama and presented many precious gems to the Supreme Soul.
Then the Viśvedevas led forth Kratu, Dakṣa, Śrava, Stava, Kāma, Satya, Dhuni, Kāla, Kuru, Prabhu, and Rocana. || 13 ||
They worshipped the supreme Lord, the beloved of Śrī and son of Kambharā; they performed the lustration ceremony with lamps and fed the Infallible One.
Viṣṇu is indeed named Mānasa, as well as Ajita and Hari; Satya, Viṣṇu, Vaikuṇṭha, Sādhya, and Trivikrama are also Viṣṇu. || 15 ||
All these Viṣṇus have made their abode in Janaloka;
having summoned the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa to the temple, [they remain there].
They honored Viṣṇu, the controller, the Supreme Brahman, the most excellent of persons;
they indeed performed the consecration ceremony for the son of Śrīgopāla.
Then they performed the Śṛṅgāra rite, the beautiful worship, and the Ārātrika ceremony;
thereafter, they indeed offered meals and betel leaves.
All the Vaiṣṇava people likewise worshipped the Supreme Lord,
and all the Vaiṣṇava Indirās, who are dear to Śrī Ramā, performed worship.
The women Lakṣmī, Rādhā, Brahmapriyā, and Haripriyā,
along with offerings presented by Indirā, were placed in the presence of Lakṣmī and the others.
Having been fed, honored, and served, all the Mothers,
as well as Indirā and the others belonging to Viṣṇu, bestowed ornaments upon him.
A divine golden crown, filled with more than its full measure of gems and other jewels;
two beautiful, divine earrings; and two golden ear-ornaments.
They gave necklaces adorned with the Kaustubha gem and set with various jewels, as well as golden armlets inlaid with diamonds and other precious stones.
Bracelets and anklets adorned with gold, pearls, and other jewels, as well as golden bangles and rings for the fingers.
They indeed gave lotuses, girdles, and beautiful necklaces;
a staff, a golden scepter, and a garment made of divine threads.
O Badrī, those beloved of Hari presented to Viṣṇu, who is Hari, golden sandals and divine anklets as ornaments for his feet. (26)
Indirā and the other goddesses presented great gifts to those beloved by Hari:
garments for the breasts, locks of hair, as well as shawls and bodices.
Well-prepared, they also gave him water-pipes, inner cloths,
hair-ornaments, moon-shaped decorations, flat combs, and beautiful flower-clusters.
He gave them golden braided ornaments, gold-made hair-crests,
and radiant crest-jewels adorned with pearls from the Nanda-ocean.
There were also divine necklaces, as well as those reaching down to the lotus-like cheeks;
there were moonlight-like ornaments for the chin and auspicious chain-earrings.
There were also beautiful golden *śrāvaṇī* and *ālambārī* flowers, as well as auspicious golden *puṣpaka* and *sthalaka* blossoms. (3.1)
The women Tārakā, Vardhikā, and Candrikā gave [the Lord] patrikās, pañcasarikās, and golden grains of fine sesame. (32)
They gave garlands of mung beans, garlands of auspiciousness, and garlands of jujube fruits; they gave garlands of barley, gold coins, and beautiful golden necklaces. ||33||
Those female attendants of Viṣṇu, dark as blue lotuses, gave garlands of leaves, chains, and strings of gems and pearls, as well as garlands of lotuses.
Then they gave her auspicious crystal necklaces and the Sūryamukhī [ornament], as well as two breast-plates made of gold and set with jewels and gems. (35)
The women gave golden bracelets adorned with jewels, as well as garlands of *pāṭalī* flowers and strings of pearls. || 36 ||
They gave golden neck-rings, garlands of sesame seeds, and *mādalī* flowers; they offered *plakṣa* leaves, great necklaces, girdles, and waist-bands.
They gave clusters of gold, golden balls, and golden rings;
they gave thigh-bands, knee-bands, and bracelets for the forearms. ||38||
The women gave them jhāṃjharī cymbals, kāmbikā lutes, and auspicious kadalikā fans; they also gave ornaments for the feet, ornaments for the toes, and ornaments for the big toes.
They gave lac-dyes, collyriums, and saffron for adornment; various pigments, liquid essences, and indeed the finest oils.
They presented the finest essences of flavors, the finest essences of fragrances, and the finest sweet delicacies,
as well as radiant garments made of gold and silver thread.
The goddesses Cindiras gave them vessels made of jasmine flowers, adorned with divine pearls, as well as other divine implements. 42.
They gave all kinds of superior medicines and household utensils; they bestowed radiant couches upon those who were like Lakṣmī herself. ||43||
The women presented various garments, hair-ornaments, mirrors, and fragrant powders for the worship. (44)
The women gave beautiful foot-ornaments that were soft and gentle, as well as lovely paintings and crowns. ||45||
Thus, the Viṣṇus and Indirās residing in Janaloka gave auspicious gifts to Hari and the wives of Hari. 46.
In Janaloka, O Badrikā, they served [the Lord] exceedingly;
in the month of Pauṣa, the Blessed One, Puruṣottama, [resided] in Janaloka.
He exchanged greetings with the people through acts of affection, hospitality, and service;
he gazed all around at the mountains, gardens, and rivers. 48.
The Blessed Lord Hari himself showed all his own goddesses to the inhabitants of Janaloka and bestowed the mantra upon them. 49.
Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Master; Svāhā!
We know Bāla Kṛṣṇa; we meditate upon Anādi Kṛṣṇa. (4.95.50)
Then the Lord of Śrī spoke this mantra to them: "Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Nārāyaṇa; may He impel us toward spiritual light. (51)
"O Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa Svāmin, O Ramāyaṇa!"—having thus purified them, Hari then gave this benediction to them. (52)
He swiftly sent his own imperishable abode to many;
the gods, headed by Yajña and Deva, offered their leave-taking to Hari. (53)
In the month of Māgha, Hari went from Janaloka to Maharloka,
where the twice-born who hold office for a kalpa reside.
Those eleven Rudras who are the sons of Brahmā born from his forehead,
arisen in a previous kalpa, who endure until the end of the kalpa, and have attained the supreme state— [55]
Requested by Rudra, the Blessed One arrived in their kingdoms;
Janārdana came to the great city of Nīlalohita Rudra. ||56||
Indeed, Nīlalohita Rudra, accompanied by ten million Rudrikās, performed worship;
he offered the ritual waving of lamps (ārātrika) and fed Keśava.
He caused him to dwell in his own palace and served him along with his beloved wife;
for the sake of worship, he gave many divine gifts to Kṛṣṇa.
Then other excellent Rudras, possessing the splendor of jewels and gems such as crowns, garments, and ornaments, led Hari, who is Nārāyaṇa.
In their own dwellings, they worshipped Acyuta according to the prescribed rites,
[offering] a thousand white bulls that possessed great luster.
When yoked to a golden chariot were those possessing humps, well-formed, with bodies like mountain peaks, moving through the sky, and fit for the foremost of draught-animals. (61)
It was enriched with one thousand and one jars, endowed with one thousand and one banners, graced by a hundred craftsmen, circular, and resembling a lotus. || 62 ||
The Rudras seated Hari Kṛṣṇa upon a golden tiger-throne and paraded the Lord everywhere through their own city, Raudrī.
In every house, on the streets, at every crossroads,
as well as in gardens and dwellings, the Rudras led the Lord Hari.
The Rudras worshipped there at every spot with supreme affection,
and the Rudrāṇīs, possessing a white luster, worshipped the Lord of Pārvatī.
With sandalwood, unbroken rice, and fragrances; with fruits, flowers, and sacred ashes; with ornaments, garments, and coins; and with divine mental offerings.
Twenty-eight crores of gods from the previous kalpa, having led him to their respective abodes one after another, worshipped the multiformed Lord.
Those gods, together with tens of thousands of deities, fed the Lord of Lords with desired foods that were even more divine than nectar, and they served him.
And those gods known as Ānandas, as well as the Bhāvadevas, the Rāmbadevas, the Ārtavas, the Āśvaras, and the Pāvakasuras; ||69||
The Havyavāhas, Sāvitrās, Auśikas, and Kauśikas likewise led Nārāyaṇa to their respective abodes and worshipped him there.
They fed the Lord of Lords and served him with great respect;
then the Gandharva gods, the Ṣaḍja beings, and the Ṛṣabha deities [did likewise].
Likewise, the Mārjālīya gods led the infallible Hari in a divine vehicle through the middle regions and established him within their own cities.
And they honored them with various unsurpassed offerings, and they fed them in many ways with divine foods and celestial delicacies. ||73||
Then there were others, the Vairājakas, the Naiṣādas, the Meghavāhanas,
the Prāṇadevas, the Cintakas, the Ākūtikas, and the Mānasasuras.
They led Nārāyaṇa to their respective palaces and honored him;
likewise, the Rāthantara gods and the Sadyojāta Haras did the same.
The Vīras, the Vāmadevas, the gods such as the Pītavāsas, the Sitakalpas, the Aghoras, and those gods who are the Viśvarūpas—[all these were present]. ||76||
Filled with devotion, they led the Supreme Soul to their respective abodes; each led Hari through his own city and home.
They honored them with divine jewels and gems and with every kind of service;
they fed them with food of nectar and satisfied them with waters of immortality.
The Rudras, having approached Nārāyaṇa, performed tāṇḍava dances;
indeed, the blue-and-red Rudra performed a beautiful tāṇḍava dance.
Śrī Badarīpriya said: "O Nārāyaṇa, Supreme Lord, tell me truly what kind of *tāṇḍava* dance he performed and what form Hara had at that time."
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said: Having worshipped Hari, Rudra became immersed in the bliss of the Self;
with a delighted soul, he prostrated before his master, Kṛṣṇa-Narāyaṇa. 8.1.
I am blessed today by the arrival of Hari; I am fulfilled in every way, since the Supreme Lord, the ocean of mercy, has come to my home. (82)
Having spoken thus, filled with joy and smiling, he performed the tāṇḍava dance;
meanwhile, those named Śṛṅgin, Bhṛṅgirīṭi, and Kirīṭin remained standing there. (83)
Ambā, Kārtika, and Vighneśa became dancers and yogis;
here Rudra assumed a form consisting of both half-woman and half-man.
With a face of gentle smiles, white with ashes, and adorned with appropriate ornaments, he stands with his right foot raised while resting upon the big toe of his left foot. 85.
With his face slightly upturned and his hands raised, he was bent at the knees;
his eyes were wide open with joy, and the celestial river flowed through his matted locks.
He has a neck enriched by a royal naga and is radiant with a black mark upon his throat;
the surface of the earth is illuminated by the streaks of fire arising from the eye in his forehead.
Clad in half a lion’s skin with his body covered by half a fine cloth, he resounded the assembly hall with the sound of the syllable "Hūṃ," endowed with a beautiful voice. ||88||
Wearing serpent-earrings on his forearms and also upon his arms,
he was further adorned with tinkling ornaments on his ankles and feet.
His rounded waist was encircled by a girdle studded with large bells,
and his chest was exceedingly beautiful, adorned with a radiant garland of severed skulls.
Adorned with dangling golden earrings at the edges of his ears, the young cobras appeared to be whirling around his ears. 9.1.
He was beautifully adorned with two moon-like tilakas on his forehead, captivating the mind;
he bore smooth, dark lines of collyrium at the corners of his eyes. ||92||
With his mass of matted hair bound by serpents and the forms of serpents upon his shoulders,
he slightly bends forward at the tips with his waist, which is white and blue.
Wearing half a loincloth, with his private parts covered by half-tied inner cloth, with half of his head adorned with earrings, and likewise possessing matted locks on the other half; ||94||
On the left side he is endowed with female ornaments, and on the right he is possessed of male ornaments;
his upper garment is tucked into the edge of the cloth covering Satī’s breasts.
In the month of Kārttika, the king of serpents, Mayūra,
hissing "phuṃ," licked the nectar produced by the dance upon his chest, which was of the nature of perspiration.
There, Gaṇeśa’s brindled mouse, though appearing like a rope around his neck, shines as it dances about, skilled in its performance. 97.
Then even the lord of beasts, the lion, who is the seat of Śiva,
lets out a roar that is accompanied by a dance assembly, increases vitality, and resounds through the quarters of the sky.
Wherever the white bull makes its sound, Hara accompanies them by providing the rhythm while playing the hand-drum (ḍamaru). 99.
With his hair standing on end and his limbs thrilled, he made the earth tremble;
shifting his feet, he balanced himself by weighing them upon the big toe of one foot.
Whirling his body, the dancer danced; he shone as he spun, first with a skillful clockwise turn, and then again with a counter-clockwise one.
With his back, his chest, his flanks,
and even with his foot and both feet, Hari struck Kṛṣṇekṣaṇa.
Fickle and devoid of shame, he danced with the trembling of his entire body;
at times he showed his breast, at times his penis, and at times merely the tip of his hand.
In some places Hara shone while shaking only his hips;
in some places his arms, in some his thighs, and in some his cheek and neck.
Shaking his eyebrows in one place and his shanks in another, Hara shone; at times casting a sidelong glance, at times a downward gaze, and at times a straight look.
In some places Śaṅkara danced, moving upwards and all around;
in some places he displayed modesty, in some places a pace that was three-quarters [of normal], and in others a pace that was double.
In some places he danced, displaying slow or steady movements;
in other places, bowing down, he displayed through his love both inner emotion and affection.
As if drawing Kṛṣṇa toward him, he danced before his Lord and Master,
whose half-body was in the form of a beautiful woman with a serene face and a golden luster.
Displaying the state of a servant, Śaṅkara danced with joy;
she was large-eyed, beautiful, and her eyes resembled lotus petals.
With the soles of her hands and feet slightly reddened, possessing a sweet voice,
she was beautiful in every limb, adorned by breasts white as ashes.
Embracing her beloved half, she shone with cosmetics applied to all her limbs;
she was the moon-crested goddess, whose peerless beauty had brought about the delusion of even the most handsome men.
Then the goddess Śivā, who is identical with Śiva, danced within her own limbs;
she then danced for the sake of pleasing the Supreme Lord.
Casting aside all shame in the presence of Kṛṣṇa, she was filled with every emotion, endowed with gestures and expressions, and possessed of the aesthetic flavor of all the limbs of dance. || 11.3 ||
Then, wearing a garland of tulasī on her neck like Śambhu, she cried out, "Nārāyaṇa!
Hara! Viṣṇu! Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa! || 14 ||
Addressing them as "Bālakṛṣṇa," she danced;
by the command of Rudra, she who had been standing apart became accompanied by musical instruments.
Then, filled with emotion, they danced in the presence of Nārāyaṇa; the Rudras, other hosts of Rudras, and even the celestial courtesans danced as well.
Placing their hands upon Kṛṣṇa’s hands, they also took hold of him with kisses;
accompanied by the sounds of musical instruments, songs, and the playing of cymbals and drums.
In every way, that mandala of the Rudra deities danced;
then those who were in the form of mounts also danced with great excitement.
Indeed, in Maharloka, where there is no longer any sense of separation, the supreme wonder was wrought by Hara, who has assumed the very forms of Dhṛta and Rudra.
The dancing was observed by Śrī Hari, who is joined with his purposeful power;
the gracious Lord, the Master, rose from his own seat.
Embracing Śaṅkara and holding him to his own chest,
becoming one with him, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, impelled by compassion, embraced them all.
They embraced Rudrāṇī, as well as Lakṣmī, Padmāvatī, and Priyā; others, devoted to bestowing blessings, embraced the various Rudrāṇīs.
They presented gifts of necklaces, divine jewels, and ornaments.
At the conclusion of the dance, Śrī Hari said, "I am pleased; I shall grant you a boon."
"Choose a boon here, all of you; whatever you desire, I shall grant it.
The Rudras said, "We choose service to you and imperishable devotion toward you."
"Grant us also the state of Brahman in your imperishable abode.
Having spoken thus, they performed the *ārātrika* ceremony and then offered the final gift (*vidāya*).
To them Kṛṣṇa gave his own mantra and also gave his own name:
"Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa Svāmī Śrī Hari is my refuge. (1.26)
The Supreme Lord then bestowed upon him divine status and auspicious speech;
then, ascending a celestial chariot amidst sounds of victory, he departed for heaven.
O Badrikā, a celestial chariot of Kṛṣṇa, radiant as the Imperishable (Akṣara), shone forth in heaven;
seeing it, the gods approached for the sake of welcoming the Siddha.

Thus ends the ninety-fifth chapter, titled "The Description of the Worship of the Blessed Lord and the Tāṇḍava Dance of Rudra in the Mansions of the Inhabitants of Maharloka," in the fourth section, the Tiṣya-santāna, of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Goddess beloved of Badarī; in the month of Phālguna, the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa first proceeded to the eternal heaven (dhruvasvarga) by means of his own celestial chariot.
Indeed, wherever King Dhruva, the devotee of Viṣṇu, eternally resides, there the wheel of the world finds its support and revolves.
Beholding the vast, divine, auspicious celestial chariot of Lord Hari, which transcends all worlds, Dhruva quickly approached it with great haste.
Accompanied by his army, all the gods, and his attendants, he honored Hari Kṛṣṇa and joyfully offered him a welcome.
Having prostrated himself like a staff, he said, "You are one of blessed fortune," and led Nārāyaṇa to his own great golden palace.
Where Viṣṇu, the bestower of all prosperity, dwells as one worthy of worship by Dhruva,
Viṣṇu then bowed down to Nārāyaṇa and prostrated himself like a staff.
Dhruva performed the massaging of the feet of Hari, who was resplendent upon a beautiful throne, and he also rendered service by offering water as nectar.
The best of devotees, having fully worshipped with the offering of a dwelling, the surrender of all possessions, and the sixteen primary services and others, performed the *ārātrika* ceremony.
The worship of the goddess Kamalā, who is Vaiṣṇavī, and of Lakṣmī and others;
and the worship of Dhruva’s eternal wife and of Brahmapriyā and others. (9)
Other great female devotees also performed the worship of Hari, and likewise the subjects of Dhruva worshipped Acyuta.
And they also offered various kinds of gifts to the glorious Supreme Soul,
including ornaments rich with divine gold and jewels, necklaces, and wealth.
They fed the Lord of Lords together with all the attendants;
the gods and goddesses performed service according to the rite of total surrender.
They performed the coronation of Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa, who bears all incarnations, and caused Acyuta to circumambulate the great kingdom of Dhruva’s sovereignty.
And the subjects, having worshipped Śrī Hari perfectly, obtained their desires; they took up the chanting of His names and meditated upon Nārāyaṇa in their hearts.
Having caused the world of Dhruva to be flooded from here and there, Kṛṣṇa quickly ascended his celestial chariot and went to the world of the Seven Sages.
First, Śrī Hari went to the excellent abode of Vasiṣṭha;
and the sage, accompanied by Arundhatī, offered a welcome to Hari.
With flowers, sandalwood paste, nectar, ambrosia, unbroken rice, and sprouts of barley,
she worshipped the Supreme Soul; indeed, Arundhatī also performed worship,
and the virtuous Arundhatī worshipped the entire company of Kṛṣṇa as well.
And the Vāsiṣṭhas, the Surādevyas, and the subjects praised the Imperishable One. || 18 ||
They performed the worship of Hari with Vedic mantras and the methods of the sages;
they fed them with desired foods, including nectar and other offerings prepared in great variety.
And likewise, in every house, the sages performed the nightly lamp-offering; with great reverence, they also offered him honor and service.
They offered blessings to Nārāyaṇa with hymns of praise;
and Bhṛgu and the Bhārgavas also led the Lord of Nārāyaṇa away.
And they worshipped and fed the Lord in their own homes;
then Aṅgiras and the descendants of Aṅgiras led Nārāyaṇa away.
They too worshipped Harikṛṣṇa with many offerings and other articles;
and Marīci, the son of Marīci, also brought Nārāyaṇa to his home.
Then Atri and the Ātreyas joyfully led Nārāyaṇa there;
they worshipped him, fed him, and placed offerings before him.
Pulastya and the Paulastyas led Nārāyaṇa to their home;
Pulaha and the Paulahas also led Hari to their own abodes.
They worshipped the Lord of Śrī, the husband of Mādhavī, with supreme devotion;
they placed offerings before Him and fed the Lord.
Those eminent sages performed service to Hari with great opulences;
O Badrikā, Hari, having accepted it, departed very quickly indeed.
Having beheld the world of Kratu and having offered respectful worship,
the Lord gave his blessings to Kṛtave and proceeded to the world of Śani.
Having performed worship for Śani and having given him his own Vaiṣṇava mantra, he then quickly joined that son of the Sun with blessings.
Hari himself indeed went to the vast world of the Guru;
Bṛhaspati then performed the consecration of Hari with the chanters of the Sāmaveda.
He worshipped the Lord with divine offerings and abundant riches;
then, having received the mantra from Hari, he indeed fed him.
He gratified Mādhava with excellent gifts;
then, having bestowed a parting gift upon him, he sent Acyuta on his way.
Then Hari quickly went to the abode of Maṅgala;
thereafter, Maṅgala worshipped the Lord with jewels and other offerings.
The Blessed One swiftly arrived at the abode of Śukra by means of his celestial chariot;
Śakra, for his part, offered a warm welcome with various forms of worship and other honors.
Then Hari quickly went to the abode of Budha;
Budha, having honored him, joyfully fed Mādhava.
Then Hari gave his leave to the circle of stars;
indeed, he departed in his own celestial vehicle to the abodes of Rohiṇī and the other constellations.
All those daughters of Dakṣa indeed worshipped Nārāyaṇa according to their respective stations; they served him and fed the infallible Acyuta.
They also worshipped the wives of Hari, together with their satisfied attendants, with offerings suitable for women. ||38||
Then the illustrious Lord quickly went to the world of the Sun;
he was Āditya, golden-hued, accompanied by that man who is joined with gold. (39)
He worshipped the Supreme Soul with all kinds of substances produced from gold,
with ornaments, nectars, divine foods, garments, and other offerings.
Pūṣan, Aryaman, Vivasvat, Tvaṣṭṛ, Viṣṇu, and Bhaga; likewise Parjanya, Varuṇa, Dhātṛ, Śakra, Mitra, and Aṃśu as well. ||41||
They worshipped the Supreme Self with the most excellent prosperity, abundance, and other offerings; and they presented royal attire, fit for a king of kings, to Nārāyaṇa.
In all their respective kingdoms, they joyfully brought Nārāyaṇa [there],
and they gave him crowns, bracelets, necklaces, and earrings.
They likewise gave beautiful chains made of precious gems,
as well as inexhaustible vessels that bestow great nectar.
They gave the wives of the Sun— Chāyā, Saṃjñā, Aśvinī, Hiraṇyā, Prabhā, and the others— to Hari, Lakṣmī, and the other gods.
They fed the Lord of the lords and then presented him with a gift of leave-taking;
thereafter, the Blessed One quickly departed for the land of Cāndrabhūmikā.
In the world of the moon, King Soma offered a welcome to Hari;
he also performed worship and service, and provided foods consisting of nectar.
The Moon gave beautiful garments and nectarian juices; he gave to Kṛṣṇa lovely jewels and gems. 48.
His wives, full of respect, gave ornaments and other gifts to the women,
and then Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa also bestowed a parting gift upon them.
And with joy he gave his own *manu* to the subjects of each respective world;
then he also gave the Nāmadhunya and the Mānasottara mountains.
In the month of Caitra, he went to Mount Mahendra, the abode of Indra in the east;
there, in the city of Amarāvatī, the Lord of the Gods caused the Lord to wander.
In that divine city, endowed with every charm and honored by the gods,
he was worshipped by the deities, the goddesses, Śacī, and the Apsarases.
Having caused the hosts of gods to drink [the water], he approached the assembly hall of Indra;
Indra honored him with many services and abundant offerings. (53)
To him he gave divine jeweled necklaces as well as other gifts;
Mahendra bestowed upon the sovereign all the enjoyments of Indra.
He fed them all and served them with devotional offerings;
he protected the Lord Śrī Puruṣottama within his own palace. ||55||
Siddhas, Cāraṇas, and Gandharvas, along with their women, attended upon Hari.
Having received leave from Agni, the Blessed One [entered] the city of Tejasvatī.
O Badrikā, he went by his own celestial chariot to the great abode of Agni;
there the fires, having bowed to Śrī Hari, offered him a most excellent welcome. (57)
Having worshipped him, they paraded him through their own city from house to house; they honored him exceedingly and fed him with great respect.
Those fires gave necklaces of jewels, gems, and other ornaments to Kṛṣṇa;
Svāhā and the others honored all the women with golden decorations.
Having received his leave with excellent sandalwood perfumes and liquid offerings that rained down like nectar,
the Blessed One departed for the city of Saṃyamanī.
Where Vaivasvata’s progeny worshipped him with reverence;
the Yamas worshipped the Lord of Lords, and King Yama also worshipped him.
The followers of Yama and the servants of Yama also worshipped the Supreme Lord;
Hari, however, went in his own celestial chariot to behold those in the hells.
Through the grace of Kṛṣṇa’s wind, the denizens of hell attained liberation;
not even a single person remained there in the cauldron to be punished by the staff.
At that time, not a single sinner remained there in the abode of Yama;
by the power of Kṛṣṇa’s grace, they all attained liberation and went to heaven.
Honored by Yama and having quickly received his leave, Kṛṣṇa went to the city of Rakṣovatī, which was protected by a multitude of Rākṣasas.
Nirṛti arrived in his own celestial chariot and offered a welcome;
the hosts of Rākṣasas, the progeny of Nirṛti, also worshipped the Lord of the Gods.
Having given them the mantra and received the supreme inheritance, Kṛṣṇa returned by means of his own celestial chariot to the happy city of Vāruṇī.
Varuṇa honored that Blessed One with supreme supernatural powers and fed him in many ways with foods produced from nectar.
They served him in many ways, and then he bestowed the Vidāya blessing upon them;
thereafter, Hari quickly departed for the city of Vāyu by means of his celestial chariot.
And in the exceedingly beautiful Gandhavatī, protected by Prabhañjana,
that Prabhañjana performed worship of Hari, the Supreme, along with his companions.
He gave jewels to Kṛṣṇa and likewise bestowed a parting gift;
Hari then went to the northern city of Kubera situated in the north.
And having been honored there by Kubera, Mādhava went swiftly to the exceedingly beautiful city of Soma, Vibhāvarī.
Honored with many jewels, abundant wealth, ornaments, garments, and the like,
as well as all the treasuries, he departed for the city of Īśāna.
In the city of Svayaśovatī, Īśāna caused Hari to wander about;
together with his attendants, he honored the Lord and his attendants with divine flavors.
And Kṛṣṇa gave him leave to depart for the city of Kāntimatī, situated on a portion of Mount Meru, which is frequented by the Lord of Night and other deities. 75.
It was joined by many apsarases and all the hosts of gods;
it was entirely Vaiṣṇava, beautiful, and inhabited by stars.
There, Niśākara, filled with great devotion, worshipped Kṛṣṇa;
he fed him in many ways and caused him to be carried about throughout the city.
Kṛṣṇa also bestowed parting gifts upon all the inhabitants of Meru, both those who were together and those who were scattered, and then he departed from house to house. 78.
Summoned for the purpose of purification, Hari went to his own abodes, [those of] the two emperors Priyavrata and Uttānapāda, who were devoted to the Supreme Self. (79)
They welcomed him with great honor, performing acts of worship and the like; they fed him and gave him priceless, excellent jewels.
Dharmadeva, Ruci, Dakṣa, Kratu, and the great sages worshipped the Supreme Soul and His retinue with offerings and other gifts. ||81||
Khecarī, Vasucārī, Brahmeśa, Brahmajīvadhī, Suṣeṇa, Śāśvata, Pṛṣṭa, Supuṣṭa, and Mahābala. ||82||
Then those divine celestial bards led Nārāyaṇa to his home;
they honored him with supreme affection, offering jewels, necklaces, and other gifts.

The knower of mantras, the one who understands mantras, the wise one, the king of mantras, resplendent with accomplishment, the supreme lord of the perfected, and the perfected ones themselves led Hari to his home. (84)
They honored him exceedingly and fed him with nectar;
so too did the Yakṣa, the Lord of Yakṣas, Jṛmbhaka, and Maṇibhadra. (89)
Pūrṇa, Prabhadraka, Mālin, Śitikuṇḍalaka,
and Narendra— these yakṣas escorted Nārāyaṇa to his home.
They worshipped with supreme devotion and presented divine offerings;
there were the Kinnaras Viṇājña, Surasena, and Pramardana. (87)
The Kinnaras—possessing excellence, skilled in practice, and knowledgeable in song—led Nārāyaṇa to their own abodes and honored him with joy. 88.
Vidyādhara, Vibudha, Vidyārāśi, Vidāmbara, Prabuddha, Kṛtajña, Śrījña, Tattvadhara, and others. ||89||
The Vidyādharas led Śrī Hari to their own dwellings and worshipped him with songs,
dances, emotional expressions, and various kinds of musical instruments.
Vāmadeva, Mahājambha, Sugrīva, and Mardaka likewise propitiated the Lord of Śrī, who was accompanied by his auspicious attendants. (91)
Bāṣkalī, Piṅgala, and Kumbha—these were the tamasic devotees;
these Daityas led Nārāyaṇa and worshipped the Supreme Lord.
Garutmān, Khagati, Nāgamardana, and Viṣṇuvāhana—these golden-hued Garuḍas [serve] the Supreme Lord. 93.
They returned to their own homes and worshipped the Lord, the Consort of Śrī;
likewise did Urvaśī, Menakā, Rambhā, Rati, and Tilottamā. (94)
Sumukhī, Sustanī, Śāntā, Kāmukī, Śāradānanā, Alambuṣā, and the other hosts of Apsarases led Hari as their husband. (95)
In their own dwellings, they worshipped their beloved Lord with the weight of their desires;
having served him by embracing him, they attained sanctity from the Lord.
They performed singing and dancing, and they rendered service to the women; they fed them excessively and caused them to apply cosmetics.
They delighted their lord of the self and embraced their beloved firmly;
they were Surabhi, Sarvatobhadra, Suśīlā, and Śrīpradā. (98)
Then Nandinī and the cows, assuming divine forms and granting all desires, led Hari to Meru and to their own hermitages.
They worshipped the Lord of Kāmarūpa preceded by a great consecration ceremony,
and they fed him their desired, sweet nectar consisting of milk.
Then Aruṇā, Anapāyī, Vimanuṣyā, Varāmbarā,
Miśrakeśī, Asiparṇā, Ālaṃbuṣā, and likewise Śucikā— || 10.1 ||
Mārīcī, Ādrikā, Vidyutparṇā, Kṣemā, Lakṣmaṇā, Manobhavā, Asitā, Puṇḍarīkā, and likewise Ajagandhinī. || 102 ||
Subāhvī, Supriyā, Subhujā, Sudatī, Ramā,
Surasā, Sumukhī, Haṃsapādī, Sūtā, Abhayā, and Jayā.
Haṃsā, Kamalā, Bhāsī, Subhagā, Sarasvatī, Arūpā, Manuvaṃtī, Sukeśī, and likewise Parṇinī. || 104 ||
Sahajā, Puñjikasthalī, Ghṛtācī, Kṛtasthalī, Viśvācī, Pūrvacitti, Pramlocā, Śāradī, and Dayā. 1.05.
Māṇikī, Anumlocā, Mañjulā, Haṃsī, and Śāntidā gave their youth to Hari; he, who loves pleasure, took delight in them.
In their own abodes, they served with the disposition of offering their very selves;
likewise, being fully united, they performed service to the beloveds of Kṛṣṇa.
They danced before Śrī Hari and sang the praises of their beloved;
they accepted his blessings and placed offerings before the Lord.
Bhīmasena, Ugrasena, Suparṇa, Varuṇa, Sūryavarcas, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gomān, Bhīma, and Patravān. || 109 ||
Arkaparṇa, Prayuta, Citraratha, Vaikali,
Śāliśiras, Subāhu, Haṃsa, Madhya, and Dāruṇa.
Jyotiṣṭama, Sadācāra, Vareṇya, Varūthaka, Vasuruci, Suruci, Viśvāvasu, and Bhānuka. || 111 ||
Bahvi, Siddha, Pūrṇa, Pūrṇāṃśa, Śatagauṇaka, and Sucandra—these Gāndharvas worshipped the Supreme Lord. || 112 ||
They led Nārāyaṇa to their own palaces and worshipped the Infallible One;
they all presented offerings and fed the Infallible One.
The divine forest of Meru,
as well as the forest deities and the divine medicinal herbs, all embodied, [worshipped] the Supreme Lord.
They worshipped him with fruits, flowers, and other offerings, as well as nectar-like foods of excellent flavors; to those residents of Mount Meru, Mādhava gave his own mantra.
He bestowed his own name upon him and likewise gave his blessings;
thereafter, he departed for the Bhuvarloka by means of his own celestial chariot.
O Badrikā, in the month of Vaiśākha, the Blessed One, who is affectionate toward his devotees,
was worshipped there by the gods who move through the sky as they honored the Imperishable One.
Āvaha, Pravaha, Savaha, Anuvaha,
Parāvaha, Vivaha, and Parivaha are the winds.
They brought the Supreme Lord to their own beautiful cities; with supreme affection, they worshipped Acyuta and fed him.
Bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, kūṣmāṇḍas, and vināyakas,
as well as vīras and vetālakas— all these dwellers of the bhuvarloka.
They worshipped the Supreme Soul and received the mantra of Hari;
they became divine-liberated beings, and Hari returned to the surface of the earth.
In the month of Jyeṣṭha, Hari, who is worshipped by all devotees, withdrew from his own abode at the sacred site of Kuṅkumavāpikā to Badarī.

Thus ends the ninety-sixth chapter, titled "The Description of the Lord’s Wandering in the Heavenly World on Mount Meru and in the Bhuvarloka, and His Return to Kuṅkumavāpikā," in the fourth section, the Tiṣya-santāna, of the glorious Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā.
Śrī Nara-Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Goddess beloved of Badarī; hear how the Blessed Lord, the creator of all beings, swiftly arrived at the sacred field of Kuṅkumavāpikā.
Whatever forms of his wives were present in the celestial chariot,
the Imperishable One caused them all to vanish right there.
Then the forms residing in celestial chariots entered into those on earth; likewise, forms in the likeness of male and female servants entered into those on earth.
Then the forms of Lomaśa and the others entered into those dwelling on the earth;
and when the state of duality had dissolved, Hari himself remained in his own essential form.
There, the celestial chariot became of a single form and attained a minute size;
the offerings consisted of ornaments, garments, and necklaces made of jewels, as well as beautiful golden items.
Kṛṣṇa gave everything to those who were worthy, each according to their need; and the ladies gave to the brahmins, the helpless, and the wretched, each according to their merit.
Hari also observed the four-month fast in Kuṅkumapattana;
then the twenty-third day of Hari’s birth, which bestows auspiciousness, arrived.
On the eighth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Kārttika, having bathed early in the morning and adorned himself with ornaments,
Kṛṣṇa came to his own assembly as the beloved one.
Then musical instruments were played and auspicious songs were sung;
at that time, the dances of the deities became manifold and wondrous.
O Badrī, that most excellent assembly hall became filled with the inhabitants of all the worlds,
and there Lomaśa arrived.
He worshipped the Supreme Soul and said to Him, "May you live long.
Śrī Gopāla, Kṛṣṇa, and the others worshipped the Supreme Lord.
Incarnations, lords, liberated ones, perfected beings, and likewise gods;
sages, ancestors, deities, humans, men, and women. (12)
They worshipped Kambharālāl, and then they offered blessings;
they all performed the *ārārtrika* ceremony and celebrated a great festival.
Prajñā, Padmāvatī, Lakṣmī, Rādhā, and others, as well as the Daityas, Dānavas, and Rākṣasas dwelling in the subterranean realms such as Atala, celebrated the festival.
The Nāgas, Sarpas, and Bhogins entreated Hari, saying:
"O Blessed One, purify us and our own abodes, such as Pātāla, by your very sight."
"So be it," Hari replied; then Hari fed all those great souls and bestowed gifts upon them as well.
They all departed for their own worlds; Kṛṣṇa, accompanied by those dwelling in Pātāla and joined by all his former followers, desired to go as well.
He was accompanied by all his wives, male and female servants, and others, as well as by Lomaśa; he was joined by virtuous sages such as Svataḥprakāśa and the rest. || 18 ||
Accompanied by his attendants such as Hemanta and others, Kṛṣṇa became twofold in every aspect; he appeared in two forms, adorned with two distinct costumes and ornaments.
When the celestial chariot was small, he made it large there;
having established everyone there in that field of saffron, he arranged them all.
Having taken all of them together onto a celestial chariot on the eleventh day, Hari, the joy of the cowherds, ascended it along with his entire retinue.
Accompanied by Suparṇa, Vāsuki, Śaṅkukarṇa, and Namuci,
he quickly caused the celestial chariot to move forward, listening to the sounds of joy and victory.
But in the excellent palace of Suparṇa at the bottom, they worshipped the Great Lord Hari, who is Suparṇa and others, there with supreme devotion.
Having paraded them throughout the entire great kingdom, they presented them as offerings:
many precious jewels and excellent foods. (24)
The yakṣas, daityas, and dānavas, excluding those who were not subject to Mucukunda,
worshipped Nārāyaṇa with supreme devotion and received the mantra of Hari.
Then, at the end of Mārgaśīrṣa, Hari gave them leave and quickly departed for the world of Vitala by means of a celestial chariot.
Then Jambhaka, Prahlāda, and Kambala likewise offered a warm welcome to Śrī Hari with great respect. (27)
The Daityas, being devoted and full of faith, worshipped the Supreme Lord;
Prahlāda protected the Lord until the end of the month.
He caused Kṛṣṇa to be paraded everywhere throughout his own home and kingdom; even the crores of Daityas led Kṛṣṇa to their own dwellings.

The wives of the Daityas, their hearts filled with dejection, worshipped Kṛṣṇa—who was accompanied by his consort and enriched by his entire retinue—with great reverence; while Lakṣmī and the others worshipped him with joy.
Then they gave many jewels and indeed excellent gems;
they also gave food and then granted them leave to depart.
In the month of Pauṣa, Kṛṣṇa went to the supreme world of Sutala;
there, the Lord Śrīpati dwelt in the house of Virocana.
The Daityas worshipped Kṛṣṇa with great affection by offering various articles and the like; they fed him exceedingly, and their people served him in numbers as vast as Mount Arbuda.
The host known as Hālāhala, numbering one hundred thousand, performed worship; and crores of Dānavas worshipped the illustrious Supreme Lord.
Led by Vipracitti, they presented offerings to Hari;
Śaṅkukarṇa and the others also escorted Nārāyaṇa to his home.
Hayagrīva and others also worshipped the Lord of Mādhavī;
likewise, the Śārabhas and the Śāmbaras worshipped the Lord of Rādhikā.
Ten thousand kings, beginning with Kālanābha and residing in Hiraṇyapura, worshipped the Beloved of Kamalā.
The Kālakeyas and Dānavas led Nārāyaṇa to their home;
the Dānava women honored him and fed the Lord.
Lord Hari gave them the mantra, "Śrī Hari is my refuge";
taking leave of him, he went to Talātala during the month of Māgha.
The Lord himself took up residence in the abode of Vainateya;
there, the sons of Vinatā reverently worshipped Hari along with his retinue.
Garutman led fourteen thousand kings to Hari’s own kingdom, where they honored him with ornaments of precious gems.
Kālanemi and the other lords of the Daityas also led the husband of Lalitā to their own regions and worshipped Sarasvatīśvara. ||42||
Likewise, even by the crores of gods and rākṣasas in their own realms, the illustrious King Kṛṣṇa was led forth and worshipped with the highest reverence. ||43||
They offered gifts to him, and Hari gave Manu to them;
he also bestowed the Nāmadhunī [river] as a gift, and then he received his leave.
In the month of Phālguna, Śrī Hari arrived at the great netherworld (mahātala) by means of his own celestial chariot,
and there he went to the palace of Mucukunda and others.
The Blessed One dwelt there and, perceiving his devotion, accepted his service;
so too did the great serpents beginning with Ananta, who were gods capable of assuming any form at will.
They worshipped the Supreme Lord and served him with devotion;
with joy, they offered excellent gifts consisting of jewels and gems. ||47||
They fed them most abundantly with many kinds of divine foods; they performed the ritual waving of lights (ārātrika) and then granted them leave to depart. ||48||
In the month of Caitra, Anādikṛṣṇanārāyaṇa went to Rasātala; honored by Bali, He made His residence in Bali’s house. ||49||
Praised by Vāmana, Kṛṣṇa wandered through all regions in every direction, desiring the liberation of his devotees from all the kingdoms of passion.
Like a king of kings, King Bali worshipped Hari Nārāyaṇa;
he honored him and fed him sweet food.
Then other preeminent Daityas, as well as Rākṣasas led by Tāraka and others such as the Hiraṇyākṣas, also gave him farewell gifts.
More than a hundred billion [beings] daily worshipped Hari, the Lord of Nārāyaṇa, in their own abodes with offerings of all their possessions.
They received that mantra and then granted him leave;
thereafter, in the month of Vaiśākha, Śrī Kṛṣṇasvāmī departed for the netherworld (pātāla).
The serpents of that region, belonging to all remaining species, protected Nārāyaṇa in their home with great respect and, being eager, worshipped him. ||55||
All other great serpents, assuming whatever forms they desired, as well as the Naga maidens and the great goddesses, served Hari and Lakṣmī. (16)
Ananta, Phullika, Vāsuki, Takṣaka, Karkoṭaka, Mahāpadma, Śaṅkhapāla, and others as well. ||57||
They led Nārāyaṇa back to their own kingdoms and, full of zeal, they worshipped him; they honored him with jewels, gems, and other offerings, and served him most exceedingly.
They fed the Lord of Lords and then presented him with a farewell gift;
Hari gave them the mantra, and thereafter he ascended his celestial chariot.
Stimulated by the sounds of musical instruments and highly honored,
Hari indeed dwells in the midst of the Ocean of Milk where Śeṣa serves as his throne.
In the month of Jyeṣṭha, the Lord Viṣṇu, the Master who possesses a mass of great energy and whose seat is Śeṣa, arrived there and worshipped Hari.
With joy, he fed him with milk-rice and the finest essences;
Lakṣmī, the auspicious one among all Lakṣmīs, performed service for him.
Viṣṇu indeed bestowed the precious jewels upon Nārāyaṇa;
having received his leave, the Blessed One departed for Śvetadvīpa.
In the month of Āṣāḍha, the beloved of Kamalā worshipped, honored, and fed with nectar the Hari known as Prajñānārāyaṇa. (64)
The lotuses, headed by Kamalā, served him in many ways;
thereafter, Kṛṣṇa took his leave and departed by means of a celestial chariot.
The Lord of Īśa gave his own supreme mantra to the Śveta-muktas,
and then he sent them to his own imperishable abode.
He arrived swiftly at Badrikāśrama in the month of Śrāvaṇa by means of a celestial chariot, saying:
"Nara and Nārāyaṇa are we; you are the Badris as well as the sages."
Accompanied by great reverence, we worshipped the Lord of All at the rivers beginning with Tanvā, at the Tāpasa [hermitage], and at the circle of sacred sites on Mount Himavat.
They all drank the water from his feet and presented auspicious, magnificent gifts;
Hari indeed stayed there for one month during the month of Bhādrapada.
He arrived at the auspicious city of Vārāṇasī by means of his own celestial chariot,
after having established the sacred ford and beheld King Dhenupāla.
Having bathed at Prayāgarāja and bowed to Bhāradvāja,
he quickly returned by his own power to his imperishable abode in the land of Saurāṣṭra.
Making all dualistic forms disappear, Acyuta then became of a single form and entered his own abode. 72.
In the sacred field of Kuṅkumavāpikā, she rested in her own abode;
thus, O beloved of Badrī, is the sanctity of all the netherworlds.
By Hari's own grace, people have been liberated;
now, the eighth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Kārttika is the anniversary of his birth. (74)
The twenty-fourth lunar day, rich in auspiciousness, has arrived;
having bathed in the morning and performed all his adornments, Kuṅkumeśvara [appeared]. (75)
He went to his own pavilion, which was beautifully adorned with an elephant-throne,
and sat down there, honored by the sages and having performed auspicious rites.
Lomaśa, intent on offering blessings, applied auspicious kunkuma tilaka marked with unbroken grains of rice upon Kṛṣṇa’s forehead and worshipped him.
The father, mother, brothers, great sages, lords of the gods,
as well as the liberated souls and the liberated women, all worshipped the Supreme Self.
The lords and incarnations, intent on bestowing blessings;
the ancestors, yakṣas, gandharvas, kiṃpuruṣas, and kinnaras. ||76||
The gods, dānavas, siddhas, virtuous women, sūtas, and cāraṇas;
the twice-born, kings, merchants, and servants—all worshipped the Imperishable One.
The goddesses, the lakes, the rivers, the sacred fords, the mothers of the gods, the guardians of the worlds, and the protectors of the quarters all worshipped the Supreme Lord. ||81||
The inhabitants of Atala and the other regions, as well as the human beings dwelling on earth—
both men and women— worshipped Hari-Kṛṣṇa during the festival.
They placed divine offerings made of gold before Hara, as well as forms consisting of jewels and gems; and they sang, "May you live long! (83)
They performed the nightly lamp-offering and then received his favor;
thereafter, Śrī Lomaśa granted them exemption from the assembly hall.
Lomaśa fed all those great men and,
having given many gifts, then granted them leave to depart.
The kings of the seven continents and others entreated Hari, who was accompanied by all [his retinue], to come from his own abode. ||86||
Saying "So be it" to them, the others then departed with joy to their own worlds and their own regions, situated within the seven continents.
Then, when the eleventh day had arrived, the illustrious Lord prepared his own male and female servants and women as he had done before.
Having indeed manifested those forms in two ways within his own celestial chariot,
Hari seated all of them, consisting of both women and men.
Amidst the sounds of musical instruments and shouts of victory in the sky from his own celestial chariot,
Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa ascended.
The sages, headed by Lomaśa, and the women, headed by Brahmapriyā,
ascended the celestial chariot to behold the seven continents.
The lords of Navadvīpa, mounted upon their respective celestial chariots,
then went before Śrī Hari to welcome him.
Filled with joy, they adorned their respective countries and cities, making the palaces beautiful and exquisitely decorated. 93.
They provided all the delightful requisites necessary for the service,
and they also had beautiful pavilions and assembly halls constructed.
Those kings caused radiant gate-towers to be built, adorned with lamps and archways; thus they increased the splendor of their subjects. 95.
And in Jambūdvīpa as well, those lords of the regions who formerly joyfully entreated Hari in order to sanctify their own respective regions; 96.
Hari said, "So be it," and by his command they all departed beforehand to their own regions for the sake of adornment.
A very great proclamation arose everywhere upon the earth:
"The beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of creation, is coming! (98)
That Blessed One is beautiful to behold, the destroyer of sin, the destroyer of suffering, the Lord;
he is Hari, the son of the cowherd, worthy of worship and salutation. 99.
Thus, O Badrikā, they await on the ground with eager longing:
"Today, or tomorrow, or the day after, Nārāyaṇa will arrive."
Then the Blessed Lord Bālakṛṣṇa, by way of circumambulation,
quickly caused the celestial chariot to ascend into the northwestern sky.

Thus ends the ninety-seventh chapter, titled "The Description of how the Blessed Lord, having purified the respective kings and subjects in the seven netherworlds beginning with Atala following the twenty-third birth festival in the *Tiṣya-santāna* of the fourth book of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*, and having purified the Ocean of Milk, Śvetadvīpa, and Badarikāśrama, arrived at Kuṅkumavāpī and celebrated the twenty-fourth festival of His own birth."
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said:
Then, O Goddess beloved of Badarī, the Blessed Lord, the Master of Lakṣmī,
quickly went by means of a celestial chariot to the palace of the Lord of Jambūdvīpa.
The Āgnīdhra priest filled [the vessel] and honored Mādhava;
with the splendors of a king of kings, he served the Lord of Mādhavī.
All the queens, including Mahālakṣmī, Rādhā, and others worthy of honor, performed worship with the presentation of great gifts and served them with supreme devotion.
Then the nine sons of Āgnīdhra led Nārāyaṇa away;
Nābhi led the Supreme Lord to the kingdom called Himāhvaya.
The king of the Kiṃpuruṣas worshipped him with supreme affection and likewise presented great gifts at his own city named Hemakūṭa.
In the great kingdom of Mahākhaṇḍa, King Hari devoutly led and worshipped Mādhava; in the region known as Naiṣadha, he likewise led him. || 6 ||
He worshipped him with heartfelt devotion and gave him excellent, precious gems;
King Ilāvṛta then took them to his own region, Ilāvṛta-khaṇḍa.
The charming king also worshipped the Lord of the Gopīs and presented him with jewels as offerings; having brought Hari to the region known as Nīlācala, he honored Him there.
King Hiraṇyānna worshipped, served, and respectfully fed Hari, and brought him to his own realm, Śvetavarṣa.
They worshipped him with supreme affection and likewise presented excellent gifts;
the King of the Kurus then led Hari toward his own Uttarakuru region.
Then King Bhadrāśva also brought him to the eastern region and worshipped Rāmarāmeśa with gold, wealth, and other offerings.
He worshipped Him with supreme devotion and presented most excellent and auspicious offerings;
then King Ketumāla led Hari to his own abode.
She worshipped him with supreme devotion and fed her virtuous husband;
then, taking his leave, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa departed quickly from there.
He indeed directed his own celestial chariot to travel to other continents.
Priyavrata had ten sons who were equal to the Prajāpatis.
Āgnīdhra, Agnibāhu, Vapuṣmat, and Dyutimat; as well as Medhā, Medhātithi, Havya, Savana, and Putraka. || 15 ||
Jyotiṣmān and Daśaka—all these were indeed auspicious Vaiṣṇavas;
Medhā, Agni, Bāhu, and Putra—these three became virtuous men.
There were seven other kings, and the Lord proceeded toward their islands;
Hari went to Medhātithi, the sovereign of Plakṣadvīpa.
In the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, Medhātithi worshipped Kṛṣṇa;
likewise, the sons of Medhātithi brought the Lord to their own kingdoms.
Śāntabhaya, Śiśira, Ānanda, Sukhodaya,
Śiva, Kṣemaka, and Dhruva— these are the seven mountain ranges.
Eagerly, they paid honor to the great king of kings; they presented various delightful gifts and worshipped him with respect.
They performed the nightly lamp-offering and drank the water from the feet of Hari;
they fed the Lord of Lords and partook of his grace.
They accepted Manu as the servant of Kṛṣṇa and served Acyuta;
thereafter, they also granted him leave after honoring him with offerings from their subjects.
Having swiftly traversed Śrīharidvīpa by means of his celestial chariot,
Kṛṣṇa then proceeded in the month of Pauṣa to the excellent Śālmalidvīpa.
That sovereign, the handsome King Samrāṭ, honored Kṛṣṇa;
filled with devotion, he constantly protected Hari within his own palace. ||24||
He constantly served the Lord with devotion and fed Him in many ways; he gave to Hari beautiful and priceless offerings such as necklaces of jewels and other ornaments. (25)
His seven sons were kings: Śveta, Harita, Jīmūta, Rohita, Vaidyuta, Mānasa, and Prabha. || 26 ||
These seven brought the Supreme Self into their own kingdoms;
having led him from palace to palace with great honor, they worshipped him repeatedly.
With fragrant substances such as sandalwood, with diamonds and other gems, with golden ornaments, with jewels and precious stones, with woolen blankets, and with vessels of gold; ||28||
The queen and the subjects also worshipped the Supreme Lord;
then Kṛṣṇa, having given Manu to them and received their leave, departed in haste.
In the month of Māgha, having ascended his celestial chariot, the emperor named Jyotiṣmat, accompanied by his army, arrived at Kuśadvīpa and paid his respects.
He caused Keśava to be paraded through his own palace and the city;
having worshipped him with flowers, unbroken grains of rice, and other offerings, he presented him with jewels and gems.
They gave food to the queen and served that infallible one;
his seven sons, who were kings, led Hari to their own [cities].
Palaces and dwellings everywhere throughout the kingdoms,
as well as Udbheda, Veṇumān, Dhṛti, Aśva, and Rathas, likewise.
Lambana, Kapila,
and Prabhākara worshipped that player of the flute with great devotion and served that infallible Lord.
They offered gifts and received the guru-mantra;
the subjects worshipped Kṛṣṇa, the husband of Sītā, with supreme devotion.
They received the mantras of Kṛṣṇa and then gave him leave to depart;
in the month of Phālguna, Hari went to Krauñcadvīpa by means of his own celestial chariot.
The sovereign king, resplendent and accompanied by his armies, paid him due honor and joyfully lodged Kṛṣṇa in his own excellent palace.
He fed the Lord of Gods and served Keśava;
he honored Kṛṣṇa, together with his entire caravan, with gold coins.
Then, with precious gems and the like, as well as saffron, unbroken rice, and sandalwood,
his seven sons led Nārāyaṇa from there.
Manohara, Kuśala, Uṣṇa, Pīvara, Muni,
Dundubhi, and Andhakāra— these kings honored the Imperishable One.
The subjects indeed performed service in many ways and worshipped the Lord;
they also gave him a farewell gift and received his mantra. ||41||
Then, in the month of Caitra, Hari went quickly to Śākadvīpa;
there, the emperor named Havya, together with his army, paid him homage.
He caused a residence for the Supreme Soul to be established in his own palace; he worshipped Him with supreme devotion and served Him with manifold feelings. (43)
He fed Govinda and gave him various gifts;
then his seven sons, who were kings, escorted Kṛṣṇa to their own abodes.
Then there were Jalada, Kumāra, Sukumāra, Maṇīcaka, Kuśottara, Modāki, and Mahādruma. (45)
They gave auspicious divine gifts to Ānanda, the beloved of Rukmiṇī; they served him with great abundance and bestowed excellent wealth upon him.
His subjects and others, having led Hari to their own dwellings, worshipped him;
and Hari, having bestowed the mantra upon them, departed quickly by means of a celestial chariot.
In the month of Vaiśākha, he went to the island of Puṣkara accompanied by a splendid caravan;
there was King Savana, the lord of Puṣkara, who was adorned by his army.
He paid him great honor and paraded him through the city;
then, having led him to his own palace, he worshipped him with various offerings.
He caused him to dwell there constantly and served him with devotion;
he fed him daily and gave him many gifts upon his departure.
His two sons, both kings, led the Supreme Lord with devotion to their respective kingdoms and caused him to dwell in their own palaces. ||51||
Mahīvīta and Dhātaki both served Hari;
his queens and the subjects as well worshipped the Lord Mādhava. ||52||
