and in every village, for every twice-born man, there is the Vaiśvadeva sacrifice.
At every gate, the form of Kṛṣṇa shines as the devourer of the fierce;
even in the ornaments of every woman, there is indeed the name "Kṛṣṇa."
The name of Hari is upon every weapon, even on all household implements;
indeed, in every shop, there exists an image of Nārāyaṇa.
In every village on the land of Maya, there is indeed an excellent temple of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa; and in every town as well, [there is one].
In the morning and evening, there arise the worship of Hari, the Lord of Lakṣmī, as well as the waving of lights and the sounding of bells and other instruments. (72)
Hymns proceed forth, as do songs and chants of praise;
offerings of food are presented, along with betel leaves and water. (73)
Temples are enjoyed and the nectar-water is drunk;
O Badrikā, every day in village after village, auspicious discourses are held in the evening. (74)
Thus, through the Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa-Saṃhitā, the land on earth indeed became Vaiṣṇava, becoming one with Mukunda. 75.
King Mukundavikrama was a perpetual ascetic;
rising every morning, he performed the meditation upon Kṛṣṇa day after day.
Having bathed, he performs the libation (tarpaṇa) for the hosts of ancestors, as well as the worship of the Sun and the twilight prayer (saṃdhyāvandana). ||77||
With his mind fixed upon the image, he performs the worship of Hari;
having first performed the invocation (āvāhana) upon a golden throne, thereafter—
Having offered water for the feet and the respectful oblation (arghya), he also gives water for sipping (ācamanīya);
he likewise provides wood for cleansing the teeth and water for purification.
He provides earth and powder for the sake of cleansing his hands, feet, and so forth;
he also prepares water in a vessel for rinsing the mouth and even applies collyrium. (4.112.80)
He offers fragrant oil-essence to the form of Kṛṣṇa, and indeed provides arka-essence, rasa-essence, and even massage. ||81||
He offers fragrant sandalwood and the five products of the cow—
milk, curd, ghee, honey, and sugar— as well as water from sacred fords.
Having caused the consecration to be performed, he also carries out the ritual sprinkling;
he also performs the gift of garments and the offering of ornaments. ||83||
She performs every kind of amorous adornment upon the dark-bodied one:
arranging his hair, applying oil, and placing flowers [upon him]. (84)
Collyrium for the eyes, a beautiful crescent-shaped mark on the forehead, musk, sandalwood paste, a flower garland, and a necklace of jewels. ||85||
He also offers necklaces, tulasī leaves, as well as a sacred thread,
unbroken grains of rice, saffron, and gulāla powder.
Pure incense and superior perfumes, flower clusters, dyeing with colors and the like, incense, lamps, food offerings, fruit, betel, and water. ||87||
Then he also gives a pillow for the head,
a cotton garment, and likewise a very beautiful bed provided with all necessary furnishings.
With devotion, she offers a swing, a fan that provides a breeze, an umbrella, beautiful chowries, a staff, a parasol, a crown, and other ornaments. (89)
He also gave Śrīvilāsin a vehicle, a mount, means for wandering, and household amusements, as well as a midday meal.
She also provides him with a massage of his feet, rest upon a beautiful bed, and even rising and wandering in the great garden in the evening. (9.1)
He also performs play during the twilight, as well as the waving of lamps;
he offers hymns of praise, worship, food, and the offering of milk-rice (pāyasa). ||92||
He also offers water for libation, mouth-fresheners, and a bed;
he even performs the massaging of Hari’s limbs, which brings him happiness. (93)
Circumambulation, prostration like a staff, various forms of service, as well as listening to the sacred narrative, chanting the praises of Kṛṣṇa, and the remembrance of Hari. (94)
He performs service and even the surrender of his self to please Kṛṣṇa;
thus Mukundavikrama carries out this entire collection of duties for the sake of the glorious Lord. (95)
O Badrī, he who is solely devoted to Nārāyaṇa always performs [this];
and his wife Satī, the dispassionate Muktibāleśvarī, does so as well. (96)
Like a devoted wife, she performs all activities for the sake of Kṛṣṇa; rich in service to her husband, her mind is entirely offered to Śrī Kṛṣṇa. (97)
Whatever is fit for the maintenance of the body, all that is for the sake of Kṛṣṇa alone;
whatever is suitable for the service of her husband, all that is for the sake of Kṛṣṇa alone. (98)
Thus, O Badrikā, by that Mukundavikrama, his own divine and non-divine conduct was indeed offered to Śrī Hari. (99)
Another Vaikuṇṭha was created by him on earth, and another Goloka was brought down to the ground; it was as if that supreme realm had been made manifest through his devotion to Hari.
In every house, ever-new wonders arise;
and Kṛṣṇa Hari himself, through devotion, appears before the vision of the devotee.
At that time, many knowers of Brahman—living beings, women, and men—proceeded to the supreme abode of Śrī Hari, the Supreme Soul. 102.
While King Mukundavikrama reigned there,
the Kṛtayuga prevailed as far as the ocean, resembling the age of the gods and humans.

Thus ends the one hundred and twelfth chapter, titled "The Description of King Mukundavikrama’s Devotion to the Blessed Lord," in the fourth section, the Tiṣya lineage, of the glorious *Lakṣmīnārāyaṇīyasaṃhitā*.
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said:
Then the Blessed Lord, the Master Badrikṛṣṇanārāyaṇa,
who bestows all happiness, was residing at that time in Kuṅkumavāpī.
For the sake of having Vāsudeva as an ally, and for the prosperity of the kingdom, he dispatched his own sons and others who were experts in the arts and sciences.
Śrī’s son was Rāsakṛṣṇa, who became the deputy commander-in-chief;
and Brahmaprabhu, the son of Prajñā, protected the office of the general.
Ananta, the son of Padmāvatī, became the superintendent of the prison;
Lāleśvara, the son of Lalitā, became the ruler of the kingdom.
At that time, Vijaya was the son of Jayā and became her counselor;
likewise, the Kaustubha gem, the bestower of justice, became the son of Māṇikyā. || 5 ||
Padmanābha was always the presiding officer of Kamalā’s assembly;
as the son of Ramā, he was a witness to Rāma and possessed authority over knowledge.
At that time, Rāyakeśī, the son of Rādhā, became the treasurer,
and Naradeva, the son of Nārāyaṇī, became the commander of the auxiliary forces.
The son of Brāhmī was Brahmarāta, who became the royal priest;
the son of Bhāgavatī was Bharga, who performed sacrificial rites.
Ūrjabala and others, as well as other Khaṇḍapālas, became his sons; indeed, those twelve hundred and fifty sons were each according to their respective [lineages].
At that time, they were engaged in the endeavors described by Hari;
thus, the kingdom then became a source of great joy on all sides.
O Badarī, your son there, known by the name Bādarāyaṇa, was a bestower of knowledge, a giver of gifts, and a provider of sacrificial fees and other offerings. || 11 ||
And the subjects, having attained knowledge, became like those who are bodiless (liberated);
possessing knowledge directly from the Lord, they [prepared] a horse and a bull for the sake of the journey.
They indeed come and go repeatedly to see Nārāyaṇa-Kṛṣṇa at the Aśvapaṭṭasara Tīrtha, the most excellent among the best of holy places.
From the dwelling of Hari, the supreme imperishable field (kṣetra) was born;
and great devotees of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa arrived there.
Some go to the imperishable abode, supreme, divine, and wonderful;
others, having attained meditative absorption (samādhi) and gone there, return once more.
They describe that abode of Hari as the imperishable, supreme station;
having heard it again and again, other people, the best of the Sātvatas, rejoice.
They praise the abode of Hari, that imperishable and supreme state, the highest and most excellent station, superior even to Goloka and Vaikuṇṭha. (17)
Where these wives of Śrī Hari, who are of the nature of Muktānikā, always shine as the servants of the beginningless Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa. ||18||
O Badrikā, having heard this praise, a desire arose in the wives of Kṛṣṇa to behold the divine, imperishable abode that is the seat of bliss. 1.9.
Then those women made a request of their lord and husband regarding that eternal, divine world of Brahmā, which shines with its own splendor.
Then Hari said to the women: "In order to behold the divine splendors of the eternal abode of the Imperishable, that [place] must not be seen by you now. (21)
Indeed, upon seeing it, the minds of embodied beings are so captivated that they have no further thought of returning;
compared to my abode, all other abodes appear truly devoid of splendor. (22)
The abodes of the lords shine like hells. ||23||
Therefore, when the nectar of my imperishable abode has been drunk here,
drinking from this world would be as tasteless as a corpse, for its essence is illusory and its flavor is exhausted.
When the sweet food of my imperishable abode is consumed here, the meal becomes devoid of flavor, illusory, and drained of its essence. (25)
When the fragrance of the Imperishable is grasped here,
the "saurabha" (fragrance) that exists in the form of a foul odor is indeed merely a deceptive mockery.
But when the milk-rice produced by the wish-fulfilling cow has been tasted by the Imperishable One,
all things born of illusion indeed become sapless.
When the imperishable is seen adorned with fruits, flowers, and the like, and when it has enjoyed excellent leaves, flowers, and so forth, they indeed arise as if moistened. (28)
The enjoyment of the riches found there is like [the enjoyment of] excrement here;
and the sight of the splendors of those inhabitants is like looking upon something of an ugly form. (29)
Wives are born like leprosy; therefore, looking upon them is not best. Indeed, at this time, my dispassion toward you all has arisen. (4.113.30)
In this world-dwelling, it will become an obstacle;
therefore, the divine abode is to be seen at the end of one's life, and not now.
Thus addressed, the wives said nothing to Nārāyaṇa;
however, an extremely intense desire to see him arose within them.
"What indeed shall we become there when described by the yogis, and what will Hari be like there—so exceedingly beautiful? (33)
As long as we do not see [the truth], peace is certainly not attained;
indeed, the intensity of the desire to see it constantly increases. (34)
Having reflected thus on another day, they said to their beloved Padmāvatī:
"O sister, O wife of Śrī Hari, you are indeed dear and highly honored. (35)
Our beloved husband, the Lord, must be entreated by you;
for the sake of attaining the vision of His abode, He will fulfill your word. (36)
Śrī Nara-Nārāyaṇa said: Urged by all her co-wives, Mādhavī’s beloved wife requested her husband for the sake of seeing his celestial abode. (37)
The beloved Śrī Padmāvatī said: "O most dear Lord, O compassionate one, show your own eternal abode today to your own wives;
please show mercy to them all. (38)
Furthermore, O Great Lord, you are capable of bringing them all here, having fulfilled the desires of all our beloved ones. (39)
Then others, numbering in the hundreds of billions and trillions, likewise made their requests;
"O Lord, O Master, reveal to us Your supreme, imperishable abode. (4.113.40)
O Lord, we all desire to behold that imperishable abode, so that by Your own will You may fulfill every aspiration conceived by us. 4.1
Furthermore, you are capable and indeed able to bring [him] here in every way;
therefore, O Lord Hari, reveal your own imperishable abode.
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said:
O Badrikā, in this manner all those women, the beloveds of Brahmā,
made an intense, unappeasable, and irreversible plea.
Then Hari, perceiving that disposition which had arisen by his own will,
endeavored through that very pretext to withdraw the expansion himself.
"So be it," the Blessed One, the creator of all beings, said to them;
and they all became delighted at the sight of the Imperishable.
"O Badrikā, let all be ready," the Blessed One said to them all.
Having heard their auspicious command, those wives—numbering in the hundreds of millions, billions, and trillions—[prepared themselves]. (46)
Adorned with all ornaments and finery, equipped with their own desired implements, and filled with great enthusiasm, the women then quickly became ready. (47)
Wearing garments of priceless cloth, their hair and attire were exceedingly beautiful; they were adorned with necklaces and ornaments rich with gold, gems, and the finest jewels. ||48||
Divine young women, radiant with increasing splendor and adorned in many colors, became ready and joyful to quickly behold the imperishable Abode. 49.
Filled with affection, they spoke words of mutual joy to one another:
"We are indeed forever blessed to have Kṛṣṇa as our Lord. (4.113.50)
Out of compassion, our beloved showed us the entire circle of the earth, and from there, all the heavens and even the netherworlds in their entirety. (51)
Various kinds of houses belonging to those who are not lords have been shown [to us], but the entire creation of the Lord by the Supreme Self has not been shown to us. (52)
Vaikuṇṭha, Goloka, the unmanifest abode (Avyākṛta),
Amṛta, and the most excellent Śrīpura were also shown by the Compassionate One.
"Today we shall behold the supreme abode, the imperishable, which is greater than everything for that Lord; we are most fortunate here, being beloved of Hari. (54)
No other women possess such fortune as ours, which unfolds thus:
we shall behold our master’s eternal abode, the root of our home. (55)
Even the Vedas do not see it; even the yogis do not see it;
even the lords do not see it at all—we shall behold that abode of Hari.
Whatever description the Blessed One provides here before us regarding your own forms, those exist in the supreme, imperishable state. (57)
"By the grace of the Compassionate One, today we shall behold those forms of our own wives—forms that are divine, super-divine, and celestial. (58)
There we shall behold our own divine Lord stationed,
attended by countless liberated souls and assuming countless incarnations.
We shall behold the supreme Lord Hari, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, who is served by infinite divine consorts.
We shall enjoy divine pleasures and dwell as we desire;
we shall rejoice with the Supreme Self, who bestows great bliss. 6.1.
We shall behold all the gardens and auspicious temples, as well as the heart-lakes and sacred rivers of the Supreme Self.
By the grace of Hari, we shall behold divine lion-thrones and other such seats, the grounds of divine assemblies, and divine pastimes of the rāsa dance.
We shall drink divine nectar, we shall realize our own true riches, and we shall eat sweet foods in the spiritual abode of Śrī Hari. (64)
Speaking thus, those beloveds of Brahmā, the beloveds of Hari, and those beloveds of Kṛṣṇa—the wives—then quickly became ready. 65.
O Badrikā, the glorious Nārāyaṇa Kṛṣṇa, being intensely eager,
then remembered the hosts of liberated souls from his own imperishable abode.
Those of divine form arrived, traveling in countless celestial chariots;
there were those who possessed divine chariots as well as those who served as the drivers of the divine chariots.
They arrived to bring her forth, free from the veil of worldly creation;
they remained steady in the sky above the sacred field of Kuṅkumavāpikā.
They rained down flowers of divine fragrance upon Kṛṣṇa,
and at that time they sounded celestial musical instruments most exceedingly.
The gods and others, inhabitants of heaven, arrived to behold [the Lord];
and Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa commanded his own beloveds.
Then he [honored] his mother and father, as well as male and female servants,
sages and great sages, virtuous men and virtuous women, and likewise his attendants.
Then, indeed, their twin children who lived with them also ascended,
one after another, into divine celestial chariots.
All the wives sat down, as did the female and male servants, the children, the attendants, and the parents; they all settled there in the sky.
Then, within a moment, those who were truthful, virtuous, and devoted to renunciation were seated in celestial chariots along with the liberated souls.
Then, the sound of conchs quickly arose to signal the movement, so that not a single man or woman remained upon the earth. (75)
The sacred field of Kuṅkumavāpikā became, for a moment, as if empty;
for all the millions of women and men remained situated within their celestial chariots. ||76||
Once again, indeed, there was the sound of the conch of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa;
no one remained on earth who desired to go to his abode.
Then Kṛṣṇa also blew his conch-shell for a third time;
at that moment, the celestial chariots accompanied by the illustrious Lomaśa indeed [appeared].
Traveling through the path of the sky, they became invisible in an instant,
having pierced through the seven celestial realms as well as the eight coverings.
Having transcended the abodes of the lords,
they went to the imperishable state at the boundary of the Imperishable on the day of the autumnal full moon.
Swift-moving celestial chariots went to the Imperishable at midday;
having caused all those traveling in the chariots to bathe in the Brahma-lake, Hari [dismissed them]. (81)
Having fashioned all the men and women with bodies appropriate for them—divine, possessing celestial forms, and entirely composed of the body of Brahmā. ||82||

[They worship] those whose form is like that of the ageless and immortal, who possess their own essential nature, who are eternal, enriched by the single reality, and whose very embodiment is existence, consciousness, and bliss. ||83||

Having endowed them all with the qualities and powers of the perfections (*siddhi*) and sovereign mastery (*aiśvarya*) appropriate for their stations, and having established them once again within celestial chariots (*vimāna*), [he departed]. 84.
The Lord Hari, the Master, the Sovereign who assumes manifold forms, went ahead;
having led everyone along with him, he proceeded first toward the supreme abode of the Imperishable.
Moreover, O Badrikā,
having gazed for a moment upon the imperishable void— the perfection of divine, unsurpassed splendor— they were struck with stupor.
Then, when they had been liberated, the Blessed Lord quickly entered them and bestowed upon them his own imperishable powers, which were worthy of his own abode.
Then, having attained a great marvel, they said: "What is this? We, who were men, have lost our womanhood entirely and have become the best of men. (88)
"In every way, we here possess the form of the Supreme Person and the form of our own respective masters; what indeed is this? This is truly a great wonder here! (89)
Having been liberated by Brahmāpriyā and the others, they questioned the Supreme Lord:
"O Blessed One, why is it that we lack masculinity here? Tell us the cause of that."
Having heard this, O Badrikā, Hari, the beginningless Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, spoke from his millions of limbs: "Let my own limbs listen! ||91||
That which is called Māyā, my very nature and the embodiment of my power, is Rādhā, the wife of Kṛṣṇa; she has been manifested by me from out of myself. (92)
Richer than the most beautiful form, more fragrant than the sweetest scent, endowed with a luster exceeding the smoothest gloss, and more splendidly radiant than the brightest shimmer. ||93||
She was well-proportioned, graceful, slender, a treasury of all beauty, endowed with the quality of attracting everyone, and most beautiful to behold. (94)
Beholding her who was so diverse and fickle, and having indeed abandoned me,
they were liberated— those affectionate ones— who regarded her as the Supreme Brahman and as my own essential nature.
They meditated upon, worshipped, and served the Great Goddess;
they especially practiced the ninefold devotion toward Rādhikā. ||96||
Knowing me, they were drawn by that [power] and at that time became absorbed in me.
Then, having understood that power of mine which brings liberation and mastery, [I acted].
Assuming a dark form, I then departed from that Imperishable One and established myself in Goloka;
I have remained there forever.
In this very imperishable state, I dwell as the primordial form, served by the liberated; and there, in that supreme imperishable abode of mine, I formed my resolve.
Whether she be Prakṛti, or Rādhā, or Māṇikī, or Lakṣmī; whether she be the beloved of Brahmā, or the beloved of Kṛṣṇa, or the beloved of Hari.
Or they may be Īśānī or Īśvarāṇī, or liberated women who are my devotees; or they may be the powers (śaktis) of my own form, or even women who are my incarnations.
They shall come to my abode, the imperishable supreme realm;
then, having become men, those women will possess the nature of the primordial Kṛṣṇa.
They shall enter, abide, and move about within my Imperishable;
"it shall not be otherwise"—this eternal decree has indeed been made by me.
In this world, the manifest form of women does not exist at all;
rather, for you, O imperishable ones, it is indeed my own form that prevails.
Then, from that, all beings of my own nature were produced there in every way,
possessing the states of living in the same world (sālokya), sharing the same power (sārṣṭi), having the same form (sārūpya), being in close proximity (sāmīpya), and becoming one with me (ekatva).
Moreover, Rādhā and the others repeatedly entreated me so that they might serve me as they desired,
in my imperishable form and in my own essential nature.
I tell you that I then undertook extreme service so that,
once liberated, they would no longer perceive my form as a woman in this imperishable state.
Likewise, let them always sport in secret within my palace,
assuming whatever forms they desire, even those of my own wives.
Even those who are liberated may still flow forth in such a manner, yet without manifestation;
thereafter, they become objects of manifestation here in the supreme, imperishable abode.
All indeed move about in human form, pervaded by my own nature;
yet they are all beyond the range of perception, for they are always beyond the range of perception of anyone other than me.
My beloveds, who possess the very nature of my own body, worship me;
likewise, you liberated souls exist as male beings within my range of perception.
Even though you are dear to me, at the proper time remain within my range;
do not resort to other forms of worship with such excessive intensity that you draw me away from here.
Likewise, let them remain concealed, each within her own private domain; having become like intoxicated women every day, let them indulge as they please.
All liberated ones serve me, for they likewise possess hidden desires;
assuming whatever forms they wish, they serve me in their own abodes.
Others do not know this sport of mine even among themselves;
thus, my power is boundless, and my sphere of activity consists of infinite pastimes.
"Out of great affection, I shall grant them the highest embrace," having said this, O Badrikā, he manifested celestial chariots before them.

Thus ends the one hundred and thirteenth chapter, titled "The Description of Śrī Hari’s Acceptance of the Prayer of His Own Consorts and Others to Behold the Supreme Imperishable Abode (Paramākṣaradhāma), His Departure for that Abode with All of Them via Ten Million Celestial Chariots, the Transformation of All of Them into the Forms of Liberated Souls there, and the Resolution of Their Inquiry," in the Tiṣya lineage within the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*. 113.
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said:
O Badrikā, then the celestial chariots proceed toward the northern part of the Brahma-lake;
the liberated souls of Brahmā, seated within those chariots, behold it with great curiosity.
It was indeed an ocean of the essence of Brahman,
extending for a thousand yojanas and immeasurable yojanas in length, bestowing the flavor of the bliss of Brahman.
The juices found there bestow eternal bliss upon those who are liberated;
likewise, consisting of divine nectar, they grant perpetual satisfaction.
And within the waters, there dwell countless ocean-born pearls,
exceedingly delighted by the enjoyment of divine, eternal, perfectly blended bliss.
They were bearers of jewels, dark in complexion, and beautified by divine earrings;
they were endowed with ornaments such as divine crowns and bracelets. || 5 ||
They move through the fluids and move through the sky; their forms consist of existence, consciousness, and bliss;
they are indeed capable of assuming any form at will, possessing both wings and hands.
They assume the forms of aquatic creatures and bear the forms of birds;
they take on the forms of trees and possess the forms of Lakṣmī and Śrī.
Beholding that ocean of the essence of Brahman, filled with many wonders,
those traveling in celestial chariots proceeded ahead toward the supreme, auspicious shore.
It was enriched with all kinds of divine jewels, possessed an expansion of divine splendor,
was covered with divine, soft sands, and was beautiful with every kind of supernatural power.

It was beautifully adorned with millions upon millions of sun-like mansions, with millions of boat-shaped houses, and with magnificent palatial halls that served as resting places for millions of celestial chariots.
It was resplendent with ten million palaces of the Brahman-realization chariots,
and it was joined by royal highways leading to the regions of the imperishable state.
The coming and going of celestial palaces has been proclaimed, as well as the descents from the floors of those abodes, palaces, and vehicles.
It was filled with countless mental machines for the exchange of goods,
and it shone with the industrious efforts of those who had renounced the pursuit of worldly gain.
The school for those who had arrived was resplendent with tens of millions upon tens of millions [of decorations],
shining brilliantly with banners and lamps adorned with signs of descent.
It was endowed with great divine tree-groves and magnificent royal gardens;
it was enriched by the splendor of continents and sub-continents, and made level by great embankments.
Abounding with divine stairways and bridges, beautified by divine tides, and charming with diamonds shining on its banks as divine descents; 16.
They beheld that place, which was filled with rest-houses and was delightful with the dwellings of countless cities, inhabited by those who possessed innumerable abodes and splendors.
Having reached such a supreme shore and beheld its splendor,
they travel in celestial chariots, honored by those who have attained the subtle body and those who are liberated.
Filled with joy, they went ahead and beheld forests filled with divine, fragrant leaves that possessed the sweetness of nectar. (19)
Traveling in their celestial chariots, they beheld forests that bestowed delight upon the eyes,
filled with divine flowering trees and rich with blossoming flower-creepers.
They beheld clusters of trees and groves of divine splendor, endowed with forms according to their desire and capable of transforming their bodies at will. 21.
He beheld trees composed of all accomplishments that fulfilled the desires of Brahmā, situated upon the divine ground of the Imperishable, and beautiful with their many-colored limbs. 22.
And they beheld divine trees rich with fruits as sweet as nectar, as well as trees consisting of bulbs,
roots, leaves, and flowers, and even those made of mere fibers.
Kadamba trees, Brahmadāru trees, Pāṭala trees, Pārijātaka trees, Sarja trees, Campakas, Aśoka trees, and Śṛṅgāra trees. ||24||
Tilakas, bakulas, lodhras, kiṃśukas, and likewise khadiras; kunda flowers, sahasrapadmas, kesaras, and sthalapadmakas. ||25||
Candana, badara, jambīraka, and excellent raṅgaka;
kṛṣṇaphala, rāmaphala, lakṣmīphala, and likewise amṛta. ||26||
White-fruited *likucas*, plantains, coconuts, dates, *khārikas*, pomegranates, rose-apples, and cumin. ||27||
Sweet limes, tamarinds, jackfruits, and likewise madhuka trees; mangoes, hog-plums, bilva trees, cirabilvas, and ratālukas. ||28||
Grapes, almonds, pistachios, excellent wood-apples, cardamom, cloves, nutmeg trees, and bitter creepers; ||29||
Bamboo, kīcaka reeds, plakṣa trees, banyan trees with their branches, śamī trees,
śiṃśapā trees, betel vines, kalpavallī creepers, and jīvanti plants.
They beheld *mālatī* and *citraparṇā* flowers, as well as lotuses; they saw *kalpadruma*, *nāspatikā*, and *cikuka* trees, and sweet mud. || 3.1 ||

They beheld those whose faces were like the sun, whose petals were like the moon, whose leaves were like Brahmā, who possessed the essence of Ramā; who were streams of nectar, swarms of bees, and full vessels of desire.
They beheld jars filled with milk, sweet pots, and vessels of sugar;
likewise, trees of sweetness that enchant the mind, cooling trees, and even camphor-trees.
They beheld sweetmeats of delightful flavor, trees exuding fragrance, pearls of great luster, clusters of jewels, golden flowers, and objects made of gold. (34)
They beheld trees made of gold, silver, and crystal;
they beheld golden necklaces, fragrant garlands, and ornaments for fruit. || 35 ||
He beheld the true resounds of the sky of consciousness, as well as the trees of the bliss of consciousness,
the *dadhikrāvṇas*, the delights of the sages, and the beautiful flows.
He beheld the wish-fulfilling creepers that grant the rains of the mind from the feet of the Siddhas,
as well as trees of lamps whose leaves are inexhaustible and whose branches are streams of clarified butter.
They beheld vessels of buttermilk with jeweled stems and golden bases; they beheld saffron-colored powders for cooling and collyriums. ||38||
Lac-dyes, tawny juices, earth-minerals, and great medicinal herbs; grains of wild rice, betel nuts, nutmegs, and jasmine creepers. ||39||
They beheld the *sadāpuṣpā* trees, which bear fruit eternally, and the *brahmaśimbī* plants;
they saw *śrīphala* fruits, *śrīdruma* trees, *āmalaka* myrobalans, and *jalapadmaka* trees.
[He saw] trees with fruit-bearing people, those with three forms, coral trees, young śigru trees, hair-bearing trees, soft edible trees, sandalwood trees, and excellent śālmali trees.
They beheld cotton plants, silk-cotton trees, rice stalks, and statues of deities, as well as lotuses bearing conscious fruit.
In this manner, there are countless great forests within the Imperishable (Akṣara), which are divine, liberated by nature, and capable of assuming any form in every way. 43.
They beheld all the groves, which were capable of moving at will and were established for the sake of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. 44.
They beheld leaves of fire, stalks, great gardens on all sides,
as well as groves, ponds, and rivers.
He beheld the imperishable ground consisting of forest gardens, ten thousand yojanas in extent,
stretching out and pervading all around.
And having beheld all the forests inhabited by liberated souls, in which infinite beings in the form of Brahman indeed dwell. ||47||
Brahmapriyā and the others, being liberated, attained supreme wonder;
they indeed performed various kinds of worship for Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa. 48.
Having traveled through the sky in a celestial chariot, O Badrikā, your husband Hari was gratified with offerings of fruit, sandalwood, and divine gifts.
Then, having traversed the forest lands and reached many mountains,
they beheld those of divine form, possessing a radiance equal to ten million suns.
[He saw] long, deep ravines frequented by forest-dwelling creatures and inhabited by those who have attained liberation,
beautifully adorned with peaks of gold, silver, and jewels.
They were filled with various divine jewels, resplendent with diamonds,
and exceedingly beautiful with peaks of diamond and summits of pearl.
They were joined by long causeways bearing rows of ruby mountains,
and possessed peaks of emerald with floors of sapphire.
Adorned with lapis lazuli, shining with peaks of topaz, with summits of karketana gems and girdles of bhīṣmaka stones.
Adorned in their middle sections with blood-red pearls,
they were endowed with crystal peaks and strings of pearls, as well as upper terraces made of coral.
He beheld mountains endowed with wish-fulfilling gems and adorned with Kaustubha stones and the like,
beautifully graced by peaks the color of rubies.
[He saw cities] enriched by the dwellings of perfected beings and liberated souls, beautified by those who have renounced the Gandharva way of life,
containing the residences where the wise and the liberated have made their homes, and provided with the dwellings of ascetics.
[He saw] those joined with the abode of liberated yogins, consecrated by union with Brahman, endowed with the stages of life free from [worldly] parts, and presided over by perfected sages. ||58||
He saw dwellings and temples constructed by tortoises that had been released, as well as houses built here and there by those who were liberated while bearing devotion. ||59||
On the plateaus, he beheld divine mountains where the villages of Śrīmahāgrāma had been established by the inhabitants of the celestial gardens who had descended from heaven.
They were adorned with bowers of millions of trees, with waterfalls of divine waters,
and with celestial rivers of the nature of Brahma.
He beheld the mountain adorned with most delightful lakes, filled with auspicious, nectar-like waters of existence, consciousness, and bliss.
[He saw] those [pools] endowed with lotuses, clusters of red lotuses, white water-lilies, auspicious night-blooming lilies, white lotuses, aravindas, and the flowers of the nalinī plant. ||63||
He beheld the banks of fragrant flowers, rich with pollen,
as well as divine swans, cranes, and fire-mouthed birds resembling Garuḍas.
He beheld parrots, peacocks, and divine pheasants,
as well as numerous cranes and cātaka birds capable of assuming forms at will.
He beheld all the flocks of divine birds of liberated form;
he beheld elephants, lions, celestial deer, and divine horses.
He beheld cows, yaks, buffaloes, and even deer and tigers; divine beings of liberated form who could assume any shape at will.
On the mountains, they beheld monkeys of divine form with large jaws, as well as winged groups of forest-dwellers.
O Badrikā, having beheld those lords of mountains extending for ten thousand yojanas,
they gazed upon the great mountain named Koṭiśṛṅga.
He beheld the mountain of gold, which was composed entirely of gold and consisted of objects produced solely from gold, appearing as numerous as countless suns.
A mountain consisting of the essence of Brahman, rich in the principles of Being, Consciousness, and Bliss, extending for countless yojanas in length and a hundred thousand yojanas in width. 71.
It was inhabited by cities belonging to countless gods and adorned with many wonders, endowed with manifold celestial lights.
It was covered by dense, heavy clouds of tens of millions upon tens of millions of divine nectars,
while its low-lying channels were shrouded by countless rivers of ambrosia.
Having beheld the great mountain adorned with divine lamps and clusters of medicinal herbs, they looked about the foothills as it was beautifully illuminated.
In those verdant regions extending for a hundred thousand yojanas,
there dwell many hosts of liberated beings residing in cities.
Traveling by aerial chariot, they beheld dwellings provided with rivers, streams, ponds, and the like, as well as enclosures, gardens, and great groves.
In the midst of a golden forest, they beheld the dancing ground of the Lord,
abounding in divine groves and thickets, and strewn with blossoms from every species of plant.
Having dwelt in Śobhitā, which bestows happiness upon Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, where indeed are the auspicious Brahma-muktānikās from the lake of Brahmā; 78.
These very Brahma-men dance for the pleasure of Kṛṣṇa upon that circular city,
ten thousand yojanas in extent and rich with divine palaces.
Its interior was like a divine assembly hall, endowed with every enjoyment,
and its auspicious peaks on all sides were pervaded by the light of millions upon millions of suns.
It was inhabited by those who were beautiful and liberated, wearing various forms;
it was divided into many sections by divine gateways, fortresses, and other structures. ||81||
It was joined with ten million celestial palaces, endowed with ten million abodes of ornaments,
rich with ten million halls of amorous delight, and possessed of ten million temples for musical instruments and the like.
The arena was a stage for circles of dancers seated upon ten million lion-thrones, its performance pavilions furnished with the finest tens of millions of requisites.
Beholding before them the divine Rāsa-maṇḍala of the Supreme Lord, which was ten million yojanas in extent, those situated in their celestial chariots proceeded forward. (84)
It was adorned with circular pavilions supported by pillars of ten million [jewels],
and was fully equipped with all the most excellent and divine requisites for the dance of Rāsa.
Indeed, those liberated from the cycle of rebirth dwell there by the command of Hari,
and there are celestial chariots made of gold and other precious materials.
Endowed with countless pitchers and adorned by its surrounding pavilions, that great pavilion shines eternally like a lotus amidst the sun. (87)
In that pavilion, there shine those who are a mass of Being-Consciousness-Bliss, whose very ground is Being-Consciousness-Bliss, and who are beloved by Being-Consciousness-Bliss. 88.
Where there are wish-fulfilling creepers, wish-fulfilling trees, and wish-fulfilling grasses; where there are wish-fulfilling vessels and clusters of flowers that manifest by mere thought.
There are excellent wish-fulfilling gems and inexhaustible vessels;
there are grounds that yield all desires and seats imbued with the elixir of perfection.
All kinds of nectars and all eternal flavors, as well as trees of great bliss, exist, born from the mind. 9.1
The winds arising from the reality of Brahman, born from the divine light, possess pleasant touch and pleasant vision; therein reside the excellent qualities. ||92||
In the maṇḍala of Rāsa, they possess the great enjoyments of all the sense faculties;
they are beyond conceptualization, unapproachable, and even inconceivable, yet they are mental.
Indeed, by the will of Kṛṣṇa, auspicious beings arise who are composed of divine Brahman, born from Brahman, full of eternal bliss, and bestowers of nourishment. 94.
All the objects of enjoyment within the pavilion bestow the attraction of happiness; indeed, those divine enjoyments are present everywhere throughout the circle of the Rāsa dance. 95.
Liberated saints dwell there, assuming forms at will, their physical bodies non-different from the essential nature of the form of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa. (9.6)
They were endowed with the entirety of the power and capacity residing in Bālakṛṣṇa, and their very selves were enriched by being equal to the great siddhis of the Supreme Lord. ||97||
And on occasions such as the anniversary of His birth,
He who performs the Rāsa-dance is accompanied by a circle of countless female devotees, including Muktānikā.
They delight themselves with songs, dances, and leaps, as well as with clapping, rhythmic foot-steps, and the rolling of their bodies.
Through embraces pregnant with emotion, through the joining of chests,
through the offering of all desires, and through being fulfilled by the Supreme Self.
The liberated ones, whose very nature is that of the Muktānikās, are eternally satisfied;
having attained Śrī Hari as their beloved who fulfills all desires, they rejoice. (101)
Beholding such a treasury of bliss— that circle of the rāsa dance—
and having performed worship with the flowers released by them, they proceeded forward, traveling in celestial chariots.

Thus ends the one hundred and fourteenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Descent at the Shore of the Ocean of Brahman-Rasa situated North of the Brahma-Lake by Brahma-priyā, Hari-priyā, and others, in the Supreme Abode of the Imperishable Brahman, within the Tiṣya lineage of the glorious Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-saṃhitā," wherein they beheld the Great Forest, the Mountain, the Golden Peak Mountain, the valleys, the gardens, the dancing grounds, and the circles for the rāsa dance. || 114 ||
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said:
From above the Rāsa-maṇḍala, those traveling in their celestial chariots beheld the pastime-maṇḍala of Hari, which extended for a hundred thousand yojanas.
There are the dwellings and palaces of those who have attained supreme liberation, as well as temples with divine finials, like the abodes of Kṛṣṇa.
Having become pearl necklaces, they serve the beloved Acyuta, where the women of Brahmā sport in the palatial mansions. || 3 ||
Muktānikā’s wives, numbering in the tens of billions and trillions, possessing divine forms, [reside] in their own palaces within the precincts of the monastery as the consort of Lord Hari.
They serve the Supreme Self day and night upon beds of bliss,
where there exist ever-new, divine, and eternal delights.
There, drinks, foods, and enjoyments exist, filled with nectar;
there, wish-fulfilling cows are found, bestowing whatever is desired by the mind.
There, all the beds are soft, perpetually filled with fragrance,
bestowing everything desired by the mind, pleasant to the touch, and composed of the nature of consciousness.
They bestow divine forms, touches, scents, sounds, tastes, and pleasures;
they possess the fragrance of chewing the leaves of the wish-fulfilling vine, betel, and other such plants.
They were adorned with fragrant, supremely sweet-smelling filaments and the like;
they fulfilled all desires and were endowed with the finest of all requisites.
Where indeed there were bathing halls, warming halls, and kitchens;
where there were dining halls, private chambers, and sleeping quarters.
Wherein there were indeed halls for liquids, halls for drama, and halls for visual arts;
wherein there were halls for song, halls for dance, and halls for costumes.
Where indeed there were halls of all kinds of adornment and halls of pleasure,
as well as halls of enjoyment and halls for the decoration of the body.
There were beautiful drawing-halls as well as halls for embracing one's beloveds; and there were divine palaces fashioned of gold and adorned with finials.
There, millions of diverse cities and wonderful palaces shine all around the circle of monasteries; and there,
dwellings for millions of liberated ones exist on every side.
The *vasatis* (lodgings) belong to both the male and female servants as well. || 15 ||
They also become male slaves and female slaves, as well as friends, circles of companions, and those who have been liberated and possess fine dwellings. (16)
There, indeed, they become radiant with the splendor of the palaces of Śrī Hari,
having thus beheld the circle of pleasure-groves belonging to those liberated souls who sport there.
Traveling in celestial chariots, they went ahead through the lands of the kingdom’s regions,
which indeed possessed sweet grains and ears of corn exceedingly rich in green color.
In those [fields], all the crops shine forth, prosperous and flourishing;
they consist entirely of divine and spiritual essence, known as the unbroken grains of śāli rice.
Wheat, barley, millet, chickpeas, and so forth indeed exist;
they are truly of the nature of divine Brahman and are capable of assuming any form at will.
Indeed, the crops, having attained their full form, grant happiness to the inhabitants;
the sugarcane fields shine all around, along with garden plots rich in vegetables, as well as oblong ponds, large wells, and tanks. (21)
The rivers of the divine waters flow, having consciousness as their essential nature. ||22||
And there are regions of the boundary lands containing fruit-bearing trees, made circular by hedges of various flowering trees. (23)
Protected from all directions, the lands abound with great harvests; they are auspicious and graced by mung beans, black gram, cowpeas, and millet. (24)
Combined with mustard seeds and saffron, along with *dugdhikā* and *bṛhatī*, and accompanied by many countless varieties of potherbs and vegetables; |||25||
They were indeed exceedingly beautiful and abundant with bulbs, flowers, petals, and other such things;
and there, indeed, were cities belonging to those known as Karṣukas.
There are villages, hamlets, and market towns belonging to those engaged in the work of cowherds; there are also cities endowed with divine unions and possessing divine activities. (27)
There, divine golden-colored and brilliantly radiant pearls and great pearls exist, where those whose nature is Brahman dwell. (28)
Likewise, those who are supremely liberated and devoted to the yoga of Brahman dwell there, being solely intent upon the one known as the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. ||29||
O Badrī, those whose collection of deeds was indeed divine and devoted to Kṛṣṇa—
them he gazed upon with joy in every way.
He [inhabits] dwellings, hermitages, lodgings, palaces, huts, houses, hollows, temples, groves, and thickets. (31)
Palaces, halls, residences, and mansions; inner apartments, schools, colleges for the arts, cow-pens, and auspicious gate-towers. || 32 ||
They [climbed] upon fortifications, walls, pillars, and even the peaks [of towers], as well as circular pavilions, upper chambers, gardens, parasols, and likewise watchtowers.
He also provided assembly halls, courtyards for righteous dance and music, arenas for wrestlers and actors, pleasure gardens, and even kitchens. (34)
Having beheld the sacrificial halls, royal palaces, marketplaces, celestial courtyards, and the triple-gated entrances, all resplendent with gold.
They were fashioned with symmetrical forms and adorned with golden domes;
they possessed innate brilliance and walls that bestow all prosperity.

Beholding the vessels for food and drink, which were adorned with wish-fulfilling jars, wish-fulfilling stoves, and wish-fulfilling bowls, and which were filled with supernatural power, providing inexhaustible and desired gifts; (37)
Endowed with all requisites, possessing divine and eternal forms, consisting of existence, consciousness, and bliss, and resplendent with the prosperity of every delight; || 38 ||
Having beheld them accompanied by banners, small flags, and female attendants, and joined by hosts of divine celestial maidens, he offered them worship.
Traveling in their celestial chariots at the head of the procession, they traversed regions spanning many *arbuda* yojanas;
having observed that the inhabitants had abandoned their dwellings, they proceeded to the excellent land of Surāṣṭra.
There, the paths were exceedingly long, leading to the union with the ocean of Brahman,
extending across forests, mountains, dwellings, and pavilions.
The mandalas come from cities and villages toward Surāṣṭra;
the excellent roads are lined with shady trees and fruit-bearing trees. ||42||
They bestow happiness upon all travelers, are auspicious and delightful, provide all enjoyments for those away from home, and grant the essence of existence and consciousness. ||43||
There exist for you those auspicious [vehicles], soft to the touch and free from the fatigue of travel; they are agreeable to both cold and heat, and bestow bliss upon all beings. (44)

Adorned with trees beautified by the flow of nectar-like water from rivers and streams at their sides, they were further graced by trees on their flanks, lovely with soft foliage and abundant fruit. ||45||
They were adorned with rows of *kadamba* trees that shone like royal insignia covered in flowers;
their well-proportioned sides were formed by trees whose canopies provided shade through the spreading of creepers.
Beside artificial rivers were groves of sugarcane, fruit trees,
and creepers, exceedingly beautiful with their interiors filled with shimmering, divine, and highly precious gems.
They dwell in the midst of fields containing huts covered by *kūṣmāṇḍa* creepers;
they are long-wandering travelers who have entered within the fields of the pillars of the three nectars.
Sprinkled by the juices from the branches of great trees that exude honey,
they were made fragrant by a rain of sap from the sandalwood trees of Brahmā.
Adorned with scattered celestial flowers, they bestow the bliss of a divine couch;
they are exceedingly purifying, with the lotus-feet of hosts of liberated souls resting upon them.
Adorned with rows of waves arising from the abundant powder of many minerals, they provide delightful resting places with altars situated along their sides. (51)
These paths are peerless in their construction of great dams against the rivers of worldly existence;
they bestow the bliss of liberation, grant satisfaction, and provide eternal happiness. ||52||

They were joined by those from the central regions traveling along their routes, accompanied by those from the crossroads; they met with those from the various branches of the roads, all acting as guides to the lands.
They consist of halls made of nectar and mountains, bestowing the joy of the gift of immortality;
their centers are pierced by the realm of Brahmā, and they extend as far as the abode of the Supreme Brahman. ||54||
They dwell in liberation from beginningless time, are filled with eternal bliss,
and do not return again for those who have attained union with liberation.
Sprinkled with auspicious substances such as *śreyas* and *rasa*, they are endowed with the path of well-being; they are vast and exceedingly extensive. (56)
Having beheld such paths to liberation, they were filled with wonder; then, traveling in their celestial chariots, they proceeded through regions extending for countless yojanas.
Having beheld those beautiful [cities] with their equal abundance of supernatural power, they proceeded with eager anticipation;
and from afar, they saw the great city of the Abode of the Imperishable (Akṣaradhāma).
It is resplendent with a divine ground of consciousness extending for a hundred million yojanas,
and it consists of dwelling mansions that are the abode of countless liberated syllables.
Endowed with a garment of splendor exceeding the great splendor of all creation;
endowed with a garment of bliss exceeding the great bliss of all creation.
It possessed the fragrance of all perfumes, was endowed with every beautiful form, contained every most delicious flavor, and was accompanied by every desirable sound.
Possessing all beauty and filled with every sweetness,
it was as magnificent as the great palace of countless liberated souls.
There, peaks endowed with divine horns shine forth, free from dependence, possessing the splendor of ten million times ten million suns and filled with jars.
And hosts who are eternally liberated, assuming forms at will,
dwell in palaces made of divine jewels, diamonds, and gems.
That abode is beyond number, the most excellent among all abodes;
it is adorned with countless divine vehicles and celestial chariots.
It was filled with innumerable cities, villages, towns, market-towns,
and hamlets, as well as gardens, groves, parks, fields, and vast stretches of land.
It is adorned with those cities of Brahman, whose essence is truth, consciousness, and bliss,
and with all its gate-towers, fortresses, and the like, as well as groves and ranges of mountains.
It was beautifully adorned with syllables, rivers, lakes, and streams,
and it shone exceedingly with mountains possessing long peaks of *kaustubha* gems.
It was surrounded on all sides by streams of countless divine milks,
and it was delightful with streams of food consisting of nectar and ambrosia.
It was enriched with vehicles, carriages, beds, and various articles of luxury; it was inhabited by beings capable of assuming any form at will and by liberated souls.
And it was inhabited by all those of identical form who have taken refuge in Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa—an infinite, boundless, limitless, and great [abode]. (71)
It was endowed with the abundance of all crops, possessed the perfection of fruits, grains, and food, and contained a city of divine, excellent golden ground, houses, and so forth. 92.
It possesses the excellent radiance of rows of great palaces adorned with countless pillars;
it is the natural source of light and the primary cause for all enjoyments arising from reality.
It has no end indeed for those who travel through the sky, even for those possessing divine vision; yet it is slightly within the range of perception for one with Kṛṣṇa’s sight.
There, countless liberated souls in the form of supreme kings, equal to Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa and whose very selves are Vṛndā, worship Him. (75)
O Badrikā, some are liberated, and millions of others, who are the very self of the assembly, meditate upon the Supreme Self, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Puruṣottama. ||76||
Others, numbering as many as lotuses, listen to the story of the wielder of the Śārṅga bow; and others, numbering as many as lotuses, praise Lord Hari.
Likewise, others offer hymns of praise to their Lord with musical instruments, while still others worship Hari, their Master, with hundreds of articles. (78)
Likewise, others even perform the service of slaves to the Supreme Soul;
the liberated women (muktānikās) offer themselves to the True Lord. (79)
Those who follow His mind rejoice and serve before Śrī Hari;
likewise, the liberated ones, being absorbed in Him, worship Hari during the sacrifice.
They feed him, bathe him, and massage that Hari;
they perform the lustration rite for that Lord and propitiate him with offerings.
They delight, they perfume, they inflame with passion, and they gladden Mādhava in many ways; they cause him to drink the nectar of immortality.
They incense and illuminate [the offerings] while assuming such forms;
likewise, they manifest in various forms exceeding a parārdha in number. (83)
Then, from their celestial chariots, they beheld this and attained supreme wonder; and seeing the various modes of service and devotion, they became free from pride. (84)
That imperishable person (akṣara-puruṣa) also, together with the infinite liberated souls, serves his own Lord, Hari, in his supreme abode. 85.
Having repeatedly become various women and men through all the actions performed by the body, he serves his own master through those very deeds. (86)
In the great palace of the Imperishable One, with archways numbering in the hundreds of billions, pillars weighing in the hundreds of billions, and peaks numbering in the hundreds of billions; (87)
O you who are rich with countless objects of enjoyment, accompanied by countless female servants, served by countless liberated souls, and whose very nature is Brahman! ||88||
O Badrī, seeing that she serves her own husband Hari even while he is known as Brahmā’s boar-incarnation, the beloveds of Brahmā serve him in every way. 89.
They became steadfast and free from pride toward their respective masters;
such was that imperishable abode for those auspicious residents.

Having seen the dwellings of those who have enjoyed [the Lord], as well as their service, and likewise having seen the abode of the Imperishable and the servant of the Imperishable, they attained great bliss. ||9 1||
O Badrī, in the vast abode of the Imperishable, extending for countless yojanas, [reside] all the lords, the liberated ones clad in divine armor. ||92||
The origins of all the cosmic eggs exist in a state of extreme subtlety;
O Vadrikā, within the Imperishable (Akṣara) resides this entire universe, both moving and unmoving. 93.
O Badrī, that which exists established as the very nature of all creation, and which dwells within the abode of the Imperishable (akṣara), exists throughout the cosmic eggs (brahmāṇḍas). ||94||
Whatever does not exist within the abode of the syllable is not found in the worlds;
within each and every divine jewel dwell distinct creations. (95)
For such auspicious jewels as these exist in the House of Akṣara;
indeed, all the abodes of Māyā are contained within a single jewel. (96)
The great terrestrial realms beginning with Goloka exist within a single jewel, and the abodes beginning with Vaikuṇṭha also exist within a single jewel. (97)
The emanations, such as Vāsudeva and others, accompanied by all supernatural powers, abide within that single jewel; it is simply impossible to provide a full description of them. (98)
Having beheld such a state of Brahman—a beautiful, imperishable abode endowed with innumerable supernatural powers—and having received the worship performed for him, [he remained there]. (99)
He saw divine abodes of descent and most excellent temples,
as well as innumerable liberated beings who were born from portions of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa.
They are the forms of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, whose essence is Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa; they have arisen throughout countless creations and abide eternally within that Imperishable. || 101 ||

Having beheld all those who have descended [to earth], who are devoted to the conduct of Brahmā, who possess the splendor of the Lord of Śrī, and who are endowed with countless sovereign powers, stationed within the supreme abode.
"This is indeed the Lord, this is indeed the Lord; this is indeed Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa"—thus did they, traveling in their celestial chariots, perceive him for a moment at that time.
Having repeatedly beheld with his divine eye countless forms of Kṛṣṇa and countless Lords Kṛṣṇa who are liberated souls, || 104 ||
Recognizing those who had attained a state of conformity [with the Dharma] as being liberated, they obtained a realization of the nature of liberation and experienced great joy. (105)
Having attained supreme wonder from seeing what they had never seen before,
Brahmāpriya and the others, stationed in their celestial chariots, praised him most fervently.
Oh, what fortune through the yoga of Hari, that we have obtained the vision of the invisible and so forth, by a mere fragment of his grace, since he is our supreme Lord! 1.07.
Having received the worship performed by Badrikā through her incarnations and other manifestations,
the Lord Kṛṣṇa, Hari, the husband of Mādhavī, stepped forward.
Accompanied by shouts of victory, sounds of joy, auspicious blessings such as unbroken grains,
the offering of handfuls of flowers, and benedictions, they went forth at the head of the procession.
All the celestial chariots belonging to those devoted to divine garments were directed toward the supreme abode of their Lord, Śrī Hari, for the sake of liberation.
By following that path and through union with that wind, which is a portion of the radiance of the supreme abode,
they indeed attained a state of swoon rich in bliss, produced by great ecstasy.

Thus ends the one hundred and fifteenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Vimānas Departing for the Supreme Abode after Beholding Hari’s Sphere of Pastimes, the Regions of the Realm, the Land of Surāṣṭra, the City of Akṣaradhāman, the Cities of the Beginningless Liberated Souls, the Multitude of Divine Devotees, the Great Splendor of Akṣara-Brahman, and the Great Splendors of the Innumerable Incarnations," in the Tiṣya lineage of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Goddess beloved of Badarī;
my heart melts as I describe the abode of Hari, as if seeing it directly before my eyes.
By describing them, I enjoy a multitude of ineffable joys;
having become single-minded, listen to my heart-warming prose. (2)
Traveling by the thousands in celestial chariots through the sky of consciousness,
they beheld with divine vision that mountain-mass of great splendor extending for a hundred million *yojanas*.
From afar, they beheld that [palace], which was increased by the splendor of a hundred thousand times a hundred million-fold Brahmanic luster, and stood a hundred *yojanas* in height.
They beheld such a mass of splendor belonging to the Imperishable Brahman that it becomes dissolved within even a space the size of an atom.
That abode, the supreme state, is the most excellent realm of the imperishable Brahman;
it possesses the power of a single hair multiplied by the weight of Mount Meru.
That is the abode of the Supreme Brahman, the primordial Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa Svāmī, the Sovereign of the Imperishable, the Supreme Self. || 7 ||
For that splendor born of the form is eternal and singular;
it is uniform, of one taste, and dense, and is named Existence-Consciousness-Bliss (Saccidānanda).
It is the embodiment of the world of the Supreme Brahman, bestowing infinite splendor in every direction;
by the single ray of its light, that imperishable one of perfect radiance [illuminates all].
That wealth is such that it is never exhausted nor does it remain deficient;
it is a sight of splendor from afar, cool, and a desired food of nectar.
It bestows upon the beholders a complete attraction and satisfaction;
it grants all bliss, rains down all nectar, and bestows supreme joy.
The beloved ones gazed from afar at that splendor which grants infinite satisfaction;
and as their celestial chariots drew closer and closer, so it appeared.
At that time, those traveling in celestial chariots became bewildered; their internal vision was overwhelmed by the brilliance, they were unable to open their eyes, and their eyelids remained closed.
Then the Blessed Lord, having entered as far as the beloveds, became the bestower of eyes and the giver of the great power of the splendor of the eyes to those in the celestial chariots.
Then his male and female servants, as well as Muktānikā and her sons, became capable of beholding Kṛṣṇa’s splendor through the eyes of Kṛṣṇa. || 15 ||
To those who were unable to grasp such form, taste, touch, and sound— the supreme objects residing in that abode— Kṛṣṇa bestowed his own powers.
Entering their bodies, he bestowed great fortitude upon those who were trembling;
and entering those who were shattered, he granted them his own strength and heroism.
Then he bestowed upon them great garments of consciousness (cidambaram), endowed with the strength of firmness;
at that time, those who were traveling in celestial chariots attained composure in order to behold the splendor.
Then the illustrious Blessed One suddenly bathed them in the supreme Great River of the Supreme Brahman, situated within the space of consciousness.
Therefore, having attained all powers, they possess the nature of the Supreme Brahman;
their bodies are equal to the Supreme Brahman, and their self-power is that of the Supreme Brahman.
Then all those who dwell in celestial chariots became worthy of that abode;
their powers were fully expanded, and they possessed divine, transcendent forms composed of the supreme syllables.
Then, by the majesty of their master, the powerful celestial chariots that had been silenced in his presence became once again resonant.
The divine principles, which indeed lead to the supreme abode,
arrived at the unsurpassed vicinity of the great splendor of the Supreme Brahman.
In the sky at the very edge of the horizon, shining with the intense splendor of the mass of great consciousness,
those who are free from pride attain the bliss of the supreme abode for as long as that space endures.
They forgot all the happiness that had been earned in the imperishable realm;
all that happiness vanished within a mere fraction of the cosmic egg of the Supreme Abode.
O Badrikā, what comparison can there be for the tip of the pleasure of Śrī Hari’s abode?
Indeed, how could there even be a count of the liberated souls in that realm of countless syllables? 26.
Indeed, they became as if merged in the supreme abode, the density of consciousness;
they were not seen externally, like planets shrouded by clouds. (27)
Having entered within that great splendor, those dwelling in the womb see one another;
yet, being situated inside and surpassed by that intensity of light, they do not see anything outside.
For those who have gone to the supreme abode, the imperishable became like darkness;
everything became as if empty—how could that which is empty be an object of perception? (29)
And everything became like a shadow of the Supreme Self;
they beheld such a supreme splendor, the supreme abode.
They beheld a great fortress made of gold and filled with splendor,
both lofty and vast, measuring a hundred thousand yojanas in extent.
There is no calculation of its length; that number does not exist at all.
Indeed, the length of that fortress is infinite and boundless.
There were gate-towers by the hundreds of thousands, and palatial chambers by the millions; there were pavilions by the hundreds of thousands, and likewise courtyards by the hundreds of thousands.
Within that [island], there are also hundreds of thousands of palaces situated upon the bridge,
and millions of inner sanctuaries which are the dwellings of those liberated from time immemorial.
There were countless pavilions there, containing countless collections of pearls, where innumerable palaces and mansions rose upwards. (35)
Countless celestial palaces move about upon their tiers,
and countless dwellings on various levels are inhabited by those who are eternally liberated.
At that time, those traveling in celestial chariots saw no other city equal to this divine one, which was as vast as a fortress and extended for countless yojanas.
This abode, which is difficult to reach from other realms, is the most excellent of all;
it consists of innumerable cities and is adorned with countless gardens. ||38||
Abounding in the splendor of countless liberated dwellings, it is the protector of the abode;
here, from the beginningless form of Kṛṣṇa, rays radiate in every direction. (39)
By means of these, eternal prosperities always descend upon the difficult terrain; and from their rays, showers of nectar fall according to one's desire.
In that fortress, rivers of the nectar of the Supreme Brahman flow through the center;
likewise, there are great rivers, lakes, oblong ponds, and groves. (41)
They become eternally full, bestowing great bliss upon those in distress;
they become streams of nectar, streams of ghee, and streams of curd.
There are streams of beverages, streams of water, and streams of honey; there are also streams of cold water, streams of warm water, and streams of delicious juices.
There are streams of foods to be licked and sucked, as well as rivers of soft foods;
there are mountains of solid foods and mountains of edibles, with the finest juices of fruits and flowers.
Delicious foods, grains, and rice, as well as sugars, all types of oil-cakes, and the finest nectars come forth. (45)
All his forms are indeed offerings of satisfaction—whether they be fresh butters, buttermilk, or even the very essence of milk. (46)
Milks and milk-rice dishes, both desired and pleasing, come into being;
as do divine nectars, the finest of all flavors, which are the essences of the wish-fulfilling trees.
They become the juices of fruits, syrups, and drinks from the wish-fulfilling creepers; they become the essence of nectar from the milk of trees, and they become prepared foods.
They possess all vegetable juices and all blended flavors;
they arise from liquids fit for every kind of amorous enjoyment. ||49||
And from his rays arise all kinds of beds, perfumes, and garments;
and there appear divine, inexhaustible heaps of all the comforts of every dwelling. (4.116.50)
All kinds of ornaments, garments, and attire produced in gardens and groves,
as well as heaps of all desired vessels and utensils, also come into being.
All excellent substances of true beauty are present, and all dyes are also both colorful and smooth. (52)
All splendors, radiances, strengths, and likewise nourishments, as well as the bodily constituents that grant happiness, arise from the black rays. (53)
From its rays are produced jewels, pearls, and diamonds;
it is the cause of all gems and all auspicious means of accomplishment. 54.
O Badrikā, whether soft or rough, gentle or intense, or middling—
whatever object is required by whom, that very thing is produced accordingly.
Bodies arise that are beyond conception, and even those that do not revert from their form;
indeed, by means of the peaks of their creative power (kalpa), they possess the ability to assume forms at will. //56//
That abode of countless and infinite enjoyments is indeed difficult to access;
for its complete description cannot be accomplished even with a lifespan measured in syllables.
Beholding the fortress, adorned with banners and arches, situated upon the celestial chariot,
they set their minds on dwelling right there, which bestowed great joy.
Nevertheless, being carried along, they proceeded ahead in their celestial chariots with the desire to look forward, in order to observe the seven difficult terrains that lay before them.
[He saw] the auspicious protectors of the realms of those liberated beings who are without beginning or end, situated to the north across an interval of a hundred million yojanas of land.
[He beheld] a ground consisting of dense splendor, the abode of innumerable cities,
which serves as the dwelling place for countless beings liberated from beginningless time.
Endowed with all supernatural powers, filled with all flavors, and captivating to the mind;
it was possessed of all kinds of grain, trees, shrubs, creepers, climbing plants, and grasses.
She whose essence is the Supreme Brahman, who bestows the bulbous root of desired fruits,
who grants all objects of enjoyment, who assumes forms at will, and who is accompanied by the river.
It was as beautiful as a lake filled with the waters of the essence of the Supreme Brahman;
it was pervaded by great rivers and streams, and was as magnificent as the great ocean.
It was beautiful and heart-pleasing, adorned with divine lakes of nectar filled with every kind of lotus, and with countless creeper-like vines of liberation.
Seated in their celestial chariots, they gazed upon her who is composed of existence, consciousness, and bliss;
seeing her, she who was clad in a long silken garment, infinite, and within the sphere of the divine.
They beheld the golden fortress that had arrived, radiant with intense splendor,
filled with great wonder, and as expansive as before.
As before it was elevated, as before it was a refuge for excellent dwellings;
it was joined with palaces and gate-towers belonging to those liberated from beginningless time.
Its splendor was enhanced by a residence filled with all objects of enjoyment and their means of attainment arising from mere thought, as well as divine instruments for pleasure.
Having beheld those traveling in celestial chariots, O Badrikā, they attained supreme wonder;
they made their preparations and awaited the abode of Hari.
Even having reached this place filled with great wonders, they did not realize it was the end;
then they proceeded further to the next stage, a long strip of ground.
It was inhabited by cities belonging to those liberated from the beginningless cycle of countless births, and it was as beautiful as before, with all the enjoyments and means for enjoyment.
Beholding that ground, which was filled with wonders, radiant, adorned with all kinds of enjoyments and accessories, and inhabited by innumerable cities; ||73||
They went first to a supreme fortress born of golden luster;
it was as long and as high as before, and enchanting.
It was exceedingly beautiful with the dwellings of countless liberated ones,
endowed with the supernatural power of fulfilling all desires, and replete with every kind of flavor and excellence.
Beholding that great fortress which bestows the reality arising from all thought and grants divine bliss, they entered the ground within it.
All those who were disdainful gazed upon the silver ground,
white like the moon and the abode of every prosperity.
They went to the fourth fortress, which was adorned with cities and other settlements belonging to those liberated since time immemorial, and which extended for countless yojanas.
Arising from a mass of splendor whose essence is the divine silver-reality, it is as extensive as before and endowed with all prosperities and objects of enjoyment. (79)

Upon seeing this, which is filled with the palaces of countless beings liberated from the beginningless cycle and endowed with pure virtues, one will surely recognize it as the temple of Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa.
Reflecting thus, they did not proceed quickly ahead,
[but rather reached] that ground which was indeed composed of the luster of divine lapis lazuli and was so vast.
Beholding her, who was clothed in divine, beginningless garments, endowed with countless supernatural powers and flavors, fulfilling all desires, and exceedingly beautiful; 82.
Having quickly beheld before her that unsurpassed woman, whose splendor surpassed the former and who was bound by a solemn vow, she proceeded toward the fifth fortress.

It was fashioned from the great brilliance contained within crystals known as *sphāṭika* gems; it was adorned with countless, beginningless pearls and beautified by divine dwellings and other such features. (84)

O Badrī, having seen before them that which was endowed with all objects of enjoyment and their means of attainment through the rays of Śrī Hari, and which bestows great bliss, they proceeded forward. 85.
The sixth fortress was likewise not long, wide, or high, yet it was enchanting, its form composed entirely of countless, great, divine *kaustubha* gems. (86)
It is adorned with divine mansions for those liberated from beginningless incalculable [births], endowed with all divine supernatural powers, and fulfilling every desire. ||87||
But those traveling in celestial chariots, realizing that this was the abode of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa and beholding him, departed further ahead in great eagerness, unable to reach him. ||88||
The vast ground of divine play, resplendent with celestial splendors,
was increased by the excellence of ever-increasing energy, essence, and prosperity.
It was auspicious, perfumed by the residence of those liberated since time immemorial and beyond numbering;
it was enriched with the splendor of a great empire and overflowing with all forms of bliss.
Beholding before them that which bestows the blissful joy of all the senses and pertains to the divine self, they all proceeded toward the seventh difficult pass.
Fashioned from the great splendor of the wish-fulfilling gem, it was as extensive as before, beautified by a great palace adorned with countless pearls and other jewels. 92.
Thinking, "This is the dwelling of the Lord, endowed with all supernatural powers and filled with every object of enjoyment," and thus failing to reach it, [he fell]. (93)
They went first to that supreme, divine Cintāmaṇi ground,
which was endowed with all supernatural powers and possessed of all forests, gardens, rivers, and other features.
It was beautiful in every respect, divine, and extended for countless yojanas; it was endowed with palaces and cities inhabited by countless liberated beings from time immemorial. ||95||
Having seen it, they quickly went to the eighth fortress, born from the essence of the Kalpa, consisting of the splendor of the Kalpa, and bestowing the enjoyment of the rays of all the Kalpas. 96.
It is entirely and everywhere pervaded by the palaces of those who are infinite, countless, liberated, and beginningless; it is the most excellent among all difficult-to-attain places. (97)
And even compared to all those previous [palaces], it was wider, longer, and taller;
it was adorned with countless stories and rows of variegated carpets.
It is endowed with rays emanating from the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, and through all kinds of splendors, it bestows the essence of the Supreme Brahman. 99.
It was endowed with countless gate-towers situated one above another,
and it was perfumed by countless stories and chambers scented with the finest musk.
It contained countless chambers within a golden pavilion of dense and radiant splendor;
it possessed countless inner recesses and was resplendent with countless archways.
It was occupied by countless vehicles, carriages,
and celestial palaces, and was beautifully adorned with gardens and groves containing innumerable moon-chambers.
Its form was composed of palaces joined by countless long spires;
it contained dwellings for countless cities and was endowed with countless towns.
It was filled with countless and infinite riches to be enjoyed,
endowed with divine articles of enjoyment, pleasures, and ornaments.
It was constructed from divine bricks, stones, and jewels throughout incalculable and infinite eons;
it was filled with countless divine halls, monasteries, and circular assembly grounds.
It was joined by pavilions with limbs variegated by colors situated within its womb,
which were like the overflowing streams of the river of divine bliss— countless, inexhaustible, and supreme in all respects.
It was adorned with great lakes of bliss and was radiant with gold,
[filled] with those who bore forms corresponding to the primordial Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa.
It is inhabited by all-facing ones who have declared their power and capability;
it is the divine palace of sovereignty belonging to the eternally liberated female deities.
Infinite above and infinite below;
infinite on the sides and infinite all around;
infinite in the center and infinite in every step.
Having beheld that shoreless further shore, they gazed upon it.
The entirety of enjoyment, the entirety of delight,
the entirety of nectar flowing in unbroken streams,
the entirety of happiness, and the seed of the universal aggregate.
They beheld that great and inaccessible fortress.
He who is the eternally single reality yet possesses manifold forms, who perfectly fulfills all the desires of the virtuous,
and who is made beautiful by supreme jewels that resemble the most excellent of all conscious beings.
He gazed upon it, which bestowed desired objects through its immense power in manifesting the abundance of all beloved things,
and which was like a wish-fulfilling tree, a wish-granting gem, a wish-yielding creeper, and a sea of nectar with moving waves containing the essence of Indra’s palace.
It is enriched with the delightful forms of all existing fragrances and the excellent flavors of all tastes;
it possesses the resonance of countless musical notes and bestows the happiness of countless sublime touches. || 113 ||
Where the cows are wish-fulfilling, where the delights are as dear as a wish-granting tree, and where the liberated ones dwell on all sides, bestowing bliss and happiness. (11.4)
In each of their individual dwellings, at the front portion of the doorway,
there stands a jewel visible through creation, which reveals everything directly before one's eyes.
In whose inner house there stands upon the wall the Sṛṣṭi-jewel,
which causes one to hear the sounds of the voices of all creation and bestows awakening;
and in the midst of whose threshold resides the Mānasa-jewel—
He bestows the direct realization of the mind of creation; he is the divine awakening.
And upon the canopy of whose house hangs the jewel of nectar, which bestows complete satisfaction and grants all joy, delight, and happiness. (118)

But for those in whose courtyard stands the wish-fulfilling tree (kalpavṛkṣa), bearing excellent jewels as its fruit, which bestows the essence of every flavor and brings eternal satisfaction; || 11.9 ||
In whose inner home dwells that jewel which bestows the bliss of touch—
the eternal, happy gem that grants the touch of Kṛṣṇa and bestows all forms of touch.
O Badrī, listen to that most excellent secret:
