in every house it yields the fruit of desire and is the supreme fulfiller of the wishes of the liberated. 121.
The *pratimuktaka* [flower] was given by Anādikṛṣṇa;
having touched its fruit, she became liberated from beginningless time, and her beloved, Muktānikā, likewise attained liberation.
If she desires to serve her beloved husband Kṛṣṇa by making him her own, then, having become his dear consort, she shall obtain that fruit by shaking [the branch] at his neck. || 123 ||
The beloved of Rati served her own husband, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa—
the supreme, full-blown bliss— having enjoyed him and having propitiated her dear Lord.
Having extracted that gem called *phala* from his throat, he becomes a man;
indeed, he alone knows this supreme sovereignty, and no other.
Whatever fruit has been given to whomsoever, that indeed accrues to him;
it does not accrue to another when it has passed into the hand of another, even through a different form.
This alone is the great wonder of the Supreme Self, the Lord who bestows all bliss and fulfills every desire of those who are liberated.
The Blessed Lord himself was there, and Cit-muktānikā was also there;
the supreme bliss of those two is this very Saccidānanda. 1.28.
Whoever knows this supreme, divine Upaniṣad, which reveals the secret of liberation, shall also attain the highest goal.

Thus ends the one hundred and sixteenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Divine Eight Fortresses, the Kingdoms, the Abodes of the Original Liberated Souls, Their Sovereignty, and the Secret Upaniṣads," in the fourth section, the Tiṣya lineage, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*, concerning the awakening of the heart in the supreme abode.

Śrī Nara-Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Goddess beloved of Badarī; those who travel in celestial chariots and are duly honored have beheld this eighth inaccessible darkness by means of those secrets belonging to the eternally liberated.
Urged by Bālakṛṣṇa, they then proceeded to other lands—
lands that were auspicious, immeasurable and innumerable, and endowed with inconceivable prosperity.
There, indeed, those who are endowed with the splendor of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa and who are eternally united with the Beginningless One dwell on all sides.
Where the beloveds of Hari who have attained liberation through the secret [teachings] dwell,
and where those liberated through identity (tādātmya) always reside upon the ground.
Where those liberated from the body dwell, possessing undivided contemplation;
where those liberated while invisible dwell, having Kṛṣṇa as their sole object of focus.
"O Badrī, this description of her state is beyond my intellect;
observing those regions, they proceeded further ahead, traveling in their celestial chariots."
They beheld such cities of the liberated ones—
towns, great cities, dwellings, and kingdoms.
In those [regions], there are rivers carrying the bliss of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa,
as well as lakes whose waters possess the fragrance of the form of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa.
In those [gardens], the long ponds possess the flavor of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa,
while they are oceans of the juice of betel-nut arising from the mouth of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa.
The earth was filled with the nectar born from the embrace of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa,
as were the dust particles upon which rested the very forms of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa.
In those forests, the trees bear the form of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa,
and the creepers there possess the likeness of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa.
The clusters of flowers are the forms of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa;
the groves are the beloveds of Kṛṣṇa; and the gardens are the yogis of Kṛṣṇa.
On all sides there are gardens consisting of Kṛṣṇa,
wherein the grasses are of liberated form and the crops are likewise.
And on all sides there are forms bearing the image of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa,
belonging to various liberated souls who are devoted to meditation upon and service of Hari.
Indeed, mandalas shone all around in the assembly halls;
they were all capable of assuming any form at will and wore the wish-fulfilling gem as their primary ornament. || 15 ||
All [these] are forms of the partial manifestation of Kṛṣṇa, the fulfiller of desires; they are the very form of Kṛṣṇa’s own body, their essential nature being non-different from Kṛṣṇa. || 16 ||
Filled with the bliss of Kṛṣṇa, they are inseparable attributes of Kṛṣṇa;
they occupy infinite regions of the earth and exclude all empty spaces. || 17 ||
Each one is present facing forward, accompanied by a form of Śrī Hari;
all the great liberated souls of the forest and the wilderness are indeed forms of Kṛṣṇa.
All those who have been liberated from mountains and the like are forms of Kṛṣṇa; all those who have been liberated from rivers and streams are also forms of Kṛṣṇa.
All those who dwell within the boundaries and enclosures are forms of Kṛṣṇa;
all those who go to gardens and groves are also forms of Kṛṣṇa.
All those who have abandoned villages and towns are embodiments of Kṛṣṇa;
all those who have abandoned residence in cities are embodiments of Kṛṣṇa.
All those liberated from the temple of Prasāda are forms of Kṛṣṇa;
all those liberated from the maṇḍala of Kṛṣṇa are also forms of Kṛṣṇa. || 22 ||
All those liberated from trees and their branches are forms of Kṛṣṇa;
all those liberated, whether forest-dwellers or city-dwellers, are forms of Kṛṣṇa.
All those who are liberated from the beloved of the Lord are forms of Kṛṣṇa;
and all those powers (śaktis) who are liberated are forms of the Lord himself. || 24 ||
The Śaktis who are dear to the Supreme Brahman and dear to Kṛṣṇa-Hari are all, without exception, embodiments of Hari, having been liberated from all secrets. (25)
O Badrī, these ornaments are sentient forms of Hari;
O Badrī, these golden garments are sentient forms of Hari. || 26 ||
O Badrī, even the ornaments and decorations are forms of Hari;
O Badrī, all the weapons as well are forms of Hari. (27)
O Badrī, all the household utensils are forms of Hari;
O Badrī, all objects of enjoyment are forms of Hari. || 28 ||
O Badrī, all the beautiful dwellings are forms of Hari; O Badrī, all the mansions are forms of Hari. || 29 ||
O Badrī, all the senses are forms of Hari;
O Badrī, even those which appear distinct are indeed forms of Hari.
O Badrī, even his own self resides there in the form of Hari;
whatever exists in that supreme abode is the very form of Kṛṣṇa.
Everything has Hari as its essence; there is nothing else that exists apart from the nature of Kṛṣṇa.
He is the blissful happiness of Kṛṣṇa, whose manifest form is established as non-different from Kṛṣṇa.
It is one alone, without a second; it sees nothing else, nor does anything else see it.
Everything is permeated by the beloved Śrī Kṛṣṇa and is manifested as his very form.
In that state, what could grasp what? One finds only one's own self-nature.
Such is the Supreme Brahman, which exists pervading everything. 34.
In the region of Badarikāṇḍa as well, the Supreme Brahman shines forth;
this is called the supreme Brāhmī Mahāvidyopaniṣad. ||35||
Having studied this, even one who is already liberated then becomes like the Supreme Brahman;
one who is not yet liberated attains liberation, and one who is liberated attains primordial liberation.
Even though already liberated from the beginningless [past], one attains the liberation of the secret;
even while being liberated through the secret, one attains the liberation of identity. || 37 ||
Released through identity with that, he attains the nature of the Supreme Brahman;
thereafter, nothing else remains to be known as supreme. (38)
Nothing else remains for him to be attained as a supreme object of desire;
he himself is the beloved, and he alone is that beloved; she herself is the beloved, and she alone is that beloved.
That which is His very equanimity, wherein there is nothing whatsoever,
from which there is nothing higher, and likewise nothing else;
that which contains within it everything that belongs to Him.
The wise man, realizing that state, does not govern separately.
Who indeed is dear there, and who is his beloved, when he himself is everything that is dear?
Embracing that most beloved and charming one in the divine abode—
The liberated one abandons the state of being separate from others. ||41||
He is this beloved, and she is that supreme beloved; he is the enjoyer, and she is the one to be enjoyed. He is within the womb, and he is both within the heart and without.
Having attained that beloved one, he destroys his suffering. ||42||
O Badrikā, those who are dear to Brahmā are the Ramās of Kṛṣṇa,
and they are indeed the Ramās of liberation who are dear to Hari;
having attained that beloved who possesses all forms, they [attain their goal].
For their minds were indeed resolved to remain right there. ||43||
Indeed, those dark-bodied women dwelling in celestial chariots,
though already liberated, were repeatedly filled with longing, desiring their husbands to be Kṛṣṇa, as if they were seeking a crest-jewel for their necks.
He gazed repeatedly at those [beings] whose expressions were imbued with smiles. ||44||
Hari, having recognized him and perceived his disposition and such supreme love,
quickly manifested himself and led him to his own city.
Higher than the highest, supreme over all, the Great Abode. ||45||
And all those who traveled in celestial chariots, beholding that ground consisting of liberation and the abode of Brahmā, went to the temple of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
It is his own secret temple, situated within the center of all the circular cities of the liberated ones, and fully endowed with great fortifications. 47.
O Badrikā, as those traveling in celestial chariots, desiring to dwell in your abode,
beheld from afar the city of the Supreme Brahman situated in the midst of the residence of the liberated,
their eyes immediately [fell upon it]. 48.
The splendors of those traveling in celestial chariots were indeed eclipsed by that overwhelming radiance.
Those traveling in their celestial chariots beheld the city of the Supreme Brahman;
they then recognized their own majesty through the splendor of their Lord.
Praying for the Supreme Self to grant him that supreme vision,
Hari bestowed upon him his own most excellent vision, the pinnacle of all.
Then all those traveling in the celestial chariot, along with their Śaktis, cast wide-eyed glances from their own eyes that seemed to stand apart from their own eyes. 52.
They became free from blinking and were ever capable of enduring the splendor of Kṛṣṇa;
their celestial chariots then swiftly proceeded to the vicinity of the city of the Supreme Brahman.

Where there is the massed splendor, the massed splendor, the massed splendor intensely struck; and even beyond that, the one whose splendor is more intense than the impact of the massed splendor of the True Principle (saddharma). ||54||
Traveling in their celestial chariots, they beheld the fortress of the city of the Supreme Brahman, which was fashioned from the essential reality of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. ||55||
It is divine, composed of all wonders, free from dependence on anything else, and perfumed by the great pearls of liberated love, like a pearl necklace set with gems.
The male and female servants, attendants, sons, and daughters— those who number in the hundreds of billions, trillions, and quadrillions— all of them are forms of Kṛṣṇa.
There, in that fortress, which is surrounded by a million yojanas,
dwell beings endowed with innumerable supernatural powers and filled with all kinds of black enjoyments.

Standing in their celestial chariots, they beheld all those guards of the inner apartments stationed at the height of the divine gate-tower and its lotus-pedestal, all of whom were in the form of Kṛṣṇa.
They recognized their equals as servants, yet they did not distinguish between daughters, sons, sages, holy men, ascetics, and virtuous women. (4.117.60)
The Lord Hari bestowed upon them an intellect intent on full cognition;
their minds quickly blossomed, and they swiftly became omniscient.
Then they all understood everything that was fit to be known:
"This is my son, this is my daughter, and this too is my servant. (62)
"This is my mother, this is my father, and this is my female servant, my friend"—having thus attained such realization, they travel in celestial chariots, filled with joy. (63)
Filled with joy and awakened to their own realization, they composed verses for one another; O Badrikā, you too quickly uttered the secret teachings even while being liberated. (64)
"This is my father, this is my mother, this is my friend;
this is my kinsman on the earth in this land, this is my son, and this is my daughter. (65)
Having seen [him] in the sky, they spoke thus clearly in many ways, filled with curiosity and moved by a natural affection arising from what they had heard and seen. (66)
Filled with love, they ran forward in agitation and excitement;
bearing in their hands the vessels and implements for worship, they were like so many forms of Kṛṣṇa.
All those [gods] dwelling in celestial chariots, with eyes full of affection,
gazing upon them with love-filled glances, then called out to them.
To welcome them, these [gods] arrived at the entry-grounds of millions upon millions of celestial palaces and upon the ground amidst difficult terrains. (69)
In the beautiful grounds of the gardens, pervaded by every fragrance and loveliness,
which indeed constitute the very chambers of the great palace of the Supreme Brahman.
Filled with joy, they uttered cries of "Victory! and cries of "Happiness!";
by the will of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, their celestial chariots descended. (71)
All of them, eager and free from fear, honored him with unbroken grains, flowers, and the like, as well as with sandalwood paste, nectar, and water.
And having descended, they embraced one another—those beloved of Hari—mutually with the joining of chests and the joining of eyes. (73)
Through the union of faces and likewise through the union of bodies—now, O Goddess beloved of Badrī, hear this most excellent secret. (74)
All those who had been situated in the celestial chariot— the women, the pearl ornaments, and so forth—
descended from the vimāna as soon as they reached the ground before him.
He gazed upon those auspicious ones who had come for the sake of his welcome— those who are liberated from time immemorial, whose nature is that of Kṛṣṇa’s beloveds, and who possess his own form.
[He saw] those who always abide in the supreme abode, who take refuge in the city of the Supreme Brahman,
who are his own self, who are both identical with and distinct from him, and who consist of his own nature and qualities.
He offers welcome to those who have come for their own worship,
regarding both them and himself as non-different in form, and himself as consisting of their reflected essence.
Having seen and realized that those who had been in their celestial chariots were present everywhere in the form of the fundamental Self,
they indeed attained supreme wonder.
Having received worship after the worship of Kṛṣṇa, they, by the command of Kṛṣṇa,
departed together with them to their respective abodes in celestial chariots.
Then the Lord, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, went to his abode together with the individual soul who had been released by the celestial chariot.
In every house, they beheld Hari in this way: another Hari, though being the original form itself, shone upon a divine elephant-throne.
Seeing the two Hari-forms, his own two forms,
the arrogant [demigods] perceived their own state of being eternally liberated as well as their secret liberation.
Possessing divine knowledge, they understood their absorption into his own self;
they all entered into the primordial form, and Kṛṣṇa vanished within Kṛṣṇa.
O Badrikā, when all those who were originally of the form of Kṛṣṇa attained their primordial forms,
they reached the supreme and most excellent divine rest.
Just as one who has traveled abroad finds peace upon returning to his own home,
so too, having attained rest, they forgot their time abroad.
Oh, the power of Kṛṣṇa bestows both divine and non-divine wisdom; it possesses the capacity to assume infinite forms and to grant countless manifestations.
Then, in an instant, the celestial chariots merged into the chariots,
and their ornaments, garments, and riches merged into his splendors.
The entire head [of the deity] is the form of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa;
indeed, he is one alone and without a second, both in form and in qualities.
"Everything has come to be"—who can truly know the divine play of Hari?
The Lord dwells in every house, manifesting for each liberated soul.
All [the goddesses], beginning with Brahmapriyā, have attained the state of being liberated from secrecy;
and there are palaces of exceeding beauty, numbering in the millions, hundreds of millions, and tens of billions.
Endowed with countless supernatural powers, they remain steadfast there in the city of the Supreme Brahman;
and by the power of the Kaṇṭha-maṇi, they are stationed within the palaces.
And they recognized their own status as wives of Kṛṣṇa, who is Hari;
likewise, they served him, their lord, the master Nārāyaṇa.
Then, enriched by the nature of half of his own limbs, they reached their own eternal city and performed a bath in the nectar of the Supreme Brahman within that abode.
They worshipped Kṛṣṇa with flowers and sandalwood paste that were themselves the unimpaired Supreme Brahman;
they partook of a meal consisting of the nectar of tasting the essence of the Supreme Brahman.
The beloved ones drank the nectar-water of the Supreme Brahman and incessantly served the Supreme Brahman, their supreme beloved. 96.
Day after day they performed the worship of the beloved Supreme Brahman;
attaining supreme devotion to the Supreme Brahman, they went to eternal liberation.
Through their intense service, they enjoyed the ocean of the bliss of the Supreme Brahman;
they perceived nothing else whatsoever as superior to that bliss, nor anything other than that bliss as true happiness.
By the grace of Kṛṣṇa, the wives attained the very nature of Kṛṣṇa himself.
Then the Blessed Lord, in order to show them His own abode, [proceeded]. 99.
Then Kṛṣṇa set his mind upon the center of millions of billions of palaces, and he spoke these pleasing words to all of them.
I am proceeding to the assembly hall known as Parabrahma Maholā;
may all [the goddesses] come swiftly there to my supreme abode. 10.1.
"You have attained here the states of *sālokya*, *sārṣṭi*, and also *sāyujya* and *sārūpya*; only oneness (*ekatva*) remains. (102)
"Even that I shall show you while I remain upon the celestial throne," O Badrikā,
having spoken thus, the Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa—
Vanishing from that temple, he quickly went to the assembly hall where he was honored by the King of Kings, the Lord of Lords, and the Supreme Sovereign.
He is worshipped by the liberated ones, the Lord, and those who are yet to be liberated, beginningless and endless; he is worshipped through his countless and infinite manifestations and glories.
Honored by countless divine powers and weapons,
he dwells as the sovereign of all creation, the lord and master of all abodes.
The noble Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, who is without beginning, Kṛṣṇa Keśava himself— Lord Hari, having gone to his own root, his own essential nature, became firmly established there.
This child Gopāla-Kṛṣṇa, the son of Yaśodā,
is the Lord, the husband of Padmāvatī, and the supreme bestower of boons upon Rādhā and Lakṣmī.
Having become known as the Supreme Self, the Supreme Brahman, the Supreme Lord, the Highest Ruler,
and indeed the Puruṣottama, he became firmly established in his abode.
O Badrikā, those Muktakoṭis arrived at the assembly hall,
joyful like women who, after their husband had gone abroad, have returned to him once more.
On the twenty-seventh day of his manifestation on earth,
specifically on the morning of the eighth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Kārttika, [he was joined] by his beloved wife and others.
Then all the liberated souls (muktas) and their consorts (muktānikās) went quickly to perform the festival remembered by the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa.
Seated upon the elephant-throne, the beloved Lord stood surrounded by the great assembly;
they worshipped their Master and likewise performed the ritual waving of lights (ārātrika).
Innumerable liberated souls arrived and worshipped Hari with divine offerings with supreme devotion, and they raised shouts of "Victory! 1.14.
Having offered worship, all those residing there departed for their own abodes; likewise, the millions of liberated ones, including Brahmapriya and others who had come as companions, also departed.
They all indeed desired to see the great Kṛṣṇas;
then he said "Om," and told them, "I shall show you the liberated ones."

Thus ends the one hundred and seventeenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Regions Beyond the Fortresses of the Eight Durgas in the Tiṣya Lineage within the Fourth Section of the Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā," concerning the fortresses of the realm of the Supreme Abode; the fortress-city of the Supreme Brahman; the dwellings of the liberated souls who are the Self of the Supreme Brahman; the unity of those residing in the city of the Supreme Brahman in their two-fold forms; their descent into their respective abodes within the city of the Supreme Brahman; their welcome and rest; and their departure toward their own eternal celestial mansions in the assembly of the Supreme Brahman. || 117 ||
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Goddess beloved of Badarī, to the supreme Raṅgamahola,
the most excellent Sabhāmahola, and also the Vāsamahola.
The great festival of the bed, the great festival of exaltation, the great festival known as the temple, the great festival of bathing and purity, and also the great festival of play. (2)
The great festival of peace and happiness, the great festival worthy of aesthetic delight, the great festival known as feasting, and likewise the great festival of worship. (3)
It is the great festival of all scriptures, the great festival of service to the devotees,
and likewise the great festival of service rendered by those who have been made like pearls within the secret [teachings].
The Paṭṭāṅganā-mahāmuktā, the Nikāma-holaka,
and likewise the Antaḥpura-mahola— these are the sixteen Maholakas.
Brahmapriyā and the others, being liberated, beheld those vast palaces,
each extending for many millions of yojanas.
That which is known as Raṅgamahola is the Mahola of the Supreme Self,
the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, and it is His dwelling place.
He is entirely composed of divine gold, the radiant essence of being, consciousness, and bliss;
He is replete with all supernatural powers, perfections, capabilities, and countless sovereign lordships.
It surpassed all other circular pavilions, being resplendent with banners raised at its summit;
it was delightful and captivating, graced by the beauty of countless pillars. || 9 ||
It possesses corner-turrets such as the wish-fulfilling creeper, the inexhaustible vessel, and the thought-gem;
it is adorned with side-halls and other structures where all objects of enjoyment and the like shine forth.
Exceedingly beautiful with golden arches hanging down from countless points,
it was auspicious on all sides due to the divine and super-divine splendors of Hari.
In the center, it was enriched with Brahma-thrones, canopies, umbrellas, and chowries;
it was showered with divine flowers and garlands by liberated deities.
Indeed, those splendors arising from the splendor of Hari’s lion-throne spread forth throughout other great worlds.
In all creations, the circular splendors of other great luminaries proceed outward, facing toward Durgā.
Upon the Brahmāsana sits Anādi-Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa,
the Supreme Lord, the primordial form, the master of all, and the eternal Sovereign.
Adorned with all ornaments and endowed with every fragrance, he was exceedingly rich in beauty beyond all forms, more handsome even than the most handsome.
A youth sixteen years of age, enchanting to all beautiful women,
rich in the splendor of every amorous grace, and captivating to the hearts of all.
He shone resplendent upon the gentle Brahmāsana, joined with a thousand pillars,
seated upon a soft throne reached by a flight of a hundred steps.
He who is worshipped with all offerings of honor and the like by millions of liberated beings—
that very one is the Supreme Self, the beloved, the Supreme Person.
Having seen Ānanda, all those who had been released from the millions of secret bonds departed;
released in Raṅgamahola, they beheld their own [liberated] selves by the millions.
Then they beheld upon the wall their own countless forms, composed of divine jewels, as well as all the various manifestations of the abodes.
Then he saw the Lord as the creator of all within the statues;
then he saw all the cosmic eggs upon the slabs. (22)
Thus they indeed obtained this supreme direct experience;
for in every single corner, all the arrays of creation are present.
Indeed, upon every floor there are all abodes;
indeed, within every panel there exist all the universes. (24)
There, there were countless Anantārādhikās, as well as countless Kamalās;
there were also countless Māṇikyās and countless Padmāvatīs. (25)
There, the beloved ones are infinite, and the Lakṣmīs are indeed infinite;
the Ramās are also infinite, and the Śris are likewise infinite. (26)
In the midst of the great assembly on the stage were the beloveds of Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, who possessed liberated bodies and bore the very forms of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa. (27)
All of them, assuming male forms, eagerly serve their beloved;
assuming secret female forms, they serve him in the bedchamber.
Assuming male forms, those countless beloveds of Brahmā and countless beloveds of Hari serve [him] in the theater hall. (29)
Innumerable women of Kṛṣṇa’s lineage serve the infallible Hari; likewise, there are countless women of Nārāyaṇa’s lineage and similar women of Mādhava’s lineage.
Likewise, there are innumerable Līlās and Vāsudevyas, as well as countless Padmās, Padminīs, and Tulasīs. (31)
Countless Śāradās, Sarasvatīs, Gaṅgās, and Yamunās—
those known as liberated souls— serve their beloved Kṛṣṇa, the Nārāyaṇa.
The most excellent women worship their beloved Lord and delight Him;
skilled in song, they swing Śrī Hari upon a swing.
The lotus-like women adorn their lord, the illustrious Śrī Kṛṣṇa,
while the golden-hued deer-women massage his limbs.
They feed the Lord with all kinds of delicious foods and drinks;
they bring joy to the Compassionate One by offering every form of embrace. (35)
Taking refuge in the secret chamber, those beloved women joyfully receive him;
they cause Hari to drink from divine sugar, cardamom, and arka-kesara flowers.
Indeed, these were mixed with excellent milk produced from the wish-fulfilling cow;
thus, in this great arena of the Mahāhola festival, there were the finest diamonds.
Innumerable jewels and beautiful golden necklaces exist;
with these, lovely women adorn their beloved, who is dear to the Goddess of Fortune.
There, those women, beginning with Brahmapriyā, were united with their lord;
there too, the Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Master, assumed a second form.
Beheld by them, the Beloved then became one with the two;
there, the Supreme Lord shone resplendent upon the Brahma-simhasana.
O Badrī, rich with the splendor of the king of kings and attended by infinite liberated souls, I beheld a great wonder at that spot. (41)
Indeed, those individual Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇas who had arrived together with him have attained dissolution into the Supreme Kṛṣṇa through that very liberation. ||42||
Beholding their own beloveds having attained dissolution into the Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, who is without beginning, upon the Brahma-simhāsana, they were struck with supreme wonder. (43)
Then those beloved ones, released, drawn forth, and fainting with bliss, being enchanted by the supreme divine Beloved, joyfully honored and praised Him. 44.
They performed the nightly lamp-offering and embraced their lord and master;
being liberated and utterly devoted to the Supreme Lord, they spoke to Śrī Hari.
O Hare Kṛṣṇa, ocean of mercy, You alone are the Supreme Person;
as the infinite soul of Kṛṣṇa, You shine forth and are always to be served by us. 46.
O Lord, display here to us all your riches;
indeed, the sixteen great divine [attendants] have been seen by us from the outside. 47.
O Lord of Prabhā, we desire to behold all that is within;
O Lord of Mādhavī, those things outside appear to us as infinite and boundless. (48)
Just as the fiery upper regions are always superior to other fiery realms belonging to the sun, so too do your great sparks of fire prevail throughout the cosmic eggs. 49.
Standing in the very center of the sixteen, your great stage-like festival shines forth in every direction like the sun, consisting of ten million suns.
O Great King, you are indeed the most excellent among us and the one who deludes our minds;
O Lord, reveal to us all the abodes of prosperity. (51)
O Badrikā, Śrī Hari wandered with them through Raṅgamahola in order to quickly reveal Himself, where indeed there are countless divine powers (ṛddhis).
Indeed, there were walls and floors made of divine wish-fulfilling gems,
as well as ornaments of gold from divine wish-fulfilling gems.
There were beautiful garlands of divine jewels, rows of divine archways,
celestial attire, all kinds of divine furnishings, and divine grounds.
All divine coverings, divine seats, [divine] forms, all divine vessels, and divine caskets and so forth. ||55||
Listen, O Śrī Badrikā, in that Raṅgamaholaka, from each and every object known as the Bījamaṇīndra, [there arises... 56.
Arising as they desire, innumerable beings of their own kind are born:
channels of form, channels of taste, channels of fragrance, and lords of jewels.
There are streams of curd, streams of honey, streams of nectar, and streams of jewels;
likewise, there are streams of the drinking of dense bliss that bestow complete satisfaction.
Then, like small streams of all-encompassing loveliness and jewels that bestow delight,
they were gazed upon by throngs of liberated souls and became sources of enjoyment.
O Badrī, those who provide the finest articles of adornment, who give ornaments and garments, and who provide the necessary attire were seen there. (4.118.60)
There were hundreds of thousands of courtyards and chambers filled with the light of existence, consciousness, and bliss;
in each one stood the Lord, the Master, together with his beloved wife.
The beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇas were beheld by each and every one of all the divine liberated women, headed by Muktānikā, within their respective mansions. 62.
There, those sapphires of beautiful form were beheld, which caused a downpour of the most excellent, dense mass of great bliss.
There were jewels for turning back [the enemy], clusters of jewels for the vine-bowers,
jewels for the great gardens and so forth, as well as jewels for the pleasure groves.
There, all the causes for jewels and the like were examined;
indeed, all the golden glories were scrutinized from every side.
The sun, the moon, and other gems, as well as mirrors, looking-glasses, and polished slabs, were all inspected by everyone on every side within the great arena. (66)
And there in that great assembly, all the various forms were beheld by throngs of secret-knowing ones who were full of longing.
This most wonderful thing came within the range of vision there, while the form of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa remained upon the stage. (68)
Indeed, the entire supreme abode was beheld by them at the crown of the head;
likewise, the imperishable abode was seen in the heart, and the abode of Māyā within the belly.
Indeed, the abodes such as the incarnations were beheld by him in his mouth;
and the worlds of the lords were truly observed within his yawn.
Then, by them, the cosmic eggs were beheld at the feet;
and within the Liṅga, Saṃkarṣaṇa, Rudra, and Śaṃkara were beheld by them.
The unobstructed creative powers were seen at his navel;
the radiant Viṣṇus were seen in his testicles.
The Great Being Mahākāla was beheld upon his brow, and Prakṛti, the Great Māyā, was beheld within his will. (73)
Vāsudeva is the witness; these two were perceived by him within his intellect.
Kṛṣṇa and Nārāyaṇa were seen by them in his two arms.
All beloved ones were seen on the left side and in the belly of Hari; and all men were seen as his own self on the right side of Hari.
Birds are on the back; aquatic creatures are on the hips;
animals that move horizontally are on the left and right sides; and trees are upon all the body hairs. (76)
The roots of his body hairs are the bulbous roots (kandas), and the hair-pores are the creepers;
his mountains are in the solid parts, and the rivers are everywhere within his channels (nāḍīs).
Within that [reality] which consists of a single essence, by the grace of that very [reality], those who have been liberated from millions of secrets beheld many diverse manifestations. (78)
On his forehead was Surāṣṭra, and in the middle of his forehead was Aśvasārasa;
the beloveds of Hari beheld these as his own true forms.
O Badrikā, is the limit of his glories not reached?
Whatever exists in his form, all that is present everywhere in this great arena of the world.
Indeed, Mādhava’s glances were cast by his beloveds according to their own desires; yet, out of compassion, he likewise directed them toward various objects there. ||8.1||
The object that had become manifest became concealed, followed by Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Lord of Śrī and the Beloved One. ||82||
Beheld by all [the goddesses] together, the Lord, who is the self of all, was gazed upon from every side;
like an embodied being situated within them, he was also seen standing outside. 83.
When all objective entities had suddenly dissolved, he was then seen as solitary;
he is the self-ruling, sovereign, and great king, truly one and without a second. ||84||
Then, having attained oneness with him, those who have been liberated since beginningless time and those who are supremely liberated were beheld by the world within Śrī Hari. ||85||
Just as innumerable fish submerged in water are indistinguishable from one another, so too those who experience the essence of unity abide in a state of non-differentiation.
Those who have no further shore, no boundary, no number, and no measure do not go anywhere; they do not emerge from anywhere, being attached to form externally. (87)
This creation, consisting of embodied forms, surpasses the supreme abode;
beholding it, those who have attained the secret of liberation were struck with supreme wonder. (88)
And their pride dissolved before him due to his inferior status;
then they requested that he remain with them as their beloved.
And after the vision of Mahāloka, Hari gave his word;
then he indeed showed him the supreme residence of Mahāloka.
Then Acyuta showed him his supreme bed, measuring one hundred thousand yojanas and filled with every kind of supernatural power.
It was adorned with couches and thrones for hundreds of millions of billions of beloved women,
and was supplied with all the finest materials suitable for every kind of elegant attire and ornament.
Having seen him, whom they had never seen before, they were struck with supreme wonder;
then Mādhava showed them his own palace.
There dwells his mother, Kambharāśrī; his father is Gopālakṛṣṇaka;
his sister is also contented, as are Śuka and the Blessed One himself. (94)
And their beloved Lord Hari always dwells as their devotee within the essential forms of their respective mothers, fathers, and other kin. (95)
While everyone there was watching, he meditated with inner compassion;
seeing that supreme wonder, they too attained great joy. ||96||
Right there, in that divine abode measuring a hundred thousand yojanas and endowed with every prosperity, Mātṛkā and the others dwelt at will within their palaces. (97)
Then the Lord of Beings showed them the great festival of the ritual bath;
beholding the procedures for the divine ablution, they were struck with supreme wonder. (98)
All the springs flow with milk, water, ghee, and honey, carrying forth streams of nectar, immortality, bliss, joy, and supreme delight. ||99||
They beheld him who was endowed with all fragrances and soft, graceful beauty;
then they gazed upon that most excellent Khelamahola.
In that place, there are indeed divine delights that provide all forms of bliss and serve as means for play, which are entirely obtainable through a wish-fulfilling tree.
Then Keśava displayed the Great Śānti [Ritual],
which bestows all peace and is equipped with all the means for achieving peace.
And then he showed him the supreme Śṛṅgāra garden,
extending for a hundred thousand yojanas, a magnificent place of great splendor.
Filling the objects of aesthetic delight for billions of lotuses, pervaded by wish-fulfilling vines in embodied form, it is auspicious and bestows all that is desired. (104)
Creeper-like saffron and lac-dye, garlands of collyrium and unbroken rice-grains,
creepers of sandalwood paste, and trees of liquid aloe-wood.
Then, beholding balls of butter— the very essence of oiliness— though possessing a mild flavor, those who had attained secret liberation experienced supreme joy.
The Liberator displayed a great variety of foods within all kinds of divine and non-divine creations. (107)
Whatever food there may be— whether it be the finest solid foods, those to be sucked, those to be licked, or drinks—
all of that has its root indeed in this divine food, which comprises everything.
Everything pertaining to the gods, to Īśvara, to the incarnations,
and to the pearls— indeed, everything belonging to oneself and even that which belongs to Brahmā— is to be observed therein.
They became eager to eat, and their husband fed them;
the Lord gave them the highest satisfaction, which transcends all external states.
Then there was a great hall for worship, a hundred thousand yojanas in extent,
filled with all the necessary articles and implements suitable for every kind of veneration.
The Blessed One revealed himself, and they performed worship;
the Lord of the Abode also revealed the great hall of all the scriptures.

Where the yoga of Kṛṣṇa arises for those yogis of meditative absorption, who have found the opportunity to realize the purpose of the scriptures concerning the abodes of all created beings. || 11.3 ||
In which single jewel all creations become visible to the eye; and upon beholding it, they arise like a great festival for the service of his devotees. 1.14
And they beheld those liberated souls who always perform service to Hari;
then Hari performed various services for those liberated ones.
Seeing the mutual service rendered by those two,
they were all struck with great wonder and considered it indeed to be supreme good fortune.
The Blessed One revealed his own great secret realm,
wherein all these beloved women [beheld] their beloved, the dear one of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
Bestowing all desires eternally, women who had witnessed this wonder—the abode of countless beauties—resorted to couches and other comforts. 1.18.
And then he showed him his harem,
where there were one hundred and forty of his own wives.
Each of them, engaged in serving their respective husband Hari with a thousand attendants,
served him constantly, O Badrī, and upon seeing him, they attained great joy.
When those women had attained absorption into their respective original sources,
then the Blessed Lord [entered] the great inner apartment at Badarī.
He, who bestows infinite honor through his miraculous powers, revealed himself to all those women who worship Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa with the affection due to a beloved.
In all creations, everywhere, they all go there;
indeed, they obtain this very beloved one in the abode known as the inner palace.
Beholding that supreme wonder and being filled with great astonishment, they bowed to their Lord for the sake of attaining union with His own self and for His eternal residence within their forms.
Hari, perceiving her intention, embraced her to his chest with love and granted her a dwelling place by internalizing her within his own heart.
He always granted residence within his own form, or within the creation known as Mūrtigarbha,
to his beloved consorts— numbering ten million times a hundred billion— who were accompanied by their female companions.
Having caused them to enter, Lord Kṛṣṇa went to his own celestial arena;
the Blessed One Kṛṣṇa, though being both single and manifold, remained alone.
Thus fulfilling the desires of his devotees, the Lord— who is also independent by virtue of His own will—
caused His own expansion to enter into Himself.
The Lord caused all his sons, daughters, and so forth, along with the full extent of his male and female servants—
his own manifestation and his own expansion— to enter into himself.
Then, having vanished in an instant, he appeared again by himself in the temple of Kuṅkumavāpikā along with Lomaśa, who was likewise self-manifested.
Accompanied by Lakṣmī, who remained in his heart, by Aśvinī, and by Māṇikyā,
as well as by Vāhayā and a celestial chariot, Śrī Hari went to Aśvasaras.
The Teacher of the World, accompanied by Prajñāpadmāvatī, drank the water;
and whatever person should remember this pilgrimage and the seven sacred sites (saptāyatana), [they shall attain merit]. || 1.32 ||
He should go to Śrīkṛṣṇasvāmyācārya’s Śrī Haridhāma,
where Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa and Prajñā Mādhavī reside.
Lakṣmī, Lomaśa, Svataḥprakāśa, and Māṇikī—
this is indeed the sevenfold shrine (saptāyatana) that people should always remember.
Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa is the Supreme Brahman; he has three powers:
his power of knowledge is proclaimed as Pramā, and his power of will is proclaimed as Lakṣmī.
Padmāvatī is the power of action (kriyā-śakti), Māṇikyā is eternal splendor, Saṃkalpa is self-luminous, Lomaśa is the nature of Brahman, and Lomatī is the state of being a Brahmin. || 136 ||
Whoever installs and worships them shall obtain all desires;
Padmāvatī is indeed the divine splendor and radiance of the form of Hari.
Lakṣmī is its loveliness; the māṇikya gem is its nature of transparency;
self-luminosity is its circumference; and the hairy skin assumes the form of body hair. (138)
Having thus understood the seven forms as being essentially Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, he transcends liberation through separation and attains liberation in embodied form (mūrti-mukti).
To Rādhā, the power who removes suffering; to Lakṣmī, the power who bestows prosperity;
to Prajñā, the power who grants one's true nature; and to Padmāvatī, the power who grants liberation. || 4.118.140 ||
Having thus known the self-luminous Brahman, which is hairy, beginningless, liberated, and characterized by seven abodes, as being of the nature of Kṛṣṇa; 141.
"In this way, they attain supreme liberation in the highest abode; of this there is no doubt.
Thus did Hari, the Supreme Lord, speak to me long ago, O Badrī. (142)

Thus, in the *Śrī-Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*, within the fourth section, the *Tiṣya-Santāna*, [this chapter describes] the manifestation of the sixteen great festivals (*maholās*) beginning with the Raṅga-maholā to those liberated through the secret path (*rahasya-muktas*) in the supreme abode; the display of His divine opulences (*ṛddhi*); the display of all opulences and all of creation within His own form; the display of the creation of those liberated through identity (*tādātmya*) with the Primordial [Lord] residing within the womb of the form of Śrī Hari; the granting of liberation through identity within the womb of that form to the secret-liberated ones who possess such longing; and [the description of] Hari, who is the collective totality (*samaṣṭi-rūpa*) of the seven abodes (*saptāyatana*).
The one hundred and eighteenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Return to Kuṅkumavāpī and Other Matters."
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said: O Badrikā, wherever those women traveled by means of their celestial chariots,
there in the world of Īśvara, they found Lord Hari as their husband in every house.
He beheld the Supreme Lord in the heavenly world, beginning with Satyaloka,
and likewise everywhere in the Vairāja worlds and the worlds of the Īśvaras.
In every abode of the incarnations, as well as in every house within the imperishable realm (akṣara-dhāman), they beheld their husband Hari thus manifested.
She beheld her husband Hari, who had been released into the midst of all the difficult terrains,
and likewise every house as an abode of the beginningless Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa.
In the great halls and likewise in the heart of Kṛṣṇa,
he beheld his own Lord as a temple and as a reflected image.
Without Ādikṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, neither in his heart nor even in his physical form— which contains ten million forms— do liberated souls (muktas) exist at all.
Innumerable forms were manifested there;
what was seen by you then was likewise seen by me then.
Those who attain identity with that [reality] will see it as such; for others, however, no vision of that kind occurs at all. (8)
The first is the most excellent, the creation from the womb of the Form, known as identity;
the second, however, is in the supreme abode, the creation of the secret state.
The third [state], however, in the supreme abode, consists indeed of great liberation;
the fourth, in the supreme abode, is the creation of liberated beings, which is equal.

The entire [creation] consists of the eightfold *durgamā* (the difficult-to-traverse), yet it is devoted to the Supreme Brahman; however, the fifth [state] resides in the imperishable abode, and its creation leads to liberation within the Imperishable.
The sixth [kalā] is the abode of all incarnations (avatāras), consisting of that very essence;
and the seventh is the auspicious creation of the lords (īśvaras), consisting of pure being (sattva).
The eighth, however, is the creation consisting of the three qualities, composed of māyā;
likewise, the ninth is the supreme creation of Śaṅkara, Brahmā, and Viṣṇu.
The tenth is the auspicious creation of the Siddhas, consisting of the virtuous;
the eleventh belongs to the Pitṛs, and the twelfth to those who dwell in heaven.
The thirteenth [day] belongs to the great seers and to human beings, O Badrikā;
the fourteenth belongs to the animals, while the fifteenth belongs to the trees.
The sixteenfold qualities have these sixteen emanations;
however, that Supreme Self, the beginningless Puruṣottama, is non-emanation.
The Lord is the sustainer of all creation, the inner controller of all, and the sovereign master;
he is endowed with all as the witness of all, yet he is unconditioned, the supreme self-ruling one.

He is the one who assumes various forms—mixed with those that are both endowed with and devoid of attributes—such as his incarnations; he is the bestower of liberation, the giver of happiness to his devotees, and the embodiment of the establishment of dharma.
He is the leader of the worlds of form and the formless, and the destroyer accompanied by them;
having thus thoroughly understood the sixteenth Upaniṣad of these [principles].
One would become dispassionate, be liberated, and proceed to the supreme state;
there is no returning for him who thus knows the Sixteenth. 4.119.20.
Śrī Badrīpriyā said: O Lord Nara-Nārāyaṇa, tell me what the Blessed Puruṣottama did after arriving at Kuṅkumavāpī.
Śrī Nara-Nārāyaṇa said:
The beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, having come to the earth, performed the Cāturmāsya vow at the sacred site of Kuṅkumavāpikā. 22.
On the twenty-eighth day of his own manifestation,
at the time of dawn on the eighth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Kārttika, following his own festival.
The Blessed One gave gifts to the twice-born, such as gold, jewels, and cows, as well as palaces made of silver and other precious metals.
And for the sake of the brahmins, he gave away bowls, gems, jewels, horses, celestial chariots, vehicles, and elephants. || 25 ||
The Blessed One gave gifts of garments adorned with gold,
of all kinds of ornaments, and of resplendent couches.
Especially of crowns, bracelets, and chains;
and of pearls, crystals, and highly lustrous gomedas.
The Blessed One gave gifts of sandals,
as well as garlands, umbrellas, chowries, and walking-sticks adorned with golden leaves.
Hari gave [these] to the lion-thrones, chests, and caskets; and to the door-panels, cushions, mats, and lion-skins.
Bālakṛṣṇaka gave gifts of the skins of elephants, tigers, bears, deer, leopards, and gavayas, as well as of articles made from ivory.
Of woolen blankets, bodices, tunics, and coats of mail; of weapons, canopies, and especially of floor-coverings. || 31 ||
The Lord gave silken garments, washed cloths, turbans, beautiful bodices, and waistbands worn at the hips.
Of balls, wheels, and cotton-filled cushions;
of scales, pestles, and mortars filled with water.
He gave swings and children’s cradles, especially jars, as well as cooking pots, small baskets, and grinding stones.
Of stoves, fans, machines, and foot-protectors;
likewise of armor, rings, arrows, and bows. || 35 ||
And also for arrows, swords, and flaming mallets;
for ropes, mirrors, and those seeking to adorn their hair. (36)
And Janārdana gave gifts to those who guard the boundaries of fields, groves, buffaloes, and rain-clouds. (37)
And [he should offer] grains of crops, especially auspicious foods, as well as young shoots, trees that bear fruit, and those that blossom. || 38 ||
Of riches, water-jars, sacrificial posts, and abundant goods; of household utensils, beds, and excellent foods. || 39 ||
Hari gave gardens, groves, and ponds; he gave carts, palanquins, and pavilions in the form of cloth canopies.
And [the gift] of outer walls and houses, especially of enclosures, as well as the gifts of saddles, wells, water-basins, and horned animals. (41)
Of ladders, four-legged stools, silk garments, troughs, jars, and especially grain-bins; ||42||
Janārdana gave gifts of arches, lamps, bells, musical instruments, and lutes and harps.
The lord of cattle gave gifts to the necklaces, the maidens, the treasuries, the wives of the servants, the male slaves, and the female slaves as well. (44)
Of palm fruits, five kinds of vessels, cotton cloths, and likewise milk; of night-soiled garments, fragrant powders, betel nuts, and mouth-perfumes. ||45||
He also gave gifts of pens, Vedas, and sciences, as well as kitchen utensils and items required for the assembly hall. (46)
Hari indeed gave gifts of great festivals and other objects,
as well as of all kinds of minerals that destroy stinging insects and envy.
He gave excellent gifts of garments, beds, and canopies,
as well as boxes of flour and ships with golden birds.
Mādhava gave gifts of couches, four-legged seats, lutes, cymbals, and all kinds of women's ornaments. (49)
The cowherd gave gifts of sacrificial vessels and their accessories,
especially of bulls, male calves, and female calves.
The Lord gave [gifts] of vessels and water-pots, as well as diamonds,
and of sugar, molasses, and sweetmeats fragrant with honey.
The Lord gave honey, fresh butter, and ghee;
likewise, he gave split pulses and unbroken grains.
The Supreme Lord is the presiding deity of wheat, chickpeas, and mung beans,
as well as of the forest-dweller’s grains and of water-pots of excellent form.
The Lord gave [him] ladles—such as the *sruk* and *sruva*—and small cups (*camacī*), as well as large vessels, grand halls, and those who bind on helmets and other headgear. (54)
O Badrikā, the Lord of Ramā gave gifts of royal garments and other types of clothing,
as well as cotton, hemp, and black gram.
Likewise, he gave parched grain, kidney beans, and millet;
as well as liquids, fragrances, and liquid sandalwood.
Likewise, the Lord gave musk, as well as the finest camphor,
and fragrant substances such as cardamom, cloves, nutmeg, and mace.
There were also gifts of mustard seeds, ginger, and bitter pungents, as well as various kinds of foods—both those to be chewed and eaten, and those to be licked or sucked. (58)
Likewise, he gave grains fit for chewing, salts,
the finest spices, tubers, and leafy vegetables.
And there were gifts of fermented rice-gruel and the like, of roots, of sugarcanes with non-sour flowers, of buttermilk, of sacrificial porridges, and of milks. (4.119.60)
The Lord gave [the kingdom] to the parrots dwelling in cages, to the menakas and other birds, to the sarikas, to the ghatakas, and to the garudas.
Of cuckoos, partridges, birds such as the bhāradvāja, peacocks, swans, and many-horned deer; ||62||
The giver of gifts bestowed gifts upon horses and camels,
and likewise provided for the livelihoods of the images of the gods.
He gave [gifts] to female figurines as well as to other male figurines;
indeed, he bestowed secret gifts of cosmic eggs and jars.
Likewise, he gave collections of halls and temples,
as well as helmets, turbans, and garments from the wish-fulfilling trees.
The illustrious Supreme Lord gave gifts of wish-fulfilling creepers;
he gave diamonds, pearls, and excellent rubies.
Hari gave sapphires, emeralds, and lapis lazuli;
he also gave karketanas, topazes, and bhīṣmaka gems.
The Lord gave all the pulakas, rudhiras, and sphaṭikas;
the Supreme Ruler gave the vidrumas, kaustubhas, and cintāmaṇis.
Rubies, swords as bright as the moon, iron blades, and likewise golden ones; sun-stones, divine glass, glass-machines, and lamps.
Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa also gave to the twice-born all kinds of golden vessels and very beautiful jhumbharas.
Prabheśvara gave many jewels to the maidens and indeed to the youths;
he gave to the poor, the helpless, guests, mendicants, and the virtuous.
He offered the gift of a mountain of gold, presented a mountain of sesame seeds, gave the gift of the golden earth, and made the offering of a wish-fulfilling tree.
The gift of a golden cow, which bestows the fortune of gold;
the gift of a sesame cow, and the gift of a thousand cows. ||73||
The lord of Padmāvatī gave gifts of gold and horses,
and the husband of the virtuous woman caused gifts of daughters to be bestowed upon the poor.
The gift of a golden bull and the gift of a golden elephant;
the gift of the eight world-protectors (lokapālas) and the offering to Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva. ||75||
That lord of the virtuous indeed performed various *śrāddha* rites on the bank of the Aśvapaṭṭasara lake; he offered oblations and gave libations. (76)
He, Kṛṣṇa alone, performed all the Śrāddha rites for his fathers, those for his mothers as well, and all the Nāndī-Śrāddhas.
Whatever has been offered by Kṛṣṇa for the sake of worship throughout the worlds, and whatever has been acquired for the kings, celestial sages, ancestors, and the lords; ||78||
And that which was acquired from the merchant-princes, as well as from the Daityas and Dānavas;
and that which was obtained from the Yakṣas, the Rākṣasas, and the Nāgas. (79)
Whatever has been earned by his own two arms for the sake of his devotees and those seeking liberation—all that, as well as his own wealth and even the wealth of his wives—[he offers]. (4.119.80)
The Lord of Monkeys gave away crores, billions, and trillions of lotuses as gifts;
indeed, everything belonging to Hari was gracious, divine, and bestowing liberation.
Having repeatedly considered [this] as a worthy recipient of gifts, gods and others, as well as lords, liberated souls, Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, and the twice-born, have become so. (82)
And even those of all other castes, desiring the greatness of Kṛṣṇa’s grace, became mendicants; indeed, they were all Kṛṣṇa-mendicants (bhikṣukas). ||8.2||
Whosoever obtained divine objects from the hand of Kṛṣṇa, they became freed from sin through the possession of those very objects. ||84||
Having repeatedly become the locus of great merit and the abode of divine qualities,
they indeed became devoted to Hari, possessing an excellence of being.
At the end of their bodies, having remembered that supreme Hari through that yoga,
they went to the supreme abode— the world of Brahmā and likewise the imperishable realm.
They went to Vaikuṇṭha, Goloka, Śrīpura, the immortal abode,
the unmanifest state, and indeed to the station of Viṣṇu.
Oh, Śrī Badrikā! Those by whom that grace-bestowing [shrine] was taken hold of became free from poverty and attained great prosperity upon the earth. (88)
In the past, during the yoga of Hari, those who were filled with joy and praised the gifts of Kṛṣṇa became partakers of supreme liberation. (89)
Even those who merely accepted his virtues attained the path of liberation;
so too did those who drank even the milk of the cows bestowed by Kṛṣṇa.
By the power of that temple’s grace, they too attained its abode;
for garlands adorned with diamonds and other gems were the very forms of Kṛṣṇa’s favor.

Those by whom ornaments were worn upon the body, those by whom even garments were donned, those who enjoyed couches and the like, and those who maintained most pure attire—[all these have been purified]. (92)
Indeed, by those very [deities] who preside over vehicles, mounts, chariots, and celestial palaces,
these sanctuaries have been rendered pure through their grace.
Those by whom the dust of Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s feet was held upon their bodies, and those by whom his dwellings were likewise held, they all attained the Supreme.
Even those who have consumed fruits obtained through the grace of Kṛṣṇa, as well as those who have used mats, seats, silken cloths, woolen blankets, and the like [belonging to him]. (95)
O Badrī, those by whom these [sites] were consecrated also became purified and went to the supreme state;
for the Blessed One dwells eternally on the bank of the Aśvapaṭṭasara lake.
He [honored] one hundred thousand Brahmins together with their wives, two hundred thousand boys,
as well as one hundred thousand maidens and youths, and one hundred thousand poor guests.
With true devotion, he indeed feeds hundreds of thousands of virtuous men, hundreds of thousands of virtuous women, and hundreds of thousands of mendicants with auspicious, sweet foods.
Always, always [offer] most excellent, fragrant, and abundant clarified butters, combined with milk-rice porridge and accompanied by sweetmeat balls (laḍḍukas). ||99||
And he would constantly feed him unwholesome vegetables, delicious boiled rice, and curd-rice mixed with clarified butter.
He gratifies the twice-born with drinks, betel leaves, and other unsurpassed mouth-fresheners, as well as with sacrificial fees consisting of gold coins.
When the twenty-eighth great festival day arrived during the rainy season,
Hari was worshipped there by Brahmins and kings on the occasion of his own birth.
The Lord was worshipped by the gods, the liberated ancestors, the Vaiṣṇavas,
and by all the virtuous embodied beings of every world.
In that same way, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa Hari is eternally worshipped;
He grants liberation to His worshippers in His own supreme abode.
O Badrikā, in your own abode on the bank of the Aśvasaras lake, the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa—the beloved Master who removes all suffering—resides. 105.

Thus ends the one hundred and nineteenth chapter, titled "The Description of how the Blessed Lord bestowed his countless self-earned riches and so forth," in the Tiṣya lineage within the fourth section of the glorious *Lakṣmīnārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Naranārāyaṇa said: O Badrikā, the Lord Śrī Harikṛṣṇa, the master who maintains great vows, remained for two years as a forest-dweller (vānaprastha), perfectly tranquil.
Constantly devoted to the vow of Brahman, he awakened others to the path of devotion;
he was well-joined with circles of sages, virtuous men, yogis, and ascetics.
Devoted to self-meditation and possessing the virtue of renunciation,
the Sadhyas and Siddhas assemble in the hall in the presence of Hari.
For discourses concerning the inner self, which bestow liberation, are being propagated;
indeed, many embodied beings, having received initiation, go to the supreme state.
O Badrikā, Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa too was free from possessions; liberated from all worldly dealings, he desired the path of renunciation.
He desired from the preceptor Lomaśa the great initiation of a renunciant saint,
and he entreated Lomaśa during the bright fortnight of the month of Kārtika.
On the eleventh day, the Supreme Lord took the great initiation for the sake of protecting the sequence of the stages of life and for the purpose of establishing dharma.
Even the Blessed Supreme Lord, the creator of Dharma himself, the embodiment of Dharma, and its ordainer, desired the great initiation. || 8 ||
The eternal support of the stages of life (āśramas), he desired the great initiation (mahādīkṣā),
from which initiations proceed and from which indeed sacrifices and vows arise.
When he desired great liberation, he also sought initiation;
for his word is the Vedic utterance, and his resolve is considered the ritual injunction.
He, by whose grace all fruit is obtained, whose surrender is higher than the highest,
and whose very glance is the great initiation (mahādīkṣā), even he desired initiation.
Whatever fruit is proclaimed for initiation, whatever knowledge is attained through initiation, and by which there may be the washing away of sins through grace; ||| 1-2 ||
Even he, the Lord of all incarnations, who is capable of granting liberation by his own will even without her, desired the great initiation.
That very touch, which through the mere stroke of a weapon leads even to the liberation of sinful living beings, he too desired as his initiation.
That touch of women which is preceded by desire always effects their elevation, and even that embrace which produces liberation— he too desired as his initiation.
He, whose toe-water is the Gaṅgā that grants liberation to all embodied beings,
and who himself grants liberation to his devotees— he too desired initiation.
O Badrikā, he who is himself the one to whom one must go through initiation exists there;
by his yoga, people from their own bodies have gone and are going to the supreme state.
By him, Brahmapriyā and the others were liberated and led to his own abode;
by that very same one, they were protected there with divine bodies.
Since virtuous people become bestowers of liberation through the attainment of mantras,
he too desired initiation, which grants liberation to all living beings.
Having obtained even a mere fragment of sovereignty that grants initiation and liberation,
he, being a beggar for initiation, longed for the Great Initiation (mahādīkṣā).
Through his worship, Romaśa and Lomaśa also became great liberated ones and great sages, long-lived and ever-granters of liberation. (21)
Because that lay disciple was a performer of all auspicious deeds, a virtuous brahmin-sage, and a supreme purifier, Kṛṣṇa desired the great initiation from him.
Hari, who is worshiped by all, worships his devotees, being overwhelmed with love;
even this Lord Kṛṣṇa worships the sage Lomaśa.
The teacher, having instructed the boy, receives from the boy that which is essential; the initiator, having instructed the sage, receives from the sage the sacrificial fee. ||24||

Thus, in order to protect that great initiation (mahādīkṣā) which had been handed down through a succession of previous teachers for the sake of creation and preservation, Kṛṣṇa sought it from Lomaśa.
On the tenth day, Śrī Hari indeed observed a fast without even water;
he consumed the five products of the cow (pañcagavya) for the purpose of purifying his body. ||26||
Likewise, he performed the Aghamarṣaṇa rite through bathing at sacred fords and other such acts;
and at night, he kept a vigil with songs, hymns of praise, and auspicious ceremonies.
Having risen early in the morning, he indeed performed his bath and meditation upon his own self,
and he also carried out the worship of the gods according to the prescribed rites.
He had his head shaved, bathed in the waters of sacred fords and other holy sites, and also performed auspicious rites such as the *śrāddha* ceremony which brings satisfaction to the ancestors. (29)
He quickly had a sacrificial pit and a beautiful pavilion constructed;
he caused the declaration of an auspicious day to be recited and poured water upon the ground.

He performed the ritual sipping of water (ācamana) and the ritual placements (nyāsa) according to the prescribed rules; then, having performed the breath-control exercises (prāṇāyāma), he carried out the worship of Gaṇeśa.

He performed the worship of the deities of the site (vāstu) and others, as well as the worship of the vardhanī and kalaśa vessels, and he also performed the worship of the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), the pavilion (maṇḍapa), and the gods.

The worship of the planets, the thorough worship of all the guardians of the directions, as well as the honoring of the world-protectors and likewise the honoring of the sages and the ancestors; ||33||
The worship of goddesses and deities, as well as the worship of the lords (Īśvaras), the worship of the mistresses (Īśanīs), and the thorough worship of the incarnations (avatāras). ||34||
Likewise, there is the worship of the Mothers, the Yoginīs, and the virtuous women;
thereafter, the worship of the Liberated Ones (Muktas) and the worship of the female Liberated Ones (Muktānikās). ||35||
He performed worship worthy of the Supreme Brahman, as well as worship of all the principles (tattvas),
and he carried out the honoring of the people of the earth.
He established the rules for atonement and performed a fire sacrifice;
he worshipped the Fire-god and offered libations to all the deities through the mouth of Agni.
The Blessed One performed a fire sacrifice consisting of milk, clarified butter, and milk-rice,
as well as fruits, flowers, honey, and sacrificial fuel-sticks that were pleasing to the oblation.
He performed the offering of *kavya* and the presentation of funeral cakes (*piṇḍas*);
he also performed a great fire-sacrifice (*mahāhoma*) with bilva fruits and other offerings, along with a stream of clarified butter.
In the midst of them, having set aside his garments, he put on saffron-colored robes: a lower garment, a breastplate-like tunic, an upper robe, and a turban.
He also took up the sacred thread, a lower garment, an upper robe,
sandals, a loincloth, and water-pots.
He applied a sectarian mark (tilaka) made of sandalwood and saffron on his forehead,
and having tied his topknot, he received from his preceptor the Vaiṣṇava Gāyatrī mantra.
"Let us know the Supreme Brahman; let us meditate upon the beginningless Kṛṣṇa;
may that Hari inspire us"—thus he received [this mantra] from Lomaśa. (43)
He took up the eight-syllabled mantra: "Oṃ, I am the Supreme Brahman," and [the prayer]:
"Omanādikṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, may You be my refuge. ||44||
And she received the sixteen-syllable mantra from the sage Lomaśa;
having thus obtained these three mantras, she bowed down to him three times.
Having bowed to Lomaśa, Agni, and the gods, and having circumambulated them, the virtuous one, the son of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, prostrated himself like a staff. ||46||
He received the grace of the gods, worshipped his guru Lomaśa,
and presented him with divine, excellent gifts, including one made of gold.
And Janārdana, becoming a renunciant, bestowed sacrificial fees;
he who is obtained like Kṛṣṇa became the beloved Śrī Kṛṣṇa. ||48||

The Vaiṣṇava is indeed the Supreme Brahman, the Swan (Haṃsa) resplendent with realized knowledge; the Lord who has entered the stage of renunciation is the Supreme Brahman, the Swan in the form of a holy man.
The Lord Nārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇa, has become beloved by all;
that Supreme Lord always abides in the state of being the Master.
Having attained lordship through initiation, he then became the Lord of Lords;
his constant vow was celibacy, the greatest of all vows being devotion. (51)
The blessed Kṛṣṇa, the son of Nārāyaṇa,
protected [the assembly] at the time of initiation in the pavilion, along with the great sages, holy men, and virtuous women.
There they offered blessings for the supreme welfare of the Supreme Soul;
the Blessed One shone forth in two forms, likewise wearing the saffron-colored robes.
Although he was the form of a king of kings, he [was honored] in the minds of all;
indeed, at the time of initiation, musical instruments were sounded on every side.
At that time, Vedic mantras, the songs of the great sages, the hymns of celestial nymphs,
and the praises of human women resounded throughout the pavilion and other areas.
Having received both the oral instruction and initiation, he entered the auspicious stage of renunciation;
he then performed the final oblation, offered the fire sacrifice, and indeed bestowed gifts.
Except for the leaf-hut, he bestowed everything else, including houses and so forth, consisting of gold, diamonds, silver, jewels, cattle, wealth, and garments.
Afterwards, the Lord Hari dwelt in the hermitage of Lomaśa in the guise of a disciple, within that circle of renunciants frequented by countless holy men.
He dwelt there with a peaceful mind and soul, showing great respect for the service of the virtuous, and was constantly devoted to the liberation of countless classes of living beings. (59)
Then Lakṣmī, having become separate, virtuous and wearing saffron robes, praised the nature of her Lord, the one who delights in the Supreme Brahman.
Oṃ, salutations to you, the glorious Supreme Brahman;
salutations to the Supreme Self, the sovereign lord of the liberated Brahmas, who dwells in the supreme abode.
Salutations to you, the yogi who dwells in the great Śrīraṅga and other abodes, who is non-different from liberation itself, and who serves those liberated in secret.

Salutations to You, who are untainted, who serve those who are greatly liberated and those liberated from the beginningless, and who are served by hosts of liberated ones through imperishable syllables.
Salutations to you who are served by Īśvara and others through their incarnations;
salutations to you who are served by the sages, the ancestors, the gods, and others. ||64||
And salutations to you, who are served by humans and others, as well as by yakṣas, gandharvas, kinnaras, nāgas, sarpas, and rākṣasas.
Salutations to you who are frequented by those born from sprouts, from eggs, and from sweat, as well as by men, women, and all beings, both stationary and moving. (66)
Salutations to you who, when properly served, grant nourishment and happiness;
salutations to you who fulfill the desires of countless yogins. ||67||
Salutations to you, the deliverer of your countless devotees;
salutations again and again to you, the Lord of Māṇikya and Badarī.
The royal sage named Badara established the hermitage of Badarikāśrama;
by a portion of whose grace [I exist], I bow to that Lord, Badrikeśvara. (69)
Salutations to you, who are pleased with that King Badara, by whom the asura Hemānala was slain at the foot of the mountain.
At the foot of his own Badarī tree, he crushed the golden fire;
I bow to that Kṛṣṇa, who appeared in the form of a virtuous sage, by whose majesty he was subdued. ||71||
I bow here to that Supreme Self, the venerable Lord Śrī Svāmī, by whose grace even the jujube fruit (*badara*) came to possess the nature of nectar within its fruit. (72)
I bow to that Lord Śrī Svāmin, the Master of the Fruit, by whose grace even a human being always attains the state of a seed within the fruit known as the jujube. 73.
Salutations to him by whom the liberation of the deceased Brahmin Śrīśīla was accomplished through the gift of a jujube fruit. (74)
Salutations to him who, even after showing himself in the forms of a virtuous monk and nun to the king for the sake of his wife’s misfortune, did not release the king from his bondage. 75.
Having given two jujube fruits to the wife of the Brahmin deity, Badrikā gave birth to a son and a daughter; O Lord of Badarī, salutations to you! (76)
I bow to that Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Nārāyaṇa, by whose majesty the wife of Kṛṣṇa was born as a young female yoginī, the daughter of Sureśvarī. ||77||
Salutations again and again to that Kṛṣṇa, who, having made the celestial-bodied Cāraṇī Nāgnakeśarī his pearl necklace, led her to the imperishable realm (Akṣara).
By means of skillful application, liberation was achieved through the agency of a playful, entertaining woman; and even the world of the gods was made into a circle of female companions. (79)
Salutations to that Lord who granted him liberation;
and salutations to his wife Bāhulakā and to Līlāvatī for her dancing.
To him who was satisfied with you, Hari gave the essence of Brahman, which is liberation; salutations always to him.
In ancient times, Hari [granted this] to the two garland-makers, Māli and Yavana, and to Mallikā. 81.
Being pleased, Kṛṣṇa then caused them both to drink the essence of Brahman and granted them liberation; homage to that Lord! (82)
To the hero of wisdom, who possessed the perception of the gods as his own kin, Hari himself granted liberation for both him and his wife; salutations to that Lord Śrī Svāmin. (83)

He, a treasure-trove of compassion, delivered by his devotion a fisherman who was wandering like one in shackles and was deeply distressed by the curse of a fish; [this was done] through his wife’s devotion. (84)
Anaya went to his own supreme abode together with that woman,
as well as her daughter, the virtuous and chaste Puṇḍarīkā.
The third [nature] is Nirvāṇikā, who is a mass of bliss;
likewise, the fivefold [group] consisting of Jñānadarbhī and the others also [worship] that Lord. (86)
Having attained liberation by worshipping him, I worship that Lord Hari,
who was freed from tuberculosis by a grateful woman named Kuthalī.
He provided protection and granted liberation; I bow to that Lord, the Master, who, through his association with the virtuous, [overcame] the poison of the enchantress Prātaraṇī. 88.
I bow to that Lord Śrī Svāmī, the Master, who performed a deliverance;
through the company of the virtuous, he liberated Gaṅgājanī from her bondage. 89.
Salutations to that Hari, who made Ramāñjanī his wife Ramā,
as well as Sunāriṇī, Kulālī, Raṇastamba, and her husband.
I bow to that Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Beloved, the Master, and the Sovereign, who by means of perfect yoga liberated His son from saṃsāra. 9.1
Being pleased by the great devotion of Hemasudhā, the wife of a goldsmith, he granted her the supreme status of Annapūrṇā.
He likewise granted liberation at the end; I bow to the glorious Lord Hari, who, through union with Rādhikā, became Viṣṭiṇī, the daughter of Vidruma. 93.
Salutations to that Lord who made Rādhā equal to Himself in His abode, and who, through the application of dharma, caused even a low-caste woman from Mālava to attain liberation. 94.
Salutations to that illustrious Lord, who provided a wife and family for the sage Hitāñjali, who had been working as a street-sweeper. 95.

The Lord, through his yoga, brought about liberation for Hetu, Añjala, and the daughters by means of listening to the discourse, and by his power, he brought about their state of freedom from delusion.
Salutations again and again to him who brought about liberation;
his five brothers, Nirañjana and the others, were likewise such [as he]. (97)
I bow to the Lord Śrī Svāmin, by whom liberation was brought forth;
and to Gomatī, the fashioner of the Yantra, as well as Nayarāja and his consort. 98.
I praise that Mādhava who protected [him] from consumption;
Kṛṣṇa effected the liberation of the cunning Kanakāṅgadā. (99)
I bow to that Lord and Master, Hari, who brought about the welfare of Bhāṇavāṇī, the female gambler, and also of King Rāyahari. 4.120.100.
That Lord who brought about the welfare of King Mādhavarāya, and who liberated the divine Vaidyotikā from Kaṃsārī; || 10 1 ||
He [saw] the potter Nararāja, his wife Ratnikā,
Ambālikā the goldsmith, and Vinodinī the smelter of ores.
Hari liberated the actor who was skilled in pleasing others,
and He also liberated Śrī Rāmasundara, who was miserly.
I bow to that Supreme Self, the Lord, the consecrated Master, the King Kṣīrodavīra, and his Queen Ruhāriṇī. || 104 ||
I bow to that Lord who liberated the courtesan Somikā along with her five sons, and who is the husband of Aruṇānī and the master of Pāṭalānī. 109.
I bow to that Lord Hari, the Master, who liberated the noble ones from the drinking of intoxicants and who caused the cessation of the banner of sweet liquor. 106.
I bow to that Lord Hari, who brought about the liberation from the one called Gaṇḍavāta and from Cakrīṇī, and who granted release from the doctrine of Yāska.
I bow to that Lord Hari, the Master, who brought about the liberation of the one who reviled him when she spoke twice, and likewise of the husband named Garjana. 108.
He who liberated the Brahmin Suraprasāda from his preceptor-killer, and that Lord who also delivered his mother and father—[to him I bow]. (109)
Salutations to you, the liberator even of King Nāgavikrama, who was devoted to the injury of the gods and possessed of nine types of enmity.
Salutations to that Lord Śrī, by whom Śālamitra, who was destroying his livelihood, and Jayālakṣmī, his beloved wife, were delivered.
I worship that Lord Hari, who, through the application of his power, freed from the messengers of Yama the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, who was a destroyer of maidens and full of poison. 11.2.
Salutations again and again to that Kṛṣṇa who liberated Sādhujīva, Kumāra, Kumārī, Sādhujīvanī, and Nirviṣāda.
Salutations to that Lord Śrī Svāmī, who granted liberation to Nārāyaṇī, Prabhāvatī, and the woman named Ghaṭamālā. 1.14.
Salutations to that Kṛṣṇa, the Lord and Master, who brought about the liberation of Anaṅgavallī, the procuress, and her companions. 115.
Salutations again and again to him who liberated the one named Ṣaṇḍhavajra from saṃsāra, and who brought about the attainment of masculinity for those who were neuter. 11.6.
Salutations to Hari, who liberated Yavasaṃdha, Māṃsāda, his wife Majāvalī, and their entire family; salutations to him! 1.17.
He who liberated the merchant Bhaṇḍa along with his family, and likewise liberated the Trigartas, the Bhavāyanas, and others. || 1.18 ||
Lord Hari liberated the wrestlers Harivīrya and others, and he also liberated the usurers Harilāla and the rest.
Salutations to that Lord who liberated the assembly of deer, such as the parrots and others, and who also liberated the serpent Vāliṭa from his curse. || 4.120.1 || 20 ||
I worship him who liberated Vilāsadeva from Luñcāda, who brought about the release of Sārahāsīya, Mārtaṇḍa, Maṇḍala, and others. 121.
[He saw] Daiva, Prakāśaka, and others who were his sons and had been duly initiated,
as well as Mauktikāyanikā and others who were his daughters and likewise virtuous women.
I bow to that illustrious Lord,
the Master, who liberated him named Duritaghoṣa, the devourer of all, from his bondage.
I worship him who liberated his wife Mahāsatyāyanī, and who liberated her sons and daughters. (1.24)
I always worship that Lord Śrī Svāmin, who liberated the great minister Dharmabhaṭa and his beloved wife Śīlayānī.
I bow to that Janārdana, who liberated Dharmādhyakṣa, the lord Mukunda, and Sāvitra, as well as his wife Nyāyākṣiṇī. 126.
I bow to that Lord and Master, Hari, who raised up the scribe Viśālarekhaka and his wife Śucikāntā.
I bow to the beloved Lord Kṛṣṇakānteśvara,
the Supreme Sovereign who liberated the Kāyasthas, Karaṇas, and others.
I bow to Him who liberated Śāha from his afflictions and others, and by whom the vulture, possessing the body of a former weaver, was uplifted. 129.
By him was the cat Uddhṛta formerly rescued, who was a cowherd at Gobāra;
and by him was the jackal Uddhṛta formerly rescued, the merchant Ṭhaṭhūṭholaka.
